text: Oh my god I loved this beach. Fairly calm in terms of waves and you get to see Ridley Scotts and a lot of them! They just practically swam around us while we fed them seaweed. Experience never to be forgotten.

title: Just relaxing
text: My favorite place to forget about everything , best beach in sri lanka , amazing people , the best place to meet new people, night life there is amazing all clubs are amazing even staff amazing & friendly

title: Clean, crowded, DON'T touch or feed the turtles.
text: A clean, smallish beach, some good snorkeling spots, better further along than the main beach. Don't be tempted to touch or feed the turtles, they are wild animals and should be observed with awe and respect, rather than encouraged to feed close to the shore or used for shameless to Instagram self-promotion.

title: Turtle heaven
text: A nice beach but no sun loungers,parts are easy to paddle and walk into the sea,it can get quite busy and boats are coming and going.The best part is seeing the turtles that are in the shallow waters along the bend of the beach,they seem to be there most of the day though we were told it’s usually early morning then late afternoon.

title: A bit crowded but still nice and clean beach
text: We visited Hikkaduwa for a day and first we thought it was over crowded but when walking towards south it was more calm, water was clear and we even saw a big turtle. We really enjoyed ‘Your choise’ beach restaurant with its ambience and nice service.

title: Nice Beach
text: This Beach was close enough to our Hotel Aditya ,and supposedly the Best Beach in the Area,so we spent the Afternoon there ,It was a weekend so the place was crowded & palapas were hard to come by,we managed to get one with a little extra cash . The place was crowded & only one restaurant to serve Food & drinks. One section of the Beach is filled with Fishing Boats. all in all nice to visit ONCE

title: Public beaches are not maintained.
text: As a result, they are polluted with plastics and flotsam. Coarse sand/fine gravel is uncomfortable to walk on. The shoreline often slopes rapidly to the sea, which is prone to large waves and undercurrents. Not recommended for very young and/or weak swimmers.

title: Obly clean in front of Royal Palms and Tangerine
text: In front of the two hotels Royal Palms Beach and Tangerine, the beach is properly clean. North of these hotels, very dirty and no cleaning whatsoever it seems. Kalutara administration has a huge potential for improvement if they are really keen on attracting tourists.

title: Walk
text: The beach is in a poor and neglected state. Only good for walks nothing else. Its better to look for other better beaches around.

title: A lovely peaceful holiday
text: I found the hotel to be friendly and there was nothing that was to much trouble. The room was immaculate everyday and comfortable. The view was stunning from the room and my favourite part of the day was watching the sun go down from the balcony. The food was superb.. I especially enjoyed my egg hoppers in the morning ... the chefs do a wonderful job and I had no complaints about choice ... the traditional food was wonderful also. The bar staff were always happy to speak with you and were very accommodating letting my husband watch cricket .. there was plenty of tea and coffee available which I enjoyed as I cant drink beer 24/7 My highest praise goes to the lovely pool guys . I have arthritis and struggle shifting sunbeds , every day they made sure I was ok and had a sun bed and plenty of shade .. I cant thank them enough.. Our rep Nigel was very informative and sorted out a great trip for us . The only reason it didn't get the full 5 stars was continually being pestered on the beach .. my husband could cope with the banter but it got draining by the second week and it's not nice to be stared at when all you want to do is get some peace looking at the sea .. I do understand they have to make a living.. Thank you for a lovely stay

title: North Kalutara Beach
text: Lovely beach but not excellent - very strong waves and currents at different times of the day - red flags used when it’s not safe. Steep drop off at the waters edge and then a sand bar for about 15m. By the water the beach is sloped and not flat - there is a flat sandy area further back from the waterfront.

title: Sunrise and Sunset View
text: The beach is very nice and clean with loads of sea shells in the sand. There are big stones near the beach which makes it very interesting to watch while high tide. The best view is during sunrise and sunset. If you are staying in Anantara or Avani hotel at Kaluthara, you can enjoy their private Kaluthara beach. Must go beach if you love to relax.

title: Interesting, both ?????? bathing and fishing boats
text: sparse with people as there are not so many hotels along the beaches. In the morning you see the fishermen coming in from the sea and you meet some cows that seem to stay close at night.

title: A good place to wander about
text: Long, reasonably clean and empty. A few colourful fishing boats to photograph and the occasional place for light refreshment - Sri Lankan style

title: Nice walk
text: Nice sandy beach to walk on. Not too bothered by hawkers who tend to congregate around the entrances to the hotels.

title: Beach under renovation
text: Problems caused by the sea earlier on so now putting in retaining wall to stop anymore erosion. Beautiful sunsets ??

title: Vet clean and amazing sunset
text: Very clean beach with amazing sunsets and lots of shells to collect and find - near the Avani and Anantara hotel and lots of Cafe outlets off the beach as well

title: Beautiful beach but beware of the undertow!
text: A beautiful beach that offers miles of golden sand. Near the hotels you can find restaurants but you can be bothered by beach sellers and guides offering tours. Be polte but firm and they'll leave you alone. A nice beach for sunbathing if that's your thing but you would need to be a really good swimmer to swim there. Large waves that break noisily onto a steeply shelving shore means that you'll need to shout to make yourself heard. If you venture into the water when the surf's up,make sure you're with someone because the undertow is evil and will take you right off your feet in a surprisingly shallow amount of water.

title: Long Stretch
text: We stayed at the Mermaid Hotel and from our room beach looked lovely. On our first walk in morning going south we found beach hard going for walking, it’s tilts too unevenly so you are walking lob sided we found, also with this being a fishing town quite a bit of diesel spillage and other rubbish along the way. Next walk we went in opposite direction and found the same. Hotel Mermaid cleans the beach right outside but obviously not the full stretch

title: Stunning!
text: Beautiful Kalutara beach. Very clean and well kept. It was a pleasure to watch the early Fishermen in the morning pull up there boats on this lovely beach. Lots of local sellers directly outside hotel on the beach selling beautiful Sri Lankan beach wraparounds. Stunning place to just sit and think and watch the roller waves wash in.

title: Narrow beach
text: Nice sandy beach but very narrow no sunbeds allowed on beach or chairs sea very tough large waves good evening stroll

title: Beautiful, but be aware
text: Long beautiful almost deserted beach lined with palm trees. How come you are all alone most of the time? Because the water is not safe to swim in, so be aware of high waves and strong currents. Well worth a stroll anyway and you can get your feet wet and still be safe. But I would not recommend swiming for everyone, only strong swimmers. Definately not for small children.

title: Nice and clean...
text: Its a nice and clean beach and one can easily walk barefoot on the fine sand...Although the waves were very tricky during our visit, it was still worthwhile..

title: Angry waves
text: Lovely scenery, beautiful sand but even as a good swimmer, I did not dare swim in the water, the waves were too rough!

title: Smooth white sand...
text: Stayed at Tangerine Hotel - just a few meters walk to shore - wonderful waves and great beach! Life guards are on duty - the sea is suitable for swimmers..

title: Not the Best for swimming
text: Best time to stroll along this beach is early morning when there are not the local people trying to sell you something, Tide and undercurrent make it not the safest of places for swimming.

title: Peaceful Beach
text: The beach is not that crowded, it is clean and peaceful. If you are in this area it is worth a visit.

title: Disappointing
text: The beach looks ok from a distance, but it is not sandy, it is rough grit and not clean with dog excrement, litter and worse still broken glass. Shoes are definitely required for any strolls on the beach.

title: polluted beach
text: Here are photos of the beach outside Tangerine resort today. it has been like this since we arrived on Sunday.

title: great beach sadley under used
text: Butifull unmolested beach great for a stroll ,my Wife and I used to go down there for a swim everyday the sea can get rough so be aware of this.some litter scattered about which should be cleaned up.

title: Beach Hotel
text: It was brilliant just sitting eating your meal looking out at the beachfront when we was on our way to the hotel from the airport was a elephant just walking at the side of the road it was amazing.

title: Lovely long beach
text: Great for walking this stretch of coast. Sea can be rough and there is a rip currant. Red flags are often used.

title: beautiful to look at....
text: ...but dangerous to swim in The waves was fare to high when we was there but to walk along the beach is amazing

title: Nice to walk along at sunset
text: Very soft sand that you sink into, good fun watching all the crabs fly out in front of you and run for the sea. Lots of people selling goods and tours but all are polite and not pushy.

title: Good Beach
text: Hotel Avani had private beach. Enjoyed morning walk and sunset . Although steep but fully secure for quick swim

title: great for nice long walks sea was a bit rough but expected at this time of year
text: lovely beach and lovely local people to chat to water was a bit rough at this time of year but was expected

title: Nice clean beach
text: Though it is a nice and clean beach but is very dangerous for swim. Just next to our resort, it was good for morning walk.

title: Broken sea shells
text: the beach looks lovely. it can be a little hard to walk on because it is all broken sea shells .Disappointed that we could not swim in the sea. Red flag was flying all the time. We went in September, which is not the summer period, so may be a little less calmer in the main season.

title: A clean and quite beach dotted with some water sport activities and restro!
text: A clean and neat beach, with space to enjoy without being bothered. The place is good for families and couples and was quite safe when we travelled. The best part was there was no littering of any kind

title: Beach near our hotel
text: Very steep there was no way I would swim in this sea too rough and a steep ledge which would be a risk for anyone with a mobility issue.

title: Great Beach Rough Sea.
text: The beach on this side of the island is all you would want if the sea was calmer. During our two weeks the red flag flew every day . Dont risk it

title: Not a beach to spend too much time on
text: Maybe it was a bad time of the year but this beach was not impressive. It was dirty and left untended by the abutting hotels, bars, commercial enterprises, etc. It could be so much nicer.

title: Kalutara beach Shri Lanka
text: I happened stay @ Royal coco resort for two days during my Shri Lanka travel in April 2017 Since the resort is lactated in the vicinity of Kalutara Beach ,I took a round of the beach both in the evening and night for two days continuously. The tourists from the European countries were found to enjoy uncrowded beach.There are some restaurants serving sea food on the bank but thy are under thatched roof and attract a few tourists Massage centers are not in a good ambiance so I avoided visiting it.There are some beautiful trees and overall the beach is clean I would rate it as a reasonably good place to visit during travel to Shri Lanka. That does not mean one should go there specially.It could be included in the itinerary

title: Golden Beach!
text: Unfortunayely I was in low season, so, I could not manage to swim in the ocean, but loved walking barefoot on golden sands... It's fantastic!

title: out of season it was awful
text: We were there in low season and the beach was awful and dangerous. It was hard to imagine in high season it would be much better.

title: Poor
text: The coast is not good to visit even for a walk.Not a place to stop.Not a tourist attraction. Drive further South for better beaches.

title: Beautiful deserted beach
text: The beach is not safe so swimming so the best thing about this lovely beach is that there r few tourists on sun beds it is just a fabulous deserted beach.

title: Fantastic place
text: Had great stay and enjoyed alot.. The place is very good. The view from the room is great..Clean beach with always safe guard ??.

title: trip to yala national reserve
text: what a great place to visit. saw 2 panthers, 2 bears, ,crocks, wild boar, troops of monkeys and numbers of. birds and small animals. However when we were there the Elephants went on holiday. others saw elephants on the days they went to visit however they never saw the panthers and bears. It looks like luck is the decider. LOVED it

title: Beach
text: Sea was very rough could not go swimming.sand is quite coarse . There were women there trying to sell dresses and a couple of beggars on beach

title: Holiday Beach Time
text: Our hotel was alongside Kalutara Beach and we went out onto it most days. The beach was quite clean compared to some I have seen in the Far East - only the odd bit of litter. The sea does look rough and appears to be deep but there is a shelf and once you have crossed that it becomes very shallow. My children enjoyed jumping the waves and as we were holding them we felt that it was safe enough to do so.

title: Gritty sand
text: The water is lovely and warm, but there is a treacherous undertow which you have to be very careful of. Not suitable for young children, or frail elderly folk. The sand is very gritty and unpleasant to walk on. The beach slopes quite steeply. Conclusion: nice to look at and listen to, but we stayed near the pool!

title: Not a very safe beach
text: We stayed in the North of Kalutara first, the beach was a very long but uncomfortable beach to walk along. The sand is coarse, sharp sand, like builders sand with patches of black sand along the beach. The beach shelved down to the rough sea and unless you are a very confident swimmer I wouldn’t attempt to swim in it! We then stayed in South Kalutara, again the beach was the same sand as was the conditions for swimming in but it was shorter and prettier and hardly any black sand.

title: Litter
text: A warm sea but rough with a very strong current. Paddle up to your knees but I wouldn’t recommend swimming. Waves come in big & are often unexpected. The patch outside our hotel (the royal palms beach hotel) was clean in the areas you could see, but a short walk past view at either end reveals litter strewn everywhere. We avoided the beach for this reason. On a plus, the sand is soft & easy to walk on.

title: Stunning windswept sea
text: Beautiful and wild beach with some enjoyable beer spots for some Lion lager. I wasn't brave enough to go in the sea!

title: Nice Walk ! Avoid the midday heat - get in and Swim !
text: Nice Walk ! Avoid the midday heat - get in and Swim !, see all sorts of wildlife on the beach, pity about the stuff washed up though if you are going swimming there's a bit of a rip current you need to watch out for but the waves are fun to body surf

title: Great experience
text: I enjoyed the stay very much , the staff is so friendly and dedicated , especially ( Bimali & Sayuri) they made our stay the greatest and so comfortable. They are the best The rooms are great , big and super clean , the food is great ,sunset view is the bests

title: A bathtub in the ocean
text: Warm waters brilliant surfs and safe flat silted sands. These beaches are brilliant in the afternoons and remain warm till well past 7. A must visit in the south east areas

title: Golden sands, intense waves
text: Really beautiful, course golden sand mixed with some sparkly black soft sand too, really picturesque. Unfortunately here, the locals / tourists / council etc don’t make any effort to clean the beach up so it does have a lot of trash on the beach and in the ocean too. The waves are prett heavy, dumpy and forceful so not the easiest beach to swim at. All in all, not the best beach in Sri Lanka but certainly not the worst.

title: Dirty beach
text: Not suitable to swim in due to strong currents, the beach is very dirty with rubbish and the locals swarm you begging for money

title: Nice beach
text: The beach is as per the pictures. The sand can be a little rough and where we are there was a slope into the sea which might not be ideal for those with walking difficulties or with small children. We were also advised not to swim in the sea due to strong currents.

title: Nice sandy beach
text: Great beach, bit of a dip as you enter the sea with a few small pebbles, but a few yards in you will be on a carpet of sand,Red flag flying most of the time, this is because the current is very strong,big waves

title: Very Quiet
text: Stretches for miles so can walk along way, sand ok very black in places and unfortunately very untidy in places with plastic bottles and rubbish. Lots of fishing boats along the way and sometimes you can see the catch of the day been brought in. One or two beach bars dotted around in between hotels. Sea very warm and very rough waves most of the time but although red flags fly most of the time and many parts have no lifeguard on duty it doesn't stop people having fun with mother nature. Not many hawkers either but occasionally you will get a restaurant or bar owner walk miles with you to try and get you into their establishment, just a firm no thank you usually does the trick.

title: Superb
text: Beautiful clean beach, lovely warm sea; just be careful of the current though. Time it right and watch the fishermen landing their catch of the day. You can even help too!

title: Sand is great
text: The sand is very nice, extra fine, the beach is not very wide, and kind somehow “raw”, it’s great for walks!

title: Nice beach but Bentota is better
text: Great sunset views and clean water. But the current is a little strong and you need to be a good swimmer. There also isn’t much beach as it slopes off quiet sharply making it hard to walk on. We found Bentota was a better beach

title: Lovely sand, warm ocean!
text: Many people wander along the beach in either direction, along the surf at the edge of the incredibly warm ocean. Waves can be quite fierce and you must take care of younger children or weak swimmers. In places the beach slopes a fair bit to get into the sea, but , once in, the bottom is flat and hard packed sand, which is lovely to walk on. Tiny crabs dash along the sea fringes, darting int holes in the sand. There are a myriad of tiny sea shells along the waters edge. The sea is very warm and lovely to swim in with care.

title: It is a truly amazing beach.
text: This beach is perfect for swimming and walking. It is simply beautiful and unspoiled by people. Very romantic too.

title: Rough waves!
text: We went in late October, the waves were rough and red flags everywhere as it was not safe to go in the water. We were told best time to go is between December and March.

title: Beautiful Sunsets - but Rough Sea
text: We went to Coco Royal Beach end of September, beginning of October this year. The Beach was really rough! Red flags out every day and wasn't really wise to get in. Also we found the Beach was full of rubbish which was disappointing, big piles or rubbish right outside our hotel gates as well. We spoke to the hotel manager and he sorted out a clear up team from the hotel to tidy up the mess outside our gates. We were told by the Pool Attendant that if we came a few weeks later, the Sea would be like a millpond and you could walk out for miles. There were some beautiful sunsets on the beach which was lovely. Do also expect to be bombarded by locals that hassle you and get aggressive! On the first day we went onto the beach and was straight away hassled by people trying to sell us gifts and trips. I told one person that I didn't want anything (politely) and that I wasn't sure what the plan was in terms of trips as we had literally just got there! He then called me a liar and shouted at me saying he hates liars and that I'm not a very nice person. This then made it uncomfortable for me and my family any time we wanted to go on the beach as he would be there following us around hassling us. I imagine this is a lovely beach during the Summer season but I do feel the locals and rubbish piles will always be an issue.

title: A clean beach could be better
text: While in Sri Lanka a visit to beach is unavoidable. This could be one favorite spot. The clean air is distinctly felt.

title: Sri Lankan Beaches !
text: We stayed at Tangerine Hotel Kalutara ,The hotel has a big garden, where you can enjoy time with your family at any time of the day. The beach is just outside the hotel and although, sea is very rough these days and not recommended for a swimming, and it is not the best beach in Srilanka so we booked an excursion with Asya tours to Galle which is located on the south cost . which has some of the best beaches in Sri lanka and has some of the best places for swimming.

title: Sue. Nottingham
text: If you are staying in Kalutara, Sri Lanka, I actually stayed in the Royal Palms Beach Hotel, if you want to do any tours I highly recommend BONI who took my mother and I on some amazing tours. He is very genuine, reliable, fully insured, trustworthy and above all cheaper than any of the tours your rep will try and sell you. He comes to the beach outside of the Royal Palms hotel or his office is 50metres to the right of the hotel. Look for the name RUSALKA which is his office. He is allowed to come in to the hotel although the hotel cannot recommend him. You will not be disappointed if you trust Boni to arrange your tours for you. There is a guy called Lucky who also works on the same beach. I would not trust or recommend this person.

title: Marvellous beach
text: As may be expected a town built along the Indian Ocean would have a lot of access to the beach. My experience of it was from Avani Resort which has full access to the beach on one side. Unlike the Mediterranean and the Carribean seas the Indian Ocean is active and pretty rough, and to be exposed to its raw power and majesty is an awe-inspiring experience!

title: Long Hall Holiday
text: The beaches near Kalutara are beautiful. Smooth sand and tropical palm trees. In September they were surprisingly quiet. I had a tropical beach to myself several times. However the local salesmen can be a nuisance. PLEASE NOTE THE WAVES ARE ALWAYS VERY STRONG AND SO ITS DANGEROUS TO SWIM IN THE SEA ANYWHERE ALONG THIS COAST

title: Please be safe
text: You can see sunset here on a good day. The beach is choppy and has no lifeguard, not really fit for swimming.

title: Lovely sandy beach spoiled by litter
text: Beautiful golden sandy beach which would be even better if there wasn't so much litter. The sea is very rough here so not suitable for swimming but that makes the huge, crashing waves more dramatic. A great spot to watch sunset.

title: A lovely beach
text: Terrific spot for sunsets. Unsafe to swim in the month we visited; October, but a lovely location to take a walk and enjoy the power of the sea. Nice sand, such a shame about the litter.

title: Pretty

Lots of debris was washed up daily on the beach so not the pristine beach as shown in some pictures.

title: Terrible beach

title: Beach & Sea

title: Red flags for the duration

title: Lovely sandy beach.

title: one the best beaches I've been to

title: Amazing tours, knowledge and service
text: We have just returned from 2 wonderful weeks in Sri Lanka, we looked at at the tour rep trips and found we could save over £100 by booking a 2 day tour and a single day trip we Suresh. Not only did he offer a very good service we also met his uncle, auntie and cousin when we went to there home to book the trips, the hospitality was wonderful and a sign of what we where to come across when ever we met the local Sri Lankan people. Suresh comes across as a very friendly tour guide but surpassed even his own high standards when he took my wife and I to his home for Sunday lunch, cooked by his wife (with help from Suresh), this was the best meal in Sri Lanka, and that is very high praise indeed, the quality of the hospitality and food was only surpassed by meeting his wonderful 3 young children. All in all I would recommend everyone to book tours with Suresh, he can be spotted easily by his Bright Red Mohecan hair style, Thank you again Suresh Chris and Diane, Hull, England

title: Affordable tours from Kalutara
text: I highly recommend Raja as a tour guide! He is a very kind person and good enough as a tour guide, speaks English and Russian, sells all the tours for the reasonable prices! title: Long Walks Along A Wide Sandy Beach
text: Even though several hotels front onto the wide sandy beach, it never seems crowded. The beach is ideal for long contemplative walks or to enjoy an early morning sunrise. However, one must also be prepared for the occasional vendor urging you to take a boat tour or the nearby turtle hatchery or a variety of other services. A firm "no thanks" sends them away searching for their next potential customer.

title: rich sands and lovely blue sea.

title: Secluded Beach

title: Kalutara Beach

title: Kalutara, Sri Lanka

title: Nothing special
text: The beach was disappointing - at a slope and with quite a lot of rubbish. the sea was very rough and not suitable for swimming, but we were advised this was due to the time of year.

title: Beautiful but beware of locals.

title: Not at all good to visit if you want a beach holiday!
text: Kalutara Beach is not what we expected. The sea is always far too rough to swim in and always has a red flag flying. There are no beach loungers or beach bars or anything to make this a friendly holiday beach to visit. Holiday's in this area are strictly reduced to pool side bathing only.

title: Sandy beech with selection of good beech restaurants, beech sellers and tour guides.
text: We have previously travelled to India and West Indies. We were expecting to be hassled by beech sellers but they were really friendly and not pushy. Bought some trousers and shirt from Domeca. Went to local beech restaurants including Rusalka. Local people trying to make a living with good value restaurants and produce whilst the hotels try and capture all tourists through All Inclusive packages. Take a chance go with the locals..it's well worth it. Also local tours are much better value and more authentic than tours the holiday reps offer. We had 2 day trips and an overnight trip for the cost of a day trip with holiday rep. We went with Rinar from Rusalka Restaurant with a/c mitsibushi van well driven by Sam. Seemed more authentic having a tour guided by local man, ex-fisherman who talks about the tsunami because he was there, and his business suffered for the subsequent 4 years. These trips really helped make the holiday.

title: endless
text: Endless sand and a wonderful place,but no swimming in the sea its to rough in september so if your looking to swim in the sea this is not the place to be!

title: Coconut hotel and resturant
text: While staying at the Avani resort just walked along fot 400m and came and had a bite to eat.This was good and the friendly owner invited us to have a look at the rooms in this new small hotel.The rooms were 5* rooms at backpackers prices- I hope people will go and enjoy its on the beach location. Patricia and Martyn

title: Nice beach
text: Nice wide beach made up with shells so can be sharp in areas unfortunately when we arrived the sea was rough with strong undercurrents so you could only paddle in the sea and not swim but I was assured from December through to April it is calm and you can swim in it

title: Terrible

title: Long walks on the beach
text: I love the length of the beach for long walks and meeting the locals. Many of tracks so that you can walk into a bar/restaurant for a cool beer/coke and a meal.

title: Wonderful beach ever!
text: Kaluthara is a Coastal area which is about 40 minutes away from Colombo city and a famous touristic beach. You can find good hotels, resorts and restaurants. Kaluthara Bodiya is another attraction in Kaluthara. Its a good beach for relax!

title: Not great.
text: We knew that we wouldn't be able to swim due to the time of year (huge waves) but were not expecting quite so much rubbish. We had a few walks but had to keep our eyes out for broken glass. On one occasion a small child ran up to me and dug his nails into my stomach really hard leaving welts and bruising. I think this was because I had not stopped to give anything to the woman he was with. This was the only bad experience I had. Mostly the sellers on the beach, although persistent are not a problem. We arranged a day trip with Lucky, one of the beach sellers outside our hotel. He took us on a river trip, then a tour of the turtle sanctuary followed by a trip to a lagoon where we could swim. He was very good and we travelled in air-conditioned comfort in a minibus. I would recommend using Lucky and understand he organises longer trips as well to Kandy and Sigiriya.

title: It's getting dirtier

title: Mediocre

title: Terrible Beach in August

title: Delightful

title: Lovely beach
text: Lovely beach, as the monsoon season was just finishing we were unable to swim in it as waves & undercurrent were to strong, however to go in up to knees & walk along was fab.

title: very strong undercurrent
text: Clean beach, no crowd, strong undercurrent so not suitable to swim. Not safe for Children to play on shore

title: Beautiful beach
text: Beautiful beach but unsuitable for swimming in certain seasons. Very strong currents, we watched some locals going in to pick up driftwood but they ensured they were tied by a rope in case they needed to be pulled back in. Area outside The Royal Palms hotel was kept immaculate, the sea brings in a lot of debris which other businesses don't clean as often.

title: Great beach but strong currents
text: Visited in July and each day sea was rough with red flags and strong winds. Lovely to sit and watch the ocean and sunsets but not swimming. At least when we were there.Pretty clean with coarse sand.

title: Not the best
text: I went in June and the sea is very rough. Red flags out all the time I was there so no swimming allowed. The beach outside my hotel, The Tangerine Beach was clean but quite narrow and steep. Don't come here if you want a beach holiday. There are beach vendors who wait at the hotel gates who constantly pester you to buy things. Because of the beach I wouldn't return to Kalutara.

title: Nice clean beach
text: Yes it's winter here and yes the waves are crashing and the red flag is out for our safety. The beach is clean and stunning we walked from the town along a beach road back to our hotel and it was a lovely relaxing walk. I can just imagine how fantastic it is to be here during Sri Lanka summer (wow).

title: Big waves
text: It's winter here so it was maybe a bit expected.. Waves are big so there is no chance of swimming.. A bit dirty but other idea nice to take a walk on the beach

title: It has it's times
text: Rated amongst best beaches this beach is good seasonally, best times I would say is during end November till about March (sometimes in between rough). Other that these periods the sea is calm during August perhaps, stretched from Katukurunda to Waskaduwa there not many places with wide beaches however some patches like Kalido area where the beach is wide during certain months like said before, close to most hotels the beach is clean and some parts not so much, few places rocky and few deep due to estuary of the Kalu Ganga (river).. Rohan Jayamanna..

title: Common beach
text: Beach is nice, quite clean, but a lot of aboriginals try to sell trips, dresses, they are a little bit annoying, but sure not dangerous and always nice, polite and pleasant. Waves was 1-2 meters high and quite strong, so we swam only once.

title: A really nice beach
text: The beach is lovely but in June cannot swim in the sea as too rough but still found walking along the beach relaxing

title: It's the ocean, anyway )
text: We were here at low season and it wasn't really comfortable to stay at the beach. Despite being friendly, local people were very annoying offering their services and goods. We tried some food at beach cafes but preferred to eat at the hotel.

title: beautiful
text: Want to be on the beach just alone? Kalutara beach is perfect for this...we met hardly anyone on the beach despite its next to the hotel. Clean and water really hot. Be aware of waves...it's not calm but it's fun...

title: Indian ocean
text: Long sandy beaches, very clean, calm sensation. Sea is warm but beware as very sadden big waves come unexpectedly. Do not swim if no lifeguards around. Especially during monsoon season, even locals don't swim in sea. Can go fishing in lakes . Lots of rivers to explore by boat, be warned lots of crocodiles around. Kalutara has one of the best beaches.

title: Take care
text: The beach was lovely mostly clean but take great care the sea is very rough and although looks tempting it's not good to swim in

title: Beach depends on the hotel you stay
text: I have noticed that the beach here varies greatly depending on where you are accessing it from. If you stay at a 5* hotel, then they will probably be cleaning their part thoroughly and you will be able to enjoy it. However, some low star hotels neglect their beaches and it ends up filled with black patches and very dirty.

title: good beach
text: we enjoy our stay there just passing days in beach and pool of hotel. we love this place and will back next time for sure.

title: A walk on the beach was risky
text: Quite a dirty and littered beach, found plastic bottles, plastic string and general litter all along this beach plus actually saw used needles which could be quite dangerous if bare footed. It was definitely not a pleasure to walk along considering you think of golden sandy beaches with palm trees (which were non-existent) on this beach.

title: Very nice
text: Pick a hotel with beach front and then you'll be able to experience more privacy and obviously a more cleaner beach that is well maintained by the hotel.

title: Too Rough to Swim
text: The beach slopes steeply and it is difficult to walk along the shore. The waves were always too rough to swim in and the red flag was in place for the whole 2 weeks of our trip. The locals advise that it is rare that the sea is suitable for swimming in. Also,the tide brings in lots of plastic, which is distributed along the beach and looks very messy. It would be good if this could be collected and disposed of, perhaps by the Avani hotel that is positioned on this beach as they are also building a sister hotel next door so will have the entire shoreline by their properties and therefore it would be in their interest to improve the aesthetics of the beach.

title: Beautiful Beach but beware of strong currents
text: Stayed for two weeks at the Turyaa Kalutara Hotel and spent many days on this beach and in the crystal clear warm water. If you are wanting to swim, this was only possible earlier morning as the current was simply too strong at any other time. Stunning beach, stunning scenery well worth a visit!!

title: Indian summer
text: Back in the Boxing Day when the tsunami struck this was a wild and deadly stretch of sand. These days it's a pristine place to dip your toes, rather than torso, in the Indian Ocean. However, on most days there are too many red flags to safely go swimming.

title: Nice beach but neglected one...
text: First it is natural and still not crowded. The ocean looks great with its restlessness and sound of waves. Yes you would get your own time to spend out there. However the waste collect of plastic bottles and tourist left over are an eye soar and spoils its ratings. The hospitality groups who own these type of space should be made accountable, responsible and answerable for the upkeep of the entire stretch. Srilanka otherwise so gentle and clean the beaches should be the showcase unfortunately it is not. I also request the guest of each such facilities to insist with he management to ensure proper cleanliness.

title: High tide and strong current
text: Enjoyed walking along the beach which had a high slope and a strong current... There are other better beaches in the area.

title: Excellent Beach
text: Extremely clean and safe beach with silver sands and beautiful views. One can walk for hours on the beach...fantastic experience for the ocean lovers

title: Lovely beach
text: not suitable for swimming but water is warm nice to walk in Not many people around just used by two hotels and a few locals

title: A clean beach without crews
text: Kalutara beach is clean and there are no crews like in Negambo beach . We watch a dead wale on the shore that was a different kind of a experience . nice to spend time with kids . However, as there were red flags we didn't go near the seashore

title: Beach
text: The beach outside the hotel is lovely,go 100 yds either side and full of litter,shame. The water is not safe , far too rough but is very picturesque .You will get the hawkers trying to sell but a firm polite no is respected.

title: Sri Lanka take 3
text: A nice walk along the beach from our hotel. Not as much activity as other beaches but still a good way to get some exercise and take some good photos especially at sunset

title: Best places to hang around in South Sri Lanka
text: This is one of the best beach areas, one very close to Bentota Hikkaduwa and Galle Would prefer families and couples to spend their precious time in this place, relax, love the life and enjoy

title: Too Rough to swim in June
text: Its a nice beach but not safe to go in the sea in June. There are quite a few guys hanging around the hotel fence that bother people as soon as they come out onto the beach. They are trying to sell their services, day trips, taxi rides etc. Can't really knock people for trying to make a living.

title: Too much rubbish
text: The sea was unfortunately too rough to swim in..great to watch though and the sound of crashing waves soothing

title: Dirty and unattractive
text: Only visited briefly but unimpressed dirty and unattractive, dirty water, dirty beach covered in litter

title: Far too dangerous
text: Came here as staying at nearby hotel. Fantastic beach spoilt by loads of rubbish ( which is a massive problem in Sri Lanka ) Its a long beach frequented by locals,not many tourists as lots of persistent beggars and hawkers. Cannot swim under any circumstances as far too rough with massive undercurrents and large waves. No life guards seen at all. Spectacular Indian Ocean spoilt by vast amounts of rubbish,swept in by the sea,but mainly by locals,such a shame.

title: Lovely Beach
text: Lovely sandy beach. Was a bit rough at time of visit, but miles of lovely sand and warm water. Did have a few people pestering you on beach to try restaurants, massage, Tuk Tuks, tours etc., but not to many and not too persistent. Most locals on beach were very pleasant

title: Not suitable for swimming
text: This beach was in front of our hotel and i was really disappointed that we couldn't swim in the sea - there's a steep incline to the sea edge from the beach, the waves were really strong and could drag somebody out to sea easily. Nice to walk along though.

title: Not worth a visit
text: Mediocre beach at best. Not sure whether whoever named this beach knows the actual colour of marble. The shops and general infrastructure at the beach are way past their glory days. Also this beach seems to be a side hustle of the local military. Dunno how I feel about that tbo. There are certainly nicer and more secluded beaches nearby that you should consider instead.

title: Beautiful beach
text: One of the most beautiful and swimmable beaches on the east coast. It's a very good place for a day trip from where ever you are staying in Tricomalee.

title: Stunning Bay for Swimming
text: The bays in Trincomalee are some of the nicest calm swimming experience one will ever have. Marble Bay has some Cabanas that you can rent. It is maintained by the military, so getting a room is not through your usual tourist avenues. The rooms are very basic, but comfortable. But the beach makes it worth the effort. We went there during the season which is April through August. We did not travel Sept 2019 but July 2018.

title: Nice beach
text: Nice beach with perfect white sand. Toilets and showers. Local people go there on Sundays. everywhere though are nice beaches and all beaches are public.

title: clean beach but probably not the best
text: very uncrowded, marble effect because of sun and water and sand reflection. there is a small store and ice cream corner. not very safe to swim in and the southern beaches are far better

title: Still think no Global warming then take a dip
text: Marble beach is for the Air Force to dip into, the locals have just a small portion partitioned with a rope.

title: Great
text: We visited on 20/12/2019 and we enjoyed but sea was very ruff due to bad whether. However me and my family enjoy with rain at the beach.

title: Good
text: This a beach just close to the Trincomalee town. There is a entrance fee. There is a public area and a private area for the Airforce.

title: WOAH
text: Marble beach is the safest beach which I ever ever seen before and and the cleanest beach .Filled with Unlimited activity's.Our family really enjoyed ourself . Marble beach has an exclusive navy runned restaurant with very good food even though we had to wait a bit of time but the food was magnificent .

title: Marble Beach Trincomalee
text: We were staying just north of Trinco and had heard that this a=was a nice beach to visit. We took a Tuk tuk for 1000 rupees. It was about a 30 mins journey. There is a naval checkpoint as you enter the beach area. We said that we were having lunch at the hotel and were waived through with no entrance fee. We had a very good Sri Lankan lunch in the small beach bar at the hotel and then had the beach to ourselves. It is a very quite spot (we were there on a weekday). At the other end of the beach which is public it was much busier. The water was very clear and we snorkelled by the rocks which was good but not exceptional.All in all a very good beach and a nice day out. We ordered a tuk tuk at the reception for our return journey=y which came quickly and was the same price.

title: Beautiful Pristine Beach managed by the Sri Lanka Air Force
text: Quiet and pristine beach - not too busy. Good for sunbathing, lazing around and snorkeling. Had lunch at the SL Air Force restaurant. Food was delicious. Went snorkeling with Bandara. He was very understanding and patient with me as I did not know how even float. I came out having seen a world that I never thought I would ever see. Amazing and beautiful!!

title: Amazing pristine beach!
text: Checked out Marble Beach while staying at Uppuveli. Well worth the journey! It's tucked in a small bay, the water is calm and gentle and the water is crystal clear. Locals also come to enjoy the beach as well as tourists so it's a nice mix. There are a couple of small hotels with their section but the public section is just as nice. Definitely recommend making a trip to enjoy a full day or afternoon!

title: Small beach, too crowded.
text: Expected way too much..the water is clear, but it's nothing special. La scala is nearby and the atmosphere there is way better.

title: Beautiful tropical beach
text: Had a great stroll along the beach plenty of really good bars and restaurants especially Tonics bar great owners very friendly and helpful

title: Hidden Gem.
text: Marble beach is one of the most beautiful beaches in the East coast of Trincomalee Sri Lank. The ocean is calm and beautiful. Actually water is very transparent and looks like Marbel!!.

title: Quiet to chill with Ã hamack
text: Beach divided in parts... One Resort for tourist and one for locals.. RÃ©ally sad especially because Resort is appripriating themself the beach that they don t even own...

title: Excellent
text: Very safe beach to have sea a sea bath. We enjoyed there well. Very clean place is look after by Air Force Army

title: Lovely beach
text: Very busy when we were there. Very safe, lots of rock pools, good cafe. Good parking. Had to pay to get in.

title: Enjoy in peace
text: Good clean beach. Not crowded. Restaurant / resort run by Air force is good. Sea is not deep so can swim well

title: Great place to visit
text: Beautiful and clean beach and very hospitable staff. Had lunch at the naval restaurant and the food was delicious

title: An Impeccable Beach
text: Simply marvelous. A must see spot if you are in an around Trincomalee. Make sure you bring your swim wear.

title: Visit on the way
text: It was a terrible place. It was locals bathing place . Idont have much to say here. We just walked up to the beach saw the locals bathing.

title: Marble Beach (Trincomalee)
text: Trincomalee offers you with some amazing beaches like Uppuveli, Nilavel, Marble and Trinco beach. Most of the tourists are seen to spend their time in Uppuveli, Nilavel beaches. Food and Stay charges get high in these places. But you don't have any option, just to enjoy the calm and serene nature. I must say all the beaches of Trincomalee are beautiful and amazing. After travelling around the world, East coast of Srilanka provides you with some untouched under water coral reefs, Go for scuba and snorkeling would be a good option.

title: Cristal clear waters in an unspoilt setting
text: Definitely the best beach visited so far in Sri Lanka. Only few visitors, mostly locals. Good for spending the day, since food and drinks (non alcoholic) are available. Easily reachable from Trincomalee also by tuctuc.

title: Not special
text: We had been recommended this beach but was crowded and not very clean or nice. Don’t see the great and lovely in it

title: Nice and peaceful beach
text: We paid 20 lkr / person just to have our own private beach.. no tourists were there that day, we went to the side where the hotel is, as there is also a part where is open to everyone. At the hotel side you normally have to pay for sun-beds, but they accept also if you order something from the bar. The beach was clean, the water was really warm and calm, you can do some snorkeling also.. there were some nice fishes there. It does worth a visit!

title: Nice & safe beach to relax
text: The water at this beach is super calm, almost no waves. Ideal with little children. You can also do some snorkling near the rocks on the left hand side of the beach. There is an ‘open to all public’ part of the beach and a ‘hotel only’ part. When you arrive, ask your driver or tuktuk to take you to the hotel only part and say you ll have lunch there so you don t have to pay the entrance fee. The lunch is basic but ok and not expensive at all. We had sandwiches. The beach has showers, toilets where you can change, a bar and umbrellas with sunbeds. It is usually very quiet. You can find very nice seashells and look for small fishes & crabs in the rocks or build a nice sand castle of course!

title: Lovely beach..almost like a pool
text: We paid a visit to this place and unfortunately were not prepared for change of clothes. very calm waters, almost like a pool. Crystal clear waters. However no place to change clothes, no good toilets. The place is controlled by Airforce and charges an entry fee. Facilities have to be improved here.

title: Hideaway
text: Far from town. Excellent beach. Just a short visit. Run by the Airforce. Looks good. Website shows various sleeping options including family facilities. Pretty outlook across the bay.

title: Well Maintained Beach
text: Marble Beach also known as Air Force Resort as it is being maintained by air force authorities. The place is quiet and peaceful with few resorts around. Water is shallow and clear.

title: Decent beach but almost nil food options
text: Decent beach. Not many food options. A small canteen with very limited options. We went there expecting shacks a la Goa...si were left a bit disappointed.

title: Easy swim, no large waves
text: Well...there was alot of reviews about this place .akes it sound like heaven on earth. Its a good 30min drive downthere..and there is no tuktuk station there u better arrange a return pick up. Expect to pay a 1000rupies. The beach itself is small and clean, basically its a beach in a gulf. Its seoarated in tow parts ..non resort one (public) resort one (free access) tourist and upper class locals. The beach is sandy so its feet friendly not too deep and the most important thing is that there is no mega ocean wave :) Consider going.

title: quiet beach but facing some large ships in the bay...
text: a bit far from trinco, quiet shallow beach, even quieter resort with restaurant, possibility to rent snorkling equipment but nothing much to see under the surface, also visited by locals

title: Very nice clean beach, mostly the locals go there, facilities of changing rooms etc
text: Nice clean beach very picturesque... mostly locals go there - we saw no women! There are changing room and toilet facilities available

title: Beautiful beach
text: Our trip to marble beach was excellent. It was breathtaking and very well maintained. Special thanks to the air force for doing a wonderful job with maintenance. They even had a small cafeteria by the beach.

title: Very nice beach
text: I recently visited Marble Beach. It is a small beach and very pleasant and popular with the locals. You have to pay a car park fee and a fee to use the beach, but it does not cost a lot. It is a good drive into the beach down a bumpy road. Not sure it was worth the time

title: Beautiful!
text: Nice...had the whole place to ourselves! The water and view were lovely and it was about 22km to reach from Dyke Rest Hostel (600LKR)

title: Good Beach
text: Beach simpatica where we found very natives. Being inside a military zone, it is necessary to pay a symbolic value to the entrance.

title: Nice local beach
text: This seems to be a beach mostly used by locals and not tourists. Went here on an public holiday/festival day and it was packed. Probably about 500 people but we had a really good time. It's a very large ropes diff section that you can swim in. There's lifeguards. Try to swim under the rope and out further and they whistle at you and call you back ?? there's a separate section (completely empty) for naval officers to swim in and further along there's another section for the naval resort guests to swim. You pay an entrance fee of 80 rupees (2 persons plus the tuk tuk) at the naval checkpoint entrance. We were the only westerners here but everyone was so friendly/ wanted to talk and practice their English. Defiantly worth a visit.

title: Early birds ...... enjoy the most
text: After failing to access the Marble Beach from the Sri Lanka Air Force resort due to exorbitant pricing for a breakfast meal, thought of accessing the public area for a morning swim and fun. Decided to be the first to enter the public beach to get the best location for a swim. Our group consisting 6 children and 13 adults, entered the public area of the Marble Beach at 8.00 am. We were able to access the beach that was closest to the SL Air Force resort. For about an hour, there were only a few people swimming and thereafter Marble Beach started getting flooded with people. We left around 11.00 am. The three hours we spent at Marble Beach was the best part of our tour to the Norther province of Sri Lanka. Great place to skinny dip; swim or float or sea bathing as far as you don't venture beyond the line where the sand bank disappears.

title: Just gorgeous
text: This is a lovely safe beach that is particularly suitable for children. The sand is fine enough to build sand castles. Just gorgeous!

title: Very disappointing
text: Type in Google the places to visit while in Trincomalee and Marble beach comes up....don't bother. The beach area is run by the Air Force, in itself not a problem but what they have done now is the Marble beach area is now closed off and you can not park there. They let you drive through it to see what you are missing to another beach section split into sections for the visitors and the commercial fisheries. While it is still an "ok "beach there are so many better ones around that you don't have to PAY to visit.

title: First and last visit
text: I want to start with the positives, the was nice relative to the surrounding area. We wanted to visit Trinco as it had been previously been cut off because of the war. My father in law, being a Sri Lankan local, decided to bring us here. It cost 50rp for foreigners to enter and a smaller sum for locals. We visited on a week day as we thought it would be less crowded. That said, there were many people about enjoying the waters. The place just didn't have a nice feel for us. The toilet didn't seem clean and seeing it made me lose the urge to go. The beach had rubbish around despite there being clearly marked bins around for disposal. The water didn't look clean either and we decided against swimming. The bar served snacks and drinks for a reasonable price. The views from the car between the entry gate and the beach, unfortunately provided nicer views than the actual destination.

title: A excellent beach controlled by the army
text: It is one of the safest beaches in Trinco to bathe, reaching this place is a bit of a hazard as the roads are too narrow and the crowds are big during weekends and holidays. The armed forces maintain this beach and have kept them really clean. The place offers good shade and clean water too.

title: Beautiful Beach
text: Beautiful sandy beach, warm calm sea water. Excellent facilities and I can fully recommend the devilled Prawns

title: Not so good
text: It is may be good for local public, but I have seen it is not like remarkable level. We hardly spend 5 minutes . So many people are taking bath. There was great rush for bathroom and wash room. There is entry tickets also there 50 rs Not recommended for foreign tourists

title: Scenic but small beach
text: It is a scenic beach but a small one. Frequently visited by the locals. Looks neat and clean. Not much of activity.

title: Nice shallow beach
text: This place is really scenic and there are absolutely no tides and it is a really safe beach and the water is crystal clear . The pebbles look like Marbles. This beach is maintained by Srilankan Navy/ Army and there is a small entry fee. It is worth the visit for the scenic route to reach the beach. I just loved the route and the beach

title: One of the beautiful beach in sri lanka
text: i went with my family . we spent there one day . beach is very clean and beautiful . actually that credit should be go to the Sri lanka navy . sri lanka navy maintained this beach very well. and we took our lunch at sri lanka navy restaurant that food was very Delicious and service also very good

title: Calm beach
text: The title is so different to hear rite... Yes it's very calm beach... No waves... No noise.... Only place were filled with chill water with lots of fun.... My husband and myself spent almost 3 hours there.... It's was a beautiful experience for us .... Security was so alert... And the facilities were awesome....

title: Overrated !! Nothing much.
text: We went there with some of my cousins in January 2017, for me there is nothing much to see or do. Maintained by Sri Lankan Navy so it's very clean. There is a small entrance fee. I don't think it is necessary for anyone to go there unless you have nothing else to do.

title: An interesting visit
text: We did not visit with a view to enjoying the beach but to view the scenery and birds. The beach is a great facility and very popular with the locals. I believe it is run by the Sri Lankan Navy, along with the nearby golf course. Interesting but not a must see - unless you want to lie on the beach.

title: Nice private beach
text: Very quiet and nice beach with fancy hotel in front. We went there with our local friends though and just had a beer. Staff was very professional and friendly.

title: Overrated - don't waste your time!
text: Trinco beach is the best beach in Trincomalee - it's in the main town & free - the sand is fine & white & the water is crystal blue. In contrast, Marble Beach is half an hour drive away from the main town, controlled by the army so you must pay an entrance fee & is highly overrated! We were told the reason why it's called Marble Beach so we were excited to see it but we were just left disappointed & confused once we got there & we spoke to other tourists that felt the same. Seriously do not waste your time like we did :(

title: What a location
text: This is one of the best beaches ever seen in Sri Lanka. This was handled by SL Air Force & they are doing a fabulous job. We stayed 2 nights & superb location with great food.

title: Awesome Clear Beach
text: This has got to be one of the cleanest and awesome beaches in Sri Lanka. Colours of the water is incredible and the beach is shallow so safe for kids. Its a definite must but be prepared for lot of crowd at the beach. Toilets at the beach are not clean. Water is prestine

title: Rain Spoilt The Fun!!
text: It was a rainy day, and we had to visit this place because of it's fame. The beach was clean and water was calm. The sand was very soft, it will be a great outdoor activity on a nice sunny day.

title: Good for walking
text: Stayed at Trimco Blu hotel and walked the beach each morning It's good for walking or running and is mainly quite clean until you get away from hotel developments whereupon the beach needs cleaned of the usual litter washed up onto the shore Great to see fishermen working and preparing their nets

title: Nice beach
text: Good spot to enjoy the day very calm beach Rs.20 to get in maintain by sl army would recommend to anyone in trinco to go enjoy the place.

title: A one day trip
text: An enchanting beach with beautiful white sand and blue skies! A must visit beach in Sri Lanka! It was a great experience being there. Would visit again!

title: Just an average beach
text: Marble beach is on the east coast of Sri Lanka, south of Trincomalee. It's within Koddiyar Bay. The beach is reached by turning off the A15 and heading east a few kilometres on a narrow paved road until you arrive at a barrier manned by the navy. A fee has to be paid to proceed further. From this point one has to travel down a gravel road for another kilometre or so. This road is very uneven and the journey was terribly uncomfortable. Anyway, when you get to the beach, there's nothing much to say about it. The beach appeared clean enough, but it doesn't have decent toilets or huts for getting changed etc. The ladies' toilet was closed and the urinals in the men's were blocked and overflowing. We went there on a weekday. It wasn't crowded and 100% of the people there were locals.

title: A clean beach
text: We spent a lovely day at Marble Beach. The beach was clean and we pretty much had the place to ourselves. There is a resort/small hotel there and a restaurant attached. The food was fine but nothing special. The water was clear and clean but beware of sea lice. Very nippy!! There were a few umbrellas on the beach and some chairs but not a lot. Perhaps they put more out when there is a crowd? A nice place to spend a few hours in the sun

title: Amazing clear water and view
text: Very good place for swimming and walking, the water was very clear, calm and not so deep or scary for not good swimmers. I had a great time that morning on the beach

title: Some Marbels are there,Nice view
text: In order to get to the beach you need to go inside a Navy camp.Tickets available at the gate.Nice view,But nothing special though.Found some rocks near the sea shore which were actually marbels (May be the reason for the name).Very crowded,better go during weekdays.

title: Nothing "Marble" about the beach
text: This is just another beach which is overcrowded and not at all relaxing. The irony is that one has to pay an entrance fee to enter unlike the the other beaches found all over Sri Lanka which are FREE. There is a totally run down beach restaurant on this supposedly "Marble" beach which has hardly anything on offer not even the basic Sri Lankan rice and curry!!!. However there is a restaurant run by the AirForce which has to be accessed separately, and is good. The facilities on the beach are not good with filthy toilets as usual in Sri Lanka!! However the Air Force surf guard is present with designated swim areas demarcated with flags. With many other FREE beaches with golden sands on offer in the Nilaveli region and the rest of Sri Lanka this so called "Marble" beach which is totally out of the way, is not worth a visit at all.

title: The Best Beach in Trinco
text: Forget Nilaveli Beach, this is the best beach in Eastern Sri Lanka. It's on a Military base, so you are not allowed to walk in. You have to come by car, and pay an entrance fee about 20LKR per person and about 100LKR for the tuk tuk, or car. It's out of town, so we hired a tuk tuk for a short day (8am to 3pm) for about 1500LKR. Were there in August 2014.

title: Great beach
text: Visited this place .also gone for whel and Dolphin watching.It was deep in Indian Ocean about19 to 20 km deep from this place.speed boat was very good enjoyed the trip.

title: not so good on a rainy day
text: this might have been a great place had we not visited during monsoon. Rain and beaches don't make for a good combination. The snacks (tea and coffee) offered at the beach didn't look very good. We skipped those. Got back in the car...and left.

title: Good place. Just too far away.
text: Yeah it was ok. It's just too far out of town to be honest. They do have rest rooms and a bar that sells food and drinks which is a plus. Also take your snorkel and go to the right side of the public area near the rocks. It's not a bigarea but you'll awesome great sea life. But do yourself a favour. Go to Dutch bay. That is by far the best beach in Trinco. And you can walk from the main st.

title: Run by Sri Lankan Air Force
text: The beach was not crowded when we visited but it can become so. The beach has beach front accommodation, an excellent restaurant and a separate bar . Unlike the beach at Trincomalee this is really a bay with bush down to the waters edge and is reasonably sheltered with good swimming and snorkeling.

title: Fantastic quiet, clean and beautiful beach
text: I definitely don't agree with all the negative reviews about this beach on TA. Yes, it's not Thailans but I do think it's one of the best pieces of beach in Sri Lanka to spent a nice day. Most off all it is clean, quiet, peaceful, the water was very clear when we visited you could see the fish through the water swimming next to your feet (bring snorkel gear if you can, although you can rent it at the air force resort around Rs500 per hour I think). We stayed at the piece of beach that is handled by the airforce. If you have lunch in their restaurant you can use the sunbeds for free. Food was a little more expensive but still OK. All the staff were really friendly, we had a wonderful relaxing day. To get to the beach (even if you go to the public part) you pay an entrance fee, Rs20 per person and we paid Rs20 for the motorbike as well. I would say definitely worth a day trip from Trinco or Uppuveli.

title: Excellent beach - Managed by Sri Lanka Air force
text: Beach is divided in to two parts. One for locals and 1 for foreigners. Managed by SLAF clean. A must visit if you travel to Trinco.

title: White and clean
text: When compared with Arugambay, Unawatuna, and Pasikudah, the beach is very clean and maintained very well by the Air Force. Beach with White sand. Relatively small.

title: Water like Marble
text: I visited the beach with my friend and the beach is beautiful.The beach is little away from Trincomalee and the water is clear like marble.The beach is fully packed with families taking bath.The waves are normal.They are collecting some entrance fee for entering the beach.The area is kept clean.A nice beach in Trincomalee.

title: Not the best
text: I was very disappointed after reviews for this beach...great for local prices but not the best beach, go to dutch bay

title: Our favourite beach in Trincomalee!
text: It might be a bit far out of the city but marble beach is definitely worth a visit. It is far less polluted, with less rubbish, than any of the other beaches we visited in Trincomalee. The water is clear and there are plenty of shady spots under trees and under umbrellas near the water. There is a beach side bar where you can buy drinks and food. Entry was only 20 rupees per person. A return tuk tuk cost us 1400 rupees from the city however if you bargain you could probably get it cheaper. Please take your rubbish home with you and don't litter this beautiful Beach paradise.

title: Zen beach. But far from the center
text: This a private beach you have to pay to go. It is located far away from the inner city and you have to book your return TukTuk if you want to come back from there. Nice beach. Clean. Calm. Ideal for a family or If you looking for serenity.

title: Must see.
text: It is a nice beach, the see is beautiful with nice colour of the water. The road to go is very good until the last 5 km. wich is very dusty. Near to this beach it is another beach Porto Vathy which is a little bigger then Marble beach, with a great beach bar(good prices). It is two beches wich is must to see if you are in Thassos.

title: Good snorkeling location for beginers
text: Helpful staff and it was a good start for beginners snorkeling. Sea is very calm and not deep and there was plenty of reef fish to see.

title: Lovely beach, swim with the locals.
text: A very nice beach, my kids were the only foreigners out swimming and mixing in with the locals. Better beach at Uppuveli but this was good to visit.

title: Gorgeous beach
text: Really enjoyed spending time at the beach here. It wasn't too crowded and the water was lovely for swimming.

title: Nothing special.
text: Not so close to Trincomalee and not worth the trip to there. We did with a scooter on a sunday and there were a lot of locals.

title: Pretty and Deserted
text: Marble beach is a lovely stretch along the east coat of Sri Lanka. You can watch the local fishermen pull in their huge fishing nets in the morning and then relax on the few sun beds that are around. The sun beds are owned by the hotels (of which there maybe 20 sun beds in total) It’s a great place to swim - so much safer then in the south . If you’re looking for complete peace and quiet this is your place. I’m you’re looking for restaurants and bars on the beach this isn’t the place for you.

title: A Beautiful Beach....... Best in Trinco
text: For an insignificant entrance fee of 20 rupees per person you can spend the day on arguably the most beautiful beach in Trinco; and do some serious cargo ship spotting to boot! Regarding the private section of the beach, there were no signs up and we had no problem exploring the whole beach although we did partake of the wonderful massage/spa at 1000 rupees - per head per head and shoulders / 60 mins; which may have given us an oily leg up! The beach bar was also clean and efficient and open to us. Try the date smoothie and the mango smoothie; they were amazing. We also used somebody's (maybe belonging to the SL airforce's sun lounger's at no cost and no hassle. Things to think about: Make an early start to avoid the afternoon crowds around the car park end of the beach. A tuk-tuk costs 2000 rupees return from Trinco for 34 km but you are free to argue the toss about a few bob. Book your driver to return at your arranged time. If you're a fussy eater, or you've had enough of C+R, bring a picnic from Kumars Cream House in town (EYS for 500 rupees) Have a good day.

title: clean beach
text: sandy clean beach with large parking space. You have to pay for it and mostly the car is parked in full sun. In the old days you could make a nice, rather long walk alongside this beach. Nowadays a substantial part is taken by a hotel, so private property. The ocean was good for a swim and dive in the waves, not suitable for surfing: too small, and at the side part too many rocks. The rocks are a nice attraction for children to play around and discover shells and small fish/prawns. Good place for picknick, small bar was opened, washroom available but not clean.

title: Marble beach
text: We stayed at this beautiful hotel in January 2018 maybe off season,lovely place all staff are very friendly and helpful, The rooms were brilliant and well equipped, the food was excellent,the only complaint was there was no WiFi,this lost them a star. There probably won't be any as it's a security issue as this hotel is run very efficiently by the airforce.

title: Lovely beach managed by the army
text: This beach has entrance fees as it is managed by the army. Lots of security on the beach itself, restricted areas. You cannot simply walk freely on the beach. Having said that the water is shallow so it wan s perfect for the kids. Water was clean. Life guards were on shore making it one of the safer beaches.

title: Difficult to get to
text: This is an average Sri Lankan beach but very difficult to get to. Please be aware there is a charge to get to the beach. Could do with some decent restaurants.

title: Beautiful beach overlooking Indian Ocean
text: The waters were amazing and extremely clean/r. Above all the sands were incredibly soft and might just be the best I've been to

title: Lovely
text: First off, you have to pay to get into Marble Beach. But it's not a lot (2 people and a car lkr90) and its worth it for a slice of clean quiet paradise. There's a section of sea which is cordoned off so you feel very safe swimming there, and when we went there the beach was virtually deserted.

title: Worth the trip only if you have time
text: A bit out of the way, expensive to get there. But lovely on a hot day,take your own food and drinks.

title: Clean sand and crystal clear water
text: My family and I loved this beach where you can wade out even if you can't swim. The sand is like soft glitter and the water is so clean tropical fish can be seen almost right up to the shore! Loved it.

title: Nice to have sea bath
text: Waves are less on this beach enable to have nice sea bath. Place bit off from town.. I think..we need to go 14km from town,otherwise very nice place. Need to get a ticket /pass from security personals. Non salt water shavers available

title: Nice Beach
text: This beach is aprrox 20 mins drive from the town of Trincomalee .We called off here after visiting the hot springs.It is on a stretch of beach owned by the Air Force with a small entry charge .Part of the beach is not for public use.This beach is a long stretch of white sands with a calm clear sea.When we visited there was a lot of locals playing in the shallow sea really enjoying theirselves .There were seats and parasols on the beach and a small snack bar.

title: Marble Beach - a meautiful beach
text: I was traveling to Tincomalee from Batticaloa and when I crossed Kinniya my driver told me that justfive minutes on right side there I one of the beautiful beach of Sri Lanka. So we did the quick tour, indeed it was beautiful and deserve to be in to do list while in Sri Lanka. We had lunch at the beach resort and food was also delicious, I wish had some more time to enjoy the beautiful view.

title: Spoilt by segregation
text: This lovely beach is a trek if staying in Trinco / uppuveli and not worth the journey out there. 2 / 3 fenced off for VIPs and very busy on the other side with local families which doesn't make for a relaxing beach afternoon. It's a very sheltered bay so would be great for safe swimming with small children and the water is crystal clear. Try nilaveli instead.

title: locals beach
text: A nice spot but nilavelli beach is nicer, be prepared to be asked to be photographed with the locals, I find this very amusing but it can be off putting to some.

title: Clean Crowded Beach
text: We went to the Marble Beach at China Bay. The water was clean and clear. Very tempting to jump on and swim. The charges to enter not much. However it was very crowded. I think going on a Poya day is not a good idea as it is a holiday. I would recommend Marble Beach on weekdays, to be able to enjoy swimming etc

title: Great beach clearly a locals favourite
text: A beautiful but odd beach situated in the air force base and run by them. Our guide took us there it was full of locals bathing which you must do in a designated area including about 75 young schoolchildren in the sea in their school uniforms on a school trip. There are better beaches at Uppuveli etc but noe give you this slice of local life.

title: Lovely for swimming and water games! Not for sunbathing
text: The journey to Marble beach seemed like it was going to be a quiet remote place to hang out (you'll defnitely need a good local driver or taxi). When we arrived it was late morning about 11am and only some trainee child monks were in the water. They quickly got out when they saw our group of mostly young women. Two of my lady friends quickly realised that here you cover up unless you want to to be stared at or disrespect someone. At first we enjoyed the beach just to ourselves then suddenly after lunchtime, a throng of school children arrived crowding on the beach splashing their feet in the water. Soon after it seemed like the whole village followed, people splashing about and playing games mostly fully clothed. The monk children returned to the water to play ball games with us which was the best! A great way to experience beach culture but don't even try to sunbathe unless you want to offend.

title: Rather regimented and small
text: Not really impressed. It takes a 20 minute drive from Trico and you pay Rs 120 for people and car parking. It is run by the army but don't ask me why. We arrived 5 pm and there were many school children, including Muslim girls swimming in their full black regalia. The beach is in an inlet so is safe for swimming (there are areas marked with flags to make sure you did not stray). There are not that many good safe areas in Trico so you take it or leave it. It is only about 100m long with rocks either side so hardly expansive but good for supervised groups. PS Europeans have a bad reputation for <cough> unhealthy interest in children so males on their own should be careful of their 'looking' behaviour. I was getting stares when I wandered away from my company.

title: Clean beach
text: Very clean water with white sand. Food is very expensive and not suitable for kids. But Fine beach to enjoy.

title: Great little beach
text: Did not stay there,but went in for a look. Quite a popular beach,good for families. The resort looked ok,run by the army,so would have to stay there to know. Have stayed at Thalsevena Resort near Jaffna which is run by the army and it is very nice,

title: If you want a clean and tidy beach...this is the one
text: I had a wonderful 2 days at this place. very clean and tidy beach managed by Sri Lankan Air force. we booked "Tamarind" and "blue Whale". Tamarind is little bit out dated but has a wonderful private beach area for children to play and also for relaxation. It has a three rooms and Open Dining area as well and all facing the lovely beach. " Blue Whale" is newly built room and a wonderful sea breeze balcony. lucky we went on New year holidays and they have organised some new year games which we were participated. Staff were very nice and helpful. food is not excellent but for the price it's worthy. if you want to relax at a beach try this place.

title: a cozy place
text: we stayed there for two nights and enjoyed soooo much, the rooms are so close to seawater, anytime any moment i can jump into the sea if i want as the beach are in privacy not in public. the breakfast is nice..generally speaking, it is a place worth visiting for weekend or holiday...

title: a peaceful paradise
text: If you are looking for a peaceful place this is it, beautiful and safe sea, lovely beach, food is excellent and the portions and varieties are vast. the airforce Management staff is excellent and friendly, they really helped us with a special food request for health purposes. the chalets are very clean, quite spacious. it's nicer to be in a group as it can be a bit too quiet, depends on what you look for. if you want to be lost to the rest of the world then you got it right, the ayuveda massage is such a wonderful experience, very reasonable charges. snorkling is just next to the resort, from here we travelled to see the famous hindu temple( nice place) and the hot water wells (nothing much to see).

title: Watchout for perverts
text: Before I write my experience, I need to put things into perspective so that the appropriate audience can be guided. If you are a bunch of guys looking to go to the beach for the day, then you will love this place. The beach is clean, acceptable water conditions for a swim and even for snorkeling. The problems lie if there are women in the group and they tend to expose a little more skin than you would typically see in such a location. My sister was not even on the beach, and there was a military guy who was secretly filming her or taking pictures with his cell phone camera. You basically have a bunch of military men running a resort with no etiquette on being respectful to women. I can only imagine if a bunch of women were to travel to this location by themselves. Who is to know what could transpire? So given this experience, I would never encourage females and certainly not Westerners (women) to visit this so called "resort" in Trincomalee. There are other safer places to put on a bathing suit and enjoy a nice tan in Trincomalee without having perverts around you. They also have rooms for rent. I guess you need to be really looking for fun to stay overnight in this place!!

title: They say the ocean looks like rolling marbles....
text: This quiet and peaceful beach is a delight. Unlike other readers we found that there was adequate place to change in the shower areas. The food was a disappointment....I had what I would call an "invisible tuna" sandwich....3 slices of bread but nary a bit of tuna! But it didn't really matter and swimming in the Indian Ocean better than lunch!

title: What a beach!
