title: Great Experience
text: Great Experience at Nilaveli Beaches and super clean. Particularly we enjoyed the trip to Pigeon Island where there is very beautiful beaches too. We spend times to watch Coral and exotics fishes in shallow water.

title: Just some random beach
text: I was visiting Nilaveli and had high expectations. But seeing this beach was nothing special. Rubbish everywhere. Plastic is covering the beach. No nice atmosphere like other beaches for example Marakolliya beach in the south can offer!

title: undiscovered
text: Still a very quiet beach, not a lot of people. Perfect place to just kick back and really relax. Beautiful weather in May!

title: Beautiful water, shame about the litter
text: This is a beautiful beach to visit. The sea is warm & the sand is golden. Almost perfect. Except for the scores of litter - mainly plastic bottles - that litter the shoreline. If it was cleaned up & looked after it would be a definite 5*.

title: A clean beach!
text: Wide, clean & quiet beach No beach sellers, no dogs, no fishermen, no cafe or restaurant .....only a small herd of cows roam the beach which suited me fine with on interruptions. Sunrise is stunning if you can get up early enough but well worth it. View over to Pigeon Island where you can snorkel or dive, boat trip of approx 10 mins you need a ticket for the island and of course pay the boatman. Again no shops or cafe on the island - wonderful, take your own water etc., Nilaveli Beach is heaven.

title: Ultra blue waters
text: The beach is nice an quiet, all you can hear is the ocean..... which is perfect for a swim unless it is rough, the waters are clear enough to go in neck deep and clearly see your feet and the tiny tropical fish around them :)

title: Beautful, serene... and cows!
text: The waves were great to ride, the atmosphere is perfect for lone travellers, couples or family. And we saw cows on the beach - hilarious!

title: greit food
text: good vegetable food, realy. good place, taste icecreame. It takes a long time for the execution of the order, but it is not critical

title: Lovely beach
text: It was a lovely place to relax it had long sandy beaches and not a busy beach so you had the beach to yourself. Found it difficult to change currency. Were entertained with the wild monkeys running a long the swimming pools.

title: On the beach under the palms...!
text: You can chose the public beach frequented by the locals and stay under a palm, or other parts of Nilaveli beach in the shadow of the bar/hotel. Both good

title: Beautiful beaxh
text: We stayed at Nagenahira beach villas and our part of the beach was beautiful - very little rubbish and few fishermen. Up the beach (500m to the north) there were always lots of people, much more rubbish, fishermen pulling in their nets, and discarded/rotting fish. Dogs and cows roam the beach but do not bother us as we lounge in the hotel deck chairs. One dog even took to shooing the cows away. The light in the evenings is beautiful.

title: Awful
text: I have no idea who may think that this place is a "paradise". It's not worth a single hour of your time. Snorekling/ diving is highly overpriced. The beach is full of hungry stray dogs, crows, cows and their poo and nagging locals. Waters full of stinging sea lice. Stay away unless VERY cool.

title: Very nice beach!
text: It is a very nice beach with loads of palm trees and clear water. There are only few restaurants along the long beach, so have plety of water and check and plan where you want to eat. In other case you will find yourself walking long miles before getting to the restaurant. You can find some shade under the palm trees.

title: Amazing beach
text: Clean, scenic and safe beach. Starting point for boating to see dolfins, whales and snorckelling : just ask on the beach ;-)

title: Nice long Beach
text: It's nice long beach with almost no people. Very calm not raf sea at high season. Very clean beach and 2-3 beach restaurants

title: white sand and and strolling cows
text: middlle and southern part are even more quiet. white sand, warm water - starting from april like a great pool with mostly calm waves. Not touristic.

title: Best beach in the area
text: Loved this beach. It's a long white sandy beach and pristine clear water. It's a lot quieter than Uppuveli - with only a lit bit of development along it. Only annoying thing was that the boats to pigeon island go back and forward all the time from here so there's a bit of boat noise. Beach and water was very clean. There's wasn't a huge amount of shade either. Very easy to get to via tuk tuk from Trinco or Uppuveli. There was a small market near the beach with places to gets drinks etc

title: Absolutely idyllic
text: This beach is 'in season' from May - October. At this time it is just beautiful. Not too many hotels means that the beach is not packed with people and touts. The sea is calm and the water warm. What more could one want.

title: Fantastic beach
text: This is one of the best beaches. When I went in the morning the entire beach was for myself and even then a Coast guard came with me to take care and srilankan people are so friendly and caring. Surely Trincomalee is the queen of beaches in Sri Lanka

title: Calm Beach
text: The nilaveli Beach is beautiful. The sea is a Bit wavy and gets eaven more on the afternoon. There were just a few tourists. There are a few hotel,guesthouses on the Beach Front. We stayed at Bella nilaveli. Also good is the 'thats why' bar and cottages.

title: Quiet, peaceful, clean
text: Amazing beach, long stretch of white sand, extremely clean. No rocks or see weed to be found. Few local dogs around but won't bother you and you can order your meal on the beach- not an issue.

title: Just average
text: We went in off season I. E. February however the beach is nothing amazing. Only average swell, nice blue water but a little misty. Beach itself is wonderfully long but there are spots where there is a lot of plastic around. And there is very little shade Good family beach but can have big rips. For us the south and west had nicer beaches this time of year. Also if you come in off season there is little food or amenities around. This was actually quite nice, just a few local boats going out to pigeon island, but come prepared with supplies.

title: One of my favorite beaches
text: The beach is wide, the sand is warm and the Indian Ocean is hard to beat. Offers a lovely experience. We saw the sunrise, and the sky turned pink at sunset. This is an amazing beach

title: Beach to relax and safe sea bath
text: December is not the season - but very good place to relax and enjoy the nature. Beach was a clean to a certain extent and a place and good for sea bath. Of course we had great pleasure in visiting the place. its a 6 hour dive from colombo - but worth it.

title: Beauty, marred
text: An absolutely beautiful stretch of beach, with a shallow entry and warm waters to enjoy. It was a bit rough when we visited, but not at all unswimable (3-4’ waves). The heavy surf did product a thick belt of shells, coral and other items at the entry, and a somewhat deep drop at the shore (which quickly levels off), making getting in or out tricky and uncomfortable on the feet. The only major negative was the amount of waste, plastics and other random debris in the ocean. It was an ugly situation, and detracted from the natural splendour of the place. Sad the people would be so shortsighted and not respect the beautiful surroundings.

title: What a peace!!!
text: Beautiful beach with a lot charm, local fishermen in their traditional boats are great to see and on the side of the beach you the locals area which is also fantastic to experience, what about cricket on the beach!!!

title: Really nice beach
text: The beach was actually better than the grass that the hotel considered beach. Went for a walk here at sunset and view lovely

title: Fantastic Beach!
text: This beach is like a swimming pool at this time of the year! Very shallow, warm and calm.the beach sand is nice to walk along and there are spots close-by for snorkeling.

title: Wonderful beach, see the big and the small wonders
text: Passikudah Beach is a beach with very different faces. Beginning with many corals, then flat and sandy, as any tourist wants to have, then mixed with corals and sand, and in the end, at elephant rock, with huge rocks. You must take your time to explore, it's worth it. Make a long walk, or, just go there for sunrise, it's really amazing, I'm still in love with it.

title: Nice place
text: Pasikudah beach is a nice place to visit. Be carefull if you go on the weekend because it's very crowdy of local people. Even that, you can walk a little bit and be alone because all the locals are gathered in the same place.

title: Passikudah Beach - low water, Kalkudah Beach - deaper and better for swimming
text: If you have very small childern than I rather recommend Passikudah Beach where is low water even if you walk 50 m to the ocean. But if you travel without childern, never go to Passikudah Beach - it is boring, it is more difficult go to swimm there. Definitely chose Kalkudah Beach where the ocean has beautiful color, it is easy to go to swim and there are almost no people on the beach.

title: Beautiful beach
text: We recently spent 4 days in this area and Passikudah beach is lovely. It is nice and clean as a beach and the water is also clean and clear. It is shallow for miles out so great for a relaxing hangout and swim. We made it a ritual to stop here everyday for a bit. Gets a little busy on weekends but not unnameable.

title: Quiet, clean beaches!
text: Had a great time at the Amaya Beach resort! Loved the quiet and clean beaches, however not many restaurants outside of the hotels. Snorkling possible .

title: Clean, nice and sandy beach
text: Not a crowded beach and no salesmen are trying to sell souveniers. Watersports i.e. jetski. Plenty of place to relax. And you feel very safe here.

title: Beautiful safe beach!
text: A safe (enclosed in a lagoon) sea to swim in, and a beautiful large white beach which is not crowded!

title: Beautiful beach
text: Sand and beautiful water, cooling wind and nice people! Jet ski available for the teenagers and nice sandwich bars for lunch.????

title: Best Beach
text: Best beach I've visited in Sri Lanka. Clean white sand and crystal clear water. You can walk quite a ways into the ocean.

title: Tranquil waters
text: The part of Passikudah Beach we had access to from the Amethyst Resort was lovely. Water is extremely calm and warm. You have to walk out quite a long way to get to deeper water so fairly safe. Protected by a reef. Not many tourists as yet, but good to see the local people enjoying the water.

title: Lovely beach but very little shade
text: Lovely long, wide beach lined with resorts but it also has public access. Only downside is that there's little shade and no loungers/parasols to hire on the beach itself.

title: Best beach in town
text: Really enjoyed Pasikudah beach during my stay in June, 2019. I stayed at Uga Bay and it was well maintained, and well guarded. The sea is very nice and calm.

title: Sri Lankan Maldives
text: Passikudah Beach is one of the best in Sri Lanka. It's so attractive, calm, has beautiful white sand. There are good quality 4-5* hotels around. It's so peaceful, no disturbance from beach boys. We enjoyed swimming, had perfect relaxation. Perfect time to travel from May to September.

title: A paradise on earth
text: What a beach... true paradise , the sand is white,white... it’s so peacefull! We love it here! We’ll come back here fore sure!!

title: Amazing Beach
text: This beach is absolutlely amazing. It deep blue ocean and clear sand make this beach one of the prettiest I have visited so far. The water is hot and almost with any waves, much more like a lake. Some areas have some dead coral so be careful with your feet. Loved it and higly recommend a visit to it.

title: Beutify unspoilt beach
text: Very quiet. Only a few hotels. Shallo water. Soft white sand. Some watersports but otherwise not much activity or dining possibilities.

title: Deserted paradise
text: Just back from Sri lanka, where we stayed in Anantaya resort on Passikudah beach. As I mentioned in a previous review for Arugam bay, it was of season and they are recovering from being closed for 2 years for Covid. Positives: The resort is really beautiful and its situated on a magnificent beach. The people at the resort could not have been any friendlier and helpful. The upgrade they gave us had a swim up pool right to our room, which was fab. The resort is really a 5 start resort and it felt like that staying there. Food was very varied and really good Less positive feedback There was no more than 10 people at the resort while we were there, which made it feel empty. Most of the bars and restaurants that were advertised were closed. (only 1 was open) They set up a temp restaurant and bar, so when people were finished dinner it then closed. (around 8pm) We knew it would be off season, but didnt realise it would be so quiet, especially in the evening. I would certainly recommend Anantaya resort and Passikudah as a fantastic destination, but plan your visit between May and September, when all the facilities should be open.

title: Very nice place at the resorts area
text: The beach area it's very good for swimming. I recommend to use the resorts area of the beach, where it's much cleaner and safe.

title: Nice Beach
text: Not crowded and a very shallow beach, you can really walk out a long way until it gets beep. Water is a very pretty color and it looks like a pst card. Very nice.

title: wonderful beach, warm clear ocean
text: just great for swimming, depth increases gradually and easy to get behind the waves. Warm and crystal clear - a wonderful beach

title: Public part of beach is full of garbage. The rest is nice.
text: Tragically, the public part of beach is full of garbage. The 5* hotels take care of the rest of the beach, so those parts are really nice. Sad that this is the case, but Sri Lanka has a terrible litter problem on most of the beaches.

title: Superb
text: Definitely the east cost of Sri Lanka is wonderful. Sea like a lake, sand superb.... Just don’t loose it.

title: Excellent for a sea bathe
text: One of the best place to have a sea bathe, If you love sandy beaches with shallow sea, this beach might be a good choice. The sea waves aren't that nicer compared to other beaches in Sri Lanka. but if you are looking to have asafe sea bathe this is definitely recommended. The best time for bathe in this place would be between 9 am until 2 pm as this place get crowded in the evenings.

title: Decent
text: Probably not the best of Sri Lankan beaches but still a nice spot. The middle of the cove is the best as the ends are rocky and the one section that seems to be frequented by locals has garbage strewn about. The rest of the beach is pretty clean. The sand is powdery and the water is clear. Downside if you aren’t staying at one of the beach resorts is that there is zero shade. All trees and structures are on private property and there is security to make sure you don’t even sit under a tree on the border of resort and beach. Easy to burn fast!

title: Loved it
text: Has to be one of the nicest resort beaches on the Island. A long stretch of lovely golden sands, Azure calm waters that you can wade quite a distance out into. Great beach for long walks early in the morning or at sunset. Avoid the section of public beach towards the southern end, its noisy and overcrowded. Great for diving, snorkeling and you can also hire Jet Skiis. One thing Passikuda lacks is a bit of the outside restaurant and bar scene. Perhaps they can allocate a specific area at the back of the resort for this.

title: Unforgettable experience.
text: Nice beach and not too busy, Very clean. Top place to spend several days in peace. This was one of best options we chose. Unforgettable experience, highly recommended.

title: Perfect beach.
text: The sand is very fine. Just aa fine as in Bretagne, France. The water is way warmer than in Bretagne. No cold sensation when getting in. The waves are very moderate. It is not crowded at all.

title: Fabulous broad sandy Beach
text: We spent wonderful 2 days at the passikudah beach and I would say this is a five star beach. Beach is incredibly Clean blue colour and calm so even kids can enjoy. Beach is broad and sandy which is beautified by palm trees. There are few beautiful hotels that you can easily access to the beach. We wanted to experience the east coast and this was one of best options we chose.

title: Beautiful beach
text: Lovely beach with several hotels in the area. The water is clean, calm and safe to swim in. There are not many restaurants in the area so dining is fairly limited to hotel restaurants.

title: Lovely Beach
text: We used this beach whilst staying at the Calm Resort complex. Nice, sandy beach with shallow sea for quite a way out. The Indian Ocean here is the warmest sea I have ever swum in.

title: Sandy but dangerous
text: The beach was clean, sandy and empty. There was a red flag both days so swimming in the sea wasn't an option.

title: Excellent beach
text: Excellent sandy beach with good infrastructure. Beach is cleaned every day. I recommend for everyone.

title: Best beach on the east coast
text: We live in the USA and can only visit Sri Lanka during our summer school holidays so we always go to Passikudah beach in June or July. The beach is beautiful and extremely clean. I love the fact that you can walk far out into the water at this time of year and there is no strong current and it’s not deep. The beach is the best behind Anantaya, Maalu Maalu and Uga Bay. However, if you go to the beach behind Anilana, it is terrible and you really can’t go into the water because all of the sand is covered with broken coral fragments. I love Anilana hotel, but not the beach behind it. Don’t miss the wonderful sunrise on Pasikudah beach. In addition, take a walk down to the fishing village at the end of the beach in the early morning hours just after sunrise as that is when the fisherman pull in their nets. It’s really interesting to see what they catch. Also keep in mind the water on this beach is calmest during June to September and it is really rough December through March.

title: White sand east cost beach
text: Fabulous very clean and neat east cost beach for every one to enjoy. Specially for water sports and relax. For nature lovers too can enjoy .

title: Beautiful views, needs a tidy!
text: Incredible beach - water so warm and clean. Such a pity about plastic bottles etc strewn across the sand.

title: Picture perfect
text: Passikudah beach is the classic beach paradise...with lovely white sand, bath-warm water and fringed with palms. It’s a big bay where a busy public beach (we were there on the full moon public holiday) sits happily alongside the quieter, hotel frontages. Only improvement would be to extend the exclusion zone for jet skis- although hardly an issue as only a couple are available, they would be better kept 100m or more offshore - they do break the peaceful setting and hamper a long swim out from the beach.

title: Exploring Sri Lanka
text: Beautiful beach ?? Quite a few big hotels use this beach and I believe you can use some of their beach bars. It is kept very clean and police were seen patrolling the beach. The sea is very clear and safe to swim in. It is quite shallow until quite a way out. There is a PADI Dive School on the beach which also rents jet ski’s, banana boat rides etc. My daughter did her PADI Open Water Qualfication whilst we were there and they were very professional and my daughter enjoyed diving with them.

title: Really calm
text: Realy lovely beach...calm and peaceful...beach is really clean water is realy warm great for children becuse water isnt deep about 250m in to the sea. The best part of the beach is in front of The Calm hotel...

title: Perfect for young children
text: We stayed at one of the large resorts, but loved our daily walks along the beach, and seeing all the locals enjoying their beautiful beach. Our 6 month old loved it!! The water was warm, no waves, he could have sat on the shoreline eating sand all day. There are cows and dogs around particularly at the public beach end which has a life guard, but it’s very relaxed. I only hope it can stay clean and not full of jet skis.

title: A beautiful and clean beach
text: Although Pasikudah is a distance from Colombo compared to the beaches on the southern coast of Sri Lanka, I would highly recommend this beach, if you are after a less crowded and clean beach. The beach is located in a bay hence it is not very rough.

title: one of the most serene beaches in srilanka
text: If you are looking for peace, peace and more peace then this is the place to be. it is far from the regular tourist circuit though on the way from trincomalee to arugambay. if not to stay for a couple of days be sure to stop to enjoy the beautiful blue waters.

title: Great beach for swimming and walking along
text: Ideal for families. Easy to swim in and spend a few hours. We spent time down in the local end and found some shade.

title: excellent
text: I snorkelled, saw a lot natural coral reef beauty, some fish but was very good and swam for miles into the ocean. Fabulous weather and scenic.

title: Oh dear!
text: Oh my goodness, it’s so sad to see this beautiful bay where we used to holiday in the 1960s full of expensive plastic hotels. It’s also so popular with locals and the littering is a huge problem. I suggest there should be warnings that if you’re caught dropping litter you should have to give up half an hour of your time to litter pick! Just one photo of a huge Hotel. I recommend staying in a small guest house instead. Nandawanam is excellent!

title: Calm waters & uncrowded beach
text: Visited during mid June and the weather was perfect. A bit sunny but the balmy breeze combined with the refreshing waters make floating around the calms pleasant. The only downside is that it is a 6 hour drive from Colombo.

title: Beautiful Bay
text: This has been the highlight of our trip to Sri Lanka. We feel that this is very close to paradise. Would definitely visit again.

title: Private beach - Quiet and Clean.
text: About 5-6 Hotels line the beach and have private access to it. It is a c shaped beach with not too much wave activity. Calm Indian Ocean waters.Swimming is safe. LSR Watersports is a large provider who organises everything here from JetSkiing to Scuba. But be prepared, that they will follow you :D You can reach a small village between resorts with public beach. Don't hesitate to look in, they are cows, groups of stray dogs and sri lankan peoples who salutes you and smiles at you. Resorts keeps their beaches clean, but behind resorts there are too many plastic bottles and waste at all on the beach. But water is clear, you can see some fishes also. There are some bars at resorts, where you can have some drink or tea, but the prices are about 900 rupies per cocktail. The village includes muslim inhabitants so women don't go there only in swim suit, it is different culture so you have to respect it. text: Amazing paradise beach! Warm clear water and white sand! Biggest drawback of this beach is that it is clearly aimed at families and people who are there to spend some money! Amazing sunshine Nice beach restaurants Peaceful area away from the road Beach activities available Cons Very windy, uncomfortable amount of sand in your face! All beds are owned by hotels for only paying guests! No shade, can’t even lie under a tree as it is hotel owned Beach resorts own most of beach, 2m from shore is where the ‘non payers’ can go! Were told the resorts “don’t want non payers too close to the guests” Hired beach beds for 900rupees from uga bay resort after negotiation! Were only alowed them until hotel guests arrived and no one was allowed to open up the accompanying umbrellas! We were made to feel very uncomfortable!! Only available food is from local shops or beach resorts! Resorts are lovely but very expensive! Overall backpackers and people on a tighter budget avoid! Nice place for families and honeymooners! title: Beautiful beach, but at what cost!
text: This is a lovely looking beach although no real character - just big resort hotels. The sea is painful to walk into as there are huge quantities of sharp coral which you can't avoid. I spoke to local business owners whilst there and discovered that in 2009, the big hotels got together and destroyed the coral reefs in order to get rid of the waves created. The local businesses fought against this but there was nothing they could do. If you walk along the beach you will see piles and piles of dead coral - quite distressing. There is a Swiss NGO working to replant the coral and if you want to learn more, go chat to the manager Siva of Hotel Vasuki - a lovely man who is trying to improve the area and incidentally serves up an absolutely amazing curry and rice.

title: Lovely Scenic Lake

The locals were all taking a swim in the waters as we passed and there was a lovely atmosphere. We stayed in Tissa for two days doing Yala Safaris and the lakeside was a great way to wind down the day.

Evening might be a bit troublesome for single woman as you may get comments and whistles by the young locals who are wandering around with their bike. Not much things to see compare the afternoon except birds flying back to their nest and maybe a beautiful sunset if the weather is good.

title: This turned out to be the highlight of our safari, better than Yala park!
text: What a nice little surprise this turned out to be, sunset boat ride was very lovely, we had a nice boatman who took us around, we saw this magical bird tree filled with hundreds of ibis and other birds, it was so breathtaking! Retrospectively speaking, this 1 hour boat ride was much more exciting than our 7 hour Yala safari the next morning. Boat ride as of mid-Feb 2018 cost Rs 3,000, picked up directly from the shores of our hotel. So worth it!

title: Lovely lake, birds, flowers, crocodiles
text: We just hired one of the guys with a boat waiting on the bank of the lake. He took us all around the lake and was knowledgable about the wildlife and plants. Engine was quite noisy but he would turn it off and let us soak in the tranquility. Definitely worth doing.

title: Beatiful tank
text: Take some time to try to spot birds and other wildlife. The terrace at Oak Ray lake resort is the perfect spot to do so.

title: Beautiful lake with plenty of birds
text: We just passed by the lake on a stroll one late afternoon, and were stunned by the beauty. There were pelicans, bee eaters and Kingfishers along with many other species. It was really a very nice Place for a stroll.

title: Highly recommend boat safari for sunset and bird watching
text: We went for a boat safari with Malaka the boatman. He is very knowledgeable on the type of birds and showed us a huge variety. The sunset views are also stunning. Highly recommend this.

title: The lake
text: It would have been nice to have been able to walk around this lake a bit. It looks really pretty but they were doing construction so we couldn't go.

title: Picturesque lake
text: It's very pleasant to walk around the lake. The southern shore of the lake is especially picturesque. It's also interesting to see local bathe in the waters. Take this route when heading to Yatala Wehera from the city centre. There are also trees on the western shore with thousands of fruit bats roosting in the day.

title: just OK
text: The lake has a charm of its own. however, this really needs to be pepped up by the tourism dept since it is not visited because visitors just see The yala sanctuary and drive off. They need to propagate it and make it a tourist spot.

title: “A Must Do” when in Tissa
text: My partner and I took the boat ride just before sunset, and it was worth the 1,000 Rupees per pax we paid. We had a very friendly boat man who provided us with a brief on the birds that inhabited the lake. He brought us to the mini-island on the lake, as well as the area where all the black-headed ibises nested. He also pointed out to us the ‘mass migration’ of bats from the padi fields to the lake area at sunset. The entire boat ride was an hour plus and the sights were priceless!

title: Lovely evening on the Lake
text: You can take boat trips on this lake, I arranged mine with a local fisherman (Nuwan), who sells fish besides where the safari drivers congregate. I arranged a price - 2500 rupees ( £12.50) for about 1.5 hours and a day and time of departure ( 4.30 pm). This is a lovely trip to take particularly if you are into wildlife and birds in particular, however the sunset views are just stunning as well, the added attraction is all the egrets coming into the trees to roost, making them look as if they are covered in large white petals, and the hundred and hundreds of bats ( large fruit bats) flying across the lake at dusk on there way to there feeding grounds.

title: stuning view
text: its a gorgeous lake and with stunning view superb. we had a long wall around the lake its was really awesome.

title: Nice walk
text: Lots of birds to see as well as water buffalo. You can take a boat ride for 1000rps per person. We walked up Wellawaya Rd as well to Debarawewa Lake which is also lovely. The best part is just after you've turned onto Wellawaya Rd, there are 1000s of fruit bats hanging from the trees, at night they fly off over Tissa Lake.

title: Best guide in Tissamahara
text: We have been in Tissamahara as a stopover between Unawatuna and Ella. We did not really know what to do and had to leave the other day very early to get the bus to Ella. Coincidentally when walking around we met Mr. Denzil. Normally I was annoyed of all these Tuk Tuk drivers that want to bring you somewhere but he was totally different. I instantly felt that for him it is not about money but about showing foreigners the beauty of his country and he totally did. He made our day! Without him the stay in Tissamaharama would have been nothing special but he definitely made it to one of the best days of the whole trip. He took us in his tuk tuk to see many different birds, buffalos, nice nature and above all these amazing trees full of bats. I have never seen something like this before. We also visited the temple with him. If you are interested, he will tell you everything about Buddhism! Afterwards we decided to go to Ella with him instead of taking the bus and we did not regret it. We saw wild animals on the way, even elephants on the street close to Yala! He is a really warm, sincere and lovely person and we are happy that we met him!

title: Gorgeous landscaping
text: We did a walk near the lake on one evening and it was an amazing feeling. The walk stretches about 3kms and myself and my friends did the whole walk.

title: don't miss the bats
text: Lovely place to stroll around in the evening. Dont miss the hundreds of fruit bats that live in the trees. Ask the locals where they are.

title: wonderful sunrise/sunset
text: fantastic views at Sunrise and sunset, especially for nature lovers. boatrides during the day are nice; a lot of people swim or fish in this wewa. Also you can walk along the footpath, mostly in the shade of the trees. In the water you can find waterhyacinths, lillies, lotusflowers...

title: Wonderfully beautiful and marvellous bird life
text: The Tissa Wewa or lagoon is absolutely beautiful and if you are lucky enough to be staying in the vicinity do see it at varying times of the day. It has glorious light at sunrise, is lovely in the full sun of the day and has a really lovely appearance at sunset when the colours are reflected in the water. One of the great attractions of the place is seeing birds flying into the trees in the late afternoon to roost for the night. Generally bird life in this area is spectacular. You will also enjoy thousands of bats hanging in the trees near to the water. Overall this is a very special place and well worth exploring.

title: loved the lake
text: beautiful, real Sri Lanka... worth a walk around...dont just nip and out for a visit to Yala.. more to do !

title: Great for a evening boatride
text: We did half a hour boat ride ,our boat driver spoke a bit of English so of not much help. Overall good sightings of birds in the island. The sunset bought alive the bats flying of the tree and was spectacular. Recommend a half hour ride at sunset .

title: Nico to take the road east of the lake
text: We rented a scooter and tried to drive around the lake. We went counter clockwise from the south of the lake, where the sidewalk is. You will pass a lot of guesthouses at first, but later come to a less explored area with farmers and cute houses (and lot's of hidden poverty). It's not possible to go around because the roas is blocked, but it's a nice sidestep from what everybody else sees at the lake.

title: Bats and birds
text: Go the far end (from the town) at about 5.30pm and watch the birds come back to roost for the night and the thousands of large fruit bats head out for the night. It is simply spectacular.

title: Wildlife haven and spectacle
text: We visited Tissa reservoir, which is one of five in the area, a number of times during our three night stay in the area. It has an abundance of wildlife including the globally threatened Spot-billed Pelican and Watercock. We also saw three species of Bittern (Yellow, Black and Cinnamon). We also found a pair of Greater Painted Snipe on the north west corner, a difficult bird to find anywhere in its African and Asian distribution. Also along the western edge of Tissa Reservoir are heronries comprising a number of species. Some trees at dusk can resemble British Magnolia trees (whilst actually being the roost of mainly Cattle Egrets). The most spectacular sight for us was seeing the many thousands of Giant Fruit Bats leaving their roost at dusk and flying past an illuminated temple through our telescope.

title: Beautiful
text: We had a hotel next to lake. It was really beautiful in the eveings. We did every evening a walk there with the hotels dog. Was really nice :) Also you can see there a lot of birds and some other animals.

title: Beautiful lake in Tissa
text: We hired bikes and had a lovely cycle around Tissa, including cycling alongside this beautiful lake. We also passed input a number of times during our day at Yala and other excursions in the area. Well worth seeing whilst in Tissa.

title: Stunning views!
text: The best part of Tissamaharama is the lake, the paths around it and the views. I enjoyed every minute of this surreal place!

title: Nice views
text: We took an evening stroll along part of the Tissa Wewa, beautiful expanse of water, used by the locals for bathing in parts and many species of birds and Im sure other wildlife!

title: Nice lake
text: Very nice lake situated near Tissa and many locals coming to here for bathing. Many different kind birds specially fruit bats too..

title: Cool environment
text: Nice cool breeze environment around the Tissa Wewa. Quite a place to have lunch with a families or friends.

title: Nice view
text: This lake is a nice view and traditionally pilgrims used to be refresh before go to worship Kataragama temple. its so crowed in most of Holidays and lost of local groups gather around this. its not recommend for bath at all.

title: Nice place
text: it is a very beautiful place to visit.lots of lotus flowers in the lake.people can bath and swim in their. i swim too . but it is a very deep lake. when you swimming make sure not to go to deep area.

title: Refreshing
text: This is a nice and huge lake, surrounded by some settlements, greeneries and nature. Nice road around the part of lake to go around - cycling around in the evening was lovely, when I also saw some people were fishing. Its really refreshing with cool breeze and greeneries around.

title: Serenity!
text: Tissa Wewa (Tissa Tank), a huge man-made lake about 1.5km from the town center. In the evening, check out the huge flocks of egrets that descend onto the trees around the lake to roost. The road along the southern edge has a wide new Lakeside Walkway for strolling. You can even buy Dhal wade, fresh water fish bites, manioc chips from the wayside carts.

title: Swimming in the Tissa lake was refreshing
text: It was 40 degrees in Tissa so we decided to swim in the lake with the locals to cool off. Yes, there are crocodiles but we decided to inside the main group of 50 locals. I could taste the soap as the locals bath there every day. Our guide Rehun from 'why not getaway' tours jumped in too and played tag with our children (aged 11 and 12) in-between the locals, who looked on amused. He thought New Zealanders were more adventurous.

title: Stunning
text: We went for a little walk around Tissa through the town and then out here – stunning place, especially the photographs.

title: Artificial Reservoir
text: Tissa Wewa is actually an artificial reservoir, thought to have been constructed in the 3rd Century BC, either by Mahanaga of Ruhuna or his successor Yatala Tissa of Ruhuna. It was constructed to irrigate paddy lands and supply water to the flourishing city of Tissamaharama. Apparently, the lake was restored in 1871 by the British to provide shade. It is definitely a good walk to take some pictures, go for a morning walk and do some picnics.

title: Spectacular bird watching
text: Pelican, spoonbill, pied kingfisher were the most remarkable of the birds we saw at Tissa Wewa. Pied Kingfisher was in full action diving into the lake several times for his catch. Lovely place to picnic.

title: Better lakes elsewhere in Sri Lanka
text: We had a short walk here one evening. Not a lot to do, just walk around the edge of the man-made lake. Lots of stray dogs around and heavy traffic. There are much better lakes in Sri Lanka to walk beside and look for wildlife. Wouldn't recommend.

title: Clam and Beautiful Lake
text: Tissa Wewa is a large beautiful Lake. We were staying in a hotel which was at the Bank of Lake. Clean water and many birds on the middle Island makes you feel fresh. Boating is available on the Lake and They also take you to Crocodile Safari.

title: Picturesque
text: the lake is picturesque has crocs and buffalos and other wildlife in it. Check out the locals swimming even though there are crocodiles. There is nothing else to do in Tissa other than go to the lake and use it as a base for the Yala safari.

title: A vast lake
text: Actually the lake was the backdrop for our hotel and we had to go just beside the lake to reach our hotel. A very calm and vast water body with variety of birds chirping around the lake in the morning

title: Sunset boat trip.
text: Lovely hour long boat trip around the lake just before sunset. Saw many bird varieties, huge fruit bats and crocodiles. Lovely to walk around as well.

title: Wildlife plus local's bathing
text: This is a pretty large lake. I was pleasantly surprised by its cleanliness, some rubbish around but not so bad. There are lily pads and grasses growing in the lake and lots of fish and birds. We also saw a few terrapins swimming around and were told there are crocodiles too. This fact doesn't deter the locals from using the lake as a laundry, bath, swimming pool and general meeting place. We saw a lovely sunset over the lake and I caught a few fish on my travel rod much to the intrigue of the locals.

title: Stunning view in a tranquil afternoon!
text: I visited Tissa Lake on my way to Yala. The lake is really wide and water is so pure that you can even see fish swimming under you foot! The view is awesome for photography and walking along the lakeside. The sky is always bright which makes the view so picturesque! This place is highly recommend if you love lakes or ponds, like me :)

title: Nice place!
text: Nice for a walk or run in the morning before safari. Vast lake not far from city centre (10 min walk)

title: Stunning Views at Sunset
text: The highlight for us in Tissa. Lots of birdlife. Plan to visit at sunset and take a leisurely walk along the lake.

title: Beautiful sunset
text: We had intended just walking around Tissa Wewa in the early evening but decided at the last minute to take a boat ride instead. We had a young Sri Lankan lad drive the boat, he also pointed out birds and was very sympathetic to maintaining the calm and quiet atmosphere by cutting the engine and allowing us to hear as well as see the birds. He was not a skilled ornithologist but had learnt a lot and was enthusiastic about what he saw. We had a lovely sunset and on the return saw hundreds of fruit bats.

title: Beautiful lake, great for walking
text: Take the time to walk next to this lake in nice weather, or during sunset. Its beautiful and a great experience.

title: just beautiful
text: it's one of the most beautifl places we visited in Sri lanka. you will see lots birds and even bats in this area. sunset is unforgetable too.

title: Bundala with Ceylon Safari Tours
text: Today we had another safari with Ceylon Safari Tours but this time we were off to Bundala with Chamara again. We had the same prompt pick up in the jeep just for the two of us. After Yala yesterday's Safari which is manic with many vehicles. Bundala is the total opposite with only a few vehicles a day and the whole tour taken at a more leisurely pace. Another bonus is that you also get a park ranger to accompany you within the jeep and his name was Randika which means we had two experienced knowledgeable guides spotting the beautiful birds. We had a wonderful experience and spotted many birds and a couple of wild animals (elephants and crocodiles). The tour included a picnic spot in an absolutely beautiful spot on the coastline before we carried on with the tour. A wonderful trip made special with Chamara and Randika , many thanks to them both for a highly recommendable trip.

title: Nice boot tour
text: Nice boot tour. Many different birds. Crocodiles. Friendly People. Surprise as the road is relatively close

title: A pleasant walk
text: We had a pleasant walk by the tank in the early evening. It was amazing to see the bats on the move as night fell. Earlier we had seen a host of water birds including kingfishers, egrets and cormorants. It would be helpful if more of the lights worked along the promenade.

title: Calm, peaceful, birds and bats
text: We so much enjoyed returning to Tissa Wewa after a year of absence. The lake, an artificial reservoir has a long history dating to the 3rd century BCE when it was constructed to irrigate paddy fields. Today one can walk alongside the beautiful lake and see numerous birds and bat colonies. Early evening is a great time to be there when the birds are flying to their roosting areas. The whole lake has an atmosphere of peace and tranquility.

title: Bats and birds
text: Wonderful bird and bat viewing, friendly locals to help you with the timing and viewing. Pleasant natural environment.

title: DIY-Safari
text: It's great to go there in the early morning or late afternoon, because you will see a lot of wildlife. Birds, fruit bats and loads of monkeys are just close by the road. Grab a bicycle or a scooter and just drive around for your Do-It-Yourself-Safari. On our search for birds we took a small dirt road to nowhere and met a really nice family who invited us to their house for fruits and drinks. Awesome place!

title: Amazing Boat RIde
text: We went for a walk and we were able to get a boat ride. It was thrilling to go in the boat. The riders helped us to pluck some flowers too. It was awesome!

title: Lake
text: This is a beautiful lake on the Kataragama Yala road.A pretty lake This lake is used to irrigate agricultural land.

title: Not to be missed!
text: We were walking along the lakeside in the evening and were approached by one of the boatmen offering a boat ride for Rs1,000 per adult (free for kids). I was sceptical at first but our son insisted - mainly because of the birds that could be seen at the lakeside. I am glad we relented. The 1-hour trip was amazing. The boatman brought us to see colonies of cormorants and ibises nesting in the trees on the "bird island", and got so close that we could see hatchlings in some of the nests. We also got close to egrets perched on wading buffaloes. The best parts were boating through a vast expanse of lotus flowers and watching thousands of bats and birds "changing shifts" in the dying light, with pink and orange streaks in the sky. We did not plan for the boat ride but it turned out to be one of the best things we did in our Sri Lanka trip - minus the crowd.

title: 'Hidden gem'
text: The owner of our guesthouse recommended this place. It was truly gorgeous and really calm. A lot of birds to see, and a few crocodiles.

title: Ask locals about the exact time when the bats fly away from the trees at sunset
text: Probably the main reason or the biggest reason for you stopping by, if you consider doing that, will be to see a lot of bats sleeping on the trees at the lake and flying away as the sunset comes. Ask locals about the exact time when they go for that so you don't miss an opportunity to see something interesting that you don't often have a chance to see.

title: Bats!
text: Ask any tuk tuk driver to take you to the bat trees for 6.30pm. It's amazing. All the (10,000) fruit bat's fly out for the night. I felt like Sir David Attenborough should of been stood behind me! My pic doesn't do it justice!

title: Very Pretty Lake
text: This lake built during the kings era is one of the most beautiful lakes I have seen. You can go on boat rides to visit the trees with bats.

title: water reservoir
text: Beautiful scenery. Wish we had time to explore the area more. The view of the Tissa Maharamaya Dagoba is stunning. The Dagoba and Wewa(tank or reservoir) Built by the people in the 3rd Century Before Christ is impressive, even though the wewa nor the dagoba are not the oldest in the area.

title: Watch birds from the rooftop terrace of the rain tree hotel
text: I would highly recommend the "the rain tree hotel" for the "free bird watching show" on their roof top terrace. It is truly amazing to watch all the birds fly back to their sleeping trees and then see the fruit bats fly out into the dark- abolute recommendation!

title: Tissa Wewa, Tissamaharama
text: Tissa Wewa is one of the attraction place in Sri Lanka. Tissa Lake was constructed long time back and it is an artifical reservior. It cater to the needs of farmers in that area to irrigate paddy throughout the year. It also fulfills requirement of water to the people of that area.

title: Accessible Wetlands and free
text: The wetland fringes of the lake are full of fantastic birds easily viewed from the path . I was amazed to get clear views , photos and videos of 3 different Bitterns : Black , Yellow and Cinammon . This last bird is scarce and hard to see . Upali my very experienced guide had never had such good sighting . Other birds include : Stork-billed and White-breasted Kingfishers , Small Minivet , Jerdon’s Leafbird , and Common Iora . The following morning we bordÃ©e an area between the lake and a nearby stream and found other new birds : Jungle Owlet , Brown Fish-Owl , White-rumpled Munia , White-naped Yellow Woodpecker and the endemic Sri Lankan Red-backed Woodpecker . This is a very rewarding birdwatching area very close to the town and it is free. You can spend many fruitful hours here in between visiting the more famous sites .

title: Thissa Lake
text: Great for a stroll along the walk around the lake and watch for all the different types of water birds. Or maybe you could take in a boat ride or peddle yourself around in a swan peddle boat.

title: Beautiful like with amazing birdlife!
text: We took a very cheap 1h boat tour and saw plenty of birds, bats and buffalos. You take a ride in the middle of lotus flours and get the chance to see the locals swimming and playing and then there is more than 20 species of birds to find! Not to miss, definitely!

title: Good sun set and Bat tour
text: We took a boat and went to the bat island. and saw a bird island too. good for photographs and a good guide from the hotel we stayed in.

title: Evening boat trip
text: We went out on an evening boat trip arranged by our hotel and it was well worthwhile. The lake was so tranquil covered in lotus leaves and flowers, loads of birds and no tourists!! We saw lots of huge pelicans roosting in the Rain tress and a huge colony of fruit bats awaking from their slumber! we even saw a few crocodiles too but that didn't seem to worry the kids splashing around!! This is a very beautiful and peaceful lake and worth the boat trip and also hire some bikes to ride around it!

title: So large
text: This is a beautiful lake, so large and photographic. There were some lovely areas with water lillies and also area were the local kids were having fun in the water.

title: Mister Denzil and the Bats
text: This man knows almost everything about Tissamaharama,Budhism and the birds arround Tissa Wewa. We had the great oppurtunity to meet him and decided to tour arround with him - how lucky we were with his informations and places we stopped. I only can tell with my heart! He is such a great man - do not to miss a chance to travel with Mister Denzil - 0094 077 5300942

title: Quaint with Clean Water
text: This place is popular with both the locals with foreigners. The water is clean and suitable to have fun. The area is beautiful and serene too. Worth a visit.

title: Very pretty lake at sunset
text: Perfect for an evening stroll before your early morning game drive in one of the parks. Loved all the birds flying in to nest on the tree in the middle island. Lovely scenic countryside surrounds with rice paddys.

title: Serene
text: The serenity of this reservoir is heightened against the sky. There is little to spot in the water but the surrounding countryside is a photo opportunity.

title: Gorgeous Lake
text: Its a gorgeous lake, so calm and serene dotted with huge trees and greenery all around. It has a lovely promenade to walk, broad and clean. The promenade has cute tables and chairs for a lovely picnic lunch. Definitely recommend to spend an evening at Tissa Lake

title: best place in tissa
text: its was my fav place in tissa. i spent an entire afternoon here. so cool and calm and also clean. nice breeze and cool water. u can see many birds here too. very cool and calm and natural

title: I walked along the “new” walkway on the south shore of Tissa Tank.
text: Tissa Tank slash Lake I walked in a circle to Tissa Dagoba & along the “new” walkway on the south shore of Tissa Tank. It was interesting to see some LARGE trees there. It is amazing no-one has chop, chop, chopped them down. Very good people of Sri Lanka. Thanks!

title: Fantastic
text: Great place in Sri Lanka. It's so close from the place where I stayed in Tissamaharama. I saw the sun rise in evening time and lot of birds too.

title: boat ride
text: great view. good to do boat ride. not to swim in there. nice in the evening sunset. Exercise walk a way is there.

title: Beautifull lake
text: Tissa wewa is a beautiful lake and apopular attraction . The pathways have been recently redone and is n8w wrll lit . A boatride to the islandis recommended

title: Beautiful serene and tons of bird life
text: We got some bikes and did a circuit around the lake and rice fields. It was a fabulous day with the clouds mirrored across the water. It's very pretty and there are interesting birds everywhere. Lovely way to just stop and enjoy Sri Lanka.

title: Beautiful
text: Take a boat ride....go to the island....feed the deer in the island....watch the birds in the island.....thousands.....nest here.....don't swim.....except in places locals swim. Don't swim far.....stay very close to the bank......crocodiles!!! Ok......Dont swim......wash your face and feet only!

title: Very Impressive Ancient Engineering
text: The Twin Baths are absolutely huge and considering how long ago they were commissioned and built, they represent a truly remarkable feat of engineering. As the name suggests there are two ornate stepped baths side by side with beautiful carved steps and gates. There are two pools, one for the monks to wash and cleanse themselves and one to enter when washed and essentially rinse! There is a working filter system at one end that keeps the water relatively clean but the guide says they are totally drained before the monsoons so as to allow new water to accumulate during the rains. We'll worth a short stop, great for pictures.

title: Beautiful and calm
text: The trees were flowering during our visit in July, which made this particularly beautiful to visit and photograph. It wasn’t too busy so could photograph without tourists popping into frame all the time. Interesting construction. Could use more English language details on history and construction and use.

title: The monkeys were cool!
text: So this place has massive potential but even the local guides aren’t quite sure what was happening here. Suggest coming up with a cool story of kings and Buddha’s of past that resonates with people and going with it. Monkeys all over the joint.

title: Twin Baths
text: Really nice architectural and artistic design. worth visiting. You could only imagine how the royals enjoyed at the time they used the baths!

title: An historical place with relevance
text: Nothing great, but if you love history and culture then you can relate it to the early days and imagine how their life would be in those days.

title: Sri lanka hols
text: Boring for us. Just two square ponds used years ago now half empty and not cery clean wgen we visited

title: Definitely Worth A Pause. A Sight To Behold & Take A Photo Of. A Place to Learn More About After But ....
text: honestly ... towards the end of a long hot day visiting ancients sights and temples in and around Anuradhapura ... We were in and out of the van within 10 minutes. This is all we could manage. However we knew we were seeing a remarkable engineering fete and because of that I can honestly rate it excellent and I am glad I have seen it.

title: Ancient ingenuity
text: These pools are interesting because of their engineering. It never ceases to amaze me what people come up with to manage their access to water. Especially in parts of the world where it is in abundance some times of the year and more scarce in others. There are tourist stalls around the pools but the vendors are fairly low key.

title: Tour.
text: Went here during our tour and found the site very interesting. The construction of the first pool was impressive but the requirement for a second one seems amazing in this day and age.

title: An amazing design
text: These two bathing ponds were filled by guiding water into a pool, the sediment would have sunk alowing the clean water to overflow and into a pipe. The water then came out of a lion-s head spout into the bath. Apparently, the King and others would disrobe in a private area made of silks and other fabrics before entering the bath via the ornate steps. I had wondered why there was a cobra carved into the bath's side; my guide informed me that it is a symbol of prosperity and good luck. Would we visit this site again? Yes.

title: You cannot help but admire the work of the builders
text: We think technology is for modern man, but those who lived in the past were much wiser than we give credit for. This huge man made tank (dam) supplies water into the bath area through a system of water & drainage channels. The baths are made from huge granite stones. This site has a lot of potential if the Government could afford to re-establish the gardens & surrounding area. Overall it is well worth visiting.

title: Amazing
text: This is also one of the must sees of Anuradhapuras ancient city. Its location is near many of the other sites, so its worth going by bike. A wonderful historical site. Best to go in the morning or late afternoon, as it gets very hot during the day. Bring water, or buy from some of the vendors, at slightly inflated prices.

title: Architectural Marvel
text: It is a part of UNESCO world heritage site of Anuradhapura. It is a masterpiece of ancient advanced technology built by Sinhales. It was used by monks for bathing. Underground inlets & outlets for water. There are 2 tanks. Larger one is 132'length,51'breadth,18'depth. Smaller is 91'length,51'breadth,14'depth. All walls & floor are made by cut pieces of granite. There are flight of steps with support. Large pots decorate it. Well laid garden also. Few small souvenir shops . Entry ticket for SAARC Nationals is $12.5 or LKR 1937.5 /per person For other tourists is $ 25 or LKR 3875 /per person This is for all Anuradhapura sites.

title: Impressing size and craftsmanship
text: The twin baths are certainly an impressive piece of craftsmanship build in stone and filled by an ingenious draining system providing water to the whole are during the rainy season.

title: You need to take a closer look ...
text: These ponds were - just like some others - contructed in a specific way and include a few details (cobra, turtle and other ornaments). It included a water filter system and underground connections at a time when such things were unknown in Europe.

title: Neat pair of connected ponds.
text: These ponds are in really good condition and are separated by a raised walkway. The pools are connected underground. On the 2nd smaller pond at the rear is a carved 5 headed snake as well as a lion ( I believe this was a water spout). The monks used these pools for their ablutions

title: Huge stone pools
text: Twin ritual baths built in the 8th century. Worth a look because of their scale. There are a few stalls on one side selling fruit, drinks and tourist trinkets. The toilets here should be avoided at all costs!

title: Interesting pools with good background story
text: These two pools were used by the monks - the seniors in one, where it seems they just sat at the edge, while or the "juniors" the other pool offered immersion and bathing. The fact that these pools existed is down to some amazing old technology to bring in water from the nearby sources - some of are also man made. This is only part of a large complex for the monks. It gives food for thought on what it must have been like. You do need a guide to give you the necessary insight.

title: Retrospect
text: If this is what the baths looked like, imagine what the whole complex looked like when it was still intact and in use. The construction leading water to the bath is amazing.

title: Well kept and interesting

title: Twin Baths

title: Want to get marry?

title: Worth a look

It was interesting to see and note some slight discrepancies in who is believed to have used these - we were told locals or monks, other reviewers here say monarchy. Will we ever know? This site is surrounded by vendors, that spoils the effect a little.

title: Two adjacent bodies of water
text: The twin ponds were used for bathing tanks in ancient Anuradhapura city. One side of the pond still exposes the simple way in which the water was filtered before it entered into the ponds

title: Not for swimming

title: Interesting historical site

Only small, but definitely stop here on a tour around Anuradhapura.

title: Don't bring your soap

title: Kuttam Pokuna

title: Ancient swimming pool
text: This seems like a swimming pool but it s a bit different with a modern one. Its called twin ponds as there two such ponds and now a days its not in use really ,even though its seems one of the great place to visit and see the and see the ancient technology in those sectors.

title: Historic Engineering!!
text: A hydrological piece of engineering in the history of the kingdom of. Anuradhpura. Dress code is relaxed, however please consider this area as religious grounds.

title: Nothing spectacular

title: Nice
text: Place is nice but if you are in hurry you can skip it to see more beautiful places.It was good but when I arrived there place was full with little students :D

title: Interesting Cultural Find
text: Not far from roadside and accessible by car. Our guide proved very useful in painting a broad history of the site. One would need a guide or printed information to appreciate the cultural aspects of the site

title: Restored Baths
text: Twin Baths (Kuttam Pokuna) For centuries this area had been depopulated by the Malaria Mosquito and the surrounding jungle had reestablished itself, covering the many temples and Stupa built by a long Line of Sri Lankan kings each trying to outdo his predecessor by building bigger and better. Fortunately some have been reconstructed by the Sri Lankan archeological society. One of these is the twin baths at Mihintale, consisting two large bathing pools, these days full of green stagnant water with the odd Terrapin in thrown in. However you can see how the water was changed every couple of days with fresh water where the worlds largest school for Buddhist Monks used to bathe.

title: Steep steps to get to the baths
text: The twin baths are part of the Anuradhapura complex and is well worth a visit. Although there is only green stagnant water in the baths, they still provide great insight into the building skills of the ancient Sri Lankans. In order to actually get a good look at this structure, one must decend and then ascend a steep set of ancient stone steps. It is however, possible to get a glimpse of the baths from the top of the steps if you cannot navigate these steps.

title: Quiet and nice place
text: Our guide said that this pool never was an empty. In the monsoon time the pool is filled by water from rain. And on sunny days will never evaporate entire water from this pool. The water is still there and prepare for using like in an ancient time...

title: Very well restored
text: All sites in Anuradhapura including this one are well restored and maintained and worth a visit by all.

title: Great Story
text: The twin baths were interesting. Enjoyed walking around each pool and imagining how busy they would have been. Very quiet place.

title: What a Nice Place for a Bath!
text: This is truly an interesting place of history. The stone layout is amazing. What a place for the people during that time to use and enjoy.

title: Must have been nice once
text: I can imagine that it may once have been very pleasant bathing here. The pools are an interesting feat of construction, but only worthy of a short visit.

title: Fascinating Ruins
text: These twin baths are part of the Anuradhapura ancient ruins. It is absolutely fascinating how these stone monuments were built. There isn't much to the twin baths but it is a picture worthy moment. This tour should be really be done only if you have a driver as otherwise it is very very hot! Remember to dress appropriately; long sleeves and perhaps in white too as the pilgrims do. This is all sacred land for the Buddhists.

title: Simple yet cool to see...

title: nice pool in the temple
text: in the middle of buddha temple u find this pool, our tour guide was excellent, preferable to visit either early morning or afternoon because the weather is warm and you are barefoot so the ground is extremely hot

text: As I said at my previous comment, anuradhapura is very big. When you visit there you are giving 25 USD. But one day is also not enough to visit this attraction. title: Just ok...

title: History

title: Interesting

title: Kuttam Pokuna (Twin ponds/pools)
text: The pair of pools were built by the Sinhalese in the ancient kingdom of Anuradhapura. These are considered as one of the significant achievements in the field of hydrological engineering and outstanding architectural and artistic creations of the ancient Sinhalese

title: ONE OF THE MANY BATHS/PONDS OF THE CULTURAL TRIANGLE
text: Two ponds, well conserved, located in the Northern part of the Anuradhapura site. One is 40m length and the smallest 28m.

title: Nothing very significant
text: There are 2 ponds of average size which were used by the monks for bathing.Having seen a lot of ponds in historical areas with much more stone carvings or much bigger, I did not feel any thing very significant. But I suppose the Anuradhapura area ticket covers this as well.

title: Quite impressive
text: The baths are mostly intact, unlike other ruined buildings on the site. Worth seeing. But not much to do other than walk around them. There are a few stalls selling tourist tat.

title: Engineering expertise
text: Comparisons can be odious but as a layman I would venture to suggest that the Romans were more advanced than the Sinhalese. Nonetheless this is a great engineering achievement given that it was built around AD600. It was tranquil and interesting. Worth a look.

title: Attractive and inspring
text: These beautifully designed twin pools were serene when we visited in the mid afternoon. There were only two other tourists apart from our group. It was interesting to hear how the original inhabitants developed a water cascading system. This site is in good condition.

title: Kids will like this place
text: These twin tanks hold a lot of fish and tourists can feed. Kids will enjoy. This is a photo spot. This is one of the few spots in Anuradhapura that does not have an entry fee.

title: Great
text: Its a nice piece of architecture which depicts how good the Sri Lankans were back in the day at designing.This is just near all other major monuments and sacred places.

title: Excellent Condition, beautiful.
text: In lovely condition evidently the Queen entered from the far end pond and the King nearer the road ornate reliefs at either end some local souvenir and drink stalls around.

title: Wonderful historic and artistic feature
text: The Kuttam Pokuna or twin baths are one of our favourite features of the many historic sites in Anuradhapura. The two pools were constructed by the Sinhalese for bathing purposes and are an outstanding achievement in terms of hydrological engineering of the time. Not only are they of archaeological and scientific interest but they are also a wonderful artistic feature. They have flights of steps leading down to the water which are decorate with scrolls and other artistic features. One can stand peacefully enjoying the tranquillity of the pools today whilst imagining Monks bathing in ancient times.

title: a scenic paysage
text: It is very good to have water space in a monastery complex, it is a solid stone building, but not a beauty.

title: A piece of historic Sri Lankan engineering ingenuity
text: Anuradhapura is one of the most historic towns in Sri Lanka and history goes back to 11th Century AD. “Kuttam Pokuna” is one of the historic monuments in this city, but there are so many other monuments surrounding this as well. “Kuttam” means pair (two) & “Pokuna” means pond in native Sinhala language, so you will see two identical ponds opposite each other. As per the history, one pond (pool) is for the king & other one is for the queen, but not sure about accuracy of that data. If you love history and Pyramids, Anuradhapura is one the similar places to visit – but please make sure you do your research first, if not you might not enjoy it.

title: Reflects great Sri Lankan engineering hisotry
text: This is one of the Ancient swimming pools which depict capabilities of ancient engineers in Sri Lanka. It is made out of Granite with intricate carvings which will tells us how good was the technical know how of Sri Lankan craftmen. Kuttam Pokuna means Twin ponds. Build during King Agbo (575-608) period. May have been used by Monks. Great hydraulic marvels that must be visited by any one visitng Sri Lanka.

title: see this as part of your local sightseeing

title: Beautiful granite faced ancient bathing pools

title: Impressive water management and carefully restored to original form

Our guide advised us that they were definitely not built for the pleasures of swimming as fun and recreation was denied the monks . Pity, really - they look well worth a cooling dip...

title: By itself not worth the trip
text: Like most things on the Anuradhapura circuit, by themselves they are fairly boring, but adding the total of all sights makes it worth the trip. Yeah, the baths are old, but they have rubbish in them and basically are a stepped swimming pool with stagnant water.

title: interesting ancient engineering

A number of market stalls adjacent and one or two beggars in the area. Public toilets (rare occurrence in Anuradhapura) 50 metres away and whilst not luxurious are usable for 20 rupees. Not a must do but worth stopping if passing.

title: unbelivable

title: not so good

title: Part of general Anaradhupura entrance
text: It seems odd that each site within Anaradhupura has it's own review here. As this was my favourite part of Anaradhupura I thought I would allocate my review to the Kuttampokuna (twin baths). The quietness of the baths, amazing intricate nature of their design and proxinity to a very good and inexpensive small place to eat draws me to them. Also, their resident turtle was friendly and an attraction in himself. I thought that given the size of Anaradhapura a driver or in our case cycles are a necessity. I estimate we cycle about 12-15km but saw only two thirds of the area. Sign posts are lacking and it is easy to miss certain sites within the area. There is so much to see in this ancient city that it is another must see place while in this part of Sri Lanka. Anaradhapura is let down by lack of sign posts and seeming lack of reinvestment of the tourist dollar.

title: Amazing
text: They are really beautiful, not exactly the same size, even if called twin pools. Nowadays I wouldn't put a foot in, the water doesn't look clean enough for an European. But you can imagine how it must have been.

title: Pretty and quiet
text: What strikes out is these twin ponds are ancient. The multi-headed naag at the end of one of them impressive and really hard to photograph. There is an interesting system of silt chambers to collect all silt from the water before it enters the ponds

title: Still worth a visit
text: The twin baths are yet another testament to the once upon a time grandeur of one of Sri Lanka's native kingdoms. I have to admit that before visiting Anuradhapura, I was not aware that Sri Lanka had such a long and rich history, that it had a civilization that was complex and advanced enough to rival that anywhere else. The whole time I was staring at the twin baths, I kept thinking "How could the people have afforded to build these back then? Where was the source of their wealth?" The twin baths, after all, are very big, especially for just two people. It can thus be looked at as either a symbol of wealth and power and/or waste and frivolous spending. Regardless, the twin baths are definitely worth a look, simply because they are so well preserved, even after a thousand years, unlike many of the other relics in and around Anuradhapura. Just be careful not to fall in! The water is indeed very green!

title: Bath place of king

title: Nice walk
text: A relaxing stroll in the park kind of setting. The trees shield the site from the sun so it's nice and cool to walk through. When we visited, not a lot of tourists were there, a picnic under the trees by the twin baths should be nice!

title: Must see at Anuradhapura

title: They were doing this well before the Romans

title: Interesting spot

title: Uninspiring

title: Not a place to swim!

title: Beautiful symmetry

title: Worth a look.

title: Really interesting
text: We had a fab guide who was really knowledgeable and was able to give us loads of information, plus point out the most interesting carving etc.

title: Part of the site, worth a visit
text: Like other reviews i say many of the key sites at Anuradhapura. For the temples you will need respectful clothing. It was really hot visiting the site so when not in temple wear a hat have sunscreen and lots of water.

title: Good visit
text: I did all the temples in one day, they’re all very beautiful and worth a visit. Enjoy Anuradhapura! Take respectful clothing, water and sun screen.

title: Kings Bath

title: Beautiful
text: This was definitely one of our highlights of Anuradhapura. Having seen many temples around Sri Lanka we were a bit exhausted. This is a beautiful, quiet place to sit and reflect a while.

title: Vacation
text: Very old pools which are feed from underground means. Rebuilt years ago but are beautiful to see. People feed the fish in the pools. Very photographic.

title: Grab a fresh coconut to drink here
text: Just away from the mighty temples of Anuradhapura, are the twin baths of the monks of old. Watch out for thieving monkeys here and admire the craftsmanship of these magnificent baths. After a very hot and tiring visit to the oldest temples of Anuradhapura, a fresh shell of coconut juice was most welcome and we sat sipping the delightful drink just adjacent to these baths. It's an area of great peace and beauty and a welcome haven from the busy main tourist drag; well worth a visit at the chance to explore your inner self!

title: Well preserved

title: Good for resting

title: Pleasant

title: Twin ponds, but not exactly twins

title: A large area with archeological digs
text: This bath area has been discovered in the dig-for older and younger monks who lived in the temple. Interesting to see and imagine their way of life

title: bathing ponds

title: well preserved

title: Take a small scoop of water which they’d then drop on your head and in your mouth
text: From my Blog: A quick ride from Abhayagiri was Kuttam Pokuna, two baths which lay on the side of the road and are flanked by yet another shanty market. Though the baths themselves are not the most impressive bodies of water you can view, it was a rare experience to see the spiritual power these baths had over those more devout than I... As I sat next to the pools, a line began to form at the top of the steps leading down to the bath. One by one, people began to descend down to the water and take a small scoop of water which they’d then drop on their head and put a few drops in their mouth’s. Though I’ve never been to India or witnessed the spirituality of pilgrims at the Ganges, I can only assume seeing these people at Kuttam Pokuna was as powerful as witnessing those at the banks of that storied river.

title: The baths of the Sinhalese kings...
text: Detailed and Interesting rock carving of the twin baths, even more interesting the engineering involved in supplying the water, back in the 8th century when the work was supposedly completed. Compared to the treasure troves of Dambulla and Pollonaruwa, to us, the royal twin baths are only marginally attractive and of interest...

title: Royal Bath
text: This is where the King and Queen bathe days gone by.The pond is well maintained. A very good place to take a photo.

title: Short stop of with intersting story.
text: The twin baths are worth stopping at. You'll see interesting architecture and, if with a guide, you'll get the history.

title: Best of stone work
text: Twin ponds is merely not an attractive set of ponds but a place where one can observe ancient water purification and desilting system, sending water column through scientifically designed set of stone containers. Steps give access to water at any level and platforms give access along the perimeter of the pond. Structure is all in stone and polished to give neatness while decorative ornaments adore the beauty of the construction. The floral vases (Pun kalasa) at the entrances to the two ponds differ in design. A five hooded Cobra image on the wall is extremely beautiful.

title: Pleasant Pools
text: These are two pleasant pols of water. Look out for the various birds that come when you are walking around the site. On one site are a range of stalls selling mainly tourist stuff. However, over the road is a shop that sells large bottles of coke at a good price. Good to cool down with on a hot day.

title: Part of Anuradhapura Ancient City ...

It is essential to hire a driver service while visiting Anuradhapura site since the attractions are located pretty far from one another. Nice place to stop over for 15-20 mins visit.

title: Show piece of ancient Sri Lankan engineering skills

title: Scenic stop off
text: Very scenic pair of ancient tanks. Part of the sacred city and included in the ticket price for that area

title: Visit only if you have the time
text: There are twin baths right next to each other. This is the only place you’ll find such a juxtaposition. That’s it.

title: ARCHITECTURAL GEM
text: The pools, made out of granite, were constructed around 500 A.D. They were for the use of the monks. Water entered one of the pools through the mouth of a makara, a mythical beast with the mouth of a crocodile, the body of a fish and the trunk of an elephant. Underground piping connected them. They are different sizes and depths.

title: Nice
text: Interesting when you see it and read the debrief at the site....nice for clicks as well...a different dimension to Anuradhapura

title: Nice pond but lame surroundings
text: That pond is nice especially the carved cobra, but the view is ruined by too many shops on one side.

title: Huge baths

title: Ancient city historical monuments
text: This old structure will reveal the engineering g expertise of ancient Sinhalese and the well established monastic tradition which contributed to the spiritual and natural well beingof the people.

title: Great engineering
text: Worth the visit on your tour of sacred places and ruins. The twin bath are in very good condition and maintained by the department of archeology. The. Water filtering system is also interesting and certainly very clever for the time. I’d advise to get a historical guide for the day. We found ours by the main Tourist Ticket Office next to the Archeology Museum ( Museum is closed every Tuesday!). Our guide cost us 3000LKR for the day (4 hours). He took us to all the interesting areas of the ruins. We would have never seen all this and got the history of the site without him. He also communicated with our driver so we were driven and picked up in all the right places. One last advice, at the end of the day, keep your tourist ticket. Do not give it back. And we could visit an extra site with our driver.

title: Visit to the ponds of the monks

title: Twin ponds/ baths

title: Okay
