title: Very worthwhile visiting
text: Having seen the smaller royal bath in the ancient city of Polonnaruwa, I was quite impressed by this older twin bath in Anuradhapura. Massive granite slabs, an underground duct with filtering system to bring water to the pool and the decorations around the massive pools was very interesting. It's very grand. Once again having a driver/guide drive you around this massive ancient site on an always hot or hotter day made it more enjoyable. This area was not as shaded as the pond area in Polonnaruwa so be prepared for the searing heat of the sun.

title: Well preserved
text: These are baths constructed in the eighth century and used by the monks for their ritual ablutions. They are quite well preserved considering their age.

title: Shame about the rubbish
text: Beautiful and proportionate stone carvings built by ancient Sinhala rulers. Twin Baths illustrates history of the class system. Both the ponds which are different in size need a fair bit of cleaning up as it is quite polluted and smelly.

title: beautiful
text: with huge hungry fish in the ponds. Very picturesque. Go early, it gets really hot and sunny later. I liked the Queen's pond a bit better, honestly.

title: Spot the difference !
text: The bathing spots for the monks. One side for the senior monks, the other for the main class. Interesting irrigation system to provide a foot bath around the two baths when it was functional. A nice stop on your tour of the city. Still pretty complete, compared to other complex sights.

title: Architecturally, It is amazing!!!
text: This is really one of the best constructions made by Ancient Sri Lankans, It will be really good the government put some funds to clean these two ponds a bit.

title: Great photo opp, but BEWARE of the "salesmen"
text: Best advice: buy some stale popcorn from the kiosks to feed the fish. This makes for a great photo opportunity. Also, beware of pushy salesmen who WILL follow you to your car.

title: Fascinating
text: Given the age of these two baths, you have to wonder at the engineering and skills of water management these people possessed. Spot lots of fish and the occasional turtle too!

title: Smelly and polluted
text: It is quite amazing that these baths were built such a long time ago and the filtration system is quite ingenious. However the water was putrid, lots of rubbish around, mangy looking dogs and a strong smell of cow manure did not endear this place to me.

title: Two Tubs
text: They have good architecture in the walls, and a history story, but after all, it's just two ponds for bathing.

title: 15 days in Sri Lanka
text: We visited the twin baths. Spent around 30 minutes there not much to see but the two pools where the king took a bath

title: Inside the Anuradhapura City
text: Twin Ponds are part of the city tour of Anuradhapura and of significance in the overall setup of the ancient city

title: Two ponds
text: Honestly, nothing much to see or do apart from two rather unexciting ponds. A quick glimpse from the car may be suffice. Sorry, there are tons of other things in this complex of much greater interest.

title: Beautiful ancient baths - shame about the litter
text: We visited the baths as part of our independent tour of Anuradhapura. We'd recommend visiting when you haven't purchased an extortionate - $25 entrance ticket for the day - as it isn't required for this site. The baths are architecturally impressive and worthy of some photographs - so long as you can avoid the litter - which is such a shame.

title: Awesome reminder of ancient Sri Lankan architecture and engineering
text: The twin ponds are said to have served as swimming baths for Buddhist monks in the monastery attached to the Abhayagiriya Dagoba. The two pond are actually different in size. The water flows in to one and then to the other through a complex irrigation system. The northern one is about 40m in length and the southern about 28m. It is possible to see all the ancient sites in Anuradhapura in one day.

title: Monks only bathing
text: Lovely peaceful place and beautifully constructed baths with water that comes from a spring below and only monks can bathe in them.j

title: Impressive
text: This pools are beautiful, have a great ancient architectural work ad nice details. It’s amazing what people could achieve 2000 years ago. Now I wouldn’t like to bathe in the pool because it’s full of rubbish (in and next to it) and the water is green. If authorities will take some time to clean this place it would be fantastic.

title: Not for the monks
text: The fascination with baths is interesting with a view to the fact that none of them was for the monks as that would have been a fun experience which was forbidden per se. This said, the structure is impressive in size and comes along the way from one sacred site to another. You cannot miss it, but it is not a must.

title: Not so special
text: The history and story of this place is so intersting. But the monument and bath are average. The cost for this park is not so cheap. It includes pollunarawura entrance.

title: Very pretty site
text: It was beautiful to see this site. It is maintained well and is quaint and hidden as compared to the rest of the sites in Anuradhapura. Its an architecture delight!

title: Shame one cannot bathe here now!
text: It must have been an impressive city in ancient times. Lots of interesting ruins around here. Best explored by bike early in the day.

title: Photo lovers spot
text: The twin bath is located a little away from the other main tourist spots of Anuradhapura . But is a beautiful place to to. It's filled up with water during the rainy time. A good spot of photo lovers

title: The engineering makes this a worthwhile stop
text: This is one of a number of sites in the ancient city of Anuaradhapura. It is worth a stop to admire the engineering and wonder how 15 000 monks bathed in them. It's a shame that they are not maintained with fresh water and what water is in them is algae filled rain water. It's worth remembering all of these historical sites only reopened in 2009 after the civil war and this is a site that will be interesting to see what happens as the tourism market grows.

title: Twin Baths
text: Beautiful place to take some photos with some different ruins and sculptures. Lots of fish in the water you can feed.

title: Nothing spectacular!
text: This review is quite late. When visiting the Sacred City of Anuradhapura the Twin Baths will definitely be included in your itinerary. Both ponds were full of garbarge; I wonder if any maintenance is being carried out by the local government. I spent only a couple of minutes taking photos.

title: Ancient hydraulics
text: Fascinating example of ancient engineering. The water to fill these tanks was brought for a lake miles away. An ancient type of sluice gate stopped the water long enough to drop suspended sediment before it entered the tanks. Its a shame it is not more carefully tended today. Both tanks have accumulated trash floating on their surfaces, marring what otherwise is a grand vision.

title: Worthy of a quick photo stop
text: These "twin" swimming-pool-like ponds are worthy of a quick photo stop. Our guide told us that they were likely used by monks at the monastery attached to Abhayagiri Dagoba.They are not identical, however.

title: Beautiful

title: Interesting symmetry and ingenious water drainage system
text: Interesting symmetrical structure of historic value; clean, large and worth a visit if on the way. Find out how water is captured and fed into the baths!

title: Interesting engineering and history
text: We visited this as part of a tour of Anuradhapura with a guide. The engineering involved to fill the baths was impressive, as was the filter to remove sediment as the water flowed in. Simple and ingenious. Worth a 10 minute stop as part of a tour of the area.

title: Beautiful baths!
text: The twin baths have beautiful stone carvings. The engineering is impressive - reminded me of the Romans. They're in great condition. A lovely, peaceful place.

title: Nice 2 ponds.

title: Interesting to see

title: Amazing cultural site

title: Marvelous Ancient Bathing Ponds
text: Kuttam Pakuna (Twin Ponds) Kuttam Pakuna (Twin Ponds) are two bathing tanks built in the middle of a garden in 6th century AD by King Aggabodhi for the monks and students, as part of Abhayagiri Monastery Complex in sacred city of Anuradhapura. It reflects wonderful skills possessed by the Sri Lankans 2000 years ago in architectural engineering and hydrological technology. Both ponds are 51 feet wide and laid down in a row. The larger one is 132 feet long and 17 feet deep while the smaller one is 91 feet long and 14 feet deep. Underground tunnels were built to fill and empty the ponds.

title: 2000 Years old Water Storage
text: What a surprise... two thousand years old water storage... still entact... and appealing... a must visit for history lovers

title: Nothing exceptional
text: As in India we have lots of these types of ponds we were not impressed by the structure. You may stop for a short photo stop but nothing to keep you interested for long.

title: An architectural master piece.

title: Interesting, but nothing spectacular
text: Let me first preface by saying Anuradhapura, of the "cultural triangle" sites, is the most out of the way, and least worth your while as a result. I would only recommend it if you were staying in Sri Lanka over 10 days or if you are a big historical/cultural buff. The ruins at Polonuwara and Sigiriya are more impressive. The baths themselves are worth about 5-10 minutes of your time, hardly worth the amount of time taken just to get there, especially if you are using a bicycle or public transport. They are, after all, the ruins of two baths (enter drumroll...). The surrounding area is decidedly not tourist friendly, unless you prefer that look. There are filthy (and closed at the time of my visit) bathroom facilities, a small shack selling a drink across the road, and lots of cows wandering about. The area around was muddy (since it had rained recently), and the pools are not closed off. Good as it preserves a better "look", but bad if you have small children. I would recommend only at the tail end of a visit to Anuradhapura, which itself I would only recommend as a bottom tier attraction within Sri Lanka. The exorbitant entrance fees alone make you almost obligated to enter.

title: Interesting and enjoyable, but feel sorry for the workers
text: You can't visit Sri Lanka without going to see a Tea Plantation, right ?! So we were really pleased that our trip included a stop over here. Obviously there are lots of tea factories all over Sri Lanka, and we only visited this one, so cannot compare to any others, but I assume they are all very similar. The tour takes you round the tea processing factory, as they explain the various stages of processing and different types of tea, and includes a cup of tea afterwards in the nice looking restaurant. There is also the obligatory shop to purchase the vast number of teas from, much of which seemed a little high in price considering they made it on the premises (?). The teas in the fancy packaging seemed quite expensive and we felt it was a bit of a tourist rip-off, so we bought some of the cheaper variety to take home as a souvenir ! The whole thing took approximately one hour, which is just about right. I was a bit disappointed that this didn't include a tour of the actual tea fields which surround and rise up into the hills around the tea factory. However.... If you ask nicely then the tour guide will let you take a sneaky detour round the back into the plantation fields, where you can take photos of the tea and also some of the tea pickers - who will gladly pose for the photos if you give them some Sri Lanken Rupees (LRK) tips ! Whilst we enjoyed the experience, we felt saddened and astonished when we saw and found out about the quality of life and working conditions the workers were still enduring in the 21st Century. None of them seemed to have any protective equipment, ear defenders, goggles, hard hats... despite working around noisy, fast moving and potentially dangerous looking machinery. Many of them were not even wearing shoes !!!! Apparently the tea pickers earn something like just 500 rupees, which is just over £2, per day. And in return for this, they get very hard and rough skin on their hands from picking the leaves all day. Not the best life to live, is it ?! So if you visit here and they do pose for photos, please be generous and give them a tip ! If just 2 tourists give them just £1 tip for some photos, then that doubles their daily wage !

title: Tea factory and plantation

title: Quality tea field experience
text: This is a great place. It’s in a beautiful setting, the factory surrounded by tea fields and when the sunshines, it looks fabulous. A great little tour of the factory – just the right length with the right amount of information - and then a complimentary cup of tea You can then browse the tea for sale in the shop without any pressure to buy. Of course, because there is no pressure and you take your time, you buy a lot more than if someone is looking over your shoulder all the time. A great place to stop en route from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya.

title: Good tea place on the way to nuwaraeliya
text: Nice and clean place to stop for a tea on the way to nuwaraeliya. I like the milk tea its hot and delicious. I went with my foriegn friends as they have a good quality tea shop. There are many varieties of tea available with a good price. If you like to go to see the tea factory just a walking distance. We were there abouy 30 minutes to get relax and to buy tea.

title: Interesting
text: An old British era tea factory. Since our visit was on the day after National, they didnt have fresh plucked leaves for processing. Only finishing section was working. You can get a free cup of black tea. You can also buy different varieties of teas which are sold in the outlet attached to it.

title: Tea garden
text: Very informative.must see enroute to Nuwara eliya.lot of tea plantations. Learnt about entire process, different types of teas .no entry fees. They offer complimentary tea 1 cup.the special teas green,gold,silver are chargeable. Theres also a shop to buy the different types of teas ,nicely packed as gifts .prices vary

title: Lovely
text: If visiting a tea factory then there is no better, good to see the tea making process and then to visit the on site tea room for tea and in our case we visited in afternoon so we had cake. Also bought a box of tea to bring home all at good prices. Very helpful staff

title: TEA TEA TEA
text: A great place to go and learn about tea . Black white & green . You start with a tour of the factory and learn about the process from picking all the way threw to packing for distribution. A very knowledgeable tour we learn a lot about tea. You are then of too the cafe for a free tea or samples (at a cost ) Then the gift shop for tea sales and purchase . A great hour or so whilst on the way thru . Definitely worth a stop in .

title: An insightful tour but rushed!
text: It was a friendly tour and a cup of tea given at the end but wouldn’t return here. Would prefer more of a personal experience and taken to see tea growing, more interactive exhibits to view in own time rather than being rushed through. We were paired with another family who were french and struggled to translate quickly enough so one lady walked off mid your after being told we had a time limit of 20 mins to get around the factory and see the whole tour. I think it was actually quicker than that! It was great to see machinery working and the factory workers. Wouldn’t liked to have a more personal experience, perhaps to do a bit of our own tea picking and the process ourselves- would be happy to pay more to do this.

title: How tea is produced
text: This is one of the few places where you are taken through the entire tea leaf making process free of charge. We were assigned a young guide Aushika who spoke good English and took us through the entire process. We learnt about the various types of tea. At the end of the tour we were asked to choose a tea that we’d like to taste at the tea room nearby. The BOPF tea was free but we had to pay to try the other tea which were reasonably priced. The chocolate cake was delicious.

title: Great tour and food
text: We were guided around by a lovely guide at no cost and sampled their tea at the cafe. You must try their pastries since they are fresh and exquisite. In comparison to the other tea factories I strongly recommend that you visit this ones

title: A proper working factory, interesting and varied items in shop
text: This was a great visit. In November, as low season, it was not at all busy and we had an interesting and informed guide. There is a very pleasant cafe and attractive, well stocked shop but maybe it is just me - I don't like being followed around by someone on my shoulder as I browse.

title: If you are here for Tea factory process, it's good. Tea plantation garden view is pretty average.
text: We came to visit Blue field just because our driver said it's one of the few places where they don't charge an entrance fee and explain the process well (though you are expected to pay a few hundreds of rupees as tips). We met our guide who knows a few Chinese and explained the process pretty clearly, though the whole visit lasted no longer than 15min. They then take you to a tea tasting section which you can enjoy a free cup of BOPF (kind of 2nd-but-last grade for tea bags. Noted we we to Damro later for tea and they claimed to use BOP which is 1 grade higher). The price of tea there is indeed 3 times more than what you can find in the supermarket or central markets (like in Nuwara Eliya and Kandy). Strangely they will tell you within the same grade the tea inside the packages are the same, but prices do varies a lot with different packages... What I learnt is that bigger brands like Lipton, Dimah, Mackswood are all sourcing teas from this tea garden partially so you can say what you buy out in the market also have no big difference in quality. What we don't really like about the place though, is the garden. We took a walk around and 1 old man approached us with a bunch of freshly picked tea leaves. Right next to him was another woman. They were not actually working, no sack no tools... They just ask you to take pictures of them and expect you to pay. Worst of all, after we gave them each 20Rs they are not happy with the amount and asked for more. If you really want to see the working tea puckers go to Pedro or Damro where you have better views and real puckers. Maybe because nowadays fewer people visit Pedro , I found the tea puckers so much more authentic and friendly than this one. They don't ask for tips. And when they receive some, I can see the real appreciation in their eyes. We ended up shooting nothing of the tea puckers in BlueField. Maybe also ask your guide or driver to see if they know that which parts of gardens have finished tea picking.

title: Simply Tea
text: Its all about knowing how tea is made. They have 100 year old equipment, robust time tested process & limited modernisation to give out great tea. A must place for tea lovers : Green, black, flavoured, white : you name it. Accepts all major cards. The Lunch organised by our tour Operator - Veena World was also of good quality.

title: Family vacation
text: The tea factory was closed when we visited so could not see the functioning But the guide gave us a tour nevertheless Had complimentary tea which was yummy Go for it

title: Very interesting
text: Well, I never realised what went into making a cup of tea! A very worthwhile hour spent visiting the factory and learning the various processes, followed by a much appreciated tasting. Beautiful terraces of tea bushes - the surrounding countryside is stunning.

title: Blue Fields Tea
text: Nice cool place. Informative tour of tea process n a nice place to chill for tea n some cakes. Food available at 2nd level. Prayer place available for Muslims. Finally the highlight, shopping for various kind of teas from healthy white tea to fruity flavored teas.

title: Ordinary
text: The tour may be more interesting during an actual workday but we visited on Sunday. Still, one problem with tours lies with their organization--considering the small space with multiple groups and the resulting verbal competition of their guides. I have experienced better presentations at other plantations.

title: Very informative and good views
text: The guide for The tea factory Mr. Abdullah was very good and proficient. He covered all the details related to tea processing Later we took some snaps of spectacular views from tea estate On return they provide a complementary black tea and restaurant is good with few simple eateries Overall a not to be missed experience

title: Something new... tea picking on your own
text: 100% run an managed by women... great!! Tip: go into the fields and pick some tea on your own. Just ask your guide, it‘s fun!!

title: Interesting tea tour
text: We did a brief tea tour here in October 2018. It was very interesting seeing how tea is made, and what's involved. Staff were very friendly.

title: Tea Factory
text: The property is spread in acres. Janu, our tour guide showed us around well. She explained well in English. The tea was delicious. The ambience of the restaurant and cozy private shacks were welcoming. They had olden style machines in display and some of the active machinery were still operational since the inception of the factory.

title: Great cafe and tea gift shop
text: Enjoyed our visit here and the tour of the process we received. The gift shop is extensive and allows you to get your gifts for your return home. The staff are warm and welcoming and the cafe very good. A nice place to visit.

title: Auto pilot visitor handling
text: Maybe we just ran into a bad guide, but this was very uninspiring. I think even a audio cassette could impress me more. Also, when taking a look at the tea garden.. You get swamped by old ladies asking for money (for a picture) and not willing you to take any pictures without them on it. Really looked forward to see this interesting site but it all resulted in pretty much a deception. To improve: get those ladies out of the garden and organize paid tours and make it worth the money.

title: One of the best
text: Worthwhile visiting. Variety of tea leaves. The whole process of tea making is marvellous, efficient and perfectly carried out. Our guide Ms. Prasadi is one of the best guides they can ever hire. She was so genuine, polite, respectful and her explanation was crystal clear. The tea gift shop is excellent. The tea plantation view is wonderful.

title: Paradise of Greenery
text: On our way from Kandy, we dropped by Bluefields. Upon reaching the estate we went to the tea fields behind the factory, where the tea pickers were working. P.S: You will find tea pickers requesting for a a photograph/video & then asking for donation. Paying them is an individual choice & is not compulsory. At the tea factory we were greeted by our guide, Dinusha Maduwanthi. She was superb at her job! She took us around the factory, while giving us an insight to the tea making process. Dinusha then walked us through the plantations. For city dwellers like ourselves, this was a totally different experience! Post the tour, visitors are treated to free tea. P. S. only the black tea is free. I tried the Silvertips Tea, which they refer to as "White Tea". Unfortunately it didn't taste any different, from regular tea & was not worth LKR 180. Otherwise our visit at Bluefields was lovely! Entry Fee: Nil Best time to visit: Morning - as you get a chance to see the tea pickers work P. S. Wear sport shoes

title: Good, yet not for the dedicated tea drinkers
text: Efficient quick and painless. Quick overview of the process, the mearly 100 years old processing machines are impressive and still operate well. It is a co-operative mainly producing white label for big brands. Simple plain experience. In case you are a serious tea person select another estate.

title: Informative
text: First appearances are that the site is a bit tired looking but we were greeted by our guide called Razar. He was obviously very passionate about the factory and how it’s still running unchanged since it was first opened nearly 100 years ago. He took us through the full process of how tea is made from the plucking to the fermentation and end product. There are better tea factories to visit in the area but our driver recommended it to us on our way to our next destination. A nice enough stop off for a free cuppa...we’ll nearly free ??

title: Interesting tour in nice surroundings. Tasty tea!
text: Stopped off here on our way from Kandy to Ella. We arrived on a Sunday when the factory wasn't active but still got an informative, free tour from a very helpful guide (tip recommended). After the tour we received a free cup on Blue Field tea, and bought some cake to go with it. At no point were we pressured into buying anything, but decided to pick up some tea from their shop, which we thought was quite good value. After our tea and cakes, we wandered around the tea fields behind the factory, where we were again provided with a free guided walk by one of the tea pickers. A nice experience, and worth a visit.

title: Very informative trip
text: Our driver recommend a stop here over the other tea plantations, and for what it was worth, he made a good choice. Unfortunately for us, we visited the tea factory on the weekend of "poga" which is a buddhist/hindu holiday so the factory was not functional that weekend. However, our guide was extremely knowledgeable and informative, who took time to understand and answer any questions we had about the tea and the tea making process. The tour then ended by us being offered a cup of tea for free to try - any cake/pastry purchase is optional and at no point did our guide try to make a sale. The tea shop beside the restaurant was being mobbed by everyone who visited and us as well. Now that we are home and i've tried their teas, I can definitely say that the tea tastes divine. Do stop by to learn and sample a cuppa.

title: Worth the visit
text: We dropped into Bluefield tea gardens on our way to Ella from Kandy. We ended up having lunch at their buffet - I think it was towards the end of their service, so some of the dishes may have suffered a little from being out for a while. It was adequate but certainly nothing to write home about. It was free for our driver. We got an informative tour of the tea factory and learnt a lot from our very informative guide Razaq. I kind of did not realise green tea was just a different harvested leaf from which black tea was from. In their tea cafe we tied their most prized type of tea - a white tea called ‘golden tips’ - I had never had this before but it is from the very young leaf buds of the the tea tree. It was so good we ended up buying 4 tins in their shop to take home with us! A new taste experience which we were excited about. The factory is one of the more traditional types and well worth the visit.

title: Worthwhile stop
text: We made a pit stop to the Blue Field Tea Gardens on our way to Kandy. Our guide Adhil gave us a quick, yet detailed tour of the factory and explained the intricate tea making process. We got to taste the different varieties of delicious tea and explore the gift shop. Definitely recommend!

title: Old school tea plantations visit
text: We had a lovely tour around the plantation and factory. Very educational and we purchased some of the expensive tea because it seemed very nice quality and all hand made.

title: Great tour & delicious teas.
text: It was great to learn about the tea plantations in Sri Lanka. Your staff are very knowledgeable and friendly. Muhammad answered all of our questions. You have a great range of teas for a good price at your gift shop and I loved exploring the factory and seeing how the tea is processed. Thank you

title: One of the old tea factories on the road to Nuwara Eliya
text: The visit to the tea factory is very artificial, the demonstrator didn't had any passion, he was also not aware of many things that we asked him.

title: Amazing tour and tasty tea
text: Great tour around the tea factory - very interesting. Afternoon tea was served and tasty cakes!! We bought several packets of tea to bring home.

title: One of the best Tea Brand
text: This is one of the best brand. They show us how the Tea is manufactured. We can buy tea ...we are given tea for tasting also. OPA is the best....

title: Very nice factory
text: Nice factory with very friendly staff. Short introduction about the tea process and small tea tasting at the end. Recommended.

title: Free factory visit and complementary tea
text: We stopped here on a tuk tuk tour out of Nuwara Eliya. The tour of the tea factory was very good showing all the stages of the processes to make tea. The chap was very knowledgeable and answered all of our questions. We then were shown to the tea room and given a complementary cup of BOP tea. There is cake also on offer. The shop was rammed with chinese tourists buying up loads of tea. Funny to see as you would almost think they can’t get it there! You have to pay extra to do a tea tasting. Toilets were clean.

title: Interesting Visit
text: I have been to other tea estates/factories, but the tour here was the best; instructional and interesting, learning about the different grades of tea. Topped off with a nice cup of tea and the opportunity to buy tea to take back home

title: Great setting good tour
text: Lovely tour with enthusiastic guide. Photos allowed. Lovely seating outdoors to sample the tea. Would recommend.

title: Interesting insight into how tea is processed
text: Interesting tour of the processing plant to see the different stages that the leaves of tea go through in order to be tea leaves! Don't think the process or the machines have changed in donkeys years. Good explanation of the different teas they produce, followed by a complimentary cup of tea! Worth visiting

title: A nice place to Have a Break on the way To Nuwaraliya
text: On the Way To Nuwaraliya From Kandy, We Stopped here for a Break This Place has Different types of Tea and Fresh tea with Fresh Smell. The restaurant offers some Good food as Well, But more than the food a Piece of Cake and fresh Tea would make the day

title: Interesting but not the best tour
text: The tour in the bluefield tea gardens was all right but not as good as other tours I’ve done in Sri Lanka. Their tea is very good though and I recommend you taste their chocolate cake.

title: Ideal tea visit
text: We were not set on any single tea plantation and went to this one at the recommendation of the driver who had picked us up at the train station. A free cup of tea is given before or after your tour, and the factory is small enough that you can get pretty close to the equipment and really understand the process. You can walk the fields behind the factory too, and there is an AMAZING view of the valley if you make it over the first hill.

title: Good stopover
text: This place is good to stop over when you are travelling from or to Kandy. Worth of doing a tour and pure tea

title: Lovely tour and tea!
text: We had a great tour of the factory, just the right length for us and the kids. Interesting learning about the different teas and how they are produced. We saw most of the machinery working, our tour was in the morning. We bought quite a bit of tea in the shop, thought the price was fine. The cafe was great with lovely free tea and reasonably priced silver tip tea. The cakes and samosas were superb and the staff were all very friendly

title: A good place to stop
text: We got a tour of the tea factory which was educational. There is a restaurant and gift shop. The food in the restaurant was inexpensive and generous portions.

title: Nice place to enjoy a cup of Tea
text: Definitely one of my tops 5 things to do in Sri-Lanka. We have enjoyed our visit to the factory and learning so much thing regarding the history of tea. As a Tea lover is was nice seeing and learning about the process of creation, not forgetting all Womens and mans hands behind the process, because it’s not something easy. Please don’t forget to be respectful and nice with those hard-working people ( a tip will be much appreciated )s

title: Nice place for a break
text: You will see this place on the way to Nuwara-Eliya, so it is a good place to take a break from the long drive. They have a nice restaurant with delicious food and clean washrooms.

title: Tea tasting in cafe.
text: As we had already done a plantation tour elsewhere we just went to the cafe. It was lovely sitting out in the garden enjoying tea and cake. I ordered a tea tasting session, 600rs for about 10 different full cups of tea. It gives you a chance to work out which ones you actually like. The tea in the shop is expensive ($35aud for 500g of orange pokoe - can buy it in Australia for $18 per kilo). Come here to taste all varieties of tea, but buy tea's elsewhere.

title: Short but informative tour
text: The tour was just the right length for me - brief but informative. Despite the signs prohibiting photography, I was allowed to take photos. Be aware though, that as soon as I snapped a pic including one of the factory ladies, the hands came out for donations - oops. At the end of the tour I was dropped off at the cafe/gift shop for a free cup of lower grade tea. Higher grade teas are available for a reasonable fee. No pressure, no sales pitch.

title: Definitely worth a visit
text: Informative free tour. Can wander the tea plantations afterwards on own. Couldn't find any tea pickers in the plantation when we went. Complimentary tea - tried the strongest tea (Dust No 1), which was a great cuppa. Great and cheap cakes in the tea shop.

title: Just a side of tea education
text: The bluefield tea factory is on the way towards the hotel which we chose in Nuwara Eliya. On arrival there a tour guide gives you a very small talk around the factory and then you get a complimentary tea to taste. Also there is a plantation for you to have a look at and walk through. They do explain well the tea process and also the grading of the tea. There is also a shop which you can buy the teas as well. However do have a look at the pricing in some cases for a little bit more money you get much more tea. Also the gift sets are a bit pricey. There is food available but where the food is there is also some flies there...

title: Great tour, great tea
text: My husband and I visited Bluefield as part of a day trip around Nuwara Eliya, and it was the highlight of the day. We started with a really informative tour of the tea factory itself, followed by a tea tasting. We could have had a free cup of tea each, but opted to pay a small amount (600 rupees, about £3) to try all the different types of tea - we were pleasantly surprised to find that this even included both types of the famous white tea, golden tips and silver tips (delicious!). We were so impressed that we bought quite a lot of tea in their shop - which was much more reasonably priced than the other tea factory we had visited earlier on that day. Altogether a great experience.

title: Amazing experience
text: It was a very interesting tour for us. This was the very first time I got to know about the tea plantation. Finally we know the process, it was very educational. We went to the around the factory with a really knowledgeable guide. It was actually exciting to study how the tea is made. There is small restaurant inside the factory our friend Ilham bought some cakes for us and waiter gave a free plan-tea for us. There are many of tea estates and tea factories on the way to Nuwara-eliya but our tour guide and our friend Mr.Ilham Rameez recommend this place absolutely it’s an amazing experience in my life .At the end we would like to thank everyone.

title: Tea estates...
text: Nuwara eliya weather is apt for tea farming and you will find many tea estates here. Great to view how they make tea

title: The Tea Factory
text: We had a personalized tour of the Tea Factory and how it operates and this was recommended to us by our driver. It was a very interesting tour for all of us. This was the very first time i got to know and all these days i was wondering how tea is looking black in color while all plantations are fully green. Now that i know the process, it was very educational.

title: Not as good as Damro Tea Plantation
text: We first visited Damro and it was great. Great view, silver service tea (free) and tour of the working factory. BUT then we went to Blue Fields and were disappointed by the tea (we paid for) and poor service. Not recommended.

title: Great tour
text: We sampled the various tea and were shown around the factory with a really good guide. It was really interesting to learn how the tea is made and the different process to arrive at the various teas. We tipped the guide at the end.

title: Interesting tour
text: This was the first time we visited a tea factory and it was interesting to learn about the lengthy process to make tea. Our guide was excellent, no charge for the tour, but we gave our guide a small tip. We would have loved to go into the fields where they were picking leaves, but it was raining so didn't, so not sure this would usually be part of the your.

title: Where do we get our tea from
text: Fabulous experience visiting the tea plantations and seeing the lady tea “pluckers” in the fields working very hard for very little. Long days and minimal pay, but happy and polite and only too willing to let you have a photograph with them. They start work early and work until late and for this they get an approximate payment of £4/£5 per day. There is a minimum amount of tea leaves that have to be stored in their back packs in order for them to get paid. However, they do get cups of tea and have a short break.

title: have food will travel
text: I was not expecting much but the free guide of the oldest tea factory in Sri Lanka was actually very informative Seeing how they dry the leaves such a tedious process. all hand picked!! the tea tasing was also fun I hadn't rallied that all tea comes from the one plant cakes were ok but it was a nice thing to do in the heart of tea country

title: Informative but beware the tea pluckers and leaches.
text: An interesting insight into a working tea factory. It could be a really good tour. It is free but actually I would rather have paid something and got a tea tasting or something as well. The factory is dimly lit and has no real soul- very odd feeling inside. Shop is ok and plenty of stock. Be very careful if the tea ladies usher you out to the fields, they will let you take their picture but agressively demand money afterwards. This is awkward for you and if they are caught can be sacked so don't do it.

title: Good way to learn about tea
text: Situated around 20km outside Nuwara Eliya Bluefields Tea is well worth the drive to get there. You can have a free tour of the factory where you will learn about how tea is grown, harvested, and processed into the product tea drinkers know and love. At the end of the tour you can choose to have a free cup of tea. The shop has a lovely selection of cakes (you pay for these). The Tea Shop has quite a collection of different teas from the Estate for purchase for a reasonable amount - price varies depending on the type of tea you buy and how much. My biggest challenge was choosing. It takes 45 minutes to 1 hour to get there by Tuk Tuk - the road winds up and down hills and valleys. It's a picturesque drive - you can see tea plantations and workers; and spectacular scenery. Allow 2-3 hours, it's worth it.

title: Great Tea Estate to visit, tour and taste
text: Find out which is your favourite tea flavour. Great tour of the estate followed by tea tasting. I did a great shop of teas in the shop for my tea crazy family at home! Really enjoyed the visit. thank you Samantha

title: Good place
text: We went to Bluefield Tea Gardens on our way to Nuwara Eliya. As soon as we entered a representative took us to the factory and explained us the process of tea making, after which they served us a cup of black tea which was complimentary. You can also order from the coffee shop menu if you want anything else. They have a store where you can buy different types of tea. You can also visit the tea garden to take pictures, but unfortunately we were not able to go there as it was raining heavily.

title: good visit
text: would visit if in the area and after a genuine / old school experience. there are other factories in the area too

title: Watch how the tea is processed then have your quality cupp of tea
text: We stopped on our way to the Forest View Lodge at the Bluefield tea gardens.The Factory staff was courteous,informative and helped the members of our group to understand how tea is processed.The Tea pluckers pose with tourists.They earn a meager salary for many hours of hard work. The Tea was good quality.The staff at the sales outlet was knowledgeable and promoted the value of tea as a health drink.They have good PR skills..The best quality tea is out of this world

title: Must visit tea plantation in Nuwara Eliya!
text: We came across this beautiful tea plantation on our way to Kandy. We were walking to the entrance and were instantly greeted by a friendly tour guide, Mursheey. This was very different to our experience at Damro Tea, where we were waiting for about 20-30 minutes with no one acknowledging that we were there or anyone offering a guide. The tours here are free and the guides will take you around the whole factory providing information about the tea making process as well as history of the plantation. It was great! There was plenty of opportunities for photos and to ask questions. At the end of the tour, you are given a free black tea. There is no obligation to tip or pay any fee, we decided to tip our tour guide as he was excellent :) would definitely recommend this visit as part of your trip in Nuwara Eliya if you get an opportunity :)

title: Beautiful tea garden
text: This area is very clean. They provide a free tour how tea is manufactured. There is also a shop where you will find different kinds of teas. It can be tour of one to two hours mostly but do try the tea at the shop. It's one the of biggest tea supplier in Sri Lanka and I totally enjoyed the view, taste and beautiful landscape there

title: Tourist stop !!
text: Too many tourists, free tour is informative , geared towards selling tea after free tour. CafÃ© was okay. All staff quite friendly

title: Good for a quick visit
text: The factory was not operating when we visited as it was a holiday. The guide gave a good explanation of the process. You did not seem to be able to wander through the plantation. There was a children’s play area. The tea seemed rather expensive so we did not buy any although there were many different grades available. We had a cup of tea but it was not served in a pot and was rather too strong for our taste. There are cakes available to buy at the counter too.

title: Nice tour and shop
text: Nice tour of the tea processing facility with a knowledgeable guide who spoke very good English. Not so impressed with the way the guide said we could/should tip her afterwards then walked away as soon as she got some money. The free tea was not as good as I expected from a tea plantation, seemed to have been brewed too long. The shop was good - every kind of tea and no pressure to buy anything.

title: great visit
text: We had a tour of this tea factory and it was so interesting to see all the process the tea goes through to give us a good brew. The shop is good and has reasonably priced tea to take home

title: Very nice tea
text: Had about a 20 minute private tour around the tea factory where you get to see how tea goes from the plants in the plantations to the tea you drink - was great to see all the old machinery still being used as well. The lady that showed us round was very nice, spoke slow and very pronounced English which was easy to understand. I’m never sure how this kind of thing works regarding payment as it was part of the tour. I gave a 500 tip which seems fair to me, she seemed happy enough. We also got a free cup of tea each at the end, you can order more of different types but the one just to try was enough for us.

title: Highly Recommended
text: We came here instead of Mackwood (now rebranded) and had a fabulous time. Met by a guide, Adil, who showed us around the plantation and explained the process. We watched pickers, took loads of photos and were impressed by the scale and organisation of the place. Back in the factory, they let us gets hands on with loading of leaves into the various hoppers. If you take a pic of a person working, please do remember to give them some rupees, it’s only polite - 50 should do it! Loved the processing plant and tea sampling - came away from the shop with various ones to try at home. All in it took about 90 minutes and was not expensive. We tipped our guide 500 which our driver said was the going rate. Too Tip: Go early morning before the school tours come!

title: Good tour with no pestering on buying products
text: The best part is that they do not pester you to buy products from their store and all the while give you proper attention while giving a tour of the factory. The tour is short but detailed enough to know the nitty-gritty of the tea process.

title: Interesting but too short
text: It was very interesting and nice to see the when the factory was running. The "tour" was a bit too short and rushed (like 5 min). Our guide was nice but it sounded like a recorded text from a book. After the tour you get a free cup of tea. It's a nice visit of you stop by on the way but it's not worth a daytrip.

title: Short stop on our way
text: Stopped here on our way to Nuwara Eliya. Unfortunately for us it was a national holiday so there was no tea picking going on. We had a tour of the factory though which was still interesting and a cuppa in the cafe. Should really have gone back the following week when it was a normal working day as I imagine there would be more to see. The tour is free and the cafe is cheap. Should have bought more tea as well as it is so good and so much cheaper than home.

title: good tour and visit
text: we were offered a place on a tour as soon as we arrived. Our guide spoke in English and had a Chinese couple and Japanese couple in addition to us. He was very knowledgeable and spoke very clearly. Tour was 15 minutes and then we went into the cafe for a nice & cheap cup of tea from the various selections on offer. Then there is a tea shop to buy your choice of teas if you wish. No pressure to buy anything. An enjoyable break on the journey to Nuwara Eliya.

title: Now I know more about tea!
text: Interesting visit to a tea factory. I drink so much of the stuff that it’s nice to see how it’s produced. We saw the whole process and then were treated to a cuppa. As we drove away we saw the women working in the plantations. It was very interesting and a good photo opportunity.

title: Interesting free tour
text: I wasn't that keen but it actually was really interesting to see how it all works! We enjoyed tea and samosa afterwards. There's a great shop but no pressure to buy anything

title: Bluefield Tea Gardens Ramboda, Nuwara Eliya, Sri Lanka
text: The Blue Field Tea Garden cum Factory was establish in 1921 here we see the procedure of manufacture of tea in factory. We see various kind of tea and test one of them after we go to their outlet and purchase some Srilankan tea. The cost of tea was just double with Indian tea but the cost in Indian currency is near about same.

title: Learn about your cuppa
text: Stopped here on a tour of tea country and had a nice tour of the factory. Saw all the old machines, some almost 100 years old and still working. After the tour, went to the tasting room and had a nice BOP (gotta come here to learn what that is). I'm not a tea drinker, but I could be one if all the tea was good. No pressure to buy tea at the shop, they just left us on our own. I like that!

title: Fantastic and informative guided tour of tea facoty
text: My father and I stopped in to Blue Fielda Tea Gardens for a guided tour of the factory and to sample the tea that they produce. We were very impressed with Mirshad who was very knowledgable and communicated the process of how the tea was processed. We were able to talk through the factory and got to explore the tea fields as well. After the tour we had a tea tasting of the 2 white teas, 1 green tea and 6 black teas. Beautiful and highly recommend this experience! Victoria and Brett

title: Good Tea Tour
text: Good start on the types of tea , production, packaging then to the external tea terraces where you can mingle with the tea pickers. Avoid the around mid day as it can be hot. As usual there is a tea shop for you to you type of tea.

title: Interesting experience with some history
text: I’m not sure why, but all of he locals want to take you to one of the more modern plantations. We did blue fields and another. This one was by far the better tour and experience. It was working, with machines processing the leaves etc. There are others with better scenery... but the other one we visited was more like a tourist trap rather than a plantation.

title: Sri lanka hols
text: Went here today and was very happy with the tour, the guide, the little cafe and the tea shop. The grounds were lovely, well kept and so colourful. While this is not the biggest tea plantation in Nuwara Elia it is Sri Lankan owned and well worth the visit. Best of all there was no pressure to buy and no one hovered over you like we have experienced in other places.

title: Excellent overview of tea growing and production
text: I really enjoyed the hour here looking at the tea plantation and then being given a tour through the factory and seeing the process. Also learnt a lot about the types of tea produced in Sri Lanka and bought some tasty Orange Pekoe(OP) as a souvenir.

title: Good variety in tea store
text: We did not take the free garden/factory tour but we shopped at the tea store. It was very well attended by tourists, and the parking lot was quite full. Attendants advised and helped people buy tea. We were surprised that the cashier refused to take credit cards without giving us a reason. Perhaps the phone lines were unreliable due to the rains, but in any event we had to reduce the number of items and pay cash for our purchase. They have a good variety of teas, and the prices were competitive.

title: Excellent tour, highly informative
text: Our tour guide, Razar, was enthusiastic and knowledgeable! The factory was actually in operation when we visited so we could the machinery in action. Highly recommend - tea shop had reasonably priced teas and the tour comes with a complimentary cup of English breakfast tea. This was one of the highlights of the trip.

title: Impressive Factory but Expensive Tea Shop
text: We visited this factory located in beautiful hilly surroundings ,with manually operated machines in a 100 years old building and came out impressed with its focus on giving large employment to locals.They only process black tea here.The guide was a knowledgeable fellow,an employee of the factory. The tour was completed with a complimentary cup of tea offered in the cafe located beside the factory.The cafe is a bare minimum joint,having select food items. An adjoining factory shop was selling all kinds of tea processed by the company.They had all kinds of varieties of tea,some gift packed too. We purchased 200 grams boxes of masala chai flavored black tea at SriLankan Rupees 1600 each,which was expensive compared to buying beautifully packed 40 pcs Dilmah tea bags at Odel, Colombo for SLR 1100. Dilmah being a premium brand is a better gifting option at this price range. Most of the tea factory and estates follow the same business practice,and I would suggest to check other brands tea prices at local superstores before buying from these factory shops-they charge a premium for their teas.

title: Very informative
text: It was good to learn how much of work goes into that cup of tea you drink. Mohammed was our guide for the day and explained every bit of the process in detail. We were even given the opportunity to pluck some tea leaves. The whole tour was free including nice cup of tea at the end of it. You can buy cakes with your tea. And then your taken to a shop where you can purchase the different types of tea leaves and tea powders. They even have a restaurant there with traditional srilankan food

title: Nice tour
text: It’s been an interesting tour. Doesn’t take much time. The guide was proffesional and nice. We’ve visited several factories while in Sri Lanka and we found this one to have the best tea shop.

title: Interesting little tour
text: Came here in April with my partner and our three youngest children. Our guide was very friendly and knowledgeable and explained everything within the factory, giving a clear explanation of how the different teas were made and explaining each stage of production. We were allowed to take photos and we were also encouraged to help on the production line (which the children really enjoyed). At the end of the tour you are served with a cup of tea and you can have a browse in the tea shop (but you do not feel under pressure to buy anything - we did not make any purchases).

title: Very friendly
text: Very friendly guides who will show you around the factory and serve you with hot piping black tea. All of this is free and no cost. You can choose to buy tea from their store, but no compulsions. A must try place.

title: Enjoyable and education tour
text: We really enjoyed the tour to this tea factory. Very informative and a great experience for the whole family.

title: Good tour guide
text: We got a tour by Razaq. Friendly man who gave us a very good and clear explanation of the working process of producing tea. Afterwards we could taste the tea and buy some in the shop. Prices were very ok (paid around 500-600Rs for 200-250gr). There is no entry fee but tips are always accepted.

title: Great experience
text: It was an unforgettable experience, we learned very interesting information about the tea production process, the lady who was guiding us was very polite and informative, she made sure that everything we see in the factory is well explained and understood.

title: Place to know about how tea is made
text: This is on the way from Kandy to Newura Eliya and is a good place to stop over not only to stretch legs but also to learn during the stop over. We got a good insight into how the tea is produced and knowledge regarding different types of tea. It has a coffee shop where you get complimentary tea. There is a pastry shop where one can buy pastries. There is a shop where they sell different varieties of tea. No need to go there exclusively to see but can be used as a good stopover.

title: Educating tea tour
text: Take 15 min time to learn about the tea production and sip a cup of fresh tea. Free of charge, while the tea in the shop is definitely overrated. Well, these guys need to get the money somehow...

title: Tea is exorbitantly priced.
text: Nothing exciting about the tea estate. Tea is so highly priced that it is advisable to purchase in Colombo

title: Good place to learn more about the tea production
text: A good place to learn more about tea production. Every group / couple gets its onw guide who will tell you all about the tea production. Make sure you keep up, as the tour is very fast. Don't mind to ask them to explain again, as they do try to get you in & out within 10 minutes. There is no activity in the factory at Sundays. So it is best to visit an other day of the week. After the (free) tour, you get a free cup of tea. There is also a restaurant if you like. The tea shop has all kinds of tea from this estate. No one was pushing us to buy anything, so you can take the tour and tea for free.

title: Excellent tour without the tourist hype
text: Set in a beautiful location, there is no cost attached to the very professionally conducted, informative factory tour that including a cup of tea at the end. It also appeared to be less crowded than some of the other better known places so we had our guide to ourselves. Her English was excellent and her knowledge vast, from information re the history of the tea growing area, the development of the processing and current marketing strategies. I learned that Dilmah is just another wholesaler like Liptons so no need to pay extra - very important information. Naturally, we purchased some of their "free-of-additives" tea and it is delicious. If you would like a relaxed hype-free tea plantation tour, this is the place ??

title: Family vacation
text: Visited this tea estate in nuwara eliya. Great location. Brought some tea for friends. Place even has kids play area They served freshly brewed black tea

title: Nice even in the rain
text: Good guide worth the stop nice tea and cake. Makes one appreciate tea more when you realise how hard tea puckers work plus the machine operators doing their bit

title: Short tour and not very authentic
text: The tour was short and did not seem very authentic, the tour was less than half an hour and it did not seem like we saw the whole actual factory. The guide was good. The factory was full with touring cars with big groups of people. There is also a shop and buffet lunch restaurant.

title: tour in less than 10minutes
text: we were thrilled to learn about tea from the history to consumer, however we were guided through the factory in a very expeditive course which lasted no more than 10minutes. we were offered a complementary tea cup at the end and left there "to enjoy"

title: Interesting tour
text: Very helpful guide was provided and took us round the factory and gave an explanatory the different types and grades of tea. The tour was free. We could take pictures. Some history of the plantation would have been useful, eg some display boards to read. We were taken to the cafÃ© and could buy tea and we also had tasty chocolate cake. It would have been even better if we could have had a tasting of the different teas, which we could have paid for as an extra. We were able to buy tea from the well presented and stocked shop.

title: A place of learning how to make "Tea".
text: Nice place to learn how to make tea from a leaf. New experience. Beautiful surrounding views. Well English speaking in house guide. Great hospitality with a fresh cup of tea.

title: Good place to see how tea is made.
text: We were given a guide to take us around to show the factory. This was free of charge. The guide was very informative and patient with all our questions. At the end of the tour we were offered free tea to taste.

title: Our visit Bluefield tea gardens.
text: On the way from nuwara Eliya to Kandy we visited Bluefield tea gardens. The tea factory situated in a beautiful area, surrounding with green tea plantations, streams, valleys. They invited with hot tasty tea with a friendly smile. We visited the factory with a instructor who explain all the way of tea process and types of tea. That's good but the instructor(guide) explain like audio display. Need little deep explanation. Any how that was a great experiences. They have a store with many verity of teas. Feel little expensive but worth.

title: Free guide
text: We'd been to tea plantations in the past in Malaysia but this offered a free guide, which made the whole thing a lot more interesting. She was very pleasant and gave us a nice insight into the process. There was even a free cuppa at the end. We just gave her a tip for her troubles.

title: A quick and interesting stop off the main road
text: Stopped here on the road from Kandy to Nuwara Eilya and had a tour this only lasts about 15-20mins and it's free although we tipped the lady who took us round a small amount. Interesting to see the tea making process and to learn about the different types of tea, we purchased some ta after the tour but there was no pressure to buy anything. At the end of the tour they give you a free cuppa which is a nice touch.

title: A good road side stop serving Bluefield brand tea with cakes, muffins etc,
text: Good tea available, can buy various Blueiled tea products, may watch Bluefield Factory for tea making process, can enjoy the scenic view;

title: Nice visit
text: Its a nice visit to do. The guide was friendly and showed us the tea plantation and afterwarfs showed us all the process to manufacture the tea. Afterwars they invite us to a cup of tea that was very good.

title: Best roundtrip to Udawalawe National Park, arranged by Mr.Indika Dissanayaka
text: We are a german couple, visiting Sri Lanka as we met Mr. Indika Dissanayaka on the beach near our hotel Pandanus Beach Resort & Spa. He is speaking german really excellent, so we decided to go on a tour to Udawalawe Nationalpark. But I don`t like to travel with a lot of other guests, because if we could take this guided tour on ourselves, we can stop where we want, stay as long as we want :-). Thanks a lot, I`ll tell all my friends to get this tour via I.D.Tours Mr. Indika Dissanayaka

title: Short tour followed by FABULOUS pot of tea.
text: The title says it all. The free tour was basic but interesting and the follow up free pot of tea was to die for

title: fantastic hill view
text: tea gardens surrounding with hills....absolutely amazing view. tea was nice as well. this is a must stop place on the way to Nuawara Eliya

title: Awesome teas
text: A great place to explore and see how Sri Lanka produces their world famous tea.. You can take guided tours at no cost but I can guarantee you will purchase something from their well fitted out shop on site. Great little cafe with amazing views of the area. Well worth the stop to experience and take some great photos.. The tea brings it all back when you arrive home..

title: Wah chai !! Refreshing tea !
text: Visit to bluefield tea garden was a great experience ! On arrival we got Nishanti taking us on a tour of the tea factory. Her clear explanation of tea - White, black and green tea making made it so clear as to why some tea brews light, some strong. My daughter said “I never knew this !” - At the end of the tour and insisted we buy some tea to take back. The factory had distinct aroma of tea leaves being dried and roasted - did not smell damp despite the rain ! Must visit and buy !

title: Interesting tour of a working plantation
text: Large factory in operation which fully explains the process of tea making. There is also a shop for tea sales( expensive) and a cafÃ© to try the tea

title: A nice insight into tea processing
text: I stopped off here on the advice of my driver on my way out of Nuwaru Eliya. It is set amongst an expanse of tea fields (which is useful!) and they provide a free tour around the factory. I went on a Sunday so the factory wasn't processing but it was very interesting to walk around and learn about how tea is processed from being picked all the way to being bagged up for auction. It's simple and educational, at the end of the day it's a working factory and you're learning about how it works. It's followed by a cup of tea (and cake if you like) in the cafe, and you can walk through to the shop and buy tea at their factory prices. There are staff in the shop (who do the tours) who will talk you through the differences of the types of tea leaves and how best to drink them. I was there about an hour for the whole thing. The getting to and from the factory will probably take most of your time but it's a nice site to visit and learn about Sri Lanka's tea production and export.

title: A bit over assuming
text: A visit to the factory is short and has little to no action taking place. Just a detail of the process minus seeing too much happening..... for me that was a downer. The sales centre is well stocked but no deals here , which was also disappointing. One does get a feel of what tea is all about, however.

title: Recomended
text: This was a stop on our way to Nuwara and after seeing all the beatifull tea plantations we learned about making tea process. The lady spoke a good english and was very nice, we tipped her 300 rp. We also enjoyed a tea and bought some for home.

title: Small Tea Factory with a good Restaurant
text: This is a scheduled stop for many tourist operators. The officials explain the process very well.They have a very good restaurant with decent spread and obviously a sales counter to promote the tea sales

title: Great Explaination from Guide
text: Once you arrived this Bluefield Tea Garden, you will be assigned a guide for free. They will explain to you the process of tea making. An eye opening experience and place to learn about green, white and black teas!. Souvenir Shop selling tea as well. But slightly expensive.

title: Lovely little place
text: What great, friendly service we received, though we did not have to pay one cent! Our tour guide was incredibly hospitable and knowledgeable, and the complementary tea at the conclusion of our tour was delicious. Good quality food in the restaurant, too. Would highly recommend.

title: Tea experience
text: Interesting experience, particularly when our group got to pick tea leaves like the pickers. The tour was excellent followed by the tasting. The downside was being hassled by people wanting to be tipped for everything!

user_location: Prague, Hlavni Mesto Praha, Czech Republic
title: Nice visit
text: 20 minute visit to the working factory. No entry fee just tip to your guide and you have a free cup of tea afterwards and bought extra some nice cakes. Taken photos in the factory allowed. We bought some tea in the shop. It hot really busy around noon when buses with tourists came. You can have a walk to tea plantations just behind factory bulding.

title: AN WONDERFUL AROMA OF TEA
text: I am a real tea drinker and taking the tour at the Bluefield Tea Gardens with one of their professional guides was ''an education''. There was so much information to digest about the different types of tea, the processes it went through before arriving at our shops and watching the various machinery process the leaves. My tea will never taste quite the same again!

title: Well worth a visit
text: Had a guided tour of the plantation and factory and it was quite fascinating and educational to learn how the leaves are picked and then turned into the various types of tea. Well worth a visit and our guide Suria was excellent.

title: A greta opportunity to see tea production
text: Visited the Bluefield Estate during our trip to the hill country, which is in itself, both beautiful and enchanting. The tour guides are very knowledgeable and the workers, pleasant and friendly. Most of us drink tea but I suspect that few of us know the picking and production process, so the tour was both informative and interesting. Naturally, we finished up with a cup of the local brew in the adjoining cafe and needless to say, Ceylon tea is very good.

title: Good place
text: The Tea factory was closed when we visited the place. The restaurant is costly...also the tea shop is very expensive

title: Passed through here on way to Yala, so nextra cost just a bigger tip
text: Well you do learn something but In my opinion it was not a working factory it was an old historic factory. Still interesting and no cost to visit but you make up for it in the shop afterwards. So all in all worth a visit if you are passing by and do end up knowing a lot about Tea, ( although still prefer Morrison’s Earl Grey ! ) We visited as a couple but good for teens to make a break in the journey Loos and and cafe there as well.

title: Quite far away. Nice tea garden with a good souvenir shop !
text: It took us about one and half hour to get there by tuk tuk. It's quite far away. The facilities are a bit old. It depends on your luck if the guide is patient to explain every steps. Our guide went quite fast. After visiting the factory, you can walk around the tea field and have a cup of tea for free. The souvenir shop is nice. There are many varieties of tea and they are nicely packed. They are not cheap though. We found that it's even cheaper to buy tea from shops in Ella.

title: Nice tea experience
text: Immediately after arrival we got 10 minutes free walk around factory. There is only black tea production. Tea shop is really good, we visited Mackwoods and Pedro tea plantation and here is not such a big nicely packed variety of tea. Cannot say whether it is overpriced as in local stores we didn't see nothing like these. A bit disappointed about degustation as it is just a one cup of usual tea. Much more worse is a plantation itself as there are lots of poor women and children asking for money and views itself is not best of the best in comparison with others.

title: Visit to Tea Gardens
text: We all enjoyed the brief but informative factory tour regarding tea leaf processing. Also enjoyed the tea tastings after this tour and purchased some tea. Lovely setting and all is clean and organised. A great place to stop in.

title: Expensive Tea Shop
text: The tea factory and its tour is very informative but tea being sold here was expensive in my opinion.

title: free tea and tour - good views for photos
text: The free factory tour was good - the cafe had good selection of cakes and patties - I like the Veg Puff - Free tea was icing on cake - We bought some green tea as souvenir which is high quality tea. Overall very happy with the visit.

title: A must visit place in Nuwara Eliya
text: Tea Garden with team factory is an awesome place to visit. The staff there explains every aspect of tea making with right set of detailing. The live demonstration of making white/ black & brown tea is fabulous. Bought couple of different team packs from the shopping store.

title: Short guided tour of tea factory
text: The guided tour of tea factory was brief as it seems the main focus is to get you inside the shop to sample the tea and of course get you to buy the tea in their shop.

title: Great educational experience
text: We had a very nice explanation about the tea production process from A-Z, which was very interesting and free. I finally understood the actual process tea goes through, from the picking of the leaves and up to the tea bag in my cup... nice

title: Good tour
text: Lovely scenic drive to plantation. Plantation guide was excellent. Really interesting to see how tea is produced and to see the inside of the building which is in original condition and bar one modern machine the process of making the tea hasn't changed. Free entry and tour and cup of tea at end of tour. Nice to have a walk around plantation to see the tea bushes and the workers picking them.

title: Mackwood is better for pictures but Bluefield has better tour
text: We visited Mackwood (now knows as Damro) straight after visiting Blue Field, as it was on the way to our hotel in Nuwara Eliya. The tour at Blue Field is much better, as the process of tea making was explianed in detail in 10-15 minutes where as it only took 5 minutes at Mackwood. However, the setting at Mackwood is much nicer and for pictures. The tea from the shop is also cheaper at Blue Field. If time allows it, try both as it takes 15-20 minutes to travel between both.

title: A good half day trip
text: We hired a van and the trip down the winding roads amidst the tea farms are a great view itself. The area is a little warmer than central. The factory location itself has a great view of the surrounding mountains and tea patches. You will know almost everything about Srilankan teas if you take the tour through. All then processes, varieties of teas etc. The guide there do it passion, for zero charge. But better give her some tips. Out in the field tea leave pickers work for a lesser daily rate. If you inquire a photo with them it would be nice to tip them. Theres a restaurant, souvenir shop and tea cafe. The lunch at the restaurant was of good quality.

title: Beautiful place
text: Nice place to.sit and relax . They have variety of tea to explore and drink. You will.love this place

title: The best Tea factory in Sri Lanka
text: This tea factory was recommended by our driver. So glad we made the trip here. The tea pickers have been located here for centuries and I believe this is one oft he oldest tea factories around with machinery going back over 100 years. Our guide was very informative and gave us a thorough walk through and explained the tea making process. The tea tasting at the end was Devine and for less then £10 you get to sample all the tea which is made. A must visit, if you are in Nuwara Eliya.

title: okie

title: Well worth a visit
text: The location is delightful, surrounded by hills covered in tea plants. We had a personal tour from a young woman who took a lot of pride in what she did.
