A real treat. I might go back there just to stock up.

title: Mr Debesh Sengupta
text: Nice tea factory on the way to Nuwara Eliya They take you round the factory and offer free cup of tea Black tea and Green tea available for Sale

title: Beautiful
text: Great intro to tea making. The tea smell was amazing in the factory, like the tea had perfumed the wood ! Tea and cakes were delicious; you pay for the cups of tea and cake rather than the tour and unlike other places I read of there was no pressure to buy tea to take home (although we did)

title: An Excellent insight into Tea Production
text: Stumbled upon this Plantation whilst travelling from Kandy to Yala. This place is definable worth visiting. Free Guided Tour which really explained just how much goes into making and processing tea. Really nice Tea room offering a free cup of Black Sample Tea. Also a shop selling all the different teas produced by the Grower. As I said there is no entry charge so its customary to thank the Guide with a small tip. Definitely worth a Visit

title: Great free tour!
text: Lovely tea field/ factory. They offered a very informative tour of the factory and how the tea is collected and produced. No tip is expected at the end unlike some free tours. We received a free cup of black tea at the end of the tour in the cafe. We also ate he buffet lunch for 800 rupee per person, which was great. Offered lovely views in the restaurant. Highly recommend

title: One of the best tea tours I have been on
text: Went to Bluefield after recommendations from my SL cousins. The factory tours was really nice, with the guide and the factory workers explaining us the different stages of the process. The smell of toasted tea leaves that hits you the moment you step into the building is welcoming and soothing. I really enjoyed the tea tasting afterwards and bought a couple of teas at the shop! It is definitely worth a visit! Bonus: tea factory tour and sampling of one variety is free!

title: Great visit
text: As mentioned by many - much better than the rather touristic Damra factory - they do take time to go through the tea manufacturing process and allow questions / pictures. Close by you can also take pictures of ladies picking tea. Tour is free of charge so please leave tip for the good quality guide or for ladies picking tea if you take pictures

title: Excellent no stress experience
text: Our driver took us into the tea factory for a free tour. Our guide was exceptionally pleasant and helpful throughout, and provided no pressure for sales (a rare quality in sri lanka). We went as a couple but the experience can be great for all types. Unfortunately there is one component of the tea factory that is not wheelchair accessible, should you need it. However, the rest of the tour is accessible from what I could tell.

title: Beautiful Tea Plantation
text: We had a lovely time in the Blue Fields Tea Gardens. They offered a free tour around the tea factory (first opened in the 1920s) which provided a lot of details on how the tea leaves are picked and processed. The tea gardens are behind the factory where you can roam around and interact with the tea pickers. They also have a restaurant where they serve buffet meals and a tea centre where you can taste and buy fresh tea.

title: Amazing Experience - Quality Tea
text: What a wonderful experience to visit Blue Field Tea Gardens & Factory. It is considered to be one of the best tea factories in the world. When we reached they gave us a guided tour as to how the tea is prepared in the factory which was very unique and informative. Kids enjoyed the most. After the tour they took us to their restaurant for fresh tea tasting which was so rich in taste. Some of the hot teas were free to taste and some had a price. There is a big shop within the factory where one can buy tea for self or families. Highly recommend and clean place.

title: Good place to experience the tea growing and process
text: This was a good place to experience the tea growing and process. We were shown around by a knowledgable local guide and her English was excellent. We tipped her a few hundred rupees at the end. You can see the basic leaves and how they are turned into different varieties of orange pekoe black tea. There is a shop where you can by the tea leaves and also you get to try a cup of the basic black tea for free. Cakes and milk is also available at an extra charge. Do walk around the gardens too where you can see all of the tea bushes where ladies picks average of.20 kg of tea leaves every day. We were hassled a bit in the gardens which was annoying by an old lady who wanted us to take her photo for money and also a guy who wanted to 'escort' us around d the gardens for money. Again we give him a couple of hundred rupees even though his English was terrible and he added no value to our visit whatsoever but he was persistent and I just wanted him to go away!

title: Nice stop on the way
text: Nice place to visit for lunch (get stuck in the buffet and you will need an hour to recover after!) The tea factory is still working - the many "no picture" boards are hilarious when the guide tells you to take pictures. A nice tea shop - great view amongst the hill tops. What more does one need.

title: Nice little visit
text: Yes it is touristic. But not a tourist trap. The girl gave a nice tour which indeed does not take more than 10minutes. But in this time everything was said. So no complaints there. They didn't push us into buying stuff. They gave us tea for free at the end of tge tour and let us be. We had a 2nd tea (paying) and some cake. All at good prices if you ask me. The store itself seems to have acceptable prices as well.

title: Good experience of tea process making
text: Good place to go if on your way. Don't go out of your way to go there though as not worth a detour. Friendly place that explains the full process of tea making from moment leaves are picked. Good education for a basic product we take for granted and use everyday. Tour of factory and good knowledge by guides. It's a basic free tour . Nothing more to it than that.

title: Tony estate in middle of Hills
text: A nice little experience that starts from Tea making factory tour. It is situated in the middle of tea estate. The tea is highly expensive.

title: Informative tour & great tea
text: The tea factory tour was very informative,from picking up the tea leaves till packing... our tour guide was very helpful , he helped us pick up gifts from the shop... and not to forget the tasty tea in the restaurant.

title: Interesting tour
text: We were taken on a tour of the factory from processing of raw tea leaves to finished product. It was very interesting. All of the loading of tea leaves is done manually by women who I suspect are paid little as is the case with pickers. It is a remarkably and surprisingly labour intensive process. I don't think I will drink a cup of tea again without thinking of the workers I saw labouring away. Anyway, so much for my left leaning tendencies - one would hope fair trade might occur as it has in the coffee trade. Well worth a visit, and the tea on sale is quite cheap.

title: It's a interesting stop en route to somewhere
text: It was a good and informative rest and pit stop. The guided tour included explanations on how the raw tea gets turned into the end product and our guide was knowledgeable enough.

title: Interesting visit
text: We had a guide explain the process of tea growing and processing which was alot more interesting than I thought it would be. We enjoyed morning tea in the very pleasant cafe.

title: Bluefield Tea Gardens
text: A trip to Sri Lanka would not be complete without a visit to a Tea Garden. And Bluefield Tea Gardens is a great example of why Sr Lanka tea is most flavorful and sought after by tea lovers the world over. They have great tour of processing of the tea leaves which was very enjoyable. The factory and it's surrounding areas form a great backdrop for pictures. A tea shop with free tea servings are an added attraction. Attractive packaging of tea leaves for sale - at the time we visited - the only drawback was we had to pay with cash - no credit card transactions were accepted - not very convenient for the international traveler.

title: Authentic Tea
text: Blue Field Tea Garden an authentic place to purchase original Sri Lankan tea with different types and taste.

title: Learn about tea!!
text: There are many tea estates and factories near Nuwara Eliya, but Blue Fields seems to be one that is better set up for visitors. Informative tours of the 100-year old factory are provided and visitors are allowed wander throughout the tea plantations. Good opportunities for photos. End the tour with a nice cup of complimentary tea and chance to buy overpriced tea in their shop. Blue Fields is about 20 kilometers from Nuwara Eliya (farther than many other tea factories), but it's a nicer experience than many others.

title: the best BOP tea and cakes
text: we had an enjoyable stop over here. The tour was highly educational with regards the tea process. The complimentary tea was divine and the cakes very tasty and inexpensive. Well worth the stop. I would recommend this.

title: Its a tea plantation that is all.
text: A slight disappointment in that the guide, just fired us through all this and the plant was not working due to a funeral. Interesting all the same and then you get some bad service at the end in the tearoom to make up for the 10 mins getting shown around. I would not recommend this as we found it to be 'oh I cant be bothered", 'what more tourists", not for us wish we had not bothered.

title: Tea at Reasonable Prices
text: We went there to take photos of the tea-leaf pickers and visited their factory and shop too. The factory visit was short, but still interesting, picking up some knowledge of the different types of tea. Their shop offers a variety of teas that they produce, all of reasonable prices, nothing that is exorbitant. I bought the golden tip and silver tip tea leaf. It is good.

title: Great Tea Plantation
text: This is our First visit to a Tea Plantation, it was High up in the Mountains in a most spectacular setting, our tour around the factory albeit brief was very informative and interesting, but be aware that as soon as you get your camera out the plantation staff will soon pop-up wanting money to be in your pictures! After our tour we was taken to the Teas Shop to sample the tea and was given an opportunity to buy some tea, this wasn't expensive nor was there a hard sell. A lovely trip!

title: Best Cup of Tea
text: Stopped at Bluefield Tea gardens for a free 15 minute tour on our way to Ella. Very informative guide and afterwards given a excellent cup of black tea. Cake or biscuits are extra and were reasonably priced so we indulged. We are now drinking a pot of tea very day which is so much better for us. Best cuppa.

title: A good knowledge of tea production
text: Here we got nice experience of how tea is produced. Explanation was given point to point in a very nice way. Staff of the factory is very helpful in explaining the process of tea. Along with explanation we got a chance to taste nice cup of tea. First time I got to know that there is white tea as well along with black tea. If time permits then this tea factory is worth a visit. We bought tea packs, our relatives liked it very much ??

title: Good to spend a few hours around a tea plantation and factory
text: I went there on a day trip and the place is good to see the process that goes into making tea and also to walk around the plantation for some time.

title: Interesting tour - not too long!
text: It was busy the day we went as it was the weekend. If you go on a Sunday you don't see the factory working but there is no noise of machinery. You get a free tour which is really interesting and then you are shown back to the cafe for a free cup of strong tea! The toilets are ok. The shop is quite small and a bit pricey. No pressure though. The shop at the St Clair's plantation (Mlesna Tea Castle) is way better, bigger and better staffed. Worth going to both.

title: very interesting
text: Bluefield is the first tea plantation we have ever visited. They offer a free guided tour and tea degustation. The guide shows the factory and explains everything about tea. You can also visit their shop and purchase some tea. Prices are OK.

title: Well maintained factory with a nice view for tea tasting
text: Visited the factory and was given a tour with explanation on the tea making process. Later on we were given a chance to have free tea tasting.The cafe that served the tea had a nice viewing area. Only minus point, felt the tea pricing was a bit steep. But then they don't force u to buy the products.

title: Nico to learn more
text: We had a tour at the factory. The nice gentlemen showed us how they make tea. It is nice to hear. After that we were offered a cup of tea. The tea was good.

title: Well worth a vist
text: We were given a tour of the tea factory by a friendly guide. Very impressive and noted the aged nature of much of the machinery. There was no pressure to buy stuff from the adjoining shop and cafÃ©. Definitely worth a visit

title: Wonderful Tea Plantation
text: Bluefield Tea Gardens is a beautiful tea plantation that to visit while in Ramboda or Nuwar Eliya area. The staff are very friendly and the tour is informative on the process of making tea. I wished that the tour was a bit longer and more detailed but to accommodate the large amount of people I think it's a bit difficult for them. The factory is clean and let me walk around to the back to get some pictures of the tea plantations and the workers. We arrived at the end of the work day (make sure to manage to go ahead of time to see all machines in operation) so we missed some of the machines however, we got the chance to talk to some of the workers before they checked out. The quality of the tea from this garden was some of the best we bought in all of Sri Lanka. I def recommend to buy your gifts and as much tea options as you can. Once you arrive, you also get the chance to sample the tea and enjoy some desserts (rather dry but good enough). Tips: - Arrive early so you get the chance to see everything in process. I believe the work day ends at 4pm. - Tip some of the workers if you can as working in the tea fields is one of the lowest paid jobs in Sri Lanka. - Sample and buy tea!

title: excellent quality tea to take back home
text: Nice tour ... an eye opener , it explains a lot about the tea we drink . The gift shop is loaded with all sorts of different high quality tea to take back home either for your own consumption or as gifts to your loved ones. I personally recommend The Blue Moon tea , the smell and taste is simply amazing.

title: Stop for tea
text: We stopped at Blue Field for tea. Enjoyed a nice chocolate cake. Great cup of tea. Nice restaurant upstairs but we didnt stop for lunch

title: Short but interesting visit
text: We stopped at these gardens to obtain a visit, we had our own guide, the visit of the factory took about 15 minutes. Afterwards we had a free cup of tea in the restaurant. They have a shop when you like to buy tea, as coffee drinkers we don't know if prices are high. We also had a small lunch which was nice.

title: We had a free cuppa and a factory visit!
text: We went to the tea factory there and one of the staff took us to the factory and explained how we get our cuppa to our table! Sadly they were not working on Sunday but we could see the machinery and the rest and also have a cuppa after the little tour. Interesting and informative to my 10 year old.

title: Intresting palce with good guided tours
text: The guided tour to team factory was very good and guide was very informative and explained the whole process patiently. The factory is very clean and allows visitors to view the process from up close. The tea shop was also very good and offered a wide range of products. Nice place to buy some premium tea. Use this opportunity to buy good tea as the tea sold in these factories is not available outside. Though ordinary tea in Nuruwa eliya etc. shops are cheaper, the quality here is far better and hence worth the cost.

title: Informative tour
text: We really enjoyed our tour at the Bluefield tea gardens. Our tour guide gave a thorough explanation of what happens at the factory and we were offered a free cup of tea at the end of the tour.

title: Very interesting place and exceptional customer service
text: Very clean and professional tea factory with a friendly and informative tour guide to show you around. After the tour, a courtesy cup of tea in the lounge. Of course, they have a shop so you can buy gifts and stock up, which we did. Unfortunately I managed to forget and leave belongings behind on a couch in the lounge... Their customer service was impressive - they found my belongings before I even realized I had lost them, put them safely aside, and then sent them on to me by courier. Could not have asked for more - thank you to staff and management at Blue Field Tea Gardens!!

title: Great tour, well priced high quality Tea
text: A local friend organised a tour here and explained that you get to buy your Tea at a fair price We foundd this to be true

title: Nice one hour stop
text: Our guide was clear and took us through the entire process. The tour obviously ends at the shop which offers a wide selection of tea.

title: One of the best Tea factory
text: Majorly women are employed in this factory and mainly manual process is undertaken for producing the tea product. All the tea plucking staff are women. As soon as you reach, staff guides you and explains you the process of tea produce in the factory. Types of tea and the benefits from each tea type is explained very well. Very informative and enthusiastic staff. Complimentary tea is served after the explanation. Natural tea products are available in powder as well as tea bag form. The staff also explains the cost for packaging involved and suggests you the right pack as per your budget. Enjoyed.

title: Great stop on the Kandy to Nuwara Elisa road.
text: Do not drive past this! Short personal walk through the tea making process in the 100 year old factory, from a very personable & interesting guide. Followed by tea, all at no charge!

title: Exemplary
text: Very nice place with lots of ftes firlds around. Simply honoured to take a tour in bluefield. Hope for the best

title: Nice factory and good visit
text: We really enjoyed the visit, our guide was very pleasant and he spent time with us, he was easy to understand and answered all our questions.

title: Fascinating place to visit
text: Had a very interesting tour around this tea factory. Our excellent guide explained all about the way the tea is grown, harvested and then produced within the factory. Had a first-rate cup of the tea as the tour finished.

title: Nice original place
text: Had a tour by a lovely Sri Lankan girl. Very interesting facts around tea. The place have a decent place yo have tea and pastry and a good shop as well. Beautiful surrounfin6.

title: Good place to visit
text: Several types of teas are prepared here! A guided tour explains the differences clearly the process of making tea! Tea tasting is possible before you want to buy or choose your favorite tea! The English spoken by guide may not be clear but if you ask question, you get answers! ??

title: Informative visit
text: We had a guide with good English and she explained very clearly the processes involved in tea production. Not rushes. Had a nice cup of tea afterwards and bought lots of tea to come home. Countryside round about is lovely.

title: Fascinating, and well worth the visit
text: We were on an organised tour of Sri Lanka and this was one of our scheduled stops. The tour around the factory was very interesting and the old British machinery still is in working condition. The ladies were then encouraged to try picking the tea out in the field for themselves, it was a great laugh watching them working so competitively in the field. Then as a reward, we were all treated to a wonderful cup of tea followed by, as usual a tea store visit.

title: Good tea factory
text: Nice tea factory, although we did not see it working as it was sunday, it is free too! But the gift shop Probably makes up for it!

title: Everything good but abysmal state of toilets
text: Short, crisp and informative tour of the showcase tea processing facility. The area around the center offers a delightful view of tea gardens interspersed with small brooks and quaint bridges. A winding road takes you up the hill for a birds-eye view of the mesmerizing valley studded with lakes. Inside the outlet, there is plenty to choose from - variety, flavours, quantity, and packaging. Staff is efficient and helpful. There is a nice cafe where you can sample different kinds of tea and complete the experience with a choice of cake on the side. Wish the owners lay as much importance to the availablity of enough and clean toilets.

title: Great factory guide informative but the lunch buffet could have been a little better
text: Found this place informative and did purchase quite a bit of tea to take back home as well as distribute among friends. They serve a free cup of black tea per person. I wish they had the option of milk tea and if not liquid milk at least milk powder as I do not fancy black tea. We had lunch here but the lunch buffet was just okay, nothing great. Dessert options were very limited. I was hoping to see more of Srilankan food.

title: Good tea factory
text: A very good tea factory, offering free tours of the facilities and complimentary cup of tea afterwards.

title: Good place to visit
text: Good information about the tea plantation...the whole process of how tea is made and the machinery used to process the tea...the people involved in it was explained in detailed...good experience..we bought different varieties of tea from there too..loved it...

title: Great place to stop
text: I stopped here for a break and had tea and cake followed by a free tour of the tea factory. My guide had a lot of knowledge and took me through the entire tea making process. It was interesting an informative. She then showed me all of the different teas on sale in the shop and explained why some were much more expensive than others. The good thing is that you can walk into the tea room and taste the teas before you buy any. It is not the cheapest place to get a cup of tea but quite unique.

title: Interesting to see a tea factory, not too special though
text: Somehow we did not find a guide, even though most other tourists did walk through the factory with a guide. A worker sent us in on our own, so we explored the factory by ourselves. There was just half a band of fresh tea leaves currently being dried and no worker (or anyone else) was around on that floor, but in the lower floor the rest of the tea processing was happening on a seemingly normal scale. It was indeed interesting to see the individual steps from the leaves up to the various tea types. The tea store was well stocked and overcrowded, with a lot of tourist buses buying huge amounts of tea. Our apartment hosts already recommended us (and were right) only to buy small amounts of tea for presents, as the price was indeed extraordinarily high and the quality the same as you find in normal shops. Afterwards, we ate a little and enjoyed a cup of tea in the Cafe. Overall a nice visit and definitely great to walk a bit among the tea fields that are so common in this area of Sri Lanka.

title: Short and sweet
text: The tour was short and simple and well done even though we didnt see much in action. The tea tasting consisted of one tea which was nice but made it difficult to understand the difference between the tea they made and sold...the others are available for a cost but I didnt have space for 5 full cups of tea :) We bought some tea from the wide selection on offer and then afterward went to the local village and found the same tea much cheaper in the shops! The selection was a lot smaller so I am still glad I bought what I did but it was disappointing to feel that they were taking full advantage of the captive market of tourists :(

title: Good explanation of the process
text: The factory tour was good and the process was explained well. As we went on a Sunday, we missed out on the opportunity to the see the machines running. The tea shop had many varities of tea but the pricing was high. Tourist factor.

title: Well worth a visit
text: A good way to see how tea is processed. Was met by an English speaking guide (tip only payment) he took us though the factory and explained the process of how tea is made. We then got a free cup of tea, and then left to browse the shop, which was reasonable price.

title: Very interesting, educational and so helpful
text: I have not visited a tea factory for years and was a bit skeptical about what I was going to see and learn. I have never been so wrong. In my early days there was no such thing as tea bags, and i thought tea bags was for grounded twigs! Now i know ground tea can give different strengths. The factory was so clean and the tour was excellent. Shop was very good. We bought some tea to take home. Best part of my story was we left a jacket/coat there and were miles away before we realised this. We gave them a call, and they were so helpful. They sent us a picture to confirm, and then sent the jacket to their store in Colombo, for us to collect before leaving Sri Lanka. Thank you, Mr. Irshad, you showed us not just how good Blue Field Tea Gardens is, but how helpful and kind Sri Lankan people are.

title: Nothing more than a tea shop
text: Our driver took us here as he said the Tea was good. It was merely a tea shop. Very busy and crowded, more expensive than the other tea factories. Not worth the price or the effort to visit.

title: Great lunch and shop
text: We came here having already visited the Labookellie tea factory, and I preferred the Labookellie tour to Bluefield - it just seemed a bit more polished. That said, Bluefield is still good for a run-down of the tea-making process. We also had lunch here, which was 990 rupees/person for a buffet. The food was lovely, particularly the eggplant curry. We also saved our shopping for Bluefield as our hotel owner had told us it was cheaper, and we weren't disappointed. Beautiful 150g decorated canisters of tea were 800-950 rupees, and there was a huge range. On the whole, Bluefield was a great place to finish a day trip through the tea fields.

title: Best tea factory tour in Sri Lanka
text: Probably the best tea tour and factory experience you'll find in Sri Lanka. Friendly guides, interesting tour, and - of course - great tea. If you're looking for a place to visit to lean more about tea in Sri Lanka, then this is the place to go!

title: Really enjoyable and lovely tea
text: I really, really enjoyed the Bluefield Tea Garden's factory tour. Make sure you take the time and do this because you will appreciate the tea and the process involved so much more. The plantations are free to wander (so lovely, although if you visited in the heat of the day like me you're wander will be brief) and there is a cafe and retail store. I didn't sample at the cafe however I did bring home three boxes of different teas to enjoy at home. For those coming back to Australia, I ensured I bought fully sealed bags and didn't have any issues with customs upon arriving in Perth (make sure you declare them though). The toilets here aren't the cleanest I will say that, however not to the point you should find somewhere else. Definitely worth a visit and I'm certainly Enjoying my tea!

title: Good place to know the tea production, but expensive to buy tea there
text: We dropped by there on the way back to Negombo. They have a tea production line there. It's a good place to understand the whole black tea diversification and production processes. The guide explained everything clearly. They provided a free cup of tea for every tourist dropping by. And they have a shop there to do some shopping. Next to the shop, there is a quite big play ground for the kids to kill time while parents do shopping. However, the tea there is not cheap comparing with Negombo. Overall, it's a pleasant experience.

title: Free tea tasting !
text: We stopped here to buy tea as souvenirs back home to our friends and relatives. The cafe was crowded as it had just finished raining and there was a bus full of tourist awaiting for the rain to stop. As we had finished buying our tea, the crowd had already left with the bus and it was quite peaceful to enjoy a cup of black tea with the tea plantation as the back drop. We didnt mind paying extra for some milk and some cakes as we just enjoyed the hot cup of steaming tea in the post rain weather. Its was a perfect time and place for hot tea. Please do try the free tea, nothing to loose. And if you like it, buy it !

title: Tea was good
text: The view of factory was ok. I enjoyed the tea, was definitely good quality, but as is in Sri Lanka, was very over priced.

title: nice pit stop, recommended for tea education!
text: Nice introduction to the processes and steps from harvesting tea up to packaging. 1 of the well known tea estate. Complimentary cup of tea drink and you can shop in the many assortment of teas ready for purchase. Do try to walk pass the factory building to the tea path so that you can have a gorgeous view of the tea plantation valleys and lady workers. Friendly staff.

title: A must visit place for a different tea experience!
text: A should and must visit place on the way to Nuwara Eliya. It's a traditional and old tea factory which is still operational and produced "N" number of flavours of tea. There is a tea tour taken by the staff where they explain about different process of tea making until packing. The tea leaf smell welcomes you which is raw and the final stage of packing gives you best aroma of tea. Post the tour, you are offered hot piping tea which makes you warm in the cold atmosphere. Post sipping it.. you are then guided to buy their best tea which had several flavours. A must visit place which takes approximately 1 hour.

title: Short tour and a shop
text: In this tea farm, you can quite easily get a tour. You just go to the shop counter and somebody will take you on a tour. The tour is free, but tip I think is expected (we gave a small one anyway). The tour is just around the factory and is maybe 15 minutes where they explain the production process. At this farm you can't see the tea plants or do any picking. The shop has a wide range of teas and I the main restaurant area gives free tea (well we got some free tea after our tour anyway).

title: Excellent Marketing
text: They do teach you what the real tea dust means and how it's produced. The way they accept you as a tourist and explains things without reservations is way to learn. Great way and excellent hospitality. Thanks for the tea too...

title: Nice place
text: Good place to understand the tea making process and a quaint little tea shop serving pastries and tea.You may also purchase branded tea from the shop.

title: Very interesting place
text: They took us through the tea manufacturing process and we were surprised to know the different grades of tea mainly white tea. The tea boxes available in their shops are slightly on the higher side, but the purity is guaranteed. It was raining when we went there and it made the place even more fragrant.

title: Informative Tour
text: The guide who took us around the bluefield tea factory was a wonderful person. She explained us all the steps in details, of how the tea is processed. She also gave us details of the different kind of tea, i.e., black, green and white tea. However, their tea shop is toooooo expensive. Although my son bought some green tea from there but I would suggest to explore the market first.

title: Tea Plantation
text: Stopped here to see how the tea is processed depending on the type. It was very interesting to learn the process and to actually see it as it is still done today. You even get to have a gratis cuppa before making your way to the shop ??

title: Tour of the factory, shop and plantation
text: The staff who took us around was very informative and taught us quite a lot about tea production in general, as well as how it is done in Bluefield. He also explained about the various types of tea that are produced here as well as in other plantations, the differences as well as how best to drink them.

title: Nice plce
text: Nice place yo visit and learn about tea industry. Worth to drink a coup of tea there and to countinue ur journy...

title: Great tour and wonderful tea
text: Really nice tour of a tea factory. Not too modernised so you get to see so much more of the process. Great guide who took us through all the different steps. The tea is good too. Well worth stopping here.

title: Very informative tour
text: The tour was very informative with a knowledgeable guide.. They gave us a free cup of tea.. We could understand various steps of tea making and different types of tea.

title: Free Tour And Free Tea.. Worth The Visit
text: Wow... what a beautiful area and tea plantation. We got a free tour of the factory from a knowledgeable guide and learned a lot about tea in the process. Afterwards we received a free cup of tea which I complimented with two small slices of a tasty "Butter" and "Fruit" cake. Grand total for the tour, tea and two slices of cake, LKR 360 including a LKR 200 tour guide tip. A "Tea & Souvenir Shop" along with a Cafe is also on the property. However, there was no pressure to make a purchase as Tea Shop is in a separate room from Cafe. Feel free to roam the ground after you are done enjoying your free cup of tea.

title: beautiful countryside and nice tour
text: We visited on a Sunday when the factory was not running, but the tour was still interesting. Our guide was knowledgeable and answered all of our questions very clearly. Lots of options for tea purchase in the shop afterwards.

title: Good Tea Factory
text: The location is simply superb and there is ample parking place and after your visit to the tea factory you can relax at the cozy restaurant where you are served complimentary tea . There are many varieties of ceylon tea being sold here which is quite expensive. This place is worth a visit.

title: A Far Better Tea Estate
text: For tea factory tour, or to purchase teas, or to have lunch, this place is overall really great. Must visit. The gardens are charming, and what a breath taking view of the mountains and rolling mist. The restaurant is cozy, with good selection of food. I loved the Iced Tea here, one of the best I've had anywhere.

title: See the Greens, take the factory tour & Sip Free Tea
text: few moments before this on all 4 sides you see Lush Green Tea Plantations. The Blue Fields Tea Factory is Big & you can see more details in the photos attached. The Tea Factory tour is approx 30 mins, where they show u the making & complete process how Ceylon Tea is made !! after the tour they drop you to it's restaurant, check the Blue Fields Restaurant review for this

title: Short & Interesting
text: First of all - it ́s free of charge - big plus! You ́ll get a guide who explains every step of the tea manufacturing - from collecting leaves to drying & shredding, different tea types etc - quite interesting! After that you can go into the restaurant and have a gratis tea and you can tip your guide - or not, however you like. The whole procedure did take only about 30 minutes, but it was worth the time! Would recommend to anyone near this area.

title: Take the tour
text: A guide will show you through the manufacturing stages of the tea. The tour is less than 30 mins and there's a free brew afterwards. It's customary to give a small tip and well appreciated. Tea is expensive in all the factories - but it's excellent quality.

title: tour and buying tea!
text: A kind lady gave us a tour, she spoke fluent english and showed us from stage 1 all the way to the packaging stage of their tea factory! we then went to the gift shop area for a cuppa free tea and bought some teabags home too. Tour was fairly short though.

title: Tour of Tea Factory
text: This was an excellent choice by our guide As usual in Sri Lanka everyone is friendly and our guide ,a young girl dressed impeccably in a Sari was informative and articulate we learnt a lot about Tea we hadn't known before and then a complimentary cup of tea and cake at the end Totally recommended

title: Good tea to drink and purchase
text: Unfortunately they were closed by the time we arrived - don't travel over Sri Lankan New Year (April 13-15) as most people close the factories due to the holidays, however the coffee shop and tea store was open and the guy inside explains the variations of tea. The store was also inexpensive when compared to mackwood (now called browns) so fret spot to buy tea to take back home to family and friends.

title: Good variety of teas
text: One can taste different varieties of teas here in payment basis. There are many types of teas on sale here in different packings. The staff is quite helpful in explaining the difference in varieties. We bought OP & OPA grades. Pl bear in mind that the drivers get a cut, as they bring the customers to the factory.

title: Tea Factory : Not that Great
text: This factory is few KM before Nuwara Eliya on way. Not that great, when we visited it was closed so couldn’t get much information about their processes. Got one last to explain us reasonably. It has got one small children park with swings and slides but in poor condition. They have Tea Cafe where they serve one particular type of tea as complimentary and you can buy other types of Tea.

title: Good collection of teas
text: A must visit for tea lovers. Blue field has a wide range of tea flavors to select from. Confirm whether the factory is operational for a better experience.

title: Good, free visit to tea factory
text: Lovely young lady gave us a good explanation and tour of the tea process .. though I wish the factory was actually working when we visited.. It was nice to walk through the plantation after the tour. We tipped many of the women labourers we saw as we felt terrible when we learnt how miserably little they are paid for their hard long hours of work. There is small PLAYGROUND which the kids enjoyed after we had our free tea sample and also had some snacks at their coffee shop. We also bought some tea for gifts.

title: Wonderful visit
text: Upon arrival I was greeted by Muhammed and off we went to the plantation. Here I had my first introduction to tea leaves and bushes. The factory workers were on breakfast break and it was lovely to see the super clean and tidy century old factory in its glory. The tour ended with a delicious cup of tea (skip the milk and sugar this time to taste authenticity)!!

title: The best tea tour in Nuwara Eliya
text: It's definitely worth dropping off at this tea factory, even if you've been to others. For a start, it's much small - the company only employs about 200 people and the place has a bit of a family feel about it. Second, we could all around the factory and watch tea being processed, which wasn't the case at the other tea factory we tried (we went on a Monday morning and they don't pick on a Sunday, so you've got to make sure they are working in the factory or you get a trip round a silent building). Our guide was friendly and informative and didn't hang around for a tip - in fact, we sought him out to give him a tip and and couldn't find him. And the tea was complimentary.

title: Beautiful grounds, great tea and informative tour
text: Of all the tea factories I've visited on my travels this would probably be my favourite. The actual tour of the factory is extremely informative and the lady explained the entire process of making tea in great detail. We were allowed to take photos of the factory's insides and then given a complimentary cup of tea. After having our free cuppa and free tour we proceeded to the gift shop which wasn't cheap but also wasn't expensive, moderately priced is what I would say best fits it. Finally we were allowed to take a stroll around the plantation completely unassisted which was lovely. The plantation and grounds are beautiful and the fact that we could go where we wanted on our own really made it special. A definitely must do in this tea lovers opinion.

title: Beautiful tea
text: gardens we visited SriLanka in Dec 2017. On our way from Nuwara to Kandy , we visited this beautiful tea garden and tea factory,. The gardens are beautiful but we were a bit disappointed as the tea factory was closed since it was Sunday. We were offered a cup of tea at the end of tour which was very good. I would recommend a visit to this garden on a weekday.

title: Nice but too expensive
text: This place is there to please the tourists We wanted milk tea after the excursion, but we had to pay for it

title: Interesting/annoying old woman
text: Good tour but we were never taken into the fields. Also an old women who basically jumped in front of the camera and demanded money was pretty off putting, as I’m happy to pay if I wanted a photo of one of the women working but i didn’t ask for a mug shot in front of the fermenting block!

title: Ok nothing great
text: I cant compare this place to any other tea factory because i only went to one. The minute you enter you are taken.on a tour of the factory. It was quite obvious that the information provided was scripted. When we asked a couple of questions the guide couldnt give proper answers. The tour ends with a complimentary cup of tea. I was told that this place has more choices of tea in its souveneir shop. The plus point is on our own we decided to walk to the tea plantation.(not part of the tour) The view is amazing. Great photo opportunities. The highlight of the visit!

title: Nothing special
text: Tea factory looks rather like place for guiding tourists than really working factory. Guide said about the tip for him at the beginning on the tour. Tea shop is recommended as they have tea in different kinds of packages and very reasonable price. If you want to buy tea you may visit the shop only and for the tea factory tour go to other place.

title: Great tour
text: Great to visit as part of the tour, was fascinating to see how the tea is produced and to be shown round the factory. Opportunities to taste tea and have food in the cafe, and buy products in the shop.

title: A must-visit Tea Factory in Nuwara
text: We stopped by at this factory on our way to the city of Nuwara Eliya. The place was surrounded with tea plantations and beautiful landscapes. There's a mini a waterfall right above it. Blue Field Tea Gardens is not just a tea factory but they offer more than that. As soon as you arrive, they will provide a tour guide (for free) who will accompany you inside the factory and explain the process of producing a world class tea product. Once the tour is over, they will serve a free cup of tea. They also have cakes, muffins, pastries, & bread for a very reasonable price. Cheap tea products were also available onsite.

title: Fantastic place and Nishanthi was an excellent guide
text: We went to this farm (over dozens of others) based on the personal recommendation of a friend + trip advisor reviews. This was well worth a morning drive out from our accommodation. Nishanthi our guide was very knowledgeable and explained the process answering our questions. At the end of the tour of the factory she guided us to the cafe where hot tea was served and where we even got explanation about the type of tea being served. The restaurant had some very tasty and piping hot snacks as well as yummy cakes and pastries for us to enjoy with our tea all with very attentive, prompt and friendly service. Clean bathrooms manned by attendants was a huge plus. It even has a small playground for children to enjoy. After enjoying the tea and the snacks we bought the many different varieties of reasonably priced tea they sell. Someone was at hand to help us select and explain the different teas that we wanted to buy. To finish off the experience we went for a nice relaxing stroll among the tea plantation enjoying the lovely vistas from high up in the mountains. Thanks blue fields for the lovely experience and many thanks Nishanthi!!!

title: Great little tour
text: Our tour guy was fantastic. Her English was exceptional and took the time to answer our questions as we went. Well worth it.

title: Tea factory tour
text: Interesting tour and nice people showing us around. Opportunity to taste teas and of course visit their shop.

title: Informative visit
text: We had a short tour around here. The girl who showed us the stages of tea production was a fountain of knowledge & was able to answer questions we asked & we learnt some interesting facts. We did buy some tea at the end because it isn't available at home.

title: Tea Factory with Good Explanatiaon
text: I visited on a Sunday. The facory was not operative but one assistant showed us around the factory and showed us the processes involved in making tea. We were also given an explanantion of the different types of tea. Then we were given a cupof tea to drink.Nice visit.

title: Short visit in the tea plantation. Double prices in the shop.
text: We had a very short visit in the tea plantaion, a longer and interesting visit in the factory. The tea shop had about double prices compared to the normal in shops and hotels.

title: Fun experience
text: Informative tour. Unfortunately, we were there on a Sunday, so we didn't get to see the factory "in action." Provided with tea after the tour. Tea Prices very reasonable. Must do when visiting Sri Lanka!

title: Ancient Factory
text: Quaint factory with a short tour where you see the tea being dried and fermented. At the end of the tour you have an opportunity to sample different types of tea and purchase.

title: Beautiful factory with nice tea tasting
text: We chose to come to this Tea factory because its blue colour looked very beautiful. In fact, even inside the factory, unexpectedly, many parts are in blue too. Nice colour. There is no fee for the tour. A guide explained the tea and differences between different kind of tea. And, showed us around the operation. We visited on Sunday and no one worked and so we could not see the real operation in the factory and tea fields. But, we could walk over to tea fields to take few photos. After the tour, a free tea was given and we could relax a bit. We did some shopping here, though not sure if it was reasonable price or not. But, at least, we took some good photos.

title: nice and cheap black tea buying
text: very good quanlity of tea,most important is the price you can't imaging!so maybe the ladies' salary who pick leaves are far low beyond we know,I guess.

title: Great tour & factory
text: We loved this tea factory tour. Very informative & the shop is good at the end and reasonably priced. The cafe is great. We preferred this tea factory over Mackwood's.

title: Excellent orange pekoe and good explanation of how tea was made.
text: The tour lasted for around 10 minutes. We were shown the fresh tea leaf, which was then dehydrated, grounded, fermented and sorted. The factory had a lovely aroma. The small restaurant served free black tea but milk tea would be charged. The tea was very smooth and had a sweet after taste which lasted for an hour.

title: Touristy but worth
text: Free to enter, short 15minutes individual guide through the factory by friendly guides of Bluefield factory. Good first impression how tea is being made, informative. Then you receive a cup of tea in the restaurant area (few dessert options to buy if one wants) And there is a tea shop with great selection of locally produced tea. The guides are there to help you, tea samples available. Depends what kind you want, it starts 4usd onwards.

title: Interesting
text: We had just tea, but it was an amazing experience in the hils on a tea estate. Tea was refreshing with many choices

title: A nice break on the way to Nuwara Eliya
text: The Bluefield Tea Gardens and factory is a great way to stretch your legs when on the way from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya. The tour of the factory was informative although very dusty. The cup of tea provided after the tour was lovely. The toilet facilities were very clean. There was food available, but we did not consume any, so cannot inform you of its quality. The price of the tea however was quite high and as such we did not purchase any.

title: Visiting a tea garden is a must if you go to Nuwara Ellya
text: And this was a very good tea garden with a nice guided tour of the tea factory- the tour is free along with a cuppa to sample post tour. Most visitors buy some fresh tea and so did we... not cheap tea but good quality I presume as I have not yet tasted it. Worth a visit.

title: Lovely Tea
text: Unfortunately as we visited on the weekend we couldn't see anything working but we had a really excellent tour and explanation of how everything worked. Afterwards we had a lovely cup of tea and opportunity to buy some local tea.

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden

location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden

location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: Worth a visit

location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: Great Tour!
text: We visited Damro as it was recommended by our driver and it was a great tour, incredibly informative! We were driven into the plantation, where there are some wonderful viewpoints and picture opportunities and then got to pick tea ourselves, with our guide also explaining which leaves were used for what tea. Afterwards a lovely employee showed us around the factory, whilst quite a brief tour it was informative and interesting and she was very nice! We were served some tea to try for free and I also had the tea cake (400 lkr = 1.10$) which was very nice!
location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: Waste of time, they don't care and won't tell you anything
text: I don't know, what happend to the place, but it was ABSOLUTE waste of time.. A company guide rushed a group of us through the factory (like 5' tour) Then we were shown the area where all different teas were available for sale. I asked the guide nicely, if we can get some more information and even see the plantation and other staff, she told us they are busy, but she can give us the tour again, we saw they are not busy, so we told her, we can see they are not busy, so she told us it is not safe to go to the field, it was raining and it's not safe (it was not raining for a week). So we got the feeling they don't care about anything else then sales, so we left very dissapointed. It's not worth of visit at all! There is a large decking viewing area at this establishment.. Where you can look at the rows of tea bushes, under it you will find the poor locals, begging for you to throw a few notes over the handrail of the decking. You only find out information once you actually leave and the guide explains more.
location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: Well organised tour
text: Well organised tour. We were picked up from our hotel and driven to the factory for the tour. The tour was really interesting and enjoyable. Highly recommended
location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: Beautiful tea plantation
text: Stopped here on our tour. I have to say this was an exceptional tour with a very knowledgeable guide. Very informative. We have visited tea plantations in India, Kerala, China and Nepal and I have to say this was by far the best experience The staff in the shop were very helpful. Purchased some beautiful teas at a very good price. Would highly recommend stopping off here.
location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: Quality single estate tea from Damro, Labookellie, Sri Lanka.
text: For centuries known as Mackwood Labookellie Tea Estate, the name of the tea estate has been changed to Damro Tea Estate recently on transfer of the estate to the Damro business group. The showroom is located in situ at Labookellie Tea Estate right on the main road from Kandy to Newerelia. The huge bill boards near the entrance are helpful to easily locate the show room. The showroom has been extensively renovated with ample parking space and comfortable seating area. The top quality of the original Mackwood Labookellie Tea Estate is still maintained. The visitors are given free tea tasting of the single estate tea from the estate. The quality of tea is very good and the prices are quite reasonable. Visitors from India can consider taking many packets of Indian sweets like Son Papdi which is in huge demand by the sales executives at the showroom. The sales executives are polite, smiling and neatly dressed in traditional Sri Lankan attire. Highly recommended for the conoseuers of authentic single estate Sri Lankan tea.
location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: Pleasant even in the rain
text: Stopped for a tour and to b sold local tea, but it was a pleasant stop. There was a short interesting tour of the factory and then a tea tasting. Unfortunately we were only offered English Breakfast Tea when there was an opportunity to sample some of the more exotic teas on sale.
location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: Informative tour but very busy.
text: Our driver chose this particular tea factory to visit, this was the only one we had time to visit so have nothing to compare it with in regards to having a better experience elsewhere. We went on a Sunday which is the only day of the week where the factory is not running so you don’t get to see any of the processes or ladies out in the plantations picking tea. The tour through the factory was very informative but somewhat rushed and difficult to hear as this is a very popular tour spot, so other groups are hot on your heels as you make your way around the factory. The tour is free and you are given a complimentary cup of tea on completion, your guide will also try and upsell you in to purchasing an overpriced piece of cake to go with your cuppa. You are not pressured into purchasing tea however if you wish to buy tea the shop was extremely busy and understaffed so hard to get any info on any tea that you want to purchase as well as pricing. We did find out why our driver took us to visit this particular factory as we noticed as soon as we purchased he disappeared and came back with his free packet of tea. The outlook of all the tea plants for as far as the eye could see was stunning and we did gain useful info regarding the process from the tour, would have preferred to visit when the factory was working.
location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: Insightful and Pleasant
text: We visited on a Saturday morning and the drive from Nuwara Eliya to Damro is not far but the views was absolutely breathtaking as it was a clear morning and seeing the people working in the plantations was an amazing sight. At the tea factory we were taken on a tour by a very knowledgeable guide and we truly enjoyed it and learned a lot. We then had a very nice cup of tea to finish off the tour. They do offer tours (safari) into the tea plantations but we did not do that. Would recommend a visit. We did find the shop a bit expensive.
location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: " a sales push exercise. "
text: Having visited this establishment on a Sunday... ( CLOSED...), which the guide we used didn't know.. ABSOLUTE waste of time.. A company guide literally rushed a group of us through the factory.. It was empty of employees, and so we saw nothing of how the process works... It took no more than 10mins to go through to the area where we Began the tour.. Then we were shown the the area where all different teas were available for sale.. So for me it's purely a 'sales push..' Total waste of time in my opinion There is a large decking viewing area at this establishment.. Where you can look at the rows of tea bushes.. Under this decking you will find the very very poor locals, who have no income or jobs.. Begging for you to throw a few notes over the handrail of the decking.. The tea pluckers earn around 2,000 rupees per day.( aprox £5.) They have to pluck 20kgs per day for that pay.. So sad .. Would never return.. You only find out information once you actually leave and the guide explains more...

Tour lasted about 30 minutes, showing the different processes that the tea passed through, followed by a nice cup of black tea in the cafÃ©. location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden

text: My favourite part was the tour and how they really explained it Tips for future Travellers get the tea cake and the chocolate cake it is amazing the tea is absolutely awesome ??
location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: Tea for Two Or Twenty-Two

location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: Worth a short visit
text: There is no charge for the short 15 minute very professional description of the tea harvesting and factory processes while walking through the factory. For safety reasons, unlike some where you walk past moving machinery, this was conducted on walkways behind glazed views. And then into the tea rooms for a complimentary cup, very pleasant. Perhaps the whole structure and operation is a little too modern and clinically presented for some, and while there are hills of tea bushes around the factory and a modern tea room they are not the most photogenic.

title: Tea Factory Tour

location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: A welcom cup of tea
text: We were driving from Peradeniya to Nuwara Eliya and our driver guide suggested we stop at the Damo Tea Centre for a break and a cup of tea. location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: BAD experience! Unprofessional in their service. Saving grace is the security guy that shelters you from our car!
text: Damro Tea Plantation BAD Experience! Too touristy and staff are not interested and not personal. Biggest regret as Sri Lanka are filled with many nice places and people. Damro staff are more interested in selling than service. In Dec 2019 before the onset of Covid19, I was personally guided around the tea plantation by a fair local girl that gave me the impression very blankly that she did NOT want to be there at all. I asked for permission to take picture of the tea process and accidentally had a picture of her looking nonchalant and sulky inside my picture! A picture paints a thousand word! have since submitted my feedback to my travel agent who checks in on my mum and I everyday. This same girl’s face only lighted up very slightly when my mum and I started purchasing many teas. Another incident that disappoints me was the complimentary black tea which we declined as it was already mid afternoon and we were afraid that the caffeine will affect our sleep when we arrive at Nuwara Eliya. Thus we requested for chamomile or peppermint tea that they said coat Sri Lankan Rupees 700 (USD3.80) which was not expensive but the tea arrived COLD! This is an abomination to a lovely country that prides itself as a top tea country! It was a rainy day in the hills and that was the last thing my poor old mum needed. Very disappointed with the entire experience! I would avoid all the “touristy” restaurants with big tour buses as we were on a private tour as the guide will have a tendency to bring the tourists there for reasons we all know why... so do your homework and have your travel agent give you a detailed itinery as to where to eat etc..we had a wonderful travel agent and I shall visit Sri Lanka again just NEVER to return to DAMRO!
location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden
title: Tea plantation

After that, you'll be shown around the factory floors where you can see the process of grading, drying and conditioning the tea leaves. It's a short tour, perhaps 20 minutes, but very interesting. After the tour, you can browse in the shop if you wish to buy any of the products. Very good.
location_name_key: damro labookellie tea centre and tea garden

location_name: Damro Labookellie Tea Centre and Tea Garden

title: Over priced tea factory
text: Damro Tea plantation has a big tea estate that caters to local and export needs. We had a brief 20 minutes tour of the factory. Picking of the tea leaves is once a week. The picked leaves are placed in huge belts to dry where huge air blowers blow air to aid in the drying process. This takes about 14 hours of drying. It takes 5 kg fresh leaves to make 1 kg of black tea. Once the leaves are dried they are sent down to the machine where it's rolled and cut as per the requirements. Then they are placed on the table for fermentation where the process of oxidation changes the colour of the tea leaves. No fermentation for green and white tear. Then the leaves are sent to the Dryer machine to stop fermentation to turn to black colour. After this they are sent to the Grading machine for different quality of grading - strong, medium, light. The tour ends with complimentary light black tea. For the huge acres of tea estate and the fact that it's a factory the rates should've been cheaper than the markets. Was very surprised to see such expensive rates.

title: Shrouded in Mystery
text: Damro was the first tea factory we visited in Sri Lanka. It was recommended by several tuktuk drivers and our homestay host. The tour was complimentary and lasted about 20 minutes, as we walked through the factory. We visited on New Year so there were no leaves being blow-dried. Our guide looked tired and recited off a script. She did nonetheless entertain our pesky questions well. After the tour we got to taste a cup each of FF1 tea in the lounge, but sadly we weren’t particularly impressed. Strangely, there wasn’t the option to try other types of tea - we would have wanted to try the loose leaf types like OP and BOP which we later discovered were more to our liking. We were, funnily enough, allowed to buy cakes, which admittedly were cheap and decent. Ultimately, as we had liked our host’s tea, which was from damro, we proceeded to make the mistake of buying too much tea on our first stop. It was only after visiting the Mackwoods museum in Nuwara Eliya’s city centre that we found out more about the history of Damro - it was a furniture company that had just (as of 2016) ventured into the plantation business, acquiring great swathes of land, including the Labookellie tea lounge, and a significant stake in the Mackwoods brand (the second oldest tea company after the parent company of Lipton). Make what you will of our experience - we still can’t figure out if we are happy with our purchases 4 days later. But the experience as a whole was somewhat uncanny. The price of tea in the gift shop we found to be average - higher than the Zesta / Lipton types in supermarkets but lower than most single-estate tea companies we visited elsewhere in Sri Lanka. Our advice would be to stay off the teabags (which we tasted and found to be quite ordinary) and stick to the loose leaf teas.

title: Mixed feelings... worker exploitation vs. great tour
text: We visited this place during our honeymoon and we have very mixed feelings about it, including how the tea pickers are treated... On one hand, our guide Salley - who used to be an employee himself - was informative, accommodating, and took us on a fascinating 30-40 minute tour of the tea factory, ending in a short tea tasting session. On the flip side, we were horrified to learn (we only found this out by asking the question) that the tea pickers who are so often glamourised by Halpewatte (and indeed other tea plantations and factories as well, not to mention on the tea packaging itself) earn just +/- $4 a day. $4 to start work every day at 7:30am in the scorching sun, barefoot, picking tea leaves and throwing them into a sack they carry on their backs. The drying room is also so hot and dark that we could not spend more than 1 minute in there - it had to have been the same temperature as a steam room with NO AIR CON. How do the workers survive day in and day out in these conditions?? Plus, the tea pickers will only earn their daily wage if they pick 15kgs of leaves that day. If you put that into perspective, $4 is the approximate price for a small box of Halpe tea in the factory shop. It doesn’t add up and it’s certainly not a fair distribution of the company’s clearly massive turnover. We also learned that the local guy who owns Halpewatte also owns the £600-a-night 98 Acres resort where we stayed and the zip line and activity pad nearby. And he can’t give his tea pickers more than $4 a day? We were batted down by the reassurance that the “government is looking to increase the daily wage to 1000 rupees”. That’s approximately $5 a day. Shame on him.

title: A Must Visit
text: Mr Siva gave us a comprehensive and informative talk about this Estate and the Sri Lankan Tea industry. We have been on quite a few tea factory tours with various groups, but this was definitely one of the better ones. The factory shop has a good range of teas for sale at reasonable prices. One word of warning if going in wet weather: the driveway to the factory is fairly steep in parts, but the view is lovely from the top!

title: Great tour, money well spent
text: I did the tour here & it surpassed my expectations. Siva the tour guide was very passionate & knowledgeable about all aspects of making tea. I walked out much better for it. Well worth the time & effort.

title: Wonderful and Interesting Tea Factory Tour
text: Really wanted to visit a tea factory during my solo trip through Sri Lanka and I heard about this facility. It was very easy to reach them, especially if you’re already in the Ella area. The tour is really well done because it combines the history of the tea growing industry, and shares with you the practices of how tea is grown, harvested, and processed. I enjoyed learning how teas are differentiated and classified but by far the best part of the tour was our guide “Sallay” ... a very knowledgeable and dignified gentleman who made the tour interesting for all the people in the tour, the sweet little children included. The next best part of the tour for me was just being in the factory watching the dignified workers processing the leaves throughout the entire process. The tour took about an hour and you will climb and descend a few flights of stairs so please be sure you’re able to climb stairs safely. There’s a nice gift shop that takes all credit cards and offers some of the most majestic panoramic views imaginable.

title: Informed tour
text: We went on a morning tour and enjoyed it thoroughly. Planned trip on the Sunday could not go ahead as it was a poya day. On the day we went (Mon), tours were taking place, but not as a full working facility. In hindsight that's was better, as it would be very noisy. After the tour, we sampled tea and could buy at factory prices. Much cheaper than anywhere else we visited to buy here. Our guide had very good English and good humour

title: Tea factory
text: We were advised to go, and it was definitely worth it. A really great tour by Sallay, could not recommend him highly enough.

title: Very insightful and Interesting
text: We thoroughly enjoyed our tour. Very insightful and interesting but to see the working factory in such detail was really great. Siva was our guide and very thorough explaining every detail and also passionate about high quality tea making - he was able to answer every question. Would suggest this tour if you’re in Ella and can fit it in, great view from the cafe at the top and lots of products to purchase with absolutely no pressure to buy.

title: Great tour - learnt loads about tea!
text: Silva was a fantastic tour guide, very knowledgeable and interesting. Great to see all the different processes of tea making and learn the different types of tea. Cost £2.50 each inc tea tasting at the end. Great shop and cafe at the end without any pressure to buy anything. Would recommend whilst in Ella - particularly good activity for when it’s raining!

title: Very informative tour
text: We took a very informative tour around the tea factory - Siva really knows his stuff and was engaging and friendly! Thanks!

title: Lovely views
text: I went out of tea season so the factory was not producing tea. However they still run regular tours of the factory. Tea tasting of the 4 types of black tea they produce and all good quality. The shop sells its tea at really good prices. The drive up was interesting but the view was really lovely so worth a visit

title: Positeav review
text: Our host SIVA was very knowledgeable. Had a great tour with him today at the tea factory. Learned a lot of tea and the science behind it. Also, great gift shop at the end of the tour and AHMAZING view.

title: Sallay was a Wonderful Tour Guide
text: I had a choice to visit a number of tea factories during my visit in Sri Lanka, however, I chose to visit the Halpewatte Tea Factory and I'm so glad I did. The factory tour was very impressive ... I had no idea how much effort was put into making tea Sallay, the group's guide was was informative and gave us all a wonderful tour. He ensured we understood the steps the tea leaves went through in order to become the beverages we enjoy and his explanations were detailed but easy to follow. It was obvious he enjoys his job at this tea factory and that made me feel especially good to support this facility.

title: Sensational tour
text: We visited the factory around midday following our hike up Ella Rock. I was expecting the factory to be non-operational at that time as all the processing happens early in the morning/night (for temperature reasons). We paid 1050 rupee for 2 x adults for an “education only tour”. Our guide was Siva & he is hands down the best tour guide we have come across. His English is perfect, and his knowledge is incredible. He explains the whole process very clearly & makes you think about how much engineering & production goes into your humble morning cuppa! There is a gift shop at the end but the prices are very reasonable & there is certainly no hard sale. Our Tuk-Tuk cost us 1300 rupee from Ella & included wait time - we felt this was very reasonable as the whole trip probably took about 1.5-2hrs. I would highly recommend this tour to anyone visiting Ella!

title: Amazing expirience!
text: The tour was very interesting with lots of new information. The guide Salley was so nice, funny, polite, has exellant english and we could feel it was important for him that we will have great time there. After this tour we much more appreciatee our good cup of tea :) Thank you salley!

title: Great informative tour
text: Great fun tour with Sallay! He really knew his stuff about tea and as went at 9am we saw the production line still going which was so cool! Learnt about how they make each tea, growing and picking process and of course export to Europe info! Finished with tasting 4 teas - yummy! Would recommend! Takes about an hour, not suitable for anyone with a physical disability as very steep stairs and access points.

title: Great fun!
text: We visited the Halpewatte Tea Factory on our way to Nuwara Eliya. We took the tea tour - lead by a passionate and insightful expert who took the time to explain the intricacies of tea picking and production, taking in the massive - skillfully engineered - machines and culminating with a tea tasting session. Good fun all round and highly recommended!

title: Great tour and tea and views
text: Go in the morning when the factory is working to see the full production process. The tours go every half hour and finish with a tasting of 4 teas, ending in the shop. The factory is high up so also has great views. Well worth the climb for an informative insight into how your daily cuppa is made. Charge for the tour is around 500 rupees.

title: Great morning tour
text: We had a great time seeing how they make the tea. We got to see how the machines work then got to try the different types of tea at the end. We did buy some tea :)

title: Site Ã visiter absolument
text: We visited the factory on a Saturday afternoon. Unfortunately there was no production. The Sivanathan guide was there and he make to us a truly exceptional visit. He knows his subject, he shows us everything and explains it in detail. Thanks to him we are aware of the whole process of making black tea. Thanks to Sivanathan for the work you do.

title: Not on a weekend
text: We visited here on a Saturday as we were passing, which was a bit disappointing as while their website says they were open, no actual staff apart from presentations or the shop, are working. Therefore any descriptions of the process would not be accompanied with action, which we had seen earlier in our trip at Damro Labookellie Tea Lounge, and for free, whereas here they wanted 600 rupees each for the presentation. To be honest being empty on a Saturday it looked a little abandoned and there were not good photo opportunities around the factory for rolling hills of tea bushes.

title: Great explanations with enthusiastic guide
text: We had a great visit with a guide from Halpewatte tea factory. Best choice is to grab a tuk tuk and get yourself a ticket inside with a guide from the building. We had a very enthusiastic one that knew all the details about production as well as the engineering behind the machines. You could see the passion of the guide regarding his job while he talked about the factory. They will give you different teas in the end for you to taste the difference of the several types of extractions.

title: Very interesting, new facts about tea manufacturing
text: Was there with my mother. Interesting place, very funny and nice guide. We enjoyed and found lot of new information about tea manufacturing.

title: Tea for two year old
text: We were apprehensive that this tour would be a step too far for our two year old granddaughter but she actually got very excited by the tea being produced and was a big hit with the workers. The guide was very informative and answered questions well. Good value!

title: Fine dining
text: Quite a stylish restaurant which serves fab tea and eats. A little pricey compared to others nearby but worth it

title: Thank you Siv?
text: Our guide Siv? speaks very good english so we could hear a very interesting story about tea production. He did his best to give us all the necessary information. I recommend this place to visit.

title: Good tour
text: 1300rp tuk tuk return from ella. 480 for tour which consisted of talk, tour of the plantation and tea tasting. Was a good thing to do in Ella.

title: Great tea tour
text: We did the tour with Mister Rajha and was very interesting, we learn about all the tea procces in a interactive way. I highly recommend to do it.

title: Well worth the visit
text: Very informative and engaging tour of the tea factory by our knowledgeable guide Rajha. We learnt about how tea is made and were able to see three steps of the process happening within the factory during our 3pm tour. If you wish to see the entire process happening, it is recommended you arrive at 8am.

title: Great factory tour with Mr. Sallay
text: We had the best afternoon with Mr.Sallay at this tea factory where he in a vivid and colorful way and with much enthusiasm took us thru the whole process of tea production. We highly recommend having a guided tour with him and to visit this authentic and beautifully located factory.

title: Visit to the tea factory
text: LOVED Siva's intelligent way of explaining the world of tea to us. Would absolutely recommend a visit. We walked all the way from Ella to the tea factory which was quite a nice stroll with lovely views.

title: Siva most amazing tour guide, the best story teller there is
text: We had a great tour, Siva was our guide made the tour very interesting. We asked some of the workers in the fields how much they make and they said that they are supposed to make 1000 rupees a day but that the owners only pay 700. Maybe one day the government will protect those who need it most.

title: Tour in the Factory
text: Excellent factory tour in a massive tea factory. Whole process was well explained. At the end of the tour we were given different qualities of tea to taste.

title: Well worth the trip
text: Very interesting to see and hear the tour information. Great views from the top as well. Great presentation by the guide.

title: A great tourguide
text: We had a great time at this tea factory. The tourguide named Sallah gave us a very good explanation on the proces of teamaking. His english is very good and he really wants to share his great knowledge on tea with you. Afterwards he let’s you taste the different types of tea and you can enjoy the view from their balcony overlooking the fields.

title: Interesting tour
text: It's a bit confusing when you arrive here but watch for a vistors sign and head through the factory and up to the top floor to get on a tour Cost was 500 rupees per person Interesting tour with a guide who spoke good English and was knowledgeable about the factory Great seeing the tea actually being processed A nice way to spend an hour or 2. Get a tuk tuk from Ella- the driver will wait for you

title: Informative.
text: Expect to pay a tuk tuk driver in downtown Ella between LKR 1300-1500 to take you up there, wait for you, then bring you back into town. Round trip about 2 hours including the very informative tour. Entertaining tour guide. A bit like an over-enthusiastic headmaster :) Naturally, you exit through the gift shop but not before they give you a taste of what you’ve just seen being made. Prices not bad at all. Just a pity we didn’t actually get out into the plantation and closer to the beautiful scenery but there’s another tea plantation en route and your tuk tuk driver will be only too happy to stop to let you take pics of tea being picked. Worth your time.

title: Very Informative
text: Visited today and was thoroughly entertained and informed by this tour. Provided an excellent insight into the process. Much like a wine tasting tour we learned of the different tastes and processes done to reach it. Bought up in the shop afterwards too for gifts.

title: Great tea tasting and shop!
