title: Siva is brilliant!!’
text: Loved this tour, Siva our guide was so passionate and knowledgeable about tea and just made us appreciate it so much more. We were able to learn all the process of making tea and do some tasting before buying some of the factory’s own product.

title: As if I could have loved tea any more!
text: I have loved tea since I can remember, yet I didn't really have any clue about it. Rajha gave us a wonderful tour and explained the whole tea-making process. We visited in the afternoon so the factory wasn't actually in full swing, but we were taken to every area and it was really enjo

title: Great guide
text: Good explanation of the tea making process and a very enthusiastic guide. We went on a Poya day, so most of the factory was closed, would probably be a bit more exciting if we hadn't visited on a national holiday!

title: Fascinating
text: this really was quite a drive, so if yuk tuk driver recommends they wait for you to finish tour say yes! There are no tuk tuks waiting for pick ups and we were very grateful knowing we didn't have to walk balk down the hill! The tour itself was absolutely fascinating, in fact the highlight of our trip in Ella. Our guide was very knowledgeable and extremely passionate about the tea making process. We were lucky to be shown around while the machines were still in operation - this definitely added to our experience ( I believe machines are operated at different times of the day in different seasons- work a check before visiting).

title: Uva tea time!
text: What a drive, but what a view! The road heading up is pretty much a single-lane country dirt road and as you head up you're hoping that you don't have to face on-coming traffic. Once you get up there to the top, you'll realize that the view here is pretty amazing. The guard at the door directed us up a flight of stairs which led to more flights of stairs that led up to the top of the factory building. For a minute it seemed like there was no tour to be offered and we were just walking to the top where the sales shop happened to be. But as we reached the top of the final set of stairs, a woman at a register greeted us and asked for 450 rs ;-) (The tour price per person). So this is where the tour starts! I thought it seemed a bit odd, to have guests have to walk up the flight twice (to get to the tour which takes place after you head back down and then again to finish the tour). Anyway, my friend and I paid and waited for the tour to start. It didn't take long. There was already a sizeable group standing by. When you arrive walk up multiple flights of stairs to get to the sales/tasting floor. This is where you pay for your tour and wait for it to start. I arrived with a decent sized group already waiting. Then it was back down the stairs, grab a seat and listen to a lecture about the process of tea picking, selecting, sorting, etc. Our tour leader was enthusiastic and very informative as well as open to questions all about tea and the various types of tea produced in the country. Afterwards, everyone got up and followed him through the factory to see the men and machines at work (and women too). My one complaint is that the group is so large it's difficult to hear the information when our tour leader spoke. No photos allowed here! Once back upstairs we were offered a sampling of 4 different levels of tea strengths/types. If only I had more room in my suitcase! I would've purchased more. (If they took credit cards then I probably would have bought more too). If you like tea then definitely stop by. They produce tea from the Uva area of Sri Lanka. There's a sampler box of tea featuring the various regions' tea for purchase as well!

title: Worth a trip for tea lovers
text: For only a few dollars you can see the whole tea factory and tea making process. And the place smells amazing, so much tea! The tour includes tea sampling which completes the tour nicely. There is a shop where you can buy what you just sampled and some other varieties.

title: Learned so much about tea!
text: This visit was super informative, and you get to go up close and personally see the tea processing. Make sure to call ahead and ensure they're processing tea that day so you can see all the action!

title: Interesting and enthusiastic tour guide
text: We visited the factory on a Sunday when there is no production. However, they still ran a tour lasting about 20-30 minutes explaining tea production and ended with sampling 5 different teas, varying in strength. It was informative and the guide used good English and answered all our questions. I'd imagine if the factory was operational and all staff in, it would've been a 5 star experience.

title: Great to be able to see the production in process
text: Very good guide with 40+ years of experience in the tea business. Great to see the large bags of tea leaves coming in and going through the various stages of the production while being on the tour. Enhanced our understanding of tea!

title: No production sunday, monday
text: If you want to see the factory at work apparently the best time to come is around 8-8:30 on any day except sunday and monday (monday is picking day). Friendly person at factory explained this to us. The tuk tuk drivers won't tell you this beforehand - they make easy money.

title: Great tour! Recommend
text: We walked from Ella centre and it took about 45 minutes - quite a steep climb at the end. Views are worth it when you get to the top. We then got a tuk tuk back for 500rp. We went on a Tuesday and arrived around 11am. By this time production was almost over, but we were in time to see some of the factory still operating, showing the final steps in production. The tour lasted about 45 minutes and the tour guide was excellent, very knowledgable and entertaining too. Tea tasting at the end. Value for money!

title: best money we ever spent
text: We went here on a saturday- the factory was not working but it was nontheless very interesting and informative!! Our tour guide explained everything really well, knew all the answers to our questions. He was the greatest <3 Tea degustation at the end was really nice too, I didn't even know there were different types of black tea :D There is also a shop wehere you can buy tea. Go here with tuk tuk from Ella town centre (1200 rupees to go there and back- its really OK price since it is a bit far)

title: Our own personal guided tour!
text: We turned up here in the afternoon, and had missed the day's production. The place was deserted, but we were asked if we would like the tour anyway, and after paying our entrance fees (they let the kids in for free!), we were given a highly entertaining and educational private tour by one of the guides there. After giving us the theory of tea lesson, he took us around the factory, and showed us all the various stages of tea production. The kids found it very interesting, and even tried all the different teas at the end of the tour! The location is stunning. To fully appreciate it, we walked there from Ella then took a tuk-tuk back into town afterwards. Highly recommended for all!

title: Enthusiastic black tea guided tour
text: Black tea is good. Green tea is bad. And the tour is highly entertaining with much detail, good tea tasting afterwards, nice tea souvenir shop. The "slight" bias towards black tea was very entertaining. Also the q&a that felt a lot like in school. You better have s.o. ask questions. Overall clearly the best tea factory tour by far.

title: Fantastic introduction to the world of tea!
text: We arrived at the tea factory around 13 and it was already too late to see the production, HOWEVER, please stay for the tour, it is really worth it (also, since there is no factory noise, it is better to hear the detailed explanation of how the tea is made)! Our guide was Rajha, who is an absolute star! Very warm and friendly, he knows all the secrets of tea making and brewing ;-) the tour starts with a class and all the production steps are explained, and then we went to see where each of them takes place. Rajha shows you everything and explains it in a very interesting way. There is a tea tasting in the end and once you are educated you can really distinguish the different kinds of tea. All in all, the tour is a great way to spend an hour or so :-) highly recommend!!

title: Great Tour, simple no frills but very informative! Lovely view!!!
text: We really enjoyed our tour here and I actually went back again to bring my mom a second time. Rajha was our guide and he was passionate about tea and was an amazing guide! Just know that production is early in the morning (first tour at 8 am) and it's so good to see the whole place in action. We rented our own scooter and drove up (although the road is a bit windy and steep) but it's a gorgeous view from the top (and on the way!). For 300 rsp, it's a bargain tour. We visited other tea factories in Sri Lanka and this was by far our favourite!

title: You must go!
text: We visited the tea factory and it was great. It was about 10 mins in a tuktuk from Ella, and it's a bargain at only 300SRP for the tour. We were there on a non production day, but this didn't make any difference to how enjoyable it was and we still saw lots of the tea making process and they turned the machines on. Siva the guide was excellent, very knowledgeable and funny, he made the tour. At the end you get to try the tea and there's a little shop.

title: I finally understand tea!
text: Best 300 rps I've spent in Sri Lanka. I learned so much about tea in a way I will never forget. We arrived at 2:15 pm and although most of the factory was not in production, what I really missed was hot noisy machines at work. Instead the factory was quiet and unrealistically serene, which felt nice for its location. Throughout the sit down explanation portion of the tour we had the time to calmly ask questions and we never felt rushed. The tour was peaceful and the quiet factory machinery were strangely perfumed with the aroma of orange pekoe. After the tour we had a chance to sample several different types of teas, and pick our favorite. The gift shop was also open, which allowed us to purchase the exact tea we sampled. A must "tea" for tea lovers and everyone alike. On a side note. Hire a tuk tuk to the factory. Save your energy for nicer hikes in and around Ella.

title: Rajha superbe guide!
text: We were advised by our guesthouse to go to this factory and we were really pleased! Not only it it one of the biggest producer of tea in Sri Lanka, we also had the privilege to have rajha as our guide! A very knowledgeable guide! Thanks! And thumbs up for the view on the terrasse!

title: Tea-riffic
text: Siva's tour was spirited, in depth, and he provided great tea recommendations after the tour. Make sure you get there very very early if you want to see the production, but the explanation tour is quite nice as well.

title: Good low key attraction
text: We visited the green tea factory. It is quite small.Very reasonable and low key. We went onto the factory floor and saw the processes. The visit lasted about 20 minutes.

title: Very Interesting
text: A very interesting tour - learnt a lot about tea and the production line. Most of the production had finished for the day so might be better to visit in the morning but still got to see the final stages which were still great to see. Tours seem to go every hour and cost 300rs and last between 40mins and an hour so well worth the money. you get to sample the different strengths of tea produced here so you have an idea of what youre buying is you get some from the little shop. the views from the top are great even though it was pretty misty when we went. Got a tuttut from Ella 1000rs return as it was poring with rain - you can walk but there is some steep hills.

title: Informative and scenic - we walked there from Ella
text: Worth seeing even if they are not producing tea at the time (when we went, they stopped producing tea at 8am). The guide was very informative and VERY passionate about the quality of tea (woe to low land tea and flavoured teas). We had lots of fun and learned a lot. We walked from Ella town. The walk took around 1 hr 10 mins and was very straightforward. The walk is quite scenic, among tea plantatinos and with some nice views. You can catch a tuk tuk of course very reasonably. Or even flag one down halfway if you get tired.

title: Must do in Ella!
text: We cannot rave enough about this tour! They run hourly (not usually in production though as that happens during the night) and it is super interesting and informative for only 300 lkr. Our guide Rajah was fabulous! Very knowledgeable and a funny personality. At the end they do make a deal of buying tea but we did because it was a great gift and good quality tea. It's about 6ks out from Ella. We paid 500 lkr for a Tuktuk as it's completely up hill. Don't miss this factory while in Ella! Beautiful views as well form the top

title: Informative visit to Halpewatte Tea Factory
text: Had a nice visit to the tea factory. Although people were not producing tea at the time of visit. We were still able to see the whole factory and how everything worked. Our guide Rajha was great, easy to understand and informative. Answered all questions with great knowledge and enthusiasm. Got to taste some different teas also. Great views from the top we're you start the tour. All in all a nice way to spend a few hours and learn abit more about tea. Short ride from Ella on a tuk-tuk and they will wait for you and take your back for 1200-1500

title: Great short tour to learn so many things!!
text: We arrived around 8:30am to the factory and our visit with Rajha started very shortly after that. He first made us sit around a table (we were 2 couples in total!) and made us smell, touch and feel the different tea leaves. We then walked around the factory where workers were actively sorting, fanning ... Rajha who worked all his life from bottom to management of a tea factory explained us carefully all the different steps of the production, as well as the distribution (Colombo tea exchange! ). We eventually finished the visit with some tasting! Loved it, definitely recommend going there and more especially Rajha if you can have a hold of him!

title: Great way to spend the morning
text: Our tour was very informative and unhurried. Rajah really loves his job and gave us a good insight into tea production. We saw all the processes and the place was rich tapestry of sound and smells, also great for kids as there is a lot to hold there attention.

title: Great morning out
text: We went to visit the factory on the 2nd January when there was no production, but our guide explained it very well how they produce the tea. It's very interesting and educational. The guide even turned on some of the machines, so he could better demonstrate the processes. I wish we visited on a day when there was production, but it was still really interesting. I think they run guided tours hourly, so you just turn up and can get on the next tour. It's a long way from the center, so you will need a tuktuk driver who is willing to wait for you. Our driver was called by our guesthouse, so we knew how much it will cost up front. All in all, a good trip.

title: Don't miss it
text: Well worth a visit! The normal tour lasts about 3 hours but we asked for a condensed version and were out in less than an hour. I have a lot more respect for tea now! Very knowledgeable guide and really interesting to see the whole process.

title: Fascinating, & stunning views!
text: We went here on a Wednesday (day after Poya day as we had heard the factory would be shut then). We walked here all the way from the bottom of the winding road up - a good 30 min walk but some stunning scenery to look at on the way! We arrived and found the factory wasn't operating at that time (around 3pm) but we were in time for a tour, costing 300R per person. Our tour was conducted by Siva who was so knowledgeable and passionate about tea! It made it all the better having him as our guide. He took us to the first floor to learn about the different parts of the tea plant, how the plants are dealt with after picking, and ultimately what ends up making its way into your cup of tea - be it loose leaf or teabags. We were fortunate that after this informative session on the tea plant, a number of tea pickers arrived with freshly picked tea leaves and the factory seemed to spring into life - so we were able to see some of the machines in action. Overall, there is a lot to take in, but the tour was done so well by Siva and he was able to answer any question you could throw at him! We finished the tour by sampling the four main types of tea produced and sold from the factory. We also bought some tea (500R for 100g). Overall, would highly recommend this factory, and thanks to Siva for a great tour!

title: A fascinating tour
text: Six of us turned up on a Sunday without realising there is no tea production or tours that day, but the lovely knowledgeable tour guide Siva gave us a brilliant private tour anyway. It actually helped having no production as we had a free run of the place and we probably saw things we wouldn't on an ordinary day. Our guide Siva worked in the industry for 40 years and really does know all there is to know about tea; how it's grown, produced and marketed and all about the history, which for a group of tea-drinking Brits was fascinating to learn about. We were taken through all areas of the factory and shown every aspect of the production line. It helps that Siva speaks perfect English. There's a lovely tea shop on the top floor and we even got a 15% off voucher for a new local restaurant called Ceylon Tea Factory. One tip - make sure you get a tuk tuk or taxi from Ella as it's a 1.7km uphill walk to the factory if you get the bus. All in all it would be criminal to visit tea country and not find out what's made it famous; this is a great place to learn! And at less than £2 for a tour it's well worth it.

title: Make sure you get here before 4pm
text: Unfortunately my visit here was a bit disappointing. Be warned that the drive up along the winding path was a bit hairy. Upwards steep and winding. I think this place has the potential to be a nice visit but we arrived after 4pm. The last factory tour is at 4pm and they don't serve tea or anything after 4pm despite the fact that they closed at 5pm. We couldn't even order a pot of tea. The tea store was rather small and very limited. The views from the balcony are spectacular though.

title: One of our favourite tours!!
text: We were shown around by Siva he was an amazing tour guide who was so passionate and knowledgeable about his job making us so much more appreciative of the work that goes into a cup of tea! We went on a Sunday so there was no production but he showed us all the machines in action. Highly recommended :) Plus the view is stunning!

title: Well worth the trip
text: I took a tuk tuk from Ella - 1500lkr return incl waiting- it’s a long uphill walk otherwise from Halpe. The tour was super interesting - I never knew how complex tea-making was! Got to walk around the working factory and try tea at the end. It cost 550lkr. Well worth it!

title: Guided tour
text: Great tour. Our guide explained whole tea process clearly and was also passionated about it. Would recommend to everyone! Only annoying thing here was some ignorant tourists who didn't follow the rules like no smoking in the area or take pictures inside factory.

title: Super interesting
text: We really enjoyed our informative tour at this factory. Shiva, the tour leader, was very engaging, has worked there a long time and emphasized the importance of tea and the history of tea. He also explained the tea making process in depth as well as all the different grades of tea. We also had a little taster at the end. Kudos to Shiva, we really enjoyed him!

title: Excellent thing to do in Ella
text: A very informative and interesting tour. They give you a ”lecture” first about the teas and the tea making process. Then they show you the factory thorougly. Tuktuk from Ella 20 minutes, tour about 1 hour. Tuktuk driver will wait for you at the factory to get you back. Easy road to go by your self too if you want to rent a scooter or a tuktuk for you to drive! At times quite hard to understand the guide’s english.

title: Frustrating
text: There were 40 (I counted) people in our tour group. The guide was nice but spoke with a very heavy accent and we could only make out about 20% of what he was saying. But that didn’t matter as when we were at the back of the group we couldn’t hear anything anyway. The snippets of information we got were quite interesting and it was nice to see the inner workings of the factory. Not sure why they couldn’t split us into 2 or 3 groups and stagger the visits to start at 10 minute intervals. Tea in the gift shop is horrendously overpriced, but having said that we bought some and so did everyone else. Overall got the feeling no one cared that visitors had a good experience, just that they made the maximum profit possible. With a few tweaks this could be a lovely experience as all the basic ingredients are there, but that would mean management and staff attitudes have to change.

title: TO BIG GROUP
text: They have a group every half an hour no matter how big it is.. So our group was over 40 people big. In the classroom somehow we still understood the guide, between the machines was not possible. 10 people should be maximum for a group. With 500 rp entry they earn with visitors more than with tea...

title: Hire a scooter to get here - cheaper than the tuk tuks
text: Worth the effort to visit, to see the process and enjoy the stunning views. We hired a scooter for the afternoon that gave us freedom and came in at half the price of the tuk tuks - surely more expensive in Ella than anywhere else in Sri Lanka. One useful tip - don’t buy the tea at the factory, buy it from the Ceylon Tea Factory Restaurant (also part of their empire and serving great food) in Town where it is 40% cheaper - the scallywags. Lost a star from us for that.

title: Informative to the brim
text: The title says it all. The gentleman that guided us first introduced the picking, separating and thedifferences between teas after which we got to see the facilities. Unfortunately it was Saturday, close to national holiday, which meant that the factory wasn't working. Still, it was a visit well worth making.

title: Informative tour
text: We headed up there just before ten o’clock. We only had a short wait for the next available tour. We are a family with children aged 9, 7 and 3yo. Although the children weren’t exactly thrilled to do a tea plantation tour, they all got progressively more and more interested as the tour went along and they got involved by the guide, who although has a strong Sri Lankan accent when spoke English (which was sometimes difficult to understand) is a real character and keep us all interested. The tour starts with a short lecture about tea types and processes methods than it continues along the various stages and machinery in the actual working factory. The factory is operational only in the mornings, due to favourable climate conditions, so we imagine morning tours get a much better grasp into tea processing. The tour end with tea tasting on the top floor, where there is a balcony from which one can enjoy sweeping views. The shop only sells a good variety of packaged tea. There is no cafe where one can enjoy a cuppa with biscuits or cake. It seems a shame we were looking forward to going to the tea factory also to sit back and enjoy a proper cup of tea.

title: Interesting tour
text: The guy who did the tour kind of seemed like he hated his job, he was very serious. He got a bit better as the tour went on though. We thought the tour was free but it is 525 R. Overall it was interesting to hear about how the tea is produced. It was quite hard to find the entrance though, I think they should have someone out the front to greet you. There are tuk tuks waiting to take you back which was good.

title: Interesting tea facts for those with an interest
text: An interesting visit and I learnt a lot about tea, though I did find my guid a bit difficult to understand through his very strong Sri Lankan accent. On the tour you have a short lesson on some interesting tea facts followed by a tour through the factory. The tour is finished off with some tea tasting and an opportunity to purchase some of their tea. The tour costs 525rp but I found it was reasonable value as I learnt some interesting things I didn’t know. The tea for purchase is also a reasonable price and all in USD. I felt this factory being in such a splendid location was missing a prime opportunity to provide a cafe setting for patrons. I hope in the future they consider adding tea and scones and a small menu for guests to really enjoy their tea and the view.

title: Explains a lot about tea what you probably didn't know
text: The Tuk Tuk drive to the factory is already nice. The tour takes about an hour. Unfortunately, they won't take you on the tea field itself. But you will see the machines and the testing at the end is nice. Worth the money.

title: Excellent tour with Rajha, highly recommended especially if you enjoy tea
text: Great tour, very happy I went. Rajha was very knowledgeable and really educated us on tea. He was very easy to understand and explained everything at the right level of detail.

title: Nice factory production closed on Sunday, difficult to use Cards
text: We went with a tuktuk all the way up. The small roads up in the mountain brought nice scenarios. Unfortunately factory closed on Sunday but they do educational trainings on Tea and Tea sizes plus a walk through inside the factory. After education Tea tastings. Very nice education on Tea, size and tastes. All tea sale in USD, and hard to use credit as they did hide the cardterminal. After request and insisting I was able to use the card to buy Tea. They were not keen to provide card sales and the guidning tour was only accepted in cash. Would recommend to go here and try to do it on week days. Very great learning.

title: Very informative tour
text: The tour in this tea factory was very good ; the guide gave us a lot of information and we saw every phase of the process of producing tea. The tea tasting at the end was also nice, their tea is very good.

title: Maybe not the best factory tour.
text: This tour is quite dull. It only took about 10 minutes, and no photos are allowed. If it was a free tour, it would be fine, but I'm not sure it's worth paying for. We saw the tea factory at the Heritance Tea Factory hotel- it was free, and much better.

title: Can be avoided as other options are better
text: Nice tea estate and one of the oldest. Tour of the factory is not free. There are other 2 tea factories in Nuwara Eliya , which I believe are better in terms of service. Staff seemed to be least interested in selling the products, which is unusual for Sri Lanka.

title: No explanation
text: We intended to go on a factory tour, but they told us the factory wasn’t running at the moment. We decided to do a tea tasting instead. 6 cups of tea were put in front of us without any explanation.. I then asked someone for an explanation, she just told me which cup was which tea, no further explanation.

title: Beautiful tea estate
text: Impressive to see all the tea plantations in Nuwara eliya, which are very big. We had a very good tour guide who showed us the factory and explained the process of making tea very clear. Also very impressive to see under which circumstances the employees live.

title: Lovely old tea factory
text: Lovely old tea factory in the hills. we were given a tour of the factory and shown how the leaves are processed. At the end we got to taste 2 kinds of tea. The tea is brewed for exactly 5 minutes.

title: An average factory tour
text: We were supposed to go to Damro but went here instead as land slides had blocked the road. A very average factory tour: the attendant walked us through the entire tea-manufacturing process in their factory. Nothing spectacular, just an average tour. They didn't have a lot of varieties of tea for sale either.

title: Really disappointing
text: We were really disappointed with our visit to Pedro Tea Factory. Firstly when we arrived noone greeted us, the staff all ignored us and it was really unclear where we were supposed to go. We figured out we had to buy tickets and were then told to wait 10 minutes until the tour started. We waited 30 minutes without any further communication about the tour. Another staff member did give us a cup of tea but with no explanation, we weren't really sure if it was actually supposed to be for us. We chose a table to sit at, but they were all very dirty with bits of food and flies and dishes unclear from previous guests. Finally our tour guide came to get us for our tour, she was very unenthusiastic and came across as in a hurry and disinterested. During the tour, our guide was very rude to other guests in our group. The guide's accent was a bit hard to understand at the best of times (not her fault as English is her second language), but she told two members of our tour group (who English was also not their first language for) that taking photos was not allowed. They clearly did not hear her/understand what was being said, and instead of gently making sure they understood, she yelled at them "do you even speak English?!". After the tour was finished she just walked off without saying goodbye or thanks or anything. Such a bad experience from start to finish! The previous day we did a tour at Damro and it was amazing! I'd definitely recommend avoiding Pedro and going to Damro instead.

title: Damro factory is much better. If you are going to visit just one, go there. If you have time, can see both
text: Nuwara Eliya is a hill-station and we were not going to leave without seeing at least a couple of tea gardens and tea factories. Two of the most famous tea gardens in this town are the Pedro Tea Factory and Damro Labookellie Tea Factory. We drove to the Pedro Tea Factory. This is NOT a working factory and therefore we decided to skip the factory tour and instead walked part of the tea garden.

title: Average
text: The guide tried her best, but she is average and her explanations were very general and not insightful. The factory is in operation only at night hence the instruction given to us on the process was more or less in theory. The factory has a good view but still not worth the price you pay and the time spent.

title: Informative tour
text: The tour we did was informative and reasonably priced. There was a very large group with no options for a smaller group. Overall glad we went but would maybe check out a different tea factory if we were to come again.

title: Amazing amazing memories
text: Amazing tour , almost overwhelming with the gorgeous scenery and staff , the smell of the tea is stunning , the staff that work there are dedicated and passionate. Hard to believe that the traditional processes end up in our tea all round the world . The tasting process is an art passed through family’s . It also goes into our favourite Ahmad tea and helped us understand why it tastes so wonderful

title: tour was a let down
text: this is apparently a working factory hence was expecting a lot from the tour. although the staff was friendly they seemed to be disinterested in conducting an informative tour. the shop has limited options in terms of packaging but was well priced. Yet to taste the tea!

title: Learning about tea production
text: One of our highlights to tea country was our trip to Pedro tea factory. The tour was amazing. The process was explained and we saw the machines and every step of tea production our guide was lovely and guided us with expertise and passion I was particularly impressed how they included a man on our tour who had an impairment. They were considerate of his needs and he wasn’t left out. Tea tasting st the end was great and we purchased tea to take home. Highly recommend if you love tea.

title: EXTREMELY DISAPPOINTING
text: This was one of the main reasons for our trip to Sri Lanka and this was such a disappointment. The tour when it got underway was taken by a lady guide who seemed so un-interested in her job and the customers were an inconvenience. It was so rushed and a large group whereby it was difficult to hear what was being said. This lady did not appear to want to be there and her body language exuded this. It was so rushed. Very very disappointing, don't waste your money, a small as the fee is, or more importantly your time you will be under whelmed

title: Not Much Happening
text: We visited Pedro Factory on Monday but there was nothing happening. We were told that the factory does not function on Mondays - very strange. According to our driver/tour guide, each time he visited this factory the equipment was not functioning.

title: Worth a visit
text: Nice setting especially combined with a walk to Lover’s Leap Waterfall Factory tour is 250rp - we went on a Sunday and not much was happening so better to try another day. It was nice walking around the tea plantation. Staff were friendly and the cup of tea great.

title: excellent tour
text: very informative tour and a lovely setting well worth visiting and trying the teas - the tea is for sale also

title: A beautiful tea plantation and factory outside N.E.
text: It wasn't a production day, no ladies in the plantation picking pekoe leafs, only a open day to have a stroll trough the plantation slopes, but this was beautiful. The shop was open for tea tasting and a lot of different types of Ceylon Black Tea for sale :) (it was february)

title: Go on a production day
text: It was a Sunday so the factory wasn’t working. We decided not to pay for a tour as we’d already seen one tea factory on a non-production day. They do let you wander the plantation which was nice, although there were no pickers working either. Free tea tasting - just one tea, and a very small shop. If you’re going, go on a production day.

title: It was okÃ©.
text: Not very special but it was fine. The view was very nice and the free tea and a good price for the cake.

title: Tour around eco friendly tea factory, not far from Nuwara Eliya
text: Interesting tour following the process from fresh tea leaves to tea packets.... with cuppa at the end. Great views. Not allowed photos in the factory. There were a lot of initiatives to look after their workforce.

title: Really interesting tour of the tea factory and walk in the grounds
text: We really enjoyed our morning tour of the Pedro Tea Factory just out of Nuwara Eliya. We got to see all the stages of tea production and sample a lovely cuppa overlooking the plantation. A great way to spend an hour or so and very informative, especially if you're a tea drinker. It's got a special gentle vibe, tucked away in the hills.

title: Really fascinating tour
text: We had a fascinating guided tour of the factory and learned all about the tea picking, withering and packing process. We then had a cup of tea and wandered through the plantation itself. Highly recommended.

title: Interesting tour with a great view
text: If you’re a tea lover and have time to kill it’s a good place to go to. The tour was nice and the views were great. Very interesting.

title: Waste of time
text: Went on tour of factory, could hardly understand the guide, nothing happening in the factory. Very little explanation of the picking process or tea varieties, offered a cup of tea at end of visit. I’m sure there are better places to visit.

title: Amazing view but not much explanation
text: We arrived at the tea boutique just when a group started the factory tour. They told us the next tour would start in 20 minutes and asked us to take a walk around the tea plantation first. The view was truly amazing. After the walk, we went back to the tea boutique and waited. The group we saw earlier finished their tour and was given tea to drink. We continued to wait but nothing happened. Then a staff asked us if we wanted tea. We asked if the tour would start soon and was told that it would not start for another 15 minutes. We ended up waiting for around 40 minutes before the tour finally started. We were given aprons and shower caps to wear. The tour guide was soft-spoken and we could only hear part of the explanations. After the tour, we wanted to buy some tea to take home. There were many different types of teas and we had no idea about differences. When we asked the staff, she only gave us some half-hearted attention. It would have been better if they could put up signs next to the teas to explain the differences.

title: You paid for what u get.
text: Potential not exploded. Could be amazing, stays on average. Good tea and views at the end. Nothing special. What a pity. The explanation is made while they dont have much going on. Hard to see it in action. Mainly cos they work at night. Hope to come back in the future and see it shining.

title: Sullen guide
text: Went to this factory to see the tea process. As others have said, nothing working on the day. We got a guide who was very quietly spoken and difficult to hear. She told me off for having my camera open and when I asked her a question she told me to ask one of the tourists and flounced off in a huff, bringing our tour to an end. Nice location but staffer was rude. She was the only rude Sri Lankan we came across in our 1 month holiday, so it really left an impression (not a good one).

title: Fabulous location
text: This tea factory offers a tour of key production processes. It is unfortunate that the factory is not actually operational during the daytime. Explanations were clear and concise. Refreshment is available and a small shop selling their products

title: The plantation in factory Tour
text: many varieties of tea and The tour was wonderful The guide was explained everything nicely also price is cheap

title: An interesting visit to a plantation and working tea factory
text: We had a visit to the Pedro tea factory , the factory is an excellent example of the processing required to convert the picked tea to the delicious end product. The tour is not long but showed the processes they went through. It was fascinating to see the old processing equipment still in use. Though it was disappointing the factory was not in use during our visit as it was a Monday and no fresh tea was being processed.

title: So much tea!!
text: This tour gives a good insight to how tea is manufactured and is located in a very picturesque setting. The tour is not too long at 30 minutes and only costs R250 pp which we felt was reasonable.

title: Tea Factory
text: The tour at the factory was kinda short but also cheap. And it was so nice to stroll on the tea plantations after the tour. Also cup of tea was offered.

title: Fine tour
text: We got a fine tour through the factory. Be aware that they work during night, so most machines are turned off. Got a nice cup of tea after the tour. The tea they sell is quite overpriced so buy elsewhere.

title: Worth a visit if the tea pluckers are working
text: A three wheeler from Nuwara Eliya centre to the Pedro costs 350-400 rupees. The estate is in a picturesque setting and the tour is very reasonably priced at 250 rupees per person. Pedro cares about its staff and the environment - both important factors when considering which plantation to visit. The workers were off and the cleaners were in when we went round, that was fine as they warned us. The best part was talking to the tea pluckers at the end. And the cup of orange pekoe!

title: Great place to learn a little and then enjoy the view
text: We arrived at Pedro Tea Factory via tuk tuk (we paid 500rupees from the city centre, negotiating it from an original 1000 rupee 'tourist rate') and were ushered to join a tour (250 rupees each for foreigners). What i couldn't really find information on, was if the tour timings were adhoc or at certain times in the day. When we arrived, everything seemed more adhoc - and it appears the tours run frequently enough and there aren't any minimum tour sizes for them to start (our tour group was 4, whereas others were 10+ people).... so arrive when you can and I'm sure the waiting time will be limited. Tour guide was friendly enough, communication was good and she was happy to take questions. You do get a free tea at the end of the tour and then we actually spent sometime just sitting and enjoying the view. There are plenty of tuk tuks waiting to take you home just outside of the gates or as many did to us on our walk down, offered to take us home.

title: Ok experience.
text: This was interesting if you’ve never been to a tea factory before, but on the day we visited the machines were not working which was a little disappointing. Also the guide who was very pleasant spoke in a quiet voice and was incomprehensible for most of the people in our group. Also we didn’t see the actual T plucking and all exactly how this was done which was disappointing and could’ve been explained in more detail. However the building and machinery was interesting to look at.

title: Ethical Tea Factory with excellent tea
text: We went to this factory because it has been awarded with multiple certificates for treating their worker ethically. They tour of the factory was only 250 rs. The tour is rather quick and the machines are not operating (they work at night) which for us was okay. It gave us a good enough idea about the production of the tea. Afterwards you get a tea and also can buy tea if you want to. I really liked to browse the little shop, since there was no hassle and nobody was pushing us to buy something. We could even try different teas and take our time to make a decision which tea we want in the end.

title: The free tea they give is great
text: All tea factories in Sri Lanka is same, we went to tea factory in Lipton seat, this one is also similar to that one, but the free tea they give after tour, is amazing ;) you have to pay 250 rupee per person...

title: Very interesting
text: We went on a Sunday so no picking or processing happening but lovely staff showed us around .Certainly puts a different perspective on a simple cup of tea ! Such hard physical work for the ladies picking . Great tea samples after the tour.

title: A Tea plantation visit is part of the Hill Country experience
text: Our group visited the Perdro Tea Plantation & factory as part of our tour of the Hill country. They produce Lovers Leap ethical tea. We were shown around the factory by a local plantation worker who explained the tea production process & showed us the various steps from picking to drying & quality control. She was very interesting in describing a very labour intensive process. We also saw tea pickers & had a cuppa in the factory tea shop. Very enjoyable & informative.

title: Pretty uninspiring tour
text: The price of the tour is not much, but the commentary was pretty uninspiring. The only two sections of the factory working at the time was the sorting of the finished tea into its various grades from the top grade orange pekoe to the tea dust. We did see the first process but I didn't hear the name where the leaves are initially dumped in big bays to be dried with wood fire heat to remove enough moisture from the leaves to make them rubbery and then allow the rolling process. But there was no machine on to show the rolling, the fermentation, or the cutting etc. After seeing the sorting, we saw the packaged product ready for auction, then it was back to the shop for a cup of their tea but no explanation of what we were drinking etc. So a pretty short and basic tour of the factory with a commentary that hard to hear at the best of times, but was inaudible when the sorting machine was on. We didn't see any tea pickers. I think by the afternoon they were all clocking off. The tea fields were nice to look at. The tea in the cafe was nice.

title: Very disappointing
text: Everything about the visit was bad. Not sure if we got a particularly unmotivated guide, but she just repeated what she memorized and explained what each machine does. We asked several follow up questions, but her answer was not insightful. Also, we all get free tea but honestly the tea tasted worst than the cheapest tea I drink back home. They provide third grade tea. After drinking that tea, I definitely didn’t want to buy any tea from the factory. Lastly, now the tour fee is 250 lak. Overall, it was a waste of time. I could google and drink better tea at home.

title: Underwhelming.
text: The tour was short and underwhelming. I came out with as little knowledge as I went in. Far nicer is the Hertance tea hotel.

title: Worth a visit
text: Factory tour with the guide was very interesting and informative. They charge a nominal fee of LKR250 for adults and my kids were allowed without a charge. They run the factory during the night shift only so couldn't see most machines working but despite that one would get a good sense of how tea is produced. We also walk down the tea bushes but didn't see any plucking activity in that part unfortunately. I would recommend this place to people who have not been to a tea factory before.

title: Nice tour and delicious tea!
text: Since this tea factory was very close to our Nuwara Eliya hotel, we decided to take a tour. It was a bit disorganized at the beginning, as we purchased our ticket and were then told to sit in a waiting area. Meanwhile, we saw people gathering and being handed aprons, and turns out this was our group, but no one told us. So we joined in and had an informative walk through the factory. Most of the work is done at night, as the tea picked during the day has to dry, so only a couple of machines were actually running. No problem, and they were nice enough to let us know this when we purchased the tour ticket. Our favorite part was the cup of tea provided at the end. We enjoyed sitting outside on the balcony with a lovely view of the plantation. We hope you enjoy the tour as much as we did!

title: Not a rounded tour
text: While the guide was fine, it wasn't a very rounded tour. They should start with showing tea plucking, through the factory with showcasing the old wood burners and letting people see the different grades. It should end with a tea tasting where ppl can try to taste the differences. Great location and definitely worth taking the walk to the waterfall as well. The guides (I overheard a few while we were there) should try to introduce themselves and give a little personal story of their relationship to the estate. I would assume our guide was the daughter of a estate worker who has learned english and is now guiding groups which is nice to see.

title: Historical tea factory
text: This is a smaller, more historical tea factory, built in 1885. The entrance costs 250 rupee ($1.40) and the tour lasts about 20 minutes. The tour is very interesting and it includes a cup of tea. You can walk around the tea plantations afterwards. You'll see women working, they allow photos, but a small donation is expected.

title: Interesting if you enjoy tea
text: Interesting tour which shows you from start to finish how tea is produced. The machinery wasn’t working the day we went but the tea tour was still worth it. Free cuppa at the end.

title: Interesting
text: Really worth the 20 minutes that the tour takes. Great to get an insight into how tea is produced as well

title: proper working lesson on tea making
text: It was a Sunday they were washing down the machinery and finishing production, fascinating. Like stepping back in time.

title: Tea culture
text: This is a great place to go with kids. They have tea factory tour.u need to pay for that.But it’s worth for the cost and affordable.

title: A waste of time.
text: The tour took 15mins at most including the walk from the boutique to the factory and back. We were provided only very basic information about the manufacturing process,none about tea fields, tea bushes or plucking. We didn't have an opportunity to ask questions,as the guide simply told us (at what seemed like a random point of the tour) to take a seat in order enjoy a cup of tea, without saying goodbye or in any other way suggesting that the tour had come to an end. Expecting her to at least tell us what kind of tea we would be served (to this moment we do not know) or asking us whether we had any questions was apparently too much to ask. We would have at least partially understood this kind of attitude had the factory been busy,but we only came across three other guests in the facilities who had already been taken care of. Definitely not worth 250 rupees. We ended up finding out a lot more about tea production from blogs written by tourists who visited other factories,which I find very sad. Honestly I fail to understand the added value of taking the tour. You can simply stroll through the countless tea fields above the factory (with better views) and later enjoy a nice cup of tea at a restaurant while reading about tea production on wikipedia. I sure hope that the tours at other factories are more worthwhile.

title: Interesting place
text: Excursions to the factory goes every half an hour. (Till 16.30, as I remember) If you want to see working machines, you need to come in early mornings (may be not all days) But it’s not necessary to see exactly working process. It’s interesting anyway. Guides speaks English, so all information is understandable. You could see old machines and know many interesting facts about tea manufacture. The smell of tea is amazing. And also you could walk among tea trees on tea plantations behind the factory. It’s very beautiful. You could see the process of picking tea leaves into special baskets. Working women could show you tea leaves and you could taste it. So also they suggest you to take a photo with them, but they also wants you to pay for photos. And it’s strange. Also you could but very good tea in a factory shop. In the shop you could ask about process of brewing tea. It’s a good gift.

title: a scenic place. Their prime intention is to make you purchase their products. the climate is very soothing.
text: Their prime intention is to make you purchase their products. the climate is very soothing. can visit.

title: Nice place
text: Overall the place is very nice. However, we did not receive a fair treatment. After purchasing the ticket they told us that the factory was not working that day and therefore the machines were off... The girl who guided us through the tour was just repeating phrases that she clearly memorized few days before... also the level of English was quite poor. On the other hand, you get the chance to walk around the plantation and to drink a nice cup of tea at the end.

title: Worth a visit
text: We went to this on our way to Heritance Tea Factory. Unfortunately it was a Sunday so the factory wasn’t working but we saw a tea factory and got a good explanation of its working. Worth the hour stop. They don’t allow photos. No idea why not.

title: A nice cup of tea
text: Excellent tour followed by a lovely cup of Pekoe. No better place to find out what makes a good cuppa and - see photos- a bit of a looker!

title: Lots of steps
text: Interesting tour but two groups merged to one as they were short staffed so over 35 people walking around the factory together was not ideal. Some of the group were elderly and the many steps and metal staircases were a bit challenging which also slowed down the tour. Free cup of tea at the end and the views from the cafe are fabulous.

title: Nice
text: Went here to have a look at the lounge .. it’s beautiful surrounded and overlooking the tea estate !! A cup of tea here just to sit and watch the view is great .. went venturing out in the tea estate itself plucking tea leaves !! The tea cake wasn’t the most delicious ones I’ve had but it was okie !!

title: Come for the tea, not the tour
text: Tea factory with factory tour and shop plus nice views. We had a brief group tour which cost 250LKR each for approx 30min tour. The tour guide was arguing with workers for a long period of time and I got the sense we were not welcome to watch the workers load up tea. That said we had a rudimentary tour of the factory and I left with more knowledge about tea than I came with. At the end we all had a complimentary cup of tea which was very nice and were encouraged to buy some tea at the shop. I think the tea here is better than other places but a bit disappointed by the tour.

title: Well conducted tour
text: The factory tour is extremely well presented and any questions from the visitors were well dealt with. Not to be missed if one has the opportunity to go

title: Nice
text: The visit was nice but a little bit short. We had a “free” tea cup at the end of the visit. The views are beautiful from the factory.

title: How tea leaves processed for consumption
text: Entry to the factory is free. but if you want to enter inside the processing unit and see the different stages of tea leaves processing you will have to pay SLR 250 per head. The entire factory visit will take around 30 minutes time. You will be served complementary tea at the end of the factory visit. there are a lot of places around for clicks. Must visit place in Nuwra Eliya. Preferred time of visit morning till 12 noon.

title: Couldn't get a cup of tea!
text: We went straight to the Tea Boutique and separately ask two staff members for a cup of tea. They each told us to sit and wait then disappeared. Waste of time.

title: Interesting process
text: Worth a visit and the guide answered all the questions although I do not know why photos were not allowed to be taken. No pressure was put on us to buy the tea.

title: Quite Interesting, nice tea
text: The tea factory is an interesting place which provides a tour which is informative. There is a lot of talk about how little the tea pickers earn (~800lkr per day) which seemed like a ploy to get tips, which probably dont find their way to the tea pickers.

title: Don't dare to take photos!
text: Interesting tour round tea factory but the over-zealous guide was obsessed by telling us not to take photos! Accused one young lady of taking them when she hadn't. Must have though we were all competitor spies although there was hardly state-of-the-art innovative machinery to spy on!

title: Better tea factories
text: There were 2 options - 250 rupees for tea factory or 1000 for tea factory and tea picking. We opted for the latter and picked tea first. The lady took us down and we got dressed in the tea picking clothing, and she only said how to pick tea leaves and then left us to it for 20 mins. She didn’t explain anything about tea picking or the process. We then walked round the tea factory which wasn’t active with another uninspired lady who was on autopilot when explaining things. At the end we were given a lovely cup of tea but were not told anything about it. Visited another tea factory in our trip and had a much better experience and learnt so much from an enthisiastic guide who turned on the machine where the factory wasn’t active for us to help visualise the process, and then we bought tea from there!

title: Disappointing visit - not worth the time or money
text: On arrival we were given the option of tea factory tour for Rs 250 or tea picking for Rs1000. We went for the latter which turned out to be a huge mistake. We were shown how to pick one tea leaf then left to our own divides for 20 minutes, whilst the guide was preoccupied with her phone. We were not told anything about the tea plantation or the tea picking process. After this we were taken on a tour of the factory, but all the machinery was off as they only use the factory at night. During the tour the guide was more interested with her friends, giggling and waving at them, than giving us any real information about the factory. She also spoke in autopilot and was inspiring. Overall a very disappointing visit and not worth the money. This trip was unforgettable for all the wrong reasons.

title: An Essential Part of a Sri Lankan trip - visit a tea factory, so we went to the Pedro Tea Factory.Guide spoke very quick
text: Disappointing tour of the tea factory as the guide had a poor English accent and spoke very quickly. Amazingly they did not sell the lovely green smocks which they insisted all visitors had to wear on the tour. BIG missed opportunity.

title: Excellent
text: We visited a number of tea factories and got tired of the hard sell. Pedro tea factory was different. It had a lovely feel. The lady who showed us around was really lovely. There tea is delicious and there was no hard sell at all. Highly recommend

title: Not bad if you’re interested in seeing tea factory
text: I wasn’t really into this, but my lady was and the tuk tuk driver recommended it... you’ll take a 15 minute walk through the factory and see how tea is made... they let you have a tasting and hope you’ll buy something.

title: Best tea factory in NE
text: Honestly we visited 2 tea factories and found this one the best . It was nice , the tour was really nicely done and the estates were soooo pretty and secluded. Totally worth the visit

title: No tours
text: We went out of our way to visit this tea factory due to a write up in the Lonely Planet. They did tours, but they were at a cost, and the factory is not in operation during the day, so there is not much to see. The tea room and gift shop was pretty uninspiring, so we spent about 5 minutes there and left. Waste of a tuk tuk fare.

title: Worth a visit!
text: Interesting place to visit. We came at about 8:30 AM (visiting hours are 8:00-11:00 AM and also in the afternoon, but I can’t remember exact hours). We immediately got a guide (entrance fee - 250 rupees per person, but guide is for free, you can leave tips, if you want). The guide was kind and told us everything about the factory clearly and we went through all the steps: from picking leaves to packing a tea. In the end of the tour we could taste a cup of their tea while enjoying the tea fields view from the big windows. You can buy some tea in their shop and have a walk trough tea fields, even talk with the workers. Really nice time we had! It took us ~ 1 hour.

title: What a great way to learn about tea
text: We were only staying about 3 mins down the road from this factory so it was the natural place to visit. Maybe not as grand or as big as some of the other factories, but our experience was excellent. Some days the factory is not in full production and this is due to the weather. When it is full and raining the tea leafs are not growing and therefore are not being picked. It was in half operation when we were there, and the lady who escorted us around for almost an hour was excellent. She advised she was the daughter of parents who had also worked at this factory for many years. She had been there for more than 8 years working also, and had climbed the ladder to a tour guide supervisor. There is a 250lkr entry fee and that covers the tour and a cup of tea at the end. The lady clearly explained in very good English the full process while taking us through the different drying, rolling, and sorting rooms of the factory. She welcomed our many questions. A worker at the factory or in the field does an 8 hour shift and gets paid 850lkrs for that shift. All workers at this factory live in company provided housing, so while the pay is very low in comparison to most western countries, the workers we spoke to are very happy to have steady work and a roof over their heads. So a great thank you to the senior tour guide at Pedro, well done! We are far more educated now.

title: Very Interesting Tour
text: When we visited the Pedro Tea Factory the weather was too wet for tea picking so the factory was not operational. Nonetheless we had an excellent guide and it was fascinating to see the equipment and learn about all the different teas and how they process the tea leaves

title: Visit the factory and enjoy a cup of tea with a great view
text: Interesting to see the factory and get a better understanding of all the process steps for making tea. Unfortunately the factory is running during nighttime, so you do not get to see the process in working, but you get to see all the Machines and get an explenation of all the steps. The tour is finished by getting to try a cup of the from the factory, and you can buy a lot of differnet tea sorts as a souvernier

title: Tea factory vis
text: We visit Pedro tea factory in August 2018. It is only 10 minutes to Nuwara Eliya the factory is working only nights. They made a quick tea factory tour and served a cup of tea at the end of the tour. They are selling also their own tea. You are paying 250 rupies ( less than 2usd) for person. You may find another place which is free on the way from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya.

title: Interesting and helpful guide
text: Visited early in the morning as an alternative activity to our trip to Horton Plains being cancelled. They were extremely helpful, despite the electricity being off, they managed to make us a hot and welcome cup of tea and a tour of the factory. The tour is free and there is a small shop to purchase the estate Tea from. It is useful to offer the factory guide a small tip of 100/200 rupees. The factory is full of the most original machinery much of which is still in operation today, so if you are a lover of this sort of thing, you would definitely enjoy a visit. I was surprised at how quickly tea leaves are turned into tea, within 24 hours and that the aluminium lined bags they pack the tea into at the end of the process can keep the tea for upto 2 years. The estate announces that it is an ethical company with some opportunity for the workers to be involved and would appear to offer more medical care and education than some others do. I wasn't sure about this place as there were some remarks about the speed of the tour and the guides accent, but we did not feel rushed at all and the guide was clear, helpful and very friendly.

title: Little bit disappointed
text: Our guide was a very poor “English” speaking lady. The tour was very fast. You do not visit the tea plantation itself, only the factory. Afterwards you might get a cup of tea.

title: Tea leaf picking
text: Actually got the chance to go amongst the tea bushes and pick tea leaves if you. I believe not many tea factories allow you to do this but this one does and it is near the town of nuwara eliya so it is very convenient if you’re staying around town. Didnt go for the tour though as we went for another tour at another factory previously and i dont see how the process would be much different.

title: A little bit disappointing
text: We went for a tour to this factory. Our guide was a lady that spoke very unclear english. She guided us at a high speed through the production facility where nobody was working. Only during the night there is production. So after the tour we have seen all the machines but still do not know exactly how the production is being done. Afterwards you receive a cup of tea.

title: TEA FACTORY
text: This is an excellent Tea factory experience. The guide Kalai vani was excellent. The view is beautiful. Tea very good. A good experience.

title: Interesting tour
text: We went here for the tour and tea picking experience. Tour was very informative but you weren’t allowed to take photos. I was impressed some of the machines were installed in 1950s- built to last in those days! Tea from here is wholesale sold on to big companies who blend it to their own specifications. There were 65kg bags in the packing area! At the end you get a cup of tea to try. Being a photographer I really wanted to get some photos of the tea pickers but it seemed they weren’t working the Monday we went. We managed to see some further out of town so got some pictures then. Worth a visit!

title: Factory tour
text: We had a short but informative tour of the factory in a small group and learnt heaps about tea making. This dispelled some of the mystery and myth. Highly recommend to anyone with an hour to spare

title: Excellent Tour
text: We enjoyed a very interesting and informative tour of the tea plantation at the Lovers Leap Pedro Tea Factory. The tour is quite short and takes you through the factory, explaining the various stages in tea production from harvest to drying, to grading and to packaging. The guide spoke English and was very well informed about the process and the history of the plant. Afterwards you are given compkimentary delicious tea on the balcony overlooking the plantation where there are lovely views and you are able to go for a walk down among the tea plants which was something we really enjoyed. They have a small shop selling their tea if you want to buy presents, absolutely no hassle or pressure though. A great morning or afternoon out; highly recommended.

title: Interesting but lacking
text: We learnt more from our guide before we got to this place. It was interesting but missing parts of information regarding the growing of tea. It would have been more interesting if the factory was actually working the afternoon we visited. We were told they only function at night due to the correct temperature for processing tea.

title: love the scenery
text: nice loving scenery and the weather was really good. the factory is very traditional as they are still using very basic machinery and process to product tea

title: Tea factory
text: A nice tea factory where they make primarily black tea. Staff is nice which takes you through the factory and explain the process.

title: Tearrific!!
text: Having read mixed reviews we were pleasantly surprised with our visit. Well signposted, easy booking, 250LKR pp, lovely guide, interesting tour and great cup of tea. Good value for money.

title: A charming visit
text: A charming tea factory. We did a factory tour followed by a cup of tea then we were able to wander through the nearby slopes watching the women pick tea. The factory was very interesting and so clean.

title: Nice Place to Visit
text: I’ve been at Pedro Tea Factory to times and it was very interesting both times. It was a friendly guide, who showed us that old and very traditional factory. After the tour you will be invited for a nice cup of tea. Also you can buy tea with a high quality for a reasonable price.

title: Nice staff and tea room
text: Pedro Tea Factory is not quite as fancy as others in the area but definitely worth a visit. The staff was friendly and helpful. There is a outside area where you can have a cup of tea and enjoy the beautiful view.

title: Quick tour, full of information and a great cup of tea.
text: A good tour, although rather quick (roughly 20-30 mins). We came on a Sunday so only one machine was working, and no tea picking - not to mention torrential rains. Our tour guide was really informative, giving us plenty of info although it would’ve been nice to hear about more about the founding of the estate and the fermentation process. But for 250lkr and a great cup of tea at the end (which we then purchased for a great price) it’s definitely worth the trip from Nuwara Eliya. The views are beautiful and I’m sure during the week when the pickers are out and the weather is more pleasant a stroll around the fields would be worth it. I’d recommend getting a list of questions you want to ask, as they’re happy to answer any questions if you find you haven’t had one answered.

title: Informative tour of tea production in the home of tea
text: You’re shown around the processing factory. The tour finishes off in the tea shop where you can then stroll around plantation. We’re big tea drinkers so we enjoyed it. We even chatted with some of the tea ladies in the fields. Fun fact: their collection bags are attached to their hats (not their backs)

title: Good tour but not much happening
text: We took this tour and another on the same day, this tour was educational and we learnt a lot about the tea making process which is good however there was no option to walk around the plantation after the tour, it seemed as though it was more effort and nobody came to show us the gift shop either which was strange. The tour cost 250LKR pp. It was a rather hurried trip and we only stayed for around 30 mins from arrival time to leaving. Other plantations offer a more relaxed welcome.

title: Poor service, poor tea
text: We visited this factory on 4th October and were looking forward to a tour around their site. Unfortunately we didn’t make it to this point. After buying our ticket for the tour we spent almost 40 minutes sat waiting for it to start, after being told it was a 10 minute wait. After around 30 mins we were told it would be another 5 minutes and waited another 10 before leaving. It was very disappointing to see that they had chosen to prioritise the bus tours over our custom. It also did not help that the waiting area was completely infested with flies. We were given a cup of tea to try whilst we waited, with one of the cups arriving with the previous users lipstick on which is always very appetising. The tea was weak and not particularly enjoyable. All of this mounted together helped our decision to leave without the tour starting. We would recommend there are plenty of other tea factories in the Nuwara Eliya area where they treat all customers with respect.

title: Interesting easy tour
text: This place is close to Nuwara Eliya. It’s a 40 min walk or a quick Auto-rickshaw. Our guy took us there from town, waited for us and took us back to the hotel for 600 rupees. We did a tour which was as only 20 min and really quite interesting. It was 250 rupees each and the woman taking the tour was quite engaging and interesting. Nice cuppa tea at the end. An easy and relatively quick way to see a good tea plantation.

title: A tour of the actual factory is comprehensive and interesting
text: This very old original tea estate offers tours to visitors of the main factory during the day as the tea is actually made at night when it is cooler. Clear explanations of the various levels of tea and a beautiful cup of tea at the end. Stunning location close to town.

title: Interesting and great setting
text: Well worth a visit, very informative and interesting. All staff were friendly and no sales pitch at the end too

title: Interesting tour of tea factory
text: once completed tour go to the tea house to enjoy a full flavoured tea. staff friendly and helpful. You can purchase tea there.

title: Interesting But Not That Great
text: To be fair, it was interesting and was set in stunning Countryside. We learned about the tea making process and that was an enjoyable experience - but because they make ‘light’ tea most of the really interesting work and processing is done overnight, meaning the tour was primarily around an empty and quiet factory - more like a museum tour, which is not what it was billed as. Worth it ifyou have time to kill and are in the area, but would not go out of your way. Plus, as always, the shop is very overpriced.

title: Good tea factory experience.
text: Visited Pedro having been left wanting on a trip to Stone Gate the previous day. Pedro is actually based on the plantation and you can see the tea plants and pickers in action. Good tour and explanation, but machines aren’t working as the quality of tea they produce is made at night (when cooler to slow down the the fermentation process) and I guess it would be dangerous anyway to walk around a factory in production anyway. Nice cup of tea afterwards, and a very soft sell in the shop, with really good prices. Afterwards had a wander through the tea plants and then walked up to Lovers Leap. Well worth a visit.

title: Waste of Time !!
text: One of the reasons we went to Sri Lanka was to see a tea factory in production. Owing to the type of tea they produce here the production only takes place at night. We were given a quick tour around looking at inactive machines which made us none the wiser. You are then left in the reception area to watch a marketing video about how wonderful Pedro is and how they are helping the community etc (and given a cup of tea!). Given the lack of tea production you see on this waste of time tour, it would be far more useful to show a video of the tea production, at least then you would not feel you were leaving as badly informed as you were when you arrived! There are tea factories where you can see tea being produced and I suggest you visit one of those!!

title: Very interesting and free tea at the end
text: We had a tour of this tea factopry during our 6 day tour of Sri Lanka. The two, of us were taken round by a very knowledgeable young lady who was able to answer all of our questions. Unfortunately photography isn't allowed inside the factory but I did manage to get one picture which gives you an idea of what it's like

title: Interesting tea factory tour
text: Had a nice 20 minute tour round the factory (note: machinery operates only at night). The tea house could do with having a larger outside terrace to enjoy the plantation views whilst sampling the different teas. Also had a wander through the plantation for some good photo ops with/of the tea pickers.

title: Nice short tour
text: Dropped by on the way from the Horton plains and weren't disappointed. A nice short tour in the plant with a cup of tea afterwards made the end of the day. One can crop the tea leaves as well but we were unlucky - it started to rain once we set off.

title: Pleasant Experience; Great views
text: We all had to have a picture of us in our green aprons you have to wear for the tour. The tour was nice - some very old equipment. Interesting how the different teas are made. Nice cup of tea on the deck overlooking a great view.

title: Fast and short
text: Its a short briefing on the flow of making tea. Factory have its specialty as i read in google. It was interesting and fun. A cup of tea as a complimentary before visit the factory. The view of tea estate was awesome! We met an estate worker while taking picture. Worker are so friendly but someone take for granted asked us to paid the worker because we taking their picture.

title: No photos please!
text: Pleasant enough guided tour although not so much to see unless you come after 11.30 when the first tea comes in from the fields. Photography not permitted! Why not? Management policy apparently. Seriously? What’s the secret. A visit to a tea plantation last year in Kerala was much more animated and entertaining because they made sure to have a small batch of tea being crushed, rolled and dried specially for the fee paying visitors. Tea shop not impressive but maybe they’re more interested in selling by the sack at market than by the packet to tourists. I missed opportunity alas

title: Better option abound
text: The guide could not have cared less. Shortest tour possible. Couldn't even be bothered giving us a cup of tea. AND had to pay for the "privilege". Much better options elsewhere - and no charge!

title: Informatory and interesting tour
text: Visited this tea plantation, whist staying at Nuwara Eliya, during our recent tour of Sri Lanka. Sited in old buildings with old machinery, built in the 50s, we were taken on an interesting 30 minute tour,which gave us a good insight into the basic process of what happens from the time the leaves are brought in from the fields, til they are graded and bagged up to be sent to the tea auctions in Columbo. For some unknown reason, not allowed to take photos during the tour. At the end of the tour there are photo opportunities outside and a chance to sample one of their products. There is a shop where you can purchase their tea, but only in large bags, so not worth the bother. Company could do with a PR overhaul, but a pleasant morning nevertheless.

title: Lovely estate
text: Enjoyable tour of the factory with an informative guide. The ticket for 200r was very reasonable as it also included cup of tea at the end. I wanted to buy some tea however they only came in large boxes so would be great if they had smaller packaging.

title: good insight into the production of tea
text: An interesting guided tour of the factory followed by a cup of their tea. Only one of their products was available to sample as part of the price. It would have been good to sample other blends as we had done at other tea fctories. Price was 200 Rupees, which was reasonable

title: Excellent English with unreal tea
text: The tour was excellent throughly explained how the tea was made from start to finish. Would recommend

title: Interesting well worth while
text: Good tour and an interesting insight into how tea is picked and prepared for packaging. Also has great views of the tea estate and a nice place to relax and drink tea (what else)

title: Beautiful but are they really ethical?
text: We visited the factory with a group and there is no doubt the surrounding area is stunning and everyone is very pleasant I was struck by the emphasis their signs made about how ethical they are I am reliably informed that the pickers are paid only 500 SLR a day - the equivalent of A$5 and not paid if they are sick Our guide was so ill she had not have sit down breaks so she would not collapse This same multi national company still has its office workers using a typewriter with carbons and a manual ledger!

user_location: Prague, Hlavni Mesto Praha, Czech Republic
title: Short visit
text: Short (15 min) visit to the factory for 200 LKR per person with a free cup of tea afterwards on a terrace with beautiful view. Our guide looked little bit annoyed. Not allowed to take pictures inside. It is easily reachable by public bus from the city centre (around 25 LKR per person, 15min). You can also take a walk from here to the Lover's Leap watterfall.

title: A great visit but a huge rip off by the tour company!
text: We paid £26.71 per person for 6 people for a private tour. The tour company didn't realise it was a public holiday and so there were no pickers on site and the factory wasn't working. There were people on site who greeted us and actually did give us a tour but, not realising we had pre-booked the visit, they said it would cost us SLR200 each - i.e. approximately £1! So - in essence, we paid £25 for a very expensive taxi ride from our hotel to the tea plantation approximately 3 km away! You can turn up at the Pedro Tea Plantation at any time and be given a tour for SLR 200 and the price of a Tuk Tuk from town. Having said that, the tour was very interesting.

title: Lovely plantation, but some room for improvements
text: There is no signage to this effect, but you buy your ticket (Rs. 200) in the nicely located tea shop. It took a while to get to it, as people line up to ask for prices of the various tea packages. Apparently, management does not want to put the prices on the shelves, but rather have each customer approach the cashier to ask. The entrance ticket is amusing. There's a list of admonishments about proper behavior in the factory, including "Do not waste time inside the Factory." After a short wait we got an apron to put on, and joined a large group on the tour. We were about 20 visitors, too many to always hear the guide. She spoke good English, but sometimes her voice was drowned out by the machinery. The best part of the visit was the nice cup of tea on the terrace overlooking the lovely plantation

title: Fascinating insight into tea production.
