text: We took the factory tour with a knowledgeable guide. The process really is visible and makes you start to think twice about what goes into our staple cups of tea. The tea pickers have back-breaking work, nevertheless they are happy to welcome you to their world. You can get a nice selection of teas from the shop - without any pressure selling.

title: Nice but too short visit
text: The plantation is very beautiful and you can also visit by your own walking through the fields. The visit at the factory does not cost so much but it's really too short and at the end we had just a cup of tea (same for everybody, you cannot choose). You can buy tea, but the prices are a little bit higher than in other stores.

title: Nice facilities but hard to understand the guide
text: The tour guide from the tea factory has strong accent. It's very hard to understand what she said. The facilities inside the factory are good though. However, the souvenir shop was disappointing. Very few options and no price tag there. Also they use special names for different types of tea so even harder to know what types of tea they are. The only advantage is this tea factory is not too far. We have been to Bluefield tea garden and ceylon tea museum in Kandy. Those are much better places to buy tea in terms of varieties and prices.

title: interesting tour and good tea
text: The guided tour is about 40 minutes and it costs 200 rp per person. At the end you can have a cup of tea. It's interesting if you haven't visited one already. The area all around it's very nice and you can walk around the tea plantations!

title: Very beautiful
text: We didn't try excursion there as it costs 300 rupees and we visitrd Bluefield earlier for free. But we really enjoyed the tea plantation view downhill (not such impressive like Lipton's seat but also good).

title: Interesting but avoid a large tour group
text: Unfortunately the size of the tour group (about 20) was too large for the factory tour guide to manage However, the tour was still interesting in terms of the process of making tea from growing to packaging for the market Tea can be purchased at very reasonable prices.

title: Very lovely tour!
text: Lovely tour of a tea factory with beautiful views and excellent service... and you get to wear a super sexy outfit to boot!

title: Worthwhile
text: Really interesting and informative tour is very workwhile. Explains a lot about the industry how tea is made and the history

title: Lovely little tour
text: It's not a big thing, give yourself an hour or two max. But it's a lovely little trip very informative of tea production and cup of tea thrown into the mix for 200 rupees. So can't complain.

title: Informative tour and lovely plantation
text: Even though the factory was not working (tea production occurs at night here) the guided tour was very informative. The tea rooms are quite nice and offer great views out over a picturesque section of the plantation. The cup of tea was lovely also!

title: Average - busy and hard to hear guide
text: It’s a pity that the group sizes are so big. We were shown around by a very sweet lady but unfortunately we couldn’t hear a word she said, due to the noise of the machinery. the gardens are pretty, and it was interesting to look around the factory but overall we felt that they should have more but small tour groups.

title: Great to see Tea production and put IT in its conceptual reference
text: To learn how to produce Tea, to understand the work environment in a Tea factory, to understand a little bit more about the plucking of Tea as Well the value chain to the end-consumer. Great and interesting. Pedro seems to be a small and regular production unit, extending with guided Tours, show room, and Tea testing, offering a small range of its products.

title: Don't bother visiting!
text: Paid 200 LKR for the factory tour which the staff told us would take 20 minutes. The machines weren't operating during our visit and we were completely fine with it. The tour took only 10 minutes and the guide wasn't knowledgeable at all. Everyone who left good reviews must have gotten a different guide. When I asked questions, she seemed very annoyed and was just hurrying us to get out of the tea factory to quickly end the tour. The guide is a local woman who is quite short and skinny (if you must know to avoid her). After the tour, they will serve you a cup of tea and it took them 20 minutes and after asking multiple times to serve us our tea. Very bad experience overall! Teas on sale are overpriced too. Other travellers we met who visited blue fields said that was really nice so perhaps check that out instead of Pedro. Bluefields offer free tour too I think! Avoid Pedro at all cost!

title: Interesting to Visit
text: The half hour tour costs 200 rupees and takes you through the workings of the factory. The guide was very honest and answered all questions including what wages the workers received. Interesting to learn that the grades of tea are sold at auction in Colombo to companies that then add flavours to the basic tea. You are served a good cup of tea either before or after the tour - no milk provided! Great you can walk through the tea plantations which are lovely.

title: A Lesson In Tea
text: The friendly guides at the tea factory give you a reasonably comprehensive tour of the tea drying and preparation process. You end up with, what else, a nice cup of tea and it was actually one of the nicest cups of tea I've ever had. A good learning experience.

title: Beautifully located nice tea cafÃ© with a great view
text: Nice tea shop. Offers guided tours in the tea factory. At the end of the tour you are served a cup of tea in the cafÃ© with a nice view. You can take walk in the hills.

title: Interesting demonstration on how tea is made.
text: Guide was very knowledgeable and was focused on explaining the tea making process rather than selling tea!

title: Pretty view, disappointing tour
text: There are nice views of the tea plantation but they can be had for free from the side of any road in the region. Our half hour 200 rupee pp tour took about 10 minutes and our guide clearly didn’t want to be there. I also found the tea at the end to be weak. Not a highlight for the trip.

title: Good to visit
text: We were greeted with a hot cup of team (no milk or cookies) but it was refreshing. It requires a small fee to enter inside the factory. Unfortunately we visited it on Sunday so we could not see if live but we still received a guided tour of the factory inside and how tea is made .

title: Closest Factory to Town
text: Its a small factory and when i visited, it was not operational. They showed us around and offered us a cup of tea at the end. Costed 200. It was OK trip and only thing working for it was that this was the closest factory to the city. Many people come by tuk tuk (400-500 Rs) but one can easily find bus from city center which drops you just outside the factory and cost you like 20 rs. The path leading to lovers leap is just opposite to factory (passing through tea plantation of pedro estate) and both activities can be coupled together.

title: Interesting little tour
text: Wasn’t a high cost for this tour and you get to have a roam afterwards. Our tour guide doesn’t seem to get that much enjoyment from the job and it felt a little underwhelming but it was still informative and I learnt stuff about tea- which was the point. It’s good to combine with a loop walk up to lovers leap and then get a tuk tuk back to town

title: Nice place to enjoy a cup of tea
text: I had already visited two tea factories so i did not bother taking the tour, but i rested in the cafe where i watched a documentary about Pedro Tea Estate and then enjoyed a free cup of tea. However there were quite a few people taking the tour and they seemed satisfied. I hiked here after passing by Lover'sLeap waterfall, but the last kilometer is along a busy road which was not too enjoyable.

title: A nice hour spent looking at tea plantation
text: A tuk tuk from town should cost about 500 each way. This is a nice tea factory. It's interesting to look around how it all works.

title: Disappointing
text: We travelled from Kandy to Pedro tea plantation by train which took us about 4 hours which was great. When we arrived at the tea plantation we were given a cup of tea and a tour of the factory which was rushed and took us twenty minutes. A total waste of time and a waste of my holiday. I was excited that I booked this tour prior to my holiday and I feel totally let down

title: Closed on Sundays
text: We dint know this and ended up just taking a stroll at the tea gardens. You can also buy the tea at the factory.

title: Small and forceful
text: The people try to force you to do the tour. The place is small and not as beautiful as other tea locations such as Talawakelle Tea Estate and Edinburgh Tea Estate. I would personally avoid and go to the above.

title: Beautiful location
text: Went there by Tuk-tuk, paid 200 rp per person for a guided tour around and a cup of tea afterwards. The tour takes no longer than 20 minutes and gives you the basic information about the tea making process. Smaller place compared to the big tea factory’s in the area. I would guess also less tourists. Which we love. After the tour we walked into the plantation and talk to the working ladies. A nice anc cheap experience.

title: OK
text: Our guide was friendly and the factory interesting. It did feel like we learnt the rudiments of the process and given we only had a limited time, this worked for us. If you want a more in depth bus-to-cup tour, you'll have to look elsewhere.

title: Enlightening experience
text: I have visited the Pedro factory twice now, once with my partner and a second time with my Mum. It is very reasonably priced at just 200rs for a 20-30 minute guided tour and cup of tea. Our guide Kalaivane was superb! Friendly, informative and the daughter of a tea picker so able to gave a very personal and honest account of the tea industry. An enlightening experience I would definitely recommend!

title: Cool Experience!
text: Visited this factory... they give you a tour inside the factory where you can see how tea is made and you can enjoy different types of tasty teas.

title: Traditional tea factory
text: Lovely, quaint, old tea factory. Tour was very informative and views were fantastic. Tea quite expensive.

title: Great experience
text: I visited with my friends and family from Norway,Serbia,China, Cambodia and Vietnam. It's very beautiful place with different varieties of tea. They explain about use and benefits of different types of tea.

title: Interesting - worth a visit
text: Good tour with a guide explaining the processes. Interesting to see how old the machinery was and still working. Strangely no photography allowed. Nice views outside of the reception area but not impressed with shop.

title: A well-organized tour of a factory in an attractive estate
text: This was our first of two tours of tea factories. It was inexpensive (about $2US) and well organized with an attractive display area and I would recommend it if you have a mild interest in the tea making process. However, we were hoping for a longer, more in-depth tour but our guide was hard to understand and her lack of English meant that she was unable to answer questions so we left a little disappointed.

title: Wonderful example of a tea plantation!
text: We came here in the afternoon of our day trip to Nuwara Eliya after riding the scenic train. Blue Lanka, our tour agency, recommended it so we thought we would give it a try. The factory is wonderful and the guide of the factory spoke great english. It was great to see the tea making in progress and smell the tea in its rawest form. Then, there was the tea tasting. The first couple teas come free while the others cost money to taste. All the teas are great and they bring out an additional rare (we don't know if it actually was) tea for us to try. This tea was 150 USD per kilo....the tea plantation was wide, beautiful and spacious. The tea ladies always beckon you over for photos (and tips). Overall, a wonderful tea plantation and I would recommend coming here.

title: Interesting tea factory in beautiful surroundings
text: Stunning nature surrounds this old tea factory, which is still in full activity. The tours around the factory gives you a good insight in the process of tea making, and makes you humble to every glass of tea you drink thereafter. Also, seeing the hard work of the tea picking ladies, makes you wonder why the tea are not more expensive, and you really wish someone would increase their income a bit. If you take a picture with them, be wise enough to give them a few hundred rupees - they will appreciate the added income

title: Interesting short visit with a cup of tee afterwards
text: We had a very short, but still interesting tour in the fabric with the basic information about the producing of tee. Afterwards you get a couple of tee (no need to pay extra).

title: Nice visit
text: Nice guided visit to understand the process of making tea. After the visit you can walk in the plantations. It would have been nice to have a tea tasting at the end, as the visit is not free.

title: Beautiful view
text: Since we arrived together with the westerner groups we, can see the favoritism in entertaining guests by the staff.

title: Avoid it.
text: We got to the tea plantation and the ladies at the counter told us that the machines were off, so if we wanted to, we could still pay to enter but no tour was going to be offered because the production had finished. We hung out at the lounge and had a cup of tea but it's a level of poverty tourism that I am not comfortable with. All you can see are the tea plantations and the women that work there. If you read a little bit about it, you'll realize that these women are very underpaid. So you end up sipping a cup of tea looking down on the workers from a viewing deck. Not really my kind of thing to do, so I'll just advice you to avoid it altogether. The tea plantations in themselves are beautiful-ish. They're green trees... there are only so many pictures you can take of green trees.

title: Learn the history of tea growing
text: Good place to visit, you are taken round the factory to see the process. You get to try some tea on the verandah. Good little shop to buy the different teas. Staff were lovely

title: Nice short tour.
text: The tour is short and I would have wanted a bit more info about the history and cultivating of the tea.

title: Amazing View, Pictorial
text: Non operational in the morning. Opening Hours: 8.30 AM Ticket: LKR 200/- with one cup of tea If you don't want to visit the factory, you can still visit the tea plantation without any charges. You can tip the workers in the plantation if you like. The hike in the fields in amazing.

title: Average
text: Should only visit this place if you have never been on a tea factory tour before. The guide was not very enthusiastic and could not communicate very well in English/answer questions that were not in the part of her script. The factory tour itself was very short and not very informative. Since the factory operates only at night we couldn't see any machine working or the end product from a particular machine. Maybe they should have kept samples from each stage for visitors to understand the various processes better. Nonetheless the view from their tasting area balcony was really nice and you were welcome to walk amongst the tree bushes

title: Just my cup of tea !
text: I really enjoyed a brief but informative visit and was happy to see a working factory and the tea making process in action. My new found knowledge will allow me to make more informative selections in the future and I will enjoy the taste even more now knowing how much hard work goes into my daily cuppa. There are numerous tea plantations in this area and many factories I can't imagine they vary much so suggest you pick whats is on route and convenient.

title: Great introduction to tea making
text: The tea factory is among a huge tea plantation. They take you on the tour in groups, while waiting for your turn or after the tour you can relish their complimentary tea drink. There is an fee of 200lkr that is charged, so in case you plan on visiting other places in Nuwara Eliya then one of the bigger tea plantations would be a better option since the tours here dont have charges.

title: A must
text: A good insight into how demanding tea picking and processing really is. Thank you to the excellent guide who showed us round and answered our questions really well.

title: Tea tour
text: Very interesting. Tour takes about 15 minutes and cost 200rupes per person. Tea reasonably priced if looking for tea purchases.

title: Interesting place
text: We visited two tea factories, one of them was "Pedro". The place is very nice, attention is excellent and you can have a complete vie of the tea process production. Very convenient to understand how it arrives to your cup.

title: Poor quality Tea
text: As I am engaged in the tea sector ,I was much interested about this place but when I tasted the cup of tea I got much dissatisfied as they offered us a cup of tea made of Tea "DUST" thats one of the low cost tea which tastes awful and I totally disappointed with this experience. But I must say the view through the tea shop was quite nice but i went there for tea so if you are looking for great cup of tea ..sorry ,thats would not be the place for such.

title: Fascinating tour of tea factory
text: Well worth a visit if you are in the area, the tour takes you through the various tea making processes and, of course, a chance to buy tea at the end. Very interesting.

title: Very informative and interesting in a lovely setting
text: First, take in the great views of the adjacent lush countryside and then take the tour which explains all one needs to know about the history and production of tea in Sri Lanka! The staff guide was most knowledgeable and responsive to questions.

title: Large Tea Factory offering a Tour for a fee
text: The Tea factory offers a tour explaining the picking and processing of tea leaves, and has a store to purchase their tea products. The tour costs Rs. 200 per person. The tea is processed at night to take advantage of the cooler temperatures, and so the processing operation (except ambient drying) was not operational during the tour. Besides, the tour guide was not very clear about description of the process. A cup of tea is offered at the end of the tour. In my opinion, charging a fee to tour a non-operational facility makes this factory unwelcome as a place to visit, when there are so many other factories in the area.

title: Professional Tour
text: Although a paid attraction, this is well worth the spend (200) with a professional guide and freedom to roam the tea plantation afterwards. Met with some tea pickers who were very happy to pose for pics (a tip will be expected for this) and explained how tghey choose the leaves etc. The Duke of Edinburgh visited this factory in 1954 as the small exhibition of paper cuttings and photos shows - an interesting addition to the tour.

title: Interesting place
text: We enjoyed our tour of the factory although our guide was a quietly spoken girl. Afterwards, we were given a cup of tea in a pleasant little restaurant. Very nice. Takes about 15-20 minutes to do the tour.

title: Interesting place
text: It is worth a visit as you get to see inside the factory and are taken through the whole tea production process. Then you get a cup of tea to taste and it is delicious. The tour and tea are free and given with the usual lovely Sri Lankan smile!

title: Worth a visit
text: We went there by bus for just a few rupees from Nuwara Elya bus station. Nothing special, but nice to see and get a tour through the factory. The tour costs 200 LKR per person and takes around 30 minutes. Afterwards you get a tea in their small shop.

title: Disappointing
text: After a wonderful train trip into the high country this tour did not in any way live up to our expectations. It was a rushed tour with the explanations of the workings of the plantations and the origins of Sri Lankan tea sadly lacking. We were taken around the facility but ended up with no further knowledge than we had arrived with. We were not shown any tea bushes or how they were picked. Sad to say the least as we had looked forward to this part of our journey. A video would have been altogether more enlightening .

title: Short Tea factory tour
text: Nice view from the estate but the girl giving the tour of the factory felt quite uninterested. Informative but with no engagement. Okey. Assume there a more genuine Tea factory options around. No tasting, only one cup served after finishing the stort tour.

title: Really enjoyed the history and insight into the Sri Lanka tea industry
text: We enjoyed the factory tour and the history of the very first tea factory in Sri Lanka very clear explanation and then tasting on terrace overlooking the tea plantations better than expected

title: Very good tea factory
text: A very good tea factory, working mainly in the night. The tour costs 200 rupees, but include a complimentary excellent cup of tea, and the plantation grounds are very well tended and magnificent to look at.

title: Not worth the money and effort to go there
text: The various reviews describing the rush in which the "tour" was made and the one cup of tea to "taste" should really have been a warning. But we thought everybody has a bad day someday, and wanted to give it a try. Bad idea. Badly organized staff, lack of communication among them, being indeed rushed through factory halls where only very few woman and machines were actually working. The lady showing us around spoke complicated to understand and with a very low voice. Heard a bit about the process but nothing at all about what makes a good tea, what are the different variations, about the company, and its (fair??) trade, the working conditions... Nada. After maximum 10min we were "done". Got one single cup of tea, no chance to do a tasting. And guess what, it wasn't even a good tea. Had we had an idea where else to go, we would have done that. So, at least we can warn other future visitors.

title: A great place to visit.
text: If you're a tea drinker check this establishment out. The tour of the factory by an informative guide is well worth the time and the short trip out of town. The vistas are beautiful, however the shop only sells several packets of tea at a time, so if space in your luggage is limited you'll be disappointed.

title: A short but informative tour and great tea
text: We simply turned up and tours were running pretty much all the time (every 15 minutes roughly, each time enough people we waiting for them to run one), it was 200 LKR each (we visited on 16-02-2017) and the tour rook about 20 minutes. After the tour they gave us free tea to try and we went for a walk around the tea gardens. You can buy all the tea they grow there. The tour was in English.

title: what else - tea -
text: Nice to know how our tea is gathered, processed and sent to the auction house in Colombo. Best of all was the cup of tea at the end

title: Tea plantation visit
text: Very interesting visit here finished with a lovely cup of their own home grown produce! Recommend a visit here.

title: very informative on tea making - loved it
text: you pay a small price and they take you on a tour. There are certain times which I forgot which had the actual processing but I think the process at night and stop in the morning for new batches.

title: Educational tour and rest stops
text: Good educational tour but go early to avoid the heat in the afternoon. Pamper yourself to a cup of good tea at their cafe and then to shopping at their souvenir shop.

title: Great insight into the tea making process
text: Well worth a visit as it provides a great insight into the tea making process through the guided tour. This was followed by some tea sampling. Pedro is an ethical tea producer so well worth a visit.

title: Tea Factory tour
text: You have to pay for the tour but it is cheap and you get a free cup of tea. Was nice and informative/Interesting. The nicest thing was to walk around the tea plantation before/after...very pretty and great views. From here you can walk up to the lovers leap waterfall which is a lovely walk.

title: Decent Tour: the closeness to the tea fields makes it
text: I did a number of tours of the tea plantations and tea factories while in Sri Lanka. This was the only one which I had to pay for (though only 200 rupees - about USD $1.25). However it was the most perfunctory. We got the factory tour in a large group (after waiting for others to slowly stop in and accumulate) and one cup of tea at the end. There was a small shop with a limited selection of teas to buy after the tour. On the plus side it has easy access from the closest town Nuwara Eliya and was right in the tea fields. Of the tea factories I visited this had the best access to the tea fields for spectacular views and the opportunity to take close up photos of the lady tea pickers. For that alone it is worth visiting - with your camera or iphone in hand.

title: Working factory experience!
text: I’ve been to several tea factories in Sri Lanka and Pedro is nice as you get to see a working factory. Sadly on the day we went it was not operating due to a public holiday but nevertheless you get to see inside it and you can tell that it’s not just a display factory like many others I’ve been to. The tour was only 200rps and included a cup of tea at the end (which wasn’t great). I wouldn’t buy tea here but if you’re into your tea and want to see a functioning factory it’s worth a visit.

title: Guided tour of empty factory and no tea tasting
text: We were looking forward to seeing a working tea factory in action, learn about tea and enjoy a tasting to understand different varieties and qualities of tea. None of this actually happened as we were shown around an empty tea factory looking at machines and being told the absolute minimum by a bored and annoyed guide. After the tour we were given a cup of tea and encouraged to buy tea from the shop. Far too commercialise. If you want to learn about tea and enjoy a tea tasting go somewhere else, this was totally not worth the time or energy.

title: Nice tea factory taking social responsibility
text: Was heading for the Lover’s Leap, when I found this tea factory, and thought I’d buy some to bring back home. Tried to ask if it was organic, the women in the tea saloon didn’t understand, so after getting a hold on the manager, I sort of Got an answer: they are “sort of organic” he said - using some chemicals. They do seem to have great focus on social responsibility, like houses for all their workers, which is great. Their lightest tea was the best, in my opinion, but also the BOP.

title: Good experience !!!
text: I came quite late there so the factory was nearly closed but the stuff was so nice to give me a tour - it’s quite short but interesting. Then you can have a cup of free tea witch is phenomenal!!! Very good experience at Pedro Tea Factory!!!

title: Good experience to see a Tea Plantation
text: It was unfortunate for me as I visited the Pedro Tea Plantation on Good Friday. There is still a factory tour but there was no production and we are only shown all the machines without the tea leaves. If you plan to explore the tea plantation, you might want to wear long pants. To get a nice shot in the middle of the tea plantation, you have to walk in between the super narrow path.

title: Lovely visit around a genuine tea factory
text: Had just complete the journey on the tea train so where better to go than visit a tea factory. As we had just stayed for two nights at a tea plantation we only really wanted to visit factory. We were taken round a by lovely lady (Sivakavi Kalaivani) who spoke amazing English with an occasional word with a Scots accent - lovely to hear. Not all the machinery was working as it was late in the afternoon but that did not spoil the experience. Commencing with the drying areas for the tea all the way down to packed product. When finished we adjourned to Lovers Leap (tearoom) where we tasted several varieties of tea - really delicious. We had taken with us a iced fruitcake from the UK so what better way to finish the afternoon with Ceylon tea and English cake. Well worth the visit.

title: Stunning location and interesting tour
text: We were staying overnight in Nuwara Eliya and borrowed bikes to visit the Pedro tea factory. The ride up the hillside was tough but it was so beautiful to cycle the paths through the plantation we didn't mind. The tour itself lasts about 30 minutes and the smell of the fresh tea is intoxicating in the drying room. Our guide spoke perfect English and was happy to answer questions. After the tour we tasted some of the tea, which was delicious! Definitely worth a visit if you have a free morning.

title: Informative tour of the Tea Factory
text: Thanks to our guide who was knowledgeable we left with a good understanding of the Tea Making process. The factory is clean, staff are helpful and efficient and the complementary Tea is fabulous! 200 rupees and the best tour we did!

title: Must have been
text: Nice quite old factory. Very interesting to see how tea is produced. Beautiful tea gardens with many traditionally clothed women.

title: Insightful
text: The tea at the end of the tour was surprisingly refreshing! The tour was a bit shorter than we expected. Also we went on a day when the factory was technically closed so we didn't get to see things in action - pick your day wisely.

title: Top Class Tea Factory In Nuwara Eliya
text: This factory is rich in history. I must admit that the factory is very well run and please do join the tour, which is very informative. At the end of the tour, you will be served with a cup of very fragrant tea. The estate itself is beautiful....very green with a panaromic view of the area. I have visited a couple of tea factories in my life and in fact, this is the best of the lot. It is a "must-see" when you are in Nuwara Eliya

title: For all tea lovers
text: I was a bit disturbed that they call these factories plus staff housing "estates" when in reality its modem plantations. Please ask your guide for more info... they don't hide information about the setup of these "estates". All staff seem happy and at peace, grateful even, for the accommodations and the work. Please take the factory tour - very informative - from start to finish. You learn the entire tea process. The best part is learning how tea "tasters" from all over Sri Lanka have such a delicate palate they can identify any tea from any region by taste and smell. I love the sustainability museum at the end of the tour. It's nice to see that such hard work and production is done with the environment in mind.

title: Great visit! Remember not to go after Poya day
text: We visited the tea factory in August 2016. It was lovely and very informative! Unfortunately, we arrived at the factory the day after Poya day, so there was no tea to process. I think the whole tour lasted about 45 minutes and you get a free cup of tea to taste afterwards.

title: Interesting Enough
text: First we were treated to a lovely cup of tea in the waiting area. We were given aprons and then taken on an informative tour through the tea factory. We saw different stages of tea production and were explained just how time consuming and precise a process it is.

title: Friendly Guide through Working Tea Factory
text: Nearby the town and a great place to spend an hour or so during a rainy monsoon morning. Pleasant tea cafÃ© and beautiful views; interesting to see how tea is processed (but be warned going upstairs is one of the hottest experiences ever -- the warm air from the drying process drifts upwards and literally a bit hard to breathe)!

title: The process of manufacturing of tea is explained very well
text: They first take you on a tour around the place showing you how tea leaves are taken through various processes and result in the final product-tea powder.After that they give you a hot cup of tea which is very soothing and refreshing.They also sell tea packets freshly prepared in the factory at a nominal price.Overall a good way to spend 1 hr!!!

title: Soft and cozy tea factory
text: Had a nice cup of tea - Lover's leap which is only sold in Pedro tea factory. Visiting tea factory is okay, we were guided by a Tamil women with detailed history and tea making process. The only point is photography is not allowed - which is not forbidden in other tea factories. It's the nearest tea factory you can reach from center, take bus in bus stand (ask them which bus to go, 10 Rs and journey is less than 10mins) After visiting finish, you could take a easy walk downward to city center , which only takes 40 mins with 3-4km.

title: Working tea factory
text: We stopped and had a tour of this working tea factory which was really interesting. It has been in operation for many years and had some of the old equipment around. Our guide was interesting but I had hoped that we could have a tasting of the different teas. Maybe next time.

title: An interesting morning spent at the tea factory
text: One can learn all about tea making in this beautiful tea factory. A guided tour takes you around the tea factory and the guide explains to the group all about the process involved from the time the tea leave is plucked to the entire process of drying and the end product which we drink!

title: Perfect short day trip
text: Loved it, smelt the tea as soon as we arrived :-) Was an interesting tour, that was very interesting & makes you think of those ladies working so hard each day for such little pay!

title: an excellent place to learn about tea
text: well worth a visit to see the different teas produced and how it is made. Guide was extremely knowledgeable and interesting

title: Working tea factory
text: Great to see how these places operated in the past. They produce great tea and are very willing to share their experience and history.

title: Worth to visit if you are a tea lover
text: It was quick and short visit at the Tea Factory. It was good to see the machines and understand the process of making tea.In the end i manage to buy the finish product at their store in the same area. Although the machines were not working at the time of my visit at least I was able to see how the tea making process in reality. Its a good learning experienced and one of a kind. I visited the tea plantation as well along the road. Very nice atmosphere all green everywhere.

title: Too quick!
text: The visit was very quick and hard to understand. Machines are not working during the visit because they work only in night time. They offer a very good cup of tea after the visit, and you can buy tea also but it's expensive. We preferred the visit of Dambatenne tea factory in Haputale.

title: Holiday/ tour
text: Wonderful visit set in a wonderful area. Staff friendly and a great tour around the working tea production. Tastings offered of various teas and the opportunity to purchase. Really enjoyed the tour and very well explained how teas are dried and prepared. Highly recommended and thank you for allowing the public to visit.

title: Well worth a visit
text: Good tour, very short but explain everything well. Interesting to see inside the factory and you can try the tea at the end. Only 200rupees

title: Eye opener
text: A tea plantation must be visited if you are in the area. We visited Pedro Tea Factory. Our guide was informative. We were able to see the different stages of tea processing, even though only some areas of the factory were working that day. You really don't need to see all the stages, as they are well explained and samples of the different types of tea are available to examine. You can taste a cuppa at the end of the tour and even wander in the beautiful plantation and take photos. If you do take a picture of a worker, offer them a bit of money. These women only earn $5 a day if they meet their quotas. It's back-breaking work.

title: Informative
text: Not being much of a tea drinker, I found the factory tour interesting and informative. But what fascinated me more were the tea pickers who worked 8 hours a day with a daily goal of picking 18 kilograms a day, all for less than $5 USD.

title: Came for a cuppa...
text: Good place for a walk. Wandering amongst the tea fields and up to the waterfall was a tealightful experience. Went to get a cuppa after and it came with a free tour (200rps). Tour was short but informative and guide was pleasant. Sat down salivating in anticipation of our post tour beverage but unfortunately it failed to materialise. Asked the waitress twice but it appears it takes more time to make a cuppa than it does to dry and process tea. We sacked it off and went to town for lunch.

title: Basic and Informative
text: There are several competing tea factories that are vying to be the top tourist draw of tea country (massive hotels, all the trappings). This one, while perfectly well set up for tourists, is clearly still mainly in the business of processing tea. They have a nice reception area, and start you off with a cup of delicious local product. Then they take you on a very informative tour, on which pictures are inexplicably forbidden (most of the machinery appears to date back to the early industrial revolution, I can't imagine a picture or two would disclose any top secrets but oh well). Guide books say nothing is going on because they do all their processing at night, but I actually saw this as an advantage: no interference, we could walk around and not get in anyone's way. Our guide was very knowledgeable. Strongly recommended!!

title: Average, there must be better tea factories
text: We were not so impressed with the tour at this factory. First of all the factory was not in action. I guess because it was a Sunday. So you look at a bunch of machines and try to figure out how it works. The tour leader was very hard to hear because of the noise of cleaning the machines. The good thing is that Pedro works in a very friendly way for the environment, fair trade and so on. The tour itself was however not so great.

title: Not worth it
text: I don't think it's worth it, but it is just 200 roepies. You will guided through the trees factory, she will tell something about the price of producing tea. But her English is not really good, it's a script. You can't understand it, it think Google helps you more about the proces.

title: Nice tea visit
text: Nice tea factory to visit. Thought I preferred the Ceylon Tea Museum near Kandy. But if you are in Nuwara Eliya and you didn't already visited something like that, don't hesitate it's worth a visit. The view there is also really nice.

title: Short trip - see how tea is made
text: Worth a visit. Old tea company- see how tea is made and the different qualities of tea. Tour of the factory. Not too comercial.

title: Very educative and worthwhile
text: The visit to the tea estate was somewhat delayed but the tour guide was very patient and it was encouraging to see how she was self developed. The lack of water and toilet paper in the toilets was a little disconcerting.

title: Not too touristy
text: Of all the tea factories, this one felt most genuine, not a tourist trap at all! Totally recommended, interesting overview of a tea factory's ins and outs, set to a beautiful view, with a lovely cup of tea as a finale!

title: Really interesting!
text: Surrounded by beautiful tea plantations, the Pedro Tea Factory was a great place to visit. We had a lovely friendly tour guide who took us round the factory, although by the time we got there, it wasn't actually in use. Our guide was knowledgeable and explained everything really well, and the tea at the end was a lovely treat!

title: Great Visit, Great Product
text: The explanation provided by the factory team is very instructive...especially that team shows guests the real-life machinery and the real process they adopt...the team member who led us was a real subject matter expert and talented in explaining and answeting questions..After knowing well the industry and various types pf Tea, it's time to taste an amazing local Tea while enjoying the unlimited Green of this noble plant...spread into big and wide valleys...memorable experience for us and our kids as well..

title: Interesting visit, beautiful location
text: We had a very interesting morning here, the tour was informative and not too long, the factory still using machinery from the 1950s which are works of art in themselves. From the tea factory it's a good walk to Lovers Leap waterfall where you can see tea pickers at work. It's an easy bus ride from Kandy.

title: Interesting tour
text: On arriving we were given a cup of the plantation tea, which was delicious, and we were able to sit out on the balcony overlooking the plantation and enjoy the morning sunshine and lovely views. The tire was interesting although quite short, I would have liked to also have a chance to learn about how they pick the tea and look after the plants (it focuses on the processing of the tea after it is picked). Still very interesting however. It can be hard to hear the guide on the factory of you have a large group. The factory promotes worker welfare and ethical tea practices, there are interesting signboards in the visitor centre about the factory's history and engagement in UN programmes.

title: If you have the time
text: For 100rp you get a 20min tour of the production process from them delivering the tea from the field to the packaging. Was interesting.

title: Pretty rapid
text: Pedro is geared up to show parties around a totally functioning tea factory. Good guide but plenty of climbing and no photography allowed. A visit gives you an idea of the whole, very quick process of producing packed tea from fresh leaves, ending with the sobering fact that the guide would have to work two days to earn enough to pay for a packet of the best English Breakfast tea.

title: Really enjoyed the visit to Pedro's
text: Beautiful experience of watching ladies picking tea leaves (very friendly to chat to) walking through fields and understanding the tea process. After the tour a complimentary cup of tea was provided. Very enjoyable tour. Advice to come there before 4pm if you want to see the machines still working.

title: Lovely visit
text: Lovely cup of tea pn arrival with a beautiful view of the plantation. The tour was informative and the guide was terrific.

title: Welcoming and interesting
text: The place is a working tea factory. They make a real effort to be both welcoming and informative. You get a well explained tour of the whole factory and emerge with a better understanding about tea.

title: Disappointed
text: We were a bit disappointed by this tour of the tea estate. Most of the areas of production were not operating and we found the man who was taking us around difficult to understand. He was speaking in English and we were the only people in the group who had English as our first language so I would imagine the other people understood even less.

title: lovely no frills plantation!
text: i've visited them today and was a great learning experience actually! my guide was a young Sri Lankan lady that had a great knowledge of tea and what goes into prepering a perfect cup. at the end of tje tpur they offer you one of the best orange pekoe i've tasted....

title: Beautiful lush tea estate!
text: Huge area of tea plantations till your sight can see. One section overlooks the sunset and lake, which is beautiful. Enjoyed walking across the estate.

title: Scenic tea factory and plantations!
text: to start with, this tea factory was built in 1880! we did a guided factory tour where we were explained the complete process of segregating, processing and treating tea leaves which is then supplied to all the big Tea brands around the world. we also saw their tea plantations and interacted with tea pickers who taught us which leaves to pick from the plantations. the premises also houses a small tea cafe with a terrace facing plantations and hills, which is quite serene! good for a short visit, Dont forget to carry some sandwiches as there is lack of good eatery around

title: Nive Place to Visit
text: We visited, when on our tour through Sri Lanka passing by, this tea factory with its old machines, had tour and bought some tea. It is worth to have a visit here - as well as strolling through the plantations - on public ways of course. Nice and beautiful place.

title: Perfect tea plantations with an ambient atmosphere
text: Amazing place, the best tea plantations in Nuwara Eliya area. Green scenery, overlooking tea and lake, great place to lost yourself in tea bushes

title: Sri Lanka Adventure
text: An hour well spent on an introduction into how the Tea Leaf is made into Tea. From plant to the finished product. Well worth a visit

title: Tour too short on time and info
text: Our tour guide did the best she could with the English language and I guess they do the tour at 20 min duration, that really is not enough.there is a huge history in tea and incredible variations in the process used to obtain final product. I was left with many questions. Otherwise friendly staff and pretty environment

title: Ammazing!
text: The walk in the plantation, though unassisted is the best thing for those looking for serenity and quiet! Lush green, with majestic pineladen mountains for a backdrop, it cannot get calmer! The tea shop has awesome and courteous staff, and amazing tea. Prices very well against the commercial ones we stopped at on the way-at peradeniya! This one is simple, crisp, and warm!! Cant miss.

title: very intersting factory
text: I enjoyed visiting Pedro Tea factory and it was really informative visit . The tour took around an hour . They greeted us with a free cup of tea that we enjoyed at their amazing terrace and then the tour began, After the tout they offer us six types of tea and we chose three types to buy. If you are travelling with kids , the visit will be really nice to them.

title: Proud staff, lovely grounds
text: We really enjoyed the tour. The lady was so proud of her culture and heritage, it was lovely. Nice grounds and walks in the area.

title: Not much to see; night time ops
text: Went here in the afternoon. No tour available. Shop is small, offers some tasting. Tea is quite nice actually. Not worth going out of your way to get her; if you are in the area, ok.

title: Quick guide to tea
text: It's easy to get here either by local bus (just say you want to get off at Pedros) or by tuk tuk 300 each way. The tour is 200 & takes 20mins. It's not the most informative & you can't take photos, but it is good to see the old machinery & it does give you a feel about tea production. At the end you do get a cup of tea, which wasn't the best I've tasted so didn't tempt me to buy their tea at the shop. Definitely worth doing & across the street is the start of lovers leap walk.

title: Well presented tour
text: Small charge to look round (200 rupees per person). Kitted out with hats and aprons and then shown each stage of production as a small family group which was lovely... no big tour. Only takes about 30mins. Very hot in the baking area but thoroughly interesting seeing each step. Welcome cuppa at the end!

title: Want to learn about tea? This is the place!
text: We toured the facility which has been in business for more than 150 years. We watched the process from collection to drying and processing leading to the final products (no pictures allowed). We got to taste and purchase the real Sri Lankan tea. People were very pleasant and the views over the tea plantations beautiful. A must stop if you are in the area.

title: overcrowded tour by a not very motivated guide
text: english was ok, but the guide was not very motivated the group was huge most people did not get what was said there are better visits!!

title: Good place, tasty tea.
text: Thanks to the Pedro tea factory staff. It was very informative tour inside of the factory (20 minutes).

title: Nice to see how they made tea
text: Nice to see how they made tea, tour is not long but interesting, you can not take pictures inside the building. You can buy tea at the factory

title: A beginners guide to teat manufacturing and tasting
text: If you are a Tea drinker, this is a must place to visit. The factory visit gives you a glimpse of how your favourite tea is made and tasting it. They offer some of their teas for free to try them but others are just for buying.

title: An insight into an every day beverage.
text: The history of the manning of tea plantations is rather sobering but things have improved. We really enjoyed being shown around by a knowledgeable Tamil Tea worker. We then wondered through the plantation learning about which leaves are used for different tastes. As the plantations are high up it is nice and cool and very lovely.

title: Visit to tea factory
text: Unfortunately the weather wasn't the best on the day. The gentleman who gave the tour seemed very passionate about the place, and provided some interesting facts. Not sure that I would have come here if I wasn't on a group tour, knowing the living and work conditions of tea plantation tea pickers. Though this place had many posters stating how they house and help their workers.

title: Lovely tea and cake but disappointing tour
text: The cafe and the views and setting are the highlight of this trip. The tour with a very uninterested guide and the hard sell afterwards put a dampener on the visit. The tour is free though and you tip as you see fit.

title: Very efficient
text: The tour was very efficient, but felt somewhat rushed and that the guide was pretty much just quoting a memorised spiel. The free cup of tea on the verandah afterwards was ordinary, but appreciated, and it does have a good view of the tea plantations. It was interesting to see the factory, but if you can plan to be there after 11am you've got a much better chance of seeing the tea coming in and being sorted. We were a bit early so the first load of the day hadn't yet arrived.

title: fast tour
text: It's easy to join a group to take a tour of this factory. The tour runs really fast, and assumes you already know something about tea and how it is produced. After the tour is over they serve you a cup of tea produced in the area.

title: Not worth the visit
text: We visited this factory on a Monday and there was no tea production happening so we were taken around the machinery which was not very interesting. Our tour guide spoke on auto pilot and was more interested in waving to her co-workers than in explaining anything to us. We were provided with a cup of tea afterwards but there was no explanation of what tea it was. At RP250 it is not expensive but it’s really not worth the time.

title: 20 min tour...
text: During our sri lanka trip we also wanted to visit a tea factory and since our accomodation in nuwara eliya was close to the san pedro facility we went there for a tour around noon. The entrance fee has meanwhile increased to 250 rupees which is still not very high, but the whole tour took also only around 20 minutes and was not very informative. At noon there was no production in the factory that day, however with production in the background we would have probably not understood our tour guide. We got a cup of tea afterwards but also without any further comments or explanation. Seems the quality of the tours in this factory has quite a wide variation.

title: Nice!
text: We bought almost all the tea from the shop and it’s really tasted! the explanation of how they make the tea is really curious

title: Tea at its best
text: We enjoy drinking tea and had never experienced what goes into growing and processing tea until we visited the Pedro Estate Nuwaraeliya tea factory. Enjoyable day out in very scenic part of Sri Lanka. Very clean and tidy facilities and great cup of tea. About 20 minute drive from city centre. Great drive. Our tour guide Sivakavj at the Banquet Boutique was the perfect guide with excellent knowledge and very friendly customer support. Ask for her personally and you will not be disappointed.

title: Average
text: I've visited many tea plantations in India and Sri Lanka. The tour here was very good and everything well explained. The guide didn't take us into the plantations or explain about Silver tips, white and green tea. Also, the tea offered after the tour is nice but the Damro tea factory is much better for a relaxing tea (free) and cake (paid) overlooking the plantations. Blue Field is also good to visit.

title: Slightly hyped up tea factory
text: The marketing for this factory is amazing, though note you are not allowed to take any pictures during the tour and have to wait until the guides are done with their lunch which can be any time after 2 pm. Tea sampling consists of 1 tea only, which is questionable given that you pay for your tour. Visit another tea factory instead.

title: Very nice, the tour was good
text: Really enjoyed the short visit here. The tour guide was really good, knew her stuff and very friendly to chat to. Visited on Christmas Day when the processing wasn’t happening so can’t comment on what it would be like on a working day.

title: Nice visit
text: Me and my family really enjoyed visit in Pedro tea factory.It was very informative and kids liked getting to know how tea is made.Tea tasting was enjoyable and it's free of charge.The landscaped are breathtaking.You can just walk freely among tea plantations and enjoy the atmosphere of this beautiful place.The prices of tea were very reasonable in comparison to other places that we visited later.

title: Cosy tea factory with good tour
text: Lovely tea factory with interesting tour which takes place every 10 minutes. Lovely outdoor area to have a cup of tea afterwards.

title: Fastest tour i got
text: Paid 250rupees for the tour.. it took about 20min all together.. the lady spoke very fast and rushed the whole process... She also asked whether she could give my change later however she didn't and I forgot about it so I don't know if she does that to everyone for side note to anyone reading this. We got some tea at the end and we didn't even know what kind of tea we we were drinking... The factory was cool inside and that's about it... I guess it's a must do for something to do in Nuwara Eliya. We took a stroll around the tea plantation which was nice and had some sick views of the dam and Mountains.

title: Lovely setting for a very interesting visit.
text: Great guide who explained everything clearly and concisely. Sixpacks of tea seem expensive at 2000 rupees but each pack of tea is 125g for just under £1.50 so good value really for a class product. Teaworkers were striking in Nuwara Eliya while we were there. They want 1000 rupees a day instead of the current 850. I so hope they get it as it is such a hard life.

title: Factory visit
text: Visited the tea factory and guided by the volunteer, about how the tea processing takes place ,step by step. Took about 25 minutes to finish the session. Then we were all served, crystal clear golden tea, aromatic and refreshing. Bought some tea packs also.

title: Off for tea
text: Average place to see tea garden, little bit of history of tea industry in Sri Lankan hill country. You could walk down the tea bushes. You can buy tea and refresh yourself with a nice and warm cup of tea.

title: Amazing Tea Garden
text: Perched on top of a hill a little away from the city center this tea garden is among one of the best in Sri Lanka. With a tour fee of LKR 250 the guide takes you through the factory with its century old machinery which are still in use. The tea produced here is a lovely light one - which you can sample for free. Another quirk about this factory is that they allow you to move very freely among the tea plantation. On a cloudy day this is amazing

title: Disappointed
text: This is not a working factory and therefore not very interesting. They are more interested in selling the tea. Very disappointed. It should be classed as a poor museum.

title: Just visited the boutique
text: When we went there the factory was closed, so we just visited the sales center and bought some items. Some people were going into the factory although it was not functioning at the time. We had to settle for another factory another time.

title: Tea factory tour and sales
text: It's just a tea factory and there is a catch. They take you for a tour of the factory and show you, in real time, how black tea is processed. At the end , they do serve you tea and you have the opportunity to buy some to take away. Not too bad as loose leaf tea is getting increasingly more difficult to find in some countries.

title: Pleasant visit with some annoyance
text: Pedro Tea Estate is close to Nuwara Eliya - a 10 minute drive maximum. We had a guided factory tour which was quite interesting despite it being presented by a not very interested in us young woman. Afterwards we enjoyed a cup of tea in their tea cafÃ© overlooking the tea garden. We were allowed to wander through the tea gardens on our own. Allow 1 hour for all. They also have a shop but you have to purchase tea in packs of 3 or 6 which is quite a lot if you have limited luggage room or are still travelling on. I thought this ridiculous and gimmicky to make you have to buy more than you want. Otherwise it's very pleasant to visit.

title: World famous Pedro Estate
text: Impressive history. Lovely view from the terrace. Great shop. We bought lots of teas and are enjoying them at home with fond memories.

title: Quick tour of a tea factory
text: This place offers tours of a tea plantation and then a cafe area to sample the products. OK for an hour or so if you are in the area.

title: We expected much more than we saw.
text: We traveled from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya by train and saw beautiful hills covered with tea plantations. From Nuwara Sliya we took tuk-tuk to Pedro Tea Factory. Factory tour was very short, year was to dry so we couldn't see entire process of tea preparation.View from factory and tea degustation were very nice.

title: Great introduction to tea industry
text: Very informative visit. Unfortunately machinery was being maintained and cleaned when we visited so we did not see it in full production but that is probably a blessing - the machines generate and need a lot of heat to do the drying of the tea. Felt sorry for the staff - very poorly paid compared to our standards.

title: Step back in time
text: If you're used to factory tours this a bit different - the end-to-end process (which is interesting) is largely carried out on machinery from the early 20th century. Very interesting visit - and of course you can buy all kinds of tea!

title: Nice view. Behind factory
text: Its look amazing big mountain around factory near factory there is tea shop you can order tea its frash tea and nice teste

title: Morning visit. Quick average tour. Nice views.
text: One of several tea factories I visited in Sri Lanka. Beautiful location, great pictures over the tea plantations. Tour was not overly informative. They were processing leaves at time of visit so it was nice to observe that and get some explanation. All be it rather short. They produce Orthodox (leaves remain somewhat in tact) and CTC (chopped leaves typically for tea bags) tea, the Orthodox production was a bit grey on detail. Nice cuppa afterwards. I would not go out of my way for this Tea factory, if you have been to Mackwoods, Bluefields or what I considered my best visit, Loolecondera Tea Factory then skip this. Pedro did not make my top 5.

title: Very interesting tour
text: Really enjoyed this tour of the tea factory led by a very pleasant knowledgeable young lady. We saw the process from arrival of the leaves through to the final packing and got a taste at the end.

title: Nicely organized tea factory tour
text: My wife and I been to the Pedro Tea Estate and we've enjoyed the tour inside the factory which seemed very organized. The tour guide was very informative and nice with kids. We highly recommend this factory than others due it's view and nicely put tour.

title: Pleasant walk through the history of tea making
text: We went to the factory early in the morning which was a good decision, because we were the only ones. The factory is small so the tour doesn't take a lot of time. I would recommend you to choose any other day except monday, because sunday is non working day and we weren't able to see first and second phase of the process. It was fascinating to see how they still produce tea with the machinery from late 19th century. The only minus was our guide which wasn't very talkative. We were asking her a lot of question and she just gave us short answers.

title: Great cup of tea!
text: Spent an hour being shown around the factory having the process explained to us. This was followed by a taste of their tea in a very pleasant cafÃ©. Tea was so good I ordered some when I got home. Good way to spend some time.

title: Great explanation and tour of a working tea factory
text: Our guide had excellent English and understood our intricate questions about the production of tea. This was a nice shortish tour (30mins?) where we could really see what happens at night when the tea is processed. Free cuppa at the end.

title: Fun visit!
text: We visited with 2 young children and they enjoyed the tour. We were lucky when we arrived as they were just finishing up the processing of the tea and the warmth and smells from the tea were fantastic. The tour was informative but not too informative that it became boring, you moved quite quickly from one station to the next, the guide we got was great. Lovely views over the plantation. Enjoyed a fresh tea complimentary after the tour, doesn't taste like tea I have every experienced before.

title: Fun visit!
text: We really enjoyed our tour here and the tea was great. Very informative. The views were so beautiful around the factory.

title: Good tour
text: A good tour of a tea factory, giving an insight into the tea making process. The guide spoke good english and was very informative.

title: Incredible views with delicious tea!
text: We loved taking a long walk through the tea fields, there is a lake you can walk to which is beautiful and, if walking isn't your thing, the views from the tea house at the top are just incredible! Plus their tea is delicious and just what you need to warm you up as it's a bit chilly up there.

title: Interesting
text: Enjoyed our visit here , nice cup of tea, interesting tour,no hard sell, sadly the tea picking women get paid a pittance for long hours in the baking sun and its hard to witness such harsh treatment and then forget about it. I'll never take my morning tea for granted again.

title: Interesting visit
text: Definitely worth a visit. For 200 Rupees per person you get about 30 minutes of explanation while walking through the factory and a cup of tea afterwards. Money/value is good in my opinion.

title: Interesting & informative
text: This is an interesting place to go & find out more about the making of black tea in a beautiful setting among some vintage machinery. The guide was excellent - patient & very happy to answer questions. Tips: As production is overnight you don't see much action. No pics inside but great shots from balcony afterwards. Stop close to the factory to snap tea pickers at work

title: i was moved by this factory
text: We visited the tea factory in November 2016. I found it very upsetting the tea pickers are very poorly paid. We were told by our guide of the tour by the time you are 40 their backs have gone and go no longer work. The machinery is so out of date (no photos allowed of the machinery). I just felt they are like modern day slaves it definitely made me think how lucky we all are with our housing and way off life.

title: Excellent Tea Factory - superb experience
text: We really enjoyed our visit to the tea factory. Its very calm and charming place. The lady took us to the factory tour thru all the processes and nicely explained the various tea categories. It ends with a hot cup of BOP tea!

title: Beautiful fields
text: It was our third tea factory (we were bored :D) and the guiding thing was like any other, nothing special, only thing we didn't like is that all their production is over night so prepare you won't see much action. Anway, this estate has the most beautiful landscape so far, it is worth going there just for the view and good pictures ;). Take a walk a sit on the balcony sippingh the tea and enjoying the view. Beautiful Sri Lanka, it really is!

title: Magical
text: Totally enchanting location beautiful landscape and stunning variety of flowers trees and shrubs a must for garden lovers. I feel the cost of ticket justified would highly recommend. So much better than sitting on the beach ...

title: Too expensive
text: At 2000 rupees at the time of writing, its too expensive for what it offers. An aimless walk in a garden and a house. It’s quite difficult to get to as well. Rather spend the couple of hours at the lovely Bentota beach.

title: Interesting exploring the garden plus a tour of the house
text: Its a lovely quiet spot away from roads and houses. We walked around the garden first exploring the different areas and interesting statues etc - best for me was the courtyard with amazing bat lilies I've never seen before. Each group has a personal tour of the house - luckily the tour ahead of us had started by the time we got there, so we able to relax and wait on the terrace. The house itself is interesting with pictures and photos, apparently now owned by old staff of Mr Bawa. As others have said it is quite expensive, and is cash only. There is nothing else around the area for drinks or snack so be prepared. Overall I preferred Lunuganga which isn't too far away but I guess that's a personal preference.

title: Wonderful
text: Bawa Garden or Brief garden is a picturesque landscaped garden that lies few kilometers inland of Bentota. With stone steps, shady paths, esthetically structured trees and plants, this is a splendid tranquil space to wander and explore. The garden and the colonial villa set in its middle was owned by Bewis Bawa, the brother of the famous architect Geoffrey Bawa.

title: Resplendent Respite in tranquil setting
text: Our driver told us about this place as we had some knowledge of the Bawa family. It is a lovely garden and a unique house built to suit the conditions. The house contains some nice art and furniture and the current custodian provides a guided tour included in the ticket price

title: Serene Gardens Well Maintained
text: Went to the 9.30am viewing with a guide. 1500 lkr. Very lush and green with a large variety of plants and foliage. Beautiful views with water on 2 sides of the estate. Used to be a rubber plantation. Took about an hour to walk around. It is not a flower garden and cannot be compared to Butchart Gardens in Canada. About 20 acres.

title: FASCINATING PROVENANCE
text: A mixture of beautifully maintained gardens and the art of Australian Donald Friend makes this a fascinating discovery. The site was bequeathed to the head gardener on the death of Bevis Bawa, and he certainly has an intriguing tale to tell.

title: Stunning garden
text: Visited the brief garden near bentoto Sri Lanka for the second time A very special place beautifully kept Easy by tuktuk from town

title: Singalese heritage garden
text: Do drive there with a car and driver. It is located in the countryside and not accessable by touring bus. Entry 5 euro per person. Truly stunning location that gives an impression how Sri Lankan nature was in the 20th century with peaceful villages and green mountains. If you wish to find some peacefulness you will enjoy the garden and surroundings with ricefields ao. This garden is more architectural than botanical. Educated guide tells about architect Major Bawa and his family history.

title: not much to see
text: just a green lush garden. one has to pay 1500 lkr as a entrance fee & ring a bell , a person wil open the gate & wil show you the way to enter the garden in a narrow path. after you finish the garden you can climb to the apartment side .. a man vl come to take you around & tel you the history of that place & about the owner of the garden . you can skip, not much recommended

title: Fascinating garden and house
text: Architecturally beautiful landscaped garden. Very clever layout with plenty of interest. If you are just looking for some pretty flowers then this is not the garden for you. If however you appreciate landscape design then you will be well rewarded. After visiting the garden, we then had a guided tour of the house, which in itself was fascinating. At LKR1000, this was very good value. We spent close on two hours here.

title: Surprised
text: We had a guide on this day we didn’t even know he was taking us to this garden ,wow what a surprise ,we enjoyed it immensely . Garden was wonderful with all its different sections ,the house and artworks and Bevis Barwa stories ,all the goingson in his home ... AMUSING ... a must see !!!

title: Can be skipped if not interested in Architechture
text: Nice maintained garden in near Bentota But entry fee is too much and also no one is there to guide in garden

title: Secret hideaway!
text: Unlike Lunuganga, this attraction can be visited at any time. We hired a tuk-tuk from our hotel in Bentota for 150rupees and the driver waited for us-the visit lasted just over an hour but you can dawdle as much as you like. You really do get the impression of this being a 'secret' garden after the journey there-hidden behind a wall in the middle of densely wooded area yet close enough to Bentota. You can visit the house with its various artworks, along with a fascinating account of Bevis Bawa and his life among the top brass in spite of his sexual proclivities. A totally unusual experience and, if you visit early like us at 9.30am, you might get the place to yourselves!

title: Small
text: This place was a bit smaller than we expected. We came straight from visiting Lununganga and it just doesn’t compare. We spent about 30-45 minutes there and that included an explanation of sorts about some of the art work and the house. It is a nice garden but not maintained to the same standard as his brothers. We enjoyed it as we like gardens, but it was extremely hot with no offer of relief from that anywhere, there isn’t much to it and it just felt like something was missing somehow.

title: Come for the garden, stay for the art
text: We did this as a day excursion from Colombo, and though our driver had a terrible time finding the place, eventually we made it (it doesn't help that when you get to the road that's actually marked "Brief Garden" you'll be met by a guard telling you it's under repair and you have to go a different way that's not marked. The tour starts in the gardens, where you're free to wander around, stopping at various pools and lookouts. At the house you may well be met by a guide--ours was the owner himself--and that's where the real fun begins. There are statues and paintings all over the place, some indeed mildly erotic, but many just plain fun. My favorite may have been the whole wall made out of wine bottles. There's something wonderful on every wall and around every corner. Even a polished coconut on a coffee table looks like a piece of art.

title: Gem of a garden
text: A hidden gem - loved it! Beautiful garden and house with lots of interest - a lot of architectural thought and a lifetime's work have gone into it. I love the fact that the house and garden was left to the Head Gardener on Bevis Bawa's death. A labour of love. I love the fact that so many Hollywood stars from the 40s/50s came and stayed there - the parties they must have had! Very interesting way to spend a couple of hours if you are in the Bentota area.

title: Terrible
text: I don’t think that this garden worth to visit It’s just a simple house with Garden in front And u should pay 10 dollar It’s very small It’s another botanical garden in Srilanka that was much more better

title: Must for nature lovers
text: A hidden gem, that should not be missed by anyone interested in gardening/plants or nature. It is amazingly beautiful, with a mixture of tropical forest/park and a European style garden, plus the house itself. The forest setting also meant bird song. We were unable to stay for the tea and cakes available at the main house, but that would have made a very nice conclusion. Surprised that not all reviewers give it top marks, but as for all gardens one aspect could be the time of the year of the visit. In early February it was certainly wonderful. Photos show that among house guests in the past were both Edward VII, Vivien Leigh and Laurence Olivier.

title: An alternative to the beach
text: Beautiful gardens, a map and plant guide would have been nice rather than just wandering aimlessly around. You can't get lost as all paths eventually go back to the bungalow. The collection of art, sculpture and furniture inside the bungalow was very interesting and you do get a guided tour of that. Entrance fee of Rs2,000 was a bit high especially as local people have to pay the same amount. A little effort in marketing the site better would attract more visitors without detracting from the tranquility of the gardens

title: A good day trip within Western Provence
text: Small garden walk, interesting design. The artwork within the house is diverse-paintings, sculptures. Unique pieces if you look closely. The road getting there was small-take a tuk or a high clearance vehicle .

title: Lovely Gardens and House
text: The tuc-tuc ride to the gate is up some tiny little roads which is quite strange for such a notable attraction. The guided tour of the house was excellent with a very knowledgable guide who was able to describe a lot about Bevis Bawa and his life in Sri Lanka. It's great that he left his house and gardens to local people and they are doing a great job in presenting it to the public. The gardens are beautiful and this place is a lovely peaceful haven.

title: 1 of 4 Seniors in Sri Lanka
text: Amazing gardens with plants and flowers to wander around. Guide was very informative regarding the history. House is full of objects and artwork collected over the years.

title: worth seeing
text: i have been before but went back for the second time,the story is very interesring ,and not a lot of people have herd about it,it is 2000 rupees to go in and a man to show you around.

title: Artists Jungle Retreat
text: This is the home and garden of Bevis Bawa, Aide-de-Camp to 2 British governors of Ceylon and elder brother of famed architect Geoffrey. Visited this place as a result of being turned away from Geoffrey Bawas 'Lunuganga' because we were 10 minutes late! Talk about bureaucracy gone mad. Those of you who have travelled to Sri Lanka and other Asian countries know that travel times can vary dramatically, apparently this fact eludes the managing trust of Lunuganga. Anyway, Brief Garden is a delightful surprise, meandering garden paths that can end suddenly and others that take you to amazing surprises. Your ticket gives you access to the gardens and house (unlike Lunuganga) and a very informative guide that worked for Bevis himself. He has a wealth of information on the gardens, house and the man himself. Ask him about the famous visitors to the property like Sir Lawerence Olivier, Vivien Leigh and Australian artist Donald Friend who came for a weekend and stayed for 6 years! Do yourselves a favour and when in Bentota visit 'Brief' Garden. You will be enchanted.

title: A beautiful area.
text: We thoroughly enjoyed visiting these charming gardens. We thought it was nice that we could just wander around on our own without having to go on a guided tour. At the end of our walk the caretaker showed us round the house which was also very interesting. Bevis Bawa seemed to be an amazing man! Definitely well worth a visit!

title: Beautiful garden, peaceful location, odd man...
text: The Bevis Bawa Brief Garden, the managed home of a wealthy eccentric old Brit, he lived an alternative lifestyle here, perhaps the less said about that the better, but his home and garden are simply beautiful. A small but incredibly peaceful location, one wonders how these locations come to be or how the wealthy land owners settle on the place. You cannot help but think about life in Sri Lanka back in the early 20th century or beforehand at the height of colonialism and desire for such hedonistic tropical retreats. Here was a man who received visitors such as Edward VIII at his well attended private parties...

title: A world away... imagine yourself in a different time...
text: Yes, imagine yourself in the house of an Edwardian gentleman somewhere in SE England... and yet the plants are too exotic, the temperature too hot and the humidity too high! This is the house and garden of Bevis Bawa, brother of the famous architect, Geoffrey. It is difficult to find: our very experienced driver-guide has been here many times before but he had to ask local people the way on several occasions. There are no signs pointing to the place! Once parked, ring the doorbell. Once you have paid the 1000 LKR each, you will be a instructed to explore the garden by yourself and then make your way in to the house. The gardenis absorbing with its many paths, wonderful flora and nooks. There are plenty of photo opportunities outside and in. Once you are inside the house, you will be met and given an on-and-off tour of the rooms. Interesting furniture and fascinating photos. There is no cafe or shop here! Thank goodness! Would I return? Yes!

title: Lovely spot if you have time on your hands
text: The garden is very quaint and one can only imagine what it must have been like in its day. The collection of artwork and history is interesting too. If you have time and are interested in gardens and art then definitely pop through.

title: Beautiful Space
text: A little bit off the beaten track, but well worth it. The large garden is so cleverly designed with many levels and features, it's a peaceful space. The house is beautifully designed too, with many interesting photos and memorrabilia. The huge painting on the wall by Donald Friend tells the story of the area, and there are many other lovely pieces. Small groups only.

title: Intriguing and enchanting!
text: At both sides of the entrance lane two beautiful sculptures on pillars to lure one in to visit this garden. And we were not disappointed, there was throughout plenty to discover, flowering trees and plants, narrow lanes, lined with old tree roots like sculptures, leading to small sitting and wide viewing area's. Intriguing sculptures. The house breathes history with its old photographs, artefacts and paintings. Especially the very large mural depicting Sri Lanka, in all its small details. The house, as well as the garden, is the perfect setting in its lush and tropical green landscape. Not to be missed while in Sri Lanka!

title: Lovely quiet place
text: A wonderful visit to a serene beautiful garden and house. The staff were lovely and we learned a lot. It's a little of the beaten track so take a tuk-tuk.

title: A hidden garden
