text: Certainly is well hidden and not very easy to find but very well kept and lovely setting. Entrance fee a little steep for what there is to see but I imagine the up keep is a huge job. Very well maintained garden with lots of places to hide and escape. A few statues and ornaments to look at and some beautiful flowers. A couple of water features, not he worlds largest house and garden but nice to escape and take in the peace and quiet. House is ok but a very small tour. Can tick it off my list of tourist attractions.

title: Absolutely wonderful.
text: A short drive from Bentota this is well worth taking the visit. It seems there is no need to book. We just showed up, were turned loose in the lush garden and then worked our way back to the old owners house for a guided tour. The property is not crowded, it is well maintained and quietly welcoming. Well worth the effort.

title: Beautiful Gardens & House
text: Buried in the middle of the Srilankan countryside Brief Gardens is a wonderful peek back in time to when Bevis Bawa designed a garden full of indigenous trees & Shrubs. We saw too many species of birds to count, & were privileged to see an iguana & a mongoose. The house is fascinating look at the way this remarkable man lived.

title: Somewhat faded in all aspects
text: The garden is about 10 kms from Bentota and is, for Sri Lanka, quote expensive to get in - 1,000 rupees. The garden is pleasant but not exceptional. The house is shabby and the artwork is drab and not very interesting. You are not given access to the upstairs. Personally, for anyone who has seen gardens or botanical gardens elsewhere or historical houses, this is not worth the visit and certainly not at that price. We had made a special stop off in Bentota for it but we were disappointed,

title: Peaceful
text: Amazing small garden and interesting house. An oasis of calm in the bustle of the nearby cities. A few more labels on the plants would enhance the visit. The tour of the house is quite short, but interesting. Lovely to get away from the beach for an hour or two.

title: Wonderful garden and villa - a must when visiting Bentota
text: Not too far from Bentota it is a must to pay a visit to Brief Garden - Bevis Bawa. The garden was made after cutting the rubber trees. The garden is designed by a landscape architect and is beautifully located on a hill overlooking the valley.The villa is also worthwile visiting. It contains a lot of art and old Dutch wooden furniture.

title: Most interesting
text: The extensive garden and country home of (in)famous Sri Lankan landscape architect, Bevis Bawa. Part of the charm of the place is that our tour was conducted by Mr. da Silva who was Bevis's head gardener for many years and who inherited the estate and still lives there. The planning of the garden, the rather outrageous gay life-style of Bevis, and his eclectic collection of art and photos are all brought to life by Mr da Silva. Lovely tranquil setting. Easily combined with a visit to Lunuganga, garden and home to Bevis's brother, Geoffrey.

title: More than Brief
text: A former rubber estate, this garden was the creation of Bevis Bawa, brother of Geoffrey Bawa, well known Sri Lankan architect. Set in 5 acres it is a stunning wild, beautiful and slightly erotic garden. Set around a beautiful house. It is open all day, and a guide will take you around the public areas of the house, but you are free to walk the grounds. The estate was divided when Bevis died, with the great proportion of the estate being left to the workers, and the house and garden being left to an architectural practice.

title: Beauty in the middle of nowhere
text: You can appreciate the amazing effort that has been made over many years to get and keep this garden in such a wonderful state. It is peaceful walking around and appreciating the landscape architecture. The house is also worth visiting and the tour guide we had was most informative. Definitely worth the effort to get to and the LKR1000 admittance.

title: Heavenly Hideaway
text: The minute I read about this place, I just knew I had to visit it. The grounds are simply gorgeous- a tamed tropical rustic maze of interconnecting paths and steps interlaced with stone ornaments and pools. The Japanese inspired terraced water feature is wonderfully serene. The villa, perched above the gardens is beautifully airy with lots of Bawa’s eclectic art collection and photographs on display. The guide is very knowledgeable and passionate about the Bevis Bawa story - well worth a visit.

title: a lovely place to get lost...
text: Brief Gardens by Bevis Bawa - This was not on my itinerary, but found it in my tour book the night before. I asked my driver if we could visit the next am. Was so very pleased I did. Serene and peaceful place to enjoy wonderful gardens, secret green spots in the landscape. I thought it would be a great place for children, or adults, to play hide-and-go-seek! Birds and the peaceful breeze through the leaves and palms is the only sounds you hear. Painting, sculpture, ceramics and books dress the modest cottage. Wonderful place for a peaceful visit for a couple of hours....

title: Interesting Venue
text: This is a good place to spend an hour to an hour and a half. The gardens aren't what the must have been when Bevis Bawa was alive but they're still spectacular. The house tour is interesting as well.

title: Beautiful garden with interesting history
text: Fascinating place to visit if you are travelling to or from Bentota. I wasn't expecting to see something like this tucked away in the jungle and it was a lovely surprise to be able to wander around the gardens and the house. I would love to been able to see all the nooks and crannies in the house, but we were able to experience was really cool. Interesting mix of cultures and the past.

title: " Brief " Encounter !
text: Those who are interested in landscaping, Open space and Architecture should visit this place. The creator is a few decades ahead of his time. This place is not Wheel-chair accessible and they should think of some way to overcome the issue soon. The other big issue is that they have no Risk Assessment and Management Plan. Nice experience and one would not regret going. Cheers

title: The Garden is good but the history of the Bungalow is the main attraction
text: The garden, hidden away amongst the dense jungles of Sri Lanka, is well worth a stroll but it's the bungalow and it's history that will capture your interest. The colonial bungalow where Bevis Bawa lived and entertained his guests is a glimpse into the heady days and lifestyle of Sri Lanka's most famous landscaper and friend of the rich and famous including actors Peter Finch and Vivien Leigh who stayed at the bulgalow. .

title: Worth for arts and architecture enthusiasts
text: Otherwise skip, as the sight is quite remote from Bentota. This garden and the adjacent villa are Bewis Bawa's magnificent work. The sight is full of artsy and homoerotic artifacts, sculpture and furniture. The design is a blend of a modernist and Asian traditional styles. The house keeper profoundly explained to us about the concept and history of the house and its dweller. Nice place.

title: Inspiring garden
text: Beautifully kept house and garden, owned by a gardener! A short tuk tuk from town thru windy narrow lane ways. Interesting history and artworks around the house.

title: Good maintained garden
text: Nice maintained garden in near bentona But entry fee is too much and also no one is there to guide in garden

title: lovely and peaceful
text: On arrival my husband and I were left to explore the grounds on our own and we could take as much or little time to do this. Warning - Don't forget to apply insect repellent before visiting unlike us - The mosquitos enjoyed feasting on our flesh !! As we arrived at the house we were joined by our guide who was eloquent in describing how and why Bevis created the house and grounds the way he did. The guide was clearly a great admirer of the great man. A lovely way to spend the afternoon.

title: Marginal decline from the earlier visit
text: Bevis Bawa was arguably the more talented of the two brothers as far as landscaping is concerned. However, it is somewhat sad to see the whole establishment slowly but surely falling in maintenance standards - it requires more than gate collections to maintain the gardens and establishment of this magnitude.. This time around it was also somewhat disturbing to see the evidence of the obvious debauchery that took place at The Brief during the man's life. But then, who is to stand in moral judgement over these matters...

title: Hard to find but enjoyable
text: I'd read about this place before coming to Sri Lanka and as I was staying nearby I thought I'd give it a go. A couple of friends I met on my holiday joined me (we visited Richmond Castle on the same day) and we all really enjoyed it. It's worth being aware that it is quite remote and a little difficult to get to, and is not like an immaculately maintained National Trust stately home or perfectly manicured public garden. It was once someone's home and has been kept that way. It feels natural and atmospheric and we really liked that about it, as it was less touristy and therefore more relaxing. Your enjoyment of the brief garden will, as with most things in life, be based on your own personal taste but don't let that put you off visiting!

title: Nice ride,disappointing and over priced garden!
text: The Brief garden is about a 30 minute tuk tuk ride away from Bentota (we paid 300 rupees for 2 of us including driver waiting time). Entrance to the garden is 1000 rupees each. The ride was so picturesque through real Sri Lankan lush country. The garden has got a nice history but as keen garden lovers and members of National Trust, visiting this garden was disappointing and overpriced. The garden was owned by Bevis Bawa who was a self taught artist and sculpture. He was also a Sri Lankan actor and there are photos of him with Vivienne Leigh and other actors. He was a heavy smoker, drinker, and homosexual which is reflected in the paintings and many sculptures in the garden and house. The garden is not very big and it took about an hour and a half to walk around the garden and visit the house with the guided tour. It was landscaped by his brother Geoffrey, whose own garden Lunuganga is supposed to be a lot better to visit but we didn't get the time. It's a pleasant enough walk around the garden but nothing really that impressive, but we saw some lovely sunbirds and even a snake! A lot of the paths needed cleaning. There are interesting items of art and furniture around the house but sadly it didn't live up to our expectations, nor to what we had heard. Some sculptures seemed in need of a good clean from the overgrowth. Definitely not worth the entrance fee, but a lovely ride.

title: Lovely Place
text: Brief Garden is somewhat off the radar as a regular tourist destination in Sri Lanka is concerned but well worth a visit if you are in Bentota. The garden itself is located down a narrow lane way and would not be accessible by any vehicle larger than a mini van. Entrance fee is a little steep at 10,000 rupees but if it's going towards the garden upkeep then so be it. The garden has some beautiful landscaping features including a Japanese garden, numerous water features, stone stepped terraces, brick archways and the original residence which houses many artefacts and paintings owned by the Bevis Bewa family.

title: Beautiful garden and nice house
text: First of all, don't forget that this was Bevis's private house so don't expect to find a palace or a museum when you come here because you won't find that. The place is very remote and difficult to access, which in my opinion makes the whole experience more charming but some may not enjoy this. The garden is big and well looked after, and if you spend enough time walking around it you may see some cute animals. Make sure you sit down and enjoy the clean air and sounds of nature for a while if you go. The house is nice too, but I'm sure it has many interesting features that I missed (as I am not an architect and I'm not familiar with many building techniques) I think it would be really nice if the staff provided some kind of information about who Bevis was and why this place is so amazing (perhaps a guided tour every 30 min?) I would recommend to visit this place if you're not travelling from too far, but maybe it's not worth spending 2-3 hours driving just for that.

title: A part of touchable personal history ...
text: ... combined with a unique garden experience, some kind of jungle, art objects, seldom flowers, the extraordinary bat-headed lily just finished to bloom and (never seen before) porcelaine roses now in it's best red colour, all incredible, sunk deep into the soul and heart. A must for people who seek silence and beauty.

title: Beautiful Gardens - another Hidden Gem
text: Brief Garden offered an opportunity for us to get away from the beach resort for a while. The garden itself is hidden away, but well worth the effort involved in finding it. Beautiful tropical plants at every turn and an interesting house filled with art that gives a insight in to the life of the owner - Bevis Bawa. Hidden Gem!

title: Come to see a fine plant collection in a lovely setting
text: We came here on our penultimate day. It's a bit tricky to find but a bit of research and a local driver is a great help and worth the trip. It's like walking into one of the exotic plant houses at Kew. I noted 5 species of Strelitzia (bird of Paradise flower) within minutes of arriving and the scarce bat lily was flowering when we visited. The garden slopes and is severally terraced with a central mini-cascade and a beautiful mini walkway lined with ginger plants. We spotted a humming bird but which flew off before it could be identified. One of the Banyan Trees was also flowering and I think that the Lord Buddha was born beneath one so they are revered for religious reasons. The guide in charge also showed us the house ground floor with some of Bevis Bawa's works of art. A remarkable character over 6 and a half feet tall during his adult life and with a certain Bohemian taste in art. We were delighted that we went.

title: Hidden gem!
text: It is not easy to find it, but local taxi/rickshaw drivers know it well and google maps also can help. It is a true garden architect and artistic place, giving a special feeling of the decadent lifestyle by former owner. Really worth the effort!

title: Beautiful gardens created by very interesting man
text: Really enjoyed our visit here. It was definitely off the beaten track and our driver had never even heard of it but it was well worth going. Beautiful gardens and architecture. Highly recommended.

title: Brief garden
text: Beautiful and peaceful place to visit. It worth to see it. Would love to spent the twenties there...

title: Nice alternative program for approx. 2hrs
text: Interesting private garden and house to see even though it has the regular plants as everywhere in the region. Some guidance is being offered in the house at the end of the whole tour. Not sure if 1000 rs. are an appropriate entrance fee but it was a nice short trip from Bentota (about 20min drive with rikshaw). Make sure your rickshaw driver waits for you..

title: Interesting Visit!
text: If you are in the area then it is highly advisable to visit this place. More than the legacy of Geoffrey Bawa it is the green landscape and the calm environment that takes over mind and soul!

title: No wonder it is a secret in a beautiful location
text: Former Plantation bungalow and gardens named after Bevis Bava's father a well known lawyer of Sri Lanka. It is located inland off Dharga town, no wonder it is secret as there are hardly any signs shown on this very narrow village road. All you need to do is ask any of the locals around here as they all know it. Once you get to the main front gates you have to ring a makeshift bell and an attendant will welcome you. Beautiful gardens with an incredible amount of tropical flowers and trees on narrow footpaths with statues dotted around. You need to spend at least half a day here to soak up the atmosphere. The entrance ticket price includes a pot of tea laid outside in the lawns of the bungalow. Inside the bungalow walls are littered with photographs of some Holywood legends and royalty who have visited the place over the years.

title: DISAPPOINTING
text: There can be little doubt that, in its prime, this house and garden was once very impressive and well-worth a visit. However, it is now very run down and only a short step from becoming ramshackle and overgrown. Still of interest for those who wish to see something of the former colonial lifestyle, but nothing more.

title: Only requires Brief Visit
text: Gardens were a bit disappointing, didn't take long to look around. The house itself is very pretty, had loads of questions but the local tour guide only knew how to say "Mr Bawa 2 metres tall!" And that was it. Our tuk tuk driver knew more. Well over priced at 1000 each.

title: Fascinating visit.
text: We took a Tuk Tuk from the Cinnamon Bey Hotel in Beruwala, 1000rps including a stop at the magnificent Buddist temple en route. Would be very difficult finding this garden without a guide. Attractive gardens with lovely views but the highlight is the bungalow tour with the resident owner explaining everything. Well worth the visit just to see all the artwork and artefacts of a recently decadent by-gone age. Probably a bit boring for youngsters. Well worth the 1000Rp entrance fee.

title: Off the beaten trail
text: On my last visit to Sri Lanka in October 2015 I had visited the Geoffrey Bawa Garden at Lunuganga (see my separate review) but had no time to visit his brother Bevis's place. So I was able to rectify this on my latest tour Access is along badly made roads and signage is not great. The garden and house would prove difficult to visit for anyone with mobility problems. The attraction would not be suitable for large groups Not as expansive as Lunuganga, Brief is more intimate and to my mind contained more colourful and lush planting with some exotic specimens. Within the grounds some impressive stone and art work. The house is also more interesting with an eclectic collection of works (some homo erotic) giving an impression of the bohemian and privileged lifestyle once enjoyed by its occupants Although off the usual tourist trail this was well worth a visit

title: Interesting
text: Lovely gardens to wander through with sculptures dotted around then guided through the house, ending with a cup of tea! Great views

title: A lovely surprise
text: We visited the Brief Garden just a short distance from hubbub of Bentota. It is a little slice of tranquility. Although the garden is smaller than Lunuganga it is still well worth a visit. We arrived there just as it started to rain but umbrellas were quickly provided. At the end of the tour of the garden before we looked around the house we had an excellent cup of tea with the owner who had inherited the house from Bevis Bawa. Take the chance if you can to make the time for this chat as it is full of interesting information about the history of the house and garden and its creator. Do go along if you have the time.

title: Bevis Bawa's retreat in a gloriously decadent and stylish house and garden
text: If you are going to Lunagunga (brother Geoffrey Bawa's weekend retreat) I recommend that you visit Brief in the morning, then have lunch at Lunagunga and go round that garden afterwards. I completely endorse the review by Romeboy which says it all much better than I can. Watch out for the photo of Larry Olivier and Peter Finch, who stayed when they were filming Elephant Walk (wonderful old poster at the Empire Hotel in Kandy!). Very tricky to find - take a driver or a tuk-tuk.

title: A real garden in the tropics, a bit of history too
text: We went by tut tut which cost approx 1500 rupees, entrance was 1000 rupees, a very interesting place, lovely gardens with little secret corners, all very tropical , ending with a tour of the house with its paintings and artworks, what a time they must have had !!!

title: Decadence, Myth, Eros, Art, Still Hang in Colonial House and Grounds - beware of steps
text: We recommend taking a tuk-tuk there as the directions to the house are minimal. Also, there are many steps (some of them high) and uneven terrain in the grounds and garden, which could be challenging for the elderly or differently-abled. This is were Bevis Bawa retired after his brief career in the army and where he surrounded himself with a bevy of boys, young men, gentlemen and similar masculine companions. While the grounds are nice, we liked the house the most. Beautifully designed, decorated and furnished, it truly reflects Bawa's taste and upbringing. The Picassos, Gauguins and Cocteaus - despite being copies - reminisce of the atmosphere and the erotic fauna that the house enjoyed in the 50s and 60s. Walking in the open-air Roman-style baths in one of the room's private courtyard, we wondered what the darkened and foggy mirror would say if it were ever allowed to tell what it saw! The current resident, the former head gardener to whom Bawa donated the house (!), is doing a good job preserving the house as it was when Bawa died: simple, elegant, decadent, and yet ready for a pool party and music and boys, should the former ghosts decide to visit one night. A magical place indeed.

title: a paradise
text: Found the location in Lonely Planet guide book. We stopped there on our way from Colombo to Galle. Our driver had difficulty to find the place. Finally we arrived and paid the 1000Rs/p fee. Worth the price! The garden and house are very well maintained. Garden and house are so beautiful and quiet, 1-2 hours visit in this enchanted place

title: Nothing great, simple home garden, Nice colonial bungalow
text: Difficult to find the place as no directions are given. Entrance fee is Rs 1000. Garden is not at all great. Plenty of greenery and quite vast. The colonial bungalow is the highlight. Boring for children. It can be seen within an hour.

title: Breathtaking
text: We visited the Brief Gardens on the recommendations of the owner of Diya Sisila last January but didn't get a chance to go last year so made a point of going this year. Well it was certainly worth the wait, it was such a tranquil peaceful place to be and it just transported us back to the 1930's. We could just imagine what life would have been like living there in that era. It obviously isn't as it should be as they don't have the money for the upkeep but they are certainly trying to maintain it as best they can with limited funds. Following the many meandering paths lead you to the house which is awash with beautiful works of art and furniture that is now looked after by a wonderful Sri Lankan gentleman and his family. He very kindly gave us a history of Bevis and Geoffrey Bawa and the house and gardens that they created followed by a lovely cup of tea. We absolutely loved this place and will definitely visit again next time we are in Sri Lanka. I understand that the price advertised on Trip Advisor for the entrance fee is 370 rupees however it is now 1000 rupees (£5) but well worth it.......Fabulous.

title: Beautifully designed and maintained natural style garden
text: Beautifully designed and maintained natural style garden. Well worth a visit if gardens interest you.The guided tour of the house and information about Bevis Bawa was fascinating and cup of tea very welcome. Apparently the road has recently been improved ,we had no problems visiting by tuk tuk.

title: Beautiful garden and the best lunch.
text: The tour around the garden was beautiful if you like to see typical Sri Lankan trees, flowers and buildings. But the most wonderful thing about this visit was the lunch in the garden. We got served twelve different curries, all of them very tasty. We would recommend a trip here, mostly to taste the food.

title: Worthwhile and captivating
text: Our driver offered to bring us to this garden. We are eternally grateful for this suggestion. The guide seemed a little "annoyed" with the visitors but after showing genuine interest in the house and the life of the Bawa's, he appeared to be a very funny, thoughtful and knowledgeable guide. Loved it!!!

title: Short visit
text: We quite enjoyed our visit here - there isn't a huge amount to see .It cost 1000LKR. A tea room would be a bonus. We were taken there by our Tuk tuk driver from Suranga Tours - who i cant recommend enough. We much preferred Lunuganga gardens.

title: Emperor's new clothes
text: We felt this was a waste of time. Not much to see either in the garden or house. 500 rupees would have been better value. Very unwelcoming. No cafe or drinks, unlike guidebook. Would advise against visiting unless desperate for something to do!

title: Great place
text: We enjoyed visiting this beautiful property together with the history of this Aristocrratic Family in the Times of the British colony. A great artist and architect of gardens design. Definitely recommendable. Pity that the foundations of Sri Lanka do not invest to keep it nicer. Renovations works are needed because it is falling a liitle bit apart in the gardens.

title: off the beaten track
text: This was a really cool thing to do. The Tuk Tuk ride is fun, it takes you off the beaten track into the jungle. Upon arrival you ring on a big gong bell. A man lets you in on the side gate and allows you to walk around the gardens yourself and when you are ready to enter the house. You can see it was probably once a beautiful garden but don't expect the botanical gardens with gorgeous flowers and lush grass. It is more rustic. Upon entering the house, it reeks up hedonistic decadent parties once upon a time. It is a great house for entertaining. Bevis apparently loved to party. The art and antiques are beautiful. It is worth the trip. Something different - hard to explain.

title: Amazing gardens, place has a quaint old world queer feel - hope those boys did well from the estate
text: Loved strolling around the gardens and through the house. Fascinating to see how it has been maintained and to reflect on that era, good and not so good. Appreciated the gay art.

title: what an interesting place to visit
text: did not know much about this place ,but three people in one day recommended,and was very pleased to have gone.look it up first to see if its what you like.

title: Fascinating garden and house
text: This was one of the highlights of our time in Sri Lanka. If you enjoy gardens, art and architecture you should not miss this. Brief is hidden away inland of busy Bentota and is a tranquil oasis created by Bevis Bawa, brother of well known architect, Geoffrey Bawa. Previously a rubber plantation, the gardens have been beautifully designed and the house is full of beautiful art works by Bawa and his friends, including Donald Friend from Australia. You need to ring the bell when you arrive and time your visit so that you can then go to Geoffrey Bawa's country house at Lunuganga which is also well worth a visit.

title: Tranquil Garden
text: The Brief Garden is a must to visit. It is tranquil and yet totally alive with bird song. At the villa we were met by a guide who informed us about the history of the house and garden. The gardens are beautiful however, we would have lingered longer in the garden if there had been a tea room or refreshments to buy then we could have just sat and taken in the full experience.

title: An absolute gem
text: What a hidden gem! One of the most impressive, calm and beautiful places we have visited. We visited as a family with adult children. Walked around the garden - perfect for pictures. We also saw some monkeys! Off the beaten path, especially from Kalutara, but we had a driver with us who knew the way. Fascinating scenery and a must stop if you are in Bentota. Guide was very polite and informative. Only suggestion is to consider opening a gift shop. Lots of potential to sell tasteful postcards of garden views or reproductions from some of the art in the house.

title: Amazing!
text: A visit to the Brief Garden and bungalow is a must if you are in the Aluthgama area. Fascinating history, imaginative landscaping, lovely building, I could have moved in immediately!

title: An amazing and eclectic house and garden
text: The gardens and house are really lovely. You're free to explore the large garden then a guide will take you around the house. The gardens are filled with sections of tropical plants and features which are truly peaceful. The house sits at the top of a hill with calming views and is filled with personal objects and photos of interest depicting Bevis Bawa's relationships with many famous individuals such as Prince Edward (later Edward VIII) Lawrence Olivier and Agatha Christie. The house and garden contain interesting pieces of art as well as phalic statues. Those with with a less open mind or narrow thinking of the world may wish to avoid

title: Beautiful gardens, really interesting history
text: We felt this was well worth visiting and the entrance fee of 1000 LKR per person was reasonable. Very peaceful gardens that you can wander through and explore at your own pace. After visiting the gardens a friendly guide showed us the house and explained the history. Having read some other reviews on TripAdvisor I would suggest that if you are homophobic then don't visit - if you aren't, then enjoy the beauty and serenity of the garden and finding out about the interesting history of the house and the Bawa brothers.

title: Loverly walk
text: A lovely walk through the grounds around the winding paths was had, followed by a walk around the house which had some querky items like the outdoor bath and statue ( see if you can find it) ideally take mosque spray with you as we got a number of bites whilst in the gardens.

title: Really nice place
text: We spent about an hour or so here. It was nice, but the weather was really humid that day and our kids were getting a bit cranky. The gardens are well kept and we would love to live in this house, it's lovely. It's 1000 rupees per adult but overall I thought it was worth it

title: it is worth a visit - hidden secret
text: Already the way to brief garden is a little adventure and makes lot of fun. You pass little village(s), get the feeling driving though jungle. Brief garden itself is an oasis of silence. It is designed/arranged very well with nice trees, flowers, tiny lakes. The house itself a gem, with artistic paintings, a wonderful view. Interior is arranged very well. First we were skeptic about the idea going there but it is more than worth.

title: Peaceful paradise garden and house
text: I have nothing to add to comments and pictures of earlier visitors. An adorable place, away from mass tourism. I would stay there forever...

title: A surprise
text: The road to this place is really challenging - and it will make you wonder where on earth are you - but once you reach the place; every bump on the way is well worth it. It charges 3000 LKR for entry. The gardens are beautiful. The house tour will take you to days of glory of the european influence - its a must visit. I would love to visit again.

title: Peace in the jungle
text: Interesting jungle garden which is very peaceful and not busy. You can walk around the garden and then the house which has works of art created by Bevis Bawa . Saw a large monkey in the trees and also a minitor lizard. Take a picnic and enjoy the experience.

title: Interesting Story
text: Take a tuk tuk ride to the Bawa house and garden. Although garden needs some maintenance it's a lovely retreat with pathways through the tropical gardens. Aspects of the house are interesting as is the story of the talented Bawa brothers.

title: A must-go place but a bit too pricey !
text: I love the Bawa family history and went there as a kind of trip to the intimacy of Bewis. In fact, this is what you get... a good insight to yesteryear artistic life. Quite a good collection of artistic objects that remind you of Jean Cocteau. The garden is less enchanting except for the cascade and the century-old frangipan tree. I found the entry price of 1000 LKR too expensive, especially when there is no special fee for children under 18. Maybe, the fact that I am a regular visitor to the island makes me a bit more sensitive to this detail??!!!

title: A mountain side feeling near to beach area
text: A wonderful garden built by Captain Bawa and it is well kept until now. Nice old photos remind the old days of Sri Lanka (Ceylon).

title: Sad to see the Bawa name tarnished
text: As a fan of Bawa's work, it was disappointing that our entrance to the property began with a bad start, firstly because the caretaker was not happy with our arrival at 2:30pm. Then sadly a member of our party was falsely accused of potential wrong-doing (I.e walking into an entry and bending to look at a painting whilst we used an outside restroom) -this was made by a female who lived on the property, not the caretaker. The caretaker' excuse for the yelling was thinly veiled by an explanation of previous trouble they had experienced with past visitors. The visit had now kicked off to a bad start and the caretaker did not offer to take us around the gardens and describe the beauty and landscape architecture. We were left to wander aimlessly through the overgrown gardens before having a tour of the house. It is clear that the caretaker is very knowledgeable, and he provided curt and limited explanations of the beautiful works inside the home itself. This was not what we expected especially with our comparison visit to Lunuganga, and some previous internet reviews prior to our visit to Brief Gardens. So you may need to piece together your own reading and research prior to visiting this tranquil acreage. It is clearly a magnificent property with alarmingly priceless artworks out in open display and unprotected from the elements. The property is in a hidden location along an unkept road that all but disappears at the gate. This journey itself is an adventure! The road is only just big enough for a 10 seater van. So sadly, our 1000 rupee entry fee pp was seen as very expensive for our party of 5, and it is a quandary because the property needs the funds from entry fees to maintain the property. Perhaps some better management and direction is required to preserve such a beautiful history.

title: Beautiful gardens and gracious house guide
text: A very enjoyable hour exploring this lovely japanese inspired garden. Touring the house afterwards was interesting and the guide was knowledgable and passionate about the home.

title: A must for those who love a splendid garden. Bevis was the brother of renowned architect Geoffrey Bawa
text: The late Bevis Bawa created a botanical garden on his own private plot. And woaw, what a nice and cosy place it is. Now it is the trusted caretaker of the house who still maintains the magic, with its cherished botanical species. I sat with him and my then still very young daughter on the verandah, sipping a cup of tea. And it was an unforgettable experience. the luxury of a simple but tranquil haven. Good to forget the stress from home!

title: Brief gardens not worth the £10 entry price !
text: Beautiful setting with great views taken there by driver. Very overgrown and in need of serious maintenance. You could glimps the beauty that was once there when the gardens were maintained but they have been taken over by weed. The house although interesting was very dark which made it impossible to really see the art work. Most of the art work was of naked men in various poses although there was one of Sri Lanka with prominent sights depicted as one large Mural. I don't think it was worth the hefty entry price.

title: Nothing to be seen.
text: We spent some strange time in the garden and were surprised not to see anything interesting. Were surprise d to lots of Homosexual paintings and sculptures. The garden and house are a little bit old fashioned and outdated. If you have a spare 1000 and you saw everything on the island than you are welcome.

title: Tropical Not a British Stately Home, but that is the charm.
text: Our driver recommended this garden & house and we were not disappointed. The gardens, started in 1928, have a huge variety of tropical plants and trees. They are presented in formal & non-formal settings and provide a beautiful walk, shaded by these huge natural structures. It's not an immaculately kept stately home in Britain, this is Sri Lanka and not enough gardeners to keep up, but that is part of the charm of this place. The house and it's history are fascinating and has been visited by many famous people including Edward VII, Vivienne Lee and the Danish Queen Mother. We were treated to a lovely cup of local tea in the garden by the house. We were the only visitors at the time and enjoyed the tranquility of this hidden gem.

title: Lovely peaceful garden and home
text: Really enjoyed this experience, the artwork, library and sculptures were interesting. The garden was lovely and peaceful. Looking back I wish we had spent more time exploring both the house and gardens.

title: interesting style
text: a long ride. expected much..maybe that was the problem. i liked the location and the spread of the land..a large place with a fine vantage view, well utilised to build the bungalow there. the house itself is very spacious. stark and spartan though.

title: Tranquil
text: Lots of grounds to cover. Tour not as good as we hoped. The pet dog knew the tour blindfolded so we followed him.

title: slightly odd place
text: well, its interesting - so if you are around do visit, but dont build your day around it the original owner had special interest hence strange pieces of art, see the picture

title: Must Do !
text: Loved Bevis Bawa's gardens and house, full of art history and faded glamour. The hospitality we received was simply wonderful, tea and biscuits chatting to the current owner was a real highlight.

title: The secret garden
text: Definitely worth leaving the beach for a couple of hours to visit this hidden gem. Bevis Bawa's garden and house are stunning and incredibly well kept. One could spend hours inspecting the garden alone. The house has been left as it was when he lived there. One can't help wandering about the crazy parties which must have gone on there!

title: Tea in paradise
text: This house and garden is lovely, though the prudish might be taken aback by some of the sculptures. We were offered tea - nothing could be more perfect.

title: An amazing oasis of beauty
text: Of all the experiences in Sri Lanka this was our number one. Our party of four took 2 tuk tuks to the house of this larger than life Sri Lankan [6ft 7 inches} The house id s full of artwork and treasures and our guide worked for Bevis so new so much. The gardens are beautifully landscaped, Tea on the lawn mad the vist perfect.

title: Design
text: Very interesting garden and house, well worth a visit and not crowded.Intereting to compare eith other Bawa buildings such as The Gsllery cafe in Colombo.

title: Peaceful birdsong
text: What a beautiful place to visit its a short tuk tuk ride to these lovely gardens and house with a interesting story now left to the staff who cared for the owner until his death you can then visit a nearby temple and see the everyday life of Sri Lanka people en-route

title: Tucked away gem
text: Down some very narrow rough roads (with no signs pointing the way), this is a great way to spend an hour or so away from the beach. The house and grounds are beautiful – and an inspiration for landscaping back at home. Don’t expect formal gardens or placards identifying plants – but rather just a nice place to explore and fantasize about escaping everyday world and moving to a garden paradise in the middle of no where yourself.

title: House and garden designed by Geoffrey Bawa for his brother
text: Geoffrey Bawa was a very important architect in Sri Lanka. This house and garden developed some of his ideas on light space and shape and vistas (and his sense of humour) as well as displaying some of the art he collected or commissioned by a range of artists and sculptors

title: Not worth the effort
text: It is located way too much in the interiors . If you are in self drive with gps then I will not suggest going there. After much meandering I found a rickshaw who asked me to follow him to the gardens otherwise I would have got lost . The entry charges are thousand rupees

title: Beautiful
text: Unspoilt full of birds. A guided tour around the villa with a very interesting history. Well worth a visit

title: Lovely Garden , a must see if your close to Beruwela!
text: We really enjoyed the Bevis Bawa Garden, it is stunning and beautiful, we were amazed by ist varaiety of plants and stautes/figures. A must see see if you like nature.

title: Nice garden and house
text: Beautiful garden and house with unusual plants, especially black flower is wonderful. For a relatively short period of time and small fee we saw a delightful garden and house created by Sri Lankan landscape architect Bevis Bawa. Enjoyment and relaxation in melt of nature and human mind.

title: Don't miss it!
text: Very atmospheric and well worth a visit. The gardens are well cared for and very interesting. Watch out for the mongoose,......

title: Lovely house and gardens
text: Just a short ride in a tuk-tuk from our hotel and well worth it..a couple of hours is enough to take in the beautiful gardens and house. Lots of flowers and birds and a free cuppa at the end of the tour.

title: Disapointing
text: Disapointed with the gardens. Not enough information or even a map. House was interesting but the whole thing was not worth the entry fee.

title: Inspiring
text: Lovely place to visit and stroll through the garden but most interesting part is the house. Fascinating for people interested in architecture and design.

title: Absolutely Must Do
text: I can't believe when people below have written that they think the gardens and home have not been maintained. I strongly recommend you organize seeing this estate. We did Lunuganga too and organized a meal there but didnt organize in enough advance at Brief to dine there but I wish I did. Email on info@briefgarden.com a few days before to do so. We took a proper car / driver to this location as the reviews say it is a rural once you get off the main road. I wouldn't like the idea of rattling around on a tuktuk to get there. It is LKR 1000 (7$USD) and our tour was unguided but at the end, the man who Brief was left to spoke to us a bit about the history so I think you can get more of a proper guided tour and info if you want. The gardens and sculptures are fascinating and I would love to live in the home myself - all the interesting furniture, art work, antiques and books. The Bawa's bohemian sanctuary properties are not to missed if you are near by.

title: Left dissapointed
text: Visited here on the strength of reviews but left extremely dissapointed. After arriving by Tuk Tuk over some rough terrain which was nice to be out of the hustle of the main roads it cost 1000 rubes to enter. I thought I was in for seeing spectacular gardens but it was generally over grown and the house was a dissapointment too. I have to say in its defence I am not a tourist who is a lover of historical land marks and a couple who were in English who were there at the same time were raving about it - so not for everyone but some yes.

title: Not to be missed when in the Bentota area
text: Beautiful gardens and residence with an interesting history. The Brief Garden is a bit off the beaten track, so arrange round-trip transportation. This site is not to be missed if in the Bentota area.

title: Interesting history lesson
text: An interesting place to visit and hear the history surrounding the house and gardens . maybe not the best place when it's raining . The road is a bit on the rough side but a bit of fun .

title: Brief visit to Brief
text: Brief Gardens are a real treat for anyone that loves a bit of horticulture. Simple masculine layout to the house and gardens alike. I love the fact that the gardens are not manicured to within an inch of there lives and certain areas have a real feel of the wild. Then of course there are the various statues dotted about, that present a real sense of mischief, you will see for yourselves. We had a lovely pot of tea up at the house, but I understand that this is not always available, so we counted ourselves as lucky. A lovely place to wander and soak up the beauty for a couple of hours, maybe longer if you really take time to enjoy it all.

title: Intriguing
text: I did not know a lot about Bevis Bawa before visiting this place and probably would have appreciated it more if I had done more research. The gardens give a hint of the magical place they once were. There was a guide in the house who explained all of the features and the stories behind the artwork. Lovely, but out-of-the-way place to visit.

title: Charming curiosity!
text: The gardens and house are a fascinating insight to Bevis Bawa's life and Sri Lankan culture in general. Some of it unexpected and a delight. The grounds are immaculately kept and full of flowers and birds, whilst the house is preserved in a 'shabby' charm!

title: Delightful
text: This is a treat of a place if you love gardens. You enter through the bungalow which is a lovely place in itself with its collection of art and wonderful old photographs of Bevis Bawa and some of the famous visitors to the Brief. The garden has quite a mysterious quality to it as you wander along winding paths surrounded by lush plants and occasionally happen upon a seating area in a clearing, or a pool or statue. We visited after a rainstorm which had left the garden a vibrant green and a dripping jungle like atmosphere. The drive there takes you through some beautiful countryside too. Well worth a visit. There is an entrance fee which at the time of writing works about to about £5.

title: A beautiful secret garden.
text: A beautiful and historic garden with an aristocratic story attached to it . An extraordinary secret garden in an unexpected location . well worth a look .

title: See how the other half lived.
text: Pleasant,verdant garden. Enjoyed a one hour ramble amongst unexpected water features and overgrown paths;even saw two mongooses at close quarters big colonial house with a bit of history.

title: Worth the drive.
text: A green and ordered oasis behind an impressive hedge. The walk leads one through the tropical gardens with some interesting plantings of tropical vegetation interspersed with landscaping reminiscent of an Italian garden. The house itself is also of interest and had an unexpected treasure trove of art on the walls. Worth the drive to get there.

title: Tranquil setting
text: We took a TukTuk for a day visiting these gardens as part of our excursion. What a beautiful and tranquil place. We were able to wander around at leisure and when visiting inside the house a guide gave us an interesting insight into the history of the owner and his family. I would strongly recommend this place for gardeners and non gardeners alike. Not too expensive either.

title: Architectural place
text: Architectural place, nice to visit for relaxation and studying architecture. you will see some endemic plants too.

title: Lovely garden with nice collection of statues
text: A nice garden to stroll around in. The grounds are rather big and there is lots to see. The visit ends with a tour of the house and the art collection of Bevis Bawa. Nice and gives some insight in his life. Loved all the stautues and little ponds and features.

title: Fantastic
text: This was a highlight, what a magnificent short day trip. What was created here is just fantastic, and what a great time it must have been to live in Sri Lanka.

title: Beautiful gardens and house.
text: Make the time to come and see this beautiful garden. Easy to get to and in some ways much more beautiful than Lunaganga. A real treat.

title: Still as gorgeous as ever.
text: This really is a wonderful garden and house now owned and run by the previous gardener and his family, who used to tend to the gardens for Mr bevis and his partner. It looks simply sumptuous in the rain and still has that wonderful charm and magic about it. Well done Dan and the de Silva family for continuing to uphold Bevis's legacy.

title: Beautiful
text: Beautiful grounds to wander through followed by a tour of the house with an informative guide, but wear mosquito repellant otherwise you'll have loads of itchy bites!

title: Interesting garden with unrealized potential
text: The biggest problem with Brief Garden is the lack of directions both to get to the gardens and once their around the garden itself. Constructed in 1929 and opened to the public 40 years later, not a lot has been done to assist the visitor. Even the toilet located in the garden is a health hazard, certainly not there to be used!

title: Peace from a bygone era
text: Personal tour of the gardens and beautiful house. Entry 1000 rupees which goes towards upkeep. Take a picnic.

title: Horrible access with absolutely no signs to guide you
text: It was a nightmare to get to the garden. There are no signs and the road is almost non-existent. After a long search we reached the place to find it desolate. We returned utterly disappointed.

user_location: The Royal Town of Sutton Coldfield, United Kingdom
title: Afternoon tea in a quaint setting
text: We spent a lovely afternoon here wandering round the neat lawns. An English garden with spectacular exotic flowers. The house is beautiful and the lovely gentleman who showed us round and made our tea brought the house to life with stories of the past. Magical

title: neglected
text: hard to find. no signs of indication. charging visitors but unable to see any maintenance. very neglected. Was greeted by a very rude, unfriendly man. visitors are locked in the garden once entered. to get out must ring a bell and wait for him to open gate.Not worth seeing. Waste of money.

title: Need of maintenance
text: This garden is in serious need of maintenance. This is a smaller property compared to its bigger cousin Lunaganga, but there are weeds everywhere, the trails are unmarked and the paths slippery with mosses. The guide seemed uninterested and rude. Like Lunaganga, this place has potential to be major tourists attraction, but in serious need of care. Unlike Lungaganga, this is in private hands. The Government should take over this to promote tourism.

title: A controlled jungle garden
text: Bevis Bawa may not have had the fame and talent of his brother Geoffrey, but his garden at The Brief is a wonderful exercise of trying to keep the jungle under some control, while letting it be part of it at the same time. Mass plantings of one plant on various locations creates a calmness next to the riot of growth nearby. Good fun to see, lots of work for the maintenance workers!

title: perfect clearing in the jungle.
text: Hidden away inland it is not the easiest of places to find. But it is worth it, not a huge garden but lovely views and interesting house. Peaceful. Bevis bawa was an interesting chap.

title: Artistic treasure
text: Brief House is approximately 10 kilometres inland with no public transport so got a tuk tuk ride. The journey after turning off the main road was great, passing through small villages in the countryside as I ventured further inland. Not well signposted but the locals happy to give directions. The entrance is like coming through a secret door into a tropical paradise. The gardens are extensive with large stands of trees and tropical vegetation in a wild layout with artistic follies scattered throughout. Brevis Bawa's house appears to be as he left it, full of amazing artwork with murals on the walls and a splendid one by Donald Friend a renowned Australian artist who came for a week and stayed 5 years. Don' t miss the collection of photos giving an insight into the lifestyle of Bawa and his famous visitors. It was a privilege to chat with the current owner, who was a long term manager for Bawa. He shared so much fascinating information about artwork, history and gardens that enriched my visit. Can only imagine the grand parties!

title: Designers and architects home
text: Lovely large tranquil gardens but the house is very interesting. it belonged to the architect and designer Bevis Bawa, a homosexual who was the darling of the Hollywood crowd in the 50's. Beautifully deigned spacious rooms, he died without children and left the house and over 24 acres to his staff,The Butler, who now owns the house will show you around.

title: Well worth making a trip
text: We took a tuk tuk from our guest house in Bentota - approx. 25 mins drive each way - paid rps 1200. The drive was interesting in itself, but then the gardens and house was amazing. We were left to wander alone around the gardens then given a guided tour of the house and its' history. Bevis Bawa had the most incredible life and this is portrayed in his former home. Make sure you see the outdoor shower and the moon gate too.

title: Steeped in History
text: The present owner explained how the house and gardens came about, they form a quiet and tranquil setting. Was used as a emergency shelter for 200 tourist in 2004 after the Tsunami. Owner refused a large compensation sum from the tourist industry but donated it to the town to pay for scholarship for local students.

title: Tranquility guaranteed
text: Beautiful gardens with many lovely flowers and plants. We even got to see a group of monkeys high in the trees feeding on fruits. It is well worth a visit if you like gardens and tranquil surroundings.

title: What a delightful place
text: Worth the trip to see this amazing estate and house. The gardens and paths are charming and the house a perfect setting in the climate. Entry is 1000 Sri Lankan Rupees per person and worth it. We took a Tuk-Tuk there and that is the best way to get around.

title: Beautiful garden but not enough details for visitors
text: It's a beautifully laid out garden, though the entrance fee is steep (SLR 1000 per person). And for the price one doesn't even get a guide to walk along and point out the sights or even give some history of the garden. Visitors are left to figure things out for themselves.

title: Beautiful place
text: Beautiful and interesting place,filled with amazing works of art of the Bawa and his friends. The house itself is an architectural pearl. The gardens are inspiring. we all loved the place. Worth a visit if you stay in Bentota or Beruwela area. A half an hour with a three wheeler which in itself is a lovely experience. Only downside is the high entrance fee, in sri-lankan terms of course. 100 rup. Per person.

title: A must!
text: The garden and the house are very nice and the guide gives you a great introduction to the life of Bevis Bawa and the estate. He was perfectly speaking english and german and made the tour very interesting. We love the estate!

title: Did not want to leave Brief Garden!
text: The beautiful expanse of greenery... Garden is manicured yet so wild in places to keep the natural charm alive.. We fell in love with this romantic garden and the family who welcomed us there. A must visit for all nature gazing lovers.

title: Garden of delights
text: We really enjoyed our two hour visit, especially as we shared tea with the charming owner. He could not have been more patient and informative about the house, garden and the Bawa family. The garden in a carefully choreographed "jungle" with some beautiful (and sometimes quirky) architectural features and ornaments. The collection of photographs and paintings in the house - which is light and spacious - helped turn the clock back to its heyday. A really memorable trip, just 1000 rupees waiting tuk tuk from the coast.

title: Well worthwhile. Fantastic for birds.
text: I found the house and garden moderately interesting, but the real "wow" was the range of birds that could be seen (and photographed). This is a "must" for bird enthusiasts: allow a half day and bring your binoculars and long lens! One of the best locations for birds that I visited during my entire tour.

title: first visit to brief garden
text: I had read about these gardens and had a half day to spare so went along. The garden is beautiful. The flowers and exotic plants were fascinating. I heard a variety of birds and enjoyed searching for sight of them. I must say however. The house gave me the creeps and I couldn't applaud the statues and paintings. I would not have wanted my son to go there as a child or young man shall we say. Definitely worth a visit though.

title: hmm
text: might be an interesting walk around the gardens if you have company and fancy a change of scene .. interesting take on colonisation and creating a space where you can live as you please .. surreally, there is a Picasso in the somewhat indiscriminate art collection

title: Such a Green & Peaceful Place
text: An unexpected garden. Full of quirky ideas. So lush and green. The wife of the owner is a lovely lady and knows so much about the history of the house and the family that formerly owned it. The photos on the walls show many film stars from bygone times. Sit and look at the view from the terrace. It is hard to leave it. In the garden are colourful birds and monkeys. At every twist and turn in the garden there is something new to look at. Don't miss this garden!

title: shangrila
text: this was the best thing we did on our visit, the house and gardens are such a pleasant surprise and very interesting too, not very big so you can do it all in an hour but you wouldnt want to eave the cool and beautiful house once youre there

title: Walk through Brief Garden
text: Was a lovely experience. Every turn, every bend in the path was interesting - so many many plants. Very beautifully laid out garden. You can spend ages in this place without getting tired - if you are a nature lover. Sitting down to have some tea and biscuits in the Bawa home was also a treat. If they do up this house and let out the rooms, then this is a must stay place.

title: Brief Gardens
text: What a fantastic look into the past. The gardens were laid out with great foresight and vision. Though the house was modest, one can only imagine heady lifestyle enjoyed by the Bawa clan. Well worth a visit

title: Divine Decadence
text: If you are open minded, like something truly out of the ordinary and off the beaten tourist track, then this is definitely for you. Take a tuk tuk for a magic ride into the past and visit the Brief Garden to discover how it was to live a decidedly debauched lifestyle in the colonial days leading up to Ceylon's independance. In the middle of a forest you come upon stunning landscaped gardens supporting a myriad of trees,plants,flowers and wildlife to soak in. You then arrive at the sparse but beautiful house, full of impressive paintings and photographs of a bygone age. To cap it all there is some pretty dubious but nevertheless eye catching sculptures to be studied! The 1000 rupee entrance fee is quite high for Sri lanka but certainly, from our point of view, worth every rupee. Before going it is worth looking up the history of Bevis & Geoffrey Bawa to give you some idea of what there is in store for you. A wonderful experience.

title: Interesitng but strange
text: Small gardens with weird history and plenty of artwork. Staff were lovely. p.s WEAR LOTS OF BITE CREAM

title: Umm....
text: Beautiful gardens but research the owner and his past first!? The atmosphere and artwork in the house were strange.

title: Likely not worth your trouble
text: Make no mistake, Brief Garden is off the beaten path. You will want to investigate whether it is worth the trouble to get there. Garden aficionados might want to visit, but don't take a rickshaw. Too, the pedophilia element surrounding Bevis Bawa adds another dimension to the question of visiting. The Rs 1000 admission fee is a bit over priced.

title: Hidden treasure
text: Wasn't expecting such magical gardens hidden away. Well worth visiting to take in the gardens and architecture, even if you're not a buff.

title: Brief Garden
text: Interesting way to spend a couple of hours wandering around the lovely grounds and viewing the house.

title: Lovely
text: Excellent and lovely garden, great welcome from Dooland and his wife. Well manicured garden in a peaceful location! Must see if you are around Beruwala area.

title: Worth a visit for lovers of good and timeless design.
text: Bevis Bawa had a great eye for design as did his boyfriend Donald. The garden and house make an interesting tour with lots of take home ideas. Yes the man was gay and young Sri Lankan males were involved but to downgrade this place because of the sexual orientation of the owner somewhat misses the point. The whole area reflects his sensitivity, sensuality and imagination and unlike his brother's property, Lunaganga, you can see inside the house as well. You may not admire the man but you must admire his talent.

title: Nice garden, shameful history
text: OK, so the house and gardens are presentable. The moon gate is interesting, but that's where it stops. Make no mistake, this place reeks of paedophilia. Everything about it, from the "special" places and hidey-holes in the gardens where young boys where taken, to the phallic statues and sad photographic portraits of young boys. Bawa, Donald Friend and their cronies should be remembered for what they were.

title: A must for Bawa fans
text: Wonderful garden and house is full of interesting art work. Fascinating contrast to Lunagunga. A must for Bawa fans.

title: pretty garden and very comfortable experience
text: A bit of a hike going there and our driver was not overly keen since it was a small dirt road but we loved wandering around the garden snapping away at the different vistas and 'rooms', mosquitoes are definitely loving seeing tourists there but manageable. As for the house, the 'keeper' was not overly enthusiastic in his commentary but we enjoyed it anyway... Mr Bawa's was obviously was a bit of an eccentric who loved to be surrounded by beautiful things and people but if the sight of a statue of a male naked & a few lascivious pictures are too much for you...don't bother (then don't bother with many other parts of the world, italy, greece, india... and BTW don't bother with art all together !)

title: Pretty gardens, but a very uncomfortable experience overall
text: The garden was beautiful and we had a very pleasant stroll through the jungle like growth. The tour of the house spoiled the experience for us, however, as the hallway exiting the house showcased paintings and photographs that implied that Bawa's boy servants were victims of pedophilia. These acts should never be condoned, let alone celebrated, and we remain shocked that this hasn't come up in previous reviews or guidebook write-ups about the place. While the gardens were quite pretty, we struggle to recommend visiting Brief Gardens for these reasons and the chilling atmosphere that burdens many areas of the property.

title: Below our expectations
text: We chose this place based on Tripadvisor number 1 rating, when we arrived we had to ask to know our way there. entrance fee is 1000 LRS the attraction is composed of Bevis Bawa's ( a Srilankan Artist) garden which he desined himself and his home, he died in 1993 hi house has some of his paintings and a lot of other artists contributions if you are an artist then this is a place for you. if you aren't into art then I think you will get a bit bored like we did.

title: Shows what great planning can do with little
text: This was a very relaxing spot. It shows you dont need fancy flowers or exotic ornaments. The placement of trees and the care taken with the garden planning shows what a talented person Bevis was

title: A Garden for Connoisseurs - a Work of Art
text: Brief Gardens is a masterpiece of landscaping. I could have spent all day here, observing the play of light and shadow in the changing daylight. It is also a wonderful opportunity for photography. A single visit will hardly do it justice. This was my second visit and I shall certainly return in another season.

title: A brief visit!
text: We were taken by tuk tuk from our hotel by a driver who obviously knew his way, but I could easily see why it might be difficult to find - as other reviewers have stated. Having read previous reviews, I doused myself in deet before arriving! However, within minutes of getting there, I had been bitten numerous times. I reapplied copious amounts of repellent whilst there, which appeared to stop further bites. I liked the serenity of the garden, but felt I was hurrying through, to ensure I didn't get bitten again. There wasn't much in bloom, but I managed a few interesting photos. The house was spartan, but had a rather nice, colonial feel about it. Normally, apparently, there is a gentle breeze wafting through, but on the day we were there it was stifling. I enjoyed the photo collection and in particular, the lovely, natural photo of Vivien Leigh and Laurence Olivier. The history of some of the artefacts in the house was explained, however, nothing was mentioned of the garden. We were not offered any refreshments and if I'm honest, I wasn't disappointed to leave.

title: Interesting garden
text: Very cool and almost like an English garden - we particularly liked the cascade run of water down the lawn from the top by the house. Tea and lemon puff biscuits were provided after the tour of the garden - a nice touch. Interesting to hear the history of the house and gardens and see the old photos of past visitors.

title: Brief Garden
text: Interesting but slightly disappointing... We expected it to be more colourful from what we'd read about it.

title: A place full of atmosphere
text: This was a great visit! Our driver took us there early in the day. It is not very easy to find, it is a hidden gem in the middle of lash trees and plantations. The tour guide is great! We got to know that the place is full of charm and stories to share. The paintings on the wall are really touching. The one of Bevis Bawa in his very late days with the boy with his arm around him is breath-taking, and leaves you with so much to think about. So much charm and so many stories in the house. The building itself is not a palace, but the garden is something to tell about. We set in the garden at the end of the tour, and enjoyed a cup of tea, and let the whole place sink in with us. It is an experience not to be missed! A very moving experience...

title: Normal Garden.

title: Artistic history
text: It's wonderful to see the work of Sri Lankan artists in situ...to see where they lived and retreated, their artistic legacy and the lovely gardens. If you are interested in the artists of the mid 20th century, including Donald Friend, this is a delightful place. But a warning...the road is windy and bumpy and long. Phone to see if it is open before you arrive.

title: Quaint slightly eccentric place but worth a visit
text: Water moniter lizards and range of plants/trees/nice landscape. A nice place to spend a couple of hours.

title: Excellent
