title: Brief Garden
text: Amazing garden and house in the middle of the jungle with wonderful views lovely sculptures and lots of interesting little nooks and crannies to explore , great place to spend a morning.Interesting library and [hotographs in the house

title: Persistence rewarded, multifold
text: Finding Brief is not easy, as testified by other reviewers, but every uncertain turn on the ever narrowing roads is rewarded from the moment you walk through the arched gate. The 1000 rupee entrance fee (which helps to maintain the gardens to the traditional standard established under Bevis Bawa) is a tourist bargain. We were free to roam at our leisure and spent nearly 3 hours exploring the gardens and house. The tea spontaneously provided was an unexpected and lovely bonus, as was the tour of the house and historic features. As Australians, we were especially interested in the sculptures and art work of Donald Friend who lived at Brief for several years. His mural of Sri Lankan life, painted on the wall of the main room, was fascinating. The wonderful hospitality of the current owners, the de Silva family, who have enjoyed a long connection to Brief dating back to the Bawa era, the extraordinary beauty and layoutvof the gardens and the tranquility of the setting made Brief the most memorable experience of our Sri Lankan trip. Better signposting and promotion would encourage more visitors I am sure.

title: BRIEF rather too brief
text: As an antidote to the hedonistic beaches of southern Sri Lanka, we decided to go inland and explore the attractions that lay within. A visit to the Brief Garden associated with Bevis Bawa (1909-1992) older brother of the more famous Geoffrey Bawa, the renowned architecht,seemed to be just what the doctor ordered. The road trip to the location once one left the main Galle Road at Bentota and traversing narrow rural roads and ups and downs was itself a challenge as there was virtually no signposting. When we finally reached it, the imposing entrance to Brief ( named after the association with lawyers holding briefs)with its ivy covered walls and cement sculptures standing guard over the iron gate was startling.Another shock was the steep entrance fees - Rs 1000SLK per head - which was collected at the door after which we were sheperded into the gardens to find our way about while an earlier Sunday meeting of a local association concluded its tea party. The gardens are the real star of the show, and despite the size having been reduced to just five acres, one could visualise the arboreal grandeur that must have existed in its full majesty. A botanist-guide who knew the trees and the manner in which they came to be would have been appreciated. We finally were admitted to the main house - just about a hour to closing time - and got a rather canned conducted tour where the guide repeated himself several times. The architecture and the imprint of Barbara Sansoni and Donald Friend,the Australian artist during his five-year stay there in the 1950s are absorbing to explore,The sculptures , paintings, courtyards, open air showers and fountains all made their own quiet statements. One could have lingered more but closing hour beckoned and a cuppatea - which sadly never came - would have befitted the admission ticket and the host.

title: Worth a visit
text: Being an architect loved visiting the house and the gardens. Well designed.Worth a visiting to see both the residence and the landscape.A unique view of the house of an architect himself.

title: Unexpected paradise
text: One does not expect to see anything like this in a Sri Lankian village. It's stunning from the entrance gate till the last step, a magical mix of tropical nature, Ancient Greece, South Asia, a song to life, beauty, love and loss.. And the park's manager deserves special mention for his intelligent tour through the park and museum with respect and devotion to the beautiful place and its great creator.

title: Brief
text: This place "Brief" was undoubtedly good but i wish there were more indicators on the road to find it. We had to struggle to get to place. Once we reached with lot of struggle, it was difficult to find the access. One of the care takers took us around. I wish this part was also better organised since the took LKR 1000 per person including the child. Since I am an architect, i would have loved to have more relevant and genuine information about the work than personal information about Bawas. They can have a more organised /aunthentic audio tour. Its a one time expenditure - audio/head phone tours. That will do justice to the purpose of visiting the place. Wish somebody connected to "Brief" notes the suggestions. Thanks

title: Wonderful visit
text: The Brief Garden was the house of the writer/artist Bewis Bawa,brother of the architect Geoffrey Bawa,a visit is a full immersion into a silent,beautiful paradise, lovely trees,flowers,well kept lawns,walled gardens.The house is full of old fashoned,colonial charme,nice drawings,statues by Geoffrey and a beautiful murale by Donald Friend,an Australian artist,nice collection of old photographs as well.The manager is gentle and invites you for tea when you visit the house. They offer also accomodation which must be a wonderful experience!

title: A Dream Garden
text: Brief Garden is beautiful - if you are staying in or near Bentota you should try and make a visit. Created by Bevis Bawa, the celebrated landscape artist - it is like entering paradise with beautiful lawns, walled gardens and a pond. There is also an intresting house to visit with an art gallery and photographs of celebrities. Make sure you put on lots of insect repellant otherwise you may get bitten as you walk round the garden. The staff are very welcoming.

title: all about good taste
text: One of the Bewis brothers has created this house and garden. Both house and garden are an example of a perfect taste, mix of colonial and modern architecture, well kept and deserted. In the garden you walk alone buth the house visit is guided. Entrance is 1000 Rupees. It's impossible to find the place without a local driver. And i's a pity that they have no merch like postcards, books etc. I'd love to buy something in this style.

title: jeffrey bawas garden
text: took a tuk tuk ride here and walked around for two hours in beautiful well kept gardens,really is a solitary place we were the only visitors at that time,wonderful!!!!

title: Worth a trip
text: The gardens are not large, but they are interesting.

title: Fantastic
text: All great!!!!!! Enjoyed very much The gardens are spectacular & the house is amazing

title: beautiful gardens and scenery
text: Had a nice afternoon here. The tuk tuk ride to the gardens is beautiful in itself. The gardens are obviously well cared for and really relaxing. Little guided tour at the end, of the house. There seemed to be a little cafe for tea outside but i didnt bother with this. All in all a nice place to pass an hour or two.

title: If you stay at Lunuganga you will be interested in seeing GHeoffrey Bawa's older brother's garden a taxi ride away.
text: It is another of the great gardens of Sri Lanka.

title: A little more greenery outside of the resort
text: I decided to take a little excursion on my own, and the Brief Gardens was recommended by the hotel. So off I went with a personal driver. Once at the Gardens you will get a personal escort to take you around. I didn't know much about the garden itself ... apparently it was designed by a famous Sri Lankan architect. The grounds were extensive and I even managed to see a little wildlife in the form of a monitor lizard! Apparently if you go in the morning opportunities to see birds and other wildlife would be a better bet. I enjoyed the few hours excursion.

title: Amazing nature all around
text: It is a trip into the wild, with lovely views in every corner. Worth a visit for the price, and the way from bentota to the brief garden by tuk tuk is simply great!

title: Fabulous study on living space, abc character.
text: Visited this preserved house and garden today, recommended by my tour guide. The walk around the garden leading to the house, was amazing. The layout and design of the portion of the house open to the public was most interesting, achieving comfort, many places to rest and enjoy the SriLamkan weather, and muse, yes of windows and busy areas to cool and filll with light. Recommended, historic, nice old photos.

title: What a wonderful tropical garden!
text: Lush, wonderful tropical garden designed by Bevis Bawa. Unfortunally, he got under marvelous shadow of his older brother Geoffrey Bawa. Love the artworks, some furniture designs and the weird statues in his garden. It works a long way to go from Negombo. Must see if you are around Bentota and Galle.

title: Tropical Garden
text: The road up to Brief gardens is narrow and winding so don't go in a minivan. It was definately a hideaway for old Bevis and his young men, and it's a fab spot. There are lots of secret seating areas and amazing views. Watch out for the leeches, they'll get you if you wear open-toed sandals, but are easy enough to get rid of (google!)

title: Not the must
text: First of all it's just place where original person lived. He had got interesting garden and house. Now it seams that not too much is invested to maintaine the garden. At the same time entrance fee is pretty expensive. It's also not so easy to get here. For our children it was boring and to hot to walk through the garden

title: Relaxing in a beautiful tropical garden
text: The garden is a lush greenery and as specialty features some fine statues honoring the male genital (one male face in a phalluslike stele, one statue of a boy enjoying to caress his love organ and one stone Phallus with pubes of tiny green plantleaves growing on it, very crative). It is wonderful sensible art, no offense.

title: Lovely find
text: Whilst not the main event (apparently that is Lungana) this is a lovely find (although it is very hard to find) and a lovely example of tropical living in a bygone era. I arrived late in the day, had I planned better I'd have seen both and booked the lunch, but Brief (and you learn why it's called that), brief as it was, was a delight.

title: a lovely estate
text: although not at the same level of the Luluganga estate this is quite a find, lovely details and momentos from the friends and visitors of the Bawa brothers

title: Overhyped Place
text: We went to visit the place on the basis of earlier reviews. The Gardens were nice but the entry cost is prohibitive and definately not worth the effort.

title: Stunning gardens
text: Beautiful gardens, great day spent there and a very interesting guide who told us all about the house and about Bevis Bawa (including some... interesting details!)

title: Hard to find but worth the effort
text: Having visited his brother's property of Lunuganga we were curious to see Bevis Bawa's home and garden. Once again there is a bell to ring, and an entrance fee of 1000 Rupees to pay. We were left to tour the grounds on our own, which was a bit daunting but since it is a relatively small area we did not get lost. It is not particularly well kept but still charming and relaxing. We had a guided tour of the house, which we found very interesting and are pleased we made the effort.

title: Tranquil Gardens
text: Worth the 3000 Rupee taxi fair from our hotel to visit these gardens in Bentota .The gardens were laid out with great foresight and vision. The house was modest but brought to life by the man who guided us round. Bevis Bawa was certainly and interesting man. 1000 Rupee entrance fee.

title: Interesting gardens and house
text: Charming gardens, with a variety of plants, and many interesting birds to watch. House also worth a visit, with helpful guide.

title: Unmissable and not just for the planting
text: We knew nothing about Bevis Bawa, although knew about his brother Geoffrey the architect. His garden reflects his life and is fantastic - lots of paths leading to secluded areas where you'll find odd and interesting sculptures (some more interesting than others!). The house is preserved and filled with his possessions. His story is fascinating and Brief Garden gives a glimpse into his hedonistic and self indulgent life. The only problem is finding the place and you are best with a tuk tuk as they know where they're going. Ring the bell and you might even get the current owner to give you the tour.

title: Beautiful!
text: It's not easy to find Brief Garden as the signs have disappeared recently so suggest that you take a tuk-tuk. It was the home of the artist Bevis Bawa, the very well connected younger brother of Geoffrey Bawa who was a renowned architect. The extensive gardens are truly wonderful and beautifully kept. It's a real tropical paradise with so much to see - all types of trees, shrubs, flowers, water features, pathways, statues, pots etc - and a real pleasure to amble around. Included in the entrance fee is a guided tour of the house, which is very interesting. It is rumoured locally that Bevis Bawa was a well endowed gentleman and there are a number of images and sculptures possibly based on him, of naked men with large attributes, which may make some visitors blush!

title: Serenity
text: This is a beautiful and serene place to visit. Set amid a coconut plantation, Brief Garden is lush and aesthetically pleasing. The caretaker is knowledgeable and offers insights into the history of the garden and house. The gardens are divided into outdoor rooms revealing Bawa's sense of style and sense of humor.We found the place with difficulty but felt the trek was worth it.

title: Beautiful Garden
text: It was clean and always well kept, pool was clear and lovely and the whole thing was private and safe

title: A hidden Gem in the Jungle
text: Brief Gardens are a 'must see' for anybody visiting the Beruwela - Aluthgama - Bentota area. Although somewhat overgrown now, the gardens still show traces of their original grandeur, and the bird life is wonderful. The bungalow and it's associated art works are splendid, and give some impression of the colonial lifestyle in Sri Lanka fourty or more years ago. Overall, don't miss it!

title: Well worth a look
text: The garden is relatively small, but divided into different 'rooms' by screens of shrubbery and trees, as well as by stone steps and a series of different levels. There is a barbecue area, several ponds, a cascade (which was dry during our visit) and shady benches to sit on and chill out. The owner of the house welcomed us personally and gave us tea and biscuits in the courtyard, followed by a tour of the house, with its amazing collection of art (particularly gay art) and comic pieces, as well as its fascinating history. It's a quirky, unique attraction and you are either going to love it or hate it. It's also a long way from the main road, and the only practical way to get there is by tuc-tuc or motorbike. I think you'll find it worth the effort though. I suggest you take a picnic and a good book and make a laid back day of it.

title: A beautiful legacy!
text: I had a few hours to kill in Bentota, waiting for a train back to Colombo, after a trip around the South coast. A Tuk Tuk driver helped me at the station with my enquiry, and then tried to persuade me to visit the gardens. By this time in my trip I was tired, and to say the least, rather jaded in my dealings with Tuk Tuk drivers. Because of his appearance and manner (very smart and polite) I decided to go. I had three hours to wait for the train and this would be an unexpected adventure. Sugath was a very good driver, and a Karate Master (0776070246) He turned out to be a gem, just like the garden! It is a wonderful, beautiful place! I can't wait to go back. The entrance fee of R1000 is a very reasonable price to pay, to walk in such beauty and tranquility. I loved the house and the stories that were told about Mr. Bawa. What a remarkable man he must have been. There is some stunning artwork in the house, and controversial statues in the garden, which Sugath kept apologising for! Not necessary, but very sweet. :) Go. If you like gardens you will love it!

title: Nothing special
text: We lived not far away from the garden, therefore decided to visit it. The garden itself didn't meet our expectations. There were almost no flowers in there, only trees and bushes. It took us 15 min to walk in the garden, it was not much to see. It was interesting to see the house, even though the guide didn't give us a lot of information. Only a few phrases about Bawa and his life. I wouldn't bother to go there if you need to drive far and the entrance fee is expensive as well.

title: Well worth a visit
text: We had been here a few years ago and thoroughly enjoyed the experience, so, since we were staying in the Bentota area, we used the opportunity for a return visit. It only takes 20 minutes or so by tuk-tuk from Aluthgama. The entrance fee of 1000 rupees might seem steep, but if you are interested in gardens you will consider it money well spent. You can walk around the grounds at your leisure and there is plenty to see, from interesting trees and plantings to colourful birds and even monkeys. When you are ready, simply walk up to the house where the guide will show you around and explain the history of the place and the background to the various works of art on view. When we went, we had the place to ourselves for most of our time there. It is truly a haven of tranquility, with beautiful views of the surrounding countryside. The return tuk-tuk ride from Aluthgama (or thereabouts) should not cost you more than 1000 rupees (including the driver's waiting time).

title: Hidden jem
text: Amazing discovery seemingly out the back of nowhere. Donald Friend's life was fascinating and finding this house in Bentota was a really special experience.

title: beautiful garden with river
text: this brief garden situated at bentota. very closed to the bentota town .from main road only three kilometers far..in side the garden you can watch very demand and rare flowers.valuable and beautiful scence too.so when you sri lanka you should visit this brief garden very nice journey.

title: peaceful
text: Amazing gardens, so peaceful. We had a slow walk around and enjoyed tea in the garden too. Cover yourself in bug spray though- the mosquitoes are everywhere.

title: Don't miss this magnificent place!
text: The grounds and home are a true delight. It is not easy to get there independently by walking or bus, so hire a tuktuk driver, who will wait for you while you are inside. Cost should be somewhere around 1,000 LKR for a return trip to Bentota.

title: Erotic garden
text: Beautiful & interesting garden. Around every corner is a surprise. Bevis obviously enjoyed himself. Good that you can wander the gardens at your own pace. We appreciated that we were able to take our driver free of charge on the tour with us. He had never been before & he was not allowed to look at the gardens or buildings at Lunuganga (Geoffrey Bawa's property). Interesting to see Donald Friend's input in some of the garden design & also his works in the house.

title: Wort to visit
text: it was a nice garden we were see in bentota area. They have interesting house inside the garden. One of guy he explained us architecture value of that home. It has created by bawa.

title: Chilled with a teaspoon of History
text: If you are feeling a bit cynical about the turtle sanctuaries, check this place out, Bevis Bawa was an interesting chap. There is a rather melancholy gentleman (he cared for the dying Bawa) who might see you after you have wandered around the gardens and offer you a very nice cup of tea and biscuits, who will show you the house and tells some interesting stories..

title: worth the effort to go
text: Wonderful private gardens - you'd struggle to find on your own. Let in by one of the staff you are free to wander at leisure the gardens with all the nature all around - before being given a guided tour of the house along with the history that went with it. £5.00 Entry and around £4 return from Bentota in a tuk tuk - it was excellent value for money.

title: worth a trip
text: beautiful gardens and an interesting tour of the house offering interesting insights into the life of the Bawa brothers.

title: A paradise garden
text: Well worth an hour or so to stroll around the stunning gardens. There are wonderful views out across the surrounding area - lush green hills with a huge variety of plants and trees. The house is the centre piece of the gardens and there was a very knowledgable guide who showed us around and pointed out all the different paintings and sculptures. We paid just under 500rs to get here in a Tuk Tuk from Bentota.

title: Exlent and butiful garden...
text: Very great place to visit and must to see the bungalow Mr: Bave. Me and my friend are very happy to see it. We were with tuk-tuk was great travel for a day.

title: Serene
