It's excellent for strolling and away from crowds. Chinese garden is peaceful and fern garden enchanting. If you get as far as Nuwara Eliya, this is a "must see and enjoy"

title: Absolutely worth to visit!
text: This garden was actually a big surprise. It is much bigger than Victoria Park in Nuwara Eliya and as plentiful of different species. There are many trees from all over the planet. Sometimes you run into monkeys. A pitty is that visitors feed them with chips and other food. Hopefully the management will end such things soon.

title: Visit during flowering season (April)
text: It's a nice garden and reputed as one of the 'must visit' places in Nuwara Eliya. However, the gardens which used to flourish with flowers during all seasons is more of a rain forest nowadays. December visits can get crowed and the entry fee of 200 Rs is an unwelcome addition.

title: Peaceful gardens
text: Ask to book the golf cart if raining or difficulty walking long periods. The cart drivers are very knowledgable so worth the commentary.

title: Large botanical garden
text: this large garden supposedly the ashok vatika described in the Ramayana, is a large botanical garden. Good for stroll. has large rose garden and fern garden.

title: Secluded site, with a pleasant walk up through the forest
text: We enjoyed our visit here, even in the rain! You are free to walk up and around the forest site at your leisure. We had a guide book with a reasonable amount of information about the site, without this we would have been lost as there are no information boards about what you are looking at and a pretty basic map at the entry lodge. The car park and visitor facilities are rudimentary, but functional. Worth a visit if you want to see an untouched, ancient site.

title: Lovely way to spend an hour or two
text: We enjoyed this place so much more than polonnaruwa - so much more relaxed, calm and much less busy. With it being in a forest, it is nice and shady too so much more comfortable walking around. Highly recommend exploring this place!

title: Off the beaten track but worth the detour
text: We drove for some twenty minutes on what could have been the quietest road in Sri Lanka and the road itself became more and more narrow. We had not seen another vehicle in ages and I was at the point of wondering "where the hell are we?" when the road jungle opened up and suddenly we were in a carpark with several other cars and about eight big buses. Hello, Ritigala. The site is a located in a beautiful piece of jungle, with ruined sites (foundations of ancient buildings) connected by roughly-hewn stairs. It's a lovely walk, most uphill. There is the most spectacular tree almost at the very top, don't miss it. You walk back down the same stairs to return to the carpark. Wear good walking shoes and take water.

title: Old Buddhist Monastry
text: We visited Ritigala in the afternoon. We were able to purchase the tickets, but we felt that we were tired and so decided to spend some time at the entrance and go back. Whilst we were driving back, we saw a huge elephant standing in our way. We stopped the car and waited as we had no other options except reversing back, but reversing all the way would have been extremely difficult as the road was not a smooth/straight one. But to our surprise, the elephant took its trunk and brought it up and down twice (as though it was blessing us!!) and then went back into the jungle again. We waited for a bit longer to make sure that the elephant had gone inside the jungle and then drove back. This was one of the exciting moments of our trip in SriLanka.

title: A great hike ...
text: Visited Ritigala today and was very impressed. It is the remains of an old forest monastry. They are no Buddha statues, merely remnants of pillars and basement but well worth a visit. It is a pretty steep hike with most of the pathway laid with stone. There are however areas unlaid. Strongly suggest wearing sensible walking shoes and not flipflops like me. Also be mindful that as you under the forest canopy it gets extremely hot and humid.

title: Enjoyable forest walk & learning about Buddhist monastery
text: Our family of five had a tour of Ritigala. This was not as exhausting as Sigiriya. A pleasant, easy walk with informative guide. The children enjoyed learning about the legend of Ritigala and the guardian spirits of the mountain.

title: Beautiful silence
text: Off the beaten track but worth a visit. Wonderful local guide who was a wealth of information. Great viewing point from the library.

title: Fascinating place with a guide
text: A little off the normal tourist track, and not that easy to get to. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit here, it wouldn't have been quite as good without the excellent guide we had. He was very enthusiastic and told us all about the monks and how they lived. I would recommend walking shoes, as at the beginning the path is uneven. It's a lovely cool and quiet spot away from the main attractions. It used to be free, but now has a small charge - much less than the other government owned attractions.

title: Cool and itrresting walk. Top notch!
text: Very easy walk. Cool as its in the rainforest. Tuk tuk is easy to get to from Habarana. Dont need guide. Cost us 310 rupees to get in and took photo of map. Was getting around for about 2 hours. Not too many tourists.

title: Great Cooler Place
text: We went there in the afternoon as per hotel staff recommendation. It was a hot day but when we arrived climate changed massively, very cooler like a rain forest. Huge trees and lots of greenery. Nice walk up to the rock/mountain through ancient Buddhist monastery. Lots of old trees and some of them are very rare. Little water falls and beautiful nature, kids enjoyed a lot. The old ruins were great and surprised by the work, hospital, library and bridges. We have been warned by locals to take care of snakes and spiders. If you are lucky you can buy Wood-apple on the way.

title: Well worth a visit
text: Always looking for a slightly different experience to the main touristy things and this one is perfect. Very interesting, picturesque and quiet. We only passed one other tourist. It seems mainly Sri Lankans frequent this place, possibly for spiritual reasons. If you are staying in the area it does not take long to get there and expect to spend no more than 90 minutes. Basic facilities but you really dont need much else - it speaks for itself. Minimal entrance fee.

title: Little gem of the area
text: During my stay in this area, my driver told us he hadn’t taken any one to Ritigala in 5 years (!) I wasn’t sure what to expect however I found the place devoid of tourists (which was great). The ruins are spread over a large area that continues via a path up into the forest. Make sure you wear appropriate hiking footwear. It’s really quiet unlike the other places and I thoroughly enjoyed it and would recommend it to any one who enjoys exploring tomb raider type ruins.

title: Very Peaceful
text: Our driver suggested visiting this place and we are so pleased he did. It has been recently restored and is not a major attraction at the moment so go soon as it will get much busier when word gets around! Ruins of an ancient monastery set in the hillside. Lots of climbing initially over rocks until you get to restored pathways so not for the elderly/unfit. The entry fee is very cheap compared to most other attractions in Sri Lanka - expect this is because it is not quite finished and facilities are very basic at the entrance. No food or drinks and really basic toilet. BUT well worth going!

title: Amazing
text: Off the beaten track and can be overlooked by tourists but well worth going Bush to see this gem. It just keeps going and going and artifacts remain sprinkled around the site so you can see the functionality of each space. Do yourself a favour and hire a local guide. Not only will they explain to you, they will also show you so much more than you would find on your own. Especially the toilet system!!!

title: Not many tourists at this place yet!
text: You need to know where to go to find this place. You are walking through the “jungle” stepping up to the monastery ruins. It is different to usual temples in Sri Lanka.

title: A mysterious, tranquil must see site in the forest
text: Our family visited this site after a recommendation by our driver and it proved to be one of the highlights of our month long trip around Sri Lanka. We arrived at the site around 330pm and despite being one of the hottest Aprils on record, the forest provides natural shade, so you can always head to Sigiriya early in the morning as we did and then Ritigala in the afternoon once you've had lunch and a rest. You are provided a plan of the site when you buy your tickets, but a guide is recommended as several paths are quite hidden and there's a point at which you are forbidden to stumble into without prior permission and protection. The higher forest contains leopards, bears and elephants are never far away. That said we were still treated to plenty of wildlife around the ruins with the monkeys being our kids favourite. We heard this site is like your own personal Indiana Jones adventure and we could see why as we had the forest all to ourselves away from the tourists. There is a tranquility about Ritigala, which we simply didn't experience anywhere else in Sri Lanka as the mysterious ruins emerge in hidden pockets around the forest. A fantastic experience, we hope to one day revisit.

title: worth visiting
text: very close to where we stayed and hotel arranged our visit,. a lot of climbing till the top but it was very comfortable climb and worth visiting,.

title: Peaceful journey
text: We visited this place in early afternoon. This mountain range consists of four peaks of which the main one is called Ritigala Kanda. Monks used to pray at various levels based on the degree of meditation they carried out. There are four courtyards. It's a good walk of 1 1/2 hrs and people must wear decent walking shoes. Be prepared for occasional shower.

title: Peaceful
text: We visited here after walking all day in Anuradhapura which was probably a mistake as there is quite a climb. We arrived an hour before closing and were amazed to see how many people were still there, having heard it's off the tourist trail. However, after 10 minutes the school parties had cleared and we had the forest much to ourselves. Previous reviews basically say it all, however, on reaching the top ruin keep walking about 50 metres an there is the most beautiful tree. Wish we had longer to explore the woods.

title: Nice place to hike a little in the forest
text: It is a little hard to get there because the road is not good, but is is worth it. Its a very peaceful forrest with a not too lang path through it. You don't see much animals there except monkeys, but some ruins and a nice forrest. The entry was 400 rupees, but we read about staff tryibg to trick you, so be careful.

title: A beautiful walk in serene environment
text: This wander through the ruins of Ritigala Monastery was a real highlight . We went quite early in the day with no one else about and this added to the serene atmosphere. Our guide was able to give us information on the various sites we came across and we really appreciated both the historical nature of the place along with its natural beauty.

title: A leisurely walk
text: Pleasant walk through the forest, very quiet and sadly we did not see any orchids and heard very few birds that the tour operator had promised! The history of the monastery was interesting although we were allowed to see the monks in their current environment

title: Little visited ancient site -- why is no one here
text: After visiting the crowded Lion Rock the next day we came to this site - 5 visiting cars vs 500 - why? this is a magnificent well restored very historical ruin on a massive scale out in the jungle. I think one reason it's not visited is that too many people want to "Do" S-L in 2 weeks and therefore haven't got time to visit the lesser know sites. But if you have got time you should visit. Lion rock wont take you all day, and you can come here in the afternoon rather than visiting the Tourist Trap shops

title: Stroll through the magnificent ancient ruins like Indiana Jones.
text: For less than 2000/= we rented a scooter at Habarana and followed the directions to Ritigala (bascilly the A11). Right at the 14km mark, you have to turn right. It's a scenic ride along sunlit meadows of lush rice fields and through dark patches of jungle where the road is lined with giant trees. We strolled through the magnificent ancient ruins, climbed the roughly-hewn stairs just to discover a small waterfall. We really enjoyed the spectacular feeling of a sunken city secluded in the jungle. Don't miss the old library, there is a stunning view across the jungle. We sat down and listened to the sounds of the monkeys and elephants while the sun slowly went down and the sky turned into an flaming orange. Magical. It's a lovely, easy 1,5 hours uphill walk. Ditch the flip-flops in favor of comfortable shoes, pack a bottle of water and jump right into this adventure. The fee is 2$. For 10$ you can hire a guide at the entrance. Beware of the monkeys, they might look cute - but they will steal your food!

title: Good option; good guide
text: We spent a very interesting half day hiking up the mountain through the monastery ruins. The hike was great and getting history of the monestaries gave us better insight inot other aspects of what we were seeing in the Cultural Triangle. We used a guide, Manjoo provided by Sri Lanka in Style tours, who was excellent and also offers tours of neighboring ruins by bicycle. We highly recommend him.

title: Charming place
text: As we drove towards Ritigala we were flagged down by a man wanting to be our guide he offered a good price, 1200rs, so we agreed and were very pleased with him. He spoke good English, the children liked him, and we walked us round at a comfortable place and was happy to allow us to linger. Heaps of history here that had been hidden by the jungle. Lovely to see and imagine what it would have been like as a monastery. We had a really good visit and think it was well worth coming.

title: Lovely little archaeological site/hike
text: Nice little hike in the jungle, with monkeys overhead, looking at archaeological ruins. The walk is not tough, and the path is well maintained. Definitely look for the side path that takes you to the ruined library, which has excellent views. You don't need a guide, as the path is clearly defined, however there are no information boards to tell you what the ruins are, although the ticket office has a guide book I think- our tuk tuk driver kindly leant us one, so we knew what we were looking at. The entrance price is currently LKR 300, and we got a tuk tuk to/from Habarana with waiting time for LKR1800.

title: Ancient Buddhist monastery
text: No need for guide. Many local people ask you to be your guide because you might get lost, but the road is very clearly indicated and there is no way you loose your track unless you want. Local visitors never take guide.

title: Must see
text: One of the best places to go in Sri Lanka. No people, quiet place with mystery atmosphere. Beautiful. Strongly recommended!

title: Interesting hill hike in the cool forest land
text: Worth a trip to visit this ancient monument. Uneven ground, so full shoes / trainers advised. A guide is not required. Atmospheric walk and interesting ruins to view.

title: Enjoyed the jungle walk
text: Not far from Habarana. We got a jeep for 2500 rupees between 4 people. An interesting walk through the forest. The ruins are not very extensive, but worth a morning trip.

title: Walk in the forrest
text: We walked about 1km before we were confronted by some aggressive monkeys and we had to turn back. We then got at guide (1000lkr) to take us all the way to the top. The monkeys were gone by then but the guide told os many interesting facts and took us a bit off road. The guard told os that only around 5 foreigners entered these woods during the off season which meant that we were all alone for 2 hours.

title: Worth seeing
text: Lovely forest walk, if you are lucky you can see monks in their traditional orange outfits. Very calming

title: Loved this place!
text: This is a special place---a group of ruins with a "jungle feel." It is off the beaten path and does not receive the volume of visitors other sites experience. The entry fee is much less than other cultural sites (~300 rps), and the site, itself, is not as well restored. However, if you want an experience that feels more remote and "in the jungle," check out this hidden jewel. It is a short hike, mostly on a rock sewn pathway, but I would still recommend that light hikers or tennis shoes be worn to access the ruins. Be sure to continue off the rock path at the end to see the huge old tree. It is amazing!

title: Amazing!
text: Me and my girlfriend did this beautiful walk solo without a guide, it was one of the most breathtaking treks I did my whole time in Sri Lanka. Lush jungle, not too tiring but with some exciting elements. Easy and very memorable.

title: Religious Mystery
text: Ritigala is the site of the ruins of a Buddhist sect of which not a great deal is known except that they lived a strict meditative lifestyle. One can imagine how it must have looked hidden on the side of a remote mountain and dream of what life must have been like then.

title: Ancient place with great history
text: Carrying a history of thousands of years.... some sources said that goes back to the era of great king RAWANA who mentioned in Ramayana.... Once a monastery and once a natural fortress.....

title: Buddhism, Ramayanaya, Nature, Yakkhas (Devils), Medicinal herbs
text: One of the must see nature reserves in Sri Lanka located just 50 kms away from Historic Dambulla. This place is mentioned in both Mahawamsa (one of the oldest and sacred books in Sri Lanka) and in Ramayana trail of Walmiki (India). If you hire a local guide he will tell you the story of the fight between two tribal leaders (Gotaimbara & Jayasena) and how Jayasena became Mahasona (a Devil) after beheaded by Gotaimbara. Most importantly, although Ritigala is located in the Dry Zone in Sri Lanka, it has a unique climatic pattern that changes when you hike further and further. Excellent for bird watching during the morning hours.

title: Special place
text: This monastery in the middle of the jungle is special. All are ruins, but with some imagination it is easy to imagine monks lived there. Like in Sigiriya, the irrigation engineering and various tanks are interesting. It is basically one path uphill, with various buildings around it. Tip: Visit the library, great views from there.

title: Beautiful, serene, ancient site
text: Our driver had no knowledge of Ritigala, so when a local rice farmer flagged our car down at the crossroads near the mountain and offered his services as a guide, we said yes. He turned out to be the most brilliant guide - full of facts and information about the ruins and beautiful, unusual trees, and able to describe in vivid detail how the community of monks would have lived, meditated and operated an ayurvedic hospital at Ritigala. When they came to establish Sri Lanka's first monastery there, the monks apparently brought plant species from the Himalayas and some of these still grow on the mountain, uniquely for SL. The road approaching Ritigala is stunning, and there were only a couple of other visitors when we were there. Our children, who experienced extreme temple fatigue at various other sites, loved Ritigala for its Indiana Jonesy atmosphere. It's an extraordinary place: 2000-year-old Ebony trees, rare types of monkey, an ancient library overlooking spectacular views, and an extremely well preserved system of walk ways, pools, and peaceful prayer places... well worth a visit. Give a donation - there's no ticket charge.

title: No tourists, very Raiders of the Lost Ark
text: Great experience wandering along the old pavement through the ruined temples in the jungle - when we visited there was not another soul there bar the monkeys.

title: excellent de tour from habarana
text: this a fantastic place,i have been many time there in the rainy season you can see small water fall also,calm relax place , the ruins are belongs to 3rd century bc,as its monastery old days ,even yuu go now, you still feel the same atmospherics situation

title: Solitude in the forest.
text: We visited this place during the afternoon so it was a bit hot, but it's mostly shady. The paths are charming and the ruins pretty cool. They aren't super super impressive but it is a good walk through the forest, although our tuk tuk driver went with us, his English was not good so a proper guide would be better if you're really into the history of the area.

title: A work in progress
text: Undergoing excavation,it is still disclosing its secrets,albeit slowly.A guide helps explain the site and puts things in perspective.A little esoteric but worth a small detour to visit

title: Trek through forest
text: I was totally confused before we embarked to ritigala from Habarna. It was a half hour drive. There are two areas there meditation center and ruins. The meditation center falls before and there is a 2 km drive through dirt road. We didn't do that. We went ahead and went past the information center to the car park area. From there we started our trek. The path is well defined. There are steps which can be easily climbed. Walking with nature around was lovely. Yoy can see ruins of various sites in between. There are hardly anyone there. We didn't find any streams as others have mentioned. We weren't sure how far we are supposed to go. Nevertheless we enjoyed. The entire walk took us 1.5 hours both ways.

title: History in the jungle
text: A wonderful place to explore. We had a local guide organised by our driver who was very informative about the monastery and its history. It is a wonderful, quiet place to walk in but it does require a reasonable level of agility to deal with the uneven surfaces which are probably also slippery after rain. The old majestic trees are splendid and the birdsong delightful. It is easy to imagine that this was a suitable place for the contemplative life.

title: Great get away from the crowds
text: We took at Tuk Tuk from Sigiriya and what a find. It was quiet seen deer, monkies. It was one best days out we enjoyed the place do yourself a favour go and explore

title: Hidden gem
text: Hidden treasure in the jungle - amazing ancient ruins. Steep terrain but worth the trek into the jungle, amazing amount of the ruins in tact. A guide is an must for the formidable area and also to explain the ruins too you. Decent walking shoes advised - water and hat.

title: Great trip
text: A great morning out. A hidden gem hardly visited by tourists. Very peaceful place to visit. No crowds. Free entry. An absolutely magical experience

title: You might even find yourselves there alone!
text: A remote temple in the middle of the forest/jungle. Not many visitors. Fantastic jungle ruins well worht seeing

title: Totally Worth It!
text: Rittigala was one of the most memorable historical sites we visited in the country thanks largely to its feeling of isolation and peace that swells from the history of this monastery that was left to the jungle some 1,000 years ago and the fact that it is well removed from the tourist hordes as my wife and I only ran into another 5 travelers during our time exploring this amazing place. Much of the ruins are simply the foundations, columns, and pathways that led around this once massive monastery, but for those people who have an imagination, love nature, and want to get off the beaten path this place is perfect. Be advised, you will need to have your own car or hire a tuk tuk to reach this place as the site is located on a dirt track 8 km north of the Habanara Highway. It is generally open from 7:30-18h with no fee, but they can ask for donations at times. Aside from the paved walkways, visitors should be advised that it is possible to bathe in the waterfalls and if you find the dirt path just downhill from there, be sure to visit the remains of the library, which in our minds was one of the best highlights of our trip

title: It worth the visit
text: I really like this place hide in the forest. We were alone visiting it!. Even though we had our own car and driver we took one of the tuk-tuks down in the main road. The tuk-tuk driver Sukat knows very well the ruins and the surroundings as he lives nearby. He is a nice guy.

title: beautifully unkempt
text: Old carvings, ancient rock caves, flowering cacti, along with pheasants, kingfishers, turtles and skinks, this was just heavenly. We didn't see another person the whole time we wandered (but then we also didn't see the etching of the headless man we read about). No maps and very few signboards added to the feeling of emptiness and mystery. Worth a pit stop between Colombo and Anuradhapura.

title: Your own discovery adventure in the forest
text: Not many other tourists. We liked it a lot. Beautiful walk through the forest with all these huge finds from the past. Highly recommended when in the area

title: Great place to explore , off the beaten track, so you will have a peaceful day.
text: Most ancient sites in Sri Lanka are known to everybody so tend to be crowded during the tourist season. Ritigala site is off the main tourist route, so its quiet and peaceful. Its a two Km long path slowly rising up the Ritigala mountains so one need at least half a day to explore. Views are fantastic from the top and the ruins all along the track.

title: Wear stout shoes or boots
text: This is a magical experience, the partial restoration tells stories and the mysteries still remain. It is almost unvisited which makes discovering it all the better. It is an extraordinary achievement to have built in stone such a complex which was home to so many. You can really appreciate how the jungle took over whilst it was abandoned, even some of the restoration is being encroached upon by the jungle. Find the library, it is a sublimely peaceful place with a breathtaking view. This is not a suitable visit for small children or the very unfit, but it was one of our best and most alone moments in Sri Lanka. If you do it without a guide then get some good information about it to understand it better. Also if you are self-driving as we were, be aware that your GPS may take you to the current Ritigala monastery, a fascinating place and not at all easily accessible. A lot of apologetic smiling and bowing later we found the ruins on the other side of the mountain.

title: Unspoilt
text: A new road makes access easier than it was a few years ago now a 15 minute tuk tuk ride from the main road. Entry is free, guide essential. With guide we rambled through the forest visiting the King's bathing pool, one of the monk's caves, a 3rd century BC toilet and a 1,000 year old tree amongst the ruins. We were there about 2.5 hours. Most interesting. Suggest you wear long trousers (a few mosquitoes) and stout footwear.

title: Magical walk through the forest
text: Really enjoyed climbing through the jungle to access Ritigala site - very beautiful and hardly anyone else.

title: Total beauty
text: This place just resonates peace and tranquility. The walk is picturesque and when you reach the top there is a beautiful little steam to cool your feet off in. Which is ideal because it is pretty hot and humid. One little warning, beware of the little leeches, wear insect repellant...

title: Amazing!
text: Great place, nature and ruins are incredible, you can easily spent half a day exploring the ruins in the jungle ! (... in theory, you do not have to exit the patch. In theory...) Transport to this place is complicated, you can get closer but bus, but you will have to take a tuktuk for the last km.

title: Could be better
text: Difficult to get to - We arrived with our driver at the faded and unused 'visitor centre' where we had to transfer to a tuk-tuk as the track was too muddy for vehicles. We came here as it sounded interesting in the lonely planet description but it wasn't that great. The part you can access (the rest is a protected area) has been part restored and there are some paths relaid. There is a fair bit of scrambling to do though which makes it more exciting but there is little to see here really and even the 'carved urinal' was a bit disappointing. Visit if you are passing but don't go out of your way.

title: well worth it if you have time
text: We arranged to visit here with our tour guide, so was driven in a jeep there. We visited on a Sunday and there was no one else there. It is govt run and a donation is asked for, we gave 500 each, which was incredibly good value for money. We spent around 2 hours wandering about, at a nice steady pace. Some of it is uphill but not too taxing. There is a tank, ruins, arches, a blood tree, queens toilet, executioners block - all in a jungle setting. It is tranquil, you can hear the birds singing, waterfalls, frogs etc. Lots of unusual rock formations and large trees. The hills surrounding were swathed in clouds. Lots of photo opps and by the time we had left we saw 3 other tourists. Shame about the scabby dogs but they were everywhere in SL. Would definitely recommend if you have time to visit.

title: Peace and Tranquility
text: We arrived after the monks had their meal and was offered food, but we declined. Loads of village people were coming in to enjoy a free meal. We walked up the 200 steps or I walked up the path which ran next to the steps. At the top in this forest setting was a peacful stupa area. You can just sit or do a meditation in this tranquil setting.

title: Excellent Countryside
text: Must visit. Lovely countryside. You have to see visit as to see the true nature of Sri Lanka. It is very important if you a Buddhist too.

title: Mysterious
text: Amazing atmospheric temple complex, buried into some truly deep jungle, get a local Tuk Tuk driver to take you there.

title: Nice track although not too long
text: You'll have to conquer a bit of bad road to get there. Our visit however was quite nice. It's a short track, climbing smoothly and it's a nice place in general. According to our travel book, in the past you could climb to the top and there was an entrance fee, but this is old information as you are not allowed anymore to climb further into the jungle. Visit is free and you are expected to give something. The guy at the entrance did not seem that happy with our 1000 rupees, although in my opinion it's enough.

title: Unique experience in the jungle
text: As others have said, Ritigala does have a bit of an Indiana Jones feel to it, although pretty much all that's left is the foundations of buildings and walk paths. I was the first one there in the morning (at 9am), so I had the whole place free to myself to walk around. A couple of groups came after me, but I only saw them on the way out. I was able to get a tuk tuk driver to take me there and back for 1,000 LKR, which also included him walking me around the site. The staff informed me right away that it was a donation to enter, and did not try to trick me into paying anything as others experienced. I spent a couple of hours there, and really enjoyed it. I would definitely recommend it for anyone who is interested in getting away from the crowds for a bit and seeing some decent ruins and massive trees.

title: Great jungle treck a la Indiana Jones
text: Practical info: you can GET HERE from Habarana by bus, get off at Ritigala. You will see a sing pointing the direction to the ruins. According to tthe sign it's 9 km. Away. That's why there will be tuk tuk drivers waiting there. They want 1500 LKR (after Bargaining) two ways. The only thing is that They want you to do the treck in an hour while you can easily spend 3 hours there. The ENTRANCE FEE is an obligatory donation, you will pay it in a small office at the entrance . Don't let the tuk tuk driver see how much you donate. After that you can enjoy yourself exploring the area. Don't be afraid to leave the path and explore also sideways. That's how we found a lookout called the Fort. A nice place to have breakfast. If you sit there for some time you will see rare birds which come there to drink water. When you will get to the top of the path after seeing a few ruins you will see the sign of a restricted reserve area. Big rare langurs live there. They are called "bear monkeys". We were able to See two of them close to the border of their area. Don't forget to bring mosquito repellent.

title: Hidden Ruins
text: Having been intrigued by pictures of this place we decided to make the trip out here to see the ruins. We took a bus bound for Anuradhapura and got off at the Ritigala Junction. From there we took a tuk-tuk. This felt like a rip-off as the driver ended up charging us 1300 rs. I could tell we were paying a good rate as he was smiling for the whole trip. Anyhow once you start up the trail to the ruins you will forget about any tuk-tuk negotiations. At the site we were told there was an entrance fee of (I want to say) 1300 rs. each, which we balked at. We were then asked to make a donation of 500 rs. each which seemed more reasonable. There was no one else on the trails and we had plenty of time to explore the various ruins. There were small offshoots at some of the trails where there were some significant additional ruins. Make sure you've got an hour or two to explore everything. Highly recommended if you are down with photography.

title: Hidden wonder
text: While the climb was a bit gruelling in the heat, Ritigala was well worth it. We chanced upon a guide, which was a good thing, as he could tell us what each ruin was. The water tank and stairs are remarkably well-preserved. Be sure to wear good shoes and carry mosquito repellent.

title: You might be the only tourist there!
text: Me and my girlfriend went there on our motorbike. It was personally one of my best visits in 4 weeks in Sri Lanka. Unlike ancient ruins like Polonnawura where there’s a lot to see but also so many tourists and you feel like in a museum, this place lets you explore as you are ALL BY YOURSELF. All we saw was the guy at the entrance, 4 dogs and another couple. There’s a main track that you can follow up and down and see a few site, but the fun begins when you look around, in the forest, and try to look for ruins. Look in the jungle for the faint tracks leading to sites or the “big stone sticks”, hinting that something cool is around. On our way down we realize there was so much to discover outside the beaten track. Everytime I went deeper in the forest I found another cool thing, remains of a praying site, mysterious grottos, name it. Sites aren’t as impressive as the other touristic ruins, but the fact that you’re discovering them yourselves and that you’re all alone really adds to the experience. You really do feel like Indiana Jones! The entrance is free (but a volontary donation is asked) and a bit hard to find.

title: almost indiana jones!
text: Great jungle ruins, quiet with few visitors adding to the experience as monkeys scream in the tree tops, and lizards scuttle across the ruins. A bit too dry to feel really Indiana Jones, children had been hoping for king Louis from the jungle book! But they still described it as awesome. Entrance was donations, no guide pushed on us so we were free to wander for a couple of hours. Amazing granite blocks, how did they do it? Worth detouring of the paved path to find the lookout fort, which was the highlight for us. Very basic toilets. Take water.

title: Nice hidden site
text: Ritigala is a nice site, quite different from Polonawura and Adurnarhupa. The site is in the jungle, with a few temple ruins to visit, and deserves a trip if you're around. However, the site should should be free, but the people of archeological department asked us to pay 10$/person to come in (of course without any receipt...). Our guide even went at the end to take his commission.

title: Nice forest few tourists
text: Went to Pidurangala rock and Ritigala ruins by tuc tuc from Habarana, was a nice trip. The forest was nice, some big impressive trees making for nice photos, not many or really amazing ruins, there is no official entrance fee, leave a donation at your own discretion. Nice walk, worth the hour or so stop if you go to Lion Rock or Pidurangala rock.

title: Quiet and peaceful walk in the jungle
text: The ruins are not particularly breat taking, but it was enjoyable walk through the jungle. I also foun the ruins intriguing even though they were not very massive or spectacular. There were only a couple of tourists so itwas possible to explore the ruins in peace and silence and spot lizards and monkeys. Felt a little like Indiana Jones :). It was very clean, no trash around. There is no admission fee but a donation is expected, we donated 1000 rupees each.

title: Quite a route march in the heat!
text: This was a lovely - if somewhat demanding - climb through the jungle to see ancient monastic ruins. Very enjoyable however, with knowledgable guide.

title: Great walk
text: This was a great walk up through rainforest to ancient Buddhist monastic ruins. The forest was lovely and we got to see plenty of wildlife. The walk up is reasonably strenuous but worth the effort. The ruins themselves are not extensive and there is a lot to see but they are very interesting in their own right.

title: Pleasant walk in the forest, that's about it.
text: On reading some of the reviews of Ritigala on TripAdvisor, I was expecting some kind of Indiana Jones-esque ancient ruin in the jungle. It's not. As we had already used half a day in a Sigiriya visit, my partner and I decided to take a trip to nearby Ritigala during our final day in the Habarana area. Our driver took us as far as he dared and we then clambered aboard the the tuk tuk that had followed us from Habarana (on reflection, we should have just got the tuk tuk from there). After a short ride along a bumpy dirt track, we arrived at a few scruffy buildings and were ushered inside one to sign the visitor book and also pay the 'donation' fee of 500Rs each. can't complain about the 500Rs as that is pretty much pocket change to most westerners. From there we were offered a tour guide to which we declined as we preferred just to explore ourselves. The ruins are not impressive at all - they don't seem particularly ancient. If you've been anywhere there are some impressive ruins - e.g. Pompeii, Athens or Latin America, you might even walk past the Ritigala ruins assuming that the real ruins are further on. Well, they aren't. When you reach a point where there's a square with some old building foundations, the rest of the path is blocked off - apparently it's because of the risk from dangerous wildlife (snakes, scorpions etc).. I'd actually have been quite interested in seeing some of those but safety first, I suppose. On the positive side, it's a reasonably pleasant walk in the forest with all the Sri Lanka forest noises that you'd expect - we didn't see much in the way of wildlife - a few interesting bright red bugs and a couple of monkeys in the trees but it's more of a walk in the park than a walk on the wild side. Truthfully, I'd skip Ritigala unless you have a lot of time to kill and have run out of other things to do. + Fairly secluded/not very busy + free/donation + pleasant forest walk - ruins distinctly unimpressive - top is blocked off

title: Monastery
text: This is very beautiful. There is a small parade of huts before entering the park. Do take time to have a drink called "orange" even though it is green. Really refreshing. The park is beautiful with a very old Buddha stature. Be respectful and cover your shoulders and legs from the knees up when entering the park.

title: Very pleasant morning trip
text: Nice walk and interesting remains of old monastery . The road there is in very bad condition making it difficult for cars. Tuk tuk drivers offer trips to the site. They charge 1500 rupees. The driver we ad ave a very good tour for tge price and was very knowledgeable about the area.

title: Alone in the jungle
text: Well worth the walk up to the site. Our car couldn't drive the last 2km, so we walked, not after been warned to be very carefully, staying on the track and turning back immediately should we meet wild elephants. Well we did not them and arrived at the site which is completely forlorn in the jungle. I've never seen trees of this size and age - it's simply amazing. Even the tiny rests of the monastery are impressive. A visit absolutely to do if you are near!

title: Worthwhile the little detour
text: Don't expect mayor ruins or heavily restored temples, but, as one guide book described it, it is a bit of an Indiana Jones experience. I loved the fact that we were the only visitors and the fact that it is a nice walk through a lush forest. The site itself is fairly small and one can cover it easily in 1 hour. Despite what some guide books say, entrance is free. The only negative thing is that, should you have a driver, he will likely refuse to drive the last 1.5km of dirt road. The only tuktuk driver around demands Rs 1300, which is far too much. You can even walk there really. Recommended

title: Tranquil setting
text: Set deep in the forest, a very peaceful place. We went early morning arriving 8.30 and were the first visitors of the day. We got a real sense of the peace and tranquility of the place helped by our excellent driver and guide. Even with the rough guide, we felt it was very helpful to have a guide to lead us around. A truly magical place

title: Forest Scramble
text: This is seldom visited but is real forest scrambling up a clear trail across huge boulders beside a stream to a hidden ruined monastery. Beautiful, trees were full of monkeys telling us to go away crashing through the branches. magical. So glad we added it to our itinerary.

title: All to ourselves
text: Went here yesterday. Jeep ride to the entrance was fun. Cool breeze a relief. The site is Truly beautiful and amazing in terms of the ruins, the history and the jungle setting. The view from the monk library was fantastic too. Walk is totally do able and worth it.

title: take a good antimoskito lotion with you...
text: Ancient monastery around 30 min walking from the parking lot in the jungle,spotting termiten,kameleons,eagles and huge beautiful trees..

title: Beautiful and peaceful.
text: Definitely recommend a trip to the beautiful and peaceful Ritigala. Although we chose not to hire a guide in most places we visited, a guide is helpful at Ritigala to make the most out of your visit. Lots of wildlife to see. A bit of a hike to see all the ruins but the walk is under the cover of a canopy of trees.

title: Great hiking
text: Bit tied to hike but it was so good to did that hiking. once you climb up to the mountain you can see whole area which was amazing. On the way to the top of the mountain we saw some old monetary ruins. I heard that it was a old castle. Great adventure to do if you hanging around dambulla.

title: another super place full of good energy
text: It is told that Budda during his visiting Sri Lanka visited that place I mean Ritigala Monastery. This is beautifull place full of positive energy, calm and green. You can walk and find the ruins of old monastery . really nice place.

title: Off beaten track
text: Very few tourists come here which is a good respite from the crowds at other major attractions . Peaceful n serene .

title: Very enjoyable walk
text: Ritigala is about 30 minutes drive from Habarana, there is a small entrance fee but the area is very quiet and we'll worth a visit. The walk around the ruins is not difficult, we spent about an hour there and could have stayed longer. Do read about the history before you go so that you can fully appreciate the area.

title: Nice walk full of suprises
text: We drove from Habarana and it was about 30 minutes drive. The walk itself is 90 minutes return with easy to moderately difficult due to granite steps. However it is far easier than other hikes as Seegiriya or Mihintale due to ancient paved footpaths. The vegetation is different to surrounding dry zone and takes you to another world. The real star is the ruines of a monastery with a hospital and a massive pool all made of granite. Pay attention to precisely 'joined' gapless granite paving stones. A guide is highly recommended if you didn't know the details. It is less visited than other main sites in the cultural triangle, I think mainly because Sri Lankan history books/school curriculum seems to give it enough respect, hence not hugely popular with locals. Thoroughly enjoyed the visit with large group of people including small kids (5y+)

title: It's just a pile of stones in the jungle....
text: However if you pause to consider how these stones were cut and placed in the area, it's pretty mind blowing! Not too difficult an ascent and we arrived at 12.30 today. Mostly visited by the "off the beaten track" tourist and we spoke to a lovely English couple who had years on us and still climbed to the top! A lot of Sri Lankans come here and it certainly wasn't crowded. We loved it, shame I was suffering from the after effects of dodgy belly and by the time we reached the last sunken garden I had barely enough strength to drag myself up the path to view the enormous tree roots that form the "fort". Was it so worth it to go, absolutely. Get there before the word gets out!! Cost for two tourists LKR 600

title: Great if you have the time and like Ruins.
text: I personally liked this experience but I could see people being disappointed if they expecting a lot. Its ruins after all. But I enjoy the slight hike and especially the "hospital" of these ruins. Do yourself the favor and either research it before, or get a cheap guide to get more out of the experience.

title: Worth visiting
text: Went with our guide. Quite a hike up rocky paths but manageable if moderately able. Mostly through rain forest. My husband picked up a tick. No leeches though and it was a drizzly day. Hard to get your head around how ancient this place is. Guide recommended

title: Hike in the jungle
text: Very nice hike through the ruins of a Buddhist monastery. Lost in the jungle. Very few (if any) tourists. Most of the walk is in the shade.

title: Retreat in the forest
text: What an amazingly beautiful and serene spot in the middle of the forest. A long drive to get there but such a welcome from the locals who had just finished serving lunch to the monks and offered us a meal.

title: Relaxing walk in the jungle
text: Nice, failry short walk in the jungle and interesting ruins. Easy to climb and lots of beautiful trees.

title: definitely worth the visit!
text: This was probably my favourite activity so far this trip. We went in the morning, by tuk tuk, and luckily we had the mountain to ourselves. The peace and serenity, only interupted by the sounds of the jungle, was so nice compared to the noise and hustle of tourists at the other ancient sites. If I was short of time, I would go here instead of Dambulla Rock, unless you are really interested in more statues of Buda. Gamini, out tuk tuk driver walked with us and explained some of the interesting features, as well as telling us about the different trees and creatures we encountered. It must have been a massive feat of engineering 1500 years ago to get the massive granite slabs up the mountain and in place. Great. P.S. free of charge, just a small donation required.;

title: don't go out of your way
text: A good place to wander around the ruins, bit of a hike, take lots of water. Not much about the history of the place though. I wouldn't go out your way to visit, but do if just passing. Free to go in, though a donation is asked for. Only wildlife we saw were loads of butterflies! And an elephant poo!

title: WOW - another gemstone in Sri Lanka's archeological heritage.
text: Amazing. Ritigala has only recently opened for tourists, it is an ancient Buddhist monastery and the highest mountain in Northern Sri Lanka. The ruins and rock inscriptions date back to 1st century BC. I recommend combining a trip to Ritigala with a stay at the Forest Rock Garden Hotel which is magnificent and won Green Hotel of the Year 2015

title: A nice place to visit if you have nothing better to do !
text: Although not as impressive as Sigirya, Ritigala is worth a visit ! This place used to be a Monastery where some monks, originally educated in Anuradhapura, established to help local people. Unfortunately, there is absolutely nothing to be found in English and this is a pretty remote area.

title: Another perfect day in Sri Lanka
text: We went by tuk tuk to Ritigala from Haberana with a great guy called Minda (probably spelt wrongly). Minda was an expert bird spotter and took us on a side trip to a lake where we saw an alligator, frogs, and eagles. We didn't bother with a guide at Ritigala, Minda came with us and pointed out various things of interest. The place is really atmospheric and although the buildings are in ruins, it is amazing to imagine the civilisation that created the monastery. On the way back we diverted to Habarana Lake where Minda showed us a monitor lizard - a great day out.

title: a walk in the jungle
text: great place to visit, not a lot of tourists, you can hear and maybe see the monkeys and you see lots of abes. Remember to bring something to drink. The walk takes around 2 hours.

title: Amazing place
text: Great place to visit. Not many do it but it is worth the effort. You can now drive up to the site - apparently this was not possible before. You have to sign in (name ,passport details etc) for the site and a donation is requested. There are a lot of steps up to the top but there are lots of places to stop and see different parts of the temple. Some of the paths are through the forest which is good. The ancient monastery is inside a national park but we did not see any animals only monkeys though we did see elephant droppings.

title: Treasure hunt
text: We went here with a local guide, who, if you ignore the requests for doubling his fee due to a 'sick child', is a good guy. Our children (6 & 4) were fascinated by the stories of cobra houses, elephant attacks and special medicine trees. They were playing 'Tomb Raider', looking for clues to find the lost treasure (magic medicine) of the Buddhist monks who once lived in this beautiful forest location. Just make sure you stay on the trails

title: Amazing mouton hard to access - By Serendib Traveller
text: Ritigala consist an ancient Buddhist monastery and mountain in Sri Lanka. Amazing geography so unusual located in the dry zone. Still no proper directions to reach up to the mouton. At the peak that weather almost similar to central hill country. But still open up to the monastery and archaeological sight. some times need to use a hard drive car or a jeep to drive through humph road. Im only recommend this to people like to take feel the real trekking experience in this non residential forest with a better organization.

title: fascinating ruins; horrible access road
text: highly recommended if you are interested in Sri Lankan flora and fauna, early Buddhism or a pleasant but steamy 2-hour hike

title: Nothing really special
text: I was expecting more of this place as I have read all the previous reviews. The place is in the middle of the forrest indeed, but there is really not much to see and the landscape is not breathtaking either. There are mostly conserved floor plans with some original stones... and lots of mosquitoes. You can see much more lush and green forrest with "Indiana Jones feel to it" in other parts of Sri Lanka (Pidurangala or Knuckles range for instance). Lonely planet description is also idyllic but don't get your hopes up. There is also one disinformation in the 2015 guide - there is no admission to this place. The guide says 10 USD. In fact you're only asked for a donation (so it's up to you how much you're willing to give). All in all it's a good place to kill some time but nothing really special. Personally I'd skip this place if I ever came back.

title: 1 of 4 Seniors in Sri Lanka
text: Unesco Site an ongoing archaelogical dig. Very interesting. Bit of a clinb to get to main building over rocks and streams but worth the effort. The viewes for the Library was great.plenty of trees and plants, very restful place.

title: Lovely forest walk
text: A fantastic walk through unspoiled forest with lots of wildlife. The remains of a nearly two thousand year old monastery dot the hillside. Beautiful environment and very peaceful. Walk tales about 1.5 hrs. Ensure you have mosquito spray if bites trouble you

title: Almost undiscovered
text: This site is perfect for travellers who wants a non-touristic experience. There are no signs and it's not all that easy to find the right way on your own. We almost missed out on most of the fun, because we couldn't seem to find the track, but luckily a guide saw us and guided us around, which included a exciting walk in the forest. The trees there are so beautiful! Don't miss out on this!

title: Awesome
text: This is an awesome historical monastery the hike up was fantastic. The hike is mostly on the rock bad cut when the monastery was active. There are steps and most of the time it is at upward in Klein which is mild in natureThe hike I must say it was pretty easy other than for the incline. There are areas of the monastery still intact which would include areas of meditation and also completely intact bathrooms that were used 1000 years ago. It has a fantastic view from the top of the mountain. There is also a 3 acre lake at the bottom which is in disrepair but it is been rehabilitated by the Department of archaeology. I used the services of a guide and he was A fountain of knowledge as he knew the history of the monastery and also combined it with the history of Buddhism in that area. I have never met a guide who so enjoyed his job and knew so much so I decided to include his name and telephone number if anyone is interested. His name is Asanka 0719560633. I would strongly recommend this hike.

title: Peace and quiet and cool
text: A nice walk through the forest exploring the old monastery. We were the only ones there - apart from a small group of buddhist monks, and the monkeys. There is restoration going on at the beginning of the walk and there is a small charge to enter.

title: A walk though the old ruins in the forest of the Ritigala monastery
text: This place was a rare experience of our trip in Sri Lanka. If you had enough of overcrowded spots and noise, add this monastery to your visit. It is an easy walk on the path through the forest. Silence and mistery will accompany you. It takes approx 1 hour. Go over the last ruins for few meters and you will also see a giant and spectacular tree. From the main road, you have to driver for approx 15 min to reach by car.

title: Shhh! It's a hidden gem; don't tell everyone.
text: Hidden away up a 3 km dirt road, Ritigala Forest Monastery is a fascinating, beautiful and stimulating place to visit. Make sure you get an official guide - Daya was ours - who charge around 1500SLR on top of the 350SLR entrance fee, as he'll give you insights into the rich history of this area, with its incredibly developed culture and brilliant design. It makes you re-think the uniqueness of the Romans, although most of Ritigala is 8th century, so a little later than the best of the Roman empire in Europe. Their skill in building and the beautiful little details - the feet carved in the stone marking where to stand on the urinal, for instance - reveal a deep and rich Buddhist culture which was fed by the beauty and rhythms of nature all around. Fabulous visit, totally worthwhile; I'm afraid I found Dambulla commercial and disappointing, but Ritigala helped me to forget!

title: Tranquil monastery
text: Such a great find and so happy that we visited. The walks through the jungle are peaceful and like something out of an explorer’s adventure. We followed the paths and saw ruins from 200 BC and a few monkeys too! Would be useful to have more signs and explanations of sites.

title: Such an amazing place!
text: We are on a tour and our driver suggested this ancient monastery as a place worth visiting - it was fantastic - the history is incredible. Our driver also suggest that we should get a local guide - we paid 1000rp for 4 of us - it’s a tip. So worth it his knowledge of the area and the wonderful things he told us. I highly recommend getting off the main road and visiting this place.

title: Isolated
text: A ruined monastery in the middle of nowhere. Well worth the trek, not another western tourist to be found. I fell for the "reduced" entrance price thing. More fool me, however my tuk tuk driver didn't let me fall for the guide scam. He asked for 2500rps but my driver gave him 200. The place was amazing.

title: Be transported to another era!
text: My mum's been wanting to visit the Ritigala Monastery for a quite awhile now and finally, on one of our many trips to see the usual Cultural Triangle sites (e.g. Sigiriya), we decided to visit Ritigala. I highly recommend it to everyone; it's kind of in the middle of nowhere but that promotes its peaceful factor. It is a site to be seen and experienced with your eyes, ears and heart. My mum and I walked through the paved stone path and among tree roots in total silence, breathing in the fresh air and keeping a reflective mindset. For the short time we spent there, we forgot all about the hustle and bustle of city life and other such materialism. A wonderful part of Sri Lankan heritage and well-worth a visit. The only sour note for us were the pesky bureaucratic "officials" who were in charge of the place - they pestered us for money for a personal tour and offered a cheaper entry ticket - but stand your ground and stay firm in your refusal. Once you leave behind the entrance, you will soon forget about bureaucracy and everything else and just only be entranced by nature!

title: What a treat
text: Our visit to Ritigala was an off the cuff decision based on the fact we read about it in the rough guide and it was near to us. What a great decision it was - a highlight of our short tour of SL. The nature reserve is 5km up a very bumpy, muddy and pot holed track. There were only four other tourists there and the hour or so walk through the jungle to view the ruins was exceptional. You'll need to hire a guide to show you where to go (R1000) and the entrance seems to depend on what the manager wants you to pay. It said R500 in the guide, but we had to pay R1000... That said, it was a beautiful, tranquil treat to wander through the jungle. My wife and I loved it. Head away from the crowd and go here. We enjoyed this much more than some of the other more well known attractions.

title: A wonderful to build a monastery
text: Very peaceful,but it is in the middle of nowhere in fact we go lost trying to find it!It was worth the journey .Sitting by the pool enjoying the site

title: Stunning, very atmospheric ruined monastery in a mountain forest
text: This is one of the loveliest and most atmospheric places I have ever been to. There are miles of ancient stone paths and steps though the forest, some of which have been restored. There are ruined refectories and enigmatic 'roundabouts' (apparently for walking meditation). The trees and wildlife are beautiful and there is the sound of waterfalls all around you. It's quite cool, but like many sites in Sri Lanka involves many hundred rock steps and a bit of a scramble at times. The atmosphere is out of this world. It is not visited all that much, which adds to its charm. It's on a rough track from the main road (our driver booked a jeep). When we got to the ticket office, still several kilometres from the entrance, a huge tree had fallen across the road and nothing had been done about it (it falls between the Forestry Department and another), so we paid a local lad to take us down the track on his motorbike! Clouds of butterflies rose up as we went along the track and I heard load roaring and crashing noises from the forest (wild elephants). There was birdsong everywhere.

title: Ritigala
text: We decided to go to Ritigala only 14 km from Habarabana to try to get a bit of the beaten track. It was very much a success. The park is an old monastery with surprisingly well conserved ruins. Tourists have obviously not truly spotted this place (yet!) and the artefacts are not covered in glas etc. but appears to be as they were left by the monks a few thousand years ago. At the entrance about 2 km from the actual park there is a visitor centre which is quickly overseen. We did not see any official staff but were met by 3-4 men with a jeep who adviced us that an ordinary car could not make it the last 2km to the park as the road was damaged. Instead they proposed to take us by jeep and give us a tour for 4000 rupees. We took it for a scam (of which there are many in Sri Lanka) but when we decided to walk the last bit one of them insisted on following us at least to park. To make a long story short the truth was that the road WAS impassable by ordinary car and the elephant danger was in fact very real. The elephant stories were later validated by pictures and other locals. As elephants are present all year nobody should try to walk, but in dry seasons (we visited in January) any car can do the trip. We ended up asking the "guide" to follow with us the entire trip which was a good decision as - his poor English aside - was very knowlegable about the site and show us stuff we would never have found by ourselves. The trip includes a approx 4km hike up a mountain side (medium intensity) and lasts about 2-3hours. There is an entrance fee of 1500 rupees pr person (be aware that the staff might try to persuade you to a lower price which they will then keep to them selves - if possible pay full and ask for a receipt). After the trip the guide was so nice as to invite us for lunch with his family. Best experience so far! He lives in a small house on the corner right in front of the visitor centre. If you pass by and want a guide be sure to ask him.

title: Indiana Jones at its best
text: Lost in a forest, you'll need a 4x4 -or in our case a Tuktuk - to get down the road here, but it's worth it to find one of the most armospheric ruins in Sril Lanka tucked into the hillside jungle

title: A pleasant change from the over-visited cultural triangle sites
text: Allow plenty of time to visit this site (1/2 day) as if you rush there and back you will miss the wildlife and atmosphere of this remote place. Look out for peacocks on the surfaced access road. When we went (early Nov 2012) the last track (unsurfaced) was badly rutted and it was tricky getting to the car park in our hired car. We arrived mid afternoon and the custodians had "run out of tickets" - so we paid nothing. You don't need a guide - just follow the main path and use the guides available on the internet. But we had someone to help spot the abundant wild life and plants - that was very good. As others have said it is a bit of a clamber round the old tank and up the slope on the opposite side of the stream - but after that it is a well made (original) pathway to the top.

title: Ruins in the forest
text: We made the mistake of walking the 6 km from the main road - don't. Take a tuk-tuk! The "officials" at the site offered to give us access at less than the official ticket price - and pocketing the money themselves. I would strongly advise that you pay the official price and get an official ticket - that way there is some chance that the site is looked after. I would also recommend that you get a guide. Ours was not expensive - R500 and did not speak that much English, but he did show us a lot of places we would not have found by walking on our own. He was also able to communicate some of what the various places were. The real joy of the place is the vast array of mostly unrestored ruins and the pathways between them. Ritigala is not a major attraction and is all the better for it. Exploring the ruins amongst the forest is a great experience and for me one of the best!

title: A Real Life Indiana Jones Movie Set
text: A step back in time. This was a wonderful place to wander around and see what ruins you can find in the woods. Some wonderful viewpoints, and sitting quietly listening to the sounds of the forest, contemplating life here as a monk many centuries ago, was fantastic.

title: Ritigala ruins.
text: We get to Ritigala and find there few people, of some archeological office , they speak just very basic English ,but our driver also don;t have good English knowledge, so after long talks between driver and local people we paid them 500 LKR ,they give us guy that would our guide with just few English words. But we enjoyed of forest cooler then outside environment,and our guide may explain us about ruins, we went on paved road to ruins, of what was before some 1500 years ,monastery facilities, bath,"cleared" circles( monks have to go 30 times around these circles to be cleared),double platform. I recommend visit this place, to people that like antiques.

title: Ritigala
text: Quite a treck for not too much to see. Nice forest though

title: An oasis of mountain walks!
text: Not on the main tourist route, a great advantage in the popular Cultural Triangle. Sadly access to the top is restricted to protect the valuable plants but there are still many birds to catch sight of and, if you are lucky, the shy bear monkeys.

title: Amazing to see
text: Amazing to see these paths and structures in the middle of nowhere halfway up a mountain. Needed an English Speaking guide and could do with some means of access to allow the less fit and able to see this amazing site.

title: A physical challenge!
text: We arrived early (circa 6am) for a walk. 4 1/2 hours later our group had completed to walk via World’s End and including both waterfalls. Toilets on route were a bonus. However conditions were extremely challenging in parts and 22000 steps later many of us were exhausted. We were advised not to take plastics into the National Park so were without water which was a mistake. DO take water with you. Lovely scenery although most of the walk/climb you look down to check your feet placing.

title: Fantastic scenery
text: A great mornings hike in the park , the terrain can get slippy and challenging with high steps but shouldn’t worry any person is in reasonable shape and take your time . A couple of toilets along the route but not a western standard so be prepared . Bring plenty of water and start early , Worlds end is a great stopping point with awesome views , lots of wildlife to be on the look out for.

title: Beautiful hike through the misty terrains
text: We started our hike through Horton Plains early in the morning to catch a sunrise over the misty hills and terrains. What can I say, it was definitely worth waking up so early. We saw plenty of deers eating fresh grass even before we entered the main gate of the park, and then had an enjoyable walk along the route towards Baker's Falls. There are two options: you can start with the Falls and finish by the Little World's End or vice versa. We chose the first option and did not regret it. After we saw the sunrise, the sun quickly disappeared behind the clouds and we did not see it much until we reached the falls and the skies became blue. We took wonderful photos and had our packed breakfast right there on a bench, which was so romantic and enjoyable. When we continued our route towards the World's End, we realized how right we were in taking that path - we almost always hiked down rather than climbing up and it made our trekking way more comfortable and less tiring. The day before we hiked the Adam's Peak, so we could not feel our legs and feet after that and this path we chose turned out to be helpful :) Unfortunately, when we reached the World's End, a big cloud hung on top and covered all the view. We waited for 30 minutes and the situation remained the same. We still were pleased with the hike and the World's End because there was a certain mystery in this endless mist over the edge. You can literally feel you are on the edge of nowhere. P.S. In my opinion, you won't need a guide to hike Horton Plains. It is super easy and it is impossible to get lost on the way. There is literally only one path and it is a round journey, so whatever way you choose - you will end up in the same place. Only if a lady is solo and scared of being attacked or something??? But generally, for me it seemed peaceful and safe. And if a leopard comes out from a bush, I don't think that having a guide will be helpful right??))) Also the time you will spend there will be at least 4-5 hrs if you do not want to run along the whole route and wish to take nice pictures and just enjoy the nature around you. So don't listen to people who tell it is like a 3-hour hike. Maybe, if you don't complete the whole circle..)

title: Great hike - hire a guide!
text: Lovely hike with amazing views. Took us about 4 hours total while carrying our 9 month old baby in a sling. We saw fluffy purple bear monkeys, reptiles, deer and even signs of leopards. It was chilly so bring layers! Make sure you hire a proper guide with a 4 wheel drive or a van to take you up - we saw some hair raising scenes of small cars struggling to drive up the mountain. I would highly recommend hiring a guide for the hike - you don't need one but you will learn so much more about the local wildlife and see so much that would otherwise miss! Can highly recommend!

title: Beautiful but Expensive!
text: The National Park is beautiful however the entrance ticket is expensive at 3000rps per person (tourist price). Locals pay a whopping rate of 60rps p/p!! This price disparity made us feel slightly exploited! You will need to pay an additional fee of 2100rps for tax and 100rps for a paper pamphlet! The park seems to be badly managed in general and overpriced for what it is. If you have an abundance of time in Nuwara Eliya and feel like a hike in nature then this could be worth jt.

title: Lovely walk .
text: However not for infirm walkers . Start early as it’s very hot in middle of day. Lovely views . Not always a good path a little bit of climbing over boulders.

title: 1 of 4 Seniors in Sri Lanka
text: Very Very rough terrain up to Mini World End then upwards to Worlds End viewing area over 2000m high views stunning. Then went onto Bakers Falls which is a large waterfall. 10k clambering scrambling sometime steep terrain. But if going need to set off when the gates open at 6am after that too hot and clouds roll in and obscure the views.Worth the effort

title: Great trek to Worlds End
text: Good to be able to walk in a National Park but very few wildlife apart from samba deer. Nice waterfall and a few steep climbs.

title: Lovely Mother Nature!!!
text: This is a lovely trekking place with fresh air and beautiful scenery along the trekking paths. Some beautiful stops worth to check out are: 1. Little World’s End view point 2. Great World’s End view point 3. Baker’s Waterfalls We were so lucky to be able to see a wild Sambar Deer right in front of us up close before the starting point of the trek. Entrance fee is quite steep at LKR3,850 per person. Suggest to go early in the morning as we departed from our hotel at Nuwara Eliya at 5am. On the way up to Horton Plains, before reaching the ticket booth, we stopped at the roadside to watch the sunrise above the sea clouds. Horton Plains is a UNESCO World Heritage Site where is protected areas for its nature beauty. It is a plateau at 2100-2300 meters above sea level. Hence, be prepared for the warm clothing since it can be very chilly early in the morning. A complete route of hiking require at least half day time (4-5 hours depends on individual fitness level) and the trekking path is relatively easy for all age, but good walking shoes are necessary, plus adequate drinking water. Packing breakfast is advisable for people who do morning trek. Tight security check of the bag/ haversack at the entrance of trekking and no plastics allowed at the park. We were so glad that we did morning trek as the weather was cool and pleasant and completed our trek slightly before noon. Hence, most people do morning trek and be there early as there will be long queue for security check. An afternoon trekking would be warm and sweaty due to warmer weather in the day. We simply love this place and the beauty of Mother Nature!!!

title: Ok but......
text: The world's end was an anti climax. We were sold the story it was an awe inspiring site, and sight, perhaps it is if you haven't traveled anywhere else. The park does show the diversity of the terrain and is a nice 10km walk but it is not for anyone seeking diversity of wildlife. It was disappointing to see the disrespect of some tourists who could not control their bodily needs until they reached the toilets provided. Perhaps more guides walking along the tracks or more signs showing where the toilets are may help ?

title: Fantastic place
text: After witnessing the litter problem in Sri Lanka it was very pleasant to visit such a clean litter free environment. Bags were searched on entry to make sure you weren't carrying any possible litter. The whole trek was very well marked and gave lots of opportunities for sight seeing.

title: Just don’t
text: We were searched bottom to top upon entry of the park to avoid any plastics, tobacco, lighters etc to enter the park, despite being nature respecting people ourselves. After entry, we saw groups of locals carrying gas bottles and tents around a random place they decided to camp inside the park. While we were robbed of our breakfast, they were cooking it in the park, while washing their hair and brushing their teeth in the river. The park is expensive (3500 rupees per person) for two viewpoints and a meagre waterfall. On top, we saw quite some wildlife, but all on the outside of the park. There’s no need to pay this fee, be searched and go through the hassle. The views, the ecosystem can be better just outside of the park.

title: Interesting but not spectacular
text: Not quite as spectacular as I’d been led to believe. We got there early and it was cold , need to wrap up, and the cafe was not open so no breakfast option available. Nice enough walk and views, spent about three hours going to Mini World’s End, World’s End and Baker’s Falls.

title: Well worth it .. but be prepared
text: We left our hotel at 5:30 AM to get there in time to see Worlds end before the mist comes in. It is cold at this time but it gets warm quickly so dress in layers. The trek is long (9 km) and the walking challenging at times (lots of rocks and roots to watch for) but it was worth it to see the view. But be aware that the trail is a loop and that it requires some degree of fitness

title: Worth the early start
text: So good to see this beautiful natural habitat kept in pristine condition. Many thanks to all those involved.

title: Ancient landscape
text: An unusual place to find on a tropical island. It rains a lot so pack sensibly and wear descent gripping footwear as the path down the circuit is difficult. The trees and fauna are lovely. You will recognise a few in your garden. The waterfall is beautiful and worth the detour down the hill. We had low visibility as in the clouds even at 6.00am so not such good views. Well worth a visit.

title: Beautiful worthwhile visit
text: This was a beautiful place to walk in, especially if you starting the cooler part of the day as it really gets hot from midmorning onwards. The terrain is quite difficult in sections. One needs considerable concentration and good balance not to twist an ankle. It requires a moderate level of fitness and good footwear. We were initially ambivalent regarding how dangerous some of the areas might be, but if people are sensible and do not attempt selfies near the edge, we could not see a problem. Take a hat and plenty of water, enjoy the walk.

title: Unusual scenery
text: I had an sunny afternoon trek through this park, the scenery is not like what we call plains in the US but more interesting. The rhododendron trees weren't blooming but the shape of them was unusual , a mix of a bonsai and an acacia. I took the trek from the visitor center through hills and a waterfall and then you see lakes then you will run into bakers falls. I didn't go to lands end , a lady said it wasn't worth it and the scenery wasn't much different, so I passed. If you have 2 days in nuwiyra eliya, visit here, but its about 30 miles away, but interesting scenery on the way to the park.

title: Worth the effort.
text: We did the early start- here around 6.30am., and as it was part of our tour, we didn't pay for it individually. It's quite a hike here- smooth paths one minute, rocky paths the next. I found it a bit hard, especially as the air is quite thin from the altitude- we couldn't chew our sandwich and breathe easily at the same time! But despite the effort we had to put in, it was SO worthwhile. Bakers Falls was lovely, and it wasn't crowded when we were there, so some lovely photos to take. World's End and Mini World's End have the most stunning view- it really feels like you're on top of the world. It's a real photo opportunity while hiking, so we really enjoyed it, despite the hard slog we had to put in!

title: An amazing expensive experience
text: The reservation is gorgeous don't miss. Entrance fee is $25!! 10 km walk through beautiful landscape

title: Foreigners skip. Pretty but a rip off
text: My friend and I visited in January 2023. Overall, I would recommend choosing antoher of the many attractions in the hill country over Horton Plains. Why go: it's a pretty and clean walk through a high-altitute plateau to a wide outlook down to the plains. We saw some deer in the open fields and interesting descriptions of the cloud forest. The walk is comparable in enjoyment to many temperate walks elsewhere. Easy to hire a return car trip from Nuwara Eliya (10,000 LKR). You can easily do the circular walk in 2-3hrw. Take sturdy shoes and a warm top layer. Start early: be at the park centre for 6:30am to get the best chance of the views before the clouds come in. If money is no question, then you will enjoy the park. Why skip: regretfully the park management seem to have taken to an extortion racket. A single person ticket for a foreigner will cost you around USD40 with the ticket price and the 'service charge', and even more if you actually want to pay in dollars (the clerk at the entrance will happily exchange to rupees for a hefty fee). That's probably about 40 times the price for locals. That is absurdly expensive for Sri Lankan standards and it's very expensive for what you get by Western standards, as it is just an unguided walk through the nature.

title: Hike Through Nature
text: Got there just after 6.30am. Had an amazing walk round the trail with some stunning views at World's End and Bakers Falls, pretty much had the whole thing to ourselves... Get there early, we finished just before 9.30am. on the way back down the road it was a constant stream of cars coming up to the trail, so would imagine it's extremely busy the later you leave it.
