Tips Get there early Wear comfortable walking shoes or trainers. Take your time, and listen to nature on the way round. So many people are in such a hurry to go round, they miss the beauty of it all

title: Hortons Plains is spectacular
text: Horton's Plains is an amazing walk taking you to Bakers Falls and Worlds End Recommend getting there for 6AM and going right first to The Falls and thereby going anti clockwise. We did both before anyone else was there so had to ourselves. We saw spotted deer, falcon and other wildlife before the crowds arrived. You cannot take single use plastics into the park, yet amazingly some local tourists managed to leave litter behind. Cost should have been $66USD but this magically got rounded up to $80. You can pay in rupees which I would recommend

title: Horton Plains via Rickshaw
text: I went early in the morning and was first at the gate at 6 am. The rickshaw ride in the dark from Nuwara Eliya took exactly an hour. And I walked the route without seeing anyone until just after Baker’s Falls at the end. A magical hike. I was back in Nuwara Eliya at 10:30 am.

title: Not so plain for a walk, walk and walk experience!!
text: Get ready for a walk, walk and walk for approximately 9.4 kms !! (Pheww) Undoubtedly this hike will give you a beautiful experience of walking in sweat, clouds, mist, rain and breeze ! One can experience all of them in the total hike ! To consider for people who are not so adventurous and who prefer less walking. The plains may mislead you about the difficulty level ! There are levels of walking and they are easy, difficult and more difficult!! And there are definitely the same the way they are listed. In the rains the rocks, the waking passage can be slippery making your hike really challenging. Till you reach bakers fall you will get an insight of your journey anyways !! One should be with very good quality hiking shoes with good grip which will be helpful while waking. Rain Coats, cap and some food stuffs are very important along with you. Remember to carry them in a paper bag as no plastics are allowed inside. They will remove the plastic covering of the water bottle too ( a good initiative though) Do try to start your journey maximum by 7:30 am to see a clear view near the world end ( if you fortunate). Else the clouds will cover you well and give another experience for photography only ?? You will enjoy the named places called and mini worlds end and worlds end. They are the places where you can have a breathtaking views if there are no clouds. Be very careful of the steep elevation of the worlds end while doing some photography. This may take a minimum of 3 to 4 hours depending on the walking speed and time. Apart from this: undoubtedly this will give an amazing feeling once you finally see the finish gate ?? # leaving your foot prints behind ?? # mythological: In the story, Hanuman set fire to Horton plains and that fire lasted for a long time. The original name, Maha Eliya Thenna carries the meaning, 'The hugely lighten ground'. Even now the upper layer of soil can be seem in a blackish grey colour. There had been some soil tests done by local universities, and it revealed that upper layer contains a high amount of Calcium Carbonate and Potash.

title: Beautiful Landscape But Don't Expect Too Much Adventure
text: I really enjoyed Horton Plains, which included mainly a calm and moderate hike with just a few uphills to climb some short peaks. If your guide is taking you to the World's End and other items on the edge of the moutain, just know that climbing uphill means going thorugh some dense bushes and canopies, so wear something more comfortable than flip flops or flats. I loved the scenery and spotting birds and lizards sunning on the tops of the plants and shrubs. My friend did not enjoy it as much, as she was expecting much more. So I would place this site between a casual stroll through a meadow and a solid moutain hike

title: Nice Location
text: Nice location..Highly Recommended to travel before midday... couples awesome place.... Do not late to back from the place

title: AMAZING SUNRISE!!! And BEAUTIFUL hike!
text: This is a beautiful hike --- it would be worthwhile to secure a guide who will know where to stop to view what will be the most AMAZING sunrise you will ever see. It simply took my breath away -- I compared the experience to Haleakula and this wins. After the sunrise we then proceeded into the park. We elected the clockwise path which is a bit shorter distance to the World's End which improves your chances of getting the view before the fogs set in. Although it did seem that even when there was fog, it was like weather at home: just wait a few minutes and it changes. The last 1/3 of the trail TO the World's End was so dense with shrubbery that without our guide I'm not sure we would have thought we were on the right path. For the number of people that take this experience, we thought it would have been more trodden, but it seems Mother Nature tries to keep it fairly dense. After viewing W/E, the remainder of the trail is a really nice nature walk. Keep your eyes out for green lizards that sit on top of the trees, little brown frogs that are fun to watch puff up with their croaking, and the variety of birds that inhabit the area. Unless you're familiar with how to spot these critters, this would be another benefit to befriending a guide.

title: Nice walk
text: This is not a tough trip at all. Easy terrain wich results in amazing view. We started the trip at 06:00 am Where there were frost all over the Plains. The trip is around 8-9km alltogether. You can also see some wild animals there as well.

title: Not Plain
text: Read so much about World End at Horton Plain. We like to visit. I am also expecting the long walk, but never did I realise that the 9.5km walk is really not simple, at least for me. The path initially was easy, as it is flat, but once entered the grassland, the path was rough with obstacles along the way. Ups & downs, under shade of the trees. Open space grassland path is easier to walk but under hot sun. We did not see any animals at all. However when reaching the mini world and hike another 1 km to the World End and further 2km Baker's Fall is really a reward. Another few km to the exit, for unfit people like me must reconsider. The path is a loop. I would say it is good for those who like hiking. Entrance fee is not cheap too. LKR7, 670 for 2 foreigners, 1 local, parking, tax.

title: Early walk at Horton Plains
text: A wonderful walk with beautiful views over the hills and lake. Deer walked down the slopes, the colors of the landscape and the nice waterfall...we enjoyed it very much. Advise: because of some rocky parts you need proper shoes.

title: Beautiful National Park
text: Beautiful National Park but go early in the morning. It gets hot in the day. It is not crowded but we had a hard time at one lookout trying to take photos of the view without a lot of 'selfie taking' tourists in the way. I think the earlier you go the better. Leave your plastic at home as they do not allow anything in. For example they cut the plastic labels off water bottles which is a great initiative. I wish all countries were this considerate of their national parks.

title: Not what I expected
text: After leaving my hotel at 5am and then walking for 9.5km over uneven ground I thought the Views at Bakers falls and Worlds end were ok , but nothing special .You need to get there early to avoid the heat , but wear layers as it's cold in the morning .Wear good walking shoes

title: What a hike!
text: This park is located covering the top of the mountain range in the area. The most popular hike leaves the ranger area complex and heads off along a very poorly maintained and rugged track to Worlds End. Here the risks are of being blown over the 900 metre fall protected by only razor wire. The views however are worth the risk. Once there the path? continues on to baxter falls. The scenery is great and the falls are worth a visit, continue on from the falls to do a loop and return the rangers area/car park.

title: Not for the week-kneed
text: Superb and Demanding trek. Lots of climbing up and down, so not for the weak-kneed. Terrific terrain with parts similar to Scottish country-side in summer. Good environmental consciousness. Unspoilt and prestine beauty. Could have better facilities for refreshments and toilet before you enter main trekking circuit of 9.5 kilometers.

title: Good experience
text: Nice yet challenging trek, very refreshing and easy on the mind and soul Very clean breaths of air and surreal visual experience Leave your electronics behind if you are planning on going here Would definitely recommend if you need a getaway This defined the mesmerising beauty that is Sri lanka

title: Nice but not worth £17 each
text: This really isnt worth the money. £34 for a couple to walk along a path and see 2 viewpoints and a waterfall. We thought the drive up to the park was more impressive. ..................

title: Highlight of my trip
text: Interesting part of the tour of our trip. We were advised to go very early having left our hotel at 5am, we were lucky that our hotel catered giving us a awesome breakfast pack. We were greeted with other tours lining up in the morning to get tickets, one word of advice is also to dress warm as in the morning it was VERY cold. The national park also restricts bringing in any food and you are checked at the entry point, it was strange however to see other tourists eating at the peak, i wasn't sure why our drink was confiscated. The hike was amazing, one of the best experiences ever, in the morning the hike was sublime, the pure calm and beautiful scenery was amazing, the best part was that luckily we had a good guide and was able to take a different route where we didn't see anyone. It felt like the whole park was ours, it was an amazing hike, to the peak the view was amazing and by the time we made it fortunately was much warmer. The hike wasn't too difficult and on the way back we saw bucket loads of tourists coming so it was another benefit to go when we did.

title: Unspectacular hiking
text: If hiking is a must-do activity, go for it. If not, pass. 9 kilometers with moderate climbing and passing through rocks, the World's End offers a view that is way less spectacular than hiking trails in other places. It claims to house the most bird species within the country, but I saw a few only and the birds are mostly common in shape and small in size. The black-shouldered kite is interesting when it is hovering like a kite in the air.

title: Magical Natural Wonderland
text: This national park is absolutely beautiful. We visited early morning and it was cloudy and misty. It has a beautiful landscape covered with montane grassland, located in central highlands in Sri Lanka. There are a lot of flora and fauna that you can see them clearly if it is not misty. we got a guided walk and our guide was very knowledgeable about the area. we recommend to take this safari walk and expect to be wet.

title: So peaceful and beautiful
text: Well worth the 5.30am start. We were even lucky with the rain stopping when we arrived and clear views at World's End. So lovely to walk through this beautiful national park which is well looked after and no plastic! Definitely recommend the walk up next to mini world's end which was a discovery - great views too. Didn't see any lizards or monkeys but saw sambar deer in the park area and leaving the park. Nice to have the plains to yourself for most of the loop.

title: Beautiful Park!
text: A lovely 9km adventure! However since it was pouring the day before- there was huge puddles that you could not avoid- so I recommend taking wellies on this hike. Worth the visit though. Lovely waterfall, however it was too foggy to view the world’s end.

title: Worlds end and a great walk
text: It is worth walking the distance just to witness the famous worlds end. The walk is about 3 miles, which is not yoo far and there is plenty to stop and see along the way. There are birds of different kinds everywhere, as well as plenty of animals, including the deer. We were lucky enough that one got very close on our way back to the car park! There is a very nice waterfall in Horton plains too, which is worth taking a small detour for. It was brilliant to be able to get so close to it. We could feel the water spraying on to us which was good in the heat of the day. Wobrlds end was spectacular. It really does look like what the words mean! The views were breathtaking. You could easily stay here and look out over everything for some time. There is also mini worlds end here which is very much the same but on a lower level. You go past this to get to, or return from worlds end. It to is worth admiring for a fair while. Definitely worth going to while here

title: Nice walk through forest, fewer animals than expected
text: I did the forest walk in the hills with a guide who recommended we leave Nuwara Eliya at 5:30am, so could start the walk at 6:30am. An early start means less likely to have mist & cloud. The guide recommended we go left at the initial branch in the track so more likely to see Worlds’ End views without cloud and then go to Baker Falls. Nice views down to valleys and lakes from the two viewing points. I should have read TripAdvisor first as then I would have packed the right shoes - I did the walk in sandals and coped ok with only a few slips, by being cautious, but it was rocky, slippery & muddy in places so would have been better in sneakers or hiking boots. The walk took me about 3 hours - the guide says it often takes 4 hours. I heard monkeys but didn’t see them. I did see a mongoose close up. Some sambar deer on the drive in & out.

title: Loved the walk through stunning scenery
text: Gorgeous 8-9km hike. Unfortunately we started our hike too late so we got caught in a gigantic cloud which made some of the parts slippery and we couldn’t see ANYTHING of “world’s end”. Nonetheless it’s a gorgeous part of this world and shouldn’t be missed. It took us about 2 hours but then we didn’t hang around the sights too long and it wasn’t busy. Definitely start your hike at around 7AM!

title: Wonderful long trek
text: We arrived on a warm but wet day but the place was not busy - it is not an easy walk and my fitbit said I did 13 kilometres and over a 100 floors - wet and slippery in some places and the terrain is very rocky in some places and quite difficult - wear proper walking shoes - Worlds End gives fantastic views and Bakers Falls spectacular - saw lots of birds/lizards etc and deer - this is truly the middle of the country and a wonderful way to spend an adventure date - VERY worthwhile - we were glad we had a guide

title: Stunning Scenery but More Challenging than you think
text: We arrived by 630 and got dropped off at the main car park for Worlds End You will come to the point where the path splits, we went right as had read this way is much quieter and it's TRUE - it's like you have the whole place to yourself, we didn't really pass anyone until over half way as those that went left passed us! The paths are narrow and congestion slows you down The difference to turning right is you go to bakers fall first, the other way you do little worlds end first, so another advantage to going right is that you see the vista from works end before the little one so you get the majesty first not the glimpse which I think could take the edge of worlds end if you saw that first The ground is quite uneven and if been damp or raining the clay soil is sloppy Some of the walk requires some mild climbing - we had read it was a non challenging easy walk and I would debate that for those with poor knees etc - its misleading to say that. It's not rock climbing but there are definitely areas that require effort and thought The views are incredible Out of this world worth every step We are fairly fit and active and took us just under three hours There are about 3 loo stops on the loop which I was really impressed with

title: Horton Plains
text: It was a tough six hours trek through the Plains. Plains could be misleading, as the tek involves quite a rocky terrain as well as slippery slopes. Would advise attempting this, when it is not raining and definitely with proper shoes.

title: Exploring the World Together
text: Horton Plains National Park is one of the most beautiful natural places on Earth. It is a tranquil place highly recommended for honeymooners. We would love to visit this amazing place again!

title: Super.
text: Super cool. Super mystery. You need to go there at 4 a.m, park opens at 6. You’ll see amazing sunrise on the road there. If clouds would be there, we think , it’s much more cooler. Because in sunny day you will see beautiful Mountain View. But in cloudy day you’ll see nothing. Absolutely nothing. Only the wall of clouds. And it’s unbelievable! Because this place is called The Worlds End. And if you want to see the end of the earth and to feel the infinity at the same time, you need to go there in a cloudy morning. You’ll feel something absolutely beyond belief. Must visit. You need to take something to eat/drink/warm clothes and snickers

title: Unremarkable hike, excessive admission fees... just not worth it
text: My lovely wife and I took the morning hike through Horton Plains National Park to World's End. It's a hugely popular hike but in truth is rather unremarkable. The trail meanders through rather mundane scenery to the lookout point which offers pretty impressive views. Having said that, I wasn't entirely blown away by them. There are, for example, plenty of vistas in Scotland that are equally if not more impressive. The high numbers of visitors mean there isn't a great deal of wildlife to be seen. There were sambar deer hanging around near the car park, which I believe there often are, and we were lucky enough to spot a purple-faced leaf monkey while driving back to Nuwara Eliya. But don't expect too much. Leopard sightings around here are almost unheard of. All in all it was actually a pleasant enough hike. But the trouble is that it costs way too much for what it is. Entry fees for the two of us came to around 8,000 rupees (£35, $44, €40) which is just crazy. You'll also have to pay transport costs on top of that - for example we paid 3,000 rupees (£13, $17, €15) for a tuk tuk from Nuwara Eliya. And it simply isn't worth the money for what it is.

title: Beautiful place
text: The Horton Plains National Park is definitely worth it. The “end of the world” provides a stunning view over the valley. The 9km itinerary is very enjoyable and spectacular. The waterfalls also are quite beautiful even tough in Sri Lanka there are much better ones. The only thing that was very annoying is that as a “foreigner” you will be charged 4000/5000 rs.

title: Goos time out
text: We had a party of 11 visiting HP. We were lucky with weather as from Nuwara Eiyla up to gate of the park we were in fog, but when we reached the start of the trek the clouds cleared and we enjoyed all the views during the walk. The walk takes 3 hours and takes you on a path with great views that you cannot see in Europe. If you travel as a number of families please buy group tictet. We got approx 25% discount for 11 tickets (4 kids and 7 adults). Overall good experience worth waiking up at 5am

title: Nice walk to get some exercise and beautiful waterfall
text: We enjoyed our walk at Horton Plains. We left Nuwara Eliya at 5am to catch the sunrise as we were driving up to the park, however it was unfortunately obscured by cloud. The walk was great at that time of day though, not too hot, and Bakers Falls are quite stunning! Also saw Samba deer, squirrels and birds. An easy 3 hour walk.

title: Nice walk with beautiful view
text: Nice walk, but nothing special. World’s end is very beautiful, so this makes it up patly. We started at 12h and had no rain or fog. We were recommended to start at 5 am but kindly rejected. Maybe we were lucky but we didn’t see any rain. The hike was 3h30 and quite difficult, but doable if you have an average condition. We took the opposite direction, so first to the falls.

title: A trek worth making
text: This national park is the source for four of Sri Lanka's major rivers, so it's not unusual to experience a bit of rain. Fortunately, the heavy rain dropped the night before our 9.5 km trek through the park, which took in the spectacular World's End. It made some uneven parts of the trail a bit slippery, so solid hiking shoes or, at minimum runners, are essential. Only a moderate level of fitness is required to navigate the main trail, which takes in World's End and Bakers Falls. However, anyone with some walking or climbing disability should take note that there are those uneven areas to negotiate. World's End is so called because of its 900 metre vertical cliff face that drops into the forest of the valley wall. It's hard to capture its scale in photographs. There are two viewing decks at World's End. Beware, particularly for children, that there are few barriers to prevent falls over the cliffs, both on the decks and on the short trail between decks. My impression was that the coiled razor wire would merely lacerate you during the fall rather than prevent it. The higher deck gives a much better view of the main cliff face. The steps down to Bakers Falls are also quite steep. Hortons Plains features a wide variety of landscape and an explosion of different colours from the many plant species that adorn the plain. The area is also a good place to see Sambar Deer, one of Sri Lanka's larger deer species.

title: Great morning hike
text: I was traveling alone and staying in a guest house in Nuwara Eliya so my transportation was arranged for by my wonderful hosts, but my tour guide/driver picked me up at 5am to take me out to Horton Plains. We got there early a) to beat the crowds, and b) because I had an afternoon train to Ella to catch, but we actually got there so early that the ticket office hadn't opened yet. The hike isn't too difficult, it's about 8 miles with a few portions of steeper climbing, but getting there in the morning allows you to see some GORGEOUS views. My driver gave me the tip of sitting and waiting at World's End because a lot can change in the scenery in a matter of minutes, and it was the best advice. I ate snacks I packed (remember to do this) and took a 40 minute rest up there and watched in awe as clouds and fog came in and out (at one point completely blocking the view and then clearing up to reveal a gorgeous drop and the plains beyond). I wanted to take pictures every time I turned the corner because I was treated to new views every mile or so - the diversity in ecosystems and flora/fauna is INSANE. If you're in Nuwara Eliya, make sure you make time for this hike! I actually stopped in Nuwara Eliya JUST so I could get out here! Definitely get an early start (apparently sometimes in the morning you can see deer and elephants if it's early enough!) so you're hiking when it's cooler and to beat the crowds.

title: The best memorable experience ever!
text: The view in this park is so breathtaking and mesmerising!!!! The ticket price to pay is worth it- this is a must visit!!!! We felt small in this park, we felt refreshed! This was definitely life changing!!!!

title: Worlds end nice walk
text: During our stay at Nuwara Elyia we went to the Horton Plains to hike the worlds end trail. Beautiful trail which is around a 3 hour walk... not very steep and good temperatures around there. As we are resident the entrance fee was low, but for foreigners, for which the entrance fee is higher, we still recommend this park. It is completely different than the rest of Sri Lanka with other surroundings and lower temperatures (around 22 C during day time)

title: Terrible experience buying tickets
text: We had a very unfortunate experience when buying tickets to enter Horton Plains National Park. We visited on the morning of Friday 12th July. Apologies for the long and less than positive review, I am also posting this hoping someone may be able to point me towards a way to lodge a complaint with the Park itself as I haven’t been able to find this online. Ticket prices are not advertised as prices tend to fluctuate so there is no price list at the ticket booth. We asked for “3 tickets, one person is local”, however this was interpreted as 3 tickets plus one local. A foreigner ticket at the time was ~2,650 rupees. With no price list, visitors the transaction is based purely on verbal communication with no calculator or screen to show how prices are calculated (there are three taxes on top of the ticket price). Understandably this is also a quick, rushed process during busy times such as when we visited. Unfortunately, we were unable to realise we were overcharged until we had driven 10 minutes from the ticket office to the park entrance. At the park entrance we spoke with a number of staff and based on what they advised we decided to enter the park rather than drive back and seek a refund (lucky we did this because as we found out, we would not have been refunded anyway and it would have ruined our visit). On our way out we approached the ticket booth and fortunately the same cashier was working (a middle aged man, moustache, larger, has worked at the park for over 15 years). We were very careful to politely inform that we were accidentally overcharged (e.g. we avoided saying “you overcharged us”, instead saying “we were accidentally overcharged”) however he immediately went on the defensive, became very rude and irrational and refused to help us. He accused us of being irresponsible and not communicating with him properly. He also said there is no possibility of a refund once a sale has been made and its the customers responsibility to know what they are being charged and that he does not make mistakes so it must be our fault. When we tried to explain that we were not trying to pass blame and a simple misunderstanding had occurred, he became argumentative and started insulting our tour guide/driver in Sinhalese and saying he was not looking after us properly. He refused to call the park manager (he said there was no phone reception, although all three of us had reception) and said nobody would help us because it was our fault. There was lots of back and forth about ticket prices not being advertised, no way of knowing what we have been charged for until transaction has been finalised etc. until we finally decided that nothing we did or said would help us obtain a refund. Overall, this left a very sour taste in our mouths and our tour guide/driver felt ashamed that a park ranger would behave in this way. Unfortunately, the cashier did not have an ounce of empathy and his behaviour screamed dishonesty and not a care on the world for doing what is right. Had he at least even tried to help us in the slightest, our experience with him would have been completely difference. Lesson: when buying tickets and you have a local guide to accompany you, be very clear to say X foreigner tickets and Y local ticket. Avoid assuming any statements like “3 people, one is local” as this will be interpreted as 3 foreigners, one local”. As for the park itself, it is beautiful and the views are amazing. It was lovely walking through such stunning scenery. However, the price is quite high especially in comparison to similar yet free experiences we have had in Sri Lanka as well as other national parks we have visited around the world.

title: Beautiful nature reserve
text: Left hotel at dawn to get there before it’s too hot. The road is good until the train station and then become bumpy. We had a 4*4 all the way from the hotel. The park is beautiful. It’s a moderate intensity trek. Take some food and water. No snacks and juice box are allowed so fruit and water are recommended. The meadow is beautiful and “worlds end” is a very nice view point. Don’t miss this park.

title: Really nice, but go everywhere.
text: Had a really great time walking around this NP. Started early morning but already a lot of people. (You can let your luggage or some bags a the entry checkpoint if needed) Awesome views. Some of the greatest views are a bit further than where everybody is. (Signs are there) Walk is a bit more tricky but worth it!

title: A great morning or afternoon hike
text: The price is quite steep, when paying for a family of 5, but it was totally worth it. Prices - Adults just under 3000 LKR and half the price for young children. That roughly equates to £12 per adult. You can see the breakdown in the photo. The hike was a gentle walk for half of the way. The last part, to get to World’s End and Baker’s Fall was trickier but still manageable. The whole hike was breathtaking. It took us 2 1/2 hrs for the whole hike (some say between 3-4 hrs). It’s is clearly signed and there really is no need to have a guide. At one point you can choose to go left or right. Going left means that you will visit World’s end first and right will take you to Baker’s Fall first. It’s a loop so it doesn’t matter which way you choose. Many people have shared that you are not allowed to take any plastic with you, however the rangers do help you with this. We went there with water bottles, as we had nothing else to carry the water, and some snacks. When we got there they removed the plastic labels off the water bottles and then provided paper bags for our snacks. We were very impressed with the care and attention towards the conservation of flora and fauna and they should be applauded for it. We didn’t see a piece of rubbish and it was completely unspoiled. A must if your are in Nuwara Eliya.

title: Not quite a leisurely hike...
text: An early morning start means seeing the most spectacular sunrise about 2000 metres up a mountain. Deer galore and quite a few monkeys on the way. The park itself is beautiful with well graded paths leading to 'worlds end' viewing point. Well worth the walk. 9 km round trip (felt like more!!) but completed within three hours with a well timed breakfast break at worlds end. Ask your hotel for takeaway sandwiches and water. Lovely waterfall not far off main path and leopards roam the area. We saw leopard scat!!!!

title: Breathtaking
text: A nice easy walk that takes a few hours with breathtaking views and very diverse scenery. One of the most beautiful places I have ever been to. You need to get there early in the morning (the park opens at 6am). Be careful not to go down one of the smaller tracks accidentally as it will take you very close to the edge of the precipice. We made this mistake leaving little worlds end lookout.

title: A challenging but rewarding hike
text: The trek through Horton Plains is a couple of hours long even for folks who think they're in decent shape. A good pair of walking shoes and comfortable athletic wear are a must. The views are well worth it, though.

title: Lovely Hike
text: It is a lovely hike across the plains. It is very thickly forested and has grassland in parts. It make a very good combination. We started from the right on tbe fork, so had the waterfall first. It is a small waterfall but something to look at. World's End and Mini Worlds End were totally fogged up. It is a good walk but needs a sturdy pair of shoes at times Am glad that the park does not allow any plastics at all. Right at the start of the park we saw lots of deers. The cost of entry for 2 was lkr 8100 for us.

title: Stunning views
text: Best hike ever . Leave early around 5/5.30am to start walking by 7 am latest. 90 min drive to the national park, great to see they work hard to stop ,plastic/rubbish in the park . It’s pristine. The aim is to reach Worlds End early before clouds drift in late morning and block the view . Take food and water , approximately a 3/4 hour walk if you stop for a rest , food . 3 separate clean toilets along the way . Well worth getting up early . Highly recommend.

title: Super hike
text: A fairly easy hike and that is coming from an unfit person. Second half of hike after Worlds End is the most difficult. Beautiful views and scenery. Enough toilet points along the way and sign posting was sufficient.

title: Interesting and challenging
text: We had a fascinating and enjoyable day here, which started with a large stag who came right down to the car park as we ate our early packed breakfast. Be warned - the 3-4hour walk is not for anyone with walking difficulties. It is a rocky path with some very steep areas, not a gentle stroll. It was very hot, shade is not always available. We climbed to the high viewpoint of World's End, wonderful views. Also saw Baker's Falls waterfall, again, lots of steps to reach it. Didn't see much wildlife, some birds, but we did find leopard poo!

title: lovely green experience
text: amazing views and animals you can see while walking. Water falls and many hiking experiences to grab

title: Get there early for the best chances of the views
text: We hired a guide/driver from Nuwara Eliya to travel to Horton Plains to ensure that we both appreciated the views as well as the wildlife. Unfortunately our hotel delayed us significantly as they forgot our packed breakfast which meant we ended up missing out on the views. Had we got there 10 mins earlier we would have seen what we headed to Nuwara Eliya for. While we missed the views, the hiking was still pleasant with nice scenery around and the waterfall made for a diverting stop. The round trip from the car park to the view point and then the waterfall is just shy of 10km. We found it an easy walk and most people should be able to do it easily. There is a fair bit of wildlife to appreciate: birds, lizards and frogs. We came across an organised birding group so I imagine its a good place to see birds. In order to have the best chance of seeing the views and the end of Sri Lanka try to get to the viewpoint before 8am as it clouds over really quickly. There definitely seems to be no point doing the walk mid/late morning or the afternoon as the whole place will be covered in cloud.

title: Great scenery, but a tough walk
text: We were taken here as a part of a tour of Sri Lanka. The circular route is 11Kms long and very tough with many steep ups and downs. The route surface is also not smooth, and you have to clamber over rocks, boulders and tree routes. This is made tougher as it frequently rains here and the rocks and mud become slippery. Not a walk for all ages or abilities. Wear sensible shoes and take water and food. The views are spectacular from Worlds End and the waterfall is worth a visit.

title: Its worth doing!
text: - We did the full loop and really enjoyed it. The landscape was very similar to Kosciusko in NSW Australia especially the low bushes. It did not have that many flowers nor birds to look at except rhododendrons. - The walk was not too arduous but if you do have walking poles would suggest to use at least one to provide support & security as certain parts of the track were steep and narrow. We (over 60 & 70 yo respectively) managed to do it under 3.5 hours without walking poles. - Arrived at 8am as per the guide's recommendation and the car park was full. When arrived it was a bit cool but certainly not cold (for Kiwis & Aussies) and getting warmer later on. - Make sure the seal and label on plastic water bottles and any plastic wraps etc. removed before the walk as it would be inspected and removed by park rangers at the park entrance. - Barkers' fall was nothing special but the views from the World's End & Little World's End were spectacular. Its worth doing!

title: Environmental diversity and an honest walk
text: The walking loop is about 9km and traverses the boundaries of where the grasslands meets the cloud forests of the mountains in Sri Lanka. A well preserved natural landscape combined with the outstanding views of Worlds End and Bakers Waterfall make this a rewarding experience.

title: A challenging trek.....but worth it.
text: The walk is quite challenging in parts with large bouldered footpaths and steep climbs through forest. The sights you see are worth the effort tho". Takes around 2-2.5hrs to complete full circuit.

title: Great hike
text: Relatively easy hike off about 9km, some great scenery especially “World End” some nice waterfalls as well.

title: If you are not a hiker, are you sure to be there?
text: It is national park in the mountains. Standard cirle is about 10 km, it tooks around 4 hours. Poular place, like great end of the world? looks not so attractive. Point of view cannot allow to see the beauty of this place. But if you cannot see, what is the reason to wake up at 4-00 am, spend time and money to get it, and walking 3-4 hours. Waterfall? It is not bad but it is not enough to be a reason to spend half day there. Really you no need to be there. If you are not hiker, of course.

title: A visit to the Horton Plains National Park
text: We got up at 5a.m. and drove to the National Park. To start with it w as dark and we drove up a steep road with many bends, we arrived at the park in an hour and it was getting lighter. Then we walked, through an area of grass and started climbing up until we reached the beautiful view of Little World's End and the Bakers Falls. Then we carried on doing a beautiful walk, Near the end of the walk we saw a lovely waterfall.

title: Not the Sri Lanka I expected
text: We like hiking but we’re a little confused by the 0500 pick up time. It turned out to be the best time to visit as there were very few people on the trails with us. We turned right that the beginning of the trail (taking the ‘long way’ to Worlds End when most groups take the left hand route) which meant most of the time, we had the trail to ourselves. We saw a deer up close and also a Leppord Foot Print in the sand. Worlds End was predictably crowded and we didn’t stay long - the nature and secery of the rest of the walk was more than enjoyable. A reasonable level of fitness is require to fully appreciate this hike. Do it early if you can stand the early start.

title: Morning Visit
text: We travelled from Ella at 4:30am to arrive at Horton Plains for sunrise. We did the 11km trek which included mini world’s end, world’s end and baker’s waterfall. These were stunning views and we were able to see an array of wildlife including a chameleon and a rare black eagle. There was a cafe to get food and drink at once we arrived back from our trek. They have a very strict plastic policy upon entry so be prepared to be searched. This was a very worthwhile day and the 11km walk took us around 3 hours to complete. We highly recommend going in the morning as it was getting very hot towards the end of our walk.

title: Nice park but high entrance fee
text: Staying in Nuwara Eliya I hired a tuk tuk for a return trip for 3000R. Leaving at 5 a.m. we got there just after 6 a.m. and there were already lots of people queuing for tickets. It was 4777R for one person plus driver which I thought was very expensive. The general advise is to get there early morning as the views at worlds end clouds over after 10 a.m. It’s a 9 km walk in a circular route, where you have the choice to go left or right at the first junction. Going left you reach worlds end first, as opposed Bakers fall by going right. I took the left to get to worlds end early and was rewarded by only having a few people there. The views are good with a vertical drop of over 800 metres. After 20 mins lots more tourists arrived so I moved on. Luckily when reaching Bakers falls later again there were very few people. The rest of the walk is nice but nothing spectacular and took around 2 hours in total. I didn’t see much in terms of wildlife but there are deer and even Leopards supposedly. In summary, this is a nice walk, but rather expensive if you compare it to walking in other national parks.

title: Must do
text: First the cashier told us to take a group (4 people) card instead of single cards, because it's cheaper. Nice trail, if you are lucky you'll see a few animals, but as there are also a lot of annoying people you should go there very early and try to separate from the crowd. The viewpoints are very nice. Stay behind the blockades.

title: Hike to Worlds End
text: If you are in the Hill country take a trip to Horton Plains National Park. Early morning is the best time to visit to have the best chance of good visibility. The walk to Small Worlds End, Large Worlds End & then Bakers falls is about 9km long. It is reasonably difficult as there are a lot of steps & uneven ground but the views make the effort worthwhile. There are viewing platforms at both Worlds Ends. If you have the energy, take the steps down to Bakers Falls as it is spectacular. Good footwear is essential for hiking in Horton Plains. No plastics are allowed in the park & any thing in plastic packaging will be confiscated at the gates.

title: A must visit when in Sri Lanka
text: Superb national park. Do take note the hike can be challenging so you may want to go at a slower pace. Tip:Take the path on your right.

title: Wonderful scenery
text: A fairly easy 3 hr. hike with short sections of steepish accents and descents - one of my knees is not very good and I was glad to have taken my walking poles with me. Although the highlights are supposed to be Baker’s Falls, World’s End, and Little World’s End, the walk through the park is spectacular with the most wonderful blue skies when I was there. As others mention there is a ridiculous queue to get into the park, not because there are too many people trying to get in, but because of the long time it seems to take to process the paperwork- there was only one person dealing with it when I was there although there seemed to be plenty of staff around.

title: Worth a trip up the mountain
text: The road up and is very steep and serpentine. The hike at the plateau is interesting and rugged. Worth the trip however. Great vistas. Wear shoes not flip flops or like one lady, high heels. Walking sticks if you’re a bit unsteady. Would recommend doing the 9km loop in the clockwise direction.

title: An enjoyable walk
text: It's not the greatest walk I've been on, but it was different and enjoyable. I wouldn't want to do it in the middle of the day as I thought it was quite hot when we walked - from about 7.20 to 10.30. There is a cloud forest in this area so you'd have to get there very early or be very lucky to strike the World's End without a lot of cloud. But they said, I didn't mind standing near the edge and watching the cloud roll in and up and over the cliff face. Sit long enough and the cloud lightens enough for you to see the valley below and some of the tea fields. If you follow the track on the left it is the shortest to the viewing platforms but it makes the walk back via the falls a steeper climb, so I personally preferred walking anti-clockwise and getting to the platform after the crowds and then having an easier walk back along the less steep ridge. Frogs, forest pigeon and a Sri Lankan giant squirrel were our rewards for walking this trail. The squirrel looked like an Australian tree kangaroo in the face but had a large bushy tail. You can hear the bear monkeys in the jungle here as well and we're so lucky in that on the very bumpy drive back down the plateau a bear monkey was posing for us on a tree Top. So keep a look out. As walks go it was moderate - some steep slippery sections, and the landscape it crosses was quite interesting - undulating hills, interspersed with grasslands and forests. I don't know what the park fees were as we did it as part of a package so in some respects it's better not to know and as I think the most expensive fees, it was nice to see the Rangers being very vigilant with hikers as far as long plastics go and to search each bag and advise to bring everything back out. So surprisingly I saw very little plastic litter - the off pieces carelessly dropped but good to see they are trying to keep the area litter free - except the toilet area - unfortunately full of rubbish.

title: Totally exceeded our expectations!
text: My friend and I had so much fun hiking through this beautiful National Park. Every time we turned our head the view was just spectacular.

title: Nice hike. Easy enough to enjoy, challenging enough to feel you exercised.
text: Nice a well marked path: you can't get lost! No need for a guide of you are here for a stroll, yet having one will help you spot more animals (especially recognise birds). Deers, monkeys and birds were our main spots. And a lot of leopard poo ?? The hike will take you to 2 impressive cliff edges and a refreshing waterfall. The hike is not difficult but the terrain is uneven so be sure to wear appropriate footwear (with ankle support if possible).

title: Good hike but shame about the razor wire
text: Did the classic Worlds End and Bakers fall hike which was lovely but it was near impossible to get a decent picture at Worlds End due to the excessive amount of razor wire telling you where the edge is. I recognise the need for it safety wise but there must be a better way of doing it! This is an early morning activity - if you do it too late in the day, the views are obscured by cloud so it is worth getting up at ridiculous o'clock!

title: A must see place in central Sri Lanka
text: Horton Plains park is around 30 kms. from Nuwara Elia. The journey through the winding roads , ups and downs and the tea plantations, protected forest areas, grass lands is spectacular. You can enjoy the rural life and agriculture practices of the locals enroute.Then there are wind mills,beautifully maintained farm lands, cows grazing in the slopes, lakes and distant waterfalls which adds more charm. It just reminds you of the grass lands of European countries. Once you reach the plains the views are amazing.Its grass lands,surrounding forests and distant mountain peaks make upfor perfect photo shoots.The national park is well maintained and conservation efforts ae to be appreciated. There is large variety of flora and fauna within the plateau . In side the park the most sought activity is to take the forest trail which is about 8-9 kms which takes 3 - 6 hours depending upon you health conditions. During the trek you can see the Bakers Fall, the famous Worlds End and Mini Worlds End .

title: Hill country national park
text: Staying in Nuwara Eliya we took a tuk tuk to Horton Plains leaving our hotel at 6.00am. We met a line of traffic entering the park but once tickets had been obtained we were on our way in. It is quite an expensive place to visit, although the same as many other national parks in Sri Lanka - $15USD per person, $8USD service charge, plus the vehicle and driver entrance 185Rs plus 15% tax on top of all of that! The tuk tuk ride from Nuwara Eliya was 3500Rs. There was a long line for the toilets at the entrance but there are more toilets inside the park where the walk starts from. It’s quite a long drive from the park entrance to start of the walk, I had assumed the walk would start at the entrance but we saw no one walking along the road. We saw several Sambar Deer though! There are bag checks at the start of the walk where plastic is confiscated. Plastic drink bottles had the plastic labels torn off them. If you have food in plastic bags you’ll be given a paper bag instead. This is great to see and it really meant that the park was very clean. The walk clockwise to World’s End is pleasant with grasslands and bush. There are toilets near little worlds end. It was misty at World’s End but the mist came and went so we were still able to see out to some lakes south at times. It’s a neat spot for watching clouds of mist rise over the 800m drop. The rest of the loop walk was nice too as it’s through the grasslands with views down to a river. There are more toilets near the waterfall. Overall the walk is fairly easy although there are some challenging areas with uneven terrain and steps.

title: only for the young and enthusiasts
text: This is a beautiful place with a long walking trail. only if you are ready to walk a long trail and fully healthy and no issues with leg pain or so. Recommended to start early in the day so that it is a cool time of the day. Please carry food along with you.Make sure we maintain the cleanliness and serinity of the place.

title: Beating my expectations - but get up early to experience the same!
text: Waking up early in the morning can seem as a hassle, so when you finally make up your mind, you will find it’s worth it. Beautiful sunrise, have seen wild rabbits, deer, a lot of birds, beaver, even a leopard according to our driver..., the mist setting and clouds raising. 2 ways to do the loop, we did the one starting to the right and believe have made the right choice as on the way out we were more exposed but to the morning sun, on the way back, we had some shade.

title: Go early and enjoy
text: Early start and worth it. The worlds end what a view. TIP bring a lunch box and pack your breakfast in it for the top. All bags are checked as you enter if there is any plastic (cling film or wrappers you have to leave them behind) you can bring a plastic water bottle but only when the label removed. Take your time up there or and the little worlds end, soak up the view with your brekkie. We covered 10.5k, not tough (we both exercise regularly) wear good footwear (we had runners) and enjoy.

title: Fabulous nature
text: Virgin fresh and clean countryside, which looks more like in New Zealand than in polluted Asia. Forests, meadows, bushes, streams and fabulous views. The usual route is from the NP entrance to Little World’s End, World’s End, Baker’s Falls and back - all together 9 km or 3-4 hours. Start early morning, ideally at 7-8am, there might be some mist later (and too hot). Foreigners pay ca 2800 LKR, locals 60 LKR. Definitely don’t miss this trip, it was probably our best experience in Sri Lanka.

title: Just lovely
text: Horton Plains were an unexpected pleasure. In many ways they reminded of parts of the UK, say Exmoor: moorland with bracken and rhododendron. The standard 9Km circuit is mostly very easy walking though one section is quite a scramble. Sensible shoes are needed. It is popular. The main sights were a little disappointing. But overall it is a very pleasant place

title: Early start, strict plastics control, moderate hike
text: A 5:00am departure from Nuwara Eliya to then hurtle through the dark with eager drivers overtaking at high speeds. Our hotel packed us a breakfast which we ate after driving but before entering the park. All disposable plastics are confiscated at the entrance apart from water bottles which have their labels removed - so be prepared. The hike itself is definitely challenging in parts around the falls, but the remaining 90% of it is easy to moderate. Our children of 11 & 8 made it around with only an average level of bickering and complaints. We saw a nice sunrise and elk on the way in but no other wildlife after that.

title: Enjoyable Hike
text: Amazing experience enjoying the beautiful surroundings. Well maintained, clean and environmentally friendly. Must for all outdoor enthusiasts.

title: A nice walk spoilt by Chinese tourist hooligans
text: You need to be here early to miss the build up of mist. We arrived around 06.50 and we certainly were not some of the first here. Despite what some people say, this is a pretty tough walk. I'm relatively fit but I'd still call it a challenging walk. My Fitbit recorded 17500 steps and 171 floors. I hate to tarnish an entire country but we were again inflicted to Chinese tourist hooligans. These moronic individuals who are only interested in taking posed selfies of themselves with 'V' fingers need to be taught how to be a tourist and respect others. We had seen it at religious sites where they run everywhere, shouting and pushing and completely disrespecting other people's religion. Today it was the utter disrespect of nature. Signs ask to be quiet, this is a place to take in the landscape, to listen to the wind. This is not a place to have Timberlake coming out of your I Phone at full blast As no one else was saying anything I'm afraid some Anglo Saxon words about their parentage was uttered and I guess they understood as they put their earphones on!!!! We were lucky to see the very rare bear monkey, an animal that is incredibly shy. Everyone around was hushed and we were able to see this amazing animal. Despite sushhhing and pointing to the monkey so they too could see it, these imbecilic people started to whistle at it like you would a dog. The monkey disappeared. At Worlds End again it was the Chinese that pushed to get the best vantage point to get selfies of themselves. China has just started tourism and this problem will only grow. Everyone appears aware of it but no one is teaching them that there are ways to be a respectable tourist. Our guide said this happens all the time. Perhaps responsible tourism behavior needs to be taught in school? The walk as mentioned is challenging, some good walking shoes should prevent slips. We saw people in flip flops. We also saw tourists with small children. This is not the place to take children. It is challenging enough on some of the steeper climbs, but looking after or carrying a child is an accident waiting to happen. It will be completely boring for them anyway and a pain for the parent. The drive from Nuwara is in the dark and therefore you don't see much, but coming back its a great drive and you see plenty of local life with good photo opportunities.

title: Why so expensive?
text: Horton Plains is an important area for nature and conservation this must be it's primary function and restrictions on where you can wander around are understandable. That said, the entrance fee of about £15 per person for what turned out to be a half day trip seems excessive. We arrived at opening time to see birds and didn't do the world's end walk, which is what most of the tourists were going for. I saw all of the species that I wanted to and was very pleased. The open air toilets were a great design and odour free. I hope the money spent goes to a good cause. In the UK national parks are free and most other countries that I've visited they only charge a nominal entrance fee. Sri Lanka could get a bad reputation for ripping off tourists. We've regularly come across one price for locals and a much larger one for foreigners. The recent implementation of free tourist visas for stays of less than one month is a great way of encouraging tourists to return after the Easter bombings. We came for two months and had to pay £160, we've spent a lot of money in that time. We'd consider returning but please reduce the visa fees.

title: amazing
text: amazing location beautiful view of sunrise many deer there lovely waterfall is very good clean location

title: Nice walk in countryside
text: Nice walk through the countryside. Track is sometimes slipery and muddy with tree roots, so do not go here in slippers. You can se here wild animals (deer, birds). If you wanna see the Worlds end. Definataly go there as soon as possible due to the clouds. Also in later time it should be overcrowded by other tourist.

title: Overpriced
text: This one is definately a case of fleece the tourist. Its a nice area, but there are equal places of note that are free or a lot cheaper.

title: Fantastic hike
text: A wonderful hike through bush and across plains to Baker's Falls - senstational, Little World's End and World's End.These last two offer spectacular views when there is a break form the swirling mist. Even the mist is amazing to watch as it swirls in and out. It is very peaceful and not at all crowded. It is hard to reach without a driver. The train stops 5 1/2 kms from the entrance and it is a hard walk. There were no tuk tuks or drivers waiting at the train to drive people. If you an get there, it is definitely worth the effort.

title: Amazing trek
text: We were their early morning and i would suggest to everyone to wear layered clothes as in the early morning due to low clouds it will be chilly. Then you start the trek which approximately take 3 to 4 hrs depends on how much time you spend taking pictures and gaze to the lovely views. 2 main highlights which are the End of world (for landscaping views) and the Baker falls (waterfall). Worth the time for this trek i really recommend to go ??

title: Wonderful walk in beautiful countryside
text: We were on a small group tour and the walk to World's End and Baker's Fall has been one of the highlights of our trip so far. You need to start early as otherwise the clouds roll in and you can't see the view. It's cold up there at that time of morning so take plenty of layers as later it gets really warm. I started with a down jacket over the top and ended up in a T shirt! Take hats and sunscreen too and sensible enclosed walking shoes. Quite rightly they don't allow any plastic containers in the park (other than water bottles with labels removed), so be prepared for a thorough bag check on arrival. I applaud this as there was almost no litter on the whole trek. There are toilets strategically placed throughout the park which I didn't use but others said they were fine. Would recommend this if you are reasonably fit. It's 9 kilometres and over quite slippery rocks at times so if you have agility problems you might struggle. I wouldn't want to do it in the rain but we had a beautiful day with great views from World's End.

title: One of the highlights of our trip to Srilanka
text: We left at 5 a.m. and it took us 2 hours to reach the entrance to the National Park. There was already a long queue for tickets. It was quite cold then, and we were glad we had worn our jackets. At the entrance, they checked our bags for plastic. They even removed the plastic wrapping on the water bottles. That was impressive. It was a 7 km trek through various type of terrain. We saw a couple of deer grazing at the start of our trek. We took the route towards the right and were glad of having started early, as it was already beginning to get warm. Half way through we reached Baker's falls which was a wonderful sight. We continued on our way through rocky terrain at times and as we neared the point called World's End,we saw this amazing view of clouds coming down. We reached there and felt that we were literally among the clouds. We could not see anything below the cliff. The clouds were covering the view. After this point comes Little World's End and then the hike back is through shaded areas. Here you get to hear the sounds of different birds. Maybe if we had binoculars we would have been able to see them.

title: Excellent
text: This place was definitely worth the 5am start. We got there early and were leaving before it started to get very busy. It took us 2.5 hours to do the hike around, amazing scenery, wonderful views, loads of deer. Two toilet facilities on the way around which was great. Bring water, a light jacket and runners. Get there early or the clouds can come in quick and you won't see anything. Highly recommend! Medium level of fitness required.

title: Amazing hike with great view and various terrain
text: Got in my hike for the new year. Woke up at 430 am to arrive at Horton Plains at 630 am. Got our tickets and started our hike around 715 am. Get a jacket as the early morning’s temperature dipped to 12 Celsius. The terrain is relatively easy and took us 3.5 hours to complete the full loop. At the fork road, we took the right route as our guide said it’s easier. Terrain started with rather flat land with brushes. Then the hike started downhill and the terrain became more trees with roots on the ground. We visited Bakers Falls first which is an amazing waterfall. Next stop is World’s End, which is the main reason to do Horton Plains. Amazing view and take a moment to take in the moment. The final stop was Little World’s End which is basically the same view but from a different point. The hike back is basically rocky and heading uphill. Highly recommended for avid hikers.

title: Brilliant morning from Nuwara Eliya
text: Fabulous hike around waterfalls, Plains, jungle and ridiculous views. Takes about 2 hours from car park to car park taking in all the sights. Fully worth it! Tip - After giving your tickets in head right towards the waterfall first instead of left to worlds end. It’s a loop so you’ll see all of it. But so much quieter on the right. Enjoy!

title: Hiking of our lives
text: 6 hours of leisure walk thru the Plains and enroute seeing sambars and squirrels and birds tweekings .. worth the hassle of getting up early in the morning And to top it all we saw mountain lions , while we were driving out the exit , trying to take picture of a sambar. See the picture to believe. Sambar took our attention to the lions in the backtround of our drame

title: Memorable views But get there early
text: We arrived just after watching the sunrise from a vantage point on road up to the park. Yes up and up and up. Roughly about £17 entrance fee. The 9km walk can be a bit challenging walking shoes helpful, though met young monk who was bare foot. Views are awe inspiring, and view points can be crowded, with many nationalities each with there own etiquette. You should get there early we arrived around 6.30am Reason being you come for the views and wildlife, ad we left around 10.30 clouds were already beginning to drift towards the park. Also don't take plastic bags they are not allowed

title: Nice hike in the nature
text: We hired a driver from Nuwara Eliya to get here-- about 1 hour drive. It's a nice, easy, circular hike-- 9km in total and takes about 3 hours. Nice view point of World's End and Baker's Waterfall is beautiful. If you're lucky you'll see the purple faced monkey. Entrance is quite expensive, 3,650 rupee ($21).

title: Over priced
text: Great place for a walk. I’m only giving it 3 stars due to the over priced entrances fees. $21usd to walk around is very expensive and is outrages. The views are amazing though

title: “Nice place for Hiking”
text: Horton Plains Park is a nice hiking area. We enjoyed more than 10 km hiking towards the amazing water falls and coming back The weather was incredibly magnificent and unbelievable. The signage can be improved to reflect the height of each top to indicate to visitors the height from ground or sea level. Please note that the distance to the falls is not indicated all the way through and it’s only indicated at the beginning of the hike. Highly recommended and it will require an easy one full day to spend there.

title: Nice place but expensive
text: Nice walk and a nice waterfall that is possible to swim in. Worlds End was very misty when we went so can't comment on views. Terrain is quick rough and could be tough going for elderly or unfit people.

title: Trail walk
text: A long and sometimes difficult trail, but worth getting up early. We saw few animals but the scenery was varied and the waterfall, though not very high, was very scenic. The toilets left a lot to be desired!

title: Amazing hike with incredible views
text: Though this is such a main touristy attraction, it's well worth it. When you first arrive around 6 am, it's full of cars and people running to the ticket booth right when it opens, which makes you nervous about the crowds. But as soon as you get on the trail, of which there are two choices, the crowds really thin and most of the time you are hiking on your own. The hike is not strenuous, with few steep uphill points, and the scenery alternates between forest and open plain which is really cool. The viewpoint at the top is amazing. Get there early- otherwise, cloud cover rolls in and the view won't be the same.

title: UNESCO Heritage National Park with Worlds End...
text: There are two main roads to go there. If you go by bus or car better go from Nuwaraeliya and if you go by train go from Nanuoya/Ohiya. Its just 1 hour from each location to Horton Plains. I went with my 4 foriegn friends.If you go morning aroud 8.00am is so better. Get tickets and go inside, its 3500LKR for foriegner. Dont bring any plastic, polithine they not allow you to bring inside so better you keep in your vehical. Only water bottle allowed. Total tour was amazing and its take around 3-3.5 hours walking in altogether 7.5 km. To the worlds-end there are 2 roads, you can choose any. Main worlds end, little worlds end and Baker's water falls are the main attraction. My foriegn friends were so enjoyed the environment too.

title: great hike in the morning to the worlds end
text: Be there very early, as from 9 it will be crwoded. the nature is gorgeous, the hike to worlds end very nice and the view there just stunning

title: Enjoy nature in all its glory
text: Other reviewers have described the terrain. It’s certainly doable and we’re not young( 68 and 72) and had climbed Adam’s Peak two days before. The air is absolutely pure ( wonderful lichen growth) and the different views at various points on the circular loop varied and beautiful. We saw birds ( 2 varieties of eagle and lots of smaller species, deer, and other mammals, but I will never forget the variety of plants from the tiniest liverworts to the towering trees. I know lots of people visit for Bakers Fall and Worlds End, but you’d be missing out if you didn’t take your time to admire and examine the wondrous plant life. Originally, husband wasn’t going to do the full loop because his legs were still suffering after Adam’s Peak but he agreed that it is not to be missed.

title: Worth getting up early for!
text: My husband and I went and it was one of the highlights of our trips to Sri Lanka. Absolutely stunning location and scenery and really brilliant to see the staff checking everyone's bags to make sure they weren't bringing in plastic and environmentally unfriendly substances into the park - but really annoying and disappointing to see whilst we were on our hike that some selfish people had thrown plastic and rubbish around. Anyway we loved this place and felt completely at one with nature. Definitely recommend it.

title: Definitely have to visit this place.
text: Throughout the trail, you can actually feel the temperature changes and you will see every impressive landscape and scenery! If you're in Sri Lanka, you definitely have to visit this place. Just be careful and wear some good hiking or walking shoes.

title: It’s an exceptional experience.
text: It's a quite rugged hike but it's definitely worth it. Once you enter the nature, you will find so many beautiful landscapes and relaxing sounds that you will never want to leave! In fact, it's an exceptional experience and a must-visit if you are in Nuwara Eliya.

title: Definitely one of the best experiences to have!
text: Scenic national park perfect to see beautiful landscapes. The canyon, waterfall and sceneries are gorgeous and breath-taking. In fact, it is a quite relaxing and fun place. Definitely one of the best experiences to have!

title: Depends of your stamina and objectives, could rate higher/lower
text: Facts: Circular walk is 11.6 KM, altitude is 2100-2300 M (it 7000+ feet), so oxygen is less at this height (down from 20.9% effective to circa. 15.5%) . If a hot day then this walk is strenuous but very doable (take plenty water). Half way round is Worlds End a vertical and panoramic viewpoint which is something (careful here a tourist lost their life “selfie” taking recently). Disappointment for me was the lack of wildlife - I had expected a richly biodiverse assortment of mammals and birds and encountered very little.

title: This is NOT a walk in the park
text: This is a national park and it does require money but I have to wonder where it goes. We were told 3 different distances to the various 'signature spots' and the signposts give a fourth opinion. This should not be attempted by anyone with a hip, knee or ankle problem and hiking boots are almost a necessity. The tracks are not maintained in any way and consist of reasonably steep climbs and descents through deep ruts strewn with boulders, rocks and loose stones. Furthermore it is suppoesed to be a nature walk, and we started before sunrise, only to find around 100 vehicles at the the first gate with several 100 tourists clamouring for tickets. We entered and drove 5kms to the second gate to find even more vehicles and people. Goodness knows what this is like later in the day although when we left at about 9.30 am there must hjave been thousands in the park. As described, walking is difficult and the experience was not helped by crowds of mainly Asian tourists squawking incessantly and noisily with some even playing their radios for all to hear. The result - no wildlife. When we got to either of the World's Ends we could hardly see a not that impressive view for the crowds of photo and selfie taking tourists. There seemed to be neither control nor wardens on hand and most of the guides were more intent on chatting up their attractive customers than controlling the mobs. Our guide, who was embaraseed by the appalling behavious of the tourists and their mentors, did attempt to quieten the mobs but his efforts were in vain. He did advise us not to attempt a visit to Bakers Falls as that requires climbing and descending by holding on to mangrove roots as the tracks are in an even bigger mess. It is a not that impressive, expensive money spinner but for whom?

title: Very nice park
text: This national park is beautiful and I enjoyed the hike there a lot. Still, the famous « world’s end » was a bit disappointing and I think the entrance fee is too high for what it is, but if you’re into hiking and want a nice day in the nature, that’s a good place to go.

title: Magic
text: Obviously to get the best experience of this place, you should visit early in the day (to beat the heat), but it's hard to actually beat the crowds--there were plenty of people there at dawn. No plastic or cigarettes or lighters are allowed through the gate (and bags are searched) so leave it all in the car. We spent about 4 hours in the park, and every minute was great. The trail was rarely at all steep and had varied terrain. Bear left when you reach the fork at the entrance and go clockwise around the trail--you get World's End first and the easy path later.

title: Loved this place
text: Nice view and nature , should have more food services and facilities , take food with you during the walk .

title: Lovely experience, but why does the coffee man short change overseas visitors?
text: The walk starts early at 7am and was frosty, but warmed up. So wear layers first thing in the morning and have a rucksack to put things in as you warm up. The walk took 3 hours and we had only a couple of five minute stops. At the end there was a coffee shop. A shame the guy behind the counter only gave 40 rupees change and not a fifty note. He kept only big notes on top and others in a drawer under the counter. This did not happen to local visitors. Such a shame, ten rupees, is it worth it?

title: Beautiful park
text: We drove through this park and it is absoulutly beautiful. Easy to find and well with the visit. Highly recommended

title: Popular Park near Nuwara Eliya
text: While based in the Nuwara Eliya area our birding group spent one half a day in the Horton Plains National Park. We arrived very early (as did everyone else), this is a popular place to watch the sun rise, but soon we left the crowds behind as our mission was to find some of the endemic birds of the region. Even with all the people there is plenty of room to avoid the crowds as this park is huge. This turned out to be a very pleasant mornings experience, even though it is a long drive to get to the park entrance.

title: Worth a Visit
text: This is a fair distance from Nuwara Eliya and at least from our hotel it would appear impossible to get there for sunrise unless you were prepared to get up very early. The approach road is very narrow. We opted to leave at 07.00 and although we missed the sunrise, we also missed the crowds. Although it is only 4.5kms to World’s End the walking at times is not easy and I can’t imagine doing it in the dark. It is going to take you between 2.5 and 3 hours of walking. The weather in this part of the world is very unpredictable and I think you should see whether you can cancel your trip if the weather is not good. We were lucky and had a very clear day. Although you go for the spectacular views, don’t rush and try to just enjoy the peace and quiet. From our experience, walk anti-clockwise as there is otherwise a very steep and difficult climb near Baker’s Falls.

title: very nice
text: Sri lank has many national parks. Horton can be considered good or average depending on where you are from. For us from North West US, it was OK

title: great walk to Worlds End
text: early start from Kandy but well worth it. The park is well laid out with obvious trails. The views are stunning from worlds end and little worlds end but only if you get there before 10am id say. Wear decent shoes, you don’t need fell boots but decent trail trainers are a good idea.

title: great views
text: super mountian views with waterfalls around many corners - well worth taking your time driving through this region - you will also notice the temperature dropping slightly so a great place to escape the heat of the lower plains

title: Vacation
text: Yes this is a must see. The highest mountain range in Sri Lanka with grand waterfalls and rivers, lakes and the supplier of half the worlds tea from the plants that surround these beautiful mountains. The homes with the beautiful vegetable gardens and terraced rice fields and misty mountain tops. Its absolutely breathtaking.

title: Honest opinion? It’s a 5 out of 10 tops.
text: Did we do it? Yes, as we were never likely to be this way again. So it’s usually a 5 or 6am depart from Nuwara Eliya to get to the entry of the park for when it opens. The entry is about an hour away from Nuwara Eliya. However with a 5am departure time you will be driving in the dark. Better, for me, to have a later departure as the views on the way in are fabulous and, indeed, the best bit of the trip. Once there entry is expensive, indeed, I think it was the top price for entry we paid on our entire Sri Lankan trip. From the entry gates you then drive further into the park before the start of the walk. Once walking it’s a well marked, well worn track. We turned left at the first fork and went to Mini World’s End. This drops you into World’s End a little earlier than if you follow the main track. It’s an interesting walk on a sunny morning, no more. We did see the Bear Monkeys though, which was a highlight. The view from Worlds End is nice enough but for me, not as good as the one from Little Adams Peak. Baker Falls on the walk out are well worth a detour. The drive back to Nuwara Eliya is very pleasant - you’ll be home by lunchtime.

title: Nice morning hike
text: Get here early if you want to see World’s End! I arrived at around 7.30am, got a picture of the hills with some cloud above them. Within minutes the whole hill and view were covered in thick cloud. I felt for those who arrived after me. The hike is reasonably rocky and wouldn’t be suitable for young children or anyone who isn’t fit. I completed the 9km in around two hours 40 with a few breaks and walked quite quickly. I completed it alone and didn’t need a guide. Everyone is friendly and I followed a few groups on the more tricky parts. Didn’t see any animals and only one interesting bird but the terrain is interesting and enjoyed the challenge.

title: The highlight of any trip to the hill country
text: Only 26 km from Nuwara Eliya but a long, steep and winding drive up to the plains. Going up through Pattipola from Nuwara Eliya allows you to visit the Ambewela Farms and view the rolling farm countryside and dairy herds. Pattipola is also the highest point on the railway going to Ella and the road crosses the tracks at the station. It's best to get to Horton Plains early. Mist rolls in later in the morning and often the views are obscured. It's a 5 km hike to World's End and back via Baker's Falls, also worth seeing. Head back out of the park via the Ohiya road for some spectacular views of the World's End gap from the road. Not exactly the same as hiking to the lookout point but stunning nevertheless. Viewing wildlife is a hit or miss prospect. We saw nothing. But there are some tame Sambhur deer at the visitor center for a photo opportunity. These animals are habituated to humans due to feeding, unfortunately, but you can get quite close, something that you could not do with truly wild animals.

title: Lovely walk, but get there early if you want to see anything from World's End.
text: Lovely walk through grassland/heathland/forest with about 20 species of bird to see. The terrain is uneven, but it is not a hard trek and only about 9.5 km in total. World's End is spectacular, but already at 8am the mist was starting to roll in, so get there early!

title: Spectacular natural beauty...
text: Visited Horton Plains and hiked two different trails for a total of 12 kilometers. The first (and most scenic) was a circuit trail called World’s End, extending from the park entrance to Baker’s Falls: a 20 meter water fall at the midway point. The Horton Plains trails follow a plateau route that is 2100 to 2300 meters in altitude. At most, expect a 150 meter elevation gain over the length of the route. Scenes are spectacular: you’ll pass so many beautiful vistas and scenic overlooks that you’ll run out of smartphone battery power before running out of photos to take. This is a must do trek but arrive early at the park (0800 latest). There are many trying to get in and the lines to get tickets are quite long.

title: Sri Lankan tour
text: Great walk and great views! Don't forget tip for toilet! Need sensible shoes and water . Some big steps so be prepared!

title: Bad timing
text: Arrived well before sunrise to join a long queue. Hard to believe that on the day before Independence Day there was only one person selling tickets. As it happened the mist stayed until late, so would not have been able to see the sun rise. Took the loop walk which we much enjoyed. A not too arduous c9k.

title: 9k walk around the National Park to see the mountain and beautiful views.
text: You have to start our early before the mist comes in over the mountain, we started at 6am and took a packed breakfast from the hotel, as we arrive we spotted a deer it was very friendly and came right up to us. A bit chilly to start off with but it turned out really hot, so take plenty of water with you. You also need to be quite fit for the walk as a lot of it is over rocky ground wear really supportive shoes four of us are 60+ and managed ok. We were taken there by our guide and even at 6am it was very busy,- need to tip the guys when you use the toilets.

title: A GREAT BUT DEMANDING WALK
text: We enjoyed what was a 10 K walk through the plains some of the views were outstanding and well worth the experience. The average age of our group was late sixties and a couple of the group struggled, but if you are reasonably fit it is achievable. Would not recommend for small children and some spots the barriers are minimal.

title: Great walk
text: Despite my dodgy hip the walk of 9.5 kilometres was interesting and we stopped not only to see the Baker's Falls but took our time looking at the birdlife.

title: Beautiful walk in nature with amazing views
