text: Definitely a recommendable experience. Go early in the morning, we arrived at 7:30am. Wear layers that you can remove as the temperature constantly changes. The views from worlds end are great and bakers fall is beautiful. We went for a swim (the only ones), it was very cold but definitely worth it! Took your breath away!! Go clockwise, so to the left at the sign once you are walking in the park. A walk through the clouds!

title: Must do, worth it !
text: This is a must do. despite the ticket widow hassle, this is absolutely one of the best hike I have ever had. it would be wise to ware light / short sleeve inside and warm coat outside, as it was quite close early in the morning, and became hot after the sun came out, fast drying cloths and running shoes or hiking shoes would be perfect. it is about 11km in total, there are some steep up and down parts, so be sure to bring water and maybe some energy bars or chocolates with you. don’t miss this , go and see it for yourself !

title: Great views but not an easy hike
text: We had a very early start to ensure good views at Worlds End, which paid off. Very beautiful scenery at both view points and although it feels like a rugby scrum when you first arrive at the start of the trail, due to the terrain, the crowds thin out. I imagine when the rhododendrons are in flower the scenery in the rest of the area must be spectacular. I was surprised how tricky the terrain was though. It was billed as a hike but there are a lot of boulders to navigate and shale surfaces which makes slipping a real risk.Anyone not fully mobile should be aware before setting out. We had a very hot day so take water, you will be checked for plastic items on the way into the trail but are allowed water bottles.

title: Absolute amazing
text: Our driver pick us up arround 4.30 in our hotel. Around 6 am the park opens hand we had to walk 9 km. The landscape and the light in the morning where absolute amazing. We had a great time there. I recomend to go there in the morning.

title: The best walk in Sri Lanka
text: We really liked it. both generations, even our teenager kids loved the walk and the view. If to go from Nuwara Elia, you have to leave around 5 am to be at the right spot before the clouds. Also it is a difficult trip for more than 3 hours. Our mistake was, that we took only 0,5 l of water for each, for that trip, on this heat you need much more. Snack (what hosts prepared for us was very much useful as well). I think if to go with kids, you need to dedicate about half of the day.

title: World's End - An unbelievable view that is worth the walk
text: We were at the park as it opened. Already a line of vehicles. Was good to head off early before the heat and the crowds. We did it clockwise, so shorter to get to World's End and longer walk (via Bakers Falls) back. It requires climbing up and down some parts of the track so needs some agility. Recommend good walking shoes or sandals. But nothing too bad if reasonable fitness. Mini World's End was good but World's End was spectacular. Getting there as early as possible seems to be better before it gets too misty. Standing on the edge of a 4,000 ft vertical drop is not good for your vertigo!!! The walk back via the Baker's Falls was also great. In the end was a loop of about 9KMs. Be aware that as you enter the walk they search your bags for any plastics and take them away from you. For example we had a couple of water bottled with plastic labels and they cut off the labels before we were allowed to take them in.

title: Proof of the Continental Drift Theory
text: It is a beautiful place, good for trekkers especially because you have to go walking long distances to view the park. Not advisable for small children, it is simply too tiring. The Horton Plains are proof of the continental drift theory and the museum in the park has details on this. I found it very interesting.

title: Excellent Walk
text: We were picked up from our hotel at 5am and driven to the entrance of the National Park to begin our walk at sunrise. It gets very busy especially on weekends, holidays etc. so go early to beat the crowds. We walked the circuit to Baker’s Fall first and then onto World’s End and mini World’s End. Not a difficult 9kms but wear good walking shoes. Worth the time as the scenery is beautiful.

title: Nice tour but overpriced
text: The landscape at Hortons Plains is really beatiful and different from what you see in other parts of sri lanka. However the entrance fee is relatively high (we paid a bit above 7000 rupees for 2 persons and a shared van for up to 4 people costs you another 4000-5000 rupees) - a bit pricey for a 3 hours walk. We left nuwara eliya at 5:15 and arrived at the park entrance at 6:15, then we had to queue for tickets for around 30 min (better leave before 5 if you decide to go). We did little world's end first which was free of clouds, but wirlds end was already covered in clouds when we git there 8:30/8:45. Try to not take any plastic bags / Joghurts etc since there is a backpack check after the park entrance where you need to remove those anyhow.

title: Horrific for 5 minutes late
text: Horrible adventure which makes me dissapointed by this country on my last day of Sri Lanka... We wanted to go through there and visit it to go Nuwara Eliya, we arrived there at 4H05PM after 3hours of driving into the mountains, the staff didnt want us to go through cause it says Tickets counter close at 4pm but the park himself closes at 6pm !!! When you check on their website it says close at 6pm... After 45 min to ask them to understand our position that if they can not let us go we will have to drive 2h30 more hours to reach our arrival.. we were about 30 min to reach our destination from horton plains !! The girl in duty call her Officer, 7 people came for us and talk to us like if we were just a piece of s**** and tell us baddly and angry to move the hell from here !!! We were basicly begging them and they were using their power against us in a way I never experienced before. I am not the guy who used to put bad reviews at all but this one needed to be known for everyone ! Make sure if you go nuwara eliya from Ella in car, that you take the right timing. Don't waste your time and money, the suroundings are much more nicer for free. The price fee is also super high for that short parc and foggy place.

title: Very disappointing
text: Don’t bother. Ridiculous entrance fee (40 euro for two foreigners, of which only 60 roepen for our tuktuk driver) for an average walk in an avarage environment. When you go very early you have to walk in a crowd, when you go later in the morning the Sri lankans scare away every animal with their chatter.

title: Nice stroll in the park
text: Horton Plains with Worlds End is one of the "musts" when visiting Nuwara Eliya, and it ́s worth the effort. Worlds End cliff is enchanting with the drop of +800 meters, but you have to be there before the mist sets in (before 9.00am.?) or else you will meet the white wall instead of the magnificent views.

title: Well worth the early start
text: We hadn't planned to head up to the Horton Plains before we got to Nuwara Eliya, but decided to on arrival and arranged an early pickup (5am) with our tuktuk driver. Nuwara Eliya is cold at that time of day,and we were very grateful for our padded jackets - make sure you prep well for a cold morning! The journey over in the dark was, well, interesting - low-lying mist on the unlit roads, speeding drivers trying to overtake at all opportunities (it is Sri Lanka after all!) and low powered tuktuk lights all made for a memorable trip! After buying our entry tickets ($45 for two people including all fees and taxes) we headed up to the trail head as the sun was coming up, with a few scattered deer out on the plains - fairly magical! The hike itself is a circular, so you can head either clockwise or anticlockwise - most guides say to go anticlockwise, as you reach Little World's End before World's End but we opted for the latter and didn't regret it at all - it's slightly easier as you get a flattish finish, and you also avoid most of the crowds - once we'd headed out the only people we saw for the first 4km or so were the quicker hikers heading past us (not sure why, this is the sort of place that deserves you take your time to soak in the atmosphere!) The early start was a killer at 4.30am, but seemed like a great idea now - the light is beautiful at that time of day and there's still the early morning frost on the ground and low-lying mist in the valleys. Baker Falls are nice (but no Iguazu!) and the views from World's End and it's little brother are great, but for me the real winner was the hike and the scenery - just magical at that time of day, and we felt at times we were no longer in Sri Lanka but maybe south America! While we didn't see much wildlife on the outward part of the hike we saw quite a bit when heading back after Little World's End - a couple of giant squirrels and a few purple-faced leaf monkeys enjoying a feed in the early morning sun - plus quite a few birds. The round trip is around 9km or so, but we took our time enjoying the journey. Very highly recommended if you're in Nuwara Eliya - indeed, probably the best thing you can do here IMO!

title: Nice walk early in the morning.
text: This place is good to go early in the morning, then we saw the most animals and it was not so hot yet. I left with a group from the Laughing leopard Hostel in Nuwara Eliya. The only downside was that we had to wait on one of the slower walkers.

title: One of the best things we've done in Sri Lanka!
text: Living here for two years I can't believe we have never done this before! It HAS TO be on your bucket list of you're outdoorsy, adventurous or just enjoy beauty in nature. We left Newara Eliya at 5am and paid and entered the park by 7am. The entire walk took us 3 hours and was stunning. You walk through so many different terrains and get to see stunning sights. I even saw families with young children managing the walk. You can choose to go right or left at the Y-bend after entering on the walk. We went left, which takes you to little world's end, then on to world's end and finally the falls. But you can go right and switch the order. I think we choose well as returning by the left route may be more difficult than via the right. Look out for the clouds covering the valley as you drive up the mountain. Magnificent!

title: Superb Morning Trail
text: Try to go early morning as you get good clear view of vally. Just carry suffcient water to keep yourself hydrated and where good pair of shoes. Once you are on Horton plains I dont think you need warm cloths as you get warm up as you keep on trailing. A must place to vist in Nuwara Eliya.

title: Challenging but worth it!
text: I’m not a morning person so the thought of setting off at 5am for a hike filled me with dread. A compromise was reached with my guide and we set out at 7am instead. My guide told me that the walk had to be done before 9am otherwise I wouldn’t be able to see anything due to the mists. Judging by the number of people walking back when I started the trek, their guides had told them the same thing! The walk itself was challenging but totally worth it for the views. The mists had indeed settled when I reached world’s end but a bit of patience and I was able to get the amazing views. There’s lots of native fauna to be seen on the way, keep an ear out for the monkeys. Tip: most people turn left to reach little world’s end first, I went straight to get to baker’s falls first. This meant the walk back, when absolutely shattered, was way easier and mostly downhill.

title: Pretty, but overpriced
text: The place is beautiful, with a few hidden gems around, worthwhile. But we felt that the entrance ticket was a bit overpriced.

title: Nothing special compared to National Parks elsewhere in the world and expensive
text: World’s End was an anticlimax, and we had good weather there. It is a good 9 km walk with varied terrain, scenery and views but nothing special compared with many walks in the UK’s National Parks and elsewhere in the world. Not worth the early start and high fees and getting there is not simple. We were travelling from Nuwara Eliya to Ella, so did the World’s End walk on the way. We hired a car and driver for LRK10,000. The Horton Plains NP fee for two people, plus the car and driver was LKR8,100. Apart from the first kilometre or so there is no sign of the money raised from foreign tourists being used to maintain the route. In places the path would become a watercourse after rain, luckily it was dry when we were there. I have no problem with foreigners being charged more than locals but the price charged should be reasonable and it would be good to see the money generated being invested in the site.

title: Wish we hadn’t bothered...
text: We should have heeded those who advised against doing this walk, particularly agree with all that Aaron and other gentleman below has said on this site. It’s a lot of money to get in, an hours drive to get there, and in fact we only saw deer outside the park. Guess it depends where you are from but we felt we could be doing a walk in one of our National Parks that is just as beautiful and free to all. SL needs to seriously rethink about some of these out of proportion fees for foreign visitors if they want to build tourism numbers.

title: Horton plains
text: We did the walk along Horton Plains to see Worlds end and bakers falls . It is worth getting there when the park opens at 6am as the walk can take a while and the clouds come in during the day. Wear sensible shoes as some of the walk is along a rocky path and it is not easy to walk along. You can see deer and lots of birds Well worth a visit

title: Wonderful scenery !
text: It was a very cool and windy place ! Required to bring wind breaker for the trek. Nice trekking. Nice scenery at the “world end”. Suggest to bring breakfast box and have it when you arrive at “world end” view point and continue to trek for waterfall.

title: Overpriced hike
text: 40euro for 2 persons is way to expensive for this. It is just a normal hike, Worlds end could be nice if your lucky, we had only clouds... I don't get where all this money goes to. There is only few staff at entrance and a worthless museum. No wildlife to be seen. Only saw some deer outside the national park area..... Better hiking to do in Ella for free.

title: Great views!
text: Wear comfy clothing and be prepared for rain! This place is a great place to walk, we walked up to World's End with it's amazing views and then around to Baker's Falls. Such a beautiful waterfall. This is an amazing part of Sri Lanka, the climate here is so different from the rest of the country. I can see why they call it Little England! We only saw some deer but still enjoyed the day and the fresh air.

title: One of the most awesome places in Sri Lanka
text: Youcan experience a different type of climate up there with different flora and fauna compared to other places in the coutry. World's end drop is just one thing visit within this amazing area.

title: deer spotting at horton plains
text: we arrived early morning to avoid the afternoon mist. we had to walk about 01 to 02 km from the entrance to get to the famous viewpoint where you could see an entire town from the top. it is advisable to stay of the edge of the cliff and avoid having any accidents as many people have fallen off this cliff.

title: Memorable Hike to the top
text: the best hiking experience in sri lanka. we visited nuwara eliya and then took the hike the day after. we started off early morning and it was amazing. we were able to spot deer, a leopard and migrating birds. wonderful experience.

title: A Trip we can never forget
text: We were in Nuwara Eliya, Small England of Sri Lanka (elevation 2000+ meters above sea level, average temp 12 degrees). We Started our trip early morning at 5.00 am which will take around 1 hour due to foggy road. It is 30 kms south of Nuwara Eliya lies the famous Horton Plains (2,100 m) sorrounded by mountain ranges. It starts about 400 meters from the Entrance Gate. Start off early and aim to get there before 6.30am for the best views over World's End, before the mist & cloud cover the area. Take the route that goes to mini World's End first from left. The hike takes about 3 to 4 hours, do not forget to bring water, snack, umbrella (in case if it rains) and wear proper hiking shoes. You will first reach to Mini World's End ( 2 Kms from Entrance). From Mini worlds Ends to Greater World's End is further 3 Kms. Further to reach Baker's Falls you need to Walk 2 Kms. On the way you will get a Public Toilet which is not very clean & hygienic with no water tap in it. Returning back to gate you will get to see Chimney Pool (1.5 Kms from Greater World's End. And at last to reach the Gate its 2 Kms In rain get muddy and slippery, especially when you go towards Baker's Falls. There is only one toilet in entire route inside the Park, so try to use one before you leave your hotel, or else at the entrance of the national park, there is a toilet. Ticket price is well worth it. Grassland plains, mangrove forests. There is a restaurant outside the gate were you can refresh yourself . We paid LKR 7,950.00 for 2 person incl all. for the entrance ticket.

title: High plains drifter
text: You need to set off early in the day to avoid the noonday sun and also find a parking space in this popular national park. The views are stunning but if you suffer from vertigo, I would give this a miss. Ground is quite uneven so ware good quality walking boots and be prepared for a workout!

title: One of the most fulfilling experience!
text: Park is easily accessible from Nuwara Eliya, you can choose from different kind of transports. On the way back you can also visit dairy firms. Park is one of the most pristine and serene natural parks i have visited till now. Took the worlds end and & bakers fall trek,which is about 9km hiking. Surprisingly they have well maintained washroom facilities inside the park too. Tips would be bring raincoats and a spare pair of cloths.

title: We enjoyed it alot, but get there EARLY!!!
text: we are two fit 20 some / 30 something year olds, in good physical shape, so this hike was a breez, a little tricky a a few points, near the Worlds End, but in general its mellow, and can be done by most. We saw small children, old people, fat people, and hundreds of locals in flip flops. So its not too difficult of a hike. We saw some deer, and alot of birds, but thats about it. Alot of good photos and if you sneak off the paths here and there you can find some even better ones.

title: Very beautiful trail
text: We were told to be there early, so we were at the park at 6 am (!). Still, the queue was long to buy tickets and entering the park. However, the effort was totally worth it, hikikg the 7km nature trail. The plains offered lovely views and so did the hot spots Worlds End and Bakers Falls.

title: Best guide for Horton Plains exploring - worth every cent
text: Mr Kaneel Rajanayeka is recommended in the Lonely Planet Guide and we were lucky our hotel's recommended guide turned out to be the man himself. While we could have walked the 9 km circuit by ourselves, Raja's expert knowledge of creatures, birds and medicinal plants made our day memorable and we learned so much. Plants used in Ayurvedic healing of arthritis, depression, even cancer, and ones which are still sometimes the basis of our western medicines, were frequently spotted. While the famous view at Worlds End was obscured by cloud, we finished the day feeling privileged to have experienced some of the Sri Lankan forest and plains. In addition he answered many of our questions about the wierd half of Nuwara Eliya town known as Little England". Raja can be contacted independently on E: nuwaraeliyatrekkingclub@hotmail.com

title: A not-too-strenuous hike, with plenty of wildlife and animals along the way
text: We enjoyed our trip to the horton plains and after completing the hike we did an afternoon trip to Ella from the Nuwara Eliya train station. The hike was stepo at some points (we did the "long hike" to world's end) but nothing that children couldn't manage. We saw a pair of chameleons and a lot of playful monkeys which was lovely and the whole hike took about 2 and a bit hours (we didn't walk to fast). However when we got to world's end there was nothing to see as the views were barred by clouds, so I would recommend if it was a noticeably cloudy day take the shorter route to save time if you would be disappointed if you did the hike and there wasn't any views (whihc wasn't the case for us as we loved all of the wildlife and scenery).

title: So many different reviews on this - yes it’s hard, but it’s worth it
text: Ok, so I’ll start out by saying I’m a pretty fit person (triathlete, trail runner). I read all the reviews before going and noticed so many different views from “nice flat and easy” to “really tough”. I ran the route, taking about 1hr 30 (I’m not a quick runner). For someone who doesn’t exercise regularly this would be really tough. But definitely give it a crack. Just know it’s not going to be easy and you need comfortable shoes. Saw so many people out there today in completely inappropriate shoes. I ran clockwise. I’ve read that anticlockwise is easier. Without having run anticlockwise, I think that would probably be right. But I guess it’s a loop. So there’s as much up as there is down, whichever way you go. But it’s so beautiful. I didn’t go with the intent of getting to World’s End before the fog came. Which is good, because I got there at about 10:15 and you couldn’t see a thing. But it’s still well worth doing as there are so many other views.

title: If tghey tell you there are inclines but no steep climbs - don't believe them
text: Disappointing. We are reasonably fit but were misled by being told there were no steep inclines. In particular there are stony areas where you have to climb up and down the rocks - harder going down in fact as it jars the knees badly. The view isn't great because you are on the top of a steep cliff and therefore can't see the cliff itself. Absolutely no guardrails or safety features before the sheer drop - in fact somebody had fallen to their death a few days earlier and, while w were there, a party of climbers came to recover the body.

title: Hike in the mountains
text: We did the round trip to see the waterfall and the worlds end. The entrance fee is a bit pricey for foreigners but that’s the way it is in Sri Lanka. You get some nice views and a glimpse of the nature here. If you are lucky and walk with open eyes you will see some animals.

title: must stay a night
text: you will must reserve a cottage in advance from forest department. there are cottages according to your capacity. great opportunity to see some wild animal next to your window. some of them friendly too..if walk thru the park will take five hour to complete. don't forget your water bottle.

title: Long Walk
text: If you're lucky, you may see wildlife....but there's no guarantee. We did see a rather rare buffalo during our ride (30 minutes before the park) but didn't see much once we began our hike. The path is well defined, and you'll see nice waterfalls. But I didn't find much that was appealing, evidenced by the fact that I didn't take many photos and was glad when the walk ended.

title: Get there early
text: We set off from Nuwara Eliya at 5am. We arrived at 6am and there was a que to buy tickets to enter. Tickets are relatively expensive but worth it. The whole walk takes about 2-3 hours including a stop for a snack. Please don’t wear flip flops! You will struggle without decent shoes as it’s not a pristine beautiful path the whole way. Views from ‘worlds end’ are stunning but you need to get to that point before 10 or 11am when everything clouds up.

title: A nice hike in the morning
text: Nothing special or unique about the park. It's just a park, fresh air, nice views, nice hike, after many days spent mostly in the car, going from one place to another.

title: You need to be surefooted
text: I didn't find this particularly taxing in terms of fitness, but there is a lot of picking your way over rocky and muddy paths, some quite steep. As advised we got there really early - make sure you allow about half an hour to queue for tickets, then drive the couple of miles more to the actual start of the trail (where there is a toilet and small cafe). You need to make sure you don't have any plastic bags, as they will be taken away at the gate, but plastic bottles are OK if the label is removed. It will be cold when you start (15 degrees when we left Nuwara Eliya at 5am, 12 degrees at the gate to Horton Plains at 6am), but once you start walking you will soon warm up, so only one extra layer is fine, and shorts would have been OK. We actually set off walking at 6.45. Shortly after the start you have a choice of which way round you go. We chose anticlockwise, but with hindsight, I think the clockwise route would have got us to World's End quicker. There is a map at the start, but few signs on the way. The terrain was tricky, with rocky paths to start, and a couple of streams to cross. It then got steeper, and much muddier, which slowed us up. Unless you've never seen a waterfall, don't waste time by diverting to Bakers Falls. It's good, but very much the supporting act, and you can always go back after you've been to World's End. We finally got to World's End at about 5 to 9, and were very fortunate indeed - literally within 5 minutes, the view had disappeared, the mist just rolling up the whole valley - quite a sight to see. So disappointing for anyone arriving after that, as there was nothing to see. The rest of the park is pleasant, but not spectacular. Further along the valley there is Mini World's End, but I can't tell you what the view would have been like! Once past these, the terrain becomes much flatter, apart from one fairly steep rocky path, and the mist doesn't encroach on the rest of the park. There's a toilet on the way back, on the edge of the hillside, open sided with a pretty decent view. I had walking shoes on, but on the way back we passed locals in flip flops!

title: A manageable walk!
text: As an obese person with a bad right knee and a recovering strained left upper thigh muscle, I was worried that I could not takÃ· on the challenge that was Horton's Plains, especially after reading horrifying reviews about it. Fortunately, all my fears were unfounded! Walking at a moderate pace, I found the walk entirely manageable though there were some tricky parts such as the rocky sections of the trail. On this note, do make sure to wear good shoes! We were also blessed as the weather conditions were in our favour. It did not rain the day before and neither did it on our hiking day. As a result, the paths were not very muddy and therefore easier to traverse. My friend and I, however, could see why the trail might be challenging should the weather be poor. A note on safety precautions to take, do not go too close to the edge of the cliff at World's End. According to our guide, a tourist had plunged to her death just a few weeks before our trip in an attempt to take a selfie. Some tips: 1. Check the weather forecast 2. It is preferable to have a guide since some paths may not be clear to the inexperienced 3. Bring some food and water 4. Do not bring plastic bags as there are thorough bagchecks before one enters the park 5. It is okay to bring bottled water into the park. However, do remove the plastic seal and label around the bottle before entering the park. 6. There are rubbish bins in the park. DO NOT LITTER. 7. Do not make too much noise as that might scare away wildlife. We had an unpleasant encounter with a group of noisy and rude tourists and had to ask them to tone it down. Do respect the environment and be comsiderate to others. That way, the walk will be pleasant for everyone! :) Overall, I enjoyed the trail as the views were lovely and it was certainly good exercise!

title: There are more tourists than animals
text: The entrance is very expensive comparing to sri lankan entrance prices and to the experience. We saw elephants. The crocodiles were too far in the water the birds are little and there were too many jeeps. I expected to see more species

title: Elephants...
text: This is a fairly large park within which several companies offer game drives. We booked with Niluka Safari, who were very good. Once in the park, the terrain is quite open, with small plains and the occasional watering hole where animals will congregate. Mainly, you'll see elephants, lots of them which is great, and they'll get quite close too. There are also lots of birds that your guide will spot and point out to you. Others to look out for - the occasional crocodile, land monitors, wild boars and some deer. Altogether, you'll get a good safari experience.

title: Excellent Safai with Lahiru
text: We found Lahiru's details from Trip advisor and booked a private safari with him via Whats App (+94762726799), we were not disappointed and saw lots of elephants. He was a great guide offering a private tour in spacious raised jeep. The tour was not rushed or limited on time, we finished when we wanted to rather than set time. Went off the beaten track away from other jeeps. We had time to view a family of elephants (with babies) on our own without 5 other jeeps fighting for the best spot for pics. Arranged pick up and drop off (this is extra to the safari, ask p for a quote).

title: Udawalawa National Park
text: A game drive in the afternoon is very exciting. Lots of elephants and many other animals and birds to see.

title: Humbling experience
text: This was a great park and to see elephants,crocodiles,lots of different species of birds was just amazing. Baby elephants being protected by the adults. This is a good conservation park and well worth a visit. Our guid was great and we had a vehicle to ourselves.

title: Awesome time in national park with Lahiru
text: I found Lahiru via his numerous good reviews on TripAdvisor. We paid €100 for me, my wife and my son for a tour. I can see why Lahiru has lots of good reviews. He was an excellent guide and really made the effort to make sure we went to places where there were not so many other jeeps (couldn’t believe how many Jeeps there were on the day!). He was polite and answered all our questions and also gave expert advice on the animals we observed. Highly recommend ??

title: Great Safari
text: This is an excellent park. Our driver was well informed and a good communicator. We saw many wildlife from exotic birds to crocodiles. The best however were the single elephants to the large heard. This is a must do trip.

title: Well managed national park
text: The big draw here is the abundance of elephants. However there is so much more to see, not least crocodiles, monkeys, birds and if you are lucky leopards. Only downside is the number of tours in operation which can at times lead to congestion which makes you question why you are there at all as it feels like we humans are intruding.

title: Natural setting to see magnificent creatures
text: Apart from having to get up at 3am for the drive there the day was well worth the effort. The guides were all very friendly but driving around the bumpy roads of the reserve in the back of a pickup truck safari car was uncomfortable. We saw all the animals from families of Elephants to Monkeys crocodiles water buffalo wild bore and many more. The visit to the Elephant orphanage at feeding time was my highlight. About 6 babies at a time let in running grabbing the pipes of the feeding tubes in their mouths to get their funnels of milk was magnificent to witness. Highly recommended.

title: Amazing safari with Lahiru
text: We enjoyed an amazing safari experience with a private guide called Lahiru. He organised everything for us- our transfer from Ella to the National Park, where we had our fantastic 4-hour safari, and our transfer on to Mirissa. During the safari Lahiru was very knowledgeable and enthusiastic- it was great to have a guide who clearly loved and respected the animals, while making sure we had an incredible safari experience- it was clear he wanted to give us the best experience possible! There are quite a lot of jeeps in the park but Lahiru managed to bring us places to see animals in secluded areas with no one else around where we got closer than we could ever have imagined to lot of animals including elephants- our highlight!! We got some amazing photos and memories to last a lifetime. We would recommend booking Lahiru if you are looking for a guide for the safari. (We contacted him directly on +94 76 272 6799)

title: what a park
text: i had an amazing day at this park...if i may recommend an early morning trip, not only to enjoy a beautiful sunrise in there but also to avoid the queue at the entrance. from what i understood from the driver, they allow only 30 cars per hour...excellent idea actually and it works really well...good variety of wildlife from kingfisher birds to elephants...highly higly highly recommended

title: Fabulous
text: This is a well organised and very enjoyable location to visit. The vehicles that take you around are extremely well maintained and comfortable, giving you an extremely excellent view of the park and all its wildlife. Amazing sites, like seeing a nature documentary from the TV. Drivers are helpful & knowledgeable, stopping at locations that will provide all you would need to see. Cannot recommend this place highly enough, a fantastic day out. Absolutely stunning.

title: Very beautiful park
text: We had a 3 hour tour booked for 3500 one way a other at the arrival point we got a tour guide in our Jeep . It’s low season so was not to busy with the jeeps only 50 in front of us before we went into the park a bit of a problem is there are only one person selling the tickets that a bit of a hold up , if you can take a tour guide with you they have a lot of power to get traffic going again when you see elephants. We saw a lot of animals and birds in that short period

title: Amazing Elephants
text: We had a great day out driving around the park. There are a variety of birds and other animals to see but the elephants are the star attraction. We went around 3 PM and spend around 3 hours. There were plenty of elephants on the lake side and it was possible to get a good view of them. We had a private driver take us from Unawatuna and back again on the same day. The drive each way was around 2.5hours. I would suggest staying overnight closer to the park and avoid driving as much.

title: Take this safari, not the Yala one...
text: This was our first safari in Sri Lanka...our driver was very good..he stopped as long as we wanted to see the sights and animals...he never rushed and we hardly saw any other jeeps. It was an amazing trip and loved it....we went to Yala after and were so disgusted byt the actions of the drivers, and surrounding the elephants ( one with a small baby) not giving them any space...definitely go to a smaller known park as there are hundreds of jeeps at Yala ...Uda walawe was fantastic,,!

title: Loved the morning safari
text: It was wonderful to see so much wildlife in its natural environment. We didn’t see many elephants but the ones we did were very close so it was really special. Our driver and guide was great in pointing out bird life and other wildlife.

title: Lahiru Jeep Safari Tour
text: We had a perfect day in Udawalawe National Park, thanks to Lahiru who organized everything from A to Z: he sent a driver who picked us up at our hotel near Tangalle, drove us to Ella afterwards and then back to our hotel. The safari was the most incredible experience in Sri Lanka so far! We saw a teenage male elephant bathing himself and were only a few metres away, four female elephants and one adult male elephant... Besides the elephants, we saw crocodiles, hyenas, different kinds of birds and chameleons, mungos, deers, wild boars and probably more. Almost everytime we were completely alone, not one other jeep was there besides us. When we arrived at the lake, we were the only ones seeing about ten crocodiles, elephants, birds and hyenas at once. Lahiru knows all the roads and places and seems to suspect which animals will be where and when. This made this trip so special. He is also a very funny guy and cares a lot about the park and the animals. Thank you a lot for this unforgettable trip. See you in Cologne... Katja + Halil You can reach Lahiru via Whatsapp or phone: +94 762726799

title: Beautiful safari, but also a lot of plastic rubbish
text: A beautiful park with a big (men made) lake. Around the lake are many kind of animals. Mainly birds and elephants. We had a afternoon drive and have seen lots of elephants, birds, crocodiles and many more. I would recommend going here and there are several places to stay close to the entrance of the park. You can arrange your safari right at the entrance by hiring a driver, car and guide and pay for the entrance fee separately. Or you can arrange a package via your hotel. The downside of the park is the plastic rubbish people leave in the park. I really can’t believe this is happening and not be cleaned by the authorities in a national park. I hope the local people will understand some day the importance of a clean environment for nature.

title: Great Safari
text: Great Safari, we saw family of baby elephants, monitor lizards, peacocks, pelicans, water buffalo, two types of monkeys. Well organised through Kalu’s Hideaway. Definitely recommend.

title: Fun place to Safari.
text: My wife and I just did a Safari here and it was pretty amazing! We had a great driver that our guest house booked for us (Mansala safari resort), which I highly recommend. The view from the small private Jeeps can’t be beat! You’re mostly going to see lots of elephants and some very close up. We saw a ton of wildlife on our 4 hour evening Safari. No lines to get in for the evening safaris so that’s a plus and the sunset doesn’t disappoint either. Yes, there’s lots of other Jeeps around as well. Yes, once there’s elephants spotted there will be other Jeeps around, especially at the bigger watering holes. We also got to see plenty of elephants and other wildlife with nobody else around as well along the drive. There are some leopards in the Park, but we did not see any on our outing. I’d definitely recommend this to anyone interested in the wildlife of Sri Lanka. It was a super cool experience. We saw, elephants, crocodiles, buffalo, peacocks, tons of birds, monkeys, a few monitor lizards etc...

title: Safari with young children
text: Left our accommodation at 5.30 in the morning and had to queue to buy a ticket for our group. Children up to six are free. Initially felt a bit like a traffic jam of jeeps but they go different ways and it then got much better. Had a wonderful moment with a group of female elephants with three babies arriving at a water hole to wash and throw dust on themselves. Lots of buffalo, birds, and several crocs. Spent over three hours driving around the bumpy tracks which was enough for the 2 year old. Worth a visit!

title: Lots of Elephants
text: We visited this park as part of a G adventures tour of Sri Lanka. We used Mahoora to provide us with an afternoon drive to see the animals. This park is known for its large number of elephants (approximately 600). We saw about 40 different elephants, some water buffalos, peacocks, a jackal and some other types of birds. It was nice to see the elephants because I didn't get to see them in Ghana.

title: Awesome safari with Lahiru! +94762726799
text: Today we had a safari with Lahiru which was really excellent, he sorted everything out, including picking us up & dropping us off after the safari, with no extra costs on the day. We saw so much wildlife, Lahiru has super powers to spot even the smallest animals and excellent local knowledge so you see the most. It seemed we were always in the right place at the right time and mostly away from all the other safari jeeps. We saw so many elephants, including some babies, crocodiles, monkeys, water buffalo, spotted deer, and many birds. Lahiru speaks excellent English and is very knowledgeable and friendly. So glad we did our safari with him! Highly recommend, his WhatsApp is +94762726799

title: Fantastic safari with Lahiru!
text: My husband and I booked an early morning Safari with Lahiru, a guide we had read a lot about and he really was excellent. His knowledge of the bird life was superb and we came away having seen so many new species of birds we were amazed! He also helped us with the photography of the birds. We also saw wonderful wildlife and the whole experience was just amazing. Lahiru is a very knowledgable guide and a lovely person and you can contact him through WhatsApp. + 94 76 272 6799 - you won’t be disappointed!

title: Uda-wowed-me!
text: We had a great morning on safari at Udawalale National Park. We got picked up from our homestay (Falcon’s Nest) at 5am and waited in the queue. Lots of drivers like to go nice and early to get in quickly - the animals are better in the morning & you usually see more. The sun rising as we travelled through the park was amazing. We saw so many elephants - one came so close that our guide had to reverse! We also saw crocodiles, water buffalo, wildcats, jeckalls, peacocks (hundreds of them!) and lots of other birds. Unfortunately no leopards for us but as there are only approx 15 in the whole park, it’s very unusual to see them! We barely saw any other jeeps throughout our 3.5 hours in the park and were able to watch the elephants so peacefully with only one other jeep. Highly recommend Udawalale if you’re wanting to see elephants :) Booking through your hotel/homestay is the best option as they tend to have a guide they use. You can also visit the Elephant Transit Home after and see the elephants being fed!

title: Wonderful evening safari in Udawalawe National Park with Lahiru.
text: Great evening safari with Lahiru- if you would like to experience a safari away from the crowds this one is for you. We managed to see about 9 baby elephants and clocked 38 different bird species. We were collected from our accomodation in a timely manner, our group of 3 had a wonderful time after booking a private safari on WhatsApp 94762726799. Our group has been on safari before in Africa and were slightly worried about the crowds but Lahiru managed to position us away from other jeeps, also of concern was animal welfare as a veterinarian but was most impressed by him “ saying it is their place not our place” and respecting the space of the elephants.

title: Great experience with Lahiru
text: We spent this morning at Udawalawa National Park with Lahiru as our guide. Myself, husband and young daughter (nearly 3), we had the jeep to ourselves. We saw more than we could have hoped, various types of birds, deer, mongoose, monkeys, crocodile, water buffalo and elephants up close. The best part was when we were by a small pond and waiting for a herd of elephant to come over, including 2 babies - we were the only ones there, it was very special. Lahiru is very knowledgable and can spot all types of animals from far away, he knows the park very well which meant we were never close to other jeeps. He’s also great at getting photos! It was very special , and our daughter loved it. It was perfectly safe for her. highly recommend Lahiru. I organised our tour very easily through WhatsApp +9476 272 6799

title: Not to miss; beautiful experience and very nice place to sleep
text: .The national park was so much more then we would’ve expected! Lots of encounters with elephants, up close!, jungle cats, fat crocodiles, monkeys etc. The safari in an open jeep was arranged by our accommodation; Mansala Safari House. Speaking of which. Do yourselves a favour and stay at this place. Close to the park in an elegant house. The comfort level was super high. Beautiful room, quiet airco!!! and the bathroom... shower outside, boutique-style, looking up seeing the palmtrees. In the morning, sitting on the veranda and being spoiled with a lovely breakfast served by the owner Tiron. Tiron deserves a medal, by the way. My husband forgot his sunglasses in Hiriketya and Tiron was sort of in the area and made the effort to drive there just to pick up the sunglasses. What a hero. Long story short. Do the safari? Yes! Stay at Mansala? Very yes!!!

title: Wonderful elephants in their natural surroundings
text: It was a lovely day out in the Udawalawe National Park. We toured with park in a jeep with a driver and English speaking guide who was great at spotting eagles, other birds, animals and of course the elephants which were wonderful to see so close up. It was a great experience and I would highly recommend a visit.

title: Safari
text: Lovely area with lots of elephants, plenty of rare and exotic birds. Best time early morning before the heat comes.

title: Elephants galore
text: After reading reviews on TA we decided to take a safari. We simply WhatsApp Lahiru, who has been mentioned many times & he made all the arrangements. A driver picked us up from our Villa, we switched into Lahiru’s jeep at the entrance, did a 4 hour ride around & then back home. It was quite a long day with lots of traveling. We found him very informative & had a keen eye to spot thing we could never have seen. We seemed lucky in that we saw so many elephants all over the park, including 1 week old calves who could barely walk in a straight line without falling over. Also plenty of birds, buffalo, lizards, a few crocodile, red spotted deer, monkeys & giant squirrels. The tracks around were rutted in places but that’s to be expected. The jeeps everybody seems to use are clearly up to job & make for a great experience.

title: Magical Safari with a superb English speaking guide Lakshan
text: We were staying at a fairly newly opened local hotel: Royal Reach Family Resort (1/2hr drive from the National Park) and their lovely staff helped us organise this unforgettable 3 hour long safari in their hotel jeep. They also promised to get us an English speaking guide who turned out to be an absolute expert on all the wonderful creatures (and plants!) to be seen there. We picked him up at the entrance of the National Park and with our guide on board our safari was off to a great start. Lakshan is a volunteer guide and he turned out to be a real expert. He worked closely with the driver to take us away from the crowds into the heart of the park, spotting herd after herd of elephants, filling us with exciting facts and anecdotes about each animal encountered along the way: peacocks perched on top of tall trees, gorgeous birds of all shapes and colours, lizards and buffaloes. Lakshan has a very extensive knowledge of the fauna and flora of Udawalawe Park and he is a skilled educator, too, He taught us how to recognise different species, how to tell the age and sex of the elephants, His enthusiasm for this place was contagious. Lakshan is also very patient so throughout the trip we had plenty of time to take fantastic pictures without being rushed. The three hours we spent with him exploring the national park were the highlight of our Sri Lankan trip. The whole safari for two people was about $60 including the jeep, entrance fees and a voluntary contribution to our guide! I cannot recommend him highly enough. If you would like to contact Lakshan - you can find him on Facebook: Lakshan Geeganaarachchi (he was the guide for Prince Edward- Earl of Essex and his wife when they visited Udawalawe last year!). He is brilliant!

title: Fantastic trip with Lahiru
text: Just came back from a really great trip to Udawalawe National Park with ace guide Lahiru (WhatsApp +94 76 272 6799). It was our first Safari, so perhaps a little inexperienced but we felt blessed to see a variety of wildlife and have an amazing up-close encounter with several Elephants. Lahiru was a friendly, knowledgable and considerate driver who took extra care ensuring the safety and comfort of my pregnant wife and two year old daughter. Highly recommended!

title: Overhyped and unorganised
text: Highly unorganised. The information centre is so further away from the check point that people are easily fooled by the safari guides standing before the check point. The guided tour are very bad we constantly asked the driver for information. Pro tip- the real rates are given inside the information centre which is further inside the check point. There are only a few elephants, buffalos, crocodiles and very few birds. Don’t waste your time and money on this.

title: nice to see
text: the Jeep was comfortable but when we arrived at the entrance, around 30 other Jeeps where waiting and when the Gate opens all go at the same time and you need to be at the beginning... otherwise its a big cloud of sand :-) we saw not that many animals but it was quiet ok. it might be that 10 Jeeps are standing around 2 elefants and the nearest Jeep remains there for a long time so you often can't see them nearer. It's peoples egoism :-) i think best to go there would be in the morning maybe you can then see more animals, but the landscape is nice too

title: GREAT PHOTOGRAPHIC OPPORTUNITIES
text: This is not like a safari in Africa as predators are few. Many of the park's secrets were revealed over a 3H safari. The birding is very good, bee eaters posing for you. The elephants steal the show. We had herds eating grass and crossing the road. At the end of the day there were three elephants, one a baby, drinking at a waterhole; epic stuff. The water areas produced their own attractions, from crocodiles with open mouths to cormorants drying their open wings to lounging water buffaloes. The roads are in fair condition with just a bit of dust to be expected. The park is largely forested with areas of bush. Any number of companies will take you for hopefully what will be as good a day there as I had.

title: Travel from afar it is worth it
text: A well run game park where your driver knows the terrain and will find you much to enjoy and photograph. Top Tip: If visiting in the afternoon make sure you have a cap or bush hat to shade the eyes

title: Well worth the visit plenty of wild life
text: We really enjoyed our visit to Udawalawe Reserve. We had a good guide and driver and we saw lots of wild life.

title: Safari with Lahiru Prasad
text: We had a fabulous safari in Udawalawe with Lahiru. He picked us up early from our accommodation in a van to avoid the bugs in the Jeep on the way to the national park. The Jeep he took us in was very comfortable and he provided us with snacks for the ride. His eyes were amazing and he was able to spot animals from far away! We had a great day and saw everything and more than what we came for! Thanks Lahiru. His number is +94762726799

title: Amazing place just pick your tour well
text: Our first safari experience and we really enjoyed it. I would say to make sure your guides are good as ours was awful, we got no information other than pointing to the animals and naming them- wow. (Don't know the name but booked through capital lanka/ BH lanka). But this didn't ruin the experience and seeing the elephants in the wild was wonderful. The first hour was quiet we maybe only saw 2-3 elephants, peacock and a land monitor. But when we went to the clearing by the lake there was 10s of elephants, birds, spotted deer, water buffalo, a crocodile in the distance, painted stork, and a mongoose. Make sure you take water and suncream with you and maybe a snack too as a large part is of course waiting around to find the animals. (Most of the cars we saw are covered but depending on time of day the sun still comes through the sides). The timing was right for us at about 3 hours, we knew a day tour or several days wouldn't interest us so great taster and amazing to see these animals in the wild.

title: To save
text: When I went to visit the Udawalawa National Park, they blocked the road at a place where Udawalawa safari vehicles were and forced me to pay 300 dollars for the safari. I got rid of them and went to my accommodation and then they provided a car for a very reasonable price. Don't be fooled by those who block the road as you go

title: Lahiru - the best safari and guide in Uduwalawe
text: We had the most amazing couple of days in Uduwalawe in February, mostly because of our amazing guide Lahiru!! We managed to see Elephants, Monkeys, Crocodiles, Buffalo, Peacocks and even Golden Jackals, Land Monitors, Chameleons, Eagles, Kites and much more! He was so good at finding lots of different animals and wanted to make the Safari as amazing as possible, even letting us use his binoculars! He also helped us find accommodation for the tour at Wild River Side, which was very clean and comfortable and the host made lovely food! We would 100% recommended Lahiru for a tour as he is extremely knowledgeable, kind, funny and helpful! Lahiru’s number is +94762726799

title: Highly recommend Lahiru’s Safari! Best experience
text: We had a safari with Lahiru (+94 76 272 6799 - WhatsApp) as a group of friends and can’t recommend it enough! We saw so many animals and he really took us away from the other jeeps and off the beaten path to find them, making it feel so much more special! He even helped us take amazing photos of the animals as we only had iPhone cameras. We were picked up and dropped us off as part of the service, there was a driver as well as Lahiru as a guide which was a lot better than just having a driver as he was able to spot animals and wildlife better. We all had such a wonderful day and would recommend a safari at Uduwalawa National Park to anyone :) (especially with Lahiru!!)

title: Solo Travelers Discriminated Against
text: Entry fees skyrocketed about 2 weeks ago. Solo travelers pay $43USD, which is about $7USD more than two travelers entering together and so on ($43USD for individuals vs $36 USD if you're a couple). Also, as a point of reference the current entrance fee for Kruger National Park in South Africa is $27USD. $43USD is an extremely high entrance fee for any National Park in the world. I know there's a cost savings on vehicles when you share one, but a solo traveler penalty is ridiculous. I tried to find people at the gate entrance to share a safari with. Many of the tourists were interested, but the guides have a "mafia" type "wilderness association" and refused to let any tourists share costs. Was it worth it? Maybe once. Well, when others described "herds of elephants" in their reviews, I was expecting herds, like in Tanzania, Kenya or like other places in Africa. I believe herds in Sri Lanka means families of elephants, which numerically speaking are smaller-- maybe 5 or 6 in a family vs 10+ in Africa. There is a good variety of wildlife-- elephants, deer, monkeys, buffalo, crocodiles, mongoose, jackals, boar, peacocks and other birds. It was nice. If you're interested in going, I eventually went with the owner of my homstay, Nalaka, +94 77 635 8192. He took me on a 4 hour jeep safari for 8,500 rp. He was great at spotting birds baby elephants, and other wildlife that other guides who denied me didn't see.

title: Fantastic experience with many elephants to see!
text: A truly awesome place! It's a huge and beautiful place, yet small enough to cover in two hours! A big win when you have kids or don't want to spend hours driving around looking for animals. I've never seen so many elephants in my life! Our tour guide was fantastic, very knowledgeable and helpful. We forgot something in the car, so he came the next day to Tangalle to give it to us. Very cool of him! (Lahiru +94 76 272 6799 - very much recomended!)

title: Amazing experience!
text: Within 5 minutes of entering the park, we saw a herd of 10 elephants bathing just 10 feet from our jeep. We were mesmerised. It was such an awesome experience.

title: Excellent 6hr safari with lahiru
text: Had an amazing 6hr safari experience with Lahiru. He prepared delicious breakfast for us to enjoy in the jeep. The pick up and entrance to the park was smooth. We would definately recommend his services. He was well priced, punctual, polite, considerate and a good communicator. He has a deep knowledge of animals and plants and answered all of our questions. His ability to get away from the crowds gives you a unique experience with the animals. We saw so many animals and more elephants than we could count. I would thoughly recommend booking with him. Lahiru +94 76 272 6799.

title: An excellent park
text: I was quite surprised, the terrain was quite like many African safaris we have been on, clay roads, very uneven in parts but very picturesque. Places you would like to stop and just wait to see if any animals cross your path. In addition to elephants, and we saw many, there were spotted deer, sambar, crocodile, jackal, water buffalo, lots and lots of peacocks in display and many other birds. Elephants were single males sometimes but also several large family groups. And nice picturesque spots to just sit in quiet and wait to see if anything passes out of the bush. Our guide from Induwaru Safari Resort where we stayed was exceptional. Care was taken when driving not to disturb animals, plenty of time allowed for viewing to our requirements, effort obviously put in not to follow the crowd. Breakfast was taken on safari, sandwiches, egg, pancakes, fruit juice and fruit. A mobile breakfast better than many we have been served in the accommodations.

title: Extraordinary with Mansala Safari
text: We had an incredible time in Udawalawe – in large part because we booked with the incredible Mansala Safari Resort. Whether staying in their beautiful hotel or just taking their safari, we can’t recommend them enough – they’re one of the best choices I’ve made while travelling. Mansala basically arrange everything – safari, binoculars, transit, entry to the national park – and you pay at the end. It was one of the cheapest options we found but also one of the best. Tiron’s guide Tharanga took us on our safari. Like Tiron, he’s locally born and a genuine animal lover. He did everything the guidebooks tell you you’ll want in a guide – he was respectful of the animals, never crowded them, avoided hotspots full of other drivers, gave us information without overloading us, and showed us everything. We saw: - A herd of baby elephants - Crocodiles - Water buffalo - Lots of deer, including stags and, essentially, bambi - A family of wild boar, including 8 gorgeous little piglets running about in what my partner called ‘the best thing I’ve ever seen’ - Lots of birds, including peacocks, storks, different types of eagles, woodsand pipers, little green bee eaters (really beautiful), cormorants, lapwings, hoopoes - A surprise tortoise - Surprise mongeese You can do an evening or morning safari, or both. We did an evening safari, which finishes before 6pm; we arrived at 2pm and went straight out onto it, which was more than enough time. The hotel itself is a lovely family-run operation, with two rooms and the family living in the building. Despite the homey, personal feel, everything from the food to the rooms to the safari is of the highest possible standard. Food is cooked by the family, eaten on the veranda with animals around – and is some of the best we ate on our trip. Eat there rather than going out into Udawalawe. The room was one of the best we stayed in in Sri Lanka, despite often paying significantly more than at Mansala – beautiful, comfortable, well-equipped, modern – everything we needed. Tiron, who runs the place, is a really kind and generous man. He was born in the house you’re staying in, knows the local area really well, and was one of our favourite people we met in Sri Lanka. When the driver he’d booked for our 2-hour drive to Mirissa was suddenly unavailable, he took us himself. His number is +94 77 795 9090 - he's given us permission to share it, and is very responsive to WhatsApps. If you want a really ethical, personal, kind experience, we can’t recommend Tiron, Tharanga and Mansala enough. We had a really special time, with really special people.

title: Safari Guide
text: My wife and I chose Lahiru as our safari guide for Udawalawe National Park. He was amazing!!! We highly recommend him. He was very punctual, and picked us up at our hotel right on time at 5:45am. He communicated with us immediately after we messaged him via WhatsApp (+94 76 272 6799) prior to the tour and we discussed what we were looking for in the safari tour. He provided exactly what we hoped for - an amazing wildlife tour of the park in the routes that weren’t busy with other jeeps. He was very knowledgeable about the different species of all animals in the park and how they compared to other species abroad. He answered all of our questions on the tour. He showed us all of the best places in the park and allowed us to enjoy and take in the park environment and nature. He was the best safari tour guide we have ever used. We highly recommend him - he was professional, courteous, and knew the park and it’s wildlife so well. He is the best!

title: Even a full day isn't enough !
text: So many birds, so many animals - such beautiful sceneries... Parakeets zoom by in flocks, loudly screechig. I loved every single minute in the park. Try to go for a full day. Once past 10AM, you have the park to yourself.

title: Amazing Safari
text: Me and my wife had the most amazing safari experience this morning. We arranged it with Lahiru (+94 (76) 272 6799) the night before - he organised transport from Ella for us and took us on an incredible tour of the park. The driver he arranged was there on time and drove very carefully to the National Park. The safari itself was awesome - Lahiru was a great guide - giving us lots of useful information about the animals and spotting some hidden animals mere mortals would never see! In total we saw 20 elephants, water buffalo, spotted deer, jackal, peacocks, lots of different birds, monkeys, monitor lizards, a mongoose and much more. Would not hesitate to book again with Lahiru and well worth the money! For anyone wanting to know the trip took about 1 hour 45 from Ella.

title: Awesome tour with the very best guide!
text: Before our first holidays in Sri Lanka we tried to get some information and tipps about a game drive in the Udawalawe National Park. One name appeared again and again with only very excited positive reviews: Lahiru (Whatsapp +94 76 272 6799). We contacted him about 2 weeks before our trip and booked a Safari (1/2 day). We were very curious - is there a difference to other guides? Well, the first difference was: he even helped us to organize a driver who picked us up in after our train-journey in Ella and brought us to Udawalawe, which was very herpful. Yesterday we had our Safari with Lahiru. He picked us up at the hotel at 2 p.m. and then ... the whole afternoon was just AWESOME and OVERWHELMING!!! Lahiru is a very good Jeep-driver who really knows the park and all it's hidden paths. Most of the time we didn't see any other safari-jeeps (while many others were driving in small convoys on the "main roads") ... but therefore more animals than we expected to see! Elephants - of course (once we were lucky to stop close to some elephants an after some minutes we found ourselfs in the middle of a herd - and buffalos, deers, some crocodiles, gold-jackals, mungos, 3 differend types of eagles, ... and lots of birds (pelicans, toucans, bee-eaters, peacocks, ...) and even the fresh trace of a leopard. It was ... NO WORDS! Lahiru knows a lot about all these animals, his eyes seem to see everything while he is driving - it was perfect. He can also name some of the animals in German. I can recommend him as safari-guide without any doubt! And don't forget to visit the elephant-orphanage. They take care about orphants from outside the national park and set them free in the park when they are grown up. You can watch the feeding - cued! Very affordable and definitely worth it!

title: Most competent guide for the National Park is LAHIRU
text: We booked our tour in the park about 2 weeks before our holiday in Udawalawe. Many travellers on tripadvisor recommended Lahiru as the most competent guide. And we totally agree. He is very aware of the smallest signs of animals. Birds, lizzards, mungos and even footsteps of a leopard in the sand..he sees it all, while driving his huge car safely and carefully over the bumpy road. He led us to places, where no other car was seen and we had the honour to see about 35-40 elephants..even 2 babys. We didn't drive in a konvoi and it seemed, that every time a car came close, we took the other way. So we had the opportunity to take fabulous pics. It was such an amazing experience..I'm still speechless and will remember this for the rest of my life. The park itself is such a gorgeous place..peacefull and quiet. You can hear so many sounds of nature. We would have liked to take a rest at the lake for a couple of hours to just sit and enjoy the scenery. Next time Sri Lanka we definitly will come back and make a visit. You should too and definitly contact Lahiru, he is very reliable and even organized a driver for our next destination. His number you can contact with Whatsapp is: +94 762726799

title: Great tour with bathing elephants thanks to our guide Chaminda
text: We had a fantastic morning with Chaminda in Udawalawe National park. We saw lots of elephants (including babies) but also crocodiles, monitor lizards, water buffalos, monkeys (macaques), golden jackals (and more) and lots and lots of birds and even eagles. We can definitely recommend asking Chaminda to be your guide: very kind, good English and he is a very good spotter! Call Chaminda: +94773379470

title: Fantastic experience with Lahiru
text: We found recommendations for Lahiru through TripAdvisor and he lived up to the expectation! Friendly and so knowledgeable.. He found so many animals.. Spotted tiny birds etc. He took the time to take us out of the main area so we weren't surrounded by other keeps and we saw more animals. We got cold water and snacks and had a fantastic time. Finished the trip off seeing a tiny baby elephant and it's mother. Was amazing! Lahiru. What's app: +94 76 272 6799

title: Quiet park with plenty to see
text: We just did one afternoon safari here and we were lucky to see iots of elephants as well as plenty of birds, a crocodile. If you want to se leopards then Yala is certainly better but there are more visitors so sometimes you do not get to see animals due to number of vehicles, to an issue here

title: My tour
text: Lahiru was a amazing man,, as a tour and a guide he is was also excellent!! He has the eye of a eagle he can spot a animal from a 100m away no mater how small!! He even spotted a lizard in a tree that no man should of been able to see!! We saw so many animals crocs, birds, wild cats, deer, so many elephants! title: Udawalawe Park with guide Lahiru
text: Based on the reviews from tripadvisor, we hired Lahiru as our guide. Using his Whatsapp number, i booked the trip ahead of time. He had arranged a Toyoto mini van to pick up and drop us from Mirissa. Very comfortable van. For the park, there was another big van customized for the Safari. We saw elephants really up close and peacock dancing. Overall, good experience.

title: Great place for a 3hr safari trip
text: This is the park to be if one wishes to see elephants. We also saw lots of birds, some deers, primates a dead deer being devoured by a crocodile, buffalos and enjoyed a nice ride. Would recommend doing it early in the morning as it wasn't crowded (about 12 jeeps or so in total).

title: Brilliant safari
text: We went early to get to the front of the queue which I would recommend. We were there at 5:30, the park opens at 6:30 and were the third jeep in. We saw lots of elephants, crocodiles, deer, buffalo, birds, lizards etc. It was excellent and when we spoke to other groups we were lucky to see so much. Go early and be ready to run when the ticket office opens.

title: Amazing Safari with Lahiru Prasad
text: Lahiru took us on the most amazing Safari at Uduwala. I got his recommendation on Trip Advisor and he did not disappoint. We saw all sorts of birds, water buffalo, monkeys, crocodiles and elephants, lots of elephants. He seemed to know all the best spots in the park and also was very knowledgeable. He would position the vehicle for better photo opportunities. We saw 3 separate groups of elephants with babies that came within feet of our vehicle. Plus many more from a distance throughout the Safari. Lahiru seems to really enjoy the animals and making sure you have the best experience. I contacted him through email which he always replied promptly Lahiru.jpdk@gmail.com Or WhatsApp +94 76 272 6799

title: Great wildlife, however...
text: Amazing wildlife. We saw a lot of elephants, peacocks, crocodiles, eagles, storks, bee eaters, a jackal, kingfishers and a lot of other birds. However, we thought that some og the jeeps drove too close to the elephants, stressing them. We arranged the safari through our hotel, and our drivers were respectful. We also thought that the people travelling only two in one car could have gone together to minimize the number of jeeps

title: Awesome Safari
text: We took a 3 hr Safari booked through Viator with Bentota Travel. Bentota Travel is another story so i'm not going to say anything about that. We arrived at the reserve after going to the elephant sanctuary and transferred to a Jeep. Access to the jeep required climbing in through a narrow gap at the back of the vehicle while standing on a Beer crate!!! Not easy for a couple of portly nearly 60 year olds, but it makes for a good story afterwards!! We engaged the services of a guide ( they do not charge as such, you just tip them at the end of the safari what you think their services were worth) I would thoroughly recommend getting a guide. We didn't know where to look and the driver is too busy keeping his eye on the track to spot for you. In the end it was so worth having him as he was able to point out Monitors, Lizards, and birds that we just wouldn't have spotted. We saw wild buffalo, jackals, numerous colourful birds and birds of prey, Turtles, Lizards, Monitors and Loads of Elephants. We were lucky enough to see a family group of about 10 elephants along with 2 week old calf, a couple of smaller family groups, numerous single elephants (Including one asleep leaning against a tree!), but the highlight was a Mother and Calf pair who crossed the track in front of us and went to the lake edge to drink. They then proceeded to bathe and play in the water. At the same time, they were surrounded by buffalo complete with storks standing on their backs (I kid you not!!) All in all, an amazing 3 hrs and some of it quite emotional. We didn't seem to drive for more than a couple of minutes without seeing something. We did however meet some Landrovers with tourists and guide who had been in the park for 2 hrs and hadn't seen anything more than a couple of birds. i think we were extremely lucky and we happened to drop on a good guide who knew his stuff. Amazing Experience. P.s. Getting out of the Jeep was much easier, I went out through the front Drivers window!!!!

title: A super safari in the PARK1
text: We took a three hour safari arranged by our hotel. We were very fortunate to see over thirty elephants around the tracks that we took. The vehicle is comfortable but the road is extremely bumpy. Many birds to see too! The driver and the guide are well versed in how to spot the animals and we were not disappointed; crocodiles, water buffaloes, cranes, eagles, owls, and the elephants! What a thrill. The safari cost is around $40 USD plus the entrance fee of $25USD for each person. Money taken in helps run the facility so great value. The more elephants protected the better. There are over three hundred elephants in this park. Don’t forget to tip your guide and driver - about 1000 rupees each.

title: Elephants and Peacocks
text: it was our first safari so my review might be biased. we saw a lot of elephants and peacocks and a few other birds. the park seems to be well maintained and drivers seem to be following rules and there seems to be a general respect for animals so all in all we had a good time.

title: park with elephants
text: The park has mainly elephants to see, make sure to book your car with a proper agency it should cost around 3600 RP for 2 + the entrance 7800 for 2 don't book at the entrance or you ll get scammed. A bit sad to have all the cars harassing these beautiful animals though... the price to pay for the protection of this place ...maybe

title: Unforgettable Safari with Lahiru
text: I booked myself & partner in for an 8 hour tour of Udawalawe which we visited today, we choose Lahiru Prasad as our guide on a friends recommendation & TA reviews & booked him via Whatsapp (+94 76 272 6799). The National Park itself has amazing scenery, lagoons, bush & jungle along with lots of wildlife. We saw many different bird species including hawk, horn bills, fish owl, hummingbird, bee-eaters & jungle fowl, along with crocodiles, spotted deer, chameleons, mongoose, monitor lizards, wild boar and a pack of the rarely spotted golden jackal! We also saw 30 Elephants, solo males & herds of females along with 2 babies, one of which was only 2 months old. Most of our elephant spottings were just us alone with no other jeeps around, we were able to sit with a herd of females & baby eating grass around the jeep for over half an hour! Without sounding like an advert this was 100% down to Lahiru, he knows the park very well & took us on different trails to find the animals that other jeeps weren’t on. He’s super knowledgeable about all the animals & answered any questions we had & managed to spot animals other jeeps with just a driver were driving past & missing. As it is also mating season the male elephants were quite difficult to approach, despite this we felt very safe & confident in Lahiru‘s Jeep. Over the 8 hours Lahiru was still stopping & showing us things until we left the park, being so close to the elephants was an unforgettable experience, thank you Lahiru & driver & Udawalawe National Park! Lahiru also took us for a proper local curry afterwards & organised a very well priced taxi on to Ella for us!

title: Very good - even for a non animal lover
text: Set off from hotel at 6am just as dawn was breaking. Fabulous view of trees against lightening sky. Couldn’t get a pic tho as driver going too fast. Arrived at the park with what seemed like a lot of people. But dubious at first we were going to be in one long traffic jam but the groups soon separated and we had the place to ourselves- mainly. Saw elephants very close up, lots of birds including eagles, water buffalo, deer, monkeys and a crocodiles nose ??. The ride was bumpy but we felt safe. The drivers are excellent at spotting things to see and are very patient. The best bit for me - sorry all you animal lovers - was a lake we stopped at. Gorgeous view of trees silhouetted across the lake. Some beautiful trees in the park too. Very worth the time and effort imo. Beautiful place - very unspoiled.

title: Highly Recomment Lahiru
text: I don't even quite remember how I found out about Lahiru (somewhere on Trip Advisor), but I'm so glad we did. I contacted him via WhatsApp literally two days before our safari, and he was immediately responsive and available. Our driver (for the 9-day itinerary -- not Lahiru) was a bit nervous about us using a safari guide he was not familiar with, but after a quick phone conversation, Lahiru put our driver/guide's mind at ease. Lahiru met us early in the morning and brought us a box breakfast and water. The safari was just my husband and I, which was wonderful ($100 USD). We were able to spend time on the animals of interest, and forego animals that were of less interest to us. He extended our safari by an hour so we could see more elephants (we had seen only a handful prior to the extended hour), and courteously called our driver/guide to ask "permission" to take us for the additional hour. Everything about the safari was professional and enjoyable. I would absolutely recommend Lahiru for safari.

title: So many elephants
text: We may not have had the most comfortable jeep (ripped vinyl seats that scratched the back of our legs) or informative guide ( our chauffer/driver who was accompanying us throughout Sri Lanka spotted more animals) but this became irrelevant with the number of elephants that we saw throughout the park. title: Great Park
text: Safari in this park was excellent - we saw more than in Yala. Good keen & passionate safari driver made for an excellent visit. Lots to see! Don't expect Africa - it is very different - but still very good!

title: Up Close and Personal with Elephants

The highlight was watching two young male elephants playing together and at times they got quite energetic and rough (like alot of young boys). An excellent safari - highly recommend.

title: A Daytrip with Lahiru
