We saw about 46 differen birds. Buddhi played on his bamboofluit, what gave a beautiful sound over the water. I had a great experience and like to recommend this eco birdwatching absolutely. Thank you Buddhi for the wonderful time and the woodapple juice!

title: Fantastic guided tour gently drifting on a boat
text: The tour lasted about 2.5 hours starting at 4pm in the afternoon. Our guide Buddhi was brilliant, very knowledgable about the local bird life, a good communicator and excellent spotter. We really enjoyed the calmness of this tour gently approaching the birds by boat only hearing the wildlife, the paddle dipping into the water and our whispering. We saw over 40 different birds and learnt a lot in the process. We are now able to spot and identify about 25 ourselves. The setting and landscape was also wonderful. Thank you Buddhi for such a great experience.

title: Bird watching, photography, boat tour
text: We had a lovely tour with Buddhi at dawn. The trip was great and we saw many bird species, Buddhi’s knowledge of birds was really good and he helped us learn and identify many species. He was keen to help us learn and gave a really good service. The boat ride was also really beautiful on the lagoon. Thank you very much for a great experience!!

title: Fabulous, peaceful visit
text: Passed a couple of hours here out in a catamaran on the lagoon. The birdlife is spectacular and our guide was very knowledgeable and great at spotting the birds too. We spent a couple of hours here, very restful.

title: A fabulous experience
text: After a drive into what felt like the middle of nowhere we were greeted by Buddhi at 6 in the morning and headed out for a very enjoyable two and a half hours out on what was a millpond smooth estuary. You could see that Buddhi loved what he was doing and was passionate and knowledgeable about the bird life in the Kalametiya. This was one of the highlights of our trip to Sri Lanka and we wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it to anyone.

title: A wonderful experience - serene, beautiful and informative
text: This is a must do for nature lovers visiting the Tangalle area. The lagoon is vast, beautiful, peaceful and full of life. We spent a leisurely couple of hours being expertly guided on a noiseless catamaran and saw lots of different birds. Even without the natural interest this is a lovely thing to do just before sunset - a stunning experience.

title: great view and lots of silence
text: paddling down the quit river was pretty nice.we may not have seen a lot on the first halve of the tour but near the end the sanctuary really started to come to life.pelicans,darters,herons,a stork or 2,godwits,spoonbills and ibisses.really worth it

title: Superb tranquil lagoon teeming with burdlife
text: How delighted we were when our hosts at the charming Asha Beach and Spa accomodation, Tangalle suggested a dawn visit to the lagoon. The guide is excellent and does a great job pointing out the birds. An unexpected treat was a little treat of cookies made by his mother. This experience is highly recommended and you do not have to be a twitcher to enjoy.

title: A great afternoon relaxing in the sun
text: We loved our afternoon with Buddhi drifting around the bird sanctuary and spotting the local birdlife. Buddhi was such a smiling, happy and welcoming host, and he made a special effort to keep our children entertained too. Thank you!

title: Don't have to know birds well to enjoy it
text: My wife and I don't have much of a combined knowledge of birds, but we figured "why not?" when our hotel offered the tour. We had read about the sanctuary, and we figured it would be a neat experience to see something like that. The boat ride was really peaceful, and the guide was very sharp at pointing out various birds and some monkeys. There is an absolutely plethora of birds, quite the variety really. I don't remember how long the whole trip was, but we were out for a while, and I think we saw a lot more than we imagined. My only regret was forgetting my lens that zoomed in much closer.

title: Beautiful unspoilt lake
text: A lovely trip on the lake with our young, but well informed and enthusiastic, guide. So many different species of birds to be seen. Bring your camera if you have one. Buddhi has a powerful pair of binoculars which allows you to get the most out of the trip. We went at the end of the day and watched the sunset from the middle of the lake. Go now whilst it is still so beautiful and unspoilt.

title: Best tour of our trip!
text: All the glowing reviews are true!! Many tour operators almost make you feel obliged to write them a TA review as they get some bonus from it; but I’m writing this review solely because Buddhi does such a fantastic tour and is truly deserving of all the praise. We were a family of 2 seniors, 2 tweens and 2 adults doing his morning tour. We only saw one other boat out on the lake and about 40 birds. Buddhi provided us with quality binoculars to use which thrilled the kids to no end. He has eagle eyes and can spot so many birds, even one 12cm one from our boat! Biscuits and water was provided which was great as we were hungry by midway having set out so early. Extra fun included in the climb up to the rock top. I’d do this tour again when I revisit Sri Lanka!! Don’t miss it!

title: Beautiful tranquil bird spotting
text: After rushing around Sri Lanka it was wonderful to have a few hours floating on the lagoon with such a charming knowledgeable guide Buddhi. We saw 48 different species of birds and were provided with water and biscuits. Just perfect.

title: highlight of our trip
text: Buddhi is a delightful young man who has realized that UK visitors love birds and so he has become a local expert. You drift around this amazing lagoon with his expert guidance and we saw around 50 species in 2 hours. Even if you aren't a birder it is fantastic. You get to wade through the water and muddy pools( not compulsory!!) and climb a huge rock from where you can see for miles. Eagles, bitterns,kingfishers, darters, sunbirds, herons, lapwings, Jacanas etc. Make sure you follow his directions for arrival as it is a bit tricky

title: Lovey
text: Beautiful trip around the sanctuary, saw monkeys, fruit bats, loads of birds including eagles! Very calm quiet and relaxing

title: Amazing tour
text: We went on the morning tour with Buddhi and his colleagues and it was AMAZING, definitely a highlight of our holiday in Sri Lanka. We were really impressed by Buddhi's knowledge about birds and love for nature. Plus, it is a beautiful national park, very peaceful and full of wildlife. I highly recommend this tour, you will not be disappointed.

title: Great tour in stunning nature!
text: We did the tour yesterday morning with Buddhi and really enjoyed it. Buddhi is a very kind and funny guy and really well trained in spotting birds no matter how far they are away. We could hardly turn our heads that fast :) But at least we saw 55 different species and even 2 rare ones, as Buddhi told us. It was a great experience in a stunning surrounding and Buddhi has a very detailled knowledge of all the different birds in that area. He even brought two very good binoculars and bird books with him, which really helped us during the tour. Overall the tour is very recommendable! Thanks Buddhi for doing that tour with us and being very patient in explaining the positions of the birds, even we couldn't see them always directly... ;)

title: Fantastic Experience
text: A really great tour and fantastic value for money. Kalametiya is beautiful and very tranquil, and we saw a huge range of different bird species. Buddhi is an excellent guide - very knowledgeable about the birds, extremely enthusiastic and adds lots of nice touches.

title: Beautiful, Idyllic & great Fun!
text: This trip was booked as part of my ‘special’ ?? birthday treat. Whilst being gently punted around a vast wetlands by 2 lovely boatmen we saw an abundance of birds, water buffalo & the piece de resistance- a Water Monitor Lizard!! Buddhi’s knowledge, enthusiasm and passion for this place is incredible. Buddhi’s extra touches like a bouquet of water hyacinths & garland of water lilies were very special. We also enjoyed some very welcome fruit and water provided by our team. With Buddhi’s ‘eagle eye’ & the provision of binoculars we saw species of birds we would never could have imagined! Who knew there were so many types of Kingdisher! After punting through the mangroves & passing lounging water buffalo we then embarked onto land to scale a rock. We paddled barefoot through the beautiful Water Hyaciths and then with Buddhi’s expert guidance & skill (and nerves of steel!) we climbed the immense rock barefoot!!! The panoramic views from here were breathtaking. THANK YOU for adding some incredible memories to my birthday ???? This tour is an absolute MUST DO if you’re visiting Sri Lanka. It’s suitable for ALL ages and will open your mind to a world of tranquil, beauty and nature at its absolute best. Book with Buddhi - you won’t be disappointed ??

title: Tranquil magical punting adventure through lagoons and mangroves!TRULY ENCHANTING!!
text: 6.30 sunrise punt silently past bathing buffalo, glide through water hyacinths and if you are lucky observe a giant lizard asleep in a tree.Leave the boat to wade through open meadows and clamber a rock for 360 degree viewpoint of mangroves, lagoons and sea.This trip is NOT just about BIRDS if you enjoy boating trips appreciate a variety of landscapes and want to view nature in its morning glory then this is the trip for you.If you are a bird enthusiast you will be in your element! The guide is english speaking knowledgeable and enthusiastic.We saw so many different species of Sri Lankan birds, so colourful compared with our own birds. I took so many stunning photographs, a truly memorable trip. DO IT! Worth every penny our guide was so passionate about his job and this enthusiasm ensured the trip was full of awe and wonder for his guests. Thank you so much Buddhi Priyankara the trip was greatly appreciated! The trip lasted about 2 and a half hours.Awesome trip and highly recommended!!

title: A must do in the south of Sri Lanka!
text: We had a really wonderful time with Buddhi on his boat. He does his job with so much passion and we could feel that at every moment during our cruise in the stunning lagoon. Even though it was raining we were lucky to see around 45 different birds, all spotted through the binoculars that Buddhi had offered us. It was great to get all the interesting information about everything we wanted to know and Buddhi really made an effort to make it a truly amazing experience for us. We would highly recommend it to everyone who is keen on seeing many beautiful birds in a peaceful landscape and just relax a bit outside of the busy beach. It is definitely worth to do!

title: Fabulous
text: This bird sanctury is well worth a trip, lots of birdlife and serene being paddled on lagoon by informative guide

title: Highlight in Sri Lanka
text: Buddhi’s enthusiasm and knowledge of local bird life make this an experience not to be missed. The variety of birds is something special and Buddhi incorporates lots of little surprises to ensure you have an unforgettable outing. It is so peaceful out on the water, the trip is excellent value and even for non bird enthusiasts this is a wonderful way to spend a few hours.

title: For Any Bird Lover
text: The owner young Buddhika and his friend Ushan are excellent on the subject. We were able to see and photograph a variety of birds with their help. Being on the paddle boat made all the difference as there was no noise of a motor which I thought was very environmental friendly. Buddhika's reed music while on the boat was enchanting and made the evening even more beautiful. That was not all! They got us to climb a rock! It was hilarious as we struggled up and down on our fours! This activity (bird watching) is a must if you are spending an evening in Hambantota.

title: Great experience
text: We took a sunrise lagoon tour with Buddhi. Such a peaceful, relaxing experience and unlike other Sr Lankan wildlife tours this really was just us and the birds. Buddhi's amazing spotting skills ensure you will see upwards of 50 different bird varieties, his knowledge and enthusiasm make this a very enjoyable experience. Amazingly beautiful place, go now before it gets discovered! (Just one complaint, Buddhi is a terrible judge of age, don't let him guess yours!)

title: Bird lover's paradise!
text: We did the tour with Buddi on 16th Jan and it was one of the highlights of our two week trip. We were staying in Tangalle at the time and had been tipped off by our driver about Kalametiya being much better than Bundala National Park for seeing birds as you can get much closer to the birds. Buddi was also recommended to us as well, and his tour does not disappoint! We saw 53 species of birds in total, and as Buddi has an encyclopedic knowledge and great eye for the birds of Sri Lanka, you'll be sure to get to see plenty! It just depends what nature has in store for you that day! Buddi has binoculars if you don't have your own and he also carries field guides with pictures for reference. You'll get to climb a small rock for scenic views, and you'll actually see some different birds whilst you're on foot. We saw a very low perched shikra on this part! The freshly sliced watermelon and bottled water was also a very nice touch, expecially as the morning temperature starts to rise. We also did a quiz back at Buddi's with a glass of fresh wood apple juice, which is well worth trying if you get the chance! Overall, a very calm, relaxing morning tour in beautiful scenery, with plenty of birds to see as well as Buffalo and sea/land monitors. If you're really lucky, you'll also get a flute solo from Buddi, a man of many talents!

title: Wonderful
text: This place is a must see for all nature and birds lovers, you can really watch many many different kinds and unbelievably beautiful birds in natural environment. Slow and silent move of the boat does not distract you or any birds so you become a part of the mother nature life in this area. Buddhi was delicate and passionate about birds, he answered all the questions we had, and even more. He's dedication and passion are really inspiring. I thank him for this excursion and safe and interesting path to the rocks. Wood Apple drink was also great before and after the trip. In total we saw 44 of 141 birds and a Buffalo. Cheers, - Vova

title: Fascinating, tranquil tour
text: We spent a magical afternoon drifting on the lagoon with Buddhi and his crew. We saw at least 30 species of birds, the nests of weaver birds, and storks in flight. This is a lovely tour, and very different from the other things we have done in Sri Lanka.

title: Best tour so far
text: The tour was excellent, Buddhi could identify so many birds and was very knowledgeable about them all. It’s his hobby and you can tell he loves what he does. We even saw water buffalo and monitor lizards as well as so many beautiful birds. It’s the highlight of our trip so far.

title: Great place for birds watching
text: Great experience watching birds in the lagoon with very friendly and knowledgeable guide. We took the afternoon (3:30pm) tour and it was quite hot but no doubt worth it

title: 100% recommendable bird watching tour and more
text: We loved the bird watching tour experience in Sri Lanka. The guides, Buddhi and his friend, are highly motivated and competent, we were sitting on a little paddle boat without engine :) and could observe 50 different species of birds in the picturesque lagoon. In the evening we even saw a flock of water buffalos on their way home. Sunset was beautiful there too. It's totally worth doing the tour!

title: amazing guide (Buddhi), amazing bird sightings
text: amazing guide (Buddhi), amazing bird sightings. took a 2 hr long boat ride and saw around 40 species. Buddhi has a passion for this. Great experience

title: 50 species of birds!
text: Our trip with Buddhi and his uncle around the lagoon was peaceful, productive, and enjoyable. He is a knowledge and personable guide. He helped us identify 50 species of birds by checklist. Highly recommended.

title: Bird watching at it's best
text: My girlfriend and me got this tour with Buddhi as a present, everything perfectly arranged from Germany. The 3h trip was stunning and fascinating. We saw 50 different birds, big & small, fishing and chilling. We also saw wild monkeys and climbed a rock in the end. Our guide was outstanding nice and good knowledged. His crew was really friendly and in the end he played so nice songs on his flute for us. Never forget this trip, thanks so much.

title: Stunning place
text: We went around late afternoon and the light was fantastic as the sun slipped away.A beautiful unpolluted place just to see without the birds but birds there were in their scores putting on a majestic display....well in other words it were proper good!

title: The bird watching was such a wonderful experience & so much more.
text: Such a beautiful location & so serene. It is well worth doing. We were there at first light in the morning & saw so much bird life. Our guide (Buddhi) was fantastic & his knowledge was invaluable.

title: Amazing experience
text: During this peaceful tour we saw 40 different species of birds. Our guide had so much knowledge and could spot and identify birds instantly! My mum was talking about the wood apple fruit and Buddhi was so kind and invited us back to his home (nearby) for a fresh glass of wood apple juice! We felt so welcomed and are thankful for the kind hospitality and great experience.

title: Excellent afternoon if birdwatching in this stunning location
text: This was an extended family tour of the south coast including birdwatching in Yala and Bundala parks. Despite having seen a good number of wetland birds already we managed to clock up a few more on Buddhi's highly enjoyable excursion round the beautiful lagoon at Kalimatiya, handy to walk to from our hotel (Turtle Bay). Even if you are not a bird watcher this is a relaxing and interesting trip which we would highly recommend. Buddhi and his colleague who steered the boat provided us with a great insight into the wetland area and he has an enthusiastic love of the area as well as good knowledge of the local wildlife. Booking and communication with Buddhi was excellent and efficient. If you are in the area and you enjoy the scenery and bird life in this special environment contact Buddhi and let him take you in his unique tour!

title: Joyous
text: This is a peaceful, simple and affordable afternoon out if you’re on the south coast. We knew nothing about birds and were mostly looking forward to the time on the boat and the views. We got all of this plus new knowledge of about 40 species of birds. Our instructor was so keen it was infectious. Highly recommended.

title: Truly unique experience
text: This trip was definitely one of the most beautiful, pleasant and inspiring experiences during our wonderful stay in Sri Lanka. While perhaps a little bit off the beaten tourist track this is also what makes this trip so special. It was a quiet and almost meditative experience accompanied by sounds of nature - no engine involved. To enjoy this trip you don't have to consider yourself a bird watching specialist. We are not at least, but have a general interest in nature and wildlife and we saw a lot of interesting birds on this trip. Our guide was so nice and enthusiastic and even helped our kids climb a rock to view the sunset. Thank you Buddhi!

title: Wonderful tranquil trip around a peaceful lagoon.
text: You do not have to be a twitcher to enjoy this wonderful 2 hour experience of tranquility. Mahesh our guide was very knowledgeable and friendly pointing out over 40 different species of bird along with monkeys and water buffalo. Thank you also to the gentleman doing the hard work punting us around the lagoon. A must do.

title: An out of the world and time place
text: Our Sri Lanka tour finished by three days in Ranna and we discovered this bird place into our guide book. We did visit many birds places and wanted to see this one but we did not expect much. Thanks to Buddhi who organized a tuktuk pickup from our hotel we arrived on time for an almost three hour tour starting from 3:30 pm. After having a refreshing fruit juice in Buddi home place we started the visit. We boarded on a small boat with our guide Buddi and a boat paddler. Once on the boat we crossed the laguna and entered into another world. We saw hundred of birds. They were everywhere. Overall we saw 47 different birds species. as well as buffalos, varans, monkeys. The sunset on the water with birds on the back of water buffalos was outstanding. You could stay a whole day in this paradise where the time seems to have stopped. The laguna is wide and very quiet. You will listen only the birds music and the sound of the water made by the paddle. Buddhi is a bird lover and he is a pationate person. He is dedicated to nature and birds. He made this visit the best birds watching we never had. We were amazed by the amount of birds we saw. Most of the time in these kind of visit you see some few birds very far away. Here you are surrounded by birds. They are everywhere just few meters away. You do not need expensive camera with long focal lenses to take nice birds photos.Surprisingly a small fish attacked by an heron jumped on the bench on which I was sitting and it was not a flying fish. My wife, who is not mad of birds as I am, came with me and was not expecting to discover such an amazing place. She went in love with the beauty and the peacefulness of the laguna. The end of the trip was accompanied by the music played by Buddhi on his flute and this added a 48th bird to our visit. We warmly want to thank Buddhi for permitting us to discover this magical place. If you are in Tangalle area this is the place you have to visit.

title: Excellent experience from booking to drop off
text: We booked this trip after searching on the internet once we arrived in Sri Lanka and were not disappointed it really was excellent value for money . Saw many groups of elephants at various locations . It was busy but 2 parks currently closed due to flooding so all trips having to use the Eco Park so it was to be expected . Roshan was a great driver / guide trying to get the most out of the experience for us . Would go again in a heartbeat, fabulous to see these great animals up so close

title: Amazingly close to elephants
text: This was an amazing experience, we got very lucky with the weather and in the middle of a monsoon got a few hours of sunshine. You get so close to the elephants it's unbelievable and they don't seem bothered at all, they continue grazing at their own pace even with the little ones around mum. Most of my photos are on my camera so excuse the selfie! The guides are really knowledgeable about the wildlife and stop, wait until you have your photo and then drive on again. Be careful when you go up the watch tower as there are some snakes chilling up there but their only small and didn't even move when we went up

title: Great experience
text: Although it rained while we were on this excursion it was still a fabulous experience. We saw heaps of elephants and were given plenty of time to watch and photograph them. Open keeps were great...until the rain came, our drive put the cover over quickly - although we got wet we still thoroughly enjoyed it.

title: From here to there and everywhere
text: Roshan is an excellent driver and safari guide. He ensured that we saw as many animals as possible on our safari. He was ethical and respectful when seeing the animals, stopping at a distance. We had a great time. We also had him take us to Ritigala and Polonnaruwa. Highly recommended.

title: Spectacular vidit
text: At first we arrived in a jeep and there were so many other jeeps, but once you get going and they take you to where the elephants are, it’s breathtakingly spectacular! To see these animals in their own environment and eating, playing, fighting and babies feeding from their mums.. an absolutely unforgettable day!

title: A must do tour
text: Amazing tour, excellent driver and tour guide who had amazing sight into picking out the birds, lizards, golden jackal, crocodile, deer, monkeys giant squirrel and of course the wonderful elephants who walked between the cars. Very informative re the flora, highly recommend this tour, once in a life time exoerience.

title: Amazing Herds of Elephants!!!!
text: As we entered we saw single elephant...went further another single elephant our child was getting more curious our guide said wait will show you more in hundreds...and as we entered main Jungle we could see Hundreds of Elephants with Baby elephants and we were Happy but we need to be careful as they can aggressive..we also saw some birds...

title: The Highlight of my Visit to Sri Lanka ????
text: Wowee! We joined an elephant jeep safari on the very first day our holiday and it was truly the best experience I could have had. Having loved elephants all my life this trip was heaven. Of course, there were lots jeeps, tracking the roaming elephants and it did seem intense at first, as we were so excited at trying to spot them in the vast reserve. But we finally came across a group of 50+ elephants grazing with their young and we did not disturb their peace. It was wonderful to watch them so close up. I will never forget this experience.

title: Elephant safari
text: Just absolutely breath taking to see such beautiful creatures roaming freely and so up close, never seen so many elephants.

title: Good trip
text: We did the elephant safari and enjoyed it immensely there where lots of elephants and monkeys, it was very rough terrain in places so beware if you have back problems. The trip was probably 3 hours and maybe a little to long in the afternoon sun with no toilet breaks . All in all very good

title: Just too many trucks
text: It's a great place to go, but unfortunately the way the "safaris" are run is that almost everyone goes at the same time and it's just a massive scrum to see anything. The amount of trucks and people simply spoil the experiance. Save your money, go and visit an elephant orphanage instead.

title: Always a Risk
text: We had a fantastic experience on our 2.5 hour safari - we saw several herds of elephants, a bull elephant, a pregnant elephant and a baby elephant. We even saw an elephant with a tusk which isn’t very common in Sr Lanka. The driver was great and the vehicle comfortable. This had been pre arranged by our tour guide so I’m not sure which company we went with but we started at a hotel called Cinnamon Lodge. Obviously there is always a risk you might not see the elephants... but certainly one worth taking.

title: EXCITING ELEPHANT SAFARI PLUS MORE
text: What an exhilarating experience, riding in jeeps where you can stand up and take your photographs or enjoy the ride. Spotted so many elephants, up close and a bit too personal at times. Saw baby calves playing chasing after birds. Loved this experience but the highlight was seeing an eagle take off, swoop diwn only meters away and snatch up a rabbit.

title: Herd of Jeeps
text: We went mid afternoon to see the elephants ‘in the wild’, and it was wonderful to see so many family groups around the park. Apparently they just over 100 there. The disappointment was the quantity of jeeps surrounding every sighting, jostling for the best viewing position. Whilst they kept on the tracks, and , frankly, the elephants pretty much ignored them, it seemed a distraction from what would otherwise be a wonderful opportunity to marvel at these magnificent animals. The park needs to be careful not to ‘kill the goose’ by overcrowding.

title: Saw 14 day old baby elephant ??
text: Saw 3 different large female herds including a 14 day old baby elephant on our 90 min safari Lots of birds too Open top jeeps that you can stand throughout to get views - very dusty so wear sunglasses to prevent dust in your eyes Over 50 jeeps operating so it’s not an intimate experience but very enjoyable non the less

title: Vacation
text: A very good safaris. I would saw we saw two Tuskers and 46 other mother elephants and babies. This is so worth the time and cost. A must do adventure.

title: Never expected a safari in Sri Lanka
text: Fabulous experience, seeing the wild elephants so close up. I think there should be less jeeps allowed in at one time as it got very congested in the park with so many jeeps around the herd

title: Highlight of our trip
text: It was the highlight of our trip and we saw more than 200 elephants. We got close enough to the elephants and it was truly a treat. It is important to have a guide who cares about the elephants (ours did) so that he can direct the driver to park his jeep in a place that will not intrude too much in the elephants' space. I did feel like the elephants were stressed by all the human activity so as visitors we can try to mitigate the stress by not insisting we get too close to the animals.

title: For The Love of Elephants
text: We took the Jeep safari tour to see the elephants, unfortunately it was not the season to see big gathering but we were able to see some here and there, the jeep can get pretty close to them so you can take your time to enjoy the experience.. it was also a nice trip for bird watching, we were able to see amazing birds. The whole tour was about 2.5 HRS for a convenient price too.

title: Absolutely the best place to see animals and birds, without too many jeeps
text: Observe elephants on mass in social groups, and many animal species. Important to get an experienced driver/guide, as our driver arranged, as some are disrespectful to the animals, and do not have enough knowledge.

title: Lots of elephants
text: Nice wildlife park. We saw lots of elephants, water buffalos, water birds and a cow just gave birth in front of us!!! Worth doing!

title: Not many Elephants when we were there!
text: Nice jeep tour. Not many elephants were there and too many jeeps going all at the same time. At one point there were traffic jam in the National Park. Didn't like that all the jeep leaves at the same time, no spacing out. Taking pics were a rush to get the best shot. Lots of dust while driving in the open top.

title: not to miss
text: we loved this park although in theory it does not compare with Yala in the number and quality of animals that can be seen. But the Jeeps are open, and photographing is easy, and in the end we saw a lot of buffalo, deer, and even some elephants... although the latter are elusive. Worth the experience.

title: Amazing experience!
text: Went on a safari to see Elephants and we saw loads. They were upfront and close and herds of them. We saw male ones, 2 week babies and so many...The safari is bumping and they remove the roof so you can stand and see. They do give you a volunteer tour guide with your driver which we weren't made aware of so you need to tip them if you get one or they can get very upset! Overall a great experience.

title: Elephants, elephants and more elephants
text: We went in the afternoon and got to see lots of elephants, walking eating splashing in the lake and best of all baby elephants playing chase with birds. It's hit an miss what other animals you see, we saw lots of owls, Eagles, peacocks and a bull.

title: Our Driver cheated us for money
text: our driver cheated us for money. before we enter to the national park the driver said we need to take a tracker with us in the jeep. for the tracker he asked money 5000lkr but inside the park when we were talking with our tracker he said his price is only 2000. the driver took the rest of that money.

title: no vehicle after a payment
text: we confirmed and requested a jeep with a driver at 2.00 p.m but i did not came we hat to arrange another jeep from hotel it was little expensive in the hotel thats why we ordered here. cannot recommend this to other travelers

title: Great experience
text: Promptly picked up from our hotel. We went to kaudulla National park from Sigiriya. Best to go in afternoon because most elephants there then. Driver and companion good at spotting animals although not much English spoken/info about animals. Saw crocs, eagles, peacocks, buffalo and 40+ elephants. Lovely to see these animals in the wild. Got very close to the elephants too. Dropped us in Dambulla for little price too!

title: A must do
text: Anyone visiting Sigiriya must do the safari at Minneriya. Sighting of the wild elephants is almost a certainty and it is an amazing experience.

title: A good mix of off-roading & animal spotting
text: The tour team made a good job of making the trip to the water hole to watch the elephants fun & engaging by making the trip feel like an off road experience - this was particularly effective in the rain! When we got to the lake, there were plenty of elephants to see, along with buffalo & a variety of birds. A very pleasant afternoon.

title: Elephants!
text: Great safari with loads of elephants, the babies are especially cute. Beautiful birds- storks,pelicans,stilts to name a few and of course peacocks. Water buffaloes were plentiful too. Shame it rained but it didn’t dampen our expectations

title: Simply breathtaking
text: This place is breathtakingly beautiful, we saw so many beautiful birds, elephants, water buffaloes, monkeys, big lizards... the area is stunning - it completely blew me away, unbelievable, we had such a good time here. There were hardly any other vehicles here when we went - and if we did pass a vehicle it was all done with smiles and a chat. An absolutely wonderful place - I would completely recommend a visit. Our teenage children had a fabulous time also (always a good sign).

title: Superb way to view many birds and animals.
text: We had a private jeep tour around the national park. It was stunning! At one point a huge iguana wandered across our vehicles path and there were two types of monkey around as well as dozens of types of bird - everything from the tiny brightly coloured Bee-eaters hovering by flowers to the massive storks standing unmoving by the waters edge. Our driver was excellent at pointing out ones we would have missed - also showing us nests etc - really knowledgeable and interesting. He never made us feel that the time was limited as he shared his obvious love of the wildlife. We skirted around two separate groups of elephants - one of some 40 animals and the other of 60+ animals - what a glorious sight! All ages of elephant - even tiny babies. What a privilege to see in such close up that binoculars were not needed. Would certainly recommend this. It was quite expensive as it cost us 60 Dollars each.

title: Good safari ruined by the basic lack of care.
text: The experience itself was good and there were many animal sightings. Elephants, water buffalos, all kinds of birds - nothing much to complain about. However, the experience was tarnished by the old and VERY dirty jeep. Its was all covered in red dust and just a few minutes in it was all over my clothes. I had to cancel some of my other plans to go to a hotel and change. The problem could have easily be solved by a little bit of care and cleanliness. It isn’t that difficult to wash the jeep once in a while.

title: Best time ever !
text: This safari was by far my favourite moment of Sri Lanka. There were hundreds of elephants which made the visit quite a spectacle. The only small problem was there was about a 30 minute queue to enter the park.

title: full of elephants
text: its great to see so many elephants along with that many jeeps in the middle of jungle. it start bit slow and once you reach there its fun and exciting to see hundreds of elephant together. its bumpy ride, so be prepared for it. we were just one couple and we were charged $80, but the jeep can accommodate 6-7 people so even if they charge more for one jeep it will be cheaper per head.

title: Lots of elephants
text: It’s amazing how many elephants, wild birds including herons, eagles, storks we saw. A couple of crocodiles too. Lovely, respectful driver who spotted everything for us and stopped for photos every time. Well worth a visit. You see more in a couple of hours than any other safari I’ve been on.

title: Hundreds of them!
text: The initial stages of the safari are slow going but once out into the plains everything changes. It is stunning aesthetically regardless of whether the elephants are grazing there or not. If they are however prepare for a melted heart because they're pretty freaking adorable.

title: Average at best
text: Compared to the African safaris this attraction is dirty and dusty and overpriced. Yes the elephants are glorious at the end of the bumpy ride but not really worth the price. Additional sightings were one monkey and one bird !!! A visit to Pinnawala is a much better hands on experience. Give this place a miss

title: Fun and very interesting
text: We have done safari in Africa so went to this with very low expectations. But it was surprisingly very fun. There were little baby tuskers who were bothering everyone in the herd. Such fun watching them

title: Best Safari Choice
text: If you want to see the wild life in srilanka (elephants, birds ...), this is the best place. It is smaller than Yala national park, and has much to see. In less than 10 min from your start up, you will meet around 40-50 elephants and other species, but elephants are majority in additions to oxes. The difference from Yala national park is that you do not wait in the jeep to start your safari, and you see the wild life in less time. Advise you all to go to minneriya and remove yala park fom your list, as we wait around 3 hours to start our safari there, and was not worth it.

title: Elephants in zoos VS elephants in the wild - no competition.
text: The Jeeps bring you up to almost touching distance of the female and baby elephants in this wonderful park. Great way to spend an afternoon and have the camera ready.

title: Sure to see elrphants
text: We went to see elephants and saw many. In addition there were wild birds, eagles and monkeys as well as other animals. A very commercial national park overridden with 4 wheel drive vehicles carrying tourists. Very different to Safari’s in South Africa. In Africa one sees maybe another one or two jeeps. Here it is in excess of twenty clustering in one place to look at the animals. However this does not seem to disturb anyone and it is nature a usual that continues as well as humans joining the next group of vehicles.

title: great place to see many elephants
text: Definitely worth a visit - if you are lucky (which most seems to be), you will see hundreds of elephants gathering around the water holes every afternoon around 2-4 pm. LOADS of safari jeeps, but still worth a visit.

title: Love Elephants
text: There were so many elephants and lots of baby elephants. They were playing in the water and spraying one another. They Mommas were very protective of their babies. They were close to the road, so you got plenty of good photos.

title: Only elephants
text: We came here for a safari but, apart from elephants, there is nothing else. Some birds - but none that you can’t see out of the park. The safari guide/driver was non-communicative and didn’t tell us where we were going, what we were seeing or any other type of info. We expected the drive to last from 14:30 tp 18:00 but we headed back at 16:30 and never stopped again, even when we saw some deer in the distance. Also worrying was the attitude of the multitude of jeeps towards the herds of elephants. Although the animals were extremely calm, a very short security distance was kept (with cars pulling up at 4-5 m from a female) and the jeeps blocked a herd’s way when they were obviously trying to get to the bushed area. On the whole: - drivers should be trained in pr skills and told to be communicative - it should be clearer that the safari is home only to elephants - an ethical guide should be implemented so that there aren’t so many jeeps crowding the animals and a respectful distance must be kept

title: Rustic elephant watching
text: This is not a luxury well run park, but it has its charm. You organize a guide with an open jeep outside of the park. You travel with a convey of other open jeeps down bump roads through the jungle to large open water bodies where you are going to see ALOT of elephants. They don't go extremely close to the elephants,its good that they give them space.There were lots of babies there too.I would recommend going at 4pm as the elephants are active then and you might have a chance of spotting a leopard too.

title: Amazing ride to the elephants
text: This is a crazy fast ride to the national park to see the elephants and other animals and birds. We had to hand on in the back of the jeep but it was a lot of fun. You drive on dirt tracks and through water and lots of mud. Some jeeps were getting bogged,Mobutu luckily our driver was great and we didn't have any problems. It was all worth it to see the many hearts of elephants with babies also. We would have seen over 50 elephants and also saw 2 young male elephants having a fight which was very interesting. I would definately recommend this attraction.

title: Ticket item elephants roaming
text: Well apart from the traffic jam of jeeps this is an amazing experience. Our guide explained the bird life as well as getting us close to a group of elephants with their young. We just watched as they grazed and played it was fantastic and something with doing. This park is one of the smaller ones with no leopards but evert pythons else. If you want a close experience with elephants in the free this should be added to your wish list. Thank you to our driver and team.

title: Wow!
text: If you want to see elephants in the wild then please visit this place a not an orphanage in which they are fenced and caged. It was truly amazing to see and remember.

title: Get your safari on
text: Our driver recommended this. We were going to wait until we got to another location in Sri Lanka but we’re glad we didn’t. Great fun standing in the Jeep and seeing an abundance of wildlife in their natural habitat.

title: Really enjoyable safari
text: Lovely safari. Would recommend going early morning or late afternoon due to the heat though. Saw lots of elephants, monkeys, water buffalo and wild birds. Was a lovely afternoon out.

title: a great trip
text: you cannot go to Sri Lanka and not see the elephants. good trip in jeeps with open tops. each jeep seated four and there was plenty f room to stand up and take photos. some real close ups of the elephants about 2 hours cost about £35 each

title: A bit disappointed
text: Was really looking forward to this safari but all we saw are PELICANS, ELEPHANTS, INGRIDS and some BUFFALOS After all those.crazy bumpy rides, that's.all we saw... at some point we got bored looking at the same animals and.wished we were just heading back . It must be the draught season so most animals are Hiding but crap! This isn't the safari I was expecting. Might as well I visit the zoo

title: Lots and lots of elephants
text: After a rickety rackety jeep ride we saw lots if elephants and quite a few birds too. These though were out numbered by jeeps.

title: Fab time, saw lots of elephants.
text: This trip was one of the highlights of our Sri-Lanka trip and well worth a visit. We arrived just after lunch so there were plenty of jeeps available, being only 3 people I was please we didn’t have to share. We saw a variety of wildlife including lots of elephants in different areas of the park, as with all parks the drivers keep others informed so you are assured of seeing something, the most jeeps at one time was about 6 which didn’t seem too crowded. The park and roadside was the only place in Sri Lanka that we saw picking us rubbish! The only downside is as with other attractions in Sigiriya it doesn’t take credit cards so bring plenty of cash!

title: Amazing elephant park
text: We've seen elephants in India but this was something else, they were so close and in such a brilliant setting. Beautiful, we saw about 170 elephants in all! Standing up in an open air jeep, fantastic!

title: So many elephants!
text: I don't know if it's because we were so lucky or if it's the time of the year that helped us, but we saw so many elephants there!!! Just awesome for everyone! Our guide was charming and very respectful to the environment and animals. Just loved this experience! (I've been in Serengeti, Ngorongoro Tanzania and Ethosha in Namibia).

title: Fabulous experience of animals in their natural surroundings
text: Very good fun trip, beautiful surroundings, saw loads of elephants it was amazing but be prepared for a bumpy ride

title: Best place to see elephants
text: It was a great experience! It's the perfect place to see plenty of elephants in the wild! We were there in the afternoon and it was amazing because there were so many elephants and they came out of the woods to drink water. Also our driver was patient and waited for us to make photos and he drove us to some great spots to have good visibility.

title: HORRIBLE EXPERIENCE !
text: We payed 120$ for a 2h30 tour safari to see elephants. Our driver was a crazy driver, he was driving in the water and got stuck in the mud. We tried all afternoon to get the jeep out of the mud but we didn't manage to do it. Then after 5hours of waiting in the sun, a friend of the driver came to pick us up as the jeep was still stuck in the mud. We didn't see any elephants. We lost our day (we left at 10 in the morning and came back at 5.30 in the afternoon). We asked for a refund and the responsible for this tour told us that it wasn't possible... I wouldn't recommand this tour at all (the one with the reservation in front of the cinnamon hotel). DON'T DO IT !!!!!!!!!!

title: Elephant sanctuary. Animals in the wild. Real thrill
text: The drivers usually charge Rs 6000 for a hotel pickup and about three hours of driving round the National Park. There is a further fee to enter the park. It's an amazing sanctuary and we saw over 100 elephants sometimes up close. It's not overrun with tourists like some of the other larger national parks. Definitely worth a visit. About 20k out of Sigiriya.

title: Respectfully done
text: Great opp to see plenty of elephants in the wild including lots of baby ones. Given some of the reviews I have read was expecting jeeps all over each other and the elephants but the drivers kept to the paths and were respectful of each other. One suggestion is either go early morning or after 3pm given there are more at dawn or dusk. The Jeep’s can also be very comfy or rough as guts with the seat quality so suggest checking out what u are expected in yours.

title: Elephants up close
text: Our jeep driver took time to locate as many elephants as possible. Yes, we saw quite a few, and it was quite memorable. At times, jeeps become very crowded and chaotic in one spot, but it all worked well. My only concern seems to be many jeep companies are located along the road outside the park, so you need to ride in them for some distance without seatbelts. Perhaps, the jeeps can be rented inside the park instead.

title: Fantastic excursion, highly recommended
text: We took a private jeep, (we were very lucky and were one of the few people to get a Land Rover!). At first we struggled to see much, and so did all of the other drivers, to the extend that our driver took us deep into the jungle for best endeavours to see something. Eventually as if our of no where we saw the most amazing site of several elephant groups. In the end we saw 7 instances of either individual elephants or groups of elephants. We went at about 1 and stayed in the park until about 4.30, this was plenty of time. Our driver also took us to the viewing tower where you can walk and get some amazing views. Highly recommended.

title: Too much money for that!
text: In the last day of our trip we decided to go there , it was completely wast of time and momey , we just saw 1 elephant after searching about 1and half hoar, we got so tired for nothing, They told us today is hot and elephant goes to bushes , and I think they take too much money for that!

title: Exciting end to the day
text: The national park was flooded by recent heavy rain but the eco park across the road was full of elephants who had moved in to escape the floods and search for food. There are far too many over enthusiastic jeep drivers careering around trying to get the best positions for their clients but we were fortunate to get an old hand who knew the best tricks and who got us within touching distance of a small family of 3 plus mother without raising any alarms. It was a most moving experience to be so close while they were not in the least disturbed by our presence. We almost wore out the camera!

title: Great day at Minneriya
text: Was picked up from my guest house exactly on time and taken to this beautiful park. We managed to get really quite close and saw lots of elephants at various spots. My guide was really friendly and made me feel at ease being a woman alone. He was able to answer all my questions and never rushed. He was also so good stopping on the way home to help me get a new SIM card because mine had broken, it was quite late at this point and I really appreciate his time and help. I would definitely recommend booking a trip with them, professional, good drivers not like some of the touts you get that drive bad and scare the elephants... Saw some of that and it was upsetting. These guys very good and respectful. Thank you for a wonderful day.

title: Safari in jeeps
text: Safari absolutely brilliant with teenagers and infants. Knowledgeable, careful driver. Saw an abundance of elephants up close including babies. Countryside so beautiful. Well worth a visit.

title: Rain ,mud,No elephants
text: We had booked to go here or so we thought . However we were taken to the Eco park at Habarana .There must have been a hundred vehicles which set off in a massive convoy .After a couple of miles the jeeps with bald tyres got stuck in the mud - there was no way to turn back , the whole convoy had to sit in the mud for an hour . The Forestry Dept were still selling gate tickets despite the terrible conditions. No animals. If you really want to go check , check and check again on conditions at the site.

title: almost unbelievable
text: Our "safari" was booked for us by the driver we had contracted for our week in Sri Lanka. Although we have no way of knowing what options might have been available, it is hard to imagine that we could have done much better. A number of species are represented in the Kauoulla National Park, but elephants are the obvious draw. We had heard that sightings earlier in the day were plentiful, but that doesn't really prepare you for the experience of encountering large (at least 50+ animals?) herds. Knowing that you are seeing them in what is their natural habitat is an incredible experience. We rode in a "jeep" with a raised passenger compartment, so at times it felt like we were almost "face-to-face" with the elephants.

title: The highlight of our sri lancan visit
text: To get as close as we did to a heard of over fifty elephants and watch them for well over 45 minutes was sensational. One had a one week old baby that was great.

title: Elephant Safari
text: We have seen herds of elephants on this safari. Most of the action is around the water body. There are too many vehicles , bothering animals . Overall , a good experience

title: must see
text: it is must see if you are going to sri lanka, just find driver with good price, nothing to add more .

title: Breathtaking
text: Well worth a visit.... the elephant population is huge and you will see all sizes from small babies to fully grown bulls... the park also hosts many more animals and got to see a lot of eagles, buffalo, crocodiles to name but a few. try and get an early sunset one otherwise there can be a lot of jeeps on the safari.

title: Wow! Wow! Wow!
text: This was a great experience. We probably saw about 200 elephants plus a number of other animals including deer. There were babies, heavily pregnant elephants and everything in between. Some of them came up quite close to the open jeeps we were travelling in. Our jeep driver and guide was fantastic and told us lots of interesting details. However others I spoke to said this was not the case with their driver. Nether the less a very rewarding experience.

title: More jeeps than elephants
text: We had heard about the elephant gathering on a nature documentary and were looking forward to this experience, however it when we arrived the reality was quite disappointing. We did see quite a number of elephants, which was great, however, this was marred by the hundreds of jeeps descending on them. At times the jeeps even blocked their access to the water and cut off their path. It was awful. Our fantastic guide told us that the gathering has not happened for the past 3 years due to the water levels being kept artificially high, stopping fresh new grass growth from water receding, which is what the elephants are attracted to. Considering the amount of money brought in by the entry fee, the government needs to manage this resource much more sustainably.

title: Elephants!
text: We took the afternoon safari which starts at 1.30 pm from Sigiriya. It took around 40 mins to reach the national park. Tickets are 3000 LKR per person. The jeep took us inside the reserve and slowly you will leave behind the city and enter a jungle. The experience is one of its kinds. Highlights of this safari is ofcourse the elephants which come right at the end. You can see the entire herd walking together. We almost had one elephant moving towards the entire group of jeeps which was a little scary. But thrilling too.

title: Elephants..
text: One of the best safari to see large groups of elephants. Best time is noon safari of 2 pm when these elephants groups come to lake.

title: Elephant safari
text: Seems there are many companies doing safari from Sigiriya. My experience with one company who took us to this safari was such a fun. Saw many elephants, very close. It was an amazing experience. It was a private jeep trip and the driver was very nice and eager to show us a lot. Trip was 3pm to about 7pm which was perfect time to see elephants dinner time and nice sunset.

title: I was blown away
text: This was one of the most wonderful holiday moments in my life - to see elephants in the wild. Although there were a lot of other vehicles, the drivers are skilled in stopping for photos where you feel you are the only one. The elephants really don't seem to mind and carry on as they have been doing for thousands of years before we showed up!

title: Not many animals
text: We traveled on a very bumpy road on an old jeep to arrive at the water hole. There were not too many elephants around and we could only view them from quite a distance. Other animals include some buffaloes and a few types of birds. The driver of the jeep was rather surprised that we were not impressed. If one wishes to see more animals, one should go to South Africa.

title: AMAZING
text: It's so great to see how lives elephants in wild. The biggest population in Sri Lanka, around 300. Price 6000 per Jeep(5-6 people) and 2500 entrance fee.

title: Great experience
text: Called up the day before and was able to arrange a Jeep no problems. Had a fantastic time, saw easily 100+ elephants, our driver was very helpful and courteous. Highly recommend !

title: Safari
text: A must do to see a lot of elephants, beautiful peacocks, some black bulls, even a jackal, crows and white egrets.

title: elies galore
text: I haven't seen such herds in the wild in Asia. The eleis are a joy to watch. We spotted a few jackals and a horn bill. The lake is stunning towards sun down and the sight of the herds against the lake is a photographers delight. Don't expect too much of the park other than the elephants.

title: If I hadn't been to Africa...
text: OK so this "safari" is OK and we did see a LOT of elephants (about 120) as we were there at the right time. We also saw a pack of jackal and a Leopard (VERY lucky spotting on our part) BUT... You are there with a hell of a lot of other jeeps and people and they stop midway through so you can "stretch your legs" which meant people smoked ??????? and then we drove back the way we came. If you have never been on a safari then definitely go as it is wonderful to be out in an open jeep.

title: A more ethical way to admire these beautiful creatures
text: We hadn't planned this into our itinerary and like many spontaneous outings, this was hugely rewarding. We were delighted when we saw just one elephant. 10 minutes later we saw 75. In their own habitat unmolested by tourists climbing them - quite wonderful.

title: Great place
text: This is one of the most beautiful place I visited. New experience with elephants life. The green and mountais view are remarkable. Kids and families will enjoy such place. You can feed elephants old and young. You can watch the bath time at the river.

title: Satisfying first time safari experience
text: This was my first safari experience and it was just satisfying. The entire goal of the trip is to see elephants on a pretty close distance. Our driver pointed out few other animals such as monkeys for example, but we could see monkeys everywhere else outside of the park. After around 2 hours we finally spotted a group of elephants and took some nice pictures. We didn't run across any other animals unfortunately.

title: Elephants - Elephants and more Elephants!!!!
text: Was getting a bit worried we may not see any however saw over 100 in the end - along with other wildlife. This was the highlight of our visit and really is a must do !

title: Fantastic Safari
text: After staying at Holiday Cottage in Sigiriya with Roshan and his family, my tour guide from Sri Lankan Nisha Tours arranged this Safari with Roshan to Minneriya National Park. I had read reviews about the amount of elephants that you are able to see here but did not expect to see such a large gathering of them. Roshan's service from being taken to the National Park to his patience while I spent time in awe of the herd that we stumbled across was fantastic, very comfortable transport and Roshan's engish is brilliant making this a really memerable afternoon. Thanks so much Roshan if anytime I return to Sri Lanka I will most definately pay you another visit.

title: You're guaranteed to see elephants
text: Unlike most Kenyan safaris (the only comparison I could make) you are taken around in a 4X4 jeep, rather than a minibus, so that's a good start. The park is not that big so you will definitely see elephants but, be aware, you will also see every other jeep in town! As they flock to the herds for a better view for their guests. So much so, that they intrude on the elephants path causing some nervous reversing when faced off by three great beasts! A great trip but a little more respect for the animals wouldn't go amiss.

title: Great visit with a great guide
text: Wonderful area with a lot of elephants. Our guide and chauffeur searched explicit for the non crowded places. We saw a lot of elephants but also a lot of jeeps. It's how it works..he explained that even wild ill elephants are being treated from the money tourists pay for a visit. However, he really tried and managed to spot elephants without a lot of jeeps around them. We spotted also a lot of beautiful birds. Really worth to join this company.

title: Wild elephant watching
text: It is very beautiful experience, that is one of its kind. Those who like to get an experience of being in between the heard of elephants (daddy elephant, mummy elephants and the cute little baby elephants) grazing the lush green grass on the bed of a man made lake. Also a guide who is well explaining the facts about the elephants and their behaviour. It is one of the most do thing in Sigiriya.

title: 150 elephants
text: The best afternoon you can imagine, casually roam in the countryside and forest with elephants, big and small.

title: Far too many Jeeps in the park
text: Minneriya National Park is where you can see wild elephants roaming from a Jeep. There are a LOT of Jeeps though. Hundreds of Jeeps which all converge on any Elephant they can find. I'm not overly convinced it is in any way ecologically sensitive

title: Great if you've never seen a wild elephant before, but dull if you have
text: Your opinion of this place will depend on your previous travel experiences. Having done safaris in other countries, we found this little more than a jeep drive around lake to see some elephants and several varieties of birds, but other members of our party who had not travelled much before, thought it was the best things ever. We saw about 30 or so elephants at fairly close range. Many jeeps jockey for the best position. Bumpy ride. Advised to tip driver at least 500 rupees per couple.

title: Good ride after long time
text: The elephant back ride in Sri Lanka is one of the To Do activities depending on your interests. Our little boy of 3yrs just loved it and kept singing his elephant rhymes. The elephant took us by the lake and we fed some cucumbers too. It is quite expensive compared to the elephant safaris in India. It costed 20$ per person for the 20min ride on the elephant.

title: It is Nice to Be the Captive Animal Every Now & Then!
text: As someone who has seen elephants mostly in captivity and, not always enjoying a high standard of life (for example, some Thai elephants), I was ecstatic to be the "caged animal" for a few hours and to observe elephants roaming freely & happily at Minneriya. Though there was other wildlife, the reason for spending AUD$120 as a couple was because of the elephants. The money spent was petty cash on that basis. No offence to the other wildlife but, were it not for the elephants, I could not say the experience is well worth the investment. The array of birds, monkeys, deer & buffalo should, however, not go without mention. A set of binoculars would be an advantage in better observing some of these other animals. We didn't have a pair and, our driver didn't either. Though I do not consider the experience to be age restrictive, I do warn that the ride is not always smooth. Be prepared to bump around a bit!

title: Amazing
text: A must on anyone's list. The park is fantastic and the elephants are in abundance. Loved every minute of it.

title: Perfect....
text: This is the way to see elephants, not in a zoo or circus, but live and free. This was the highlight of our trip to Sri Lanka. One slight issue.... maybe too many jeeps on the track at one time.

title: Elephants Move Freely and well Protected
text: This park is a must see if in the area. Bumpy and dusty road to reach n need 4WD vehicle. Many are available for rent plus a guide for around $40 plus entrance fee. Ask yr tour guide. Elephants by the hundreds with babies r there. Freely moving, feeding without fear and near the lake. U can get very close without getting them upset. Safaris r starting afternoon and u get to see them going to the lake almost by sunset. Monkeys, peacocks, monkeys, birds r available.

title: Elephant reserve
text: this was such a treat the girls loved it and so did we!!! the elephants were going for their afternoon dip in the lagoon as the sun was setting it was just magical!!

title: Elephant Safari
text: You need to avoid rainy seasons. I could see only one elephant crossing the road during a four hour trip. Most Jeeps are not four wheel driven cabs. Two vehicles got stuck in the mud. We had to wait for a real 4X4 cab. Some cab drives might mislead you. they some times pretend as there are no more cabs. and demands you to pay more. Get your hotel to arrange one for you.

title: Amazing Safari
text: We went there in the afternoon, the safari in a private jeep lasted for two n half hour. we saw hundreds of elephants grassing just by meters away from us. There are lots of other animals like bulls, jackals and bird also there.

title: AMAZING!!
text: We had a fantastic jeep safari with driver Johan. Encountered more than 100 elephants, really close. Also saw beautiful birds. Unfortunately we had to share the space with lots of other jeeps, but still an amazing experience. An absolute must do excursion!

title: ELEPHANT HAVEN
text: I suggest you come early in the morning or late afternoon. We went in the aftenoon as waited for the sun to set in a safari -- feels like the African Safari that we see on movies. Really breathtaking place! A whole new experience to do a safari ride. A must go and do when you are in Sri Lanka.

title: Real thing
text: Even if the area is crowded the experience is amazing. Many wild animals and in particular elephants - but also birds and other species made this an unforgettable experience. We wanted to avoid the tourist elephant traps in pinnavala so to see the free animals in minniriya was a true privilege Of course there are (too) many jeeps, but it was all with respect to the animal From what we later experienced this was the best animal experience In Sri Lanka

title: Wonderful to see all the elephants
text: Very good t our but pretty much all centred around the elephants ad not many other animals. Rather too many jeeps though at time s crowding the elephants. Our driver was really thoughtful and kept a respectful distance from the wonderful elephants. Butt others were less caring and at one point got in the way of a family that were trying to reach the water hole. That's a shame. We went in the late afternoon, perhaps early morning is less crowded

title: Elephant Heaven!
text: We took a jeep safari to watch for animals & birds. The main goal was to see the elephants--which we saw in abundance--from the oldest bull elephant to a tiny 2-week old baby. We watched several herds for a couple of hours because it was so interesting to see them interact with each other in the wild. We were happy that Sri Lanka has chosen to develop their national park system to protect these magnificent animals!

title: A day I will never forget
text: Wild elephants up close.... do I need to say anything else! Bucket list tick! Take a good camera and enjoy these beautiful animals

title: More jeeps than animals
text: My personal experience in this safari was not that great. To begin with I think its overpriced. The enrty fee to the park is around LKR 3500 per head. After that you have to book/ rent a jeep separately. As in most cases you have to bargain to get a good deal with the jeep rental - We got one for LKR3000. So we ended up spending LKR 10000 (2 of us) for this safari and we got we got to see was - a few peacocks; Langur monkeys and domesticated cows and buffaloes! I know it depends on your luck if you get to see certain animals in a safari - its always a chance you have to take. There were many jeeps and they all follow a fixed path. Overall it was a bumpy 3 hour ride up and down the national park and we were quite disappointed with the safari. I think a safari at Udawalawe or Yala would be a better option. We actually spotted to elephants right after we left the safari! They had strayed onto the roads from the jungle!

title: Worth a visit
text: We booked a 3h jeep safari and saw lots of elephants. Even though there are more jeeps than elephants in the park the drivers generally kept their distance to the animals. I was rarely under the impression that the elephants were disturbed or stressed by our presence- they seemed used to the jeeps and didn't show any reaction. Better than I expected having read other comments before the tour.

title: Lots of elephants
text: Lots and lots of jeeps at the same time. However, we managed to see lots of elephants - and also buffalos, monkeys and different birds. A really nice safari - though there were a lot of waiting before it started.

title: Ask the homestay owner for a better deal
text: 100% worth a visit, we saw 30+ elephants in their natural habitat! Definately ask your homestay owner to look into though- our owner managed to find another couple to share the Jeep with, halving the cost to hire it for the afternoon and also reducing the price you pay for entry in the park (each group pays a fixed amount extra to enter the park on top of the price per person and the price of the Jeep). Altogether it only cost us less than 10,000 Rs for an unforgettable experience.

title: Great experience! Recommended!
text: We visited Minneriya National Park the first day of our trip in Sri Lanka and it was really unique experience, because we had never seen elephants from that close and in their natural habitat! Our guide, who was really good suggested that we had this safari, since it was not arranged by the travel agency, and it was really worth visiting. We enjoyed the beautiful route inside the park with an open jeep. Except for elephants the residents of that park are buffalos and birds. Since anyone visits Sri Lanka I would recommend this activity for sure!

title: Beautiful park, lots of elephants
text: The jeep was uncomfortable and the road extremely bumpy. We saw tons of elephants, but no other animals aside from monkeys and a few pelicans. Oh, and a crocodile in the distance ;)

title: Limited wildlife.
text: This place worked out quite expensive I felt. It is also a long and very rough ride into the park before you see anything. The only animals here are elephant and water buffalo. We did see lots of elephants in large groups but that was it.

title: Calling All Ellie Lovers :)
text: At first I thought I could see a lot of animals here but in fact only elephants in this National Park. You got to go there by renting a jeep car, just prepare your butts for the crazy bumpy roads LOL The price ticket for foreigners is about LKR 2,200/pax, while for local is about LKR1,250/pax (USD 1 = LKR 152). Don't forget to apply sunblock all over your body! :D

title: Elephant Lovers Paradise!
text: There isn't much variety here int his park, but if you love elephants, you're in heaven. To those who've been on African safari, do NOT place your expectation here. This is a very simple almost sanctuary feel and no other big game are present. When you come know that the elephant is here to enchant and show you true simplicity of another safari life.

title: Family of five
text: This National Park is great for viewing elephants and we saw a herd of over 100. At one stage we were so close we could almost touch the elephant, while in the protection of a jeep. When vehicles are turned off you can feel the calm tranquil atmosphere when the herd was feeding. Baby elephants are always a good sign and we saw plenty of them. Something special and definitely worth a visit. Only negative would be the amount of jeeps.

title: Elephants Galore!
text: We were fortunate to see a lot of wild elephants at this park, family groups with calves as young as two weeks protected by their Aunts, and lone large males wandering about. The bird life was also very good.

title: Elephant gathering
text: a 3 hour experience to watch the gathering late afternoon. Saw other animals along the way- kingfishers, spotted deer, monkeys, peacocks to name a few. Watching the elephants in their natural habitat was a wonderful sight and a holiday highlight.

title: Hundreds of elephants
text: Going inside the bush for 30 40 minutes to see some elephant behind a tree doesn't let you understand immediately what are you going to discover! Just few minutes later you're going to meet groups of elephants just eating and walking with no stress by the human being. The drivers (most of them)know how far have to stay from the babies to not be attacked by the elephant. We have seen one attacked by the elephant because his jeep was too close to the crossing path of the elephant.. Be careful. It must be on your to do list!!!

title: 100+ Elephants
text: We arrived for an afternoon/early evening drive through the park. Our driver was friendly and knowledgeable. He pointed out other wildlife on the drive towards the lake. The elephants gather there to feed. I counted over 100 elephants by the water. It was a busy day to go as it was a local holiday. There were almost as many jeeps watching the elephants. Unlike African Safari the drivers stick to the tracks so the elephants could decide how close they wanted to come to the jeeps. We saw a number of tuskers and enjoyed watching them. Slightly disappointing we didn't see much other wildlife in the park. But we had seen the elephants which was the main purpose of visit.

title: Outstanding experience so close to the fascinating land giants
text: Elephants are always a great watch. For someone who enjoyed them in some zoos earlier- this was a phenomenal experience. The sheer number of elephants was a delight and to be so close to the wild was enchanting and trilling at the same time. Special thanks to our guide/tours (Kanota tours) who recommended this attraction over an alternate safari plan we had and we loved every second of this ! An unforgettable experience.

title: As good as Africa?
text: I was truly touched by the sights. I saw a lot of elephants and many of them very close. Once you get through the forest with the jeeps the area opens up in a lake-side savannah, I felt it was breathtaking. I saw heards, individuals, pregnant cows and small babies. I feel like my expectations are really high now for any African safari (at least when it comes to elephants)

title: Safari to Minneriya National Park.
text: First we did not want to visit the park, but our driver Nuwan Sameraa said that there were many elefants to see and he arranged the driver. The safari was very good and we saw lots of elefants, birds and even crocodils. We enyoid the Safari.

title: Lovely safari for elephants
text: The park has an incredible amount of elephants. We also saw snakes, monkeys, crocodiles, water buffalo and various birds. Our homestay organised a visit for 11,500 rupees. It was however extremely busy with other safari tours and did get extremely dusty at points.

title: Hundreds of elephants
text: Quite touristy attraction and there is not much of animal spotting but you get to seen hundreds of elephants by the lake (together with hundreds of fellow tourists and dozens of other jeeps). Still worth a visit.

title: Our Small Safari
text: We were told to reach the premises by 1 pm, landed there well on time & we entered Mineriya National Park. Did not see much crowd whilst we entered, thought we would not get to see a lot but we were delighted to see quite a few herds of elephants, wild buffalo's, different species of birds, monkeys. We enjoyed our drive & by the time we returned there were around 100 jeeps entering the safari. As per our Driver, we were on time to visit the place, any later we could not have seen the animals as they would all go back into the forest.

title: mother elephants protecting a baby
text: we had an excellent experience witnessing 2 elephants protecting a baby. We saw about 20 elephants in total. We went at 12 and the park was empty, as we were leaving at 3, we passed at least 30 trucks going in. I can't imagine how crowded that would have been.

title: Elephant heaven
text: This was a good trip, we saw hundreds of elephants around the lake, although they can be quite aggressive if the jeeps get too close.

title: a lot of elephants
text: We hired an external jeep so to bargain a much better price. Our visit was roughly 3,5 hours an we enjoyed many elephants from few meters distance. Even a mother with the child.

title: Lovely gathering of wild elephants
text: So glad we chose this over the elephant orphanage as it offered us a chance to enjoy the elephants in a natural setting. We started out at about 4pm and spent a good 2 hours around the National Park. There were monkeys, crocodiles, birds etc and the setting was just lovely

title: Safari for elephant and nature lovers
text: Spent 5000 rupees ppl for the safari in this national park we enjoyed the scenery and view of elephant herds quite a lot. There's one thing for sure is that you will be satisfied if your target is only enjoying the ride on Jeep & elephants instead of expecting to varieties of wild animals. Again, you can enjoy the ride in the park with natural scenery just don't expect it to be like a wild land with thousands of animals on it.

title: Great safair
text: saw 80 elephants, a jackal, boar loads of birds eagles and crocodiles what more could you want for £35. Loads of great photo ops

title: One of my best days ever
text: saw over 200 elephants on a hot sunny day. loved it but take a hat and drinks it gets hot in the back of the trucks

title: Viewing Elephant herds in nature is a MUST in Sri-Lanka
text: We stayed in Dambulla and from there did all our trips in this area. Elephant Safari was definitely breathtaking, not too difficult. We had a Jeep pick us up, and drove to the reserve, in the reserve we saw Elephant herds, buffalo herd crossing the water, wild peacocks dancing with their full plumage in display, really wonderful. Can be done in the afternoon time.

title: A highlight of our trip to Sri Lanka
text: We loved this! Saw tons of female elephants and baby elephants and a couple of tuskers (males). Dozens of water buffalo nearly submerged in the lake. So may birds, and monkeys too. We enjoyed that the jeeps would drive up and cut the engine so we could watch the animals in their natural habitat in silence. We've visited an elephant sanctuary in Chiang Mai Thailand, and this was a much better experience. Highly recommend.

title: For the price, it's ookaaay
text: Set governmental price are the same for every national park and additionally you have to pay for a jeep. But the prices are still expensive. I won't undermine the nature however, it's beautiful, water buffaloes, elephants, crocodiles, jackals and birds of every kind. It's a must see if you love elephants. Plus, try and go in the afternoon!

title: A surprising safari
text: When we planned to visit Sigiriya, jungle safari was not an option in our list. Our tour operator suggested it and so we decided to go. He arranged a jeep and the first view into the jungle was not very impressive But then the moment we reached near the lake, it was really mesmerising. Herds and herds of elephants were seen. The best part was how the adults were protecting the little ones. The numbers were so huge that after a point we lost track on how many elephants we had seen.There were also many different variety of birds. Would say that this is a must visit place for bird watchers Overall a surprising safari which we really enjoyed!!

title: good
text: We went with chanaka adventure. Saw loads of elephants, birds, crocodiles and peacocks. Driver helped to spot animals. 4x4 was clean and spacious. We had to pay for chanaka adventure , entrance tickets and entrance for the vehicle also, so make sure what you pay for.

title: Won't do this again.
text: Lots of elephants here, but be prepared to get a "dust bath". The driver's seem to take great delight in out manuvering their associates. The result is that no one wants to leave much space between themselves and the car ahead so the driver in the cab is protected, but the his unlucky passengers are constantly enveloped in a cloud of dust.

title: Too Many Jeeps
