text: It was amazing to see the elephants at Minneriya, but it was incredible busy. More jeeps that elephants, but we've ticked the box.

title: Amazing!
text: Great afternoon looking for elephants in the national park. We saw lots of other wildlife as well which has ignited our idea of possibly doing a safari in Africa as one of our next holidays

title: Elephants, Elephants & Elephants
text: They are in their natural habitat and can be seen while traveling in a 4x4 accompanied by a Park Ranger. It is home to other wild life species as well. A must visit!! The entry fee for foreigners - RS. 2,500/- +/- There is a park ranger fee too. Locals free.

title: Highlight of the day
text: We quickly decided to visit Minneriya national park. Unexpectedly we saw approx. 30+x elefants eating grass. We were close up to 10 meters. A baby elefant approx 3 weeks old, we felt touching him. The driver was very experienced, showing us this unique view. And we had really luck to this unique situation. Highly recommended

title: Great way to see elephants in the wild
text: This was a very interesting experience enhanced by the fact that we had an excellent ecological guide and skilful driver. Driving off road to see the elephants after relatively heavy rains meant that the tracks were very slippy and it was difficult to cross the river. Some of the jeeps (2 wheel drives) got stuck in the river. It was fun to see the mothers with their babies near the river. No leopard sightings though!

title: beautiful park but too much noise
text: this national park is very beautiful with loads of elephants and many other animals to see from the jeeps. But for an animal loving person the safari jeeps are too many and too noisy and too near to the irritated animals than one can really enjoy it.

title: Amazing
text: The main attraction is the elephants, however there is an abundance of interesting bird life as well as a herd of wild buffaloes

title: Lots of elephants
text: Go in pm, from 1:30 to catch the sunset. Can be organised with your guesthouse in Sigiriya and is totally worthy, tho the main attraction is elephants. The surrounding is amazingly beautiful and the experience is nice. Not much tourist, we saw only few jeeps but at least over 50 elephants. Cost was 4500 all inclusive per person from Sigiriya in a jeep of 4.

title: Amazing
text: Have done a lot of safaris in Africa but this was a very good experience to see so many elephants so near in a open jeep.

title: Nice but not great...
text: The elephant safari is nice and interesting. Just too many vehicles going around the park. Limiting the number of vehicles might be a good idea, or imposing at least 4 pax per vehicle, as many jeeps carry only couples + driver. But overall a good experience as we didn't want a "zoo like" thing

title: Elephants everywhere
text: Just about 40 mins drive and you enter a huge clearing like nowhere. Herds of elephants keep coming and it's a delight to see them eating , and the baby elephants playing . The drivers are well experienced and there are many jeeps around you. I

title: Amazing sights, beautiful animals
text: Apart from all the beautiful birds (herons, peacocks, pelicans, eagles etc) who saw three different herds of elephants amounting to over 200 individuals, including many calves. We were able to get close in the 4x4 we were in and were able to get great photos. Minneriya is beautiful - particular forested and then large wet plains near the lake. Definitely worth doing.

title: An close encounter with the elephantts
text: A very interesting experience to visit and watch the elephants. There are very old jeeps to take you into the park and it was very rough ride, so be prepared. The jeeps are really good so don't expect to be comfortable. However, you can really see the elephants in a very close distance.

title: Wacky races meets Mad Max
text: We arrived as part of a party on an organised holiday tour having spent the morning at Sigiria rock. We climbed aboard our Mihranda Jeeps (don't forget to tip the driver !) and drove into the jungle in search of elephants. After about half an hour of driving and seeing absolutely nothing we came upon a herd of about 30 elephants near to a dried up lake (or tank as they call lakes ) we followed them around for some time, the jeeps kept overtaking each other and jockeying for position to get the best views of the elephants that came up close to our convoy. Not relly much else to see other than the elephants, apparently Sri Lanka has experienced a drought this year and most of the lakes have dried up, we then endured another half hour trip back to base, not seeing anything else exciting. However on a safari trip a few days later, which began in the early morning darkness, literally hundreds of jeeps took part in a race worthy of the title of the review looking for elephants and stuff, we actually saw a leopard who was rather nonplussed at being surrounded by about 100 mihranda jeeps full of tourists taking photo's of him, he was on top of a rock, got up, stretched and promptly went back to sleep. Epic !

title: "Big Elephants, Medium Elephants, Baby, Oh! Baby Elephants!"
text: I did the safari in the afternoon. My tour guide/driver was excellent. The bumpy road was really bumpy, so dress comfortably, bring your camera and excitement as it is truly a galore of Elephants. Many people came, all riding the safari jeep. Seen most of the people standing up and enjoying the view of the plethora of amazing elephants, big, medium and small. The best part of the safari is seeing the baby elephants and feeding at that time. One elephants was on the defense because one jeep got too close. I think that parking the jeep and just viewing the elephants is the best part of the safari.

title: Short Safari. Total excitement
text: So you cannot compare it to any Indian or African safari, buts a good quick and dirty ride into the wild! The experience of moving about in an open UV and the feeling of getting close to wild elephants is what one enjoys. Evenings are the best times and there is a sure shot view of Elephants in huge droves You will get to see a variety of birds but beyond that there is not much to see. This isn't a very expensive safari ...so for a group you will be paying around 8-10000 LKR. For a total time of about 2-2.5 hours.

title: A good place to see some elephant
text: Its a place where you can see some elephant at a very close distance and best to visit in the evening

title: ELEPHANTS !!
text: We have travelled to the Kandalla National Park before but nothing can prepare you for a herd of wild elephants grazing quite happily with 100s of people clicking away. Mums and their babies and teenager, aunts and the matriarch. It is a truly amazing experience. Cost including jeep and safari and entrance fee 10,000 LKR.

title: Elephants place
text: we hired a local jeep for 5-6k and we roamed aroudn the park for about 2-3 hours we could get a close look at the grazing elephants 3- 4 herds each having 3-7 elephants including calf's we had a look at water buffaloes from the far.. yala was closed so we opted for this . mainly elephants , a few birds int he water

title: Nature at its finest
text: Went here with Sanka Tours, amazing experience. The guide was very helpful and made sure we was happy with the walks and how far we walked. We did 10.3 miles in total, the sounds of the rainforest and the nature it holds is breath taking. The leech socks provided are a must they was loads and loads of leeches, but we was prepared for this so wasn’t socked about it. For anyone planning on going to the rainforest I would recommend wearing trainers and long trousers with the leech socks, plenty of water as it’s hot. But definitely worth the experience if you like walking/nature

title: Don't forget your leech socks
text: This trip I entered from the northern Kalawana side, only 3hrs from Colombo. I stayed at Jansens (recommended) where it's a short drive to the ticket office / entrance of Sinharajah. Jansens offers early breakfast and package lunch pack if you need. Get to the park entrance at 7am when they open for the early morning walk. You *MUST* wear leech socks as the rain forest is filled with them - go to a Alpine camping store in Colombo for 1500rupees, or I think you can even rent them from the ticket office. Note the hike is 4-6hrs. I walked every path available and it was 6hrs, but that included some side trips. Unfortunately the long hike to Singhagala of 10hrs has been closed since Covid, which is what i had planned for. Price is reasonable at 1200rupees for a foreigner plus 2500 for a guide. Excellent rainforest for hiking, birdwatching, and just enjoying the great outdoors.

title: Stunning forest buzzing with life!
text: Stunning forest buzzing with mammals, reptiles, insects and birds. I saw the following: Spot winged thrush, Chestnut backed owlet, Giant wood spider, Kangaroo lizard, Green pit viper, Brown fish owl, Sri Lankan frogmouth, Purple face leaf langur, Crimson backed flameback, Green vine snake, Giant squirrel, Hump nose lizard, Jungle fowl. The guide was excellent and managed to spot the tiniest detail. I did the half day tour but this only covers a small part of the forest, it's pretty large. I still managed to get to a waterfall for a swim, which was really nice. I was terrified of leeches, but I only saw a tiny one which had no success getting past the sole of my shoe. The guide covered my shoes and socks with salt which probably helped.

title: Scenic experience
text: We booked a tour guide via booking.com. It was worth it as he was very knowledgeable about nature and animals and knew the rainforest well. It was very beautiful and we got to swim in a water fall. Didn’t see as many animals as we had hoped though and it was quite a long walk.

title: Great rainforest hike with experienced guide
text: We (family of 4 from South Africa) visited Sinharaja on 28 February 2022, and stayed overnight at the Kurulu Ella Eco resort, right on top of the mountain. Had a pleasant stay at the resort that had a waterfall right in its own back yard, and then arranged with Danushka to be our guide in the rainforest trek the next morning. He came with a safari jeep and driver, picked us up at 8am and we entered the reserve by about 9.30. The road up was quite windy but extremely scenic. Entry into the Reserve was a breeze. Inside we were given our leech socks that covered till the knee area, and shoes were sprayed. The hike was amazing, we covered two of the three waterfalls, and were given a good explanation of the plants and animals we encountered. The dipping of our feet at the waterfalls was a tingling sensation as the many small fish nibbled on the skin. The rocks were very slippery and even though we had good hiking shoes, they did not grip on the wet rocks, so we had to be very careful. After 4 hours we were back at the jeep and exited. Had a memorable day there. Leeches still cling onto your knee high socks and shoes, and we got used to removing them with our hands as we saw our guide do this. If you did get stung, they suck your blood, you feel some pain but it is not fatal, so not to worry about these parasites too much. Best to do in morning, as it rains almost every afternoon. You cannot hike on your own and must engage a registered guide. Estimates of cost for 4 persons inclusive of entrance fee, guide, safari jeep, leach socks and spray was 12800 rupees for 4 pax which I thought was reasonable, other guides charge more. Happy to recommend Danushka. He can be contacted at +94 77 100 5329 (Whats app), or +94 77 525 4486 (tel)

title: The last piece of rainforest in Sri Lanka
text: The ride from Kudawa up the mountain to the entrance of the park is really nice - you need a 4x4 though as the road is in pretty bad shape. Half way up there are several nice panoramic views over the valley and the lush green mountains. You can choose several walks through the park. There are guides at the entrance to accompany you. Do use them, they know the fauna and flora inside out. Maybe you'll even get to see the rare and famous Serendib Scops-Owl !

title: Sinharaja
text: Nice feeling in the world heritage site i love the kakunella waterfall as cool, clear and,....... etc water..........

title: Good forest reserve, No cars
text: I enjoyed two good walks in this forest reserve, where everyone has to walk (except a few locals on motorbikes, But you hardly see them), and all the visitors go with the guide. The guide is very good and helpful and new the animals birds and plants and their Latin names. More paths would be nice.

title: Rain Forest Highway!
text: Not what we expected at all and not the fault of our experienced and informed guide! The locals use the "path" we were using as a short cut from one side of the park to the other by scooter or motor bike. One even tooted to warn us to jump out of the way. Not only is this pollution but means animals are hiding further back in the undergrowth we hardly saw anything of interest which was an absolute shame. The waterfall / swimming was a welcome relief and lovely. The powers that be need to stop this practice without fail it is detrimental not only to visitors experiences but the last remaining rain forest in Sri Lanka

title: Totally amazing experience
text: A biodiversity hotspot, Sinharaja rainforest is Sri Lanka’s largest remaining stretch of tropical rainforest. Sinharaja is home to hundreds of endemic flora and fauna, including reptiles, birds, insects, mammals and trees. However, the height of the forest canopy as well as the thickness of the vegetation makes it quite difficult to spot wildlife. Moreover, unlike in other national parks in Sri Lanka, access to the forest is only by foot, guided by a trained ranger.

title: Great animals, beautiful jungle, easy walk
text: We stayed in Deniyaya, there it’s 16km to the ‘pitadeniya’ entrance. The road is fine now, they just renew it. Last 2 kilometers you have to walk. Entrance fee is 575 LKR per person, you need a guide, they are at the ticket office, it’s around 2000/2500 for 2 persons. You walk with the guide to a waterfall (you can swim there) and back, easy path, takes around 3 hours. He will point you some nice animals: green pit viper, green vine snake, hump-nosed lizard, giant squirrel and kangaroo lizard. Guides know where the are but they are not really enthusiastic, seems like they do it only for the money.

title: Lungs of the island
text: The hilly virgin rainforest was so lush and green. It’s surely a gem of endemic species of mammals, birds, and reptiles. I’d love how the government was able to preserve the natural beauty of this spot! Remarkable indeed!

title: Magical Rain Forest
text: This is an exceptional park, with really good bird life, and also plenty of butterflies and dragonflies.

title: Best birdwatching site in Sri Lanka
text: This large rain forest is simply wonderful and I was so pleased that I had decided to stay for 3 days . It fully justifies the appellation of a World Heritage Site . On my first afternoon we birdied around the village . Our first bird was Serendip Scops Owl quickly followed by another I endemic Sri Lankan Rufous Babbler . Other sightings included : Hanging Parrot , Small Barbet , Pale-billed Flowerpecker and Indian Pygmy Woodpecker . Early next morning we entered the forest, glad to be on foot after a steep bone shaking jeep ride . Our first new mammal was the curious Purple-faced Leaf Monkey followed by another selection of great birds , including : Spot-winged Ground Thrush , Legge’s Flowerpecker , a pair of Frogmouths , Ashy-headed Laughing Thrush , Malabar Trogon , Velvet-fronted Nuthatch and Black-rumped Blue Monarch . However the best two birds took a long time to find . Firstly we followed a small track into the forest and made our way slowly and quietly through the undergrowth and crossing streams until we gained clear views of the elusive endemic the Sri Lankan Scaly Thrush . Secondly following advice from a local guide we retraced our steps and left the main forest following the call of our target bird high in the canopy . After much neck breaking scanning of the tree tops we finally had sight of the Red-faced Malkoha . After lunch we changed out plans to return to the Heritage Centre in search of the Sri Lankan Blue Magpie as our early morning visit was disrupted by a large group of school children . However there were still dozens of excited children around , then after an hour the heavens opened . Finally we did see a very bedraggled Blue a Magpie and Layard’s Squirrel . Early next morning we drove up to Martin’s Rest , one or the first specialised birding accommodation in the forest . Where we had breakfast on the balcony overlooking the forest . Just before breakfast we saw our final endemic bird , White-faced Starling . Thank to a Upali my guide I had now seen all the 34 endemic birds of Sri Lanka . After more birding we returned to the Heritage Centre and were rewarded with excellent close up views of the spectacular Sri Lankan Blue Magpie , plus Oriental Honey Buzzard and a beautiful Forget-me-not butterfly . Late afternoon after lunch we took a steep trek up a winding track in search of roosting owls . However after a strenuous climb we were unsuccessful but we did see a Brown-throated Needletail flying over . On our final morning we entered the forest for the last time and although we saw few new birds I did get clearer views and photographs of birds seen earlier , such as : Dark-fronted Babbler , Ashy-headed Laughing Thrush , Sri Lankan Crested Drongo , Spot -winged Ground Thrush , and one until now elusive bird Slaty-legged Crake . After a refreshing drink of tea with a local family we finally walked out of the forest . 3 days which I will never forget .

title: Forest Hike
text: Our first challenge was a tough 500m uphill slippery trail. Really enjoyed, but you need to be some what fit to achieve it. We didn’t really know what to expect throughout the whole experience but it turned out to be very enjoyable. We bought the leech socks 700 rupees for 2 pairs. We saw spiders, lizards, monkeys, snakes. Not many birds. Probably the biggest challenge was going back down the 1st ascent at the end. Very slippery. Really enjoyed the few hours though. Beautifully peaceful in the forest.

title: Birders Paradise - Blue Magpie, Jungle Spur Fowl, Sri Lankan Frogmouths & Serendib Scops Owl
text: We had a couple of great days in this place, seen a high number of birds Getting there can be a bit of a challenge and the walks are somewhat difficult, but its we'll worth it Our guides were fantastic and went out of their way to find birds for us. the photography can be a little challenging but that's half the fun Make sure you have leech socks and keep covered as there are plenty of them around. Great place

title: Birdwatching in the Sinharaja Rainforest
text: A group of us (eight birdwatchers), plus a couple birding guides (and also a local guide for inside the reserve), spent 2 1/2 days birding in the Sinharaja Rainforest Reserve and along various roads in the near vicinity. The reserve entry fees were taken care of by our birding tour leaders so there was no hassle in this regards. The diversity of birds in this area as well as the number of endemics is phenomenal. It was a long drive over rough roads to get to the reserve proper but was well worth the effort. Definitely worth a visit if you get to Sri Lanka - do this area during the dry season.

title: Some spectacular wildlife, fee and guide disappointing
text: No clear information available for entrance fees. After some discussion the entry fee was Rp 650 per head. We asked for entry tickets but never got them. Guide is compulsory and fees are per head, not per group.* Tour is on foot only. We haggled and got 6 hours tour for Rs 2600 per person including entry. The local guide we had was able to point out some animals but gave us a lot of wrong information as well. Highlights were the hob nosed lizards, green viper, purple faced langurs, comb tailed fishes and giant squirrels. There are some endemic birds species to be seen (we saw 10) but you need to educate yourself to identify them. Our guide didn’t even have binoculars. *No discount even for SAARC visitors.

title: Wonderful visit through a peaceful and beautiful rainforest.
text: We opted to get a government guide at the ticket counter. It was just my husband and I which made for the perfectly quiet nature walk. She didn't speak much English but it didn't really matter. She was adept at spotting and pointing out wildlife and we had no problem communicating. We had a wonderful time and I only ended up with one leach on me. We ended the tour with a dip in a waterfall. As we left the reserve we stopped at a local vendor selling snacks and ended our day sharing snacks with our lovely guide one of only two women working as government guides.

title: A good day trip to uncover biodiversity
text: A UNESCO world heritage and hotspot to uncover biodiversity. This rain forest is good for day trip, with a lot beautiful reptiles and creatures. However, tourists need to be cautious about tricky guides. We were arranged with a guy in the beginning but who's not qualified at all, we argued and fortunately to have another certified one replaced. The guide is very crucial in this kind of trip.

title: Loved my three day visit ...
text: Had three glorious days in the Reserve and would return in an instant given the chance! It was the highlight of my 12 night trip to the island. So much to see and the park guides are wonderful - we were lucky to have Santa who quickly realised that although I was with a bird-watching group, my interests were wide and varied. He made sure I saw the pitcher plants (carniverous), beautiful orchids, a couple of different snake, gorgeously-coloured lizards, as well as an example of just the tip of the tea that is picked, amongst many, many beautiful birds and two different types of monkey. Just remember your leech socks as we saw (and some friends encountered) quite a number of them Although they don't carry disease, they are really not pleasant to have on you!

title: Super Rain Forest Reserve - Endemic Rich
text: My wife and I visited this Reserve daily during our 3 day stay, during our Birdwatching Tour of Sri Lanka ????. The Forest is rich in wildlife in particular the Endemic Bird Species of Sri Lanka ????. We managed to record 19 of the 34 Endemic species without too much difficulty. Red-faced Malkoha and Sri Lanka Blue Magpie and the very rare Serendib Scops Owl, being amongst the highlights. The track to the Forest trail is 5km and challenging to walk, we chose to use one of the Jeep shuttles, even so this too was challenging. During our walks we encountered over 60 different species of bird, 3 species of snake and a few lizards ??. We also managed to see the National Bird of Sri Lanka ???? the Sri Lanka Junglefowl and the National Butterfly, the Ceylon Birdwing. The trails are challenging and most definitely not suitable to anyone with mobility issues. LEECH SOCKS ARE A MUST. Highly Recommended.

title: Amazing Experiance
text: It was fantastic experience to take a trek in such a rich rainforest. It was like we entered a completely different world as you step in to the forest from the village border. It is full of different flora and fauna which you will miss if you do not pay full attention. You can gain a vast knowledge about rainforests, identify how they are layered and different flora and fauna in different layers. However, make sure you go with the right guide to get the maximum advantage of the trek.

title: Good to see
text: Firstly, don't pay through the nose at your hotel/guest house. Go to the forest entrance and ask for a guide, we went the evening before and arranged a guide for 2000Rps which on the day became 3000Rps (£13 or $17) for a 5 hour walk for 2 people. But still better than $35 per person from the hotel. You'll still have to pay the 575Rps entrance either way. Secondly DO wear leachproof socks. I got bitten on the path walking to a restaurant near the forest wearing sandals. 'its too dry, there are no leeches...' many said this. The bleeding lasted 2 days. Wear the socks, don't be put off, it's worth it. You'll not go deep into the forest, the first part of any walk is along the path shared by locals, motorcycles and many many dogs. On the longer walks you go in a bit deeper but not far as it's necessary to protect primary rainforest like this. You will see: snakes, spiders, monkeys, giant squirrels, and lots of lizards. They will be pointed out to you and I believe will be in the same place day after day. You may see birds, but you will hear them and waterfalls. Wear walking boots or shoes, take plenty to drink and some snacks. Don't expect the full jungle experience, it's a nice walk on the edge of a pristine environment. Best it stays that way.

title: PEACE.
text: I went with four friends with two children. This place is truly stunning. And peaceful. Natural beauty. Nature lover's paradise. I wanted to say longer.Not over comercial. The giude was fantastic. And pointed out many bird's and details. Visitors centre very informative. A Very nice jiuce bar cafe.near the entrance. A wonderful day out.Strong shoes a must.mjh.

title: birds galore
text: hard climbing but well worth it, my guide found a wide range of birds for me including green billed coucal and blue magpie.

title: An enjoyable lesson to learn about the forest
text: Sinharaja Forest Reserve is yet very well known to tourist that in a day there are in average about 25 groups of tourists visiting the forest via Kudawa entrance. But that also makes it less commercialised than those more well known national parks. A guide is required to be accompanied in the tour of Rs1000. We have bought the long socks as well to protect ourselves from the leeches of Rs 350 per pair. It was thankful to have Jayala with us who has 8 years of experience of working as guide there. Without his explanation to us about the trees and the animals around, the whole tour might turn out to be a sheer forest hiking. Also, the guides there in general have very sharp eyes and good sense of whereabouts of the animals and insects. Some real tiny lizards and frogs could hardly be seen because also of their camouflage. And on the other hand the birds or even the pink face leave eating macaques are shy from people. To be able to have better view on the forest lives around, one may need a good binocular or long distance telephoto lens not less than 300mm. Just be aware of the leeches that I have got one bite to my tummy without a bit of feeling till the guide realized a patch of blood on my t-shirt. Overall, we enjoyed a lot learning throughout the tour arousing our interest to know more.

title: Amazing ecosystem
text: We had two days of hiking in the Sinharaja Forest Reserve with an incredible guide, Banduella from EcoVila hotel in Deniyaya. Banduella is an expert at finding and identifying plants and animals of the rainforest and help you enjoy so many things you wouldn't see on your own. Swimming in waterfalls when it gets too hot is a fantastic treat.

title: Very Different
text: The forest reserve is high up in the rain forest and the drive up is adventurous. The accommodation is converted metal shipping containers and quite unique. It is spectacular but not exactly luxurious. It is ideal for the enthusiastic nature lover. They offer several different treks and I did the early morning bird watching trek which was quite challenging but well worth the effort. The guide Jagerh was a complete expert, hugely enthusiastic and a delight to spend 2 1/2 hours with.

title: Fantastic scenery
text: Went for a couple of hikes and stayed overnight. Loved the trip with some stunning scenery. Beautiful place, would have liked to stay longer. A bit difficult to get to but worthwhile

title: Nice walk with snakes and spiders
text: We went there by tuck tuck. When we arraived there, we had a nice 4 hours walk thru the Jungle on a good trail. Our guide showed us a snake and some spiders. It was a great experience. The Landscape and nature are amazing.

title: I found Aywa
text: Dificult roads to get there, but incredible landscapes - similar to Avatar movie. On a road trip, one day in the rainforest is a must go

title: Great
text: Although we had a great time here and saw lots of wildlife, including snakes beware of the scams. Here's what happened to us and we had an organised driver, who I actually didn't always trust unfortunately. He tried to tell us we needed to find a guide prior to the entrance, so I gave up arguing and simply caught Tuk Tuk up to entrance. When we arrived I was wary, pretty sure it wasn't the official entrance so just played the game. The man who approached us wanted 2600SR per person, husband butted in and said yeh ok I just kept my trap shut at that point. Then we started walking off so I kept asking where is the official entrance I want a receipt. He kept saying it's up ahead, and yes we finally did get there. We then had to pay approx 550SR each entrance. I knew this was right but had to sought out the rest. I queried the lady at desk and said don't we pay for an official guide here after taking a photo of the entrance, she then looked blankly at our supposed guide then asked ME how much, I replied I'd read that it was 1000SR which she then agreed to. Well surprise surprise then an official guide materialised. You could then tell the difference the official guide had a Polo shirt with the appropriate logos and our so called guide had a T-shirt printed up to look identical. We did our 3hr walk to the waterfall and back, as we only wanted to do the short trek and we did have a great time for a few 1000 SR cheaper than they tried to fleece us and we gave him a tip. My warning is when you get dropped off at house at top hill continue walking down hill to official gate. We will never know if I didn't demand that we go to gate and buy a ticket whether we would have ended up on some random walk somewhere as I have read has happened to others.

title: Lovely place
text: Its an amazing calm place in sri lanka, love the green colour and thewater falls. Nice tour towards to Sinharaja forest. Well recommend to visit.

title: plenty of Wildlife
text: We enjoyed our walk in the forest reserve. The guides are very good at pointing out wildlife: lizards, snails, snakes, and a variety of birds. Because its heavily wooded its hard to get great photographs of the birds, compared to the national parks in the south of SR, but its an interesting walk.

title: Birds
text: One of the most beautiful reserves in Sri Lanka and important for local ecosystem. Famous for bird watching and I suggest to have guide here for better exp

title: Nice walk through the rainforest
text: We made a trip to sinharaja forest starting from unawatuna. Our guide was great seeing all the hidden animals that we would have never noticed. Snakes, birds, butterflies, plants, squirrels - we explored Mother Nature at her best. Finally we enjoyed the sun at a beautiful waterfall - absolutely refreshing. We can totally recommend!

title: Rainforest
text: A great experience with an experienced guide. This world heritage site is worth a visit for: - diverse Forna - exotic birds - getting close to nature - trekking

title: The natural gem in Sri Lanka - Sinharadja
text: One of the few areas left in Sri Lanka, where agriculture or mass tourism has not affected the beauty of the rainforrest. A licensed guide is mandatory but will you also help to get the best photos, experience. Several types of tours are possible and if you're keen on any group of wildlife (provided present there) to see, you can eventually prepare and discuss that (long) in advance, to get the best advise and timing. Protection against leeches (salt powder on your shoes, socks is recommended and can be bought prior entering the forrest.

title: Unsafe walking track filled with Leeches
text: We paid the 2300 for this waste of time experience. We walked only 15 mins each way and that was more than enough. The track was filled with dangerous loose rocks. You had to look down always so as not to fall, this missing what could be an attractive Rainforest Walk. The place is filled with Leeches and we encountered three in our short stay. Much better walks elsewhere.

title: Beautiful forest
text: We had a lovely hike in the rainforest with a knowledgeable guide. Make sure to take the Northern entrance! South side seems to be a scam. After the hustle and bustle of city destinations this was simply perfect to rest our minds listening to bird calls and the concert of cicadas! In the morning and under the shade of the canopy it was almost pleasantly cool but you should bring along a water bottle. The total length of the trail is about 10 km. There is some rough/uneven and steep terrain on some of the paths so hiking shoes are recommended, although I’m sure easier routes are also available as we met another group with a couple of elderly members. Binoculars could be useful for getting a better look at animals high up in the trees. Be sure to get leech socks (sold at the entrance office) to avoid bites. As the vegetation is thick it is rather unlikely to spot larger animals but there is still loads to see. Apart from the amazingly diverse plant life including carnivorous pitcher plants we saw many different kinds of insects, including millipedes as thick as your fingers, giant forest spiders patiently sitting in their huge webs and beautiful butterflies fluttering past. Our guide spotted a couple of kangaroo jumping lizards in the middle of courtship and pointed a giant squirrel to us high up in a tree. We also saw a few birds only found in the Sinharaja area. I caught a glimpse of a small snake as well.

title: Very beautiful rainforest
text: This is a great old rainforest, with several trails. We went with a nature guide who runs a guesthouse nearby (see other review). The forest itself was a great experience but the wildlife was totally absent on my trip. I came back very disappointed and feel even more so when I look at the lovely pictures others have put up. I don't know what went wrong. The night before our walk, it rained a lot. The guide said this would lead to better sightings, but we kept walking without seeing any birds or animals. We went as far as the waterfall, then on the way back it started pouring with torrential rain, which was a great experience - it is a rain forest after all so the warm rain soaking you right through to the bones was unique and welcome. However, it made the chances of seeing any wildlife even smaller. We saw some centipedes, a couple of colourful lizards and finally towards the end of the walk after walking through rain for 2 hours, a green pit viper. That's all. Not one bird. That's our luck I suppose. All our other wildlife trips in Sri Lanka proved very lucky, except this one. But we got soaked with rain in a primary rainforest, so I'm not too unhappy. Oh, and the leeches were everywhere, despite salt on the shoes and socks. Obviously salt will get washed away when it rains. So use leech socks.

title: Great Trekking, Unspoiled Beauty
text: We took two fairly long treks two days in a row. Our guide was Nimal both treks, and he was very good. He never rushed us, and went out of his way to give us a great experience. We think most people only do one trek. We had overestimated our time needs here, so we did a second trek. We were glad we did, as we saw different creatures the second day. Abundance of wildlife. Our treks were 5+ hours (and we were sore since some of the trails are very rocky), but we really enjoyed this wild place. We should have gotten leach socks the first day. My Smartwool socks were breached, but we bought socks the second day and had no issues. Hardly any biting insects, even with a good rain every afternoon.

title: Big money hustlas
text: We stayed at the Sinharaja Forest Sanctuary which is at walking distance from the Sinharaja Forest Reserve. Sanjaya was presented as the Forest Reserve guide affiliated with Sinharaja Forest Sanctuary. We were told things are very organized in the area, impossible to hire another guide other than the one affiliated with your lodge. A system that opens the gate to monopolistic pricing strategy we were soon to find out. A walk of 5-7 hours ending at the Singahala mountain with me and my husband, was priced at 20.000 Rs, entrance fee included. In Sri Lanka normal wages are like 1000 to 2000 Rs/day. What followed was an awkward negociation ending in an agreement for a shorter track of 3-4 hours for 6000 Rs. Next day we started off early, he walked a very slow pace on a dirt road with much motorcycle traffic towards a building in the forrest. Arriving there he said he had to buy the entry tickets so we handed him the 6000 Rs but didn't see him actually purchase anything. We took some pictures on what I think are pricing indications for guided tours (pic attached). From there to the waterfall was a more quiet stroll, we encountered many other guides with tourists all heading to the waterfall. So the walk could be done by any 70 year person. After this first waterfall he asked if we wanted to return to the lodge. I had heared about an other waterfall with little fish that nibble at the corn on your feet. He didn't seem too pleased. We continued steep up the mountain which was very much OK for us. No further information on the surroundings from that point on. On the way back the guide started to limp, a knee injury it seemed. He wanted to take a break so we waited a while. Later on he wanted to and have a drink but we had lunch ordered at the lodge. It came accross as looking for opportunity to ask for more money. Near the end I asked for the entrance tickets which he could not produce. He said he would get them later that afternoon and bring them to our lodge. We got some tickets but these seemed old and tampered with (pic included). I would still advise to visit the Sinharaja Forest Reserve although we did not have the best experience. Think the Forest Reserve has to put some things in order to avoid malpractice. Tourists are willing to pay for Reserve entrance, money to be used to preserve the Forest Reserve. In my opinion some people have very sticky fingers.

title: "SINHARAJA IS THE ONE OF OLDEST RAIN FOREST IN SOUTH ASIA"
text: " Sinharaja " was the one who taught me much about writing and photography even though I’m still a novice in those areas. Time it properly as the rains can be extremely difficult to explore the terrain. Leech Protection is vital unless it’s a very dry season. I’ve found the Leech Socks for sale at the Sinharaja Entrance Ticket Office (Rs. 350/- per pair) are very good at leech protection. Time the journey properly and we found the Highway- Matugama-Kalawana Route to be the easiest and the quickest. We reached the entrance under 2.5hrs without a major rush. Bird’s Paradise and Martin’s Lodge are recommendable accommodation options. There are multiple trails inside Sinharaja and except Sinhagala Trail others can be managed in one day quite easily. You’d probably need a full day to do the Sinhagala Trail. Do remain silent inside the forest in order not to disturb the wildlife. pls. enjoy her beauty and leave her in peace without destroying the most precious thing we have. Don’t break plants or flowers or try to bring them home. Most of these plants won’t grow in your garden. So please enjoy them where they are.The road from Kalawana to Kudawa is largely completed except at a few places so you wouldn’t have trouble getting there in any vehicle. Pitakele Doovili Ella is about 2-3km from the Sinharaja Entrance. However when you are coming from Kalawana, there’s a junction just passing a metal bridge before the Sinharaja Gate. You have to then take the right and the first left uphill concrete paved path. On this road travel for about 1.5-2km until the interlock stones paved stretch of the road and you have to get downhill to the river to view the waterfall. Bring back memories and leave only footprints. Remain silent and enjoy the tranquility of one of the most precious rain forests in the world.

title: A must see when in Sri Lanka
text: Fabulous forest reserve for bird lovers and nature lovers in general. This forest has been rescued from and attempted mass logging in late 1970's, when a dedicated group of scientist mounted a scientifically informed campaign. Since then it has been designated as a Man And Biosphere reserve as well as a world nature heritage site. Today it is the largest intact tract of lowland rainforest in Sri Lanka, which is home to numerous endemic tree, bird and other species. It is considered to be a significant hot spot of global biodiversity and a keystone in evolution. The majestic towering trees, many clear and pure brooks, hundreds of bird species, and the winding paths within this forest are simply impressive. Guided hikes are included in the modest entrance fee. These guides are employees of the forest dept, and appear to be very well informed. This forest reserve is easily accessible by main roads (last few km on a 4-wheel drive vehicle or on foot). Several options to stay at the boundary of the forest or one option within the border (Martin's Lodge).

title: Spectacular Sinharaja
text: A highlight of our recent wonderful trip organised by Tailor-made, a division of Jetwing Travels, was the magnificent Sinharaja Forest. We were privileged to stay at the Rainforest Ecolodge, on the edge of the forest. This meant we were right on site very early in the morning to go on a terrific birding walk. With the help of the guide we managed to see a number of specials including the Blue Magpie. The accommodation is interesting in converted containers which are very comfortable.

title: Peaceful Hike
text: We were picked up by our driver via Shelton Tours. Unfortunately our early 4.30 am start was slightly marred by the driver getting lost and adding 30 minutes to the journey, thus possibly missing some of the birds we wanted to see. That said our jungle guide was lovely and showed us as much as possible. It was quiet and relaxing, with the hike lasting 5 hours so very good value. Great to see endemic birds such as blue magpies nesting. Highly recommend visiting to see black monies, snakes, huge spiders and a sleeping owl. Our driver returned us to our villa safely and was very pleasant.

title: Beautiful rainforest
text: I've always wanted to go into a "jungle" and here my dream came true!! Dense and full of mysterious plants, with lianas to climb, reptiles and birds, one of the highlights of my trip to Sri Lanka. One should not underestimate the guide - without someone who knows what is what and where to find the interesting things, walking through the forest could feel like watching it through a glass wall, inaccessible. I was incredibly lucky to come across a guide called Pali, based at the Sinharaja Rest hostel. He is one of the most passionate biologists I have ever met (and I am a biologist!!), despite the wealth of experience (30 years of being a guide in Sinharaja!) he still has so much passion and energy that for a short moment the forest has become my home, like it is his. He pointed to all the interesting plants, explaining their use, letting us try some of them (like the medicinal ones). Highly highly recommended.

title: Impressive
text: With a very good guide it was a very nice trip. The guide showed us things we normally would have passed by as you can see on the picture, amazing!

title: Beautiful and worth the visit
text: We had a fantastic guide through the Forest, the paths are fairly well trodden so it's a very doable walk. We opted for the 6 hour walk which involved two waterfalls and saw spiders, snakes, giant squirrels, mongooses, land lizards as well as an aray of birds, too many to list. Well worth the money to preserve this beautiful part of the world. Take your swim stuff as the waterfalls are great fun to swim in.

title: Great place for easy walking with unique views
text: The basic trail is very easy, and along the way you can see some snakes, frogs, wood snails, spider webs, all types pf lizards and more jungle reptiles. Watch out of the leech, but can overcome very easy by simple asking of leech socks

title: Nice little walk in the forest
text: We took sun travels tour from Unawatuna beach. We compared the prices a little and took the cheapest. 2,5 hours ride to the forest, 3 hours walk and swimming in the waterfall. The forest is nice but three hours is quite short time to see. Mostly trees and plantains. Unfortunately our guide nor the driver spoke English so basically we only was told the things guide has learned to say. We did not get any introduction of the forest nor the wild life in it. Worth of visit definitely still!

title: For all tree lovers: walk under the canopy
text: We stayed for 6 hours in the jungle and walked about 6-8 km. Our guide from Hikkaduwa and local guides showed us different plants, insects, frogs, monkeys, and birds, also endemic. Many more than I can remember. The best part of the trip was being inside the rain forest, breathing it and listening to the beautiful sounds of the forest. It was not crowded, we met only one bunch of other tourists on the path that day. Recommendations Get a good guide and a local driver. The guide can give you the names of all the species, also in latin if you wish. Wear walking/hiking shoes and long trousers. The paths can be steep or slippery. Bring an extra t-shirt if you wish to have a dip into a natural pool. Take binoculars with you, just to make sure you see the birds.

title: Interesting Rain Forest
text: We walked a short 5 km route from the entrance to the waterfall. Beautiful vegetation, ovens and animals that he showed on the guide. At the waterfall you can take a bath :) Very interesting place, but the price of 3600 RSL per person is a bit excessive for a 5km walk ...

title: Beautiful primary rain forest
text: This is the most beautiful national parkwe visited in Sri Lanka. Unfortunately, it is quite difficult to spot the birds and wildlife due to the dense vegetation. Our guide was amazing, she recognized all birds by sound and found us great picture opportunities. It is a pity everybody follows the same trail, making it a little crowded. For bird lovers this park is a must. I wish we could have spent more time there.

title: Fantastic experience - fantastic guide
text: An incredible experience with a great guide. (We booked from Deniyaya Rest House 4/1/2018 so if you see this a huge thanks from Julia and Adrian). It’s about 3 or 4 hours. I’m not good with snakes or spiders but overcame my fear - they’re just there and after a bit you just kind of get used to each other. Our guide was great. He knows exactly what might be around - he’s been going there since he was a child with his grandfather.

title: To naturalists on a note
text: If the call of nature, for you the sofa is important, then boldly come here. Come to 9 am, go to the sales office, and wait until the group is typed (6-8 people). To help you, there is a guide who will show you some interesting nuances and places where forest dwellers live. We were here on hot days (there was no rain for three weeks), so we did not hear about leeches and mosquitoes. Take water with you, Citronella (buy in stores in Sri Lanka), stable shoes (cobblestone roads), and put on a cotton sweater with a long sleeve. Head, will offer several options for roads (the route includes a way to the top, to the mountains, the length 16 km). Next choose you, on which path, you are ready to Enjoy!

title: Great Place, shame on guides
text: this is a paradise but get there prepared for boring guides. We wished we had a real enthusiast with us. We wanted to walk for more and do more adventurous hikes but we couldn't..our guide was a tape-recorder and not interacting at all. A shame really because this is so typical in Sri Lanka..they think tourists don't know much and they haven't seen a tree or a bird in their lives so anything will do.. The place is huge and the biodiversity impressive. Visibility is a bit challenging, take binoculars with you as the trees are really high and birds are difficult to spot. Leeches we haven't seen but we got the socks as it could be a problem when it rains.

title: Incredible experience
text: Stayed in Unawatuna so it ended up taking me around 3 hours to get to the trail. You reach a point where you can’t drive anymore so you park and take a tuktuk to the start of the hike. I did the 4 and a half hour trek and I enjoyed every bit of it. You don’t see a ton of wildlife but the trek itself is very refreshing for the soul. In short, if you’re looking for a nice hike that isn’t too far from the south west, this is the best one. Make sure you check out the two waterfalls and go for a swim if you can, it’s super clean and refreshing. I would say that this is at a beginner level so if you’re in good shape you shouldn’t have a problem finishing this trail. They have a 24 km option which I might do the next time I come, that one is supposedly quite difficult as it involves a lot of climbing. Lastly, on the topic of leeches, I wore long pants and tucked my socks in so I didn’t have a problem but I highly recommend that you come prepared because those things are pretty nasty as my guide had a few on his legs. It’s all part of the adventure at the end of the day, so don’t let that change your plans. A special shoutout to my guide Pradeep who did a great job explaining everything to me and making the whole experience very memorable. Thanks again Pradeep, you’re a champ. The trek, tuktuk and guide costs around 8000 SLR.

title: An adventure in the rain forest.
text: Start early morning, when the sun brushes the vegetation, giving a very colourful mix. I am not particularly interested in bird watching, but I thoroughly enjoyed the light treck in the middle of nature and the ranger pointed out plants and animals, which I would have missed otherwise. WARNING: you will be offered high socks with your ticket for a small fee. These are not a luxury. They protect from leeches, which are numerous in the deeper parts of the forest.

title: Great walking but watch for the leeches
text: There seems to be a general myth that detergent and soapy water will get rid of leeches and this old timer is here to tell you that it DOES NOT. As well, the leeches here are faster than in China, Vietnam, Thailand and Australia - faster even that Kitulgala, Sri Lanka! Make sure you bring a cigarette (easiest) or take several handfuls of salt as a teaspoons will not do the trick once a leech has latched on. This was my second only guided trip in 45 years of travel (first being enforced years back in PR China) and though I can manage snakes,poisonous spiders and rats, I am not so great with leeches. Out of consideration for the guide, I kept my eyes on the treetops until we reached a tiny store where someone had a "beedie". Then another helpful individual informed us that leeches often hbernate in large balls high in the trees and drop onto warm blooded creatures passing by underneath. I have since asked several other experienced walkers in Sri Lanka to be told that this is true. Don't be put off; just be prepared. Another tip, if you are taken to the Buddhist retreat be prepared for the Austrian monk to insult you if you are (a) Christian (b) Australian or (c) polite. He does, however have a recipe for a kind of herbal infusion which is effective against high blood sugar. So taken with caution, this can be an interesting experience - as you watch those leeches gallop towards your shoe fastenings just light up a cigarette - and maybe wear a hat!!

title: This forest truly represents the ancient forests that have covered the earth
text: The Rainforest guide found a lot of birds and indigious animals for us to photograph, including a very rare Frog-owl with his mate. We truly enjoyed the experience! The forest is impressive and the paths are well used. The hike was doable; it is wise to wear sensible shoes and protect legs and arms against the sun, as well as the insects.

title: Paridise
text: What a stunning experience - must do! One of the great things about Sri Lanka is the variety within geographical proximity. You can travel from the beach to the rainforest and back within a day!

title: Lovely trek wildlife spotting!
text: Love visiting unesco heritage sites! Saw lizards, snakes, bird life, monkeys with the help of our guide from sinharaja rest.

title: Great waterfall to swim in. Watch out for the leeches!
text: A group of 12 of us took a private car from Galle to Sinharaja rainforest as a day trip. It is possible to do the journey by public buses but would have involved changing bus and an extra couple of hours so we decided a car was worth the extra money. The journey took 2.5 hours and 12,000 rps return. Entry to the reserve is 600 rps and I would definitely recommend getting a guide (1000 rps per person) otherwise you will miss all the wildlife. Our guide was really great, picking up snakes and lizards for us and pointing out lots of insects, different trees and bushes etc. We saw green pit vipers, giant millipedes, lizards, huge spiders. He also took us to an amazing waterfall that you can swim in and jump off the rocks into the pool if you want to - way too high for me! We were finished by about 1pm. One thing to note is there are loads of leeches!! So wear trainers, long trousers and socks to tuck your trousers into. A t shirt is fine though. Our guide also bought salt to rub onto our shoes and ankles as this apparently stops them from leeching on. They are small but pretty gross! We had a really fun day but I wouldn't say this is a must do. The waterfall was the highlight for me as we didn't see a huge amount of wildlife.

title: Wild and alive.
text: Walking trough the forest the most creatures you see are insects there are many birds and some monkeys which are shy, overall a magnificent place.

title: Great experience
text: This is an accessible rain forest. Great to see all the birds and other creatures. Interesting plants as well.

title: Fascinating primary rainforest
text: I have visited a few rainforest reserves but this is the pick of the bunch. Great guides. Abundance of wildlife. Easy access. Very beautiful

title: real nature
text: Very nice reserve, you need to take a guide or you will miss a lot of interesting animals, like rare snakes and spiders. Not an easy walk, good condition needed. Take your swimming shorts, the swim in the waterfall is a great reward after this walk.

title: Refreshing trek to the top
text: The trip to the Sinharaja Forest reserve had been a memorable one. we had left for a weekend gate away without any preparations and perhaps that was one of the reasons we loved it most. The jungle took us completely off guard , unprepared for the drizzle and rain while we trekked to the top of a mountain. At some places we had to hack through the dense undercover of the trees. The leeches on our legs seemed scary at first but we got used to it. It was exhilarating to reach the top , a small place for five of us to just lie down from complete exhaustion. The view from the top will be forever embedded in my memories. Sri Lanka in any way , has a special place in my heart.

title: Nature and wildlife
text: The forest is very large. We did a walk from the main gate and the next day from another gate. Normally the park is very quiet, but sometimes there are large groups of schoolchildren.

title: Like a walk in Finnish woods after a rain
text: I was a little bit disappointed. I expected something more, but we didn't see much: just a few snakes, spiders and lot of birds.

title: Excellent birding
text: You can see most of Sri Lanka's endemic birds here. The trails are well marked and in good condition. It is mandatory to have one of the park staff accompany you. The ones we met were very helpful and birds, plants and animals in the park.

title: Spoiled and exploited
text: This was presented to me as a pristine rain forest on the list of the unesco world heritage. You need to pay entrance and take a guide to get in. So far so good. But once you entered this 'pristine' rain forrest every 5 minutes you need to jump out of the way for a motorbike! The explanation is that locals have the right to drive through this 'pristine' rain forrest. Here and there there are cables and of course litter. Basically this is a tourist death trap, where you are milked by your local guide, selling you unwanted bottles of water, lunch boxes etc. You finally end up at a river with a waterfall where hundreds of other tourists take a swim and dump their litter. The unesco definitely needs to come and take a look here and make some improvements as indeed this forrest is beautiful but everything but pristine. Note: this trip is not intended for the weak of health the path is long (approximately 16km) and dangerous/slippery at places, especially when it is wet (it is a rain forrest after all) also prepare for bugs and leeches. The path is going up and down all the time in this weather it is physically very demanding. Do not accept anything from your guide without asking first if it is included, it was a scam going on when we did the tour in feb 2017. Clothes: good walking shoes, long trousers,long sleeves,deet, travel light. Only take water no need for lunch boxes, the swim in the river is optional

title: It's not called a rain forest for nothing
text: A wonderful place with many birds, animals and insects to see. You are advised to buy the special canvas leggings which you put on inside your shoes and which cinch at the knee, like long socks, as a deterrent against leeches. The track up the hill is very rough, with big stones, sharp stones, and boulders. This will be much easier to walk on with proper walking boots.

title: Easily accessible rainforest
text: We took the bus to deniyaya and stayed in the village for two nights. Our host offered us a tour through the rainforest and I can highly recommend it.The flora and fauna is incredibly diverse. Since it was the first rainforest for me I was quite amazed by the dense green network of plants and the intriguing background sounds of animals, togethe composing a unique atmosphere. We also saw animals like snakes, insects, birds, lizards and monkeys. After walking on small paths through the forest we finally arrived at a beautiful waterfall were you could swimm and even jump down. This was the absolute highlight. Concerning leeches, I only had one, we were told that January is dry season, therefore there are not so many.

title: Amazing for Birder's
text: Sinharaja Forest reserve is a rain forest located in the south-west of Sri Lanka. Sinharaja is a dense forest and contains an amazing variety of flora and fauna. This is a must-go destination for avid birders. One can sight most of the endemic birds of Sri Lanka in Sinharaja. Red-faced Malkoha, Sri Lanka Scimitar Babbler, Scaly Thrush, Green-billed Coucal, Ashy-headed LaughingThrush, Malabar Trogon.. were some of the gems that I sighted here. The most amazing sight was the mixed flocks unique to Sinharaja. You will find groups containing Malkoha, Trogons, Coucals, Starlings moving within the forest as a single flock. The forest canopy is very dense and may not provide the best photo opportunities. But Sinharaja should not be missed at any cost, for the variety of birds on display.

title: Great Place for Birders
text: We saw many endemic birds, found in Sri Lanka only. The Forest provides a guide, but we also had our own tour guide. The Forest guides do not speak a lot of English, but they can find the birds. We wore leech socks and did have leeches on our clothes. Tuck your shirt in. Wear a hat. Sunscreen, etc. Be prepared for heat and humidity.

title: Hot spot for Birders
text: Great birding from well defined trails wandering up and down through the rain forest. Park guide essential - and well,worth it- our guide knew all the calls and had the more difficult species staked out. Dry weather meant no problems with leeches.

title: Well worth the visit!
text: The Sinharaja Rainforest tour guide was one of the top must-do activities on our list and it certainly was worth it. Just a few notes for other fellow tourists: Should you wish to visit the rainforest, it takes approximately two and a half hours from Unawatuna. By car it should cost no more than 7,000 LKR there and back, and it is best to take a large vehicle due to the poorly constructed roads. Should you wish to have a guided tour (which I would highly recommend), they should not ask for more than 3000-5000 LKR which covers entrance fee, the tuk tuk ride to the beginning of the rainforest and the guided tour itself. Our guide (forgive me but I have forgotten his name) was absolutely brilliant – charming, knowledgeable and great with a camera. It is advisable to go earlier in the morning if one wishes to see lots of animals. Nevertheless, our guide managed to show us vipers, spiders, monkeys etc. even during the late afternoon. On both the 4km and 9km trek, you have the option of visiting natural waterfalls, and swimming in them (if we had known in advance we would have brought our swimming kit). Overall, it was a fantastic couple of hours and well worth the car ride.

title: A trek here will make you incredibly happy :D
text: Sinharaja is supremely tough to get to, but it's worth it! A trek with one of the guides here will take you through a dense, loud jungle. You'll see lots of stuff - from snakes, to endemic plants, to monkeys. Apart from that, those who like the water will be treated to multiple waterfalls, a lake with 'doctor fish' that nibble at your feet (free spa!) and swimmable areas. If you really like your nature - replete with Latin names and all that - you'll be even happier. Can't recommend this enough, and the nearby Rainforest Resort / Hostel is the best place to stay!

title: Rainforest with wild spices and poisonous snakes
text: Fortunately we had a good guide. He showed us many places with a different amphibiaan species especially poisonous snakes! He didn't talk fluent english but he tried to explain us everything what he found! Thanks to him we saw interesting species of plants and animals!

title: Beautiful but...
text: It is certainly an amazing forest. Thou visiting is limited experience as very difficult to see the so wanted animals. The most amazing has been seeing the forest at sunset, in the night with the fog, in the early morning, and driving along it on the north side!

title: Sinharaja Forest Reserve
text: Excellent reserve with many hard to find Sri Lankan endemic bird species. To get to the reserve you have to have a local driver in a 4x4 vehicle which quite often will be an old WW2 jeep. Once in the Reserve there is some walking and beware there are leeches.

title: Great whole day trip / Good wildlife, poor guide
text: Stayed at Rain forest View lodge near the Deniyaya entrance & had a bittersweet experience. While the forest was excellent.Guide spoke no English at all. Carry water and snacks.

title: Excellent tour
text: We went to Sinharaja from Unawatuna. It's around 90 kms away from Unawatuna. We started at 7.30 am from Galle & reached there by 10 am. Then we did 3 hours tour in forest reserve. We opted for shorter trail which is of about 7 kms. It was really a nice experience. Waterfall was most amazing of the trail. The forest is beautiful , clean & untouched. Our tour guide Vini was very helpful & knowledge person. He took special efforts to take close up pictures of snake, inserts & reptiles. We could not see any bird as we were bit late.Need to be at the place by 7 am for bird watching. The trail is bit difficult but view is amazing.

title: good birding
text: we came here for birding. accessed by jeep over some very rough tracks. have to have a National Parks guide and a minder. good trails. you need leech socks!

title: Ok if your passing...
text: Very quiet place, guide issued to you on arrival at park. Ours seemed a bit dis-interested. Trail along well used path. Saw a few birds, snake, plants. Ok if your passing but dont make a special trip to go.

title: Biodiversity hotspot
text: This is a wonderful place to experience nature. It is home to a myriad of wonderful birds, plants and animals - but be prepared that you will see just a small amount of what is here. Our guide was very knowledgeable, finding Sri Lanka Frogmouth for us when the rain had begun and all the birds had taken cover, but the visit is a walk out to the research centre then back along the same route - limiting the amount of ground that you cover, unless you take the more challenging path up to the cave.. In November it is usual for the rain to come from late morning for a few hours, and expect it to be heavy, so my advice would be to go first thing in the morning, before the rain so that there are more birds, animals and insects in view. The best place to see birds is in the clearings - there aren't so many of these so take your time when you find one and wait a while at these places hoping for a flock to pass through. It is advisable to take an umbrella. There are also leeches. To limit how much these little nasties get on to you tuck top/shirt into trousers, trouser bottoms into socks, then use leech socks if available - although I and my husband were using waterproof sealskinz socks and these were actually more effect than the leech socks that our guide used. Take alcohol wipes, in case any manage to attach. They tend to march on to potential hosts from the ground so keep laces short, tuck into tongue of boots/shoes if possible. Keep checking clothing for leeches - amazing how fast they move - and they show up more on light coloured clothes.

title: Wonderful
text: This is by far the greatest and fullest of life jungle/forest I have ever been to, not just in Asia. Lots of animals, endless breathtaking sounds and a feel of adventure - guaranteed.

title: Beatiful nature
text: Took the short hike around 3,5 hours. There is alot to see and its hard to see animals without a guide. Our guide spotted alot of small various species that we ourself never would of seen. End of the hike there was a smallwaterfall which you could take a swim in! Great experience!

title: Beautiful lowland raninforest
text: Such a diverse array of wildlife, different to the rest of the country. Had 2 days to visit and wish we could have stayed longer.

title: Not grandiose
text: This is not bad.. But simple than anything I have seen, in the 2 years I have lived in Sri Lanka. My walk has lasted only 4 hours to go and back. What the guide showed me wasn't spectacular (different trees, biggest squirels..)okkkk. It's tood bad that the back way is in the same way as the first one. So we see everything twice. When we arrived at the waterfall, I was expecting to a big one but it's not. Anyway, the small environment is lovely. Enough breathtaking, you can enjoy the swim. You have to pay for the entrance + one guide, it's too expensive for what it is. I say again, I have seen so much better in the Center and the North!

title: Concentrated Biodiversity Experience
text: The walk in the rainforest was a great experience! you never know what you will see but there is always something to see, especially with a good guide. We had an excellent guide "Thandula", who not only speaks excellent english but really is an expert of the birds and animals of the park. I would highly recommend him. The park staff are very conscienscious about preventing people from littering in the park and hence it is very clean. It is a bit tedious to get to the park with public transport but definitely worth it!

title: Beautiful and interesting
text: In a 2-3h walk our guide showed us different plants and flowers (eg. gave us wild cinnamon to smell). Also, he spotted various animals: monkeys, giant squirrels, nice butterflies and lizards. At the end of the tour he took us off the broad/paved path and we climbed a smaller path through the forest (only for fit people and with solid shoes) All in all a very enjoyable and interesting walk.

title: Wow
text: Our 6 hour stroll into this Biosphere Reserve was beautiful. Our guide from the Sinharaja Rest was incredibly knowledgable having been guiding people for over 20 years. We saw giant squirrel, snakes, beetles and spiders (tarantula) and amazingly tall virgin forest. We had our packed lunch at a waterfall where we, and others, swam. A memorable and beautiful day.

title: Primary forest, lots of birds and lezard
text: My husband and myself did a one week trip in Sri Lanka. We started in Ella and then joined the Sinharaja forest. Such an amazing experience, full of birds songs, waterfalls, swim in natural pools. However, to enjoy, you need to be Ok with humidity and potentially some insect. Usually, this is not my cup of tea, but for one day, this is perfectly fine. Tours are organized with guides, either whole day or half day. If you are lucky, you could also find some different kind of Monkeys. Enjoy the show !

title: An OK walk - not a lot to see
text: We visited here with two friends and our driver, who also organised a spotter/guide to help us identify things along the way. Our walk was along quite an easy track and we could go as far as we wanted. In fact we went to the end of the track and back again which was about four miles, in five hours (because we were stopping and photographing) with a half an hour stop in the middle. We saw some endemic species of birds and plants and my highlights were pitcher plants which were fantastic and which I had never seen growing in the wild, and a pair of Sri Lankan frogmouth birds that the ranger knew about at the side of the track. We also saw a lovely tiny green snake at the entrance to the walk which we photographed. Overall, not particularly strenuous if you stay on the main path. Leeches were mentioned as being a major problem on this walk but we didn't have leech socks and only our guide got leeched, just the once.

title: As a nature enthusiast - "Heavenly"
text: If you love trees, water falls, absolute quiescence and hiking, this is most definitely a must visit when in Sri Lanka. We entered through the district known as 'Ratnapura' which was a 2.5 hours drive by car from Colombo. It is vital to take the highway from Colombo or face traffic which could lengthen the journey to anywhere between 4 to 6 hours. Furthermore, it is extremely important to bring along a pair of 'leech socks' in order to hike the forest with ease. These socks are sold at the souvenir shop at the entrance. Loved every moment in the forest. Such a feeling to breathe in that fresh unpolluted air inside the forest with only the sounds of water falls, birds and the occasional monkeys resonating around the surrounding. The guides are extremely educated on the surrounding and its inhabitants. We came across monkeys, varied types of butterflies, birds, fishes and lizards most of which were endemic to the beautiful island of Sri Lanka. Further down we found a beautiful little zen like area where the water flows gently from the main water fall that is in the area. We spent more than an hour there just sitting and gazing at the flowing water and listening to the beautiful sounds of the forest.

title: Facilities for tourists are really quite inadequate (but rain forest is amazing)
text: (1) Entrance from north side of forest is accessed through small roads and some stoney tracks - fine for vehicles etc but not a main road by any stretch of imagination - not many signs to it until you get much closer. (2) Car park right by the tourist entrance - very basic facilities - toilets are just a hole in the ground covered with a loo lid. (3) Seems to be very random if they open their "cafe" which is just a basic coffee tea facility (when we visited midday it was "closed" and no reason given) (4) Guide takes you up - they really need to get this better - our guide spoke virtually no english except single words "spider" "snake" etc - if they can't speak the language a guide book in a different language saying what you see would be really beneficial to take with them. (seems we just sadly got the wrong guide as other reviews say many are excellent) (5) Admission fee reasonable no objection to paying. (6) Guide didn't warn us about leeches. The tourist "centre" if you can call it that sells leechproof socks. Buy them and put them on. We discovered that they don't just live in water and will drop from trees or leaves onto to the ground or you if they sense a chance at a blood meal - so put full covering on legs and top. If you do get bitten it is harmless just a nibble pain and then you will bleed for a while but stops - you will not die :) (7) We saw snakes, reptiles, monkeys, spiders, all sorts so very worthwhile. (8) Suggestion bring tea, coffee, drinks, snacks etc as could find there is nothing at the tourist centre on arrival or after. Busy time is mornings when tour buses arrive lunchtime less so. Best time to see birds are morning trips but plenty of other stuff on view other times!

title: Nice, if you bring leech socks
text: -We booked the 10h Tour to the Lions Rock directly at our hotel (Sinharaja Rain Forest View Villas) and paid $95 for 2 people including a lunch packet. From what I could find in the internet it seemed like a fair price. I think it was $65 for 2 people for the 6h Waterfall tour. - we asked for a guide that spoke good English. Thank God we did, because I don't know who were would have gotten otherwise. Our guide "spoke English", but hardly understood anything - we felt that our guides (we had 2, one who "talked" to us and one who did the guiding) weren't really prepared for the job. He didn't check with us, if we had enough water, the right clothes and when we came across a snake that be hadn't spotted before he got really worried and has quite a panicky look on his face. I don't want to think about what would have happened, had we been bitten!! I don't think they could have helped us. - leeches in abundance!!! We knew there would be leeches and we had them before, but not like this. We would have enjoyed the tour a lot more, had we had leech socks. -the tour was challenging and we were glad when the guiding guide offered to take our backpack (and we're both not unfit). The way was maybe too challenging to enjoy the scenery and you had to watch your every step, make sure you don't get sucked dry by the leeches when you stopped. In hindsight the 6h Tour might have been the nicer, if more "touristy" option. And it very much depends on your guide, which we couldn't really influence :-(

title: I wish I knew the name of our guide!
text: Shortly, we'll be uploading the photo of our guide. We can't remember his name but he was incredible. He was so sweet, friendly, helpful, knowledgeable and willing to show us the best of Sinharaja! We learnt so much along our way but I won't put too much on here as it's great to learn as you go. He asked us if we wanted to go on a long walk uphill. We was exhausted when we finished but we got to the highest point of Sinharaja on top of a mountain and the view at the top was spectatular. A once in a lifetime sort of view. Besides this, we saw so many animals, plants and insects. Our guide was very funny too as we had a little giggle as we struggled up the mountain and he hopped up as if it was the easiest thing ever! He was a little shocked to learn we didn't walk hills most of the time! It was something so normal to him. He showed us how to drink the river walk which we did (reluctantly) but don't be scared as the water was so fresh and cold and I couldn't quite believe it wasn't half frozen bottled water as it tasted so nice. This was one of our best days in Sri Lanka and I think this was definitely because of the staff as well as the beautiful things Sinharaja has to offer. You have to visit this place! You'll miss out if you don't go!

title: Interesting 3 hours in the rain forest
text: A couple of previous reviewers have referred to this as 'rainforest lite' and that would probably be a fair description. However, that is not necessarily a bad thing. The paths are well made and mostly flat and make for relatively easy walking. We booked an official park guide to take us round and he was very good at spotting many small reptiles, birds and insects. Don't expect to spot much in the way of furry animals here though other than a few monkeys. We were lucky enough to see a couple of large groups of purple faced monkeys at quite close quarters which was fantastic. We had hoped to see the waterfalls we had read about but it seems we had entered the park at the wrong entrance - due to the fact that our driver had never been here before and did not know to take us to the Galle entrance. Doesn't compare with some more unspoilt tropical rainforests but enjoy it for what it is - an enjoyable 3 hour walk in some beautiful scenery.

title: Disappointing visit to a wonderful place
text: This forest is a wonderful place, a beautiful tropical forest, quite some interesting animals and a beautiful waterfall. However, it was very disappointing that there is no fixed prices, that there is motorbikes driving in the forest all the time (in order to reach a village nearby), there is dogs that the guides do not try to keep out and our guide was smoking the whole tour. It doesn't seem like they take very good care of this incredible place, and that is very sad.

title: Interesting walk
text: Interesting 2-4h walk, particularly if you have not walked in a tropical forest before. The paths are made partially of cement slabs and rocks, and are well market throughout. Some parts are not suitable for disabled people, but good for children. The sight of elephant tracks (and dung) make it exciting for the children. If you use a guide, don’t expect great naturalist or linguistic skills, but they have a trained eye for interesting plants and invertebrates. You will struggle, however, to find a single leech or mosquito. This is the rainy season, and the most experienced guides walked in shorts and flip-flops, which is telling. Swimming is safe. The paths inside the park are crossed daily by hundreds of local people, often in motorbikes, and certainly not accompanied by guides. In addition to all the visitors, this makes it a crowded park, particularly in the paths close to the entrances. The entrance ticket to the park costs now about Rs 600. One should not have to pay more than that for a guide (per adult). This is already a bit higher than the Sri Lankan tourists in small groups pay for a guide. The best strategy is to sit in a restaurant by the park entrance, enjoy a beer or an excellent curry, and negotiate the price with one of the local villagers that are, so-called, certified guides. The first offer you get may be 5 times higher than the park fee, which is obviously a swindle. Take it easy, prices will come down. But, remember that by 17:30 it starts to get dark. Plan to arrive early.

title: Interesting walk in the nature
text: It is a small rain forest and you don't get to see a lot of it if you take a three-four hour tour. But all and all it was a nice walk. We spotted some monkeys, giant squirrel, snakes, lizards, scorpion, spiders,... And we had a chance to swim in the river by one of the waterfalls, which was refreshing and fun.
