I think we spent around 1.5 hours in the Forest and we saw deer, birds, butterflies and monkeys.

title: Wild...
text: Sri Lanka is also famous for wild life and majority of the land is reserved for sanctury. This one is smaller one and you can sight monkeys, deers, wild boars and birds.. if lucky.

title: Disapointing
text: Bit disappointed by our visit here today. We had a lovely walk through the jungle and the view point over the city is lovely a peaceful (in my opinion even better than 'the' Kandy view point) however we saw very few wildlife. We had to really scour our surroundings as we walked to see three dear in the distance. Didn't see any birds or boar, despite looking around for ages. Not sure if it was the time of year, the fact it has rained, the time of day..m but we were walking around for just over two hours, really looking and being quiet and saw very little. Entry price was reasonable though and the history behind the reserve is interesting. So I don't regret going, just bit disappointed. Don't expect too much! You had to walk up a bit of a hill to get to the entrance but after that, not too hilly.

title: Very beautiful forest for the Nature Lovers.
text: We were visited Kandy you should not miss the opportunity to spend a few hours in Udawattekele Sanctuary where you can see deer, wild boar monkeys and possibly some birds. As soon as you have aid your entrance fee you will see the rather muddy Royal Pond then you can wander on to the viewpoint and the information center before hiking round the other side and seeing the meditation caves. Actually this is really a beautiful forest and Silent environment mind free place. This place to near at Kandy lake and Sri Daladha Maligawa(Temple of Tooth).

title: Beaut spot
text: Lovely quiet spot for a morning's meandering.Didn't see too many animals but should we it's their territory.

title: Beautiful Walk
text: We (my wife and I) booked this through the hotel we were staying at, the Cinnamon Citadel, Kandy. We only had a few hours to spare before moving south down the country and were glad we took this opportunity. We were picked up in a car at the hotel, and driven there in what only took about 15 minutes. It was early morning, roughly 7am, and the park was empty. Other than our guide we did not see anyone else. This made it all the more peaceful. If you're an early riser, i'd recommend going early. It lent itself to some wonderful scenes of mist clearing and the sun starting to break through the trees. Good photo opportunities. As others have said, there are plenty of monkeys going about their daily business. Additional wildlife we encountered included a deer, a few species of butterfly and a kingfisfer. One of the unexpected points of note, was the enourmous Puss-well (Giant Liana) tree. It's about 200 years old and spreads over an area of nearly 2 hectares. That information is thanks to a photo I took of the sign rather than my memory, but the way which the trees branches twisted and grew were certainly memorable and something i'd never seen before. There were longer routes to take, so you could spend more than the couple of hours we did, depending upon how much you enjoy such walks. The scenary within the forest was very good throughout and you also get to see some good views over Kandy at one point. Wildlife was intermittant, which was fine for us. The sections we did were fairly flat. There was one steep section to see a cave, which was optional rather than on the main route. If you book via that hotel, we found the guide Nithan to be very knowledgable. He is someone who is massively passionate about wildlife, and we got on to talking about his current research papers on plastics and how Sri Lanka might implement policies to address the amount currently impacting the wildlife in Kandy and beyond. Overall we throughlly enjoyed this and would happily recommend to enyone who likes fairly easy walks in a beautiful surrounding with a spot of wildlife.

title: Heavenly if you like nature walks
text: Even tho our visit was short, it was a highlight of Kandy. We saw monkeys only. Perhaps mid-afternoon was not the best time to go. We did see a giant monitor lizard and a scorpion. The trees were magnificent. We walked past it at first, it is set back off the road by the side of a Buddhist edifice. The loos were nice. It was a bit expensive and getting past the bureaucracy in the hut was very amusing and colonial

title: Quiet, pleasant walk
text: This was a pleasant walk, mainly on the level and in the shade of trees. We only saw one deer and a few birds, but lots of monkey action including a turf war! Easy to find your own way around and a great view over Kandy at the southwest corner. Allow 2-3 hours with stops for monkey viewing. One toilet but no other facilities so bring water but in a non-disposable container.

title: Peaceful escape from the city
text: A great escape from the hustle and bustle of the city. Once you enter the reserve its so peaceful with just the sounds of the animals, hard to believe how close to the city you really are. Nice easy stroll around the loop took around an hour. Nice to do the afternoon to get out of the intense heat and under the shade of the trees!

title: within yet away from the city
text: The best time we spent in Kandy was the walk in this forest reserve – we liked it much more than visiting the Tooth Temple and the Dance Show. We were wondering whether leeches would be there, but we haven't seen any, despite the heavy rains a couple of days before our visit. There were hardly any tourists there in the morning (around 9–10 am). We spent two hours walking there, before we didn't have much more time, but we could have spent three or more.

title: Lovely place to stroll that feels a million miles away from the noise of Kandy city
text: Great easy to follow paths around jungle area on edge of the city. Choice of 3km or 5km routes and the charming old lady at the entrance is only to happy to help. Its only 660 rupees

title: Wonderful forest park
text: The price when we visited was 650 per person (around 4 usd) which was totally acceptable. Compared with the botanical gardens it's cheap and we liked it way way more. It's a large and beautiful forest park, and we saw tons of diverse trees, monkeys, birds and even got lucky and saw two spooked deer! Definitely a highlight of our Kandy visit!

title: Beautiful forest walk
text: A lovely place for a quiet walk where you can spot a few birds and admire the huge trees. The route is about 5km if you follow the map right around There is a viewpoint where you can see the town of Kandy below. At certain points along the trail there are massively long lianas which cross the path. You can also spot monkjac deer, and of course some monkeys. Look out for an Asian Paradise flycatcher with its long orange plumage. If it rains, as it did for part of the time when we went, beware of leeches which might manage to get on your skin. The visitor centre has interesting facts that you can read. There is a modest entrance fee.

title: Great nature walk in Kandy
text: There’s only one entrance into this reserve so make sure you head to the right place. It shuts at 5pm, we got there at 4pm but the lady gave us a map and showed us the walk that would bring us back by 5pm. You have to leave where you come in. It was a very peaceful walk at that time. We didn’t see much wildlife apart from a few monkeys and birds but still very enjoyable walk. You have to pay a small entrance fee but it’s worth the money. There’s a great point to view kandy from on the walk and some good places to stop and take photos

title: An escaid
text: Not too much to see but a cracking view half way around and nice and peaceful away from the hustle and bustle of Kandy. For £3 a person, worth it.

title: Stunning!
text: This is only just out of town but high up - you get several good views down over the lake and town. It is a huge forest with enormous trees, excellent birdwatching, monkeys and we also saw a wild pig. It is beautifully shaded to walk around but take plenty of water - despite a signpost to a cafeteria, we certainly didn't come across anything! Very few people there when we visited - it was very peaceful.

title: Simple Circuit Though Mature Forest, Some Wildlife
text: My phone navigation was a little confusing - made it look like there were many entrances. But, in actuality, there is only one and the area is mostly fenced off from any other access. It makes for a pleasant walk in the heat of the day. A lot of mature trees with mature vines. You can see through the forest in every direction, but there are only a couple views outside the forest. I encountered monkeys that were fairly shy. I saw deer tracks in mud. There were other people walking. Everyone kept pretty quiet.

title: Great walk / visit to Udawattakele Royal Forest Park.
text: In the centre of Kandy - a real gem. Biodiverse as it comprises wet and dry zone species. Lovely few hours walk (start early), well trodden paths, fantastic bird life (a guide to identify species may be a consideration).

title: Scenic walk with wildlife overlooking Kandy
text: We couldn't believe this sanctuary exists so close to a bustling city like Kandy. Yes you can hear some vehicle noises but you're in Kandy! We saw wild boar, barking deer, lots of monkeys and birds. The walk is a little steep at the beginning but levels out and it loops around a large lake. We stopped at the information centre and spent some time watching the monkeys playing in the bamboo. The paths are wide and it will take an hour or so to view but we totally enjoyed it.

title: Nice place for a quiet walk
text: The map doesn't exactly match the actual paths but it's close enough, and not so large that you'll get lost anyway (you can always just retrace your steps). In a couple of hours we walked every path in the sanctuary. It's very peaceful and we only occasionally saw other people. It's a pleasant walk in the jungle and we saw plenty of wildlife.

title: Decent Forest Excursion
text: Steep climb up to the entrance but once inside the park it's pretty easy walking on wide pathways. Took about an hour to walk the loop. I entered at 4 pm and was under the assumption they closed at 6 pm. Glad I didn't dawdle, as when I exited at 5 pm it looked like they were waiting for me so they could lock the gate for the night. Summary: the walk was interesting but not really spectacular scenery. Saw a few monkeys but no other animals. There are some shady benches for resting/contemplation. Bathrooms had western toilets. I knocked the rating down a peg because of the price - not really worth 660 LKR. But if you're in Kandy and burning out on all the traffic and honking horns, and if you don't mind the entrance fee, it may be worth a diversion for a walk in the woods.

title: Surprisingly hidden gem.
text: Considering we were in the sanctuary for around 3 hours, we didn't encounter many other people, and we couldn't believe we were still in Kandy. This is the perfect way to escape the hubbub of the city and see a lot of wildlife. We saw barking deer, lots of monkeys and lots of birds. Beware of leeches, wear socks and trainers!!

title: Lovely walk
text: Beautiful forest with perfectly marked paths. There is a short 3km circuit or a longer 5km one. We spent a bit over an hour here. We saw loads of monkeys and some deer.

title: One of my favourite places in Kandy
text: Udawatta Kale is one of my favourite places in Kandy. If you are the type who loves taking a silent stroll in the woods, get lost in the past or dream aimlessly, with just the sound of your own footsteps & leaves dancing in the wind, then this is the ideal place for you. I always make sure that I go for at least a short walk whenever I visit this ancient city, Kandy. One thing I always miss, is the Garrison Cemetery inside the forest. Definitely next Time :)) Entrace ticket: Rs30 - 20/02/16

title: A nice and easy walk
text: An old royal forestpark today open for public for a fee of cirka 650 rupies. I do not argue the fee because I guess they need money to maintain the accessebility to the park. As a tourist you get a little folder with a map. This map and som extra googlemap ;-) was nice to have when walking the roads and paths leading thru the park. Plenty of monkeys (very calm) and butterflies but not much else of fauna. The flora is nice but not exceptional (i visited in april pretty warm and dry). I enjoyed the park just taking it easy and enjoying the shade. Well worth a visit. The entrypoint is from de westside of the park.

title: cool place
text: had a wonderful time in a cool place never been to a place like this with lots of monkies and had a wolk around

title: The lady asked us where we were from before answering about the cost of tickets
text: You will see everything you can see inside on the way there(giant bamboo, wild boar, monkeys..). 600rs per person??! Give me a welcome drink or something!

title: Peaceful haven just outside of Kandy
text: It is amazing that there is this large nature sanctuary just a stone's throw away from the hustle and bustle of Kandy town. We had a lovely 2 hour hike around this peaceful forest. Wonderful trees and we saw a deer and some wild boar, as an added bonus. Be warned however. The map that you get give is terrible and the sign posts along the path are misleading, but forget about getting from A to B in a hurry. Meander and take in the sights. Lovely.

title: A welcome peaceful retreat
text: This place is beautiful , full of amazing sounds from the animals and was a welcome escape from the heat and noise of Kandy. It's unbelievable that this gem has such a busy city on its doorstep. We went mid afternoon and walked around for a couple of hours.

title: Nothing much to do here
text: The place has a pathway and trail to walk around but other than a couple of vista points wherein you could see the Tooth Temple and Kandy Lake from far the place overall is not much.

title: Lovely walk
text: We caught the bus into the city and then walked to the forest. The paths are well marked although we found the map given to us on entry slightly difficult to follow. Lovely walk, really peaceful place with lots of clean air which is much needed after the pollution of kandy traffic. We saw lots of monkeys, deer and turtles in the lake. Missed the wild boar unfortunately. One of the nicest places we visited in kandy.

title: Pleasant
text: Had a nice walk through here keeping off the hottest of the day's sun. Plenty of monkeys for entertainment. The walk could benefit from some extra signage/better maps as we managed to get a bit lost (as did several others we met) near the German Hermitage. But other than that it was very pleasant.

title: A quiet area to wander
text: Udawattekele can be reached by walking from Kandy but it is uphill, a tuktuk cost us £1.50 and we walked back down. The forest has well marked tracks to follow, is quiet and shaded and very enjoyable. We were there early afternoon and did not see many birds or animals but still appreciated the peace and quiet.

title: Nice walking area, even with stroller
text: This is a nice area that you easy reach with tuk-tuk. There are good paths so you can walk with a stroller. Nice forest and fine viewpoint over Kandy. Monkeys, pigs, deer, turtles, water monitor were observed.

title: Best thing in kandy
text: Spent an afternoon walking around in the park. Saw a bunch of monkeys, some deer and wild boar. Lovely walks in the woods.

title: Great forest and walk
text: Reading the review on this site we were very hesitant to go. But the forest is a really rewarding experience, The forest is beautiful, the paths are very easy to walk on and not artificial, so you have the feeling of being in a forest and not in a park. We were alone for most of the time. It’s definitely worth the couple of dollars of entrance fees.

title: Green hideaway in heart of Kandy
text: If you need to escape the City, but don’t want to have to travel out too far or pay too much, then this is a great option. Easy to walk there and then walk around (I would say child friendly), it costs half of what the Botanical Gardens does (662 rupees)- it still annoys me when you have to pay to enter such places, but maybe I have been spoilt back home with free entry. Anyway, it is a very well preserved natural park full of wildlife. I saw deer, butterfly, monkeys and even an eagle soar overhead. You can hear so much more though. I spent a lovely 2 hours wandering around the paths and enjoying the view out across Kandy from the viewpoint. Really glad I went.

title: "GOOD PLACE" KANDY
text: located between beautiful ......green hills ........with lovely wind .....good walk wear proper comfortable peaceful walk with lots of wildlife

title: Morning Stroll
text: Perfect morning stroll with wildlife--- way to escape the busy overwhelming streets of Kandy. I absolutely loved this park--- it was a good walk around.

title: Beautiful Place
text: We had a wonderful walk at this place. There are a lot of fish in this water. We were giving them food and they were just coming close to us. We also had a beautiful view of this lake from our apartment.

title: Beautiful peaceful walk with lots of wildlife
text: We went to the sanctuary on a Monday morning and had a wonderful experience. We were literally the only people in the sanctuary aside from a couple workers cleaning the paths - it was very peaceful. We saw barking deer, monkeys, wild boars and heard and saw about a hundred bird species. The sanctuary is very well maintained. We spent about 3 hours there and think the money for entry was well worth it. You do not need a guide, although they may be able to provide explanation of the sanctuary’s history (we read about it before and after and found that was enough). The only thing to watch out for is the leeches. We only had an issue with this when trying to hike to the lookout (which in the end we couldn’t find - it may be overgrown by large trees now or we may have missed the trail as there are a few leading to the top). The leeches are quite small but easy to spot wriggling up your shoes. Spraying your shoes/feet and legs with insect repellent beforehand would solve this problem. It was also raining a little off and on while we were there so you may not have this issue on dry days. Enjoy the sanctuary and keep it as clean as it was when we visited!

title: Not worth the money
text: A nice walk in the forest but cost to foreigners is now about 1100 rupees ($10) and not worth it. We may have been unlucky as saw or heard few birds. Saw monkeys. Nice view over Kandy from top. Paths are well kept and clean, and quiet place to walk but way way too expensive and had to argue with booth personnel for change. He had change but did not want to give it out.

title: Lovely place to stretch your legs near Kandy
text: This is a lovely forest close to Kandy town. As the streets are so busy we loved the opportunity to be able to walk around freely. The entrance fee for two of us was 1350 rupees. We saw lots of gorgeous monkeys and had some friendly dogs walk with us for awhile. My husband also saw a large snake cross the path (maybe 2m)!! The track is easy and not muddy, we were fine in flip flops. I was a little bit worried after the snake sighting but I'm sure it's fine if you stick to the paths.

title: Quiet forest walk in the centre of Kandy
text: It is hard to imagine you are so close to the noise and bustle of Kandy city centre as you walk through along the paths of this former royal forest. It makes a cool peaceful interlude in sightseeing

title: A wonderful walk in the park, and only a stone's throw from the town center
text: If you are visiting Kandy you should not miss the opportunity to spend a few hours in Udawattekele Sanctuary where you can see deer, wild boar monkeys and possibly some birds. As soon as you have aid your entrance fee you will see the rather muddy Royal Pond then you can wander on to the viewpoint and the information center before hiking round the other side and seeing the meditation caves. This is really a beautiful forest which shelters you from the heat of Kandy, and gets you away from the polluted city due to exhaust fumes. there are plenty of benches to rest on and you will see many monkeys.

title: Best thing in Kandy
text: This should really feature much higher on the list of things to do! It’s a lovely hours walk around the jungle and it’s in the middle of the city!! Saw some monkeys and jungle dear and the vegetation is amazing just look out for leaches. The only annoying thing was that they wouldn’t let me go on my own so the tuk tuk driver had to come with me - for safety - as I’m just a woman...grrr

title: A jungle in the middle of the city
text: We spent 2 hours waliking in this Forrest which is basically located right above the temple of the tooth, but is unknown to most tourists. We Saw wild boars, monkeys, birds. There is a great viewpoint over the lake & city. It is a really relaxing activity to do to escape Kandys pollution and noise. Recommended!

title: A great walk
text: This is a jungle nature reserve just a stones throw from the busy centre. It felt as though we were the only people there. You can walk for miles through it. There is a rangers hut with an interesting display of the wildlife you may see.

title: Great walk
text: A peaceful place to escape the city and go walking in the forest Lots of birds and monkeys A pleasant series of trails exist which vary from about a mile up to three miles in length

title: Wildlife walk
text: Went to the entrance by tuk tuk and then walked one of the trails on the map we were given. Huge trees with amazing lianas trailing over them. Great treat was a large group of monkeys crossing the path and completely ignoring us whilst playing / squabbling amongst themselves

title: Not worth the entrance fee. Only if you have extra time (and money) to spend.
text: How to get there by foot: Indentify Kandy municipality council on the map and walk there. The building will be on your left, you continue up on that main street. A panel will then point you in the direction of the entrance (always straight on anyway). The entrance fee is only 30LKR for Sril Lankan people. But for the "foreigners", who are of course very wealthy, it is 660LKR, which is "only" 22 times the normal price. Wouhou! Nevermind... you are now in the forest, and you can enjoy the walk. We spend 2 hours and saw lots of deers and monkeys. However, it is a forest, nothing special, and you can generaly walk in any forest in the world for free. The only reason we went there is because we had so extra time to spend in Kandy, but if you skip it, you won't miss anything. PS: for the amount of money they get from the "foreigners", they could at least clean the toilets (just after the entrance, on the left). They are absolutely disgusting and have never been clean, that's for sure.

title: Beautiful beautiful forest
text: We took a lovely walk along the trails of this lovely national park, enjoyed the greenery, the peaceful ambiance and the view of the city and pond below. Hard to believe such a gem is right in the heart of the city. You can choose the length of the trek you take. Advise the map handed at the entrance.

title: Has some good views of Kandy lake but not much else
text: The park visit involves a ticket and the office gives you a map to traverse the park. The park as such is not very clear in terms of routes and way and does not have much to do. It does have some good view points to see Kandy Lake and click a few pictures.

title: Live in the Planet of the Apes
text: A short drive from the Temple of Tooth, Kandy, the Udawatta Forest is truly a sanctuary. There are more than one walking routes, 3km, 5 km and 7 km. No cycling only walking. There is a small charge of Rs 30 per adult which is truly peanuts. Kandy's cool weather makes it an easy walk to do. The HUGE, and I mean HUGE trees along the way will take your breath away. There is a city view point which gave a beautiful view of the Kandy town and the lake. The forest makes you feel like a set of Planet of the Apes due to the sheer number of monkeys there....and they do follow you jumping from tree to tree in a thrilling reenactment of the movie. The little things were not aggressive at the same time we did not take any chances either...held on to our cameras and kept a watchful eye. The place is an environmental bliss with a lot of photo opportunities. The place has toilet facilities however in true SL style, they were wet.

title: Tranquility in the Trees
text: What a fantastic find just a short walk away from the crazy Kandy town! Grab some snacks and head here for a peaceful picnic amongst some fabulous fauna and flora. Udawattekelle boasts everything from butterflies to giant bamboos. If you enjoy a good wander in the woods, you'll love these windy walkways. The signs are sweet sentiment although they don't really point you in the right direction ! Don't worry all roads lead to home, or in this case the gate, so enjoy getting lost in mother nature's finest!

title: We loved visiting!
text: A great chance to escape the kandy chaos. Really peaceful walks in the shade. A chance to look out over kandy too which is a great photo opportunity. There is a fee for entry

title: Wildlife and mosquitos
text: You are in the jungle there are no real views however we saw a cobra, a python, deer and wild boar, and monkey. Also got bitten a million times by Mosquito's, it is not particularly picturesque but its good to kill a couple of hours if you have them.

title: Well...
text: Sorry to say it wasn't worth the entrance fee (660 LKR). We saw two water monitors playing in the lake which was cool. Other than that- got attacked by leeches (!) and lost the track couple of times due to the misleading signs. Would not recommend.

title: One of the best
text: A real forest full of intact old & traditional trees. It is huge and you can spend up to 3 hours walking & climbing. A tour guide is needed not to get lost and to explain about some details inside the sanctuary. Nice museum inside.

title: A cool peaceful walk in this bustling hot city.
text: Saw monkeys, barking deer, wild boar and a wide range of birds a peaceful place I. The heart of a bustling city.

title: Much cooler than expected and u can bicycle
text: After reading the reviews I was a bit nervous there would be thousands of leeches and even after a bit of bush bashing we came out leech free. We took our bikes around the 3km loop which was really fun. The forest was actually really nice for being surrounded by a large city, although not really the kind of place to go if you are expecting to see heaps of wildlife. There were lots of monkeys, butterflies, a deer, some turtle, fish but that's about all. Not so much in the way of birdlife. Worth checking out though for a nice stroll.

title: Worth having a wander
text: We visited the Royal Forest Patk, Udawattakele, yesterday morning and spend a couple of hours wandering around the interesting trails. It's a lovely rest from the sun, as the majority of the trail is shaded by the trees. We saw monkeys, wild boar, deer, birds & butterflies within the forest park and only a few other people. There are a couple of places to stop, admire the nature and perhaps have a picnic (although you might have to watch out for food-stealing monkeys). The park is definitely worth the 650 rupees fee (£3.25 - the price of a coffee in England) & you are given a map upon payment. The city viewpoint has lovely views of the lake and this is the first point we saw a family of wild boars. From here we tried to go down a trail that pointed to Garison Cemetery (on the park map), however a man called to us from the top of the stairs, saying it was out of the park grounds and we couldn't enter, so we turned back. Next we tried to find Kodimale flag point (the highest point of the forest), there was a sign pointing us in the right direction from the main track, success! But after following this track we found a five way fork with no further sign... we walked down a few of these paths but couldn't see to find the flag point. There is also a temple on the map however the route down to this was closed of, we did however find some of the caves which were interesting to see. In terms of nature & an enjoyable walk I would give the forest four stars, but because some of the points of interest in the park seemed difficult to find/we weren't permitted to see, (perhaps could do with a few more signposts,) I gave it three. Definitely would still recommend as an enjoyable way to spend a couple of hours.

title: Solo female traveller, be careful
text: I travelled in the late morning when there are people scattered in the park. A lone local man wandering around and asked me if I have water. Quite strange already. Then he followed me into a small dirt trail to a view point (with no view actually). Luckily there were a couple there. After that he followed me to like every single corner! And he seems to know the park really well so that he knew to take a short cut when I walked very fast to try to get rid of him. I made sure I was not mistaken by waiting and let him pass and retrieved to the crossing and saw him coming back. I did not know what he wanted. Finally I went with other travellers and exit the park. This totally ruined my experience of the park. I wrote this to warn other female solo traveller especially physically small like me to be very careful when you visit this park.

title: A piece of tranquility amidst the urban chaos
text: If you get tired of all the urban hustle and bustle, this forest sanctuary is exactly what you need. It is literally a piece of a rainforest right in the middle of the city. Simply the umbral paths, listen to numerous birds and observe the wildlife. Visit it early morning for best experience, as you will enjoy the incredible misty atmosphere with beautiful rays of light breaking through the canopy. You will also pretty much have the entire forest for yourself, as there’re no tourists there in the morning. The entrance price for foreigners is a tad too high though and it seems to only get higher as time goes by.

title: Dec holiday
text: This udawattekel is on the Kandy Lake . As I said all these buildings are well kept and painted white. It on the lake and I dud not visit inside.

title: An extraordinary oasis by the bustle of Kandy
text: We had a lovely walk in this jungle. In the space of just an hour we saw terrapin, barking deer, wild boar and a variety of birds.

title: Forest reserve adjacent to CBD in Kandy
text: Quiet forest with low visitor numbers in Kandy. Good place for a walk, the paths were hilly in places. Did not see any inside but the paths inside appeared to have been used by vehicles. Not much wildlife at the time (late in the day). Lots of tall tropical trees (some in flower), few local fruit trees, vines, a large waterhole were seen. This was effectively a small rain forest area, good for a few hours of walking.

title: Recommended!
text: We visited for three and a half hours. It cost 1255 rupees for two of us to enter. As usual locals got served first, so it took a while to get through. You get given a map but it’s not detailed so take a photo of the large map on a board on your left just as you go through. It details both routes you can walk. Easy to follow though there are some signs to direct you. Toilets near the entrance but really filthy and full of used sanitary products so I chose to pee in the woods! Take water as there’s nowhere to buy any refreshments. The forest is beautiful. We saw hundreds of monkeys very close up as they have no fear of humans. One stole my boyfriends lunch! We saw a deer too and heard many birds. The paths are easy to walk, I managed fine in flipflops. A welcome break from the traffic and easy to walk to from town. About 20 mins walk from the temple of the tooth relic.

title: Calm tranquil place a contrast to the centre of Kandy
text: A must see place for lovers of nature. The map isn't the best but part of the experience... Lots of places to explore and find ... A great few hours enjoying nature at its best. Not many people which helped make it enjoyable. We took a tuk tuk up and walked back down from the entrance.

title: Beautiful park
text: Very nice park just in the middle of the city. We saw some wildlife and had a quiet morning walking around.

title: Nice afternoon
text: Took a 3 hr walk around the place. They need a better map, but i managed to find my way back to the entrance okay. There is only one entrance into the park even though it looks like there are roads that go up into it from just beside the temple - the guards will let you know if you are wrong.

title: Great place for a morning excursion in the jungle.
text: It is kind of strange to take a walk in the jungle in the middle of the city, but Udawattekele offers just that. The paths are in the shade underneath the canopies, and there are quite a few birds around. Most of them are just heard, but sometimes, they can be spotted as well (bring binoculars). We didn't see any mammals but the toque macaques, but I understand they are there somewhere.

title: Nice visit
text: We came here to escape the hustle and bustle of the city. Spent a lovely couple of hours walking the trails, mainly shaded by the gorgeous trees which was a welcome relief. Saw lots of monkeys and a huge water monitor. Great viewpoint of Kandy and the lake. Nice to visit for a few hours respite!

title: Nice Walk
text: If you want to get away from the buzz of Kandy for a couple of hours, you can take a nice walk there. We saw some deer, turtles and fish in the pond by the entrance. There is also a German Buddhist monk there who does not mind visitors. It is safe and the paths are in good condition.

title: A breath of fresh air and incredible views walking distance from Kandy.
text: We visited around 3pm following a busy day roaming around Kandy town. As you walk up the hill past Trinity College you leave the hustle and bustle of Kandy behind and are met with peace; bar the sounds of nature. We followed a circular route around the sanctuary for a couple of hours seeing no one and enjoying the tranquility. Towards the end of the circuit you can go down to a beautiful viewing spot with stunning views over the city-perfect for sun set! As we returned the sun was setting and animals began to come out of hiding to feed and drink. We saw barking deer, boar and of course some cheeky langur monkeys. A wonderful, relaxing experience worth every rupee!

title: Fantastic place
text: This is a wonderful place to escape from the noise and traffic of Kandy. Just a short walk from the centre of town, you get to see local wildlife including monkeys, deer and maybe a snake or two. There is a brilliant view of the town from the viewpoint. Take water and enjoy a few hours away from it all....

title: Beautiful refuge with vile toilets
text: This is a beautiful jungle retreat in the heart of bustling Kandy. Really worth the 650 LKR entrance fee, and providing you go when it is dry there is a very obvious path with no leeches in sight. The view over Kandy at point 4 on the map is worth the admission price alone. However, do NOT go to the washroom where. The men's are 'OK', but the women's are in some kind of faeces-strewn dungeon. Seriously, avoid at all costs. Also, take some bottled water with you, as they don't sell any in the park.

title: quiet place
text: It is near by Kandy city centre. You can walk there. It is quiet place where you can rest and beautiful view on Kandy.

title: Stunning oasis of natural beauty right in the centre of Kandy
text: Quite a walk on a hot day, but SO worth it for all the wonderful macaques - we observed 3 different families and were awe struck by them. Wear proper walking shoes/boots and stay on the main paths and out of the wetter undergrowth to avoid the much-reviewed leeches.

title: Great walk with lots of wildlife
text: This was one of our first experiences of the Sri Lankan countryside and we saw lots of interesting wildlife including monkeys, deer, turtles, snakes etc. Definitely worth a visit, the only thing was that the signage was a little poor and we didn't go to all the places we wished to.

title: Peaceful retreat
text: After a morning being squashed at the Temple of the Tooth the Udawattekele Sanctuary was an oasis of calm. The walk through the forest was almost deserted apart from some monkeys, wild pigs and lots of butterflies. The viewpoint over Kandy was worth a visit as was the small visitor's centre which gave some information about the local wildlife. Despite being given a small map we managed to get lost as the signage is not good and the map is useless. However we thoroughly enjoyed the walk. make sure you wear sensible shoes as leeches lurk in the undergrowth.

title: A great walk through the forest/ Jungle but a little light on visible wildlife.
text: Worth going for the walk alone but don't hold out for much wildlife. We saw a few monkeys, a deer and a few birds but thats about it. The view of Kandy is great though. Don't fret about getting lost, though the sinage is terrible all paths lead to Kandy!

title: A green forest of tranquility within Kandy city
text: Amazing place. Quite unbelievable that Kandy city hosts such a great forest. Very clean and evergreen. The best place to look for tranquility in Kandy. Apart from the giant flora and fauna, the forest possesses a Kandy view point, a temple, a few caves, giant liana etc. There are some unfair restrictions for locals. No unmarried couples would be allowed inside and no food or bags would be allowed as well. No such restrictions for foreigners. Tickets 650LKR for foreigners and only 30LKR for locals. A must visit if you are travelling to hill country.

title: Spectacular trees
text: This is worth a visit and is an easy stroll through beautiful forest. I'm not sure why people complain of leeches because the main track is actually a dry dirt road fit for cars to drive on. Maybe it's different after a lot of rain, but just make sure you wear covered shoes. There are options of going off the main track into the forest for a more challenging hike and in that case you might want to be more covered up. It was a very easy 5km walk to go the whole way around on the main track. We didn't see any animals or birds other than 2 separate groups of macaques that were on the track. Im a little afraid of macaques and don't like going near them. Both times, the larger leader of the troupe came close to check us out but they mostly kept their distance from us. I've learnt it's always best not to feed them or show them you have any food at all. I don't look at them directly and just keep walking. There were deer or boar tracks everywhere so there must be quite a few animals in the forest, but it was a public holiday and maybe too many people around. It really wasn't crowded though, with only a few groups of people on the tracks. Even without seeing many animals or birds (we could hear them though), there are some amazing trees, the park is free of rubbish and it's a very calming and enjoyable walk. Cost 650 rupee and you get a leaflet/map.

title: A Nice Place
text: This is a bit isolated and not many people visit. But if walking in a forest is something you enjoy, then do spend half a day here. A local tuk tuk can drop you here. While returning you have a short walk to get transportation. Carry lots of water and some snacks as there is no food available. Ensure you have thick socks and good footwear, there are leeches lurking around. And an umbrella would be handy as it rains sometimes.

title: Favourite place in Kandy
text: This was actually my favourite place in Kandy. There was hardly anyone there, it was peaceful and teeming with wildlife. We saw baboons, wild boar, a snake, fish, birds and my friend swears he saw a crocodile! Great place for a leisurely walk to get out of the hustle and bustle and away from the coach loads of tourists.

title: Very nice but beware of leeches!
text: The Sanctuary is a wonderful place - wild vegetation and lots of animals. We saw monkeys, owls and deers. However, I strongly suggest to wear sneakers because of leeches, that you can find especially on the longer walks. The Lovers walk is very easy and charming.

title: Beautiful place outside of crazy coty
text: Loved this place. Could walk around and forget that you're in a bustling city. Nice and cool - shaded by trees. Saw monkeys, scorpions and some amazing tree formations. Only takes an hour or so if you don't do the full loop so easy to find the time!!

title: a quiet place just out of town
text: We did a big tour around the park and heared a lot of birds, but we didn't see any because we were not properly equipped. Be sure to put on you leech socks. The park is beautiful and there is a wide variety of plants.

title: Wonderful place for bird watchers and trekkers
text: We had a wonderful time walking in this sanctuary. They had maps and directions in place and we could walk on our own without the need of guides. Being birdwatchers, we could spot many bird species. We visited twice as we enjoyed the trek. Very calm place with sounds of birds chirping.

title: Udawattekele sanctuary
text: This is also a beautiful place . It was a royal forest reserve where no one was allowed to go . It feels nice walking around this place and learn the history.

title: Tree-mendous
text: Entrance price seems a little steep but this area has been conserved for nature since the 19th century. If you can get over that cost you'll probably see a load of trees, some lizards, a whole bunch of monkeys and maybe a deer or two. Not to mention the birds and the views over Kandy. A pleasant way to kill an hour or two and get away from the city. There's an easy 3km trail to follow.

title: Gorgeous walk
text: The sun is blocked by the tall, tall trees, and the birds are chirping to each other. Enjoy the walk, the many trails, the calm nature and seeing the different animals! You won't want to miss this place. We saw a snake, some monkeys, birds, butterflies, etc. such a lovely afternoon!!! Definitely recommend

title: Hidden gem
text: Although very close to the town even the tuktuk driver did not know where this was and had to ask directions! Very little visited this is a lovely peaceful place with abundant birdlife and mammals. Best time to go is the morning. The easy to follow trails - although the provided map is useful - are mostly shaded and open out every so often giving splendid views of the countryside and over Kandy.

title: Hidden Sri Lanka
text: This really is a sanctuary in the middle of the city. The old Royal Gardens and now a Nature Reserve and Forest is a haven from the hustle and bustle of central Kandy. Well worth a visit. See if you can find the hermit monk living in a cave.

title: For nature lovers, lovers and bird watchers
text: Entrance fee Rs 650 - Open 6 am to 6 pm If you're not fond of noisy cities or need a nature break this is the place to head for. I went there to birdwatch once in the late afternoon and again early the following morning. Had a fantastic time and saw many many exotic birds and other animals. No evidence of courting couples along Lovers Walk, I pretty much had the place to myself. There is also a great view point overlooking Kandy & it's lake from the hills above. Apart from the lovely vista the area was abundant with birdlife and kept me enthralled for a few hours. The forest was very dry and no leeches were about, If you want to go in earlier than 6pm, speak to the front gate person the day before and they will alert the guard to sell you the entrance ticket. I found there was plenty of birding outside and up to the gate to keep me busy until they opened. Staff were very friendly and helpful. Only negative was they had run out of maps. You can also organise for a guide (tip) to take you around and show you interesting things you might otherwise walk past.

title: peacfull walks close to the city
text: We enjoyed our visit to the sanctuary, it is very peaceful and not at all crowded. close to the city and easy to find, allow a couple of hours and take drinks there is no where to buy food or drink.

title: Escape the crowds
text: You quickly feel you are away from the city and you can get a very pleasant walk in. Leeches supposedly are a problem - but I think Ok when it's dry. Saw pigs and barking deer and macaques - hoping to see birds but probably need early morning trip for them.

title: Great for a walk in the nature, away from the busy city.
text: We had a lovely walk here. it was very easy and so quiet! You get to see monkeys, birds and wonderful view of kandy at a special point. It is really nice to have this wonderful park in the city of kandy. We recommend everybody to come and experience it!

title: Calm and dark
text: Udawattekele Sanctuary is a great place to have relaxing walk. It has tall trees, beutiful small lake at the middle of the forest. there is an Buddhist monastery (Thapowanaya temple) at the entrance of the forest. there is a place to the south of the small lake that you could see the Kandy town from the top. also this within the walking distance from the Kandy city. 20 minutes walk

title: Amazing jungle; just mind the scamming Rangers
text: This park is just incredible. The rangers at the front who sell tickets are scammers through. The entrance fee is 650 rupees. So I counted out 6 x 100 rupee notes and one 50 rupee note. They said ok and gave me a map (no ticket) but just 30 seconds after walking off they called me back and said that I was short 100 rupees. While my back was turned they pocketed one of the 100 rupee notes leaving only 5 on the counter. It was pointless to argue so I just handed over one more. Despite this the sanctuary is beautiful and well worth a visit. It's 250 acres just behind the Temple of the Tooth. Head west from the Temple up the street with the Pizza Hut and the Queen hotel on the corner. Go about 400m and turn right at the first set of traffic lights. Follow the winding road up the hill (easily walkable). The rainforest is pristine as it has been preserved by the Kings since the 1200s. The walking trails are well marked and easy. There are troops of monkeys which show no interest in people and which, unlike elsewhere in SE Asia are not aggressive and just walk calmly past you as if you're not there. It's amazing to walk past a whole family of monkeys so close (within a metre) while they mind their own business, carrying their babies and grooming each other with none of the aggressive behaviour you usually see in monkeys that live this close to humans. In a 2 hour visit I also saw wild boar and tiny deer. It's so peaceful and lovely and incredible to think it's an easy 20 min walk from Kandy city. Just closely watch what you pay as you go in!

title: Silent Forest Retreat in Nature so close to the city.
text: So close to bustling Kandy city, it is difficult to imagine one can find such a beautiful quiet forest area to enjoy nature and interesting walking tracks! This forest is reportedly over 200 years now, and feels a special place of history. I would suggest two to three hours be allowed so that one can truly enjoy the serenity of the forest, such a relief from the noise and business of the town. Only downside are the leeches, of whoch there appear to be a multitude! Mostly if venturing off the paths, however. Recently I am shocked to hear that it is being proposed to cut a bypass road through this beauiful, historic, nature reserve and forest!!! I certainly hope this never happens! We need to preserve every patch of forest on the planet, no matter how small! My advice...go visit this patch of paradise before it perhaps disappears! Have they also considered that the revenue from visitors fees will also be lost?

title: Not sure why they charge to enter...
text: Our walk around the sanctuary was nice, nothing extraordinary. There were lots of monkeys which at first excited me greatly, until I realised there are monkeys everywhere in Sri Lanka, and I didn't have to pay to see them. We didn't see anyone other than park rangers on the walk which was lovely and relaxing, but again confused as to what we were paying for. At the end of the walk we found ourself having to exit the reserve through a dodgy area, we ended up on a back road behind a temple scrambling over plants. According to the map, this was the exit. At the bottom there was a chained up elephant which left me in tears, he looked so sad and badly treated. Overall we had a nice walk in the sanctuary but wouldn't recommend it especially with the price tag.

title: Without many sites
text: A cozy walk in a circle for about 1.5 hours. Not many sites and the signs along the route are not so detailed and informative. We even could not find the German caves. Can skip for limieted time.

title: Great place for a quiet walk
text: This forest is pretty easy to navigate without a guide, using the map given out at the entrance. Even if you do lose your way, you can't go too wrong and you'll inevitably find your way back to the entrance. The forest is really lovely and there's a lot of wildlife. We saw lots of monkeys as well as wild boar, deer, a snake and some nice birds. A great way to spend a couple of hours and also a good way to avoid the heat of the sun.

title: Beautiful
text: A beautiful and Fantastic place to see lots of wildlife ..Loved the hike into this sanctuary, we saw monkeys and birds. A must visit place.

title: Wow
text: A lovely rain forest with a huge "pus wela", which covers 2 acres and is over 200 years old. Mind the many leeches, which are all over the place after rain. Although leeches are not dangerous, their bites hurt, so don't wear sandals! We saw monkeys, a boar and many birds.

title: Nice forest, but nothing special
text: The entrance fee is OK (650 Rps per person) and you get a map. The map is fine, but we couldn't find some of the caves, which are indicated on the map and the signposts in the park. We are birdwatchers, so we walk very slowly, listening for every sound and looking for every movement in the trees or in the understory. Although the sanctuary is on the edge of Kandy, you here the sounds of the city all the time and a few times a car was driving on the main track. We liked the big group of macaques, which are hanging around the entrance area. We liked the walk and the sanctuary, but except for some spots with Giant Bamboo or beautiful vines it felt like an ordinary forest. That's why we give 3*.

title: A typical forest but near the city
text: I don't know how many people choose this place as their another attraction in Kandy, but this is a very good place to travel for nature lover. You wont feel that you were so close to Kandy city center.

title: A bit of a disappointment.
text: As a "birdie" I had expected this to be a rich source of interest, but it is composed almost entirely of forest, and viewable birds were at a distinct premium! There were very few other visitors, and we all seemed to be outnumbered by soldiers in combat gear with AK47s. They were very friendly, but their presence was a bit unnerving! Then there were the persistent leaches that went for my legs after a brief rain shower. All very entertaining, but not quite what I'd expected!

title: advanture experience
text: we had an advanture when we were there. we walked slowly in this forest. suddenly our leader sayed to us "do not stop and run please run". we can not see anything or any animal but while we were runing he explained some worms with ability to seek your blood are here and if you stay and stop any where they attack you, if any person like to know what happen for us please contact with my email address: hkhosrojerdi@gmail.com

title: Tranquillity at its finest
text: If you have an hour or two to spare whilst visiting Kandy I would highly recommend making a stop at Udawattakele! The entrance fee is around 550 rupees, and this entitles you to a 3-4km walk around the forest area, there are even wild monkeys all over the forest which was so lovely to watch. My only criticism is that the sign posts are very poorly labelled and I got lost a few times!

title: Well maintained jungle area, with vines and monkeys
text: We went with our elementary aged children. There are broad and smooth dirt road type paths, as well as hiking trails. There are lots of monkey, and even vines you can swing on. We had a very nice time; I'd like to return. There are bathrooms scattered throughout, but no drinking water.

title: A tranquil haven
text: Udawattakele Royal Forest Park is an amazingly tranquil haven just above the cultural centre of Kandy. It is tamed jungle with a number of well constructed paths running through it. I was very impressed by the giant liana and we saw monkeys and a deer. The entrance fee of about $10 for the two of us was a bit steep but fine if the money goes to preserving this magic area. Also a nice temperature being very shady.

title: Hugely overpriced for what if offers
text: If you are planning to go there, get prepared to pay 650 rupee at the entrance, this came as a big surprise to me as this is almost half what you would pay to enter the infamous temple of the tooth located in the same city. It is a 15 minute walk from the temple of the tooth, last stretch is a walk uphill. There is a gate and a guard charging tourists at the entrance which I found very opportunistic and unpleasant, especially that price asked is expensive Sri Lanka standards and you are given nothing in return. Inside, there are paths between trees leading to a lake. You can also see birds and monkeys along the way. (Big area) If you have time to kill in Kandy and feel like a walk in nature, go for it, but to be honest, I think there is plenty of beautiful natural places to check out in Sri Lanka without having to pay an entrance fee!

title: A wonderful refuge and 5min from Kandy
text: It is unbelievable that this sanctuary is so close from.the city and so peaceful and serene. There are parts where you only hear birds...

title: Great place to visit
text: This is a hidden gem in Kandy. Good place to walk and enjoy a beautiful forest. Map can be a bit misleading. We passed the turnoff point to the look out and had to backtrack. The tree canopy keeps the sunlight out so it is a cool and relaxing walk.

title: The human bones in cement definitely made it worth it
text: I visited this forest for a few hours and it was quite nice. It is amazingly dense and green, and there are beautiful lizards and birds to see. It is a very nice trail to follow in a loop. The most extraordinary sight was the hermitage caves at the outskirts, because of some strange reason there was the sad remains of a cement buddha there, with human bones sticking out from it. I’ve never seen anything like it. That eerie place with strange symbols, broken walls and noisy cicadas made my day.

title: A breath of fresh air
text: Away from the chaos of a dirty city is this jungle sanctuary. Nothing too special, but peaceful and a beautiful environment of trees. The amazing liana that stretches for two hectares is a real treat. Cool in the midday heat

title: Excellent to get away from the noise of the city
text: Located above the city of Kandy, the sanctuary is ideal to get away from the noisy roads of Kandy and relax in between of hundreds of differents plants. Pricing is a little lottery, we paid 1.325 LKR for 2 persons. You can either walk up there (30 minutes from CC) or take a TukTuk for ~300 LKR. The main walk through the sanctuary is about 4 km long.

title: Nice jungle, no people
text: This jungle or forest is really close to Kandy. I loved it to walk around. Monkey's, birds and a deer is saw. The park is really nice but not a lott of people go there so it's good to relax and get away from the busy town. Tip, bring water and food there is nothing in or near the entrance to buy. Easily 1-2 hours of walking around.

title: Jungle adventure
text: A amazing place to visit and escape the madness of Kandy city. Reasonable entry price when you can spend all day in there encountering wild monkeys, a whole hosts of birds, and deer. There are also a number of different hermitages scattered around the woods so mindful to be respectful while in the area. Kandy view point is located in here as well near the cemetery with stunning views over Kandy lake and city. We visited on a rainy day and although we had to wear waterproofs before we got in, once you enter the sanctuary, the tree cover is so heavy you don't really need them. Also there is only one bathroom as you enter - not the best or cleanest (don't expect toilet paper!) but better than going in the bush and getting leeches somewhere they shouldn't be!

title: Fantastic
text: We had a really wonderful 3 hours here with a very good driver & vehicle. We think we saw every available animal the park had to offer , right down to amazing little dug beetles doing their work in the middle of the road. This was our 3 park in this area & well worth a visit. The water holes & lakes make this not only great for the animals but very good for the visitors as well. We recommend you visit this park

title: Peaceful, cool and a hint of mystery
text: A beautiful sanctuary in the middle of the hustle and bustle, beautiful scenery lots of wildlife, to quote a famous aussie movie "Ah the serenity"

title: Very beautiful
text: This sanctuary is located just behind the kandy town. You can even walk from the busy town to get their. It's like a different world just close to the town with hustle and bustle . Filled with tropical trees and various climbers and beautiful birds and monkeys.

title: Nicer than being in Kandy town
text: We stayed in Kandy two nights but only really had one day. Kandy town itself is quite overwhelming, very busy, dusty and dirty. Generally in Sri Lanka the people are friendly, welcoming and kind, however we found many people in Kandy (and certainly not all) quiet rude and always trying to con tourists. For example tuk tuks should cost around 100 rupees per mile but we were charged 500 rupees to go from town to the sanctuary (just over a mile). I know you are expected to negotiate however the people here seem to have gotten wind of prices in the U.K. and the west generally and just charge whatever they think you will pay. To some extent I don't mind paying more as a tourist however here you get the impression that the locals are enjoying conning you. The sanctuary was a nice way to get out of the town. It was quiet and peaceful and offered a quick getaway from town. We only really saw monkeys in the park and there was nowhere to buy water. There are toilets but they aren't the nicest.. there was also quite a lot of rubbish around the place which was a shame as the monkeys were playing with the plastic bottles. The entrance fee is 650 rupees (approximately £4ish) which is very reasonable however the local entry cost which is listed at the door is 30 rupees (20p) another example of how people seem to think here. Again I really don't mind paying double or even triple the local cost as a tourist but twenty times the cost is crazy especially when the same goes for food, transport and accommodation. The prices are higher in other cities for a reason, the place is clean and sewage is not flowing through the streets! If you do need to go to Kandy the park is worth a visit but if going to Sigiria rock or attractions in the north then stay closer to them for a more enjoyable day trip and to avoid Kandy town.

title: A wonderful walk
text: A great walk. I would advise to take a tuk tuk to the entrance or you will be exhausted climbing to reach it before you even get in. Walk back to the lake when you come out. Beautiful place, no one else around, we didn't see any birds or wild pigs at all, only lots of monkeys by the monastery and caves. Hot an humid, take some salt with you, if you get leeches stuck to your skin, don't pull them out, sprinkle salt on them and they will drop off. You cannot beat the view of Kandy and the lake from this sanctuary viewpoint.

title: Forest walk
text: We went on a long walk through the forest. Not many people there so it was peaceful . There is a lake there too. A beautiful p[lace not far from Kandy.

title: Nice quiet stroll
text: This is a nice place to have som quiet time after experiencing the city of Kandy. There is a lot of different threes, and we also saw monkeys, wild boar, deer and a lot of birds during our walk. A nice and calm forest.

title: Nice overlook, well marked trails
text: As said in other reviews, this place is a nice getaway from the city. Most people took tuk tuk to entrance, but it's easy enough to hike (go west of tooth temple, not east). Unlike a lot of reviews with leeches, we didn't encounter any, and we did every trail. Perhaps these are more a problem in rainy season?

title: Get away from all the tooting
text: Took our lunch & spent a few hours walking round, talking to like minded people. Lovely to be away from the city noise & dirt. When we arrived we were greeted by the monkeys, inside there are more monkeys, deer, wild boar, lizards snakes & lovely birds & butterflies. Well worth the visit. ,

title: Highly Recommended
text: Why do so few people visit here? It's right next to the city and offers a great experience - see monkeys close up at the entrance, enjoy the twisted vines of the jungle as you walk through listening to the birds. Easy walking in the shade, a good track and you're almost alone. Try it out.

title: Nice walk through the nature
text: If you are quiet and patient, you might have e few sights of animals (apes, different birds, deer..) And if you are not careful you might have some other encounters - not so desirable - with LEECHES on wet days. Be careful, wear good shoes and spray your lower legs and feet

title: Lovely walk
text: Lovely walk, couldn't believe this was in a city. Beware of leeches though - we had lots stuck to our shoes!

title: In a wonderful spot, but busy
text: Magnificent, this country has so many shrines and places of antiquity to visit, all well worth it. We visited again last year and it was good to go over old and new ground.

title: Run Forrest, Ruuuuuuun!
text: Pro: it's a timeout of this hectic, noisy, busy and polluted city Kandy. Beautiful trees with lianas, but we didn't take the time to take pictures. Why? Read cons! Cons: thousands of leeches! We had to RUN through the sanctuary in order to not get eaten. Walking fast didn't help, it was a proper run. Really not relaxing at all. Btw: to get eaten by leeches you pay 1300 RS - cheaper than the gym though, therefore consider to put this point to pro.

title: Worth the walk up the hill.
text: This rainforest is generally very well maintained with signposts and a map to help you find your way. The walk is gentle and inside the forest, surprisingly cool. There are loads of monkeys near the entrance and a few that we saw in the park. We also saw a handful of deer and heard loads of birds. It was a pleasant 2 hours stroll.

title: Peaceful and stunningly beautiful big trees
text: This is way Sri Lanka must have looked like before the humans arrived. A beautiful walk through the forest Definitely a must if you are in Kandy

title: Nice walk!
text: Not too far from the city center is Udawattekele. A nice hike through the forest with a view point on the city and possible monkeys to be encountered!

title: A nice walk in the forest
text: A forest sanctuary, well preserved, with some caves at one end. Lots of different butterflies. Worth a visit.

title: Wear shoes!
text: Loved the hike into this sanctuary - we saw snakes and monkeys and a lot of bird life. We`d have done more hiking here were it not for the leeches - you definitely want to wear close-toed shoes here.

title: Magical forest so close to town
text: This is a great place to escape the bustle of Kandy, but is really close - maybe 20 mins walk from Temple of the Tooth. Verdant, green, tropical. Several walks are possible so you can walk for hours if you like. Wildlife is varied but watch out for leeches - spray or cover feet and legs! Recommended for anyone who likes nature.

title: A nice walk, but not a must-see.
text: After checking out the Temple of the Tooth and other attractions in Kandy itself, we hired a tuktuk to the Udawattekele Sanctuary. It was very nice to escape from the crowd and the heath of the city, and take a walk under the treas. However, we were often disturbed by cars passing by! It is a bit overpriced, but a nice change, when you miss nature in the city.

title: great
text: we saw some great wild life there , enjoyed the ride to get there , our guide was excellent and well worth having

title: Nature oasis almost in the heart of Kandy
text: Very friendly staff at the entrance and a breath taking environmental surrounding. If you walk through the Rain Forrest you feel very linked to nature (and few hundred years back in time), surrounded from butterflies, birds and many monkeys, which come very close towards you. The air is so fresh, it is fantastic. A must-visit for everyone who likes to be outside.

title: A very pleasant forest walk
text: A lovely, pleasant, forest walks, easy level paths - I managed fine with my ordinary sandals. Not many flowering plants at the time when I visited (late March) but the trees, the climbers and the general greenery are beautiful. Especially lovely on a sunny day when the trees provide shade. Saw groups of monkeys in a couple of places - they seemed quite bold and let me come up very close. Heard plenty of birds but couldn't see them high up in the trees - not being a bird person I couldn't tell what they were, but for a bird expert armed with binoculars this forest must be very exciting! Signage is variable and the map (which is provided on a leaflet you get when you pay for your entrance) is a little confusing - the man who took my fee explained which is the best way to go for the amount of time I wanted to spend there - I wouldn't have known without his advice. Plenty of stone benches scattered around the path.. Beware of the small blood-sucking leeches though - I've been warned about them but this was my first experience of these creatures in 2.5 months, only noticed some hours later when changing my clothes that about 4 of the blood-suckers were having a party on my left leg!

title: Amazing discovery. Great for a long walk in the wild.
text: Price around 700 LKR/person. This was a great rainforest experience. All those birds singing, monkeys jumping and almost no tourists around. Simply great. I regret we had only 3 hours to spend there. Most def a great place for people who like walking in the woods. There are a few tracks to follow and a few different landscapes.

title: nice place for a walk but not spectaculair
text: A nice place to go for a walk, it's really quiet near the bustling city of Kandy. We didn't see much animals (some turtles, monitor and just a few birds) so that was a bit of a disappointment, but there were some nice big trees. They are afraid of poachers, so they will check your bag for plants, etc. when you leave the forest.

title: Nice for a walk on a nice day
text: It's hard to believe that there's such a nice, peaceful nature reserve within around 15-20 minutes walk from Kandy city centre, and I only discovered this place after being here for 2 weeks. It's definitely worth visiting if you like walking in nature. It cost around 700 rupees to get in, which is actually quite reasonable. USEFUL TIPS: If you can, try to avoid going a day after heavy rain. Also, you may wish to wear walking boots instead of sandals as I kept getting a lot of dirt in my sandals which was quite annoying.

title: Nice place to be
text: A good sanctuary in the here of Kandy. Very peaceful and is a good place especially if you have enough time to spend in Kandy. But be careful for the leeches so have some acidic solution such as perfume as it will be handy.

title: Rain forest in the middle of Kandy
text: A nice rain forest in the middle of Kandy A true gem for 2 hours walk with the family we enjoied the variety of flora and birds

title: Lovely peaceful rainforest in the middle of Kandy town
text: Altho they charge foreigners - even residents- Rs 600 considerably more than locals (Rs28!) , if you feel like a long forest walk away from the madding crowds it is well worth going for 2-3 hour ramble. Fabulous indigenous rainforest vegetation including the world's biggest liana (Pus) and giant bamboos. It is very little visited even at a weekend. There is a cycle track for mountain bikers but we didn't see any bikers. Note last entry at 4.30pm. From here you can walk down to the Garrison cemetery (alot of steps down & up!) which is interesting for its recording of the British colonial history in this area. And also visit the Trinity College chapel which is said to be one of the most beautiful Anglican chapels in the country. We didn't manage to get past the gate (have to wear long trousers, not shorts) but some friends managed to charm the guard later in the day and raved about it. All off the beaten path, and a welcome change from the crowds at the Temple of the Tooth and Botanical Gardens.

title: Beautiful place but worth going in a group
text: We had a wonderful walk in the sanctuary and half way around one of the main paths we were stopped by a young boy with a knife demanding money. We were half an hours walk from the exit and there was no one around so although well worth a trip, please be careful not to go alone out of season. We were fine and I cant see anyone else who has had a similar experience so I think we were just unlucky and it could have been anywhere but still worth remebering it's a woodland with no security.

title: Peaceful
text: Very peaceful; offers some great opportunities to spot wildlife. I saw a snake and a kangaroo lizard amongst others.

title: Beautiful forest but be aware!
text: It's a beautiful forest near Kandy city centre. We saw a deer, monkeys, a boar and a lot of insects. Entrance fee is 650 rs pp. At the end, we took the wrong path with a lot of leeches! Best to bring some mosquito spray to spray on the leeches and take attention to take the correct route. Be aware of groups with young boys. They slap you on the butt if you are a woman. We were here on a Sunday, so maybe it's better to go on a weekday as they are at school. We told the caretaker and he was really helpful.

title: amazing forest
text: a little forest at the outskirts of the city centre. A great place to visit f you are interested in horticulture and bird watching. Many other small rare creatures. I suggest to stay still for thirty minuets and listen to the combination of birds, and creatures singing. I made a recording of the sounds here.

title: A haven of peace and quiet in Knady
text: Spent a lovely 2 to 3 hours slowly walking around this wildlife area. It was quiet and peaceful, yet is only a kilometre (if that) from Kandy town centre. Lots of monkeys - bonnet macaques and turtles in the large pond. We were also lucky enough to see an owl. From the edge of the sanctuary, there are beautiful views over the town and Kandy lake.

title: Cheapest and best way to relax and do a bit of excersise in kandy
text: Cheapest and best way to relax and do a bit of excersise in kandy. Amazes me how many people skip this when they come to Kandy, its so close to the centre of town yet once inside you wouldnt know it as its so quiet and peaceful. Highly recommend

title: place for relax
text: if you are able to visit this sanctuary you will be amaze. this place is located near to Kandy city and this place has a great history. if you are lucky enough, you will be able to get some great information about this sanctuary and ancient Kandy kingdom from one of the local person lives around here.

title: Real forest experience a few minutes from Kandy city centre
text: Udawattekele is an area of natural forest on the very doorstep of Kandy city. I visited it with my 14 year old daughter at 06.00 in the morning and we had the whole place pretty much to ourselves - we stayed for around 4 hours. You get given a map and suggested itinerary at the entrance and the very clear paths make it just about impossible to get lost. We saw deer, wild boar and the inevitable monkeys along with a variety of birds and insects (but absolutely no leeches!). But the sheer variety of vegetation is enough to make it worth going it itself.

title: A very special place in the heart of the town
text: Superb little forest - just above the Temple of the Tooth. Take a picnic lunch and lots of water and just spend an afternoon or morning wondering around. Lots of birds, butterflies etc

title: Best thing in kandy!
text: Nice and relaxing walk in kandy to get away from the hustle and bustle. We walked around for about 2 hours, could spend longer in there or be done a bit quicker though. We did get some leeches on us so might be best to wear long pants and tuck them into socks. Maps also arnt the clearest but isnt too hard to find your way. 700 rupes to enter but as it is a conservation area it goes to a goos cause

title: The best place in Kandy! ! !
text: Really enjoyed our time walking around this beautiful forest, if you're keen for peace and quiet out of hectic Kandy then definitely come here. We did however get a bit lost due to the maps not being very informative. We made our way down a not so well trotted path and got bitten by a few leeches. Come prepared incase you happen to get lost or want to explore other trails, tuck your pants into your socks! The entrance price is a bit steep at 700 rupees per person, but not uncommon for Sri Lanka

title: Nature forest
text: One of its kind in Asian, this is a uniquely preserved nature forest and you can spend the whole day in this nature forest, it is so relaxing. Entry tickets apply but less than $20.00.

title: Beautiful Wooded Retreat In The Heart Of A Bustling City
text: Beautiful and quiet escape from the noise and chaos of Kandy City. Just watch out for the leeches and wild boar!

title: NATURE AT IT'S BEST
text: Amazing view full of nature at it's best and not polluted, and exceptionally breath taking. Any one would enjoy this!

title: Must visit
text: We went for a walk just right after a heavy rain. It was a bit muddy but very nice forest walk and fresh air. Lots of birds and butterflies, and monkeys were just jumping around above us.

title: Hidden Gem
text: It was my first ever visit to this hidden gem. I had long walks around the sanctuary and loved it all! A must visit to enjoy the nature in a bustling city area. You wont hear a thing other than singing birds.

title: Have to see.
text: Out friends loved it. The dancers are great and the costumes make it amazing.Great for kids and families. The fire walking was great. Fire in general is cool. Would do it again.

title: Not worth it.
text: We got completely lost and had to exit the sanctuary to find a tuk tuk driver to take us back to the entrance.

title: Ubspoiled forest but watch out for the Leeches
text: Unspoilt with some amazing wildlife, a lovely quiet place as well

title: nice walk
text: We enjoyed our walk around the sanctuary . Very shaded and not loads of birds as a little late in day for them apparenbtly but nonetheless a relaxing bit of shade on a hot day and very tranquil.

title: Not worth the money spent
text: Having to pay the steep entrance fees along with the safari charges and guide tips - certainly not worth just to see few elephants. Safari in some other national parks around the world are far far better. Just another commercial establishment like the many others in Srilanka.

title: I loved my little walk through this forest!
text: I was completely alone and in 20 minutes walk from Kandy center I felt like I was in a real jungle/forest with monkeys swinging around and peace in the air. Tip: Watch out for leeches. Little ones that will sneakily to your shoe and then to your ankle :) Don't be scared of that. Go check it out for some fresh air, a GREAT view of Kandy at point E (I think) on the map, and a chance to watch monkeys in their habit and possible little deer that cruise through there.

title: Forest
text: Nice and peaceful walk in a forest. You can see many animals like monkeys, agamas, etc. You will get a map at entrance. You need about 2 hours for it.

title: Udawattekele Sanctuary nice
text: A breath of fresh air (so to speak in the heat) after the center of Kandy. A beautiful forest with one side a beautiful view of the city but quite noisy as close to the road. On the other you are surrounded by nature with very few visitors, damage some cars or motorcycles go through some trails. Another bad point, the plan is anything but clear to find some points of view. Anyway we enjoyed the meet monkeys, iguanas, snakes and wild boars !!

title: kandy forest walk
text: Udawattekele forest is close to the centre of KANDY and very easy to reach by tuctuc taxi. There are views toward the city and kandy lake . Easy broad paths that lead through the tropical forest around the pond. A lot of rainforest birds can be heard and spiders and monkeys can be seen. recommended.

title: Super but watch your ankles!
text: After three days hill walking in the tea plantation of Sri Lanka at 3000mtrs we decided to have a rest day today in Kandy. That lasted till 12noon when the hotel manager suggested that we go to the rain forest for a walk. One tuk tuk later, We headed in with our map and local emergence phone, provided by the hotel. At first it was wonderful, huge trees covered in giant vines with monkeys and snakes all over the place. Ants and millepedes the size of your largest finger. Confidently guiding my family with the map i directed them deeper and deeper into the rain forest. The canopy was so dense that it made the forest floor dark. We stopped for a drink then I felt it! I though it was an ant bite, sharpe and pin point pain. I looked down and nearly dropped with the shock. There were five or six leeches on my leg and foot. Bear Grills I am not, I flicked them off and sprinted forward hoping to leave them behind us, the kids followed in panic as there father led the way. My Wife calm and collected walked along, laughing until she too realised that if you stood still the leeches were all over you. I looked down at the ground and the forest floor was alive with leeches. Every two or three inches there was a leech stretching it's neck upward, swaying hoping to find some pale Irish skin. We ran for 3 to 4km through deep jungle as the leeches could not latch on when you ran. In the panic and noise of us all getting eaten alive I realised that i missed jogging. This was fun, soft ground, great scenery and laughs (fear). Who knew, all I missed was the correct motivation. I wondered if they used leeches on usain bolt, no? Should have, they work. Well after a 30min run we got back to the path and onto civilisation. My 10yr old son looked up at me and said "Dad you have three leeches on your face" f€&@....... I shouted. I had read the map backwards and led us all into the jungle and off trail. Sorry guys! Two hours later in a super market I found the last leech in my runner, full and bloated. Kids want to move back to Eire!

title: Elephants fun
text: Great opportunity to get up close to an elephant, be prepared though the handlers will expect paying, but well worth the 1000 rupees I paid, excellent experience.

title: overpriced
