text: A beautiful forest, amazing vines, trees, Dorian fruit trees Nice view over kandy,. Saw very little wildlife. husband attracted a couple of leeches, rest of us were fine. Cost almost £10 for a family of 4 which I think is too much. I know we need to pay to preserve such lovely areas, but I feel Sri Lanka is cashing in too much. Visit if you have some spare time, makes a pleasant escape from the bustle of kandy.

title: Leaches!
text: I really should have listened to past reviewers. There are serious leaches. I ended up trail running by the end, which I never do. Do not go here. It was awful!

title: greeny..
text: The Sinharaja Rain Forest is spectacular. We saw so many endemic birds, snakes and plants to Sri Lanka. We also got to tick off the Sri Lankan Blue Magpie and Sri Lankan Frogmouth from our "to see" list, which was extremely exciting.

title: we went here instead of the elephant orphanage.
text: it was nice, what can you say, the elephants were rodden bareback to save chaffing, but my driver insisted we come here instead of the orphanage, I thought a mistake, if I did it again I would do both...beware these are all pricy exercises.

title: woodland in the city
text: this beautiful little forest is located within the city yet is a true forest with lots of birds and insects giving it a calm feel. an afternoon sroll under the large canopy and shrubs was an amazing feeling before luch.

title: Beautiful!! An amazing experience
text: Its a jungle walk with sound of nature all around..chirping of birds, a myna's song, woodpeckers' call, owl's gaze, wild flowers, old tree roots winding all around and sun rays peeking from the lush green thick mane of the trees! kids loved it!!

title: A true sanctuary yet so nearby the crowded town center
text: Do your self a favour and take a threewheeler around 6AM to the Royal Forest Park entrance. For 650 LKR (locals pay 30 rupees) you enter the quietest easy-to-access tropical forest just a stone-throw away from the overcrowded Kandy town center. After entering the forest take a left-left to follow the anti-clockwise route until you eventually reach a visitor's center (one hour walk). From there, continue 100m to exit the park left-ish towards the Kandy lake side and you are back into the city. Do not expect too much birds but clean air and quietness are kind of priceless too. Walking paths are well maintained so buggy's can be taken there (only in dry season). The reason that you can't bring any food into the park is that Sri Lankans don't understand the concept of not throwing anything away ... Only recommendation I could make is to let people enter on the other side as well. Why isn't this allowed??

title: Enjoyable early morning walk
text: It was a pleasant surprise to be given a map when we paid our entrance fee to the sanctuary. So often in Sri Lanka we have found that we have had to pay high entrance fees, then no map. We went early, in order to enjoy the birdlife. It was a very pleasant, slow two hour walk, as we tried to identify the wide variety of birdcalls we heard. This was a struggle, as the sanctuary is well wooded and the birds quite elusive. We identified and photographed a few, also saw a family of wild boar, a troop of monkeys and a deer. Highlights for us were spotting Lesser Goldenback and Crimsonbacked Goldenbacks (woodpeckers) and seeing a Lesser Hill Mynah on its nest in a hole in a tree. The walk is very well signposted with a number of routes. We only did the main circuit, which is about 3km. Very quiet, very peaceful.

title: Don't tell everyone about this place!
text: A lovely area of forest sits on the hill above Kandy. So peaceful and varied with many species of the trees and other plants which grow in the Hill Country. Huge spiral lianas wind up into the canopy in places and birdsong fills the air. It is a bit difficult to match the map on your ticket to the paths and signs at junctions in the forest add to the unclear advice you get from the bored person who issues the entrance tickets. But this is an unpolluted oasis above the city and one well worth a visit - not to be missed.

title: Stunning trees and plants...mind the leaches
text: Great little walk round the loop path of the Sanctuary through some awe inspiring trees and vines. We saw very little wildlife except for a brief hint of a deer and possible turtle in the pond, but the leaches were out in force in the wet and mud, so ensure you have closed shoes - my flipflops were useless!

title: watch out for leeches if wet
text: we went after a lot of rain intop this rain forest. Despite the easy to walk paths being wide and free of vegetation, little leeches found us. Take a bar of soap to get them off-better still rub ankles with soap before start. Im sure if dry theyd not be a problem and wed have enjoyed it !. We saw no birds

title: Amazing vegetation!
text: Saw really incredible Liane plants, they look like the huge chains of ship anchors, amazing how they grow up into the air, some really high, across the paths. Can only imagine they grew over some saplings and then waited a couple of hundred years for the tree to grow and carry them up into the air. Truely asonishing to see it for the first time.

title: Good afternoon activity
text: I had a good weather when I ventured here. I didn't really get leeches or was sunburnt. The path was a bit confusing especially if you follow the map so it';s better to ask the person at the gate about it first. It's a refuge from the noise of the city.

title: Nice place to stroll
text: very nice stroll that gives you a feeling of nature while still being in the city. Nice great trees, thick jungle, you can peer at specific animals at some point : lizards, snakes, butterflies. It is well maintained with good pathways with clear indications so giving a chance to walk around for everyone. those who want more of an adventure feeling can go on smaller paths. Inside the park you have buddhist retreat places. Some great viewpoints to observe from a higher perspective the Kandy valley and surrounding mountains.

title: Did see a few other tourists
text: Enjoyed this solace in the town. We had a troop of monkeys literally cross our path. I don't think they realised we were there. They were doing something with the toilets, I don't know what exactly was happening but it is an area they need to improve on.

title: Excellent place to walk around
text: Fantastic place to see lots of wildlife right next to the city centre. We saw monkeys, deer, lizards, turtles in their natural habitat, it was amazing! We normally do things quickly but took a good couple of hours to walk around. Great place to visit although beware for leeches! Even though we'd read about them and covered up with closed shoes and long trousers, my husband still managed to get a bite from one, only noticed a few hours later when he took his jeans off and his leg was pouring of blood!

title: Primeval forest located above Sri Dalada Maligawa
text: It is also known as the forbidden forest of the kings of Kandy. A great place to hike for a couple of hours enjoying he nature and viewing some bird life. With some luck you might see wild boar, Money's, Hare, Squirrels, Porcupines, and seven some reptiles, Water monitors, Lizards, Tortise and a variety of birds,. The pond in the heart of the jungle is believed to be the the place where queens in the pas bathed and used as their player garden. The brown fish owl is a famous sighting in the forest though you have to spend a little Ike to spot it and in one visit you might not see all above... Would highly recommend this visit I anyone who has 1-2 hours o spare whilst in Kandy. During the wet season just be cautious about the leeches.

title: Real Jungle!
text: An amazing area of untouched tropical jungle within walking distance of the city. Don't go off-track - there's leeches, as we quickly found out! Lots of wildlife and amazing vegetation.

title: A great hike
text: This is a great hike - beautiful country, paths are good and plenty of monkeys. We heard a lot of birds but didnt see too many so probably best to go early morning if you can. We took about 2 hours but you could do it in an hour if you didnt have lots of time. But there are small leaches so wear shoes, socks and long pants - and after check your legs. I got back to the hotel and was lying around on the bed and noticed blood everywhere!

title: beautiful sanctuary but beware of the leeches
text: the scenry is just beautiful: a rainforest not far outside of Kandy - huge trees, some monkeys, dense vegetation, nice views of Kandy - a little information centre - just nice to walk. we were there in the rainy season, and then the leeches are obviously very active - unfortunatly we got lost - and so took a tiny path, the rain started - and as soon we stopped to get orientation, leeches crawled up your shoes - so many that we couldn't avoid bites. I think if we'd stayed on the swept paths there would have been less risk - so it was partly our fault of course

title: Beautiful but a little over crowded
text: Baker falls is an amazing natural site, but it is a little over shadowed by the entry price and it being over crowded.

title: Beautiful Baker Falls
text: Baker falls come midway enroute to world's end. The falls is full all round the year which looks very scenic. One cannot go near the falls or take a dip in the water for safety reasons.

title: Wonderful bit of nature
text: This is in a national park and on a circular trail. It is an awe-inspiring waterfall and you can get closer to it if you are careful and brave enough to go down the slope.

title: Worth the detour
text: This waterfall is worth the detour to see it. There is a small platform to take pictures. Take care of your camera, the place is very humid and the fall produces a lot of mist.

title: Pretty waterfall
text: The water falls are down several steep steps but are worth the walk down to them. Take your time walking back up and it's not too difficult. The falls have two levels of platform near them for taking good photos

title: Beautiful Waterfall
text: You will get this waterfall along the Horton plains trail walk. It will be first stop if you decide the start the trail anti clockwise. In my case it was the last stop as we had started the trail clockwise. You have to take a small detour to reach the falls and I was surprised to read some reviews which claim this path to be difficult. There are a few steep steps, but for an average person it would take hardly 5 minutes to get down. Near the falls you have an option of sitting down in the shade for a while and if you are adventurous enough you could get close to the water and splash around for a while. If you are doing the Horton plains trail, you should definitely not miss this waterfall.

title: Lovely falls
text: These falls are very picturesque but there is quite a climb down steps to them. Definitely not suitable for those with mobility problems.

title: Amazing & Lovely Place to Relax, Eat, Get Wet !! 1st Stop of the Trek !!
text: This will be your 1st stop in the Horton Plains, if you are going anti clockwise (advisable : read my Horton Plains Review !!) Scenic waterfalls named after some Britisher Mr Baker who discovered it.. Do not just see this fall from a distant, but go close to it & the stream below to enjoy the most of it.. if you are hungry by the time you reach here, you can find some space for yourself in the the shade nearby & open the Breakfast which your Hotel would have given you.. the falls wasn't dry & was full of water even in the March, i believe it to be Summers for Sri Lanka.. You could just take few selfies, sit peacefully & hear the sound of Water falling.. & enjoy Nature at it's Best !!

title: Time to relax and eat

Unfortunately the stale sandwich from Heritance tea factory was only worth a bite. Then packed to be taken out of park. So we had some nice fresh fruit and relaxed at falls.

title: Amazing and peaceful
text: It is in the middle of the 9km hike. The signs are very clear there to the waterfall and it is safe and amazing. Take your time in smelling the fresh air and let the breeze of this waterfall touch your face by getting to the lower level which is close to the waterfall

title: Lovely waterfall
text: Lovely waterfall in the Horton Plains National Park. Walk through the park, along a very easy to follow trail. The train is rocky and muddy is some places, so dress accordingly. The fall is off the main path, but easily found, so follow the steps down, and onto the viewing platform. Here you can feel the spray from the waterfall. Apparently there are lots of lizards in this area, but we didn't see any!

title: Sucker for waterfalls!
text: I can't resist a waterfalls, so was happy to make the 100 meters spur off the World's End loop trail to reach Baker's Falls, and about 3 kms from the start trek's starting point, going to the right from the fork of the trek. The falls is beautiful, albeit not spectacular. One of the three main attractions on the World's End track, along with World's End and Mini World's End viewpoints.

title: On the Worlds End Hike
text: It's worth swinging by Baker's Falls on the World's End hike It's a small waterfall in a beautiful setting.

title: Beautiful 20 metre falls, surrounded by flowers and with a perma- rainbow
text: This was for me easily the highlight of the 9km circuit walk. Accessed via about 100 steps from the path, it is serenely beautiful, with multiple cascades, surrounded by rhodendron and other flora, and a permanent rainbow. Camera's at the ready, and enjoy the beauty of nature.

title: Water fall in the middle of the hortain planes nature trail
text: You get to see this wide beautiful waterfall when doing the 10 kms long hortan planes nature trail. Don't be discouraged and stop your walk half way through but take your time and finish the walk where you get to see both world's end as well as this nice waterfall

title: Part of the Horton Plains hike
text: Part of the trek in Horton plains and possibly the most difficult to access, but doable. Would recommend hiking shoes or sneakers.

title: Favorite spot in Horton Plains National Park
text: This was my favorite spot along the 10km loop at Horton Plains, although the entree fee is ridiculously overpriced. While it's no Niagara or Iguazu, it's a good spot to take a break on the hike.

title: Impressive waterfall
text: You get this waterfall for free on the same trail as Worlds End. It is an impressive and large waterfall, with a platform that allows you to get right up close to the water. The steps down are quite steep, so take care with your step.

title: Lovely and breezy small waterfall
text: Located inside the horton plains national park , it has the most amazing breeze . When you go close to the waterfall tiny drops of water splashes over the body, baker's fall is a wonderful little piece of nature.

title: Great view
text: A decent waterfall to have a look. Its on the hortons trek. The place is great to take some good pics. The trek to the waterfalls is certainly worth.

title: Thumb's down
text: Just a falls. Not that impressive for a tourist visit. I Would definitely not recommend this to a friend. Waste of time

title: Beautiful Falls
text: Baker's Falls is located inside the Horton Plains National Park. Visited the falls while coming back from the World's End. Indeed a very beautiful falls. Getting down to the view point is a bit difficult.

title: Nice
text: Bakers falls is along the hike at Horton's plains national park. Steep climb off the trail to get here. Not a very big waterfall, but a nice place to stop when doing the trek.

title: Splendid!
text: It is on the way to the 'world's end'. Nature in in full boom. Lovely falls! You can sit there and take pictures,a nd enjoy the beauty of these falls

title: Breathtaking view and moderate hike
text: You can reach Horton's plain by car or tuktuk. The whole route to hortons plain is very scenic. We stopped at few places to take pictures. There is a little cafeteria at the entry of hortons plain. We bought a packet of jumbo salted peanuts and ginger snaps from there to enjoy during the hike. We started our hike around 12.30 in the afternoon. Weather was pleasant with smattering of sunshine and chilly wind. Please do wear your trainers as the terrain is rocky and do carry a windsheater to save you from the chilly wind. There are three places to see - Bakers waterfall which is the shortest hike, then mini world's end and the farthest is world's end. We went upto Baker's fall and it took us 1.5 hours going and coming back. The view is breathtaking! You are surrounded by nature all around you!! It feels like you are in europe. There are mountains all around covered with trees, a small waterfall leading to a pond. Bakers falls is really beautiful. There is an observation deck where you can sit for a little time before starting back. on reading some reviews i thought the hike would be difficult. But my hubby who has knee problem could do this hike easily. I think the cool weather and so much of beauty all around you keeps you mesmerised. On our way back we stopped at cafeteria for a hot cup of tea and some biscuits. Whenever you are in nuwara eliya it is a must do. I would love to do the whole hike upto world's end if i visit this place again.

title: Must see, must do
text: Must, must do! Just must do. The Baker's fall are a part of The Horton Plains National park which is one of the most beautiful locations in Sri Lanka. It is a 9km circle which has three stops along the way – Mini World’s End, World’s End and Baker’s Fall. The trail is easy (will short patches of incline along the way which are easy to climb) and breathtakingly beautiful. Finish it off with a cup of tea and biscuits at the canteen overlooking the plains. On more practical information, the entrance to the plains is an hour’s drive from Nuwara Elliya (approximately) and the tickets are slightly expensive (but worth every penny). Take the route on the left (which reaches baker’s fall last) since it’s a better way to circle the plains. Also, if you get tired halfway and feel the urge to turn back – don’t, because even if you turn back you’ll have the same distance to cover and you’ll miss the trail on the other side.

title: Small Waterfalls at Horton Plains
text: We visited as part of our walk in the park. There is a steep but not to arduous path down to them. Perhaps, as it was out of the rainy season, the true spectacle was not evident. I however found them average and not a patch on others I have seen in the world. That said they are worth a detour on the walk.

title: Small but beautiful
text: This Fall is comparatively smaller but it has its own charm and uniqueness. It's beautiful and the water flow is strong. Though you can't spend a lot of time admiring it as other hikers are waiting for their turn to appreciate this natural beauty. Photos don't do justice to this beauty.

title: Just ok
text: Its an OK attraction. Waterfall is quite small and when we went the platform was quite crowded. Would go to HP for the trekking not so much to see this

title: WOW
text: Important place to visit in Horton Plains National park. most people are visit on this last of the walk. but we saw this first. that side the best.

title: Great way to start the Horton Plains hike (if you turn right at the start)
text: While the falls are a short hike off the trail down some rather steep steps, they are certainly worth the walk. I was there in dry season and the falls were still impressive!

title: splash of water after a long trek
text: it was so refreshing to see bakers fall after the long world's end trek. though the water was too cold to take a dip, sitting besides it was equally soothing

title: Pretty falls
text: A lovely part of the Horton Plains experience, we enjoyed admiring the falls though watching some of the other tourists climb up and slide down gave us some anxiety. A good spot for to drink some water and relax before the last slog to the park gates.

title: Picturesque falls
text: The Bakers Falls are part of a series of sights within Horton Plains. See my review of Horton Plains which includes hints/tips on visiting this beautiful natural sight. Must-see as part of a visit to Sri Lanka!

title: Impressive
text: My partner and I visited the falls whilst touring the country. This is a beautiful area and great if you enjoy walking. Wear comfortable walking shoes and set off early to avoid crowds. There are some good photos to take. There are toilets and free parking.

title: Decent falls
text: We visited in a fairly dry period and the falls were not very dramatic. However it is evident that in wetter periods a lot more water would be falling, enhancing the drama

title: Spectacular and beautiful reward
text: Located in Horton's Plains National Park as part of the 9.5km trek that also takes in World's End, Baker's falls offers a contrast in scenery after walking across the drier plains section, where we spotted some sambal deer and lovely mountain scenery. You hear the waterfalls before you see them. To view Baker's Falls requires descending about 50 steep steps to reach the first of several viewing areas. On a hot humid day the spray from the falls is refreshing.

title: Wonderful Waterfall
text: The loop around Hortons Plains National Park brings you to Bakers Falls which you hear before you see. Its a stunner with a good viewing platform. My advice is don't try and go back to the car park from here double back as its a killer otherwise!!

title: Nice, small waterfalls, not much of a tourist atttraction....
text: The waterfalls are part of the Horton Plains National Park, they are nice and small but, nothing special, not a tourist attraction in or view...

title: Waterfall
text: It was such a relaxing place to sit after 1 hour of walking.. the waterfall really changes your mood to a better one .. really loved it

title: Like hundreds of waterfalls in SL, nothing special
text: OK, it is nice, you get to stand on the viewing platform near the falls. But you also need to trek hours and pay lots of dollars to see what is essentially a waterfall that is no different to many others in the region that you can see and swim around for free. DO the trek for the World End's view if you must, but the Baker's falls is not special enough to do the trek.

title: Small but beautiful waterfall in Horton Plains National Park
text: This small and placid waterfall is only 20 metres in height and was discovered, and named after, Sir Samuel Baker, who was a British big game hunter and explorer. It is located in Horton Plains National Park, a montane and cloud forest region which is unique in Sri Lanka. Sadly, Sir Samuel Baker was one of the British colonialists that was responsible for exterminating the elephants that inhabited this region in Sri Lanka and who were apparently different from the other elephants residing in the island.

title: Beautiful
text: Probably the best so called activity that you can do in Horton’s National Park, but still doesn’t worth the entrance fee. You can see soo many beautiful waterfalls for free, people are just lazy searching for them.

title: Bakers Falls

title: Nice but not worth it

title: Beautyful

title: We skipped it due to too many tourists

title: Rush of Waters
text: Nice falls, though not as large.Do make that stop to see it. It is towards the middle of the 9 km loop.

title: Worth a short stop at Horton Plains NP
text: It's a five minute walk from the round trip at Horton Plains NP to the Baker's Falls. They are not as impressive as we expected but still worth a short stop. There are two further ways down (off the main path) where you can get directly to the river and offers a better view of the falls.

title: Fresh and calming checkpoint
text: Through the sunny days was this place more calming when you can breath fresh waterfall air. You can see local people in the water and you can also try it if you have enough of courage.

title: Just a checkpoint
text: If you are on the trail, you will come across with Baker's Falls. Nothing specifically interesting, just a checkpoint for trekking.

title: Delightful, soothing experience
text: I've seen many waterfalls & this wasn't magnificent in any way....but ther was a thoughtfully provide bench where we could sit up close to the water fall, eat a snack after a long walk, enjoy the sound of the rushing water, watch as the water flowed through various crevices it had created for itself....

title: nice waterfall
text: You will see Baker's Fall while hiking the 9km Loop Trail at Horton Plain's Nat'l Park. The falls were nice with our good clear weather but not exceptional. Only recommended if you have the time and fancy waking up at 5am.

text: Falls are nice to visit and walk (a good three hours to do the loop) goes through many different types of environments - all different and beautiful in their own way. Wear good walking shoes:)

title: Beautiful Waterfall in a Lovely Walking / Hiking Area
text: Bakers Falls is half hour or so from the visitors centre on Horton Plains, the walk around which is simply lovely; it was close to being the highlight of our Sri Lanka vacation, in fact. The Falls themselves have a two-tier viewing platform, and on the day we were there, in full flow. Attractive rather than spectacular, the spot is definitely worth a visit

title: Very close view
text: Baker's falls is a moderate sized waterfall with several streams. The viewpoint is very close in front of the waterfall, so one can see everything in every detail. From the viewpoint, one can climb down the stones almost into the waterfall itself.

title: It was nice
text: the fall is not extra ordinary. since there are much more nicer waterfalls in sri lanka. but when you consider the whole journey around Horton plains it really add values to the walk.

title: Nice stop after World's End
text: A nice and relaxing stop after World's End. The steps are manageable. Take a break before you continue your journey.

title: Worth the walk
text: You reach there after a long walk in Horton Plains, very relaxing place with the sound of the fall gashing down, before continue your walk to world end.. enjoy

title: A nice waterfall
text: During your trip in the park you reach this waterfall. It is a nice waterfall and a perfect place to take a little rest. If you walk the whole tour it takes about 5 hours of walking.

title: Nice waterfall
text: A very nice waterfall at the Horton Plains National Park. You will find it when you do the complete walk of around 8-9 kilometers.

title: Picturesque
text: Great waterfall, a peacful place where you can only hear the sound of water. Managed to take great pictures here.

title: A waterfall is a waterfall is a waterfall!
text: Waterfalls are waterfalls. No matter what the height is, or what the width is... waterfalls make you freshen up in a moment and bring back that energy the Sun sapped away! Part of the Horton Plains 9+km trail, I went to the Baker's Falls towards the end. An easy climb down and a challenging climb up, its all worth it. For the more adventurous, do what I did - hop down through the back onto the rocks and touch the ice cold waters! :)

title: Nice to see, but there are better in Sri Lanka.
text: A nice waterfall, and part of the Horton Plains circuit walk. Good viewing platform. It can be rather slippery getting to the falls as you walk through forest, so wear good shoes.

title: Nice part of Horton Plains visit
text: The waterfalls are very nice...the climb down to see them requires a somewhat challenging climb up to return to the trail!

title: Pretty waterfall
text: Along the World's End Trail. Nice stop, nice photo op. But waterfalls are waterfalls. This isn't Vic Falls or Angel Falls.

title: Beautiful Falls
text: The falls are worth visiting along the Trek in the Horton National Park But they clerly need to make a better access as the stairs leading down to the falls are so big even for a tall person like me specially when they charge you so much for the entrace fees

title: Small falls
text: This a not a big fall, but a nice break during your Horton Plains hike to admire the water and perhaps fuel up if you have not had the chance to do so before you continue the rest of the way. Keep your hands free to help you grip the branches as you climb up and down to get to the falls. Skip this part if it is raining and slippery. Don't attempt this carrying your child.

title: Ancient and beautiful
text: The oldest stupa in Sri Lanka, and really beautiful. It's not the biggest, but it is one of the most beautiful we saw. The surrounding pillars once supported a roof, so you get a sense of the size of the building in which it once sat. If touring Anuradhapura this is a site you should not miss.

title: Water everywhere...
text: We got pissed of when visiting this stupa, coz they poured water everywhere on the top which made dry flower offerings become disgusting and one should walk around in this mess without shoes?

title: The First Dagoba
text: Thuparamaya is the oldest dagoba of Sri Lanka. It was built over an ancient Hindu temple. The dagoba is surrounded by the ruins of the yore that give a scenic look to the place. The locals in white attire make the place look like a lake full of swans. One must carry a pair of socks to visit this place as we have to walk barefoot that gives a feel of firewalk.

title: Srilanka's first Dagoba
text: Historical stupa and still magnificent to look at. It supposedly contains the Buddha's collarbone. It helps to wear socks as walking up to the site on the very hot stones and sand pathways can be very difficult in bare feet.

title: Oldest dagoba and great moonstone by small temple ruin. Get out of the car!
text: It's not as big as some other temples but beautiful nonetheless and I believe the oldest in Anuradhapura. The small ruined temple to the right has some lovely carvings at the steps and a beautifully preserved moonstone. Nice to wander around for a few mins

title: Divine
text: We visited this place along with Family during Christmas holidays and it is a great place to visit and pay homage

title: Quick stop along the way
text: This is one of the smallest dagobas in the area and can be visited along the way from one sacred site to another. If you plan to see all 8 sacred sites, this one can be done en route and you may not even have to get out of the car.

title: All Dagobas, must visit!
text: All the Stupas and Dagobas must be visited!! They are sort of similar but different in their own way :) Some are massive while some of smaller in size.

title: Thuparamaya Stupa at Anuradhapura is worth a visit
text: This is a compact(small)stupa, said to be containing the collar bone of Buddha,in that respect it is an important shrine.A walk around the stupa is recommended.

title: Disappointed because it is reconstructed
text: Small, but sacred to to Buddhists, this stupa claims the title of the "first one built in Sri Lanka." It offers a great Kodak moment, but I was disappointed to learn that the structure is not ancient at all, but rather a reconstruction undertaken in the mid-19th century. Out guide told us that it was not even rebuilt in the correct shape!

title: Smallest but nicer dagoba
text: I went to see this beautiful place in the morning which was great because there was almost no people and the stone ground was still cool. This dagoba is much different from the others, first because it isn ́t that big and second because of the stone columns surrounding it. This dagoba is very sacred to Buddhists because they believe that there is the collarbone of the Buddha inside. Next to this dagoba ther are the ruins of ancient temple which is worth seeng as well.

title: Thuparamaya - Oldest Stupa in Sri Lanka
text: Thuparamaya is the oldest stupa in Sri Lanka and the first to be built in the country after the introduction of Buddhism. It was built in the time of King Devamnampiyatissa (247BC – 207BC) enshrining the collarbone relic of Gauthama Buddha which was brought to Sri Lanka by Arahat Mahinda, son of King Ashoka of India.

title: Oldest Stupa in Anuradhapura
text: This is the oldest Stupa in Anuradhapura, probably in Sri Lanka itself. Smaller in size, but quite attractive. This is a functioning temple and hence dress properly (you will see the local people wearing white dress) and remove Shoes and hat while entering the temple. The floor gets very hot during the day and hence better to wear the socks.

title: Different
text: I have to say that this was my favorite sight in Anuradhapura as it was very different from the other places we looked around. To see this dagoba was just tantalizing as it has these pillars around it that make you think of Roman or Greek ruins instead of Asian. The pillars were used to support the roof that once spanned over the dagoba to protect it. You have to go and see it for yourself to truly understand

title: Tremendously atmospheric
text: We really enjoy visiting this place, which has a unique atmosphere. One of the great pleasures of Anuradhapura is the fact that no two constructions are alike and this one is different because of its wonderful columns or pillars which rise some 12 feet into the air in from of it giving the appearance a statement of grandeur. The whole construction is small compared to other buildings in the cultural centre but it is beautifully located in green surroundings and well worth visiting.

title: Sacred place
text: Sri Lanka first - but probably one of the oldest still be seen all over the world - stupa and Theravada Buddhism's most sacred place. No too big, but very charming and the structure of circle sanctuary (vatadage) very interesting. Don't miss it! Don't forget, hat and shoes forbidden inside the sacred area. You will need sun protection cream, and exchange socks is very practical. The reason not just the dirty floor (these places wasn't really dirty), very often the stone very hot without shoes. I recommend you, before the visit you must read some historical fact about this place, will be interesting the visit!

title: Stunningly beautiful and photogenic dagoba
text: Reputedly the oldest dagoba in the world, Thuparama is surrounded by carefully placed pillars which enhance the visual appeal dramatically. They certainly knew how to present a building back then! It is also situated in a lovely green parkland area. If you're lucky, you'll have a brilliant blue sky as contrast for your photographs.

title: A very old and important dagoba site
text: This is a much restored but very old and important dagoba site, quite small in comparison to the others in the area but very much venerated.

title: The best visit in all Anuradhapura
text: For us, this was the best visit in all the Unesco site. The columns around the dagoba give it a unique charm and "special" feeling, compared with the similar looking (in style) constructions. It's nice to visit by bike. When researching for the trip, we decided against Polonnoruwa because Anura would be more atmospheric, mystical and alive. After speaking with other travelers and seeing pictures, I think Polo would have maybe been nicer. What I do find abusive is the entrance fee: 25 dollars is way too much, even if you get a DVD in the package. Most other tourists, guides, people from GHs agreed that much harm is done with these exaggerated prices and the cancellation of the combo ticket. A normal day salary in SL is 1200 rupees. One hour in a bus, is less than 100 rupees. A normal rice and curry costs around 300 - 500 rupees. How on earth can you justify 3259 rupees to pay for an entrance ticket??? I understand we pay more than the locals, but this is probably 40 or 50 times more. Probably to pay a Government with approximately 60 ministers, many of them opponents, friends and family to the President..........

title: A place of Worship
text: Considered the oldest Buddhist stupa in Sr Lanka, built in the 1st Century BC. Calm and quiet, respectful,place of worship

title: Another dagoba
text: Festivities were on and some procession was in progress when we were there. Looked better than other dagobas in Anuradhapura.

title: Holiest Place in Anuradhapura
text: This site does not attract the tourist crowds that the Ruwanwellseya does yet it possesses the holiest relic, namely the collarbone of Buddha. Small and recently restored it is surrounded by columns which once held up a roof. Similar columns abound all over this vast archaeological site. All are remnants of buildings and their role are roof props. It retains an odd air of peace and serenity in a site which is mobbed at times of Poya, especially in June

title: Interesting Dagoba with protruding pillars
text: The main dagoba does not look very impressive as compared to other Dagoba in Anuradhapura Temple site. But what I find interesting about this temple is it has numerous ancient looking pillars jutting out about 12 ft high around the main dagoba. Some are vertical and some are tilted. Some are spread over the floor. Not sure the reasons for their existence. Probably to serve as a legacy of the original temple. As in all temples compound in Sri Lanka, you need to remove your footwear to enter. You need to bear with the afternoon heat and hot floor surface. The crude surface floor is just bearable to walk around.

title: Most beautiful stupa in Anuradhapura
text: Compared to Ruwanwelisaya Pagoda, the Anuradhapura stupa is much smaller. Nevertheless, I personally like this stupa and its stone pillars around. It is considered the first stupa in Sri Lanka. Since it is one of the most sacred places in Anuradhapura, there are always a few religious rituals performed here every weekend. We unexpectedly arrived on a saturday and could witness and took part in those rituals. The locals wear all-white clothes to enter the place, bringing lotus and various offerings to the stupa. The surrounding is peaceful and calm. Highly recommended to visit. Entrance ticket to the entire Anuradhapura site is USD 25 / pax.

title: Impressive Dagoba (or Stupa).
text: This is an enormous Stupa of great signifcance. It is almost too big to photograph so we have more memories than pictures. Take socks (as this is a 'working' religious site you have to remove your shoes and store them for a few rupees). We visited near mid day which was too hot, it would have been better earlier or later in the day, but a magnificant sight.

title: The highlight of our explorations
text: This was a highlight for me during our explorations of Anuradhapura. The dagoba is beautiful, peaceful and the pillars around it look simply stunning. It makes for an incredible photo, and an even better experience to stand there and see it for yourself.

title: Wear some thick socks!
text: I visited the week before a full moon festival so the Dagoba was white washed and looked amazing. As with all Buddhist temples you need to take off your shoes before going in and as my review title says wear socks. Unfortunately I didn't follow my own advise and with my visit being at noon the sand and bricks were so hot I had to run between shade. That aside the Dagoba was impressive and well worth a visit. Also a short walk to see the Sacred Bo tree which is 2000 years old.

title: A different stupa surrounded by with all the old pillars at odd angles
text: This stupa features on the cover of one of the editions of Lonely Planet so you can have fun trying to match up the picture. (we succeeded) It is an attractive small stupa but the pillars impart a somewhat surreal atmosphere. One of the problems with many of the stupas here is that you are expected to removed shoes and hats in the blistering heat. OK for locals who are used to it but hard for soft westerners. We pleaded that we had a problem with skin cancer and they let us off except right at the shrines. Entry fee to Anuradhapura was also extortionately high for foreigners.

title: Ok, small and uninspiring
text: Unlike most of the Dagobas, it was small with a few pillars with a small shrine. Very much a recommend to those Buddhists. As a simple tourist it wasn't spectacular.

title: Active religious site
text: The atmosphere at this stupa site was really good, with pilgrims actively worshipping and living feeling about the place. The monkeys stealing and eating the lotus flowers within moments of pilgrims placing them at the shrines was initially very funny to watch, but ultimately telling about the pilgrims' acceptance of the greater circle of life and existence as they weren't bothered by the monkeys' behavior as many people would be. A lesson to be learned.

title: Definitely Photogenic
text: Although a smaller stupa, it is much more photogenic due to the many pillars surrounding it. The temple is still being used and there was a prayer ceremony going on when I visited the place. Easy to get in. No ticket checks.

title: Very photogenic
text: Good place to stop for a photo and short visit! The stupa is a good blend of old and new and the grounds are well kept. We visited in the afternoon and the stones were hot so get ready for some shadow to shadow hopping.

title: Beautiful and serene
text: This was featured on the latest cover of the Lonely Planet guide book, to see it in real was breath taking, it's a lovely subject for photography. Do make a point to see it in sun set.

title: Thuparama
text: Thuparama, a brick-built gedige (Sinhala: vaulted shrine) is in a fine state of preservation. Thuparma, the oldest image house at Polonnaruwa goes back the reign of King Vijayabahu the first (1055-1110 A.D.). A brick base about one meter high with three projections once carried an image of Buddha, which is now simple a pile of bricks. The stone images in the Thuparama date back to Anuradhapura period.

title: A nice Dagoba from Ancient times
text: Well kept Dagoba is nice to visit. However, we found most Dagoba's to be very similar.

title: Amazing little temple
text: I like this temple since it shows the old remains and the remoddled stupa in white, so you can see the contrast of old and new. The whole visit takes only 5 minutes.

title: A truely picturesque stupa surrounded by a vatadage
text: The oldest stupa in Sri Lanka, it is said to enshrine the clavicle of Buddha. The current stupa is a later renovation of the original stupa erected by Devanampiya Tissa in the 3rd century BC. The current bell-shaped stupa is encircled by smaller shrines and stone pillars that 'may' have supported a wooden roof.

title: Ancient, Beautiful, plus great paintings
text: The pillars make the temple looks stunning. There are many ancient rocks around the area. The temple itself is pretty.

title: Another religious and historical place
text: This would be one of the list of temples in your tour. Must see the moon stone near the entrance. The pillars are very tempting.

title: lovely
text: We came to visit at the time of the holiday so there were a lot of Buddhists. They did not mind, as I believe that they are constantly interupted by the tourists.

title: Small dagoba, but interesting due to the surrounding columns
text: A smaller dagoba, compared to its larger brothers, but particularly interesting due to the circular columns (actually two circles) that surround the building itself. It is one of the ten-ish places you have to visit in Anuradhapura.

title: Last stupa of the day and exhausted
text: Unfortunately this was our last stop in a big day out of sightseeing.The monks were meditating whilst we were there and I didn’t want to get in their way.The floor was boiling and I had to move quickly and hop around to stop my feet burning.Not much different to other Dagobas that we visited

title: Spread out
text: The stupa and its immediate surrounding buildings and the art work and carvings in the building are remarkable, but the larger area also has many more interesting ruins.

title: saw from the car
text: it was so under whelming that we didn't even get out of the car to see it. took photos becausee the guide insisted we do it.

title: Oldest Stupa in Sri Lanka
text: Thuparamaya is the oldest Dagaba in Sri Lanka . It has a unique architectural feature called "vatadage", This stupa was built by King Dewanampiyatissa. must visit ...sacred place to visit

title: The earliest Dagoba to be constructed in the Island
text: The Thuparamaya Stupa is the earliest Dagoba to be constructed in the island, dating back to the reign of King Devanampiya Tissa (247-207 BC). It is just few minutes away from Ruwanweliseya. If you are in Ruwanweliseya and have some minutes to spare should visit this. Since this is a sacred place please don't wear short skirts and exposing blouses. Also if you are visiting on day time it can be very hot, recommend wearing socks.

title: Its all part of the entrance fee....
text: Yes another Stupa in another former city. The thing with this is that it has clearly gone under same maintenance that to my mind takes away an element of its history.

title: Most religious stupa
text: This seemed to be the most religious stupa in the complex with the amount of the people around when I visited and also the various offerings that were being performed here.

title: Wear socks
text: If you're going to do the Sacred city tour - wear socks. We didn't and our feet got so hot - by the time we got to this stupa we couldn't be bothered getting out of the tuk tuk

title: Smaller, but still impressive
text: This is one of the smaller stupa's in Anuradhapura, but has more going on at the site than the others and is quite impressive to see. There is more around the area as well, with some ruins from the monastery. As with all temples, you must remove your shoes and dress appropriately. Be aware that the ground can get very hot indeed!

title: Architectural jewel!!
text: This is really an architectural jewel of Anuradhapura!! If you visit it in the dry and hot season (for example, in April), bring a pair of socks!!

title: A small stupa which situated close to ruwanmeliseya stupa
text: This is the one of the first stupa that is build in Sri lanka . Its not much bigger as other stupas that we see here in Anuradhapura but there s a belief that there was a roof around the stupa but now there s no such roof but we can see the stone pillars around the stupa.

title: A Kind Of Interesting Place
text: This is one of the earliest monuments of the country and so from that point of view worth a visit. It was not something that takes a great deal of time in itself but it is another one of these places which is a bit of a trek by car to get to. There is not a lot to see as such and I suppose a visit here might be more meaningful or interesting if you are lucky enough to get there when there is any ceremony or something like that going on.

title: Spiritual highs
text: Aftrer an afternoon of visiting dagobas and participatiing in some of the ceremonies we climbed to the top of a lookout where I interacted with local people, sharing a laugh and small talk. I saw a sunset from the topmost tower, offered flowers and took in the sights.

title: One of the great stupas
text: One of the great massive stupas around Anuradhapura, although with little to see up close. Offers one of the most iconic photos in the area.

title: Nice Place
text: We did not go inside this Stupa but we did see when we were on our way to Abhayagiri Dagoba. Its beautifully lit with diyas during evening.

title: Ruins are Interesting
text: Enjoyed the grounds more than the Dagoba. It is a very spiritual place but it was just another Dagoba to me. Had hoped for more.

title: Magnificent Stupa
text: There were quite a lot of people the time I was here. What a really interesting place to visit. Once again, a sacred place to visit, so be respectful. Nice construction, such a holy place to be.

title: Reconstruction of the original
text: Reportedly the first stupa constructed in Sri Lanka, it has clearly been heavily reconstructed and the shrines are very modern even looking a bit dukeboxy. Part of the collarbone of the Buddha is believed to be enshrined here, so it is a place of pilgrimage. However, unlike the Boo tree site the atmosphere here is a bit surreal, with someone announcing on a microphone the names of those who have donated and how much.

title: The first recorded stupa in Sri Lanka
text: The first recorded stupa to be built in Sri Lanka and the legend goes that it enshrines the collarbone of the Buddha . It is a little gem that more than holds its own amongst the larger dagobas in Anuradhapura. For me, it is special given the large number of pilgrims when I visited. PS wear socks if you are visiting during the day - the stones you walk on get hot!

title: Really beautiful and serene
text: As for all the dagobas here, this is really worth seeing and imagining the scale and beauty of the place in its heyday.

title: The Oldest Dagoba in Anuradhapura
text: Thuparamaya Dagobah Thuparamaya Dagobah is the oldest historical structure and first stupa built in 3rd century after the introduction of Buddhism in Sri Lanka by King Devanampiyatissa on the request of Mahinda, an envoy of Ashoka, the great Emperor of India. The collarbone of Mahatma Buddha was enshrined in this Dagobah Thuparamaya is derived from the words "stupa" and "aramaya" which means residential complex for bhikshus, hermits and monks. During the course of history, this dagobah was destroyed and rebuilt many times. The present monument was built in 1862 in the shape of a bell with a diameter of 60 feet

title: The area around Anuradhapura is wonderful
text: So much to take in and so many Stupas to take in, the twin ponds are also worth visiting and there are some lovely local snacks to be had by the side of the ponds. The sacred tree is worth visiting and it is interesting to watch the locals wait for a leaf to fall from it, apparently one of the oldest trees in the world the Sri Maha Bodhi has been lovingly tended for 23 centuries.

title: Archeological site with some ruins...
text: This is the first Buddhist Temple in Sri Lanka, built since 3rd century, to house the right collar-bone of Buddha. There are nearby ruins site with some interesting stone carvings especially the famous “Moondtone” carvings which is semicircular usually stood at the foot of first step in Buddhist buildings/ temple. We even explored further to the Elephant Pond as the given name is due to the huge size of the pond. More details to see along the history of Anuradhapura Kingdom in relation to Buddhism culture. It is inclusive in the entrance fee of USD25 or LKR4,550 for the Anuradhapura ancient sites. Hiring a driver is necessary to the scarcity of the site.

title: Nice Holy Site
text: The oldest of the sacred sites in this area although heavily restored. Has a nice atmosphere and is worth seeing as part of the sacred city

title: THE AREA'S FIRST DAGOBA
text: The first dagoba, or stupa, in the area was built to house the right collar bone relic of the Budddha. It was likely the first dagoba built in the country after the introduction of Buddhism. Its root 'aramaya' is a residential complex for monks. This was a photo only visit without access.

title: Nice
text: The structure is inspiring - pious worshippers, statues of Lord Buddha all around, calm ambience - your mind is busy wondering!

title: Nice Dagoba
text: Nice dagoba with usually many religious people clad in white attire praying, making for an interesting photo op

title: Sacred Site
text: One of several important Ancient moments at Anuradhapura. Quite striking. Be sure to dress modestly (no shorts, or bare shoulders for women) to be respectful. Also required to remove shoes, and be prepared the sand surrounding the dragons can get very hot, and has the occasional sharp stones.

title: Thuparama Dagoba
text: Thuparama Dagoba is one of the smallest dagobas but it is apparently the oldest of the dagobas. It is a fascinating place to visit and is busy with worshippers and full of life as a result.I suggest that you have socks with you as if you are walking around barefoot the floor can get really hot.

title: Well worth a stop during a tour of Anuradhapura - and no entrance fee
text: Visited Thuparama during a cycle tour of the various dagobas in Anuradhapure. Thuparama is one of the smaller dagobas in town but it's the most fascinating as it's one of the most popular places of worship in Anuradhapura (unlike many of the others) and is full of life as a result. It's also said to be the oldest Buddhist temple in Sri Lanka. A visit won't take long at all but its well worth it. It easy to find a spot to lock up a bike too. There's no entrance fee to visit. Just make sure you take socks as if you are walking around barefoot the floor can get really hot.

title: One of the oldest "Stupa" of Sri Lanka depicting Buddhist culture
text: Thuparama is a relatively smaller "Stupa" of many in the ancient city of Anuradhapura with a well known history of over 2400 years. The specialty of this is the stone pillars located around it indicating the existence of a timber structure to act as a roof for this small "Stupa" or the dome shaped brick structure. This is a good place for those interested in meditating and it is located pretty close to the other main and large "Stupa" called Ruwanweliseya. The path between these two could be an ideal place for those interested in practicing walking meditation to calm the mind by concentrating on the steps while walking slowly.

title: A smaller but nonetheless impressive Dagoba
text: The Dagoba of Thuparama is one of the smaller but still impressive Dagobas in the sacred city. It's one of the few in this area which is still used as a holy place and temple. While you're here for admiring the beauty of this Dagoba, others came for worshipping. Please behave respectfully as well as dress appropriately, cover your shoulders and knees. No shoes allowed.

title: One of the smaller dagobas
text: One of the smaller dagobas it is still an active site of worship unlike some of the larger historic dagobas so actually had more people here than at what I would have considered the more impressive sites, but that's because most people here were locals in peaceful contemplation not tourists.

title: Old columns
text: The columns standing around the stupa are what remain of the ancient building first built here. I didnt think ahead, and visited in the middle of the day, when the stone is hot hot hot. My feet didnt feel very good when I put my shoes back on.

title: Perhaps the most interesting stupa of Anuradhapura
text: The Thuparama is the first stupa built in Sri Lanka after the introduction of Buddhism, and it was built during the reign of King Devanampiya Tissa (about 300 BC) to enshrine the right collar bone of Buddha. Originally it was in the shape of a heap of paddy but as restorations were done in later years, it took the form as seen today. The story of the stupa, its immaculate white color and the brown, ancient stone pillars surrounding it, give it a strange, special aura and make it, in our opinion, the most interesting stupa in Anuradhapura.

title: BUDDHIST
text: This is one of the old Buddhist temple here. The Dagoba is surrounded by old pillars.This is beautiful temple you need about half an hour here.

title: Great experience
text: It was amazing to stand in front of this Stupa. So big, so white. I walked around it as you should do when you come from afar. But better bring some socks as you have to remove your shoes and the stones on a sunny day can be very very hot!

title: Beautiful Temple
text: Its a historical temple visited by both local and foreign tourist. Amazing sculptures and architectures

title: Not worth the time and money
text: Governments main job is to rip the tourist off and even the officials behave this way, arrogant and not customer oriented at all. It is all about money here. The price for tourist RP 3500 compared to almost nothing paid by locals. You have to pay that to be able to access the entire area. Not worth the money. "My generous donation will help you preserve the heritage" (as stated on the ticket) however should the locals be also interested to take a part? After you pay the entrance fee almost nothing is in English. You have to open google to get at least some information. Also you would expect at least basic English knowledge of the staff if you charge this entrance fee. We had a disagreement with the staff I took as 15 mins to find someone who can speak basic English. Or at least clean up at the historical sites from all the garbage. I can't really see here that the money is actually going in the heritage. Didn't buy it. Also to be honest there is not that much you can see for the money here unless you are really a big history fan or Buddhist.

title: Nice monument
text: This was our first temple in the Anuradhapura tour and it was particularly nice especially for the bright color of the Buddha.

title: Stunning
text: Nothing more to add. It's a must see place and is so colourful. I could spend hours just looking at the detail.

title: Very beautiful place
text: We visited this beautiful old Stupa as part of a full visit to the old town of Anuradhapura! There was a gentlemen there who explained us a bit about the Stupa. The full visit is really recommended but you have to get a bike or do it by car/tuktuk which is way less fun. If you do the tour by yourself better to have google maps with you as a lot of things are hidden.....

title: Beautiful stupa with the red brick covering
text: This was suppose to be the tallest stupa when it as built. Huge area surrounding the stupa and the red brick outer covering is very beautiful

title: 17 years old monk !
text: 17 years old monk explained us hole story of Buddha ! He was amazing , calm , mature ... such a great energy.. even he allowed us to take some photo !

title: Serene
text: The views of this ancient stupa was breathtaking and the surroundings were so serene. This stupa is off the tourist track and from the hustle and bustle of loud tourists worth the visit

title: Impressive

title: 93.3 million baked bricks were used in its construction.
text: The Jetavanaramaya is a stupa located in the ruins of Jetavana in the sacred world heritage city of Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka. Mahasena of Anuradhapura (273–301) initiated the construction of the stupa following the destruction of the mahavihara. His son Maghavanna I completed the construction of the stupa. it is also significant in recorded history as one of the tallest structures in the ancient world and the second tallest non-pyramidal buildings after Pharos (lighthouse) of Alexandria; the height of the stupa is 400 feet, making it the tallest stupa in the ancient world. The structure is no longer the tallest, but it is still the largest, with a base-area of 2,508,000 sq ft. Approximately 93.3 million baked bricks were used in its construction. Its not very popular as some other stupas in the area still very impressive and a must see sight if you are at that area. It is a religious sight and you have to walk bear foot.

title: Mind-boggling architecture of ancient world !
text: The Jetavanaramaya is a stupa located in the ruins of Jetavana in the sacred world heritage city of ANURADHAPURA,, which was also the ancient capital, Sri Lanka. It was completed at the beginning of 4th Century AD. A part of a sash or belt tied by the Buddha is believed to be the relic that is enshrined here. It is also significant in recorded history as one of the tallest structures in the ancient world; the height of the stupa is 400 feet (122 m),making it the tallest stupa in the ancient world. Approximately 93.3 million baked bricks were used in its construction. Conservation work has been funded by the income from ticket sales, mainly to foreign tourists . The entry fee for Foreign tourists is quite high at Rs.3750 per person. As you are required to remove your shoes ; on a hot day you may not be able to walk around the stupa.

title: amazing ancient site
text: This was the first site in Anuradhapura that we were taken to by our driver/guide and we were very impressed. To think that this 'building' pre-dates Christianity puts it, to my mind, alongside the pyramids in Egypt. OK there is not a great deal to do here except wander round but it is truly amazing. Additionally we were treated to the company of several coachloads of Sri Lankan children visiting at the same time as us. They were delightful and seemed to be fascinated by our fair skins and hair ( our driver suspected that they had come from remote village schools and not familiar with Westerners) and wanted to be photographed with us. This was a worthwhile visit for us. I would also like to put an alternative viewpoint to those posters who complain about the cost of entry to Anuradapura. The cost at around 3500 rupees is under UK£20, less than you would pay for a decent evening meal and this is for the whole city site which I doubt could be visited in full in one whole day. It is an historic site of world importance which housed an amazingly sophisticated civilisation pre-dating the birth of Christ. That it is not better known is surprising. As for the fact that locals pay a lesser entry fee (and this applies to sites throughout Sri Lanka and in some shops and restaurants too), I grant that this is an unusual arrangement but I personally do not begrudge them. We Westerners have probably spent more on our trip than the average Sri Lankan earns in a year. Third World country residents need all the help they can in improving their lot
