title: Largest Stupa in Anuradhapura
text: Jethawanaramaya is the largest stupa in the area and probably the largest in Sri Lanka itself. Our guide mentioned that this is the largest brick structure in the world. Irrespective of the superlatives, this is a magnificent structure. The size does impress you. There is a very long history around this Stupa. The Stupa was built by King Mahasena ( 3rd Century AD) and was renovated and developed by successive kings. At the time of King Parakaramabahu the Great ( 10th Century) the Stupa was around 120mtrs high.Currently the Stupa stands at 73 mtrs till the broken Spire. We visited in the morning time and there were hardly any one at the stupa. There wasn't any one to check the tickets too.

title: Huge and Impressive
text: I preferred this to the Ruwanwelisseya Dagoba as it is far less crowded and appears a little forgotten compared to its rival, but the greater proximity to the trees and the additional troops of monkeys drives a feeling of awe and exoticism to the stupa. This is amplified further by the sheer size and worn exterior, and with there being fewer visitors to distract you its somewhere you can take it all in and enjoy in your own time.

title: Huge and testimony to building skills
text: This stupa is more than 120 metres high and quite incredible to look at even from a distance given that it contains so many bricks. It shows a level of technological sophistication existed hundreds of years ago. I observed many monkeys in and around this stupa.

title: Interesting Historic Site
text: Very Good. The Stupa is one of the oldest in Sri-lanka and a place of importance to Buddhists. The building is old and very tall for the date it was built.

title: Enjoyable, but same for me as most of the Sub-Continent
text: I do not suggest a driver. I prefer solo. Try not to engage the locals The tuk-tuk driver tried to get me to pay 2000 rupees for the day. I enjoyed the pictures and the hike and the history. As I learned in Nepal and Kenya, always barter and start REAL small.

title: One of the ancient monuments you should not missed with Buddha's relic consecrated
text: The ancient wisdom of building dome shape from the unknown bare hands method always a big wow to witness! One of largest stupa with widest base structures, believed to host as large as 10,000 monks during that time.

title: One of the tallest structures of the ancient world
text: Definitely worth to be seen. Stupas are where the ashes of Buddhist monks are kept. You can walk around it but barefoot only. Many monkeys can be seen on the stupa as well. The stupa is 122m. high so it's quite impressive.

title: Great experience
text: Again whole Anuradhapura Sri Lanka trip gave us very pleasant feeling , nice place to explore and also to spend days in a great historical site.

title: Unique
text: All I know is that I keep wondering what happened to the top of the stupa itself as out of the three giant stupas in Anuradhapura it is the only one missing a chunk. Also out of the three stupas this one seemed to be the most tranquil and the least visited (very few people there when I visited). I say go and take a walk around. There were also a lot of monkeys at this compound and they made for great entertainment.

title: Unique and inspiring
text: This is one of the greatest attractions of the ancient sacred city of Anuradhapura and is a 'must' to see. One of the many wonderful things about the Anuradhapura experience is the immense variety of structures to be seen and this huge building of Jethawanaramaya is very different from others because of its construction from brick. It is quite amazing how the brickwork was done. If one purchases a ticket for the main attractions of Anuradhapura, this stupa is included in the price. As with all of the sacred places, shoes must be removed before entering and appropriate clothing worn.

title: The third highest building in the ancient world, after pyramids in Giza.
text: One of the very important monument of the Sri Lankan early kingdoms and buddhism history! Don't miss it! Don't forget, hat and shoes forbidden inside the sacred area. You will need sun protection cream, and exchange socks is very practical. The reason not just the dirty floor (these places wasn't really dirty), very often the stone very hot without shoes. I recommend you, before the visit you must read some historical fact about this place, will be interesting the visit!

title: An integral part of the Anuradhapura experience
text: A wonderful structure which must be visited whilst in Anuradhapura. It is quite different to the other stupas in the area and the brickwork is impressive. It is included in the main ticket.

title: Vast and awe-inspiring
text: Amazing that this massive, apparently younger structure is so old - and the brickwork is really impressive.

title: Too high entrance fee
text: This is just like any other buddhist stupa only probably huger than the rest. The entrance fee is too high LKR 3250 per person. SAARC nations get it at half that price, but it is still expensive. When you buy the ticket, you get entrace to about 7-8 religious places, but all are alike. There are either brick stupas or white ones. The same kind of ponds with garbage strewn in the sides. The guardian stone and the moonstone also aren't anything great. You need to remove your footwear to visit these temples. I don't have a problem with that. It is religious. The only problem was the stone heats up too quickly and it was like walking on burning coal. Something needs to be done for this. By the end of the tour, we were less interested in seeing the monuments and more interested in finding shade for our feet. The museum has random pieces of pottery, jewellery and statues. Some are from India and other countries. All in all, I did not find it worth the price of the entrance ticket. And if you are from India, it is not too different from the local ruins we find in Hampi, Halebeedu etc.

title: Don't Forget the Museum
text: Another impressive dagaba, this time with the bricks exposed. It is located away from the main pilgrim site. Even so it attracts the masses at religious festivals. The small museum displays the finds made from around this structure

title: A wonderful Dagoba
text: A perfect dagoba , build long time ago ...perfect design and esthetic result is top ....move around don't forget to go according a clockwise way .

title: Huuuuuge
text: They say that you can build a three metres high wall from London to Edinburgh with the bricks that were used to build this Dagoba. Pretty impressive. And could you please use some of the massive entree fees(US$ 25) to Anuradhapura historical site to clean up all the litter. Would show as much respect for these holu sites as taking of your shoes.

title: Really Impressive!
text: A really impressive piece of historic architecture. Absolutely put this on your list of places to visit whilst exploring the ruins and historic sites of Anuradhapura.

title: Good
text: Like most of the Dagobas it is large with a small shrine. Very much a recommend to those Buddhists. As a simple tourist I enjoyed it but wasn't spectacular.

title: After visiting Myanmar this is really poor
text: This Stupa might be nice in case you haven't visited Myanmar - but after visiting Myanmar with all the great Stupas - this one is below average.

title: Towering and impressive dagoba (ancient domed temple)
text: Let me first preface by saying Anuradhapura is a long distance to travel from the main coastal resorts and so you should probably only consider if you are touring the island. It was about a two hour drive from Sigiriya. The area is too big to cover on foot in a single day and, whilst bicycles and TukTuks are easy and cheap to hire, I would recommend a driver/guide who can direct you to and provide commentary on the most significant sites. The four main stupas (Jethawanaramaya/Jethavanarama, Rutwanwelisaya, Thuparama and Abhayaagiri) are all different. You won’t need more than 10-15 minutes at each unless you want to stay to worship, We don’t think there is any entrance charge – we weren’t asked for any money and there were no ticket checks. As for all temples, you must dress respectfully (legs and shoulders covered). You need to remove hats and shoes but you can wear socks which I would recommend as the stones underfoot can be hot and sharp. Of the four main stupas, we liked Jethawanaramaya/Jethavanarama the best. At 400ft high with a 370ft diameter base on a 670ft square rock base, this is the largest stupa in Anuradpura and one of the tallest brick structures in the world. It was built in the 3rd century. The dome is unpainted. It was very quiet and tranquil. Once part of a huge monastery and you can see the ruins all around. It is worth visiting the museum where you can see a good collection of guardstones and ancient jewellery. There is a clean toilet here too. Rutwanwelisaya has a massive white painted dome. It is 180ft (used to be twice that). It is surrounded by wall with over 300 elephant sculptures but almost all these are restored or replacements. It can get busy with devotees coming to pray. Thuparama is the smallest and oldest of the main stupas in Anuradhapura (what you see is mainly reconstructed). Its significance is that it is said to enshrine the collarbone of the Buddha and as such there are lots of pilgrims actively worshipping. A white dome surrounded by stone pillars which used to support a wooden cover. See separate review of Abhayaagiri.

title: Impressive opener
text: First we would like to say what we think the Anuradhapura Sacred precinct is and what it isn't. It is not Angkor Wat. We met lots of people that were slightly disappointed because they were expecting Angkor Wat scaled temples. It is however very impressive in its own way, especially if you use your imagination to envision what was once there and that thousands of monks once roamed around here. Apart from the Stupa, only the foundations of the monasteries are left because the buildings were wooden structures and rotted away centuries ago. But the sheer size of the this complex and the other complexes makes it worth coming here. Details such as beautifully carved gnome like creatures, animals and Cobra Kings provide delicate finishing touches of the monuments.

title: Our favourite on our "ruined" day
text: This was our first and best of the day. It is massive structure which dwarfs you the closer you get. The kids enjoyed walking around

title: Become a dwarf in the shadow of this Stupa
text: Jethawana Stupa is huge. Its huge from along way away and its even bigger as you get closer. You can see it from Minihtale and everywhere in Anuradhapura! Its 80 m high and 220 m wide. You cant miss it and you will be drawn to it. Its so impressive, its a statement about the power of the religion which built it. I prefer to view it in the morning.

title: Arrive late afternoon
text: We arrived at late afternoon, a timing when it was uncrowded and definitely cooler. Dusk spectacular.

title: An amazing brick structure
text: As one of the tallest brick structures in the world this stupa is truly awe inspiring. We went here in the evening and it was far less busy than the other main temples in the city. Well worth a visit for all those who like history and to admire the marvels of the past.

title: This entire area is worth the visit
text: All of the ancient ruins in this area are very interesting. The museum that starts the touring area is very informative. Lots of barefoot walking involved and much on hot ground.

title: Another marvellous example of human endeavour
text: Whilst some seem to be unimpressed it is amazing to think of the effort that went into constructing this building which is large but nevertheless very beautiful. I agree that sensible folk might enjoy their tour of the Sacred City more in the early part of the day to avoid the heat and crowds. Allows time just to enjoy being there without hiding from the sun or having the ales of your feet burnt. This is one stop that all who visit Anuradhapura will want to make

title: same as Jethawanaramaya Stupa
text: This is the same thing, yeah? twice in TripAdvisor = once as stupa and once as dagoba. Oh well. It was cool to see it, very large, impressive and fascinating ruins around it.

title: Largest?
text: There seems to be some confusion about whether this is indeed the largest, it was impressive nevertheless and wandering about the ruins (including a nice large image house) was fun.

title: Simple Beautiful, need to be taken care of.
text: When we get there you feel big, and proud about what the Sri Lankan king’s did for Buddhism. This place need government attention, and need to be looked after well.

title: Amazing structure
text: For me I find it hard to comprehend the age of the stupa, quite amazing. Best seen early in the morning no heat, no people, just a few monkeys and a lot of bird life. I think it would be difficult to walk around the stupa in the middle of the day, as you have to remove your shoes and it would be hot on your feet.

title: Largest Stupa
text: OK so it's the largest Stupak, with many millions of bricks, but apart from walking around the outside, that's it.

title: Good Stupa
text: This building is very good and deserves its status. However my lasting memory of the Sacred city will be the filth and rubbish, not to mention the scabby starving dogs. If the city is so sacred why do the locals treat it so badly?

title: Absolutely astounding
text: The whole Anuradhapura area is a sight. We got bikes and went around to look at everything, all the Stupas and it was gorgeous. We did't even get that 25 USD ticket, you can get so close to the Stupas and even walk through the ruins, it was enough for us. It feels a little like tomb raiding, a mystical place with lots of monkeys running around. We even got to see a varan near the Jethawana Stupa.

title: Nice deserted stupa
text: Other stupas were filled with people but this stupa was a bit off the beaten track and not as well restored so had only a few people but with wildlife just roaming around. Monkeys climbing over the stupa and the rich red brick of the stupa made for some nice shots.

title: Well preserved site
text: It was a nice visit to see the old Stupa with devotees around it. Peaceful place to go around. Close to a small informative museum

title: Impressive
text: The ruins are very impressive and compare favorably with other Southeast Asia destinations. A day well spent

title: Large and important to Buddhists
text: Having said that it’s not that impressive if you’ve seen this kind of thing in Myanmar and Thailand. If you haven’t it’s worth a look.

title: An Atamasthana Attraction.One of the Eight sacred locations in Anuradhapura.
text: Also known as Uththararamaya it is the 4th largest manmade structure and the 2nd largest Dhagoba in the world.

title: The tallest of the Buddhist stupa
text: Apart of being a sacred edifice, Jethawanaramaya by far is the giant of all the stupas. Of the man-made structures in the world it has been recorded that this edifice was only the third to pyramids and the tallest of all the stupas in the world rising to almost over 120 meters. With the gradual weathering over the years and collapse, apparently the height has reduced and what remains today is the outcome of the last restoration by another great Sri lankan king - Parakramabahu in 12th century. The Stupa is conserved beautifully and reflects the engineering skills of the ancient Sri lankan people.

title: Not so popular but interesting
text: This stupa is close to the archeological museum which in closed for reconstruction. Therefore there was nobody there when we visited the stupa. Really an experience, especially with a big her of monkeys climbing the stupa

title: 3rd biggest stupa in the world
text: You feel very humble when you standing close it , glad to see it getting well maintained and the playful monkeys around it

title: Largest Stupa in the World
text: This was our first stop visiting the Anuradhapura ancient site which is the UNESCO World Heritage Site. Entrance fee for the entire site is LKR4,550 or USD25 per person per entry. It is the significant structure as biggest and tallest building in the ancient world of Anuradhapura Kingdom in 3rd-4th century. Best way to visit the site is by hiring a driver since the site is huge and scattered and not within walking distance. We engaged our driver service with “BLUE HAVEN TOURS” with fantastic and dedicated driver. Dress appropriately with cover shoulder and pants/ dress below knee. If possible, wear socks as walking on the sandstone under the daylight can be burning for the feet. Drinking water is essential too. Nice start to explore the Anuradhapura Ancient site. Unfortunately, the museum was closed for renovations during our visit, otherwise it would be informative prior to visiting to the sites.

title: Review of the entire Anuradhapura experience-self guided
text: We are traveling by rented tuktuk and had read that we could drive ourselves to the different sites after purchasing our ticket. We did not hire a guide, as we had read extensively and had a map. However, the map provided by the ticket counter wasn’t entirely accurate and so it was a little tricky to figure out where exactly things were, as they are quite spread out. Allow yourself a full day, perhaps find a good guide, dress appropriately for temple visits (we did not know that white dress is recommended for viewing the ancient Bodhisattva Tree, but luckily covered my black shirt with a sarong I’d brought), and bring water! There are some good food stalls next to the Moonstone site that sell cold coconuts for water, and make excellent veggie and coconut roti-highly recommend this too. An excellent day spent.

title: This place was amazing!
text: The sheer scale of it cannot be captured in a photo. If you are travelling here, I highly recommend hiring a guide to explain the significance of it, as the information they provide gives the experience a new level of depth allowing you to appreciate the site even more.

title: Magnificent Stupa
text: Very fine stupa. Nice ambiance around it. Visited late afternoon which was a good time for the light for photos

title: Rustic Stupa with Strong Spiritual Vibe
text: This stupa left the strongest impression. Hidden by forest overgrowth and abandoned for centuries, the plants enveloping it have been cut away and what you see is what was left. Rustic in appearance and only slightly restored, this stupa also has a small shrine to the Buddha, with a large reclining Buddha statue with offerings laid before it. It has a curious authenticity, and you can best view what these stupas are made of: Millions of handmade bricks. This was once the largest brick structure in the world.

title: MONUMENTAL SCALE
text: At 122m, this is the tallest stupa ever built. Some 93 million baked bricks were used in the construction. Its foundation is 8.5m deep, sitting on bedrock. Like many sites here, it was rebuilt. It was built as an act of attrition.

title: Superb
text: The stupas at Anuradhapura are mind-blowing! Jethawanaramaya Stupa is massive, and you keep wondering how they built these huge structures during those times!

title: Incredible stupa.
text: We visited this area and saw this magnificent stupa when touring Sri Lanka. It was a recommended visit by our guide who took us to some amazing areas. We took some great photos as the area wasn’t too busy as it was the low season. I imagine it could get very busy and hot during the peak season. There were some people selling items but they were not a nuisance.

title: Another great Buddhist pilgrimage site
text: This stupa is believed to contain a sacred bowl which lord Buddha is believed to have ate from. The bowl is believed to be buried almost 200 feet deep.

title: Amazing place
text: This is worth seeing on your trip around the sacred lands. This is enormous. I was told that there are an estimated 93 million bricks used for this relic, as it is solid inside. The shear quantity is impossible to fathom and still makes me think now. The grounds themselves are very large and every angle keeps showing you the scale of this.

title: First of our visits in Anuradhapura
text: This is the tallest and largest of the stupas in Anuradhapura. Originally it was 400fy high. It is a world heritage monument. It has a long history with the first Sinhala Buddhist king who built the stupa. He dedicated to a monk named Tissa who lived in a local temple. Jetavana is the stupa of this monastery. It will s huge to walk around and admire the architecture and engineering even if one is not a Buddhist. Enshrined in the stupa are relics that some believe belong to lord Buddha himself.

title: How did they build this?
text: Largest stupa in the world. Lost of monkeys running on top of stupa, an amazing sight. Incredible feat of engineering for it to be built during it time with no heavy machinery or technology.

title: Fascinating visit.
text: This is very different from other stupas as it is made of brick and a visit is worth it and the nearby museum as many wonderful artefacts including jewellery and carvings.

title: Different Than The Rest
text: This was build almost 2,000 years ago and was one of the tallest buildings in the world at that time. Most of the stupas in the area are white, so this one stands out. Nice place to take a photo, but don't fly a drone here. They are very strict about this and could even arrest you.

title: Great temple and plenty of birdlife
text: This was our first stop using our Anuradhapura cultural ticket and we really enjoyed exploring Jetavanaramaya Dagoba. Walking through the grounds before we reached the dagoba we came across a number of different birds including egrets, grey hornbills, flycatchers and bee-eaters, which was lovely. The dagoba itself is huge - it's lost some height so must have been really impressive back in its day. Walking around the base is a must but be minded to wear socks - the floor is hot and a bit gritty and my husband even managed to stand on broken glass, so barefoot is not ideal. There's a brightly painted reclining buddha here too. Take time to explore the grounds as they are a pleasant place to get lost. We didn't spend long at all in the museum - just walked around the 3 different rooms rather quickly. Lots of decent bike parking if you are cycling the temples.

title: Interesting
text: Interesting place in good condition, beautiful paintings showing the story of Buddha and the kingdoms

title: An attraction for devote Buddhists
text: It has almost the same Buddhist statues you find in most Buddhist places. Interesting only if your a devoted Buddhist, if not I would recommend you skip this place.

title: Disappointing after Dambulla
text: Having been to Dambulla caves this stupa just seemed too bright and over renovated. Admittedly we didn't have a guide but generally the temple site is pretty and worth a visit as part of the Anuradhapura experience.

title: One more ancient stupa
text: Good to visit if you are devout Buddhist. Not being a Buddhist nor of religious bent of mind and the stupa not being of particular architectural interest, I could easily have given it a miss.

title: Vacation
text: A Reclining Buddha inside part of the Stupa's structures. Brighty painted and walls also. People come inside to prey. Dress accordingly.

title: Big stupa with large reclining buddha
text: Along with the Abhayagiri Dagaba this is one of the main attractions of the Anuradhapura heritage site and, to be fair it’s an impressive structure - a huge domed structure built from over 90 million bricks. There is also a chamber housing a large reclining buddha. Other than the scale of the structure thete’s Not a lot to it and I have to say we found th3 whole archaeological site to be somewhat disappointing - over rated and hugely overpriced.

title: The reclining Buddha photo Tripadvisor headlines isn't here, its at Isurumuniya
text: This is an ancient temple, the one that is reputed to be the largest brick built structure in the world using over 90 million individual bricks. Very impressive, they compare this to the pyramids of Giza as an ancient structure, and having been there a few times I can understand why considering the work that would have taken place is comparable to Egypt. In fact If all the stupas in Anuradhapura were together on an open plain like those in Giza these might be as famous, but dotted around the old city with lots of the famous green vegitation and trees of Sri Lanka it renders the comparison impossible. As with most of Anuradhapura signage was practically non existent with very little in the way of historical description at each monument.

title: Nice reclining Buddha
text: Located at the stuppa this is a nice reclining Buddha. The whole entrance is surrounded by Hindu scenes from the Ramayana which of course ties it to Sri Lanka.

title: Tallest stupa in Sri Lanka
text: There are several very famous stupas, and this is the tallest. It is visited by families, children and visitors offering flowers and lighting incense. A very popular place and a recommended visit.

title: BIG STUPA
text: Its HUGE. As far as I could tell, it is the main sight of this section of ancient ruins in Anuradhapura. As always, there is an area where everyone leaves their shoes.

title: Worth a visit
text: A calm and peaceful place, well worth the visit. As always it's barefoot so avoid the midday sun. Early in the day would be best.

title: Very Impressive
text: Incredible piece of engineering and a very impressive sight. Well worth a look at this Stupa as well as the other ones dotted around Anuradhapura. We were driven around by Ranil from artlankatours.com Ranil gave us a whistle-stop tour of the main attractions in the city and was very knowledgeable about all of them, highly recommend him.

title: Another Dagoba / Stupa
text: This was our third dagoba / stupa of the day and if we are honest, they were beginning to get repetitive. However, having paid an eye watering 3,500 Sri Lankan rupees each, we were determined to see as much as possible in the day. Underwhelmed by the whole experience.

title: Huge Dagoba
text: This was our third dagoba of the day and whilst the temple and the reclining Buddha were impressive, our poor bare feet could not cope with another circuit of another dagoba. The tourist board should reconsider its policy of forcing people to cram so many sites into one day (as there is no way we'd pay an additional 3,500 Sri Lankan rupees as a European visitor for the pleasure of having a more leisurely visit over two days).

title: Impressive feat of engineering
text: This is the biggest stupa in the world in terms of area and an impressive feat of engineering. The stupa has an attached museum, which is above average and gives a lot of context about the visit to the stupa. The area around the stupa has lots of archaeology, so interesting also for the history buffs.

title: Small bricks amazing size Stupa
text: This Stupa is believed to be the biggest brick built structure in the world and when you visit it you will be amazed at the size (small) of the bricks used in its construction, it is an amazing sight.

title: Fantastic
text: This site is listed twice here and may support the must see importance of it amidst the sacred sites in Anuradhapura. Please see rating for first listing of Jetavanarama Dagoba.

title: Most impressive stupa ever
text: Somewhat ignored by most pilgrims, yet this is the most impressive of the stupas in the historic city (and one of the 8 sacred sites). Without much ado, the focus here is clearly on the stupa (highest brick stupa ever built), the Bo Tree and the Buddha image. A tour towards the end of the day will give you fantastic light for your walk around. Makes for superb photo shots! The remains of the adjacent monastery are impressive both in size as well as functionality. Do not miss this stupa on your tour!

title: Jetavanarama Dagoba
text: Can't enter this temple but can walk right around the perimeter. Very large, so remember to wear a sun hat or carry an umbrella as there is no shelter from sun.

title: One amongst many Dagobas!
text: There are many Dagobas and Stupas in Anuradhapura but each one must be visited to experience the scale again and again. Walk around it and grasp its vastness. Be sure to carry socks as in summers the floor get too hot to walk on and one cant wear footwear here!

title: Amazing Scale!
text: The scale of this Stupa does it. It is amazing to just walk all around it and experience its vastness. Must visit and must walk around. Be careful of summers! It gets very hot and the stone floor burns the feet as you cant wear footwear. Carry socks!!

title: Superb site
text: The massive stupa remains in front of your eye for hours after the visit. The broken top of the stupa has its own interesting story and the circumferential pradikshina (roundabout) is best attempted in the mornings or evenings when the sun is a good deal lower. The weather can be intensely hot at times - hence dress accordingly. However do note that caps and hats are not allowed - also women are expected to cover their shoulders and cover themselves below their knees. Together with its sister stupa, this one offers some of the best preserved potions of the Anuradhapura archaeological complex!

title: Incredible!
text: This towering structure is the largest stupa in Anuradhapura and demands a stop. Unfortunately my spouse and I experienced a heavy rain during our tour and we were unable to get good photos. As such, we did not get to see all that wished.

title: See both Stupas and enjoy the jungle
text: A major step back in time to see this brick tower rising from the jungle. Stepping of tonthe renovated stuba you then have a picture of a lost world and one refurbished and continuing as a place of worship.

title: Biggest brick stupa!
text: Stopped here on a quick visit to Anuradhapura. No ticket needed, just drove up, took shoes off and visited. Be careful, the cement gets very hot! Not much info in English, so read about it before visiting. Enjoy!

title: The scale of these stupa is unbelievable
text: Really interesting part of the anuradhapura complex. The sheer scale is amazing and as it's not rendered you can see how they were built. It gives you a feel for how magnificent the site was in its heyday

title: Massive and Vast ancient kingdom!
text: The scale of ancient settlement Anurahpura is one of the most impressive archeological sights the technology and the cultural enlightment of these ancient forbears of the modern day Ceylonese is amazing. This city is vast and takes a full days expoloration. Be aware take plenty of water and sunscreen.

title: Amazing temple
text: We arrived at about 4 pm and we witnessed a prayer ceremonie with traditional trumpet play. Amazing impressive site. Apparantly, according to our driver, the ceremonie was rare and symbolised prayer to people. To see the temples, you need to pay a pass worth 3500 roepies a person. Only tourists pay this.

title: Unique and inspiring
text: I have travelled all over Asia but the stupas and temples here in Sri Lanka are unique. The size and mass and scale of Jethawanaramaya is truly awe inspiring. Why this sight is not up there with the likes of the Pyramids or Angkor Wat I don't know. The size of the surrounding plaza makes it easy to step aside and be Alone for a moment. Take time to sit away in a corner to soak this place up. Watch the locals worship. Just be... Try to hook in to a moment of spirituality. Surrounded by ancient ruins this site is easily accessible by car and should be incorporated into any tour but it's beauty is its simplicity so I am not sure a guide is necessary. Don't think about it.... Go there!

title: A vision of local history
text: There's ruins seem to share a theme with others in other parts do the world ie Canbodia where Indian themes are present.

title: Amazing piece of history
text: This stupa has been restored but without rendering the outside walls as was the norm in this period,because of that you can see more of how it was built and all the brickwork

title: Jethawanaramaya Stupa
text: Incredibly, we were the only ones there when we visited. Something Like 93 Million bricks were used in its construction Very impressive and a must see if in the area.

title: Once the Tallest Structure in the World after Pyramids
text: JETAVANA DAGOBA The Jetavana Dagoba (Stupa), a UNESCO world heritage site, is the highest brick-built Dagobah in the world, founded by King Mahasena (276-303 AC) upon Mahayana Buddhism, on the ruins of an old monatery. When built with over 93 million bricks in 27 years, it was the third tallest structure in the world after two pyramids of Khufu & Khafra in Giza, Cairo (Egypt). Originally its height was 397 feet and it was erected on land measuring 8 acres. Its diameter was more than 330 feet. Today it is 230 feet high and restoration work is in progress. Before wearing down of its pinnacle, erosion of ground and burial of the base, its height was 400 feet. The Jetavana monastery in its hey days housed bout 3000 monks. It is one of the sixteen most sacred cultural destinations in Anuradhapura.

title: One of the most calming places in evening
text: We visited Jethawanaramaya Stupa in the evening. The lighting was really great and the calmness is at its best. Its not very popular as some other stupas in the area. On that day we were the only people there. And the brick work is quite beautiful with the lights.

title: Oldest Vihara of Sri Lanka
text: Great Place to see.. Oldest Vihara .. of 1st century...Worth visiting ... structure is entact... and appealing...

title: Another beautiful stupa - but take socks

title: Sacred stupa
text: The Ruwanwelisaya is a stupa, considered sacred to many Buddhists all over the world. The stupa was a ruin in the 19th century and, after a fundraising campaign, was renovated in the early 20th century. Anuradhapura was the first historical capital of Sri Lanka and today is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (part of the Cultural Triangle), often on the touristic routes. Dating back to 380AD, the site contains ancient ruins, dagobas and temples, all "contained" in an archaeological park. You will need to organise transport to explore them as I think there is simply too much distance to cover by foot. The most common options are either by tuk tuk or by bicycle. In my opinion, in general, the whole site is pretty disappointing. As the country has better attractions (i.e.Polonnaruwa), I would visit Anuradhapura only in case you have some spare time (and an extra budget). Unfortunately, not worth it from my point of view USEFUL INFO Entry ticket to the site: 25,00 USD per person (only cash) Journey time from Sigiriya by tuk tuk: around 1h30mins PRO TIP Since it is a religious site still in use today, please bear in mind that everybody is asked to dress properly (shoulders and knees must be covered, and shoes and hats must be removed). Because of the latter, I highly suggest to carry also a pair of socks into your bag as sometimes the ground can be very warm/hot.

title: Originally, two millennia old, but looks to be regularly maintained and recently embellished
text: This huge white stupa is another place of active Buddhist worship, though less busy than Sri Maha Bodhi. Its construction is said to have begun over 2,000 years ago, but from its well-maintained look, much of it may be of more recent origin. It is characterised by a parade of elephants carved in relief all around the base of the stupa. As a place of worship, shoes have to be removed to enter the area. Ruwanwelisaya is usually listed as among the sights of “Sacred City/Ancient Ruins” park, but it lies outside the paid area, in other words, entry is free. From here it is a short walk southwards to the ruins of Lovamahapaya Brazen Palace (nothing much to see, free) and further south, to Sri Maha Bodhi, the chief Buddhist site in the area (also free). General info about places in the “Sacred City/Ancient Ruins” park: The sights are quite spread out such that while walking from one sight to the second may be possible, covering many more on foot is impractical. You’ll need a map and a bicycle or a tuktuk hired for the day. Also, there few toilets, and few places to buy drinking water. Be prepared.

title: It's A Landmark Thing
text: When you set aside religion and look at these ancient sights as landmarks to this area and to the country. As a tourist they are worth a visit as much as you would visit the Eiffel Tower in Paris and the Statue of Liberty in New York etc, etc. There is something to get from visiting them. Something to feel and understand. It is the feeling of the heat of the paved slabs or rock steps under your feet and an appreciation and understanding forming of what worship is like for these people here. It is the physical exertion on your body to reach the highest point. It is the tranquility of the landscape that these sights are built around. It is the bewilderment of the age of the relics and the size in which some have been made. It is the sights of monkeys behaving like this is their home. It is the noise of traditional music as an organ may be playing if you were to visit a Cathedral. It is the gentle murmurs of worship coming from peoples prayers. It is the shade of the tree whether it be regarded as holy or not. It is the smell of incense and the sight of flowers given as a gift. It is the welcoming smiles of the Sri Lankan people who are happy to include you here regardless of your religion. It is something you do and recommend you do when you are visiting another country.

title: Hard to justify 25USD entrance fee
text: To visit the ancient Anuradhapura city it will cost you 25USD (for Sri Maha Bodhi Temple there are additional 200LRK + "donation" for the place where they store shoes that you have to take off before entering the dagoba). I find the entrance fee heavily overprices for what it is. The Ruwanwelisaya Dagoba is just one of many historical sites scattered across many km2. When buying the ticket (which is at quite some random place) you get basically nothing. No map/no brochure nothing. So unless you do home work on how to visit the place/what to see you will have to hire a guide (so additional cost). If you do not have a driver there will be also an additional cost to hire a transportation as well as the area can not be seen on foot. The Anuradhapura has few pagodas (dagobas) which are in general well preserved (looking very similar) and then tons on badly preserved buildings (only things what is left over are some brinks showing the outline of the buildings) and this is basically it. Few sites will have some basic information about the site. There is also an museum which is like 2 or 3 rooms with few artifacts that one can see in like 10min. If you are on the budget/time constrains I would skip this place all together and just visit Polonnaruwa as I think it is more to see/better preserved sites and just a better value for the 25USD that you will pay for Polonnaruwa as well.

title: One of the most sacred places in Sri Lanka
text: I visit here normally 4-6 time an year. It was built by King Dutugemunu c. 140 B.C., who became lord of all Sri Lanka after a war in which the Chola King Elara, was defeated. It is also known as ‘‘‘Mahathupa’’’, ‘‘‘Swarnamali Chaitya’’’, ‘‘‘Suvarnamali Mahaceti’’’ (in Pali) and ‘‘‘Rathnamali Dagaba’’’. The stupa is one of the world’s tallest monuments, standing at 103 m (338 ft) and with a circumference of 290 m (951 ft). If you get down from Anuradhapura Railway station you have can have a 20 mins walk and arrive here. But also you can get a tuk tuk also. It can be expensive for foreigners, make sure you negotiate the price before starting the journey since the rate in tuk tuks aren't fixed in Sri Lanka. Make sure you are not wearing short skirts, short trousers, tight trousers, sleeveless tops, tank tops etc. Also don't wear hats, caps or any kind of slippers since this is a very sacred place for Buddhists. It can be hot in day time. Make sure you are wearing socks or else it will be really hard walk. Don't turn your back to stupa when taking pics. It will be really beautiful at night with the lights on as you can see in the pictures. in Poya days it can be crowded.

title: A memorable visit.
text: We visited this historic stupa as part of our tour of Sri Lanka,and yes, it is a very sacred place for Buddhists and well worth a visit. We were there on the day the Bodhi tree - a very ancient tree - was celebrating an anniversary and there were hundreds of pilgrims dressed in white and bringing gifts of flowers. A very memorable visit. Appropriate dress for all Buddhist temples includes no hats or shoes.We were asked to wear long trousers, but as it's very hot and you're often travelling elsewhere, I would say that zip off trousers for men are really useful. Ladies - knees must be covered , crops were fine and some other tourists wore a sarong to cover their shorts whilst visiting. Another reviewer has mentioned the heat of the paving you have to walk on with bare feet.We were there late morning and the paving ( and there's a lot of it!) was red hot - so hot that we were hopping from one foot to another trying to avoid burning our feet. Little trainer socks are invaluable!! It's quite acceptable to wear them and your feet don't burn. All stupas / temples require shoes to be removed (there's always someone to look after them for you for a very small sum) but some are surrounded by large gritty areas and those little socks are great! It's a wonderful country - so many great sights and lovely people!

title: Super Stupas
text: This is a general review of the whole of Anuradhapura. If you are going to Anuradhapura it is highly unlikely that you will just go to see just one of the many attractions there. This is an interesting place to visit for those interested in history and culture. It covers the ruins of a vast Buddhist monastic city. There are gigantic stupas the size of Egyptian pyramids, which contain holy Buddhist relics and an incredible irrigation system that are both nearly 2000 years old. Also to be visited on the site is the Sri Maha Bohdi – apparently one of the world’s oldest and most revered trees. It is probably worth retaining the services of an official guide, such is the complexity of the history and scale of the site. We attended on a Sunday which due to the site’s highly religious importance meant it was very crowded with pilgrims. From a cultural point of view this was fascinating, but those interested in the history of the place might find a less busy, mid-week visit, more rewarding. Whenever you choose, Anuradhapura is certainly worth seeing.

title: Magnificent Buddha Vihara
text: RUWANWELISAYA DAGOBAH Ruwanwelisaya is an awe inspiring Dagobah of magnificent architectural style, built during the reign of King Dutugemunu (140 BC). The Dagobah has circumference of 950 feet and height of 338 feet. In 19th century AD, this Dagobah was nothing more than ruins of a magnificent structure. In 20th century, it was renovated and restored with local donations and assistance from UNESCO. It is now a World Heritage Site. A Dagobah is a sacred place of veneration. Generally it is a shrine like domed structure in which are placed relics related to Buddha, Buddhism or remains of Buddhist monks and nuns. The place is also used for meditation and worship. It is also called Stupa, Pagoda or Chedi.

The guide took us to 2 pools and gave a brief description of the structures. Overall he did a good job.

title: World's Magnificent Stupa - NOV 24
text: Ruwanwalisaya is a stupa sacrad to many Buddhist all over the world, It was built by King Dutugamunu, It is believed that the relics of the Buddha are enshrined with the stupa, which is the largest collection of his relics anywhere. Additional tips: * The Stupa quite busy during the poya days, * Men are required to wear long pants and women must cover their shoulders and were lose pants or skirts. * Parking available in walking distance. * Area quite hot during day time * Please protect the site.

title: Amazing Stupa and area.
text: My partner and I have just returned from a great tour of Sri Lanka and this was an excellent site we visited with our guide who was excellent in providing historical details of this area. We took some amazing photos although it was a pity that there was some scaffolding and work being undertaken. Dress modestly and remove shoes. Wear socks as the ground can be very hot. Wet wipes can be useful for cleaning mucky feet. The site was quite busy although it would be very busy at high season. It could also be very hot at certain times of the day. We visited in the morning.

title: Vast!
text: The size of this monument will take your breath away! The white colouring also goes to show how much time is taken on these creations. I was told that the colour is redone yearly for the pilgrimages which must be a colossal task. It is worth going to see this first hand and to witness how much religion means to the sri Lankans

title: The second most sacred place in Sri Lanka
text: This huge white stupa built around 150 BC is the second most sacred Buddhist centre in Sri Lanka after the Tooth Relic Temple in Kandy. What impressed an uninitiated me most, in addition to its antiquity, is the aastha (great belief and devotion is the closest I can some to in English) Sri Lankan Buddhists still have. I saw groups of devotees chanting and a couple lying prostrate and praying. Great place to visit, if you are a devout Buddhist. Be sure legs and arms are covered or you will not be allowed to enter.

title: Vacation
text: The only white plaster Stupa of the three. I believe its the tallest of the three and a very active Temple. Long pants and sleeved shirts are required and no shoes so wear socks, The ground is very hot. Oldest kingdom in Sri Lanka and worth the visit. Plan on 3/4 of a day to see all thier is to see here.

title: Beware of tuk tuk drivers!
text: Mine is intended to be a general review about my trip to Anuradhapura. The archeological area to visit is really huge. You can see many beautiful stupas like Ruwanwelisaya and many other things. If you want to visit the area in the matter my suggestion is to rent a bike. If you think of walking only you are going to miss many things also because you cannot find many signs. Another way to move around is by tuk tuk. You can bargain the price and get a full service at a reasonable price. 1500 rupees is a good deal. However you need to be aware of tuk tuk drivers. I would say that 99% of tuk tuk drivers are really nice but black sheep are behind the corner. The price of the ticket to enter Anuradhapura archeological area is pretty expensive. More precisely it costs 4600 rupees. A ticket is made of three stubs that need to be torn off every time you enter one of the three areas. There are some tuk tuk drivers who might ask you to give them your ticket so that they can show it to the surveillance staff in order to enter the area. If they ask for your ticket, DO NOT give it to them. The ticket belongs to you. It doesn't belong to the tuk tuk drivers. The point is that there are some tuk tuk drivers who take their customers tickets just to show them what they want to show. They aim at ending their trip with the customers asap so that they can start a new trip with other tourists who will be sold the same tickets partly used by the previous tourists.To cut it short tuk tuk drivers resell those tickets to other tourists at a reduced price and take the money deriving from the sell. So be careful. I also want to give some quick information on how to arrive in Anuradhapura if you come from Dambulla. Dambulla is a small city. There is not bus station but of course there are bus stops. The one where you can catch the bus to Anuradhapura is on Kandy road (the main road) 200 meters after the clock tower on your left next to Bata shoe shop. The bus numbers to consider are 15 and 43. If you wanna go to Polonnaruwa from Dambulla the bus stop is the same. The bus number is either 41 or 48. Hope these suggestions are of help.

title: Bustling temple
text: This was the first dagoba we visited during our tour of the archaeological park so it caught us when we were still enthusiastic. It’s a huge white plastered stupa set within a courtyard behind a perimeter wall that includes an impressive frieze of elephants. It’s also clearly very much a working temple and during our visit we witnessed 4 different processions of pilgrims bringing their offerings - all very colourful and atmospheric.

title: interesting
text: all the sites are very interesting. But they are widespread so it is good to have a tuk tuk or bicycle to go round

title: Captivating
text: We went in the evening, and it was one of the most interesting sights on our trip. So many worshipers gathered around, wrapping the stupa in prayer flags, and clouds of incense all around. 100% do an evening visit around sunset and just after.

title: What a day to visit
text: Having been to Mihintale in the morning, the best was left to the afternoon. Shoes off again and we walked a long way without them, so wear thick socks as the ground is hot, although there are areas where they have laid astro which is easy to walk on. Entry was 9500 rupees which covered the different sites in Anuradhapura. We came on a national holiday, Makarsankranti/Pongal, and thousands of buddhists from as far away as Colombo will come for the day as this is the most significant temple in Sri Lanka. It is reputedly built with 100 million bricks and the original temple was built in 140BC. Over time it has had to be rebuilt as at one time it was a ruin in the 19th century and it was rebuilt to twice the original size and completed in 1940. It is 103 metres high and 290 metres in circumference. Stupas were built to enshrine relics of Buddha Most people were dresses in white and families were there as well. There was incense pervading the atmosphere and people were buying flowers and gifts to be left by the temple. People were praying near the temple and it was so peaceful even with so many people (not many Europeans visit here and they are really missing out). There was a procession of people making their way to the temple and a bolt of cloth in bright red was gradually unwound as people took hold of the cloth so the cloth procession just got longer and longer as more people joined it. Just an amazing place to visit and a wonderful day.

title: Definitely worth seeing
text: A fantastic site in a beautiful location. The monument is truly monumental and it is interesting to observe the significance that this site has for sri lankan, who make pilgrimmages to it from all across the country. I cannot recommend enough the guide that took us that day. He had the best english out of all the guides we met and was extremely knowledgeable about the history of the ruins and buddhist philosophy. I also liked that he took the time to share his knowledge without trying to rush you through the tour. He took us on 3 1/2 hour tour through all the highlights of the ancient city at a very reasonable price of 3500 rupees. You can contact him on wasanthamapa1968@gmail.com. Name: Wasantha.

title: Impressive
text: A large white structure still in use as a place of worship so very colourful with lots of locals on the day we visited. A very impressive site. As with most of Anuradhapura, signage was practically non existent with very little in the way of historical description at each monument.

title: old stupa
text: One of many ancient sights to see in Anuradhapura. Follow the crowds to circle the stupa. There are smaller stupas in each corner.

title: Wonderful to see
text: Nice to see a amazing site like this, far from the madding crowds. Try to avoid the midday sun. Barefoot visit so can be harsh on soft western feet !

title: Massive Stupa full of vibrance and spirituality
text: Review from my Blog As soon as we arrived at Ruwanweliseya, the first thing I noticed was the long line of people assisting with the wrapping of the base of the stupa once in a bright orange cloth. The next thing I notices, was the group of people working feverishly infront of the dagoba, braiding tree branches together to provide roofing for the hastily built market that lay in the parking lot at the foot of the structure... As I got closer, I began to truly understand the length of the cloth being wrapped around the structure. Not only did this put it’s size in perspective, but seeing the size of the workers in comparison to this massave structure was truly awesome. I shed my sandals and began to walk around the stupa. The ground was hot, and the rocks on the side facing the sun were like hotplates as you walked.,, Every so often as you walked around the structure you would see small structures showcasing Buddha’s. At many of these you’d see entire families with cloths laid out, sitting for presumably hours and meditating en mass When I finally finished circling I headed to the small shanty market set up infront of the temple and picked up some water.

title: Impressive and Peaceful
text: A massive stupa (largest in the world), it is well worth visiting when you're in Anuradhapura. You can get impressive views from afar with as many photo ops as you want, but to truly experience this stupa you need to take off your shoes and walk around (clockwise) to get a sense of its sacred nature. You'll see a number of Buddhists praying to help you get into the proper spirit and may be fortunate enough to hear local drumming, music, chanting, etc.

title: These ruins world class engineering marvels. Very inspiring and emanates the peace of the Buddha
text: Great place to visit. However make sure you start out the visits EARLY at least by 6 AM ( before the sun gets very hot and dry ) Per tradition you have to leave your footwear at the entrance. By midday when the sun gets hot, so does the ground of the temple, making it extremely uncomfortably hot and blistering on bare feet despite the socks. Take a spare pair of socks. Deck in cotton or loose comfortable clothing. The temple grounds will not allow any revealing clothing, tank tops or shorts. Temperatures by mid day sun reach 85- 95 Fahrenheit.

title: A sacred temple. Dress appropriately
text: We visited the place at around 7 pm and found the place a bit busy but extremely calming and peaceful. Would have loved to site there for more time and absorb the atmosphere. A great place to visit and reflect.

title: quaint and beautiful
text: we were very lucky as the day in which we went to visit, there was a festive celebration and there was a lot going on, culturally. overall the place was beautiful and majestic quaint

title: Awesome stupa
text: It's white, large and magnificent. We went on a weekend where we saw a continuous stream of people bring yarns and yarns of coloured cloth to tie around the Stupa besides lotus flowers and other offerings. There were monks all around to help. It was quite a sight.

title: So Big and Impressive
text: This is a really nice place to visit. Of course, you have to take off your shoes or sandals for respect. Nice place to walk around observe everyone worshipping.

title: A huge structure.
text: Firstly, if you're not used to going barefoot then avoid the middle of the day as the stones can get very hot. That said a walk around this massive structure will give an insight into what it must have taken to build this thing. Also it's well worth a visit after dark as the illuminations are very good.

title: Very impressive dagobah
text: Approximately 107 meters high, shining white and very impressive stupa / Dagobah is located in Anuradhapura in the sacred city. When you enter the area, you need to take off your shoes. The wall around the Dagobah is decorated with 344 elephants reliefs. Walk around the impressive building.

title: Another White Dagoba
text: This was the last place we visited on our tuk tuk tour and based on reviews we had very high expectations. There were a lot of worshipers at the site and the "foreigner shoerack" was a bit of a hassle. It is a very spiritual place. Had hoped for more.

title: Interesting place
text: Top of the list of attractions in the area and quite busy in the mornings. Go early because there is a lot of walking and quite a bit has to be barefoot (as it is within the Buddhist shrine). The stones get quite hot! Wear socks.

title: Not as good as Polonnaruwa
text: We visited various sites in Anuradhapura during our time in Sri Lanka but it was a bit underwhelming. It's an older site than Polonnaruwa and therefore less preserved. There is less to see and it is harder to understand it's historical significance. My advice would be to cover legs and shoulders, to carry a handbook and to make use of a licensed guide, in order to get even a little bit out of the visit. Guides don't cost anything but a minimum tip of Rs. 500-1000 would be recommended as they're extremely knowledgable.

title: Living religious site
text: Nice break from other attractions were you only see ruins and rubble. This place has intensely alive with many Sri Lankan's worshipping and praying. Good place to feel everyday Buddhism among locals.

title: Lovely place - could be better
text: Some of his review you will find repeated for other places in Anuradhapura as I could not write a generic one. Firstly, for sites of relgious signigicance, no footwear, hats or bare legs/shoulders. My tips would be; if in doubt carry a wrap/sarong/shawl and a pair of socks with you as the ground can get uncomfortably hot. Beautiful glaring white building of historical significance. Read up about it before visiting as very little information is written in non Tamil or Singalese.

title: Probably one of the biggest dagaoba
text: Probably one of the biggest Dagoba in Sri Lanka. Note that the floor can get very hot during the day and maybe you should consider keeping your socks while visiting. It is really a pilgrimage place and very interesting to visit. There are also many monkeys in the park around the Dagoba.

title: Impressive
text: What an impressive visit we had here; if you are in Anuradaphura this is an absolute not-to-miss. Be aware that shoes are not allowed and your knees need to be covered

title: Beautiful! Visit at sunset to get both daytime and nighttime photos! Go with a guide if possible
text: TIP: leave your shoes on the bus/your car so you dont need to pay for them to tend to your shoes. - would recommend visiting this place at sunset so you can get nice daytime as well as nighttime photos. it looks impressive any hour of the day - we didnt have a guide so were quite clueless as to the significance of the temple so try to go with one! -an impressive, magnificent sight to behold, could be considered a wonder of the world in my books! - the grounds are EXPANSIVE so dont worry about it being crowded unless it is a festival day in sri lanka, do double check before you go. - the grounds will probably be really hot in the afternoon so just bear in mind you have to walk barefoot and as i said try to visit in the late afternoon during sunset.

title: Marvellous Stupa
text: Its a pilgrim site for Buddhist, i like this stupa very much. Its so majestic and serene. I went to this stupa twice already. In Srilanka its a custom to take off sandals or shoes to enter the temple area or dagoba area. Socks are allowed. resisting and be patience to the hot floor will also be part of heart training. Must go. Do pradaksina ( walk around the dagoda 3 times).

title: Ancient Stupa at Ancient City
text: A very ancient stupa and there were so many people coming to pray. You have to take off your footwears but socks are still allowed. You have to keep them at the counter and pay small donation to the keepers (maybe about LKR50 but it's up to you) It will be extremely hot when you visit in the afternoon, it was suggested to visit in the evening because the lightings would be great. And also there are a lot of wild/un-owned dogs around but they don't bite.

title: The tallest stupa of the ancient city
text: This stupa is one of the tallest monuments in the world. The outside wall is decorated with black elephants throughout the circumference of outer wall. The stupa is considered to be very scared and hence usually this place is crowded.

title: A Magnificent Stupa in Anuradhapura Sri Lanka
text: Built by King Dutugamunu around 200 BC. Another must visit site for anyone visiting Sri Lanka. Buddha's relics are kept here. One of the biggest Buddhist stupa's in the world.

title: The Pagoda of King Dutu Gamunu
text: Tallest pagoda in Sri Lanka and this was made by the Great ruler King Dutugamunu. People in Sri Lanka believe that There is Lord Buddha's relics inside this pagoda. This away from the Colombo area and it's 4-5 hours journey from the Colombo. This is very religious place in Sri Lanka. You should be here when you will be in Sri Lanka

title: Majestic Dagoba (stupa) started in 2nd century BC
text: Enclosed by a wall with a frieze of elephants, this enormous restored Dagoba, 180ft high, testifies to the splendour of Anuradhapura at its peak in the 9th century. It is so big that it is difficult to take a full picture once inside the surrounding walls. We were amazed to see how 7 workers on a very tall bamboo ladder clean and maintain the stupa. It can get very hot in the afternoon as there is absolutely no shade.

title: Impressive Dagoba
text: Completely restored with white painted plaster, this is a memorable sight. Even more impressive are the bamboo ladders that climb to the top that the painters need to climb to work - scary. This is probably the most important and impressive dagoba at this site and should not be missed.

title: Very impressive, but take care when hot
text: This is a very impressive artefact, steeped in religious history, with a real feeling that the locals who throng to this pace really do care. It is quite a feat of engineering and manpower. Apparently, the manpower was essentially voluntary, with the people really involved and cared for - cf the building of the pyramids. A word of warning, the footpath to the main area, from where you have to go shoeless, can get hot for the pale skinned visitors. After noon, it can be VERY hot as the local administration, in its wisdom decided to convert to tiles from sand. Bad move! Well worth a visit.

title: Part of the Ancient City and important pilgrimage temple
text: This stupa is huge.At the time we were there they had the men scrubbing the outside and painting.Not a job I would want.Be prepared to be amongst the throngs of the faithful which is nice.Very hot on your bare feet so maybe bring socks as we were recommended to do but didn’t.Lots to see.

title: Amazing sight
text: A must see, impressive structure and a beautiful view! Unfortunately also a lot of tourists at this place but thats unevitable these years..

title: Amazing
text: The size of this structure to house a treasure is amazing, and it doesn't even have an entry that one can view the treasure. Absolutely amazing.

title: Nothing special
text: We came here and it was just another stupa! Nothing special to make your way here if you don’t have time you can Skip it

title: Place of Pilgrimage
text: Our driver claimed this is the largest stupa in Asia. I'll reserve judgement on that. But it is a place where Buddhist faithful congregate in great numbers. You get a good sense of Sri Lankan Buddhist piety here.

title: Awesome structure
text: Another beautiful Dagoba on this amazing site. Walking distance from the Sri Maha Bodhi Temple. Pictures don't do it justice. Beautiful elephant frieze round the wall base

title: Must go place if you are a Buddhist
text: We go every time when we visit Sri Lanka. Place can get very busy, especially full moon days. A lot of worshipers come here. Get the timing correct. floor is made by granite so it gets very hot during midday. It will take 20-30 minutes to walk around it. Buddha's relics are kept here, Hence this is must go place for Buddhists. Also walking distance to Sri Maha Boodhi, Bo tree.

title: not to skip this good to visit
text: this is largest sthupa in Anuradhapura. built by king of Buddhist time and fond it as sacred place must see Lord buddha engrave

title: NIce
text: There is nothing outstanding.. Just one more stupa, except this one was white so I guess makes for a nice background in a photo

title: Massive stupa
text: Lovely place which gives a sense of what humans can achieve. Massive stupa. Not as crowded as some other places. Enjoyed our time there

title: Amazing and awe inspiring
text: There is really no way to capture the scale and the sense of awe that this Stuppa makes one feel when you are there. There are counters to hold your shoes and it’s great to be able to circumambulate and earn merit.

title: Awe inspiring
text: Visited here in a recent tour with my wife. It was a beautiful sight - the stupa is absolutely huge and with a lot of people visiting on the day, it was incredidbly atmospheric too. Quite unlike anything I have seen before - a must-see if you are visiting the country.

title: Large stupa
text: This is a very large & decorated stupa in Anuradhapura. The outside of the temple is decorated with large elephants. It is still used & busy on a daily basis.

title: 7 day Srilankan trip
text: was a good experience to see these types for the first time. I think its the biggest or the second biggest of Dagoba

title: Neat place to learn about buddhism
text: This was one of my first stops in Sri Lanka. It was neat to see so many people praying and making offerings to Buddha. It really gave me insight into Buddhism. Bring a few rupees to check your shoes if I recall correctly.

title: Massive and Beautiful
text: Absolutely massive white domed stupa, perhaps one of the most impressive structures in Anaradhapura. You can walk around the paved circumference and admire the ornate carvings at the base, the elephant carvings in particular. You have to take off your shoes of course but be sure to keep your socks on as the stones can be burning hot as it is totally exposed to the sun. Shorts need to be below the knees and shoulders need to be covered. Just over 50m high, the original structure was much higher, the highest stupa in the world when first consecrated. Very, very impressive. Go early as it is one of the most crowded sites in Anuradhapura Nd as I mentioned the heat is a factor.

title: Strikingly peaceful
text: On a hot day, with burning hot pavers suggest wearing socks or keep to the white quartz stone where you can find them. You can walk at good pace though. We visited midday, so hot but not many other people around. Very peaceful and calm (if you can stand in one place for more than 30 secs. The Dagoba is beautiful and very sacred. Standing at the side and looking up to the clouds was fun, and made the earth sway.

title: the buddhist destination in sri lanka
text: and seeing all the students enjoy it added t the experience. It can get quite warm and note that shoes and hats are not allowed in the temple vicinity.

title: Move on!
text: The stupas around here are big but lack any sort of atmosphere. There needs to be a lot more work to get these places into something that is interesting. I’m sure it will happen over the next few years. It has lots of potential.

title: Like any other historical place
text: You need to have a local guide to explain you the story and take you through the right monuments during the trip.

title: Sri lanka hols
text: Loved this temple, very beautifully kept with current work happening to maintain. Very spiritual place with many locals praying and chanting. Very enjoyable

title: Amazing Stupa
text: Totally breathtaking. This huge stupa is an incredible testimony to ancient architecture and devotion For me the best thing in the sacred city of Anuradhapura

title: Nice
text: As the stupas at Anuradhapura are all impressive, Abhayagiri Dagaba is no different! Wonderful, a real sight for the eye.

title: Great Stupa
text: This stupa has built by King Walagamba, in order to pay his gratitude towards the Buddhist monks. This area is considered to be carrying the secrets of Theravada Buddhism. This stupa has met-up with several disastrous situations in the past, but with the help of government and the fellow Sri Lankans, the stupa rebuilt in several years back. This Vihara area contains with a museum as well, which hinders the history of Abayagiri Stupa.

title: Best site at Anaradhapura
text: There’s some scaffolding on parts of this dagoba at the moment, so you’ll need to find the best vantage point from which to photograph it. The park as a whole is a sprawling complex with ticket checkpoints all over the place. By far the best way to see it all is on a bicycle. We spent an awesome day riding through some beautiful scenery, with monuments peeking through the foliage. Having done Polunnaruwa earlier in our trip, we found Anaradhapura a little disappointing. If you’re planning your itinerary and are unsure if you need a night or two here, I don’t think you do if you’re taking in the far superior park at Polunnaruwa. It’s all a bit same-same here. The two big dagobas are certainly impressive but the rest of the sites aren’t much to write home about. The “sacred bodhi tree” was a let down. Really just a temple for locals. You see very little of the tree itself. All in all, a lovely day out cycling through rural Sri Lanka, but the day will not be remembered for the monuments.

title: A large stupa
text: This stupa is unusual in not having a white covering. Otherwise its layout and features are much like other stupas. It is very large though

title: Imposing dagoba
text: You can't help be wowed by Abhayagiri dagoba, with its tranquil woodland setting, its history and the huge stupa. But there's more to Abhayagiri Dagoba than its sheer size - there are a few carvings, and moonstones and a few other relics around. A walk around the base of the dagoba is a must to really appreciate its size (wearing socks as the ground is so hot). A must see in Anuradhapure and included in the cultural ticket. A visit by bike is highly recommended.

title: The site I liked the most in Anuradhapura
text: Focal points of the Abhayagiry complex is an ancient stupa, the Abhayagiri Dagaba, which was the original custodian of the Tooth relic in the country (today in Kandy). Also because of its beautiful interiors, this site has been the one I liked the most in Anuradhapura. As many knows, Anuradhapura was the first historical capital of Sri Lanka and today is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (part of the Cultural Triangle), often on the touristic routes. Dating back to 380AD, the archaeological park contains ancient ruins, dagobas and temples, and a museum. You will need to organise transport to explore it as I think there is simply too much distance to cover by foot. We opt for a tuk tuk. Others for a bicycle, that doesn't seem a bad alternative. In my opinion, in general, the whole site is pretty disappointing. As the country has better attractions (i.e.Polonnaruwa), I would visit Anuradhapura only in case you have some spare time (and an extra budget). Unfortunately, not worth it from my point of view. USEFUL INFO Entry ticket to the site: 25,00 USD per person (only cash) Journey time from Sigiriya by tuk tuk: around 1h30mins PRO TIP Since it is a religious site still in use today, please bear in mind that everybody is asked to dress properly (shoulders and knees must be covered, and shoes and hats must be removed). Because of the latter, I highly suggest to carry also a pair of socks into your bag as sometimes the ground can be very warm/hot.

title: Good visit
text: I did all the temples in one day, they’re all very beautiful and worth a visit. Enjoy Anuradhapura! Take respectful clothing, water and sun screen.

title: Ancient Buddhist Stupa
text: This is another Buddhist temple stupa similar to others found in Anuradhapura. It is said that this a British Army Officer discovered this temple during their occupation of Ceylon

title: Magnificent Stupa
text: At Udamaluwa, this enormous Stupa is a sight to see. Our tour visit was on a hot afternoon & as it is a religious site you must remove hat & shoes - beware burnt soles! An absolute must see if in this area. The surrounding elephant head carvings are impressive on their own. We didn’t go inside though

title: Very Impressive
text: My wife and I visited this ancient Stupa during our recent birdwatching tour of Sri Lanka, we had pre booked a guide to show us the Anuradhapura Temples and Stupas, as without one we wouldn’t have gained such an insight in Buddha and his teachings. This Stupa is over 2000 years old and we found it to be by far the most impressive. Unlike many others this is in its original brick form. It was originally covered in white painted plaster but over the years this has been allowed to fall away, there is still a small area with remnants of the original plaster. It was far to hot for us the enter the curtilage of the Stupa so we just enjoyed it from the the shade of some nearby trees. This was a really impressive building which we’d have liked to have viewed close up, maybe next time. Highly Recommended

title: One of the tallest brick structures of the world
text: Abhayagiri Dagaba has been built well over 2000 years ago by a king who is known for restoring the "Therawada Buddhism" which is considered as the more conservative type of Buddhism that follows the original teachings of the "Lord Buddha". This is a very large compound and this tall "Stupa" has been restored while retaining its remained shape and hence does not look like a perfect dome. This allows the visitor to see some of the ancient special lime based plasters used to give a pleasing finish covering the brickwork. The present appearance is purely based on bricks since no attempt has been made to restore it to the original shape in order to allow the visitors to see what was there before the restoration began about 15 years ago.

title: Beware hot feet!
text: I'm sorry to distract from the beauty of this stupa and point out the practicalities but the Anuradhapura site is enormous and for all the temples shoes must be removed. When you're walking on the equivalent of hot coles you tend to miss out on the experience... perhaps wear trainer socks and then you can enjoy it more!

title: Another ancient stupa
text: Made of bricks and, unlike Ruwanvelisaya not painted white, the stupa is quite impressive. Ruins of ancient dwellings where the monks lived can be seen in the vicinity.

title: Vacation
text: Second largest Stupa in the area and made of brick construction and color. No shoes allowed and very hot so wear socks. I prefer this opposed to the white stucco one. Very old and impressive.

title: Big stupa
text: This is one of the main attractions of the Anuradhapura heritage site, the other being the Jetawana Dagaba, and , to be fair, it’s a fairly dramatic piece of construction and, in its day, was apparently the next biggest building on the world after the pyramids of Giza. Other than the scale of the structure there’s not a lot to it and, to be honest, we found the whole of the archaeological site to be something of a disappointment. It certainly doesn’t rank alongside the likes of Sukhothai or Ayutthaya in Thailand yet at $25 entry fee the price is well above these locations. The park is basically a collection of stupas supplemented by ruins of other buildings that are little more than stone outlines on the ground. Nice area to cycle around but largely over rated and overpriced.

title: Must see Dagoba
text: This is "the must see" Dagoba in Anuradhapura's sacred city. This impressive buddhist temple is entirely made out of bricks. Once 100 meters high it was the second highes building in the ancient world. Only the Pyramids of Gizeh where higher. Nowadays, it's "only" 75 meters but still stunning. Please behave respectfully as well as dress appropriately, cover your shoulders and knees. No shoes allowed.
