title: Don't just visit the stupa, wander about the nearby ruins too
text: The Abhayagiri Dagoba is a huge brick stupa built slightly over 2,000 years ago, and for centuries after that, served as the focal point of an expansive monastery complex, stretching for hectares around. Other than sheer size, the stupa itself isn’t much to see -- though you should spend some time contemplating its age and the feat of construction it represented for its time -- but the parkland around is chockful of ruined foundations of all sorts of buildings. The stupa/dagoba was the focal centre of a major monastic complex, said to once have housed and served 5,000 monks. Today, it’s a shady area with mature trees, with hardly anyone else around, so it’s a pleasant stroll wandering around the ruins. As bonus, I saw three wild peacocks strutting around the site too. Not so pleasant were inquisitive monkeys and wild dogs. Also, sun block cream and insect repellent would be handy. Among the ruins to the east, a short walk away leads you to a lovely piece of sculpture called the Samadhi Buddha. More ruins can be found to the west of the stupa; these ruins (“Ratnaprasada”) once housed the more ascetic monks. To the northwest of the stupa is the most elaborately-carved “moonstone” in Anuradhapura -- a “moonstone” is a stone slab placed before a set of steps. It’s interesting to try to imagine the hustle and bustle that once characterised this site, with monks chanting prayers, debating sacred texts, and lay people presenting donations. No doubt it was also a location for political intrigue since organised religion was closely intertwined with government in those times. I also wondered what sort of economy could support such a large number of monks. But today, it’s a tranquil, relaxing parkland. About 300 – 400m south of Abhayagiri Dagoba is the Abhayagiri Museum. See my review of it under that name. The stupa, museum and ruins around are all within the paid area of Anuradhapura's “Sacred City/Ancient Ruins” archaeological park. However, tickets to the Archaeological park can only be purchased from the Archaeological Museum (not to be confused with the Abhayagiri Museum) located about 2 km south (ridiculous!) of the Abhayagiri Dagoba. Cost = US$25, or 3,780 Sri Lankan rupees and valid only for the same day. General info about places in the “Sacred City/Ancient Ruins” park: The sights are quite spread out such that while walking from one sight to the second may be possible, covering many more on foot is impractical. You’ll need a map and a bicycle or tuktuk hired for the day. Also, there few toilets, and few places to buy water, though there is at least one rustic shop near the Abhayagiri Dagoba that has cold drinking water for sale.

title: It's A Landmark Thing And As A Tourist ...
text: When you set aside religion and look at these ancient sights as landmarks to this area and to the country. As a tourist they are worth a visit as much as you would visit the Eiffel Tower in Paris and the Statue of Liberty in New York etc, etc. There is something to get from visiting them. Something to feel and understand. It is the feeling of the heat of the paved slabs or rock steps under your feet and an appreciation and understanding forming of what worship is like for these people here. It is the physical exertion on your body to reach the highest point. It is the tranquility of the landscape that these sights are built around. It is the bewilderment of the age of the relics and the size in which some have been made. It is the sights of monkeys behaving like this is their home. It is the noise of traditional music as an organ may be playing if you were to visit a Cathedral. It is the gentle murmurs of worship coming from peoples prayers. It is the shade of the tree whether it be regarded as holy or not. It is the smell of incense and the sight of flowers given as a gift. It is the welcoming smiles of the Sri Lankan people who are happy to include you here regardless of your religion. It is something you do and recommend you do when you are visiting another country.

title: Expectations
text: Whether the LKR3.5K/foreigner fee (half price for under-13s) for access to Anuradhapura’s ruins is “worth it” depends on your expectations. Angkor Wat it’s not; but it’s cool. If you want to see it, pay it (and if you don’t, don’t). (Sure, you can sneak around and see most stuff without having paid. But do you think of yourself as a cheater? If not, why cheat?) NB at least as of the date of this review, the Archeology Museum is “closed for renovations.” That sucks. But, expectations. The guards didn’t seem to like us climbing up the base rings of the Abhayagiri Dagoba (stupa). That sucks. But, expectations. The Sanctuary at Tissawewa, which we’d pegged to be high-class, was a disappointment. No ice! No Diet Coke! “No, we don’t have that dish, or that one either.” The “New Zealand beef” in the salad was practically inedible. Expectations. The contemporary-Buddhism-related sites (temples, the tree) require legs be covered down to below the knee. Dress appropriately, or buy and carry a sarong to put over your shorts (or borrow one from your guesthouse host). Par contre, the “wear white” signs didn’t seem enforced at all. The tree, although it certainly didn’t look 2,300 years old (and probably is a descendant of the original tree, not actually it), felt like the most genuine piece of Anuradhapura. The bikes our guesthouse gave us, like all the other bikes we saw tourists on, were complete crap, which measurably decreased the pleasure of cycling around. On our way out of town we noticed a sign for Indika Bikes, at the Tourist Information Center Restaurant between the Dutugemunu Roundabout and The Lakeside at Nuwarawewa (across from the tyre place) looked like it was offering nicer bikes.

title: Magnificent Ancient Vihara
text: ABHAYAGIRI TEMPLE Abhayagiri Vihara (temple) in Anuradhapura is one of the most sacred places and oldest temples of Theravada Buddhism. It is one of eight most venerated places (Atamasthana) and one of the five highest/tallest Viharas in Anuradhapura. Abhayagiri monastery was founded by King Vatttagamani Abhaya (also called Valagambahu) (89-77 BC) in 88 BC.as a religious school. Originally its height was more than 330 feet and it was built on the ruins of a Jain hermitage, destroyed by Abhaya. Within next 200 years it became a great international institution for Buddhist learning alongwith its rival orthodox monasteries of Mahavihara and Jetavana which professed Mahayana Buddhism. Abhayagiri means ‘Hill of Protection’ or ‘Fearless Hill’. Reportedly a statue of a bull made of pure gold, containing relics of the Buddha was buried in the core of the stupa. Reportedly the dagoba was built over a footprint of the Buddha with a circumference of 1300 feet (400 meters).

title: Exquiste moonstone and guardstone - best in the area
text: Let me first preface by saying Anuradhapura is a long distance to travel from the main coastal resorts and so you should probably only consider if you are touring the island. It was about a two hour drive from Sigiriya. The area is too big to cover on foot in a single day and, whilst bicycles and TukTuks are easy and cheap to hire, I would recommend a driver/guide who can direct you to and provide commentary on the most significant sites. Abhayaagiri was a complex of monastic buildings founded in the first or second century BC. It is still being uncovered and restored. The stupa is huge (230fit high and very similar to Jethavanarama) but as it still under renovation there is lots of scaffolding. The grounds are the main attraction. The Twin Bathing Pools (Kottum Putan) are very tranquil and worth a 5-10 minute stop as it’s a great example of the amazing engineering and water management that was typical across ancient Sri Lanka. Here solid stone was carved out to create two large pools used by thousands of monks for bathing. Elsewhere across the island earth was excavated on an even larger scale to create huge water tanks which were used for feeding crops as well as bathing. If you are in the area I would recommend that you also visit the ruins of King Mahasen’s Palace to see an exquisite example of a moonstone doorstep with finely detailed symbolic carvings; the Ratnaprasada (Gem Place) for the guardstone; and the Mahapali Refectory with its huge rice trough and bathing pools.

title: A place to reflect yourself
text: The simplicity of this sculpture brings you back to the basics of life. When you observe the buddhist pilgrims, yu become quit and respectful.

title: Ancient statue
text: This is one of the minor sites ogf the ancient city of Anuradhapura. If you cycle around, this is very near the Moonstone and other of the sites. It's a place of worship, so your knees should be covered, and shoes must be taken off.

title: Divine Masterpiece
text: Next to Twin bath we visited this place . Large forested area with many buildings ruins where lot of granite pillars standing. There is a guard there to tell us to remove shoes to go near samadhi statue. Peaceful place to visit

title: The Samadhi Statue worth a visit
text: Like most of the sites, the statue is located in an enormous area full of smaller and bigger sites, all of which has it ́s own history. The Samadhi statue is thought to be constructed in the 3rd or 4th century. Found on (in?) the ground in the late 1800s, it is a well preserved statue in marble with a broken nose. The statue itself is surrounded by several old ruins, many of which still remains to be uncovered

title: You need to find the secret of this statue in order to appreciate it
text: Maybe you think this is just one more Buddha statue. Our driver told us to take two pictures from either side and compare. If you do this you will find out about one of the specifics of this statue - apart from the fact that it belonged to one of the largest complexes in Anuradhapura.

title: A must visit.
text: This buddah is an early example of Sinhalese carving and is very famous amongst the local people. Here is buddah is sitting in a meditation position- a classic pose. The buddah is in good condition despite being carved out of limestone, and now is sitting under a concrete roof. It was thought to be one of four statues but all that remains of the are a set of legs!

title: Lovely Buddha Statue
text: It is said in many guidebooks that this is the most sublime statue of Buddha in Sri Lanka. Well, I wouldn't go that far, but it is a lovely statue nonetheless. Worth a stop, especially if you enjoy ancient Buddhist art.

title: Impressive sculture
text: This is an impressive and well done sculpture of budha in his lotus position. Well worth a visit together with the other items in its vicinity

title: Inspiring Expression of Meditation
text: This is one of the best-loved expressions of the Buddha meditating in Sri Lanka. Dating from the 4th century CE, it is a timeless evocation of world transcendence.

title: A Grand exquisite Buddha Statue
text: The Samadhi posture statue of Buddha is considered to be the finest one in Srilanka. It is of 3rd/4th century period. The 7 feet statue has stood the test of time and is a holy place. The statue presents three different views when seen through over three directions. It is situated in the middle of Mahamevnawa Park in Anuradhapura,This meditate pose of Lord Buddha is called Dhyana Mudra, sitting cross legged and upturned palms placed one over the other on the lap. It is said that the eyes of Buddha are unique in that no where in the world such an arrangements could be seen. A relatively calm atmosphere when I visited this place on 27.9/2017 in the evening.A serene experience indeed.

title: Average
text: As part of the entrance fee , I hoped for more than an average Buddhist statue . It may well look happy and sad from different angles but it appeared just another Buddhist statue to me and I wondered what all the hype is about .

title: Amazing
text: Samadhi Buddha statue is another amazing creation of the ancient Sri Lankan artists. Samadhi Statue is a must see place in the Anuradhapura trip

title: Not worth the money
text: Governments main job is to rip the tourist off and even the officials behave this way, arrogant and not customer oriented at all. It is all about money here. The price for tourist RP 3500 compared to almost nothing paid by locals. You have to pay that to be able to access the entire area. Not worth the money. "My generous donation will help you preserve the heritage" (as stated on the ticket) however should the locals be also interested to take a part? After you pay the entrance fee almost nothing is in English. You have to open google to get at least some information. Also you would expect at least basic English knowledge of the staff if you charge this entrance fee. We had a disagreement with the staff I took as 15 mins to find someone who can speak basic English. Or at least clean up at the historical sites from all the garbage. I can't really see here that the money is actually going in the heritage. Didn't buy it. Also to be honest there is not that much you can see for the money here unless you are really a big history fan or Buddhist.

title: Serene place (part of the entrance fee)
text: This is a religious place, so shoes off, legs and shoulders covered. Locals make offerings here, so it is a place to respect. The statue is interesting as is the thought there used to be four of them, the second is only partially there. Worth a visit as part of the Anuradhapura visit.

title: A serene statue of Buddha
text: Buddha in Sri Lanka more or less you always see in the reclining position while this statue is the sitting position in dhayana mudra. A very beautiful statue.

title: Famous Buddha Statue...Don't miss it!
text: It is made out of dolomite marble and stands 7 feet 3 inches (2.21 meters) in height and it is considered one of the best sculptures in the Anuradhapura era.If you are going to Anuradhapura don't miss this.Also go there when it is morning or evening.Coz you can sit there for a while meditating.The experience is tremendous. It is thought to be done during the 3rd or the 4th century and it was found in the present location in 1886 fallen to the ground with damages to the nose.

title: Very nice statue
text: Nice statue in a tranquil spot - under some trees. You have to walk through the souvenir market to get to it

title: Yes. It's nice
text: In SL you can think. Another Buddha statue. Another temple. Does this one stand out. No. Was it worth seeing. I guess.

title: So serene
text: Beautiful statue - so serene and what a marvellous unspoilt setting - not many tourist around so peaceful and quiet

title: Nothing extraordinary
text: You can visit their for some photos but remember not to turn your back towards the statue. One of the many buddha statue you will see in sri lanka.

title: Impressive!
text: Shoes and hats off! Don't turn your back on the Buddha! The crowds, their devotion and dedication and offerings make this a worthwhile place to visit!

title: Just another buddha
text: Just another buddha ... Its nothing soooo special, made by stone. The locals love this place, so it gets crowdy compared to other places

title: A old statue with a history
text: This statue is not very incredible in itself, but it has a history which is worth noting. An English general would one day during the occupation start shooting at the statue, you can see three patches on the statue where he hit. When the general was shooting suddenly a Tusker (Elephant with tusks) came out of the forest and killed him on the spot. For the Buddhist this shows that the place is utterly sacred.

title: Nice statue but nothing compared to others in Sri Lanka
text: Nice statue, but you will see much more beautiful statues around sri Lanka. Anuradhapura it self is nice, but all the sights are so scattered that you never have the idea that you are visiting an ancient city. The local people are also living in between the ancient stupas and other sights. You can't blame them but it is a pity of the total experience. We liked other big sights as Sigiriya and Polonnaruwa more mainly because of this.

title: Popular with local pilgrims
text: A holy place in the area of Abhayagiri Dagoba, very popular with local pilgrims. A marble statue of a seated Buddha with a particular thing: if you look at it from three sides (in front, from right and from left) you will notice three different expressions of the face! Remove your shoes before approaching the statue.

title: no hats/shoes
text: and no pictures with your back to the statue! Fun snacks and lemonade in the walkway outside leading to the carpark.

title: Remember to look at the statue in Three directions
text: This statue tells us the story of meditation. When you look at the face of this statue from the left side you will see a sad face, and straight look will show you meditation pause, and then the right view will have smile on the face, therefore Remember to look at the statue in Three directions. This is one of the greatest creations of Sri Lankan history.

title: Go on a Friday to experience meditation in the park
text: Beautiful Buddha statue in a lovely park. Best advice: wear inexpensive flip flops that you can take off easily because you must walk barefoot at these holy places. Don't wear sneakers because 1)they are difficult to take off easily and 2)when it rains, they will be soaked and uncomfortable. Also, don't wear expensive sandals because of the rain/mud. The locals just wear inexpensive sandals and flip flops.

title: Peaceful, spiritual area
text: Enjoyed walking to the statue, lots of lovely trees and bird life. Lots of locals meeting and sitting in groups learning how to meditate from the monks. A beautiful scene visually, the white dress of the devotees and the orange robes of the monks seated amongst the trees. Very peaceful setting.

title: Really nice place
text: Really enjoyed spending time in Anuradhapura. Samadhie Statue is a must see. Really peaceful place where the locals come.

title: Wonderful Unesco world herritage park
text: The old city is a must to visit when you are in Sri Lanka! 7 stupa's and a convent ruin where 3500 monks lived is incredible to imagine!

title: Majestic
text: Lord Buddha with historical background is clearly depicted at this place and is quite relaxing and divine location

title: Oldest Buddha statue of Sri Lanka
text: This is the first one of the places you should visit in Anuradhapura. If you are a non Buddhist but love to explore archeological sites this would be another land mark for you. This is a Buddha statue located in the Abhayagiri Stupa complex. This is a statue of Gautama Buddha in meditation posture or Dhyana Mudra made out of out of dolomite marble and stands 7 feet 3 inches (2.21 metres) in height and width. This belongs to the old Abhayagiri chapter teaching monastery which was built in the 89-77 BC. Old records of Faxian Buddhist monk from china mentioned that this Agayagiri monastary was a huge university at that age with four faculties. This is belongs to one of those faculty. Some of the historical archives give evidence that the king bought a Buddha statue from “Maha Vihara – great monastery located around the “Sri maha Bodhi” temple. So some archeologists clams that this is that statue. The first prime minister of India Javahallal Neru once visited this Buddha statue and said this place gives him inner peace. And he kept a photo graph of this statue also in his residence.

title: Tranquility unsurpassed in a statue. A must for Anuradhapura visit
text: This Buddha statue said to be made of stone is just over 7 feet tall and sits on a square base.. The Buddha is said to be depicted in a state of "Samadhi" which is difficult to translate directly -as a state of intense concentration and deep awareness is fitting. It dates to 2 or 3 AD. When you gaze at the statue, a feeling of calmness and peace overcomes you. The expression on his face is overpowering. The statue is now protected by a concrete hood which does take away some of the attraction of this most famous meditation statue of the World. The expression as seen by the observer is said to change depending on the angle from it is viewed. It is situated in a beautiful park and the whole atmosphere is one of serenity. It is not too far from the main Dagobas and is well worth a visit. If you go all the way to Anuradhapura to witness the ruins of an ancient and advanced civilisation, you will feel very bad if you miss this amazing statue.

title: For the religious only
text: This statue is for the religious only who believe in it's significance. For everyone else it's just a fairly worn statue. It's kind of out of the way and I came along because I was seeing Abhayagiri Dagoba anyway. Otherwise, give it a miss.

title: two Buddha statues in the Dhyana Mudra
text: Mahamevn?wa Park (in the Northern part): you walk by the park and you feel peace and dignity of the place, then you conturn the both granite statues, on the left - a tree with big fruit like a cannonball tree - Couroupita guianensis. Buddhist scriptures tell the Maya Devi have given birth to Buddha under the shade of a Sala Tree and passed away between two of these trees. Buddha is shown with scented flower petals on his deathbed.

title: An attractive and important statue
text: This is an attractive and important statue, especially for the Sinhalese who praise it highly. The statue is partly restored (the nose) and personally I preferred the samadhi sculpture (and the other statues) at Gal Vihara.

title: Ok it is old, but seriously!
text: Yeah it is an old Buddha, but it is very small and had us wondering if we were in the right place. As it is near some other sights you might as well take a look but not worth the journey to see it alone.

title: If touring Anuradpura then a must
text: To some another Buddha, to us it was one of the first Buddhas we saw in Anuradapura and it was where our guide began to explain to us the various poses of the Buddha. It does feel spiritual at this site and I am glad we visited it. It was where we learnt not to have our backsides to Buddha when being photographed (as our guide eloquently put it)

title: Another stature.
text: As a non Buddhist, I didn't find this sandstone statue exceptional. Maybe it's a case of too much within the site. If you are passing through, it's worth a look but not a special effort.

title: Impressive
text: This huge Buddha is a very impressive statue, what a beautiful work. Maybe it's good to see this one before visiting the huge granite statues in Polonnaruwu (Gal Vihara) which are more impressive. But the setting here is beautiful, I visited in the evening, there were no other tourists around, all very peaceful.

title: The most beautiful Buddha stature I have seen
text: Located in Mahamewna park, a very pleasing park with lots of tall trees and comforting breeze from nearby tanks, Samadhi Pratima (meaning statue in English) speaks of ancient aesthetic and architectural skills of Sinhalese people of 3rd BC. From left it gives a feeling of slight sympathy and from right a feeling of happiness. This is a must see site if you love art.

title: Just an average statue
text: This is just the statue of Buddha in the so called 'Samadhi' position. There are lot of such Samadhi statues in Sri Lanka. Really makes me think how this is different in an way. You'll have to leave your slippers outside and walk on the pathway for quite some distance. The pathway is not that well maintained and can hurt your leg.

title: Take the time to have a look at this one
text: The slightly different expressions when looking from one side or the other of the face are intriguing. I didn't pay to much attention to it when I was there, but, as the other reviews say, this is indeed one of the most peaceful buddha statues we have seen in Sri Lanka.

title: Historical value larger than artistic
text: One should not judge holy statues by their artistics value. In this case these ar not totally on par. And it would be much better and more peacefull not to have to run the gauntlet of shops that reach up to 20 meters from the statue.

title: One of many memorable statues of the Buddha
text: This is a must see A beautiful rendition of the Buddha in Samadhi. As a tourist and not a Buddhist it was still a powerful experience to just stand and contemplate the Buddhas life and the life of his devotees who carved this so many centuries ago for us still to be enjoying. The full Moon festival of Poya meant that there was many Devotees of today visiting this Holy Statue and it was a delight for us to see even small children bringing their offerings. A must see

title: I can still see the face
text: I can still see the face on this remarkable representation of the Buddha. He is obviously in deep meditation. If you look from one side he appears to be happy and from the other, he appears to be sad. From the front, he appears to be deeply at peace. A memory to savour.

title: Serene Buddha
text: This large Buddha is carved from limestone and dates from the 4th century AD. Unfortunately the artistry of the figure is compromised by a rather ugly concrete shelter under which it sits.

title: Nice, but nothing special
text: We visited this place while roaming around the stupas of Anuradhapura. It is a nice statue, but is also something you can give a miss if you are short on time.

title: Just a Buddha Statue
text: A significant Buddha statue, highly praised by the locals, although with little interest to the non-religious traveller.

title: Protected Buddha
text: Stopped at the edge of a small village and had to walk past a myriad of shops, many tourist until at the far end an isolated statue of a Buddha, covered with 4 posts holding up roof and protecting the Buddha from the elements. Man asking us to remove shoes as we approached. However ground very mucky and rough even for socks and we observed quite clearly some 30 metres away.

title: One of the best sculptures in the world
text: Must visit place in Sri Lanka. One of the amazing sculptures in the world. Situated in Ancient city of Anuradhapura.

title: beautiful Buddha statue
text: The Buddha statue has a nice stone canopy over it ,is surrounded by lovely trees and part of the Anuradhapura old capital

title: Decent
text: A decent place to go. Nothing really great. Can skip this place if there is scarcity of time. We stopped by for some pics.

title: Just Can't Help to Have Peace when You See this Buddha
text: Located in a nice park, this Buddha is beautiful. There are plants and trees around which adds to the tranquility one might feel when visiting this place. My tour guide told me to take off my shoes as we approach the Buddha.

title: Located in a Quiet Park
text: Nice gardens and inside a perimeter wall. The statue itself is beautiful but for me it was just another buddha statue.

title: Seated Buddha statue
text: This seated Buddha statue is reportedly one of the best sculptures of the Anuradhapura era, and as one of the sacred places at Anuradhapura is a place of devotion. However for non buddhists there is not too much to appreciate.

title: Must visit
text: A very nice construction. And lovely environment surrounded by many ancient ruins. This and Abayagiriya stupa both can be visited together. Very sheltered place with many trees. A bycicle ride will be ideal. There is parking for larger vehicles. Not very suitable to go after 5.00 p.m

title: Spiritually elevating.
text: This is the finest and spiritually elevating image of Buddha in entire Sri Lanka. From 4th Century AD, the beautiful posture reflect compassion and benign Grace of Buddha in perfection.A must place to visit in Anuradhapura.

title: Beautiful serene statue
text: Well worth a visit while you are in anuradhapura. Remember you can take photos but not with your back facing the statue

title: Marvelous Buddha Statue
text: SAMADHI BUDDHA Samadhi Buddha is a statue of Mahatma Buddha in Mahameghawana (also called Mahamevnawa) Park in the midst of ancient city of Anuradhapura, near Abhayagiri Monastery. This statue shows Buddha in the posture of Dhiyan Mudra. This 7 feet high statue with Buddha face showing three different moods (plain, sad, smiling) from 3 different sides, is considered one of the best sculpture in ancient history of Sri Lanka, supposed to be carved from dolomite marble in 4th to 6th century AD. It was found at the present place in 1886, fallen on the ground with damaged nose. It was then repaired and erected.

title: Statue of Lord Buddha
text: Its near by the twin baths only and a statue of Lord Buddha in Samadhi.. No Photograpghy allowed... You can just see

title: Buddha’s Enlightenment
text: Samadhi refers to Buddha’s enlightenment which is depicted by the statue with the sitting position of meditation. The statue is located in the Mahamevnawa Park in between the Twin Ponds and Thuparamaya Temple. It is inclusive in the entrance fee for Anuradhapura Ancient Site at USD25 or LKR4,550. Hiring a driver is necessary since various sites are far from each other. Appropriate dressing required and no shoes are allowed. There are locals here for the worshiping. Good representation of the heritage of Buddhism culture since Anuradhapura Kingdom in 3rd century.

title: ONE OF THE MORE STRIKING REPRESENTATIONS OF THE BUDDHA
text: At any Buddhist site you are going to see many depictions of the Buddha. Perhaps it was the colour [ivory with hints of greenish yellow] that caught my eye. It is the meditation pose. It is just eight feet tall. It dates from around the 4th c A.D. It is made out of dolomite marble. Its setting with trees behind it adds to its grandeur.

title: Nice
text: Rich in history, the reading at the site helps your mind invoke images of the past....lots of worshippers around as well..

title: Unimpressive Statue
text: You can go there while touring Anuradhapura, but that diminutive statue has strictly nothing to rave about

title: A nice buddha
text: This is a very well preserved buddha statue. You can clearly see all the details still, even so far as a strap line on the shoulder. It was in the middle of the woods which made the whole setting even better for me personally. It is worth having a look at.

title: Very busy
text: This buddha statue is large. It is thought to date from 4th century AD. However old it is, it is an impressive piece of stonework. Very busy so choose the time of your visit

title: Worth a visit if around Abhayagiri Dagoba but doesn't necessarily warrant a dedicated trip
text: This statue of seated Buddha is within the Abhayagiri Dagoba complex and is included within the $30 Anuradhapura cultural ticket and you get your token for the statue ripped off when you enter the complex. Its a short and easy cycle ride from the main pagaoda and you can park your bike up at the main car park, from where you walk by a large number of market stalls before reaching the statue. The statue itself is relatively small and there is a rope on the floor where your ticket is inspected again and you may enter (without shoes) for a closer look. You can also see quite well from outside the area too. The statue attracts tourists and worshipers alike which is good to see. A visit doesn't take long and I'm glad we didn't make a specific trip as it doesn't quite warrant one if you are short of time in Anuradhapura.

title: Beautiful statue of Bodhisattva or Buddha sitting in Siddhasana near Abhayagiri Stupa !
text: The statue resembles the meditating Buddha sitting in Siddhasana and palms turned up, right palm almost on top of left palm!. Samadhi statue which is 8 feet tall is made of granite entirely and is a wonder to followers and worshipers. The statue also symbolizes Dhayana Mudra. The posture of meditation of this Statue is a popular for learning of meditation. It was done during the 3rd or the 4th century. It is made out of dolomite marble and stands 7 feet 3 inches in height ! There is another statue similar close by but it's right arm is broken !

title: Vacation
text: Very nice statue of Buddha in a sitting position. Holy place so no shoes. Set inside a huge complex that dates back over two thousand years.

title: Routine artefact
text: Well, it’s a certainly a statue of buddha and he’s certainly sitting down so I guess it does what it says on the tin.

title: Buddha statue
text: This is another Buddha statue. Take off your shoes before you get close. I was expecting something more spectacular but it was not coloured, or as big as I expected.

title: The statue may not be impressive, but the surroundings make a visit worth it
text: From my Blog: I approached the statue, and to be honest was not as impressed as I thought I’d be. The realist in me saw it as a basic statue, while the traveller in me scolded myself for judging this as merely a place to visit while dismissing the spiritual power this site holds for so many. As I walked off, in the corner of my eye I saw two boys who could not be more than 9 years old playing cricket between two small temple ruins. I took a moment to let where I was hit me. How many times in your life do you have the privilege of being allowed into another religions sacred grounds? How often in your life do you see children playing amongst ruins built thousands of years ago?

title: Samadhi Status ( samadi budu pilimaya) - anuradhapura Sri Lanka.
text: The Samadhi ( means in deep meditation) Status which belongs to the 4th - 3rd century BC is the work of an anonymous master - sculptor of the Anuradhapura period who has breathed life into a solid rock. Here, the Buddha is depicted in the Dhyana Mudra, The posture of meditation. This unique piecs of sculpture, was fallen to the ground when re-discovered in 1886. It is 7 feet 3 inches in height and is a depiction of the spiritual purity and serenity of Load Buddha.

title: Considered a masterpiece of sculpture
text: This Buddha statue is considered a masterpiece of sculpture. Don't miss going to the nearby sacred Sri Maha Bodhi tree as well.

title: Along Pilgrimage Route
text: Although tourists may not be especially impressed with yet another Lord Buddha statue, this site is important for locals and worth visiting as you explore various pilgrimage spots in Sri Lanka. So it's not to be overlooked. You can research later to discover additional layers of meaning for this site.

title: Not impressed
text: It is a Buddha. It isn’t the biggest, thought it is supposed to be the most exquisite in Sri Lanka. I didn’t think so, but it’s worth a visit if you are in the neighbourhood

title: BUDDHIST
text: This is another beautiful temple area to visit.The Buddha statue in the middle. The surrounding area has shady trees .

title: Serene Samadhi statue
text: Walked through the market stalls (selling mostly tat) to get to this attraction, what a shame. The statue site is well kept and there is a peaceful serene feeling when you are there.

title: Peaceful
text: After visiting the buzzing sites of the big dagobas and stupas all day, you may appreciate the peaceful setting of this sacred site. Embedded in a beautiful park, this site invites you to take a breath and mediate while enjoying its beauty. A very good place for a short break in your pilgrim day.

title: Serene!
text: It was beautiful to visit this site. I reached there and saw a man raking the lotus flowers kept as offerings on the table in front. It was lovely to experience the space as such and walk around it. The statue is beautiful!!

title: Peace after monsoon rain
text: I visited here late afternoon after a monsoon downpour . Quiet and utterly peaceful. Take a while and be in the moment with this elegant understated ancient representation of the Buddha.

title: Historical Statue
text: Like everything in this historical area of Sri Lanka this statue is well worth a visit. The culture in this area does not dissapoint

title: It's a statue
text: It's a Buddha statue like many others, but it's old. Since it's near Abhayagiri, you might as well stop to see it on the way. But it's not worth going out of the way to see. A plus is that there are food and drink stalls nearby.

title: A serene and beautiful Buddha
text: This Buddha is beautiful - not as large as the Gal Vihara Buddhas at Polonnaruwa, but perfect and peaceful. You can buy flowers on the way to leave as an offering. This is an active place of worship with many more Sri Lankans than tourists - take shoes and hat off The atmosphere is tranquil and spiritual.

title: Tranquility
text: Samadhi Statue is a must stop for all visitors to Anuradhapura. The tranquility in the surroundings is miraculous!

title: Budha Statue
text: As such this may seem like another Budha Statue in Samadhi state. Probably the Statue at Gal Vihara in Polonnaruwa is more impressive. This place originally had 4 Budha statues facing each direction, with a tree in the middle. Right now only one statue is left out. Though our guide mentioned that Budha looks sad when seen from one side and happy when seen from the other, I was not able to really identify that. Place is considered sacred and hence you need to remove the footwear. Since there are a lot of trees, no need to worry about the hot floor. No Separate tickets.

title: More than meets the eye
text: This is a stunning statue to see up close. As you walk around it, you can see that the expression on Lord Buddha's face changes. Its fascinating and speaks to the great craftsmanship that went into building this statue. Folks come and set flowers before the statue, so its a calm and serene place. Definitely recommend stopping by if you are in the area.

title: Utterly stunning craftsmanship
text: This statue of Lord Buddha is made in a way that it depicts different emotions of life, when looked from different angles. Just looking at the statue brings in calmness and serenity into your soul. It also is situated in a very calm surrounding.

title: One of Four
text: This statue was original one of four that faced in each direction. Though this one and the base of the one opposite it are all that remains. It is in a very serene setting and made me feel very humble. You do have to remove your shoes to walk up the dirt path to it and to walk around the general area. The neatest thing is that from one side it is frowning and from the other smiling. Please be respectful when you visit.

title: Buddha in characteristic posture
text: This statue is of the Buddha depicted in the position of Dhyana Mudra, the posture of meditation associated with Nirvana. It is a very attractive and culturally important statue carved from granite. Standing around 8 feet in height it is nowhere near as vast as many other similar statues found in the cultural triangle of Sri Lanka but has an elegance and charm that is worthy of a visit. It is located in Mahamevnawa Park in Anuradhapura which in itself is a place of peace and tranquillity.

title: Huge and magnificent
text: This temple is magnificent, dramatic and huge. It is much bigger than any other temple that we saw on Sri Lanka. Well worth a visit for the pure drama.

title: Serene
text: We visited this sacred hindu temple in March 2019. It's a beautiful temple with a calm atmosphere.If you visit north of Sri Lanka, you must visit this temple.

title: A most holy and beautiful temple
text: A very beautifully decorated Temple, and a most holy Hindu one in Sri Lanka. Men must take of Shirts. A must see while your in Jaffna

title: Wonderful temple which is open to visitors
text: Jaffna Nallur Kovil - a sacred Hindu temple - has beautiful, bright paintings and statues. While we were there a ceremony/service took place accompanied by drumming, a shehnai (wind instrument) and lit oil lamps. It was a special experience.

title: Very Moving experience
text: We visited this temple on our one day in Jaffna and would definitely recommend it as a must do for anyone visiting the north of SriLanka. We arrived as a Puja was about to commence and were lucky to take part in the ceremony. The devotion of the people attending was remarkable. A very hot day so a visit to the fresh juice shop opposite the temple entrance was most welcome afterwards. Definitely worth a visit also. Delicious banana lassi

title: Magnificent
text: Really nice experience. Beatifull building. Experiencing a puja is also wonderful. No photography inside allowed and man should be shirtless

title: Amazing
text: A beautiful building - no photos allowed inside. As there was a ceremony underway, all men had to remove their shirts.

title: Interesting stop on walking tour of city
text: We walked to fort and later in day along to nallur kovil which was stunning to view and well worth seeing

title: Iconic temple
text: An hindu temple, which is one of the largest I have visited. Apart from the size there is nothing much to see inside.

title: Ornate temple
text: Large temple with a number of ornate gopuram gatehouse towers. Located a little way out of the centre so a tuk-tuk is needed if you’re not staying locally.

title: One of the most impressive hindu temples in Sri Lanka
text: The Nallur Kovli is the most impressive building in Jaffna. Decorated with little statues, this breathtaking gold-ish temples rises high into the sky. The temple area is huge, cows are roaming the area while people a re sitting in the shade of the trees. The inside is even more breathtaking, the walls are covered with huge, colorful paintings depicting holy scenes and the whole place exhales a spiritual calmness like no other temple in Jaffna. The most impressing ritual is performed in the afternoon when the idol rides on a chariot to it's "resting chamber". The Nallur Kovil is accessible for everyone as long as they follow the "dresscode": no shoes as usual. Covered knees and shoulders for women, no shirts for men. text: This temple is most revered in Kaffna where the majority of the population are Hindu. As we went round, the ceremonies started and although there were very few none Hindus there, no one seemed to mind us observing the proceedings, which were extremely colourful, noisy and seemed at times to unfamiliar eyes, to be a little bit chaotic. title: Must-Visit
text: Nallur Kovil is the largest Hindu temple, in terms of area covered, in the whole of Sri Lanka, and is clearly an important place of worship to Jaffna Hindus. It is located a couple of km outside Jaffna centre, an easy bike ride along Temple Road (not sure where the name came from ??), in the sub-centre of Nallur, which served as the capital of the Jaffna kings from the 10th Century until the arrival of the Portuguese here in the late 16th century. The main temple building is massive, although quite dark and dingy in places. No photography is allowed inside, which is understandable but slightly regrettable in that there are some wonderful painted murals that I would have liked to share with others. Worshippers make a contribution of precisely 1 Rp (for which you even get a receipt!), which I think is a beautiful concept - it is the same for everyone, from pauper to president ?? GENERAL DESCRIPTION: The Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil is one of Jaffna’s most significant Hindu temples and is the fourth re-built structure, since the original temple was built in 948. The temple is a socially important institution for the Sri Lankan Tamils Hindu identity of north Sri Lanka and for the Sri Lankan Tamil diaspora. Located in the ancient capital town of Nallur in Jaffna, it is recorded that the center of the city was once a bustling market place, surrounded by a square fortification that sheltered courtly buildings for kings, Brahmin priests and soldiers. The old Nallur Kandaswamy temple functioned within this ancient defensive fort, among a city that was laid out like the traditional temple town according to Hindu traditions.

title: Fantastic visit to our first Hindu Temple. Nallur Kandaswamy temple
text: We were not sure of procedure or how to approach our visit to this temple. However, we did our research and donned a sarong to cover our lower half. The Hindu Temple Nallur Kandaswamy temple is situated in the not so tourist area of Jaffna. Visitors before entering the Temple complex must remove their shoes; men need to remove their shirts as well. The Temple is about 1.5km northeast of the centre. It is exceptionally beautifully colourful, as one would expect from a Hindu Temple dedicated to sacred deity is Lord Murugan (or Skanda). One thing that struck me was the friendliness of the devotees and visitors entering the Temple complex. Even though we could not speak Tamil or Sinhalese the people actually pushed us into places where we could view the ceremony of the "Puja" and then took us by hand to the following 3 or 4 places so as we could be and feel integrated into the ceremonial process. In western religions it's normally first come first served and you're pushed out of the way by the surge of petitions and penitents trying to gain a favour or miracle from the devotion. But here the people were so keen for us to see the adoration of their gods and the ceremony unfold that we were at times led by the hand to "the next installment" - for want of a better phrase. Then once the ceremony had finished we wandered around the Temple complex and some visitors - from the southern part of India, took us to one side and helped us understand what we had just witnessed Several friendly priests, some of whom speak English, can answer questions about the temple and its traditions. Do go to this and any Temple that you find near you on your visits and be inspired and blessed as we were that day at The Nallur Kandaswamy Temple.

title: A must visit while in Jaffna town
text: We spent two days in around Jaffna town. The Nallur Kovil ( Hindu temple) is in the center of town and easily the main attraction. Recently restored and repainted with a magnificent central shrine and several smaller shrines in the perimeter of the main shrine. try to coordinate visit with a time of "pooja" ceremony ( several times per day morning and evenings) when the priests offer prayers and offerings on behalf of the devotees gathered. This is done to the accompaniment of traditional music ( drums and long flute ) providing atmosphere and charm. After the pooja ceremony take time to walk around the inner perimeter of the main temple, with long corridors in classical style to take in the several large murals and carved stone statues depicting other gods and goddesses exquisitely done in gold and vivid colors. Also take note of the 20 foot carved wooden doors at each of the entrances and the "gopurams" towers that painted in gold. Striking are the two newer gopurams on the north and south completed recently. to enter the temple you must go barefooted and males must be bare waist up. No photography. Outside and in the surrounding streets outside this temple are several smaller "kovils" that also prvide interesting viewing and early morning "poojas". Well worth a visit to this vicinity... devote about 1-2 hours

title: Spectacular building, incredible energy
text: Be sure to visit while a puja is happening (5am, 10am, noon, 415pm, 430pm, 5pm and 645pm). This is a spectacular building, both from the outside and the inside. You'll need to remove your shoes to enter. (take them with you or leave them at the gate). Men need to remove their shirts to enter the temple (tuck it in your waistband at the front of your trousers). Women need either a skirt or long trousers and long sleeves. Don't be afraid to join in, the locals will put you right straight away if you do something wrong or watch them first. We entered and immediately were pushed along with the crowd - where women and men were separated and walking bakcwards, we walked in front of the deity as it was borne around the inside of the temple. The deity is lit up (electric lights, as there's a small generator following it round), and there are frequent stops and offerings. It's a magnificent spectacle - no one looks bored and everyone is engaged. The ceremony is noisy, - with drums, with wind instruments and with worshippers getting involved. Let the noise and the experience wash over you - its like a healing ceremony, as it was explained to us. Believers come as often as they need, to soak in the atmosphere of the ceremony and if you do come along during the ceremony you'll feel it all resonate through you. There are no photos allowed inside the temple and there were no social conversations, this was about the ceremony.

title: Beautiful Hindu Tempel and great Architecture
text: Beautiful Hindu Tempel and great Architecture. If you're in Jaffna, a must see Tempel. Unfortunately no photos are allowed inside the tempel. But it was one of the coolest tempel in whole Sri Lanka, therefore no regrets.

title: Beautiful temple, but why build more towers?
text: A large beautiful temple with monumental brightly-painted ornate towers. But I am not sure why they are building another tower. The money could be spent on other charitable social programmes.

title: A bit boring
text: One of the major sights in Jaffna, so probably worth seeing. Just dont plan to spend too much time on it - after all, it is quite boring.

title: temple
text: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil or Nallur Murugan Kovil (Tamil: ??????? ?????????? ??????) is one of the most significant Hindu temples in the Jaffna District of Northern Province, Sri Lanka. It stands in the town of Nallur. The presiding deity is Lord Murugan in the form of the holy Vel. The idol of the Nallur Devi or goddess was given to the temple in the 10th century CE by the Chola queen Sembiyan Mahadevi, in the style of Sembian bronzes.
